title: migration: path lowering misclassifies custom */path interceptors
description:
## Scope

Repair the v1-to-v2 event-registration migration path where the shipped M-73 scanner/codemod encounters interceptor-bearing reg-event-db or reg-event-fx calls. Scope includes migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod, its focused tests/README, the directly coupled re-frame-migration reference/eval, and one focused integration proof against the actual v2 reg-event contract.

## Correctness finding

The guide promises that M-73 composes with M-70, but the implementation performs a head/handler-only rewrite and deliberately preserves every middle slot. For the canonical path-interceptor example it emits an rf/reg-event whose metadata still contains the removed inline (rf/path ...) call; for historical positional chains it emits a reg-event with the retired vector middle slot. Both outputs are invalid v2 and hard-fail while the namespace loads. The codemod then reports the site as :rewrite/:rename rather than an unresolved M-70 finding, so its green unit suite certifies a broken migration.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:482-505 tells users to prefer the shipped codemod and specifies the mechanical conversion from {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} to {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]]]}.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:883-903 calls the codemod first-class/tested and gives the same positional [(rf/path :counter)] to metadata-ref conversion.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj:31-33 instead states that path-interceptor metadata is preserved untouched. analyse-call at 301-342 classifies every reg-event-fx as a pure rename and simple reg-event-db solely by its last handler; it never analyses middle-slot shape or entries. apply-rewrite-at at 665-688 replaces only the registrar head and db handler.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/test/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod_test.clj:102-114 and 125-134 explicitly assert that {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} survives while the call is renamed to reg-event, pinning the invalid output.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1962-1983 makes rf/path a throwing removal stub (:rf.error/path-removed). implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:71-82 and 126-165 require interceptor refs and reject inline values with :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed; 803-837 rejects a positional vector middle slot with :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the shipped codemod rewrite over this v1 source:

       (rf/reg-event-db :counter/inc
         {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
         (fn [db _] (update db :value inc)))

2. Observe that it reports :action :rewrite and emits reg-event while preserving {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}.
3. Load/evaluate the emitted registration with the actual v2 re-frame.core namespace.
4. Observe the namespace-load hard failure :rf.error/path-removed before the handler registers. The positional-vector variant is also retained and is rejected as :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot; a custom inline value retained in metadata is rejected as :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The current successful rewrite is:

    (rf/reg-event :counter/inc
      {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
      (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :value inc)}))

Loading it against v2 calls the removed rf/path stub before the handler can register. A positional v1 chain is likewise left as the now-illegal vector middle slot, and a custom inline value carried into metadata is rejected by reg-event.

Invariant: every site the codemod reports as mechanically rewritten must be a valid v2 registration shape, or it must remain an explicit unresolved M-70 finding. A source transform is not successful merely because it parses and no retired registrar name remains.

## Recommended minimal fix

Teach the codemod one small middle-slot normalization that composes M-70 with M-73:

1. Recognize the standard path constructor in bare, positional-vector, metadata-interceptors, and metadata-plus-vector source shapes; lower each (rf/path p...) to [:rf.interceptor/path [p...]], create or merge the metadata map, and preserve chain order/comments.
2. Preserve entries that are already v2 refs.
3. For any other inline/bare interceptor whose stable registered id cannot be derived without author intent, emit an explicit M-70 Type-B finding and do not claim the event migration complete. Do not leave an invalid inline value hidden behind a successful M-73 result.
4. Scan both retired reg-event-* forms and already rewritten reg-event forms for these invalid middle-slot/inline survivors so a rerun can recover a partially migrated tree.
5. Replace the string-only preservation assertions with exact normalization tests plus a focused registration integration test using the actual v2 core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A codemod test rewrites the canonical metadata source above to a reg-event containing exactly [:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]], with no executable rf/path call, and preserves the db-handler transformation.
- A codemod test rewrites a historical positional path vector and a metadata-plus-vector path chain into the one metadata-map :interceptors ref shape; multiple entries preserve declaration order.
- An executable integration test evaluates/registers the canonical transformed result against the actual v2 core and completes without :rf.error/path-removed, :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot, :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed, or :rf.error/unregistered-interceptor.
- Negative control: feeding the current preserved-inline output to that same integration harness deterministically throws :rf.error/path-removed (or the inline-value equivalent throws :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed), proving the test observes registration rather than only parsing/substring shape. Restoring the old preserve-middle behavior makes the positive test red.
- A custom inline interceptor with no stable id is surfaced as an unresolved M-70 Type-B finding and is not reported as a completed :rename/:rewrite; a rerun over an already-renamed invalid reg-event finds it.
- Non-vacuity controls show interceptor-free reg-event-fx still pure-renames, interceptor-free simple reg-event-db still performs its existing db wrap, already-canonical ref chains remain valid, and running the codemod twice is stable.
- Add a focused re-frame-migration eval fixture whose v1 event contains a path interceptor; its expected result uses the standard ref and the eval fails if the removed inline call or positional vector survives.
- The codemod unit suite and the focused runtime integration test pass.

## Non-goals

- No general Clojure analyser or arbitrary macro evaluation.
- No auto-naming or semantic re-authoring of custom interceptors; those remain M-70 Type B.
- No compatibility alias restoring rf/path, inline interceptor values, or positional reg-event chains in v2.
- No unrelated migration-rule rewrite, formatting cleanup, or broad runtime hardening.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title and description searches were run for: M-73 codemod, reg-event codemod, path interceptor codemod, inline interceptor migration, rf.interceptor/path, middle slot codemod, preserved metadata interceptor, M-70, M-73, reg-event-db, and codemod. A full all-status issue export was also scanned across title/description/notes for the same vocabulary. No existing open, in-progress, blocked, deferred, or closed bead owns this codemod-output/runtime-registration mismatch. rf2-0qzh covered CI discovery/classification for the codemod, not transform correctness; reagent/hicasso codemod beads are different tools and surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Canonical metadata, positional-vector, and metadata-plus-vector path-interceptor inputs lower to metadata :interceptors entries of [:rf.interceptor/path <path-vector>] while preserving handler semantics and chain order.
2. The canonical transformed output is executed against actual v2 reg-event and registers successfully.
3. A negative-control fixture containing the old preserved inline rf/path output throws the expected hard error in that same harness; reverting the normalization makes the positive test fail.
4. Custom inline interceptors without a stable id become explicit unresolved M-70 Type-B findings rather than successful M-73 rewrites, including when found in an already-renamed reg-event.
5. Interceptor-free fx/db rewrites, already-canonical ref chains, and a second codemod run remain successful and stable.
6. A focused migration-skill eval rejects any answer/output that leaves rf/path executable or a positional interceptor vector in reg-event.
7. Focused codemod and runtime integration suites pass.

Skill :482-505 and migration README :883-903 promise the [:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]] conversion the codemod does not perform. AUDIT PR #8828 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: path-call-info identifies the standard re-frame constructor only by (= "path" (name hv)). It therefore treats every qualified custom function named path as rf/path. A deterministic probe on merged main with (app.interceptors/path :tenant) inside a real rf/reg-event-db returned :action :rewrite and emitted [:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]], silently replacing the custom interceptor's semantics instead of producing the promised unresolved M-70 :flag :interceptors. This contradicts the PR's central boundary that only the standard constructor is mechanical and every other custom inline call stays unchanged for author intent. Existing tests cover a custom var, rf/debug, and a dynamic rf/path arg, but not a custom qualified function sharing the simple name. Minimal repair: resolve the call head to re-frame.core/path from the namespace's require/refer aliases, or conservatively flag ambiguous qualified path symbols; add a custom/path negative test while retaining the standard qualified/alias/bare fixtures and idempotence.

Implementation-quality/completeness: the new :integration alias is not invoked by .github/workflows/test.yml or scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh. PR checks ran only clojure -M:test, so the real-v2 registration proof and all four negative controls are currently manual/orphaned. Add clojure -M:integration to the existing changed-surface codemod CI job (keeping it separate from the self-contained :test classpath).

Duplicate search across all statuses for custom path interceptor, symbol named path, path alias codemod, and M-70 custom call found no separate owner. Both residues are exact acceptance/quality gaps in rf2-8odvg.
AUDIT PR #8846 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness: the new namespace resolver still treats namespace-level availability as call-site resolution. In a file that refers re-frame.core/path, a lexically shadowing `let` binding named `path` is therefore silently lowered as the framework constructor. Deterministic probe on merge b38d2e0: `(ns app.events (:require [re-frame.core :refer [reg-event-db path]])) (let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil true]` — a successful rewrite containing `:rf.interceptor/path` — even though the call denotes the custom binding. This contradicts the implementation comment at lines 344-350 and the README guarantee that a local/custom path function flags rather than changes semantics.

Minimal repair: for bare `path`, account for lexical bindings at the interceptor call site, or conservatively refuse lowering when an enclosing scope binds `path`; add one deterministic local-shadow negative fixture plus idempotence. This does not require a general analyser. The separate orphaned integration-CI residue remains owned by rf2-36u96 and is not duplicated here.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 12:14:32 AUSEST (worker, PR #8857, commit ae9a7d7e59). The reopen's probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base 4e27fbbe49 BEFORE any edit and returned [:rewrite nil true] — premise confirmed at source, not assumed. Root cause exactly as the note stated: path-head resolution was a per-SOURCE fact derived from the ns form (path-head-context), with no call-site half, so ns-level AVAILABILITY stood in for what a bare head DENOTES.

FIX: reused the in-file machinery rather than adding a second mechanism. The free-occurrence analysis already carried a binding-form vocabulary (binding-vector-forms, seq-binding-forms, collect-binding-names); that vocabulary is hoisted into one shared section above both consumers, and a new enclosing-scope-binds? walks OUT from the registrar call over the same table. The two analyses now ask opposite questions in opposite directions over one vocabulary. Added the defn family (defn/defn-/defmacro), whose params scope over a registration in the body and which the downward walk had no reason to know. standard-path-head? consults the new :shadowed-bare-path? for BARE heads only — a namespace-qualified symbol names a var and cannot be shadowed by a local.

Conservative refusal, as the note permitted: an enclosing binder routes the site to the existing :flag :interceptors (unresolved M-70 Type B) and leaves the source byte-for-byte unchanged. Position-insensitive inside a binding vector, and an unreadable binding vector counts as binding the name — both errors can only produce a flag where a lowering was possible, never a silent semantic swap.

EVIDENCE (exits captured in the same shell as each run): probe [:rewrite nil true] -> [:flag :interceptors false] with the source byte-identical. clojure -M:test exit 0, 72/245 -> exit 0, 77/276. clojure -M:integration exit 0, 6/10 both sides. NON-VACUITY: one-line revert ((not shadowed-bare-path?) -> true) gives captured exit 1 with 25 failures falling in exactly the three new shadow deftests, at unchanged 77/276 totals so nothing was skipped; the two non-over-reach controls (qualified head inside a shadowing let still lowers; a sibling-form path binding does not suppress the site) stayed green. Restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

Tests added: shadowed-bare-path-flagged-not-lowered (the audit probe), shadowed-bare-path-flagged-across-binding-forms (let / if-let / fn / defn / letfn / doseq), shadowing-does-not-suppress-a-qualified-head, shadowing-elsewhere-does-not-suppress-a-referred-bare-path, shadowed-bare-path-idempotent. README's path-resolution guarantee updated to state the call-site half; its gate is check_doc_slugs.py, NOT check_readme_links.py (migration/ is in the latter's DOCS_GATE_ROOTS exclusion and in the former's DEFAULT_ROOTS) — established by planting a broken link: docs gate exit 1 naming file and line, readme gate exit 0.

The orphaned-integration-CI residue is rf2-36u96's, landed as the second commit of the same PR.
AUDIT PR #8857 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: the lexical-shadow repair recognizes only unqualified binding-form heads. A valid qualified macro such as `clojure.core/let` is absent from `binding-vector-forms`, so `enclosing-scope-binds?` misses its local `path`. Deterministic probe at merge db8949e406: `(clojure.core/let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil]` and emitted `[:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]]`, silently replacing the custom interceptor. The same checkout evaluates `(clojure.core/let [path (fn [x] [:custom x])] (path :tenant))` as `[:custom :tenant]`, proving the source form is valid rather than synthetic.

Minimal repair: normalize recognized binding heads by simple name only when they resolve to clojure.core, or explicitly include their qualified clojure.core spellings; retain conservative refusal for ambiguous/custom macros. Add a qualified-let negative fixture plus the existing bare and sibling controls. All-status searches for `clojure.core/let`, qualified/namespaced binding forms, qualified binders, and `enclosing-scope-binds?` found no separate owner; this is the exact unresolved lexical-shadow acceptance boundary of rf2-8odvg.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 (worker, PR #8896, commit b57bbac2f2). Scope: the AUDIT PR #8857 reopen only — the newest text-bearing mutation on this bead, established by walking bd history newest-first to the bead beginning (394 entries, 5 text-bearing changes, oldest entry notes-length 0 so the walk reached creation). The DESCRIPTION is historical: its central premise (head/handler-only rewrite, every middle slot preserved) was discharged by the three merged PRs #8828 / #8846 / #8857, and the two sibling acceptance items were confirmed present at tip — the migration-skill eval fixture in skills/re-frame-migration/evals/evals.json, and clojure -M:integration wired into .github/workflows/test.yml.

PREMISE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED. The audit probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base a272031831 BEFORE any edit: the clojure.core/let form returned [:rewrite nil] and emitted the framework ref, while the bare-let control on the same run returned [:flag :interceptors] — isolating qualification, not shadowing, as the cause. The validity control evaluated the probe form to [:custom :tenant] in the same JVM, so it is real Clojure.

ROOT CAUSE: form-binds? asked the binding vocabulary whether it held a head VERBATIM. The vocabulary is keyed by unqualified symbols, so a qualified spelling of a binder was not a binder, and an unrecognised head bound nothing at all.

FIX — A RULE, NOT A ROSTER. Enumerating binder spellings one at a time is what reopened this bead three times, each on the next spelling of one hole, so the roster lookup is replaced by two rules that both fail CLOSED, towards the flag: (1) a recognised binder is matched by its SIMPLE name (binding-head), so clojure.core/let, cljs.core/let and an aliased c/let all count — the namespace is DISCARDED rather than resolved, deliberately, because resolving it is the fail-open choice that would leave an unrecognised my.macros/let binding nothing; (2) a head outside the vocabulary falls to unrecognised-form-binds?, where a vector child that binds the name — read as either a binding vector or a params vector — makes the form a binder, covering defmethod, when-first, dotimes, deftype methods and project macros without a general analyser (excluded by the non-goals). The catch-all is narrow: it fires only when a form enclosing the registration has a vector child that literally binds the name, and can only ever add a flag.

DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: the free-occurrence walk (free-in-form?) shares this vocabulary but consults it in the opposite direction, and a miss there fails SAFE — an unrecognised head falls through to free-in-children?, whose bare LHS occurrence reads as free, and referenced is the branch that keeps the name-preserving rebind. Normalising it would have been an unrelated behaviour change. The asymmetry is now stated at the shared vocabulary in-source.

EVIDENCE, each exit captured with the redirect and echo on one command line in one shell: clojure -M:test exit 0 at 77 tests / 276 assertions before, exit 0 at 82 / 310 after; clojure -M:integration exit 0 at 6 / 10 both sides; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. The probe flipped from [:rewrite nil] to [:flag :interceptors] with the source byte-identical. Doc-gate coverage was PROVEN rather than assumed by planting a broken link in the codemod README: exit 1 naming the file and line, restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object rather than by reading a diff.

TESTS ADDED (5): shadowed-bare-path-flagged-under-a-qualified-binder (the audit probe, plus cljs.core/let, an aliased c/let, clojure.core/fn); shadowed-bare-path-flagged-under-an-unrecognised-binder (defmethod, when-first, dotimes, a project macro); unrecognised-head-without-a-path-binding-still-lowers (NON-VACUITY for the catch-all: deftest/testing, comment, a defmethod binding another param, a doseq binding another name all still lower); qualified-binder-shadowing-does-not-suppress-a-qualified-head (over-reach control); qualified-binder-shadow-idempotent.

DOCS: migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/README.md carried this guarantee in two places and both now state that kin is a rule rather than a roster. The HOT-ZONE migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md was NOT touched — it does not state the shadow guarantee, so nothing in it became untrue.
close_reason: Lexical-shadow boundary closed by PR #8896 (commit b57bbac2f2). The AUDIT PR #8857 reopen — the newest text-bearing mutation, found by walking bd history to the bead beginning — was reproduced at source before any edit: a qualified binder such as clojure.core/let around a registration left a bare path head reading as the framework constructor, and the site lowered to the interceptor ref, silently replacing the custom interceptor. Cause: form-binds? matched heads VERBATIM against a vocabulary keyed by unqualified symbols. Repaired with two fail-closed rules replacing the roster lookup — binders matched by simple name, and an unrecognised head whose vector child binds the name treated as a binder — which also covers defmethod / when-first / dotimes / project macros without a general analyser. Five tests added including a non-vacuity control that unrecognised heads NOT binding path still lower. Gates, exits captured in-shell: clojure -M:test exit 0 (77/276 to 82/310), clojure -M:integration exit 0 (6/10), check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 with coverage proven by a planted broken link (exit 1) and restore verified by blob hash. The bead DESCRIPTION is historical — its original premise was discharged by merged PRs #8828 / #8846 / #8857, and both sibling acceptance items (the migration-skill eval fixture, and clojure -M:integration wired into test.yml) were confirmed present at tip.

title: implementor skill: foundation gate can pass a reference-keyed live sub-cache
description:
## Scope

Correct the completion and EP-006 verification workflow in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/**` so a non-CLJS port cannot be declared foundation-complete while its live subscription cache is keyed by host reference identity. Keep the corpus score as an honest corpus score; add only the one port-owned live witness needed for the observability gap already acknowledged by the pinned Spec. Limit supporting checks/evals to this outcome.

## Correctness finding

The skill makes the conformance corpus the acceptance test and its Done gate accepts a green `:core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*` run as foundation completion. Its EP-006 row specifically calls the two `:identity/cedn1` Mode-B fixtures "sub-cache fixtures." Those fixtures never touch a frame, `subscribe`, a cache slot, ref-counting, or disposal: they call the canonical-identity primitive directly. The owning Spec explicitly says the missing live assertion would subscribe one query through two distinct host allocations and observe one cache-slot creation.

A TypeScript port can therefore implement CEDN-1 correctly, use Immer for structural sharing, but store query arrays in a native reference-keyed `Map`. Every required fixture can pass and the skill can report v1 completion even though equal freshly allocated queries create separate derived containers forever. This is a false-green proof of a pattern-required runtime contract, not a request for broader coverage.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:9-10,31,52,70-75` repeatedly says the corpus is the acceptance test and defines Done as the three required fixture families being green.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:35` describes `:identity/cedn1` as the EP-006 "sub-cache fixtures"; lines 40 and 68 make fixture-set greens acceptance gates, and line 78 permits completion after those discovered gates.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:78-90` requires a port-owned self-test only when a mandated surface has no fixture. It does not cover a fixture that exists but observes only a prerequisite, and line 90 equates `N / N` with conformance against the claim.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:793-820` requires `rf=`-keyed live lookup and explains that native JS `Map`/array identity breaks de-duplication, ref-count convergence, and disposal. It also notes that Immer supplies neither value equality nor a value-keyed map.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:824-829` says the two fixtures assert only canonical cache-key identity and explicitly leaves the deeper live-runtime assertion as follow-up because the current Mode-A DSL cannot subscribe two distinct host allocations.
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn:36-76` is a Mode-B `:fixture/calls` file containing only `:canonical-identical` and `:canonical-distinct` calls. Its companion `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn` likewise tests canonical bytes/identity only.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:1026-1039` executes those calls through `identity/identical-identity?`; no subscription-cache code is reached.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json:4-25` is trigger-only, so no outcome regression prevents the skill from accepting this corpus-green/runtime-red port.
- The focused implementor guards are currently green, but they check EP order, required family names, partition vocabulary, and bead leakage; neither exercises this completion invariant (`python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --self-test`, `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --verbose --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --self-test`, and `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --verbose --ci`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a minimum TypeScript-shaped port, implement the CEDN-1 canonical operations correctly and use a native `Map<QueryVector, CacheEntry>` for the live sub-cache.
2. Run all claimed required-family fixtures. The two named sub-cache fixtures pass because they invoke only the canonical identity functions, and the required-foundation score can reach `claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable`.
3. Allocate two separate arrays with equal contents, for example `q1 = ['editor/field-error', 'title']` and `q2 = ['editor/field-error', 'title']`, and subscribe both in one frame.
4. Observe two native-Map keys, two derived containers, and two first-run computations. Releasing the readers cannot converge on one slot's last-reader disposal even though the skill's current completion proof is green.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A React view constructs its query array afresh on every render. Under reference-keyed lookup, every render misses the cache, repeats the subscription computation, and leaves an independently referenced entry whose lifecycle cannot converge with the prior readers. The port is reported conformant despite violating the required invariant: two separately allocated query vectors that are `rf=` must resolve to one live cache entry, one shared computation, and one ref-count; that entry disposes exactly once after the last equal reader releases it. A non-equal query must remain a different entry.

## Recommended minimal fix

Add one explicit EP-006 completion proof to the skill: on a host whose ordinary map keys collections by reference (or whenever the selected cache mechanism does not intrinsically provide `rf=` keys), run a port-owned live test using two separately allocated but `rf=`-equal query values. Require the result at the EP-006 checkpoint and in the v1 Done gate alongside the corpus score. In `conformance.md`, name this as the pinned Spec's known observability gap: the existing identity fixtures prove the canonical-key prerequisite, not live cache wiring, so a port-owned self-test is required even though fixture files exist.

Keep the proof mechanism-agnostic. The port may use an `rf=`-keyed persistent map or an interned canonical key; the skill should require the observable one-slot/one-lifecycle result, not prescribe a library. Add a focused outcome regression for the skill so a corpus-green/live-red TypeScript-shaped port is diagnosed as incomplete.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The published EP-006 workflow and Done checklist explicitly distinguish canonical-identity fixture success from live sub-cache success. A non-CLJS/reference-keyed host cannot be called EP-006-, foundation-, or v1-complete until the live witness below has run green; the reported conformance fraction remains the fixture result rather than being silently inflated.
2. The required executable witness creates `q1` and `q2` through separate host allocations, first proves `rf=(q1,q2)`, subscribes both in the same frame through the public/runtime subscription path, and observes exactly one cache slot, one derived container/first-run computation, and a shared ref-count. Releasing one reader keeps the slot live; releasing the second removes it and invokes disposal exactly once.
3. Negative control: a third query with a different argument value is not `rf=` to `q1` and produces a second cache slot and second first-run computation. This prevents a degenerate implementation that interns or collapses every query from satisfying the positive witness.
4. Non-vacuity mutation control: temporarily replace the value-keyed lookup in the test port with the host's native reference-keyed `Map`. The existing `sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn`, `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn`, and required-foundation corpus run remain green, while the live witness exits nonzero on two slots/two first-runs. Restore the conforming lookup and record the same witness green.
5. A focused checked-in skill outcome eval presents that exact corpus-green/live-red TypeScript-shaped checkpoint. The expected result withholds EP-006/v1 completion, names reference-keyed live lookup as the port bug, and asks/runs the live witness; a paired one-slot control is accepted. The eval must execute through the skill's normal route, not merely search for a phrase in Markdown.
6. Existing implementor order/partition self-tests and CI modes remain green. Any focused guard added for this invariant has its own red control (remove the live-proof requirement and the guard/eval fails) and does not pin a copied fixture catalogue or implementation token.

## Non-goals

title: skill/re-frame2: JVM with-frame recipe silently skips every test body
description:
## Scope

Correct the JVM frame-pinning recipe in skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md and add the smallest skill-side regression witness in the existing re-frame2 skill eval/drift-gate surface. The library macro itself is correct and is not in scope.

## Correctness finding

The testing leaf tells JVM authors to use (rf/with-frame frame-id (fn [] ...)) as a "function form." No such function form exists. rf/with-frame is the same body-splicing macro on JVM and CLJS.

Because the thunk is a legal body expression, this does not fail loudly: the macro binds the frame, evaluates the fn literal, returns that function, and exits the binding without invoking it. In a clojure.test use-fixtures wrapper this silently prevents the test function from running. The suite can exit 0 after running zero tests and zero assertions.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md:135-148 first shows the correct macro body form, then explicitly overrides it for JVM readers with: "On JVM use the (rf/with-frame frame-id (fn [] ...)) function form."
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1319-1335 defines with-frame only as a macro with arglist [frame-id body+]. There is no facade function twin.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:233-251 expands it to a binding whose body is spliced directly with ~@body. A supplied fn literal is returned, not called.
- skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/frames.md:178 correctly says the macro expands on both CLJS and JVM. references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:34 also gives the body form. The testing leaf is internally inconsistent with both.
- JVM implementation tests use the real fixture shape, for example implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace_test.clj:63-69 and always_on_validation_production_test.clj:108-109: (rf/with-frame frame-id (test-fn)), not a thunk literal.
- A deterministic probe run from implementation/core:

    clojure -M -e "(require '[re-frame.core :as rf]) (let [ran? (atom false) result (rf/with-frame :probe (fn [] (reset! ran? true)))] (prn {:body-ran? @ran? :returned-thunk? (fn? result)}) (result) (prn {:body-ran-after-manual-call? @ran?}))"

  Current output was {:body-ran? false, :returned-thunk? true}, then {:body-ran-after-manual-call? true}. This proves with-frame itself never invoked the taught thunk.
- A second probe installed the taught shape as a clojure.test :each fixture around a deftest whose body sets an atom and contains a failing assertion. clojure.test reported "Ran 0 tests containing 0 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.", returned a zero-failure summary, left the body atom false, and the process exited 0.
- The current eval corpus has no with-frame scenario, and python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py, check_skill_eval_docs.py, check_skill_eval_packaging.py, check_skill_package_refs.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py, and check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py all exit 0 over this bad instruction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a JVM test namespace, create an atom ran? initialized false.
2. Install an :each fixture shaped as (fn [test-fn] (rf/with-frame :app/test (fn [] (test-fn)))).
3. Define a deftest that resets ran? true and contains (is false).
4. Run the namespace with clojure.test.
5. Observe that the test body does not execute, the summary reports zero tests/assertions and zero failures/errors, and the process exits successfully.
6. Change only the fixture body to (rf/with-frame :app/test (test-fn)). The test now executes and the deliberate failing assertion makes the run red.

## Expected Behavior

Skill-generated JVM tests pin the frame with the public macro body form. A fixture must invoke test-fn inside the binding, so every test and assertion executes and failures make the declared gate non-zero.

## Actual Behavior

The platform-specific instruction wraps the test call in an uninvoked thunk. It converts a failing suite into a vacuous green run while appearing to follow the canonical testing leaf exactly.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A programmer or AI follows the testing leaf while adding frame-scoped JVM tests, commonly by writing a use-fixtures wrapper. Every test under that fixture is skipped. CI reports success, so broken event, subscription, machine, SSR, or resource behavior can ship with tests that never ran.

Invariant: a testing recipe must never turn the test runner's test function into an inert return value. The documented frame scope must execute its body on both host platforms.

## Recommended minimal fix

Delete the nonexistent JVM "function form" distinction. Teach one public shape on both platforms:

- General body: (rf/with-frame frame-id body...)
- clojure.test fixture: (rf/with-frame frame-id (test-fn))

Keep only the CLJS macro-import note that is genuinely platform-specific. Do not add a facade function twin or recommend direct binding of internal dynamic Vars.

Add one bounded regression check or eval expectation for the exact JVM fixture shape, backed by the executable zero-test control above, so the silent thunk form cannot return.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. references/cross-cutting/testing.md states that rf/with-frame is a macro on both JVM and CLJS and shows a JVM use-fixtures example that calls (test-fn) inside the macro body; no positive instruction names or demonstrates a JVM thunk/function form.
2. A focused JVM probe using the corrected fixture runs at least one named test and at least one assertion, sets a body-executed sentinel true, and exits 0 for a passing assertion.
3. The same probe with the assertion deliberately false exits non-zero or returns a summary with one failure, proving the fixture cannot skip the test body.
4. Non-vacuity: mutate only the documented/generated fixture back to (rf/with-frame frame-id (fn [] (test-fn))). The skill regression check/eval must fail, and the behavioral control must reproduce zero executed tests/assertions with the sentinel false.
5. Extend either the existing eval corpus or scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py plus its self-test with this exact platform-specific regression. The check must accept (rf/with-frame frame-id (test-fn)) and reject the positive thunk recipe without banning ordinary fn bodies elsewhere.
6. python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --self-test, python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py, python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py, and the relevant skill packaging/reference gates pass.

## Non-goals

- Changing re-frame.core/with-frame or adding a second JVM function API.
- Redesigning frame scope, with-new-frame, capture-frame, clojure.test fixtures, or the test-support library.
- A general Markdown snippet compiler or exhaustive prose parser.
- Rewriting unrelated testing recipes, eval prompts, or skill leaves.
- Treating an explicit thunk return as illegal application code outside this positive fixture instruction.

## Related / duplicate search

Fresh all-status title, description, and notes searches covered with-frame, function form, JVM fixture, test fixture, returns the thunk, test-fn, zero tests, and skills/re-frame2. No bead owns this false-green instruction.

rf2-g9k0g is the closed adjacent surface-review task that allowed the authoring agent to run a project's declared gate; it does not cover whether the skill's JVM fixture recipe causes that gate to execute tests. rf2-czlb and rf2-6c12m.13 mention with-frame only in unrelated Hicasso boundary/capture-frame work.

SURFACES: skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md + scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py (+ self-test) or the eval corpus; no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: none - live skills-shared-own holds other skill files/scripts (check_skill_package_refs.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py), not testing.md or the re_frame2 drift script. GATES: python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --self-test; python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py; python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py; all light, no heavy lane. AMBIGUITY: AC5 offers eval-corpus OR drift-script extension - recommend the drift-script check (accept the (test-fn) body form, reject the positive thunk recipe) as the smaller change. SHAPE: solo, first wave (small, fast).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8822. testing.md now teaches the macro body form on both hosts with a JVM use-fixtures example invoking (test-fn) INSIDE the macro body; no positive thunk/function-form instruction remains. Rule 8 in check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py rejects a fn literal (or #(...)) in with-frame's direct body-head position, fenced and inline alike, with self-test fixtures both ways plus the real-corpus reintroduction mutation. Behavioral witness: old taught form + (is false) ran 0 tests / 0 assertions, body sentinel false, exit 0 (false green); corrected form + same assertion ran 1 test / 1 assertion, 1 failure, exit 1 (honest red); corrected form + passing assertion exit 0. Non-vacuity: Rule 8 red on the pre-fix leaf at testing.md:148 (sole finding corpus-wide), red again on the AC4 mutation, restore verified by git blob hash. Gates on rebased base 1246e4e422: drift --self-test 0, drift 0, eval_docs 0, doc_slugs 0, eval_packaging 0, package_refs 0.

title: bug(machines-viz): stale ELK settle can overwrite the current topology
description:
## Scope

Correct the `MachineChart` async layout-settle boundary in `tools/machines-viz`. The fix covers every ELK pass owned by one mounted Form-2 chart instance (initial layout and measured relayout) when a newer `:definition`, direction, layout option, density, Context-band row count, or adaptive-mode key supersedes it. Add one deterministic CLJS regression at the existing component seam. No Xray API or selection-flow redesign is required.

## Correctness finding

`MachineChart` starts a new asynchronous ELK pass whenever `this-key` differs from `@layout-key`, but every pass callback later commits its result unconditionally. The callback closes over its own `this-key`; it never checks that this key is still the active `@layout-key` before `reset!`-ing `layout-state` and scheduling `fitView`.

A slow result for topology A can therefore resolve after topology B has already become current and settled, overwrite B's positions, routed edge points, edge-label positions, or layout-error state, and schedule a fit for A. The next render still projects definition B, but against A's layout maps. B node ids absent from A's result fall back to `{x 0, y 0}`, so the visible current machine can collapse at the origin or carry routes from another topology until another real layout invalidation happens. This is a wrong-visualization failure, not a cosmetic timing detail: a developer can be shown topology B with geometry produced for A.

## Evidence

- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:1302-1303` derives the active layout key, and lines 1420-1427 update `layout-key` and launch a new pass while an older Promise may still be pending.
- `chart.cljs:1310-1348` closes each pass over `this-key`, but lines 1331-1348 accept every non-nil callback result, unconditionally `reset! layout-state`, update `:fit-key`, and schedule `fitView`; there is no `= this-key @layout-key` current-generation check.
- `chart.cljs:671-686` maps every ELK Promise resolution or rejection directly to `done-fn`; it provides neither cancellation nor latest-request arbitration.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/projection.cljc:1384` and lines 1742-1743 default missing position ids to `{x 0, y 0}`. Lines 1709-1711 read routed edge/label maps by the current edge ids. Thus an A result committed while B is current produces observable corrupt B geometry rather than being harmless unused data.
- The public contract explicitly supports changed definitions and keeps previous positions in flight: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:1403-1425`. A stale completion is therefore reachable through normal API use, not an unsupported prop sequence.
- Xray's Static Machines detail keeps the chart at the same unkeyed component position while selection changes: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/definition_detail.cljs:213-283` passes the newly selected definition through `topology.cljs:97-133` and `panels/machine_canvas.cljs:329-373` to one `MachineChart` component type. React/Reagent preserves the Form-2 instance and its pending callbacks across that prop change.
- The test suite already models exactly this reuse. `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/parse_cache_cljs_test.cljs:2-24` says repeated calls to one Form-2 render function simulate a new definition, but its harness replaces `compute-layout!` with a no-op (`:55-117`), so it cannot exercise completion order. `auto_fit_view_cljs_test.cljs:263-303` mirrors only the synchronous fit-key predicate. No test captures two real layout callbacks and resolves them in reverse order.

## Failure scenario / invariant

Deterministic sequence:

1. Render definition A; capture its pending layout callback `done-A`.
2. Re-render the same `MachineChart` instance with definition B; `@layout-key` becomes B and capture `done-B`.
3. Invoke `done-B` first with B-only sentinel positions/routes. B correctly becomes visible.
4. Invoke `done-A` second with A-only sentinel positions/routes. Current code overwrites `layout-state` with A and schedules an A-key fit even though the current props and `@layout-key` are B.
5. Re-render B. Its nodes read absent positions and fall back to the origin; its current routed geometry has been lost.

Invariant: only the completion whose closed layout key equals the chart instance's current layout key may mutate visible layout state or trigger post-settle fitting. Completion order must not change the final visualization. This applies equally to a stale first pass and a stale measured second pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use the existing Node-runnable Form-2 test seam: create one `MachineChart` inner render function, replace `compute-layout!` with a capturing stub, render definition A and then definition B before completing either callback, resolve B's callback with B-only sentinel geometry, then resolve A's callback with A-only geometry. Render B once more and inspect the positions passed to `projection/xyflow-graph` (and the `invoke-fit-view!` spy). On current main, the final projection receives A's stale layout map and the stale callback can schedule another fit; B-only node ids therefore use the origin fallback.

## Recommended minimal fix

At the component-owned callback in `run-layout!`, gate all visible settle side effects on `(= this-key @layout-key)`. An obsolete result should simply be ignored: do not replace `layout-state`, do not update `fit-state`, and do not schedule `fitView`. Keep the current key construction, previous-layout-during-flight behavior, parse/projection caches, ELK instance, and error-result shape unchanged.

Do not add Promise cancellation machinery or serialize all layouts. A one-generation equality check at the single commit boundary is sufficient and also covers measured relayout callbacks because they close over the same `this-key`.

## Non-goals

- Changing which props invalidate layout or changing the layout-key contents.
- Debouncing machine selection, serializing ELK work, terminating/recreating the shared ELK worker, or adding cancellation tokens throughout `compute-layout!`.
- Remounting `MachineChart` per machine id as a workaround; preserving the Form-2 instance and its caches is intentional.
- Changing ELK algorithms, visual styling, topology projection, auto-fit timing, Xray selection UX, or public component props.
- Broad async hardening unrelated to committing the latest layout result.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title, description, and notes searches for `stale ELK`, `ELK Promise`, `out-of-order layout`, `async layout`, `layout settle`, `stale layout`, `focused-machine change`, `definition switch`, and `layout result` returned no matching bead. A broader all-status `ELK` search found only open `rf2-rc0yh` (skill setup SPA) and `rf2-zq34m` (template SPA), neither about layout arbitration. Open `rf2-sxw06` is the distinct Mermaid-copy workflow. Historical source references `rf2-s5kyp` (focused-machine auto-fit) and `rf2-jl72i` (parse cache); those changes create/test the normal prop-change path but do not arbitrate reversed Promise completion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a Node-runnable CLJS component regression that creates one real `MachineChart` Form-2 render function, renders distinct definitions A then B without completing A, and captures the two `compute-layout!` callbacks.
- The regression invokes `done-B` with B-only sentinel positions, routed edge points, and edge-label positions, then invokes `done-A` with different A-only sentinels. A subsequent B render must still project the exact B sentinels and must not expose A's layout-error or geometry.
- Non-vacuity/control: assert exactly two callbacks were captured and explicitly invoked; assert `done-B` visibly changes the projected positions from the pre-layout fallback before `done-A` is invoked. With the current-generation guard locally removed/inverted, the final B assertion must fail.
- A stale completion must not update `:fit-key` or call `invoke-fit-view!`; the current B completion still schedules exactly the existing one post-settle fit when an instance is available.
- Cover the same invariant for a stale measured relayout callback, either as a second arm of the focused regression or by driving the captured old callback through non-nil measured dimensions.
- Preserve the current in-flight behavior: after B starts and before B settles, the last committed layout remains visible rather than flashing an empty graph.
- Existing machines-viz parse-cache, auto-fit, compute-layout error, projection, and chart DOM suites remain green; no public prop or Xray selection API changes.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 19:38:35 AUSEST (read-only agent at 35402e4322): HOLDS. chart.cljs run-layout! callback (:1311-1349) reset!s layout-state and swaps :fit-key unconditionally - no (= this-key @layout-key) guard anywhere in the commit; :1420-1427 resets layout-key and launches a new pass while an older Promise may pend; compute-layout! :668-689 maps every resolution/rejection straight to done-fn; projection.cljc defaults missing position ids to {x 0 y 0} (:1384, :1742-1746), so a stale A commit visibly corrupts current B. The one-generation equality gate the bead specifies is the right minimal fix. SURFACES: tools/machines-viz/** only (it has its OWN shadow-cljs.edn - the hot-zone top-level implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is not touched); no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: none live or sibling. GATES: npm run test:tools-machines-viz --prefix implementation [HEAVY - shadow-cljs compile; serialize with other heavy lanes]. Per standing rule the PR must update tools spec or state spec unchanged because no public prop/API change (true here). AMBIGUITY: none material - the bead pre-empts cancellation machinery; keep to the equality check at the single commit boundary, cover the measured-relayout arm. SHAPE: solo, first wave.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8826 (worker/machines-viz-settle-x19xi, bb518cada2). Design: key-equality stale guard at the single commit boundary — run-layout!'s callback now commits only when (= this-key @layout-key); each pass closes over its launch key and layout-key is reset before every launch, so every commit is current-or-dropped with zero new state (no generation counter, no cancellation machinery, per the bead's recommended minimal fix). One guard covers both the initial and measured-relayout passes (both route through the same run-layout! closure); a stale result is dropped whole: no layout-state, no :fit-key, no fitView. Regression: stale_settle_cljs_test.cljs — deterministic Node CLJS at the existing Form-2 set!-seam (captured compute-layout! callbacks invoked directly, out of order; no Promises/sleeps), 3 arms: stale initial settle (geometry + fit), stale measured relayout (+ in-flight keep-previous pin), stale layout-error settle (no banner over healthy topology). Gates (npm run test:tools-machines-viz, foreground, captured exits): fix in place = 844 tests / 3745 assertions / 0 failures, exit 0. Control (guard removed at one line) = 11 failures all in the new suite (5 initial / 4 measured / 2 error) naming the stale overwrite, exit 1; restore verified by blob hash equal to committed object b2e3b5c7eb2f. Consolidated test:cljs lane also selects the new -cljs-test ns; CI relied on for it. Spec unchanged because no public prop / layout-invalidation trigger / API surface changed (stated in PR body per standing rule).

title: bug(story-mcp): retire the transport-unreachable blocking recorder
description:
## Scope

Retire the unreachable blocking recorder workflow from the published headless Story-MCP catalogue. Limit the change to `tools/story-mcp/**` plus directly coupled current Story MCP-surface prose/fixtures. Preserve Story core's recorder primitives and the settled Pair-owned live-browser route.

## Correctness finding

`record-as-variant` advertises a successful non-empty capture while making the actor that must produce the events unreachable. The handler performs `start-recording!`, blocks the only stdio dispatch loop for `:duration-ms`, then calls `stop-recording!`. While it sleeps, the server cannot read or dispatch a second MCP request. A human canvas cannot supply events either: the shipped server is a headless JVM subprocess with no JVM-to-browser bridge. Therefore a normal MCP client has no transport-reachable way to drive an event during the recording window. The tool normally returns a successful empty snippet, not the recorded interaction its name and contract promise.

This violates the tool-boundary invariant: every advertised success path must be exercisable through the published transport, without an undisclosed in-process collaborator. A green zero-event response is especially misleading because it looks like a valid recording artefact.

## Evidence

- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:297-333` owns one synchronous read -> dispatch -> write loop; it does not read the next frame until the current handler returns.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:343-350` starts the recorder, calls blocking `sleep-ms`, and only then stops it. Lines 43-62 and 136-178 explicitly define the duration window as blocking the server loop.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:418-457` advertises this as a first-class tool that starts, blocks, stops, and returns captured dispatches.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:586-593` says the agent or human drives dispatches during that blocked window. `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:425-436` separately describes start, intervening MCP interactions, and stop, but Story-MCP exposes no independent start/stop request pair and the live browser is explicitly Pair-owned.
- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:15-20,54-95` and `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:37-72` establish that the shipped process sees only its own JVM registry and has no browser/nREPL bridge.
- The focused JVM tests do not exercise the transport path: `tools/story-mcp/test/re_frame/story_mcp/tools_test.clj:1854-1920` installs an `add-watch` on the recorder atom that injects events synchronously inside `start-recording!` on the handler's own thread. That is a hidden in-process collaborator unavailable to MCP clients.
- The official SDK witness explicitly accepts only the vacuous arm: `tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-story.cjs:633-653` calls the tool with zero duration and requires `recorded-event-count` to be 0. No stdio/SDK witness produces one captured event.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Story-MCP through its documented consumer alias with one JVM-loadable variant registered.
2. Complete `initialize`, then call `record-as-variant` for that variant with `duration-ms: 5000`.
3. Before that call returns, write a second valid `tools/call` intended to execute the variant to the same server stdin.
4. Observe that no response to the second call arrives during the recording window; the synchronous run loop cannot read it until `record-as-variant` has stopped recording and returned.
5. Observe that the first call succeeds with `recorded-event-count: 0` and an empty generated script. Interacting with a browser Story canvas cannot change this JVM recorder because the server has no browser bridge.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The second MCP request remains unread until after the first call has already stopped recording. A browser interaction cannot reach the JVM recorder. The result is a green, empty artefact from a capture path whose advertised producer cannot overlap its window.

Required invariant: a catalogue tool must not report successful capture when every producer available through that catalogue is sequenced outside its capture window.

## Recommended minimal fix

Take the pre-alpha subtraction: remove `record-as-variant` from Story-MCP's live registry, generated descriptor manifest, tool-name fixture, current Story-MCP specs/README, and its adapter-only tests. Keep the recorder in `tools/story/` for its real in-process/browser consumers, and state once that interactive canvas recording is performed through Pair in the attached CLJS runtime.

Do not make the stdio loop concurrent, add background jobs/session tokens, add a second browser bridge, or preserve a deprecated alias. If a future concrete headless use case needs capture, require an executable SDK witness with a transport-reachable event producer before adding a turn-shaped start/finish surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A live official-SDK `tools/list` response no longer contains `record-as-variant`; the committed tool-name fixture, generated descriptor manifest, catalogue counts, README, and current normative Story-MCP API/spec tables agree with the reduced registry.
2. An SDK `tools/call` naming `record-as-variant` receives the server's existing method-not-found response, and a before/after read of the Story recorder state proves the rejected call did not start or alter a recording.
3. No reachable Story-MCP handler starts a recorder and sleeps for a duration window, and no current Story-MCP prose claims an agent or human can inject events while its only stdio loop is blocked. Browser-canvas recording is routed to the established Pair/live-CLJS door without adding another transport.
4. Non-vacuity: the end-to-end witness first proves the same launched server has a working catalogue and execution path (`register-variant` followed by `run-variant` returns the fixture verdict), then proves recorder absence. The absence assertion must not pass merely because initialization, registry loading, or all tool dispatch is broken.
5. Control: a focused inventory test compares the live `tools/list` surface with the committed fixture and explicitly rejects the retired name; temporarily reintroducing the descriptor (or the forbidden fixture name) makes that test red, restoring the edit makes it green.
6. Story core recorder tests remain green, demonstrating that only the impossible headless adapter is removed. Story-MCP JVM tests, descriptor generation/check, stdio roundtrip, and official SDK Story conformance pass with the reduced surface.

## Non-goals

- No changes to `re-frame.story` recorder semantics, event filtering, coeffect capture, snippet generation, or browser UI recording.
- No concurrent/multiplexed stdio dispatcher, worker queue, progress stream, polling protocol, session token, or background scheduler.
- No nREPL/JVM-to-browser bridge and no new Pair-MCP tool.
- No redesign of `register-variant`, `run-variant`, write gating, sensitive-read egress, dedup, or token caps.
- No compatibility warning, alias, deprecation period, or migration ceremony for the pre-alpha tool.

## Related / duplicate search

- `rf2-p1keh` (open) removes false cross-process Story-MCP calls from the Pair skill and keeps live Story work on Pair's attached browser. It explicitly does not change Story-MCP; this bug removes the impossible headless recorder tool itself, so the outcomes are complementary, not duplicates.
- `rf2-cfq8a` (closed) made JVM-loadable project stories reachable at Story-MCP launch; it preserves the headless/live-browser boundary and does not make an actor reachable during a blocked recorder call.
- `rf2-7dewo` (closed) converged Story variant vocabulary and touched recorder write-back spelling; it did not address capture reachability.
- All-status title, description, and notes searches for `record-as-variant`, recorder, `duration-ms`, blocking/recording window, `start-recording!`, `stop-recording!`, drives interactions, zero/empty capture, turn-shaped, browser bridge, same JVM, and existing MCP write surface found no bead owning this outcome.

title: epoch: replace-frame-state! can overwrite a same-id successor
description:
## Scope

Make the dev-only Tool-Pair state-injection transaction in `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` and `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` exact-incarnation from precondition sampling through the physical write and synthetic-epoch publication. Add focused JVM/CLJS epoch tests; touch nearby Tool-Pair/API wording only if needed to state the existing lifecycle invariant. The existing exact core write primitive is sufficient.

## Correctness finding

`replace-frame-state!` validates only a bare frame id and returns no incarnation token. Its perform path then re-resolves that id for the drain lock, coherent read, two-arity `frame/replace-frame-state!` write, owner claim, history append, trace, and listener fan-out. If validated incarnation A is destroyed and same-id successor B is seated before the write, the stale A gesture writes into B, records the transition in B's history, and returns `true`. If A disappears just after its physical write, the synthetic-record tail can instead append A's before/after snapshot into B's ring. Restore already closes both classes of race by carrying the exact token end to end; injection does not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the plain-atom adapter, register a `[:set-owner x]` event, make frame A, and seed its app-db to `{:owner :A}`.
2. Wrap `tool-pair/check-replace-frame-state-preconditions!` so it runs the real check, asserts `:outcome :ok`, then destroys A, makes same-id B, dispatches `[:set-owner :B]` into B, and returns A's successful check result.
3. Call public `(rf/replace-frame-state! frame-id {:rf.db/app {:owner :STALE-A}})`.
4. On current main the result is `true`; B's app-db is `{:owner :STALE-A}` and B's history contains both its own `{:owner :B}` epoch and the stale synthetic `{:owner :STALE-A}` epoch.
5. Sibling tail probe: wrap the physical two-arity core write so it writes A, then destroys A and seats/seeds B before returning. The call again returns `true`; B's live db remains `{:owner :B}`, but B's ring gains `{:event-id :rf.epoch/db-replaced, :db-before {:owner :A}, :db-after {:owner :INJECTED-A}}`.

## Evidence

- `epoch/tool_pair.cljc:376-389` derives an exact token from the same captured frame record for restore, and `:499` returns it. `check-replace-frame-state-preconditions!` at `:1024-1066` returns only `{:outcome :ok}`.
- `epoch.cljc:547-553` therefore calls `perform-replace-frame-state!` with only the bare id and patch. `perform-replace!` at `:469-493` re-resolves the id, reads by id, and the closure at `:506` uses the non-exact two-arity core write.
- `record-synthetic-replace-epoch!` at `epoch.cljc:431-450` looks up whichever token is current, ignores the result of `claim-frame-owner!`, then writes and publishes by bare id. It does not fence trace/listener tails after owner loss.
- Core already supplies the needed primitive: `frame/replace-frame-state!`'s three-arity at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1969-1980` refuses unless the captured token still names the live incarnation. Restore uses it at `epoch/tool_pair.cljc:895`.
- Existing epoch tests at `epoch_test.clj:4914-5069` cover A becoming absent between validation and write. The restore-only tests at `:5136-5374` cover A becoming same-id B. No injection test interposes B.
- Public probe output on current main: `{:result true, :successor-db {:owner :STALE-A}, :successor-history-db-after [{:owner :B} {:owner :STALE-A}]}`. Tail probe output: B remains `{:owner :B}` but inherits A's `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` record, and the call returns `true`.
- Xray's `replace-app-db!` at `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs:1490-1523` and Pair-MCP's gated `replace-app-db` tool trust this boolean and report success.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A tool targets a route/component frame while it is unmounting. Validation resolves incarnation A; lifecycle teardown then reuses the public frame keyword for fresh incarnation B. The stale tool gesture can overwrite both partitions of B and say success, or splice A's synthetic undo record into B's history so a later restore puts A-shaped state into B. This crosses the lifecycle authority boundary and can corrupt a newly mounted screen while presenting a valid tool response.

Invariant: a mutation validated against incarnation A may write and publish bookkeeping only while A remains the exact owner. A successor B under the same id must remain byte-for-byte and history-for-history untouched. Owner loss before the physical write follows the canonical `false` plus `:rf.error/no-such-handler` path; owner loss after an A write has linearized must never retarget A's synthetic record, trace, anchor, or listener publication into B.

## Recommended minimal fix

Mirror the shipped restore transaction instead of adding a new abstraction:

1. Derive `:incarnation-token` from the same `frame-record` captured by `check-replace-frame-state-preconditions!`, return it on `:ok`, and reject if that exact record loses ownership during sampling.
2. Thread the token through public `replace-frame-state!`, `perform-replace-frame-state!`, and `perform-replace!`; recheck exact liveness inside the serialized region and use core's existing three-arity exact `frame/replace-frame-state!`.
3. Make synthetic recording accept the same token and commit/anchor only under exact frame-owner ownership, with exact-liveness guards around callback-bearing trace/listener tails, following the existing `commit-record!`/restore pattern. Do not claim whichever same-id token happens to be current.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A deterministic public JVM test performs a real successful precheck against A (assert `:outcome :ok` and A/B distinct tokens), interposes destroy-A/make-B/seed-B before the public call continues, and proves the call returns `false`, emits canonical `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, emits no `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`, and leaves B's full frame-state and history exactly at captured baselines.
2. Pin the same A-to-B pre-write invariant in the CLJS epoch lane without timing sleeps.
3. A focused post-write-tail test interposes A-to-B churn after an exact A physical write but before synthetic bookkeeping. Prove no A synthetic record, anchor, trace, or listener delivery appears in B and B remains unchanged. Assert the A write actually ran so the arm cannot pass by skipping it.
4. Non-vacuity/control: the identical patch with no churn returns `true`, changes the intended frame, appends exactly one matching synthetic record, and fans the expected success notification. Disabling the token fence reproduces the current `true` plus B overwrite/history contamination.
5. Exercise the app-only shape used by Xray/Pair-MCP and one both-partition patch; the no-churn control preserves an omitted partition.
6. Existing destroyed-without-successor, drain-serialization, no-op-write, restore exact-incarnation, and production-elision epoch tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- No public incarnation-token argument, compare-and-set/version API, new lock, retry loop, or successor mutation.
- No change to Pair-MCP/Xray write authorization, response envelopes, or frame-id ergonomics.
- No redesign of frame lifecycle, epoch ids, history retention, restore semantics, or synthetic-record shape.
- No compatibility alias or broad concurrency-hardening sweep.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all 1,113 beads, including closed issues, by title/description/notes and with `bd search --status all` for `replace-frame-state`, `replace frame state`, `state injection`, `stale write`, `destroyed frame`, `same-id`, `successor frame`, `incarnation token`, and `cross-incarnation`. The only in-progress bead is `rf2-jui1c`, an unrelated interceptor prose sweep and remains locked. Open `rf2-ov144` adds replay-by-epoch-id; open `rf2-cq0yi` cleans core generation-pool provenance; neither owns this transaction. Closed `rf2-40kv` and `rf2-x874` concern adapter/Hicasso stale-frame routing, not epoch injection. Commits `a6aac856cf` and `33b1355938` fixed the analogous restore race only. No duplicate owns `replace-frame-state!` retargeting or synthetic-history contamination.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 19:38:35 AUSEST (read-only agent at 35402e4322): HOLDS. check-replace-frame-state-preconditions! (tool_pair.cljc :1024-1069) returns bare {:outcome :ok} with no incarnation token, while the restore counterpart (:374-390, :499) derives and returns the exact token from the captured record; epoch.cljc :549-553 calls perform-replace-frame-state! with the bare id; perform-replace! :469-493 re-resolves by id and the write closure :506 uses the two-arity (non-exact) frame/replace-frame-state!; record-synthetic-replace-epoch! :431-450 claims whichever token is CURRENT and ignores the claim result. The needed primitive exists: frame.cljc :1977-1980 three-arity exact-incarnation write, already used by restore at tool_pair :895 - this is a mirror job with shipped prior art. SURFACES: implementation/epoch/** + focused JVM/CLJS epoch tests; spec/Tool-Pair.md wording is only-if-needed and HOT-ZONE - recommend skipping the spec edit (the lifecycle invariant is already stated on the restore side) or flagging before touching it. COLLISIONS: none live or sibling (core frame.cljc is read, not edited). GATES: clojure -M:test from implementation/epoch (JVM, light); npm run test:cljs --prefix implementation [HEAVY - shadow compile] for the CLJS-lane pin. AMBIGUITY: none - mirror the restore transaction exactly; no public token argument. SHAPE: solo, first wave.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8824 (branch worker/epoch-replace-gj2bo, commit ccef1b615c rebased onto origin/main 693522886c). replace-frame-state! is now an exact-incarnation transaction end to end, mirroring the shipped restore path: check-replace-frame-state-preconditions! derives the exact token from the SAME captured frame record, gates the bare-id schema sampling on exact liveness, and returns the token on :ok; the public fn threads it through perform-replace-frame-state!/perform-replace!; the serialized region gates on event-continuation-live? and installs via core's exact 3-arity frame/replace-frame-state!; record-synthetic-replace-epoch! claims/commits only under that exact token (commit-frame-owner-record!) with liveness re-checks around trace/listener tails; live-container-or-fail removed (subsumed). Tests: JVM public pre-write churn (app-only Xray/Pair-MCP shape + both-partition), post-write-tail churn (A write asserted to have run), no-churn controls incl. omitted-partition preservation; CLJS pins the pre-write A-to-B invariant deterministically. Gates: epoch JVM suite clojure -M:test foreground on the rebased tree = exit 0, 543 tests / 7176 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors. Control 1 (write-boundary exactness reverted): focused run exit 1, 14 failures naming the stale write ('must be REJECTED; got true', ':STALE-A never installed'), no-churn control test stayed green. Control 2 (tail token fence alone disabled at one line): exit 1, 5 failures naming the splice into B's ring/anchor/trace/listeners. Restore blob-hash-verified: git hash-object == HEAD object dde73810a5. CLJS lane relies on CI test:cljs (declared in PR Quality gates).

title: surface-review(conformance-security): strip standardized oncommand from SSR HTML
description:
## Scope Close the current SSR static-markup handler-filter gap for the standardized lowercase `oncommand` attribute in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`, with focused coverage in the existing SSR escaping security suite. Keep the existing conservative attribute-name grammar and benign non-handler `on*` behavior. ## Correctness finding `attr-string` strips camelCase/kebab `on*` props structurally and lowercase handler names through a hand-maintained allowlist. The allowlist omits `oncommand`. Because `oncommand` is all lowercase, it misses the structural regex too, passes the attribute-name grammar, and is emitted verbatim into SSR HTML even though current browsers install it as executable inline JavaScript. This violates the documented invariant that server-rendered strings never carry live event-handler attributes. It is not speculative hardening: the current WHATWG HTML Standard names `oncommand` as an event handler content attribute, and the repository's installed Chromium executes it. ## Evidence - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:353-413`: the structural matcher catches only `on` plus uppercase or hyphen; lowercase names depend on `event-handler-allowlist`. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:369-397`: the lowercase allowlist contains nearby standardized handlers but no `oncommand`. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:591-621`: a prop not stripped is grammar-validated and serialized as an HTML attribute. - `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/ssr_escaping_security_cljs_test.cljc:22-174`: generated and named handler corpora do not include `oncommand`; the benign controls explicitly preserve `online`/`once`/`only`/`on`. - Current JVM probe: `(h/attr-string {:oncommand :pwned})` returns `" oncommand=\":pwned\""`. - Current bundled Playwright/Chromium probe: after loading `
`, dispatching `new Event('command')` reports `{"pwned":1,"handler":"function"}`. - WHATWG HTML Standard, GlobalEventHandlers/content-attribute list: `oncommand` is an event handler content attribute: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#global-attributes ## Failure scenario/invariant An SSR app spreads a user-controlled custom-attribute map into hiccup, the exact threat model documented beside `attr-string`. An attacker supplies the grammar-valid key `oncommand` and JavaScript as its value. Server rendering emits the inline handler. When a `command` event reaches that element, the browser executes the attacker's code before or independently of hydration. Invariant: every browser-recognized event-handler prop covered by the shipped SSR contract is absent from static markup in every HTML-equivalent casing, while benign non-handler names such as `online` continue to serialize. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. From `implementation/ssr`, require `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` and evaluate `(h/attr-string {:oncommand :pwned})`; observe that the returned HTML contains `oncommand` instead of the empty string. 2. Load `
` in the repository's bundled Playwright Chromium. 3. Set `globalThis.pwned=0`, dispatch `new Event('command')` on `#x`, and observe `globalThis.pwned` becomes `1` and `typeof x.oncommand` is `"function"`. ## Recommended minimal fix Add the standardized lowercase `oncommand` spelling to the existing event-handler allowlist and to the named/generated security corpus. Keep the current two-layer matcher and grammar; do not broaden it to all lowercase `on*` names, because the suite deliberately preserves benign attributes such as `online`, `once`, and `only`. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A focused CLJ+CLJS security regression passes `:oncommand`, `:ONCOMMAND`, and a mixed-case spelling with a string JavaScript payload through `h/attr-string`; each yields the empty string and contains neither the handler name nor payload. 2. An end-to-end `emit/emit-element` case renders a benign sibling attribute/text while omitting `oncommand` and its payload entirely. 3. Non-vacuity: the regression is demonstrated red on the current implementation by asserting the current exact survivor (`oncommand` is present in `attr-string`/emitted HTML); the same payload under a benign attribute is shown serializable so fixture/value omission cannot satisfy the test. 4. The existing `online`/`once`/`only`/`on` non-handler controls remain green, proving the fix did not replace the curated rule with an over-broad lowercase `on*` drop. 5. The focused SSR escaping security namespace passes on both JVM and the shared CLJS Node/security lanes. ## Non-goals - No CSP, sanitizer, DOMPurify, hydration, or renderer redesign. - No blanket rejection of programmer-authored inline script/style content. - No broad `on[a-z]` matcher that drops benign non-handler attributes. - No changes to client event binding or unrelated attribute/value escaping. ## Related/duplicate search Searched all bead statuses by `oncommand`, SSR event handler, event-handler, attribute allowlist, static markup, XSS, HTML, escaping, `ssr-invalid-attribute-name`, `html-helpers`, and description/notes matches. No bead owns this gap. The only in-progress bead is unrelated prose cleanup. `rf2-mocn3` is a distinct open SSR Form-2 arity bug; `rf2-qxg24` is a distinct test-tier changed-surface classifier task.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 19:38:35 AUSEST (read-only agent at 35402e4322): HOLDS. event-handler-allowlist (html_helpers.cljc :370-399) contains no oncommand (it does carry onbeforetoggle/onpagereveal/onpageswap, so the omission is a curation gap, not policy); the structural regex :353-354 requires uppercase-or-hyphen after on, so all-lowercase oncommand rides through; grammar-valid unstripped names serialize (:591-621 region); grep confirms zero oncommand occurrences under implementation/ssr + implementation/security at tip; WHATWG lists oncommand as an event handler content attribute. One-word allowlist add + security-corpus rows. SURFACES: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc + implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/ssr_escaping_security_cljs_test.cljc; no hot-zone. COLLISIONS: none live or sibling. GATES: clojure -M:test from implementation/security and from implementation/ssr (JVM, light); npm run test:security --prefix implementation [HEAVY - shadow node compile lane]. AMBIGUITY: none - the bead correctly forbids a broad lowercase on* matcher (keeps online/once/only alive). SHAPE: solo - smallest and most security-relevant of the eleven; dispatch first.
