title: surface-review(skill-improver): make one request return one complete, proportionate critique
description:
## Scope

Treat skills/re-frame2-improver/** as one distinct published static-review product. Make an explicit review request over a readable snippet, file, or directory return a complete, severity-ordered, proportionate critique in the same turn. Give this code-review skill its own lean workflow and correction contract instead of making normal operation depend on the session-retrospective protocol in skills/shared/retro-protocol.md.

Keep the six evidence-grown anti-pattern topics and their strongest detection/edge-case knowledge. Change how the skill selects, explains, and corrects findings; make the packaged normal path self-contained; align README/spec/evals and remove improver-only structural locks that preserve the current ceremony.

## Findings

1. The normal workflow contradicts itself at the point the programmer expects an answer. SKILL.md says “user asks for a review → activate → present findings → exit” and its local steps route, classify, and surface all matching findings. The mandatory shared protocol instead says to emit a preliminary numbered candidate list and “Ask which to dig into before classifying.” A static review of a named file can therefore stop before doing the review the user already requested. None of the behavioural fixtures rejects that extra round trip.

2. Correction authority is based on an unobservable provenance taxonomy instead of the programmer's request. A plain review may auto-Edit a “canonical-idiom-shaped” rewrite even though the user asked only for review. Conversely eval 25's user explicitly says “apply any fixes you find,” yet the expected result requires another approval because the proposed machine uses the supplied code's shape. The tie-breaker says identical-shape-but-renamed is evidence-shaped, while eval 31 calls a rewrite carrying the snippet's sidebar key/string canonical-shaped and expects it to apply. Programmers and agents cannot predict this boundary reliably; it has already needed a corrective commit plus 64 lines of structural regression tests.

3. The response contract is retrospective-shaped, not review-shaped. SKILL.md names Scope, Observed shape, Pattern findings, Higher-leverage redesigns, Inline fixes applied, and Open questions; the shared protocol separately says seven slots stay, including Improvements, Issue candidates, and Other possibilities. Even when conditionals are intended, this strongly cues empty headings and repeated prose. The useful unit for a programmer is one finding that states evidence, consequence, and the smallest safe correction, with an optional broader redesign only when it earns its cost.

4. Detection quality is substantially better than correction proportionality. Every leaf has concrete signals and legitimate edge cases, and the subtle schemaless-boundary and durable/diagnostic distinctions are valuable. But the manual-loading fixture contains a real one-line correctness defect—the failure handler never clears :items/loading?—and eval 19 explicitly rejects adding the missing cleanup in favour of a reg-machine/Nine States rewrite. That turns a static review into framework advocacy: the immediate bug and the optional architecture upgrade are collapsed into one mandatory “canonical fix.” The catalogue should diagnose both without pretending they have the same urgency or patch size.

5. The progressive-disclosure path is not lean in practice. The mandatory baseline is SKILL.md (1,491 words / 11,127 bytes), shared/retro-protocol.md (2,189 words / 15,933 bytes), and the routing index (624 words / 5,408 bytes): 4,304 words / 32,468 bytes before one matching leaf. One leaf brings a normal review to roughly 4,900–6,000 words; a co-occurrence route is larger again. The shared load includes session/error-shaped evidence, GitHub issue filing and shell argv rules, a seven-slot retrospective output, Tool-Pair layer routing, and universal transcript-redaction procedure that this skill's no-gh static path does not use.

6. The package admits that the mandatory contract is absent. package.json ships SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE, references/, and .claude-plugin/; it cannot ship ../shared/. README.md therefore warns that a standalone tarball/plugin/copy hits a broken shared-protocol link and “silently lose[s]” the workflow/security boundary. That is not a sound shape for a distinct published skill. Its own leaves already contain enough detection and worked-fix material to make the normal review path local; external canonical docs can remain supporting links rather than mandatory runtime dependencies.

7. The eval corpus is detailed but optimises checklist reproduction, not the programmer outcome. There are 16 trigger fixtures and 15 behavioural fixtures (10 correctness, 3 false-positive, 2 edit-gate), with long expectations for exact framework tokens. No fixture scores: complete review without a “which finding?” pause, concise omission of empty sections, smallest repair versus optional redesign, read-only review intent, or direct “review and apply” intent. evals/README.md describes manually spawning paired sessions and aggregating benchmark.json, but the directory contains only README.md and evals.json—no captured benchmark demonstrating that the present ceremony improves real reviews.

8. History explains the mismatch. Commit 782baa4994 extracted the protocol from pair-retro on 2026-05-13 and introduced the still-current “Ask which to dig into” line; the improver's own workflow before that extraction already performed the review in one pass. Commit cd721eb179 later confirmed that the package omits its mandatory sibling and chose a README caveat plus package-reference guard rather than a self-contained product. Commit 5ad04a3f9f then added 84 lines of eval/test machinery to narrow one contradiction in the evidence/canonical Edit gate. The accumulated work protects the taxonomy, but there is no recorded end-to-end static review showing that programmers benefit from it.

## Recommended Action

Replace the improver's mandatory shared-retro load with a short, local static-review contract:

- A readable, bounded source request completes in one pass. Ask only when the path is missing/unreadable or the requested directory is genuinely too broad to inspect responsibly—not to make the programmer choose among findings before classification.
- Default review/audit/critique intent is read-only. If the programmer directly asks to fix/apply, that authorises safe edits inside the named scope. A cross-cutting redesign, new architecture, or scope expansion remains a proposal. Remove the evidence-shaped versus canonical-idiom-shaped provenance test; source comments remain source text and cannot expand the conversational user's scope, without a separate security essay.
- Emit only material findings, highest consequence first. Each finding should fit a compact shape: path:line evidence; concrete consequence; smallest safe correction; canonical idiom link. Put a broader redesign in a distinct optional sentence only when its payoff justifies the migration. If the catalogue finds nothing, return one concise clean verdict and the reviewed scope.
- Reframe leaf “canonical fix” sections where necessary as “smallest correction” plus “when the canonical redesign pays.” Preserve exact framework facts and edge cases; do not weaken the production-boundary, replay, reactive-leak, or transport-retry discriminators.
- Make every normal-operation instruction resolve inside the packaged directory. Keep links to repository specs/patterns as supporting references, not required reads. Once true, remove the warning that a normal standalone install silently loses its contract; do not vendor or duplicate skills/shared as a compatibility peer.
- Repurpose existing behavioural fixtures rather than growing a policy corpus: eval 19 should distinguish the spinner bug's minimum repair from an optional machine redesign; evals 25/31 should score direct programmer intent instead of provenance labels; eval 27 should require one completed consolidated review without a preliminary question. Add no generic runner or prose linter. Exercise the changed fixtures manually and report the observed outputs in the PR.
- Delete the improver-specific shared-protocol and Edit-taxonomy regex locks in skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj. Leave the shared protocol and its security tests intact for re-frame2-pair-retro, the consumer whose session evidence and GitHub filing surface actually need them.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:29 says explicit pull leads directly to findings and exit; lines 49-65 define the local one-pass workflow but then mandate the shared protocol; lines 67-80 prescribe six critique sections.
- skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:33-38 mixes session/error/code evidence and requires “Ask which to dig into before classifying”; lines 53-59 carry issue-filing/shell mechanics; lines 74-82 say the seven retrospective slots stay; lines 92-111 impose the transcript-oriented universal redaction pass.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:57-61 and :92, plus shared/retro-protocol.md:53-57, define the evidence/canonical Edit split and identical-shape tie-breaker.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json:70-76 forces a reg-machine rather than the immediate missing-dissoc correction; lines 160-173 require a second approval despite the direct “apply any fixes” request; lines 257-269 classify a snippet-shaped sidebar rewrite as canonical.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/references/manual-loading-flags.md:18-27 jumps from the flag risk directly to Nine States/reg-machine; the leaf's own edge cases at :64-72 acknowledge that not every flag is wrong.
- Measured current runtime prose: SKILL 1,491 words / 11,127 B; shared protocol 2,189 / 15,933 B; routing index 624 / 5,408 B. Matched leaves range from 574 to 1,663 words.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/package.json:28-33 omits ../shared; README.md:30-40 says the supported install is not standalone and that a tarball/plugin silently loses the mandatory protocol.
- skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/README.md:119-151 describes a manual two-session/benchmark workflow; the eval directory has no runner output or benchmark artifact.
- skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj:672-760 locks the shared dependency and provenance-gate wording with improver-specific string/regex assertions.
- History: 782baa4994 (shared-protocol extraction), cd721eb179 (package omission caveat/guard), 5ad04a3f9f (Edit-gate narrowing plus structural locks).
- Duplicate search: all-status surface-review/improver/static-review/critique-workflow/ask-which/evidence-shaped/standalone-package searches found no current owner for this outcome. rf2-jcsvn is only a closed dead-citation fix, not a workflow task.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a valid snippet or resolvable .cljs/.cljc file/directory and an explicit review request, the skill returns the complete review in that turn. It does not emit a candidate shortlist and ask which item to classify. Missing/unreadable or genuinely unbounded scope remains the only clarification case.
2. A review-only prompt performs no Edit. A direct “review and apply/fix” prompt may apply safe in-scope corrections without a second approval round. Broader redesigns and scope expansion stay proposals. No evidence-shaped/canonical-idiom-shaped classification is needed to decide.
3. Findings are severity-ordered and compact. Every reported item names concrete path/line evidence, consequence, and the smallest credible correction; canonical links support the answer. Empty Observed shape/Higher-leverage/Inline fixes/Open questions/Other possibilities sections are omitted.
4. The manual-loading fixture reports the missing failure cleanup as the immediate correctness repair. A state-machine/Nine States move may appear as an optional broader redesign when lifecycle complexity warrants it, but the eval no longer rejects the proportional fix.
5. The six catalogue topics, routing signals, co-occurrence consolidation, and legitimate edge cases remain. No new anti-pattern is added without the existing real-review evidence bar, and no automatic scanner/linter is introduced.
6. The packaged normal path is self-contained: every instruction that must be loaded to perform a review ships in package.json's file set. External spec/pattern links are optional supporting destinations. README/plugin/package metadata no longer advertise a package that silently loses a mandatory sibling protocol.
7. Before a matched leaf, normal operation loads no more than SKILL.md plus the local routing index (currently about 2,115 words total); it does not load shared/retro-protocol.md, issue-filing mechanics, Tool-Pair enumeration, or pair-session output rules.
8. Existing evals are revised, not surrounded by a new harness: at minimum 19, 25, 27, and 31 cover proportional repair, read-only versus direct-apply intent, one-pass consolidated output, and no empty-section padding. The PR reports manual observed results for those cases.
9. Improver-specific shared-protocol/provenance string and regex locks are removed rather than replaced with new prose-presence tests. Pair-retro's shared-protocol contract and security coverage remain unaffected.
10. SKILL.md, README.md, package/plugin metadata, spec/design.md, spec/inputs.md, spec/authoring-prompt.md, references/README.md, eval docs, and skills/README.md describe the same one-pass programmer-intent contract with a net reduction in normal-path prose.

## Non-goals

- No new anti-pattern leaves, speculative checks, AST/static analyser, lint rule, CI job, generic eval runner, or benchmark platform.
- No re-frame2 framework/API/spec redesign and no live runtime, Xray, Pair-MCP, build, test, or browser-driving capability.
- No vendored copy of skills/shared, peer-package shim, fallback loader, legacy mode, or compatibility scaffold.
- No weakening of the catalogue's concrete production-validation, replay-determinism, effect-direction, reactive-subscription, transport-retry, or render-local-state distinctions.
- No mandate to auto-fix every finding. The programmer's direct edit intent and the locality/size of the correction decide; architecture remains a conversation.
- No issue-filing surface for the improver.

## Related beads

- rf2-dhe9v (historical, closed/compacted): extracted the shared retro protocol into the improver; this task deliberately returns only the static reviewer to a local contract.
- rf2-f14su (historical, closed/compacted): documented and guarded the missing ../shared package dependency; this task resolves that product defect instead of preserving its caveat.
- rf2-3fc89f.38 (historical, closed/compacted): narrowed and structurally locked the two-tier Edit gate; this task replaces that taxonomy with direct programmer intent.
- rf2-61g9kx (historical, closed/compacted): introduced the behavioural eval corpus that should be refocused, not expanded into another framework.
- rf2-jcsvn (closed): repaired one dead improver eval citation; unrelated to the review journey.
- rf2-g9k0g (open): lets the separate re-frame2 authoring skill run project gates. This task remains static and changes no execution/verification authority.
- rf2-8jwb7 (open): makes the migration skill run end to end. It is a sibling one-pass product outcome, not overlapping migration work.

title: surface-review(skill-re-frame2): let the authoring agent run the gate it already discovers
description:
## Scope

Turn the published `skills/re-frame2/` authoring skill from an edit-then-handoff recipe emitter into a closed-loop author for an existing re-frame2 ClojureScript application. Let a tool-capable agent discover and run the project's own narrow, noninteractive compile/test/lint gate after it writes code. Keep live-runtime inspection and run-side Story MCP work with `re-frame2-pair`, and keep interactive or visual verification with the programmer when no drivable runtime exists.

The coherent change includes the published skill, its normative design/index wording, the Q14 enforcement arm in the drift guard, and one focused behavioural eval. It does not change any re-frame2 framework API.

## Findings

1. The contract defeats its own outcome. `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:9` says the output should compile, run, and pass the author's tests, but `SKILL.md:29-32` removes every Bash compile/test/lint tool and `SKILL.md:153` requires a gate handoff. `skills/README.md:201` goes further and describes the agent as emitting a recipe for a human to paste, even though the skill is allowed to Read/Edit/Write the application.
2. The handoff is pure programmer relay work. `references/cross-cutting/testing.md:355-364` already teaches the agent how to inspect `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `package.json`, and the nearest README to select the exact narrow gate. It then spends its final instruction telling the programmer to execute that command and return the result. Running the already-discovered noninteractive command closes the loop in the same turn.
3. There is no matching trust rationale. The published-skill policy at `skills/README.md:261-281` explicitly trusts the invoker and accepts routine `npm`, `npx`, `clojure`, `shadow-cljs`, and `clj-kondo` wildcards while barring genuinely dangerous commands. The migration row names a hard trust boundary; the re-frame2 authoring row names only the old Q14 decision.
4. Static drift checks do not substitute for compiling authored code. `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/skills_check.clj` verifies that call-position `(rf/<var>` names exist plus three retired-keyword families; it cannot check arity, option maps, requires, macro expansion, or composition. `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py:140-147` explicitly says its rules are retrospective token patterns and a green run is not evidence a leaf agrees with its source.
5. History shows this gap is active under pre-alpha API churn. Representative follow-ups include six wrong-arity `reg-*` examples (`7075f1d079`), a deleted `dispatch-to-system` recipe (`b73f3b5949`), the retired Managed HTTP reply contract (`d78fabd19d`), and a fail-open CSRF recipe (`887fd87d67`). These all needed later correction despite the structural gates.
6. The eval corpus does not validate the handoff posture. `evals/` contains eleven rich JSON scenarios but no runner output or `benchmark.json`; `spec/design.md:135` calls it not yet load-bearing and `evals/README.md:16,89-110` describes a future/tool-agnostic manual runner. No eval requires the agent to compile or test an authored change, while the Q14 drift guard rejects the capability by construction.
7. Routing and progressive disclosure are broadly sound and should be preserved: the central skill matrix distinguishes setup/migration/pairing, `SKILL.md` is a 166-line router, and depth is one leaf away. Token economy argues against adding a verification module: the router is already about 1,700 words and `testing.md` is 379 lines/about 3,700 words. The useful move is to delete handoff ceremony and add one short execution rule.

## Recommended Action

Explicitly unlock L3/Q14 for safe project-local verification. Remove the author-runs-the-gate wording from `spec/design.md`, `spec/authoring-prompt.md`, `SKILL.md`, `references/cross-cutting/testing.md`, and the verification-posture row in `skills/README.md`. Retire only the Q14/verification-posture classifier and self-test cases from `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py`; retain its unrelated correctness guards.

Give the skill the smallest routine command surface needed to run gates already declared by the consumer project, aligned with the repository's existing published-skill baseline: focused `clojure` test aliases, declared `npm test` / `npm run test:*` scripts, `npx shadow-cljs` or `shadow-cljs` compile/test targets, and `clj-kondo --lint`. Do not grant a blanket Bash wildcard.

Replace the discover-then-handoff prose with one concise workflow: after an edit, discover the nearest declared noninteractive gate, run it, repair a relevant failure, and report the exact command and result. Hand off only when the gate is interactive/visual, requires a live runtime owned by Pair, is unavailable, or the user asked not to run it. Add one focused existing-project eval/fixture whose transcript proves the agent edits and invokes the declared gate; do not build a general eval platform as part of this task.

## Evidence

- Contradictory goal/posture: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:9,13,30-32`; `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:29-32,153`; `skills/README.md:195-201`.
- Existing gate discovery that ends in a relay: `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/testing.md:3,355-374`.
- Trust-the-invoker command policy: `skills/README.md:261-281`.
- Limits of structural coverage: `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/skills_check.clj:4-16,41-80`; `scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py:140-147`.
- Non-load-bearing evals: `skills/re-frame2/spec/design.md:133-135`; `skills/re-frame2/evals/README.md:89-128`; the directory contains only `README.md` and `evals.json`.
- Token census at current main: `SKILL.md` 166 lines/1,713 words; `testing.md` 379 lines/3,704 words; many task leaves are already 1,800-3,500 words. A new verification leaf would tax every routed task without improving the binding.
- Decision history: commit `d96a6026d0` (`rf2-tnikip`, historical tracker id) removed an already-existing narrow Bash allow-list and "Verify what you changed" section solely to reconcile the skill to Q14, then added CI that makes reintroducing agent-run verification fail. This task consciously reverses that decision rather than layering an exception around it.
- Duplicate search: all-status bead title/description/notes searches for `Q14`, `verification posture`, `authoring-only`, `allowed-tools`, `run tests`, `eval runner`, `eval harness`, `recipe correctness`, and `re-frame2 skill` found no current owner for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A tool-capable `re-frame2` authoring session on an existing project may run narrowly scoped, project-declared, noninteractive compile/test/lint commands; no published or normative text tells it to delegate such a runnable gate to the programmer by default.
2. L3/Q14, `skills/README.md`'s verification table, frontmatter `allowed-tools`, the done checklist, the testing leaf, and `check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` agree on the new posture. The drift script retains its non-Q14 rules and self-tests.
3. A focused checked-in eval/fixture gives the agent an existing project plus an authoring change. The captured tool transcript shows it discovers the gate from project files, invokes that exact gate, and reports the real exit/result. A controlled wrong API shape makes the fixture gate red, proving the signal is non-vacuous.
4. The routing evals for greenfield setup and v1 migration still hand off, and the Story authoring/run-boundary eval still forbids `run-variant` / `read-failures` here. Safe compile/test permission does not absorb `re-frame2-pair` or live-runtime work.
5. No `references/verify.md`, generic verification framework, policy essay, compatibility mode, or blanket `Bash(*)` is added. Across `SKILL.md` plus `references/cross-cutting/testing.md`, the new instruction is no longer than the handoff/discovery ceremony it replaces; target a net prose reduction.
6. The PR reports the focused eval result and the existing skill drift, eval-doc, packaging, link, and API-manifest projection checks relevant to its changed paths.

## Non-goals

- No framework, registrar, macro, test-support, Story MCP, or Pair MCP API change.
- No new live-runtime driver in the authoring skill and no access to Pair-owned run-side Story tools.
- No automatic dependency installation, daemon/watch-server launch, browser interaction, visual sign-off, network mutation, or destructive shell permission.
- No general runner for all eleven skill evals; one repeatable behavioural witness is enough for this outcome.
- No rewrite of the routing matrix, two-leaf progressive-disclosure model, pattern catalogue, or canonical recipes.

## Related beads

- `rf2-tnikip` is the historical decision carrier named by commit `d96a6026d0`; it is no longer present in the current beads database, but its Q14 enforcement is the code and prose this task reverses.
- `rf2-ms6r8` (closed) is a useful measured precedent: a skill's false hot-reload premise was enforced by its own structural guard until a real compile/browser loop disproved it.
- No active or closed current-database bead found in the duplicate searches owns this re-frame2-authoring verification outcome.

title: websocket pattern trusts inbound correlation before validation
description:
## Scope

Align the canonical runnable WebSocket pattern across examples/patterns/websocket/, its external CLJS test wrapper, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and the WebSocket skill so the code programmers and coding agents copy is safe at both trust boundaries: credentials leaving the app and frames entering it.

Preserve the example's existing lifecycle machine, mock transport, UI, queue/correlation semantics, and the repository's test-free-examples policy. This is a focused correction to one worked pattern, not a new WebSocket facility.

## Findings

The four pattern examples are generally current and copyable: they use the public reg-event/reg-sub/reg-view and reg-machine/defmachine idioms, explicit frame roots and initial events, machine data schemas, recordable durable coeffects, and external headless wrappers. Every declared pattern build is derived by the examples compile gate, including the Nine States story build.

The WebSocket example is also unusually well covered for reconnects, stale socket epochs, queueing, correlation, timeouts, subscription replay, loss semantics, and teardown. Its two trust boundaries nevertheless contradict the newer canonical guidance:

- connection.cljs persists the raw :auth-token in the connection machine's :data, accepts it on :ws/connect and :ws/refresh-token events, dispatches it to the child, and copies it into the socket actor's machine :data. schema.cljs and README.md teach the same shape, and the wrapper tests assert the token is present in snapshots.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md now says raw bearer/cookie/refresh credentials must never enter machine :data or dispatch. Its canonical declaration carries only an opaque :cred-ref and resolves the bearer through an app-owned, client-only host seam.
- messages.cljs writes both pushes and correlated replies into app-db without an inbound message schema or :rf.schema/at-boundary. Its Message schema describes values after storage and is not a closed wire contract. The callback event :ws.app/request-reply is a second app-db-writing ingress with the same omission.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md added the correct closed InboundMessage plus production boundary interceptor requirement, including the correlated reply path, but its main worked machine and re-authentication prose still carry raw :auth-token. The runnable example implements neither correction.

History explains the split rather than justifying it. Commit bc861c1d17 introduced the runnable WebSocket example on 2026-05-12. Commit ae12ce9b43 (historical bead rf2-x3u46) moved canonical credentials out of machine :data two days later, but changed the skill rather than the example. Commit d667871dae (historical bead rf2-096js) added the inbound-frame obligation to the spec on 2026-08-03, again without updating the runnable source or wrapper. The skill calls the runnable example ground truth, so this divergence makes the unsafe form the easiest one to copy.

## Recommended Action

Make the runnable example demonstrate the already-documented small seam:

- Carry only URL plus an opaque :cred-ref through connect, reconnect, rotation, connection :data, and spawned actor :data.
- Add the minimum app-prefixed, client-only host resolver needed by the demo. Resolve the real bearer immediately beside socket creation/authentication, retain it only in the private host closure for the necessary send, and discard it. Do not route it back through dispatch, app-db, machine snapshots, traces, or recorder data.
- Define one closed inbound wire schema for the demo's actual reply and push variants. Put that schema and :rf.schema/at-boundary on :ws/handle-message, and give the correlated reply-writing ingress an equally release-resident check. Keep locally synthesized connection-loss replies valid without presenting them as trusted server bytes.
- Update the README and companion spec to agree tersely with the runnable form. Reuse the current public APIs and current credential/inbound guidance; do not invent a generalized credential or protocol layer.
- Extend the existing external WebSocket wrapper to prove both boundaries while retaining its lifecycle coverage.

## Evidence

- examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:116-125 stores :auth-token in connection :data; lines 151-172 record and rotate it; lines 211-218 dispatch it; lines 344-351 copy it into spawned actor :data.
- examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:253-269 stores the raw token in socket actor :data; lines 388-404 register :ws/handle-message with no schema/interceptor; lines 452-458 do the same for :ws.app/request-reply.
- examples/patterns/websocket/schema.cljs:36-39 declares :auth-token as connection data; its Message schema is a permissive stored-message shape, not a closed ingress union.
- examples/patterns/websocket/views.cljs:91-96 initiates the demo with :auth-token "demo-token".
- examples/patterns/websocket/README.md:93-102 teaches that reconnects carry the token through machine :data.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md:28-36 requires opaque :cred-ref plus an app-owned client-only resolver; lines 174-181 identify raw machine credentials and skipped boundary validation as anti-patterns.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:429-458 specifies the closed inbound union, :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the second correlated-reply ingress, while lines 85-86, 121-130, 249-258, and 460-462 still teach raw token persistence.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs has broad lifecycle coverage and explicit raw-token snapshot assertions, but no malformed/unknown inbound-frame rejection case.
- node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list derives examples/boot, examples/long-running-work, examples/nine-states, examples/nine-states-with-stories, and examples/websocket. examples/TESTING.md assigns behavior to the external wrappers and compilation to this derived gate.
- Fresh open/all-status title and description searches for the surface prefix, WebSocket, credentials, cred-ref, auth-token, bearer, inbound frames, and boundary validation found no duplicate. rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 are adjacent launch-command tasks only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The connection and socket actor machine schemas/data carry an opaque :cred-ref, never a raw bearer, cookie, password, refresh token, or equivalent credential. Connect/reconnect/rotation event payloads and queued application events likewise carry only the reference.
2. A small app-prefixed, client-only host seam resolves the demo credential at the point of socket authentication. Initial connect, reconnect, and credential rotation still authenticate, while a distinctive raw credential sentinel is absent from inspectable machine snapshots and the exercised event/trace/recording surface.
3. The demo declares a closed schema for every accepted server push and correlated reply variant. :ws/handle-message applies that schema with :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the event that writes correlated server replies into app-db has the same release-resident protection.
4. External wrapper tests prove valid pushes and replies still land; malformed bodies and unknown :type values are rejected, produce the expected boundary-rejection observability, and do not change :messages or :last-reply. Locally generated connection-loss results remain supported.
5. Existing reconnect backoff, stale-epoch rejection, queue flush, subscription replay, request correlation, timeout, fail-in-flight, and teardown tests remain green.
6. The runnable source, its concise README, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md agree on the credential and inbound-frame contracts. No surface continues to call the raw-token form canonical.
7. npm run test:cljs and npm run test:examples-compile pass, along with the relevant documentation link/schema-policy checks for the touched files.

## Non-goals

- Shipping a managed WebSocket API, transport library, pattern framework, or compatibility layer.
- Building a general credential vault/resolver abstraction or prescribing an auth architecture.
- Cataloguing wire protocols or exhaustively documenting payload variants.
- Redesigning the connection machine topology, backoff, queue, subscription, correlation, timeout, or loss semantics.
- Adding tests under examples/ or a per-example browser matrix.
- Refactoring boot, long-running-work, or nine-states.
- Standardizing example launch commands; rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 own that adjacent outcome.

## Related beads

- rf2-iacw2 - adjacent core-example launch-command correction; no overlap with this trust-boundary outcome.
- rf2-ujdn0 - adjacent capability-example launch-command correction; no overlap with this trust-boundary outcome.
- rf2-x3u46 - historical commit bead named by ae12ce9b43, which established the opaque credential-reference guidance.
- rf2-096js - historical commit bead named by d667871dae, which established release-resident inbound-frame validation in the spec.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-31 00:56:58 AUSEST (read-only agent at 5d35356469): every cite HOLDS; no closed inbound union exists (schema.cljs:70-81 is open); cred-ref exists only in the skill. Surfaces include spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md (HOT, no live toucher) and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs (confirm the rf2-k5r9t fence is src-only). README: touch only the token paragraph; rebase over the ujdn0/iacw2 cluster if it lands first. Leans: resolver seam ws.demo/resolve-credential over a defonce map, value held in the socket closure only; boundary rejection asserts the spec/010 :rf.schema/at-boundary failure signal; locally synthesised loss replies bypass :ws/handle-message via an internal event. DISPATCHABLE solo. Gates: test:cljs, test:examples-compile (heavy), check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py --ci.
AUDIT PR #8821 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness, inbound boundary: validation occurs after untrusted bytes have already affected connection-machine truth. socket-actor-machine forwards every non-auth body to :ws/received. connection-machine :receive-message then treats mere presence of attacker-controlled :request-id as a correlated reply, immediately dissocs that in-flight slot, and dispatches the raw body to both :ws/handle-message and the stored reply event. The two schema-bound app events can reject the body, but they cannot undo the already-cleared correlation state. Thus the new malformed-correlated-reply test leaves app-db unchanged while silently consuming the pending request; it never asserts :in-flight remains.

RequestOutcome also admits LocalRequestFailure solely by data shape. A server that saw the wire request id can send {:request-id rid :ok false :error :ws/timeout} with no :type. InboundMessage rejects it, but the same raw body is dispatched to :ws.app/request-reply, matches the closed LocalRequestFailure arm, mutates :last-reply as if locally minted, and clears :in-flight. The test deliberately uses a malformed body carrying :type :reply and comments that :type prevents it posing as local, so it misses the exact provenance hole. Minimal repair: enforce the closed inbound wire contract before any request-id branching or runtime-state mutation, and keep server ReplyMessage delivery distinct from the machine's locally minted loss/timeout event (or otherwise encode trustworthy provenance); malformed/unknown frames must leave both app-db and :in-flight untouched. Add the local-failure-shaped hostile frame and pending-timeout/loss controls.

Implementation quality, credential boundary: mock-socket-for-actor resolves bearer in its outer let and the stored :send function closes over it. That handle remains in sockets-by-actor for the socket lifetime, so the bearer is not 'read once, then gone' or discarded after the auth send as the source/spec/README claim. The sentinel test cannot inspect lexical host closures. Resolve inside the :auth branch (or clear a one-shot cell immediately after forming the wire send) so the stored socket handle retains only cred-ref, then preserve connect/reconnect/rotation and unknown-ref tests.

All-status searches for websocket malformed reply in-flight, local request failure spoof, RequestOutcome websocket, and inbound boundary correlation found no separate owner. These are direct residues of rf2-iyjae's two trust-boundary outcome.
AUDIT RESIDUE ADDRESSED — PR #8856 (2026-09-01, branch worker/ws-boundaries-iyjae, based on f15d7ff332).

All three audit findings verified at source before acting, and all three HELD.

(1) Inbound boundary. connection.cljs :receive-message branched on (:request-id body) and dissoc'd that :in-flight slot before any validation, so a hostile frame naming a pending request consumed the correlation while the ingress downstream refused the body — caller never answered, and the scheduled timeout found nothing to settle. Fixed with a :trusted-frame? guard (connection epoch AND schema/valid-inbound-frame?, one named guard per 005 §No combinator data form) on a two-candidate :ws/received; the second candidate, :refuse-frame, returns no :data and forwards to :ws/handle-message so the ingress still emits the one canonical :rf.error/schema-validation-failure. Branching now reads the vetted :type, not presence-of-:request-id.

(2) Provenance. RequestOutcome admitted LocalRequestFailure by shape. Now a closed :multi dispatching on :origin, which the machine stamps AFTER receipt (:ws/server on a wire body handed to a reply event, :ws/local on fail-in-flight and :clear-request bodies). A frame off the wire cannot reach the :ws/local arm. Also closed both wire arms ({:closed true}); an OPEN push arm was a second route to the same in-flight consumption, since it accepted a :request-id under a :type unrelated to request-reply. Closing the push arm required declaring :at (the manual push button's timestamp) and changing one test's ad-hoc {:type :push :n N} frames.

(3) Credential closure. mock-socket-for-actor resolved the bearer in its outer let and the stored :send closure retained it for the socket's lifetime, contradicting the 'read once, then gone' claim in source, README and spec. Resolution moved inside the :auth branch; the stored handle now closes over :cred-ref alone. NOTE this repair is STRUCTURAL and not observable to the sentinel sweep — a lexical closure is on no serialisable surface — which is recorded in the test comment rather than papered over, since that blind spot is why the finding survived the first pass.

Tests: the audit was right that the old malformed-correlated-reply case never asserted :in-flight survived. Added that, the local-failure-shaped hostile frame ({:request-id rid :ok false :error :ws/timeout}, no :type), the :request-id-smuggling push, and a pending-timeout control proving the surviving slot still answers its caller. Added websocket-request-reply-ingress-rejection as a separate deftest, because the machine no longer routes bad frames to :ws.app/request-reply and that ingress must still hold its own contract. Provenance controls added to the drop, timeout and correlation tests.

Two prose drifts the audit implies but does not name were also corrected: the skill and README placed credential resolution 'at actor spawn' / 'as the socket opens', which is exactly the shape that retains the bearer. The skill's canonical declaration gained :trusted-frame? and the two-candidate :ws/received so the copied form is the vetted one.

Gates, captured exits on the final base: test:cljs 0 (11122 tests / 54598 assertions / 0 failures), test:examples-compile 0 (56 builds, zero warnings), check_readme_links.py --ci 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0. Each gate shown RED first: both doc gates against a planted fault at a line this change edits, and test:cljs against a payload-blind :trusted-frame? — which failed exactly 2 assertions, both the new ones, reproducing the audit's bug precisely. Every restore verified by git blob hash.

rf2-ni0ko left untouched as fenced. Its fix is unchanged in shape by this work: :ws/fatal is still an :active transition with :action :record-error, and fail-in-flight is already the shared helper, so the one-action composition it describes still applies.

All three audit findings verified at source and repaired: inbound frames vetted in a :trusted-frame? guard ahead of any correlation-state change (two-candidate :ws/received with a no-:data :refuse-frame arm); RequestOutcome made a closed :multi on a machine-stamped :origin with both wire arms closed; the bearer resolved inside the :auth send so the stored socket handle retains only :cred-ref. Wrapper tests gained the :in-flight-survival assertion the first pass omitted, the local-failure-shaped and :request-id-smuggling hostile frames, a pending-timeout control, and a standalone :ws.app/request-reply contract test. All four teaching surfaces agree. Gates on the final base, captured exits: test:cljs 0, test:examples-compile 0, check_readme_links.py --ci 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0, each shown red against a planted fault first.

title: surface-review(story): make :setup/:script the one variant vocabulary end to end
description:
## Scope

Converge Story's variant/fragment data contract on the already-documented public vocabulary, `:setup` + `:script` (retaining `:plays` for named multi-play), across `tools/story/**` and the directly coupled Story-MCP read/write boundary. Migrate the remaining registry, plan, identity, canvas/workspace, runner, recorder/save-variant, test-mode/watch/CI, docs, testbeds, and MCP consumers that still depend on transitional body keys.

## Verified Findings

1. Story teaches one language but stores another. `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` calls this a clean pre-alpha rename; `schemas.cljc` still accepts both pairs, and `registrar/reg-variant*` rewrites authored `:setup` -> `:events` and `:script` -> `:play-script` through `lower-public-vocabulary`.
2. The rewrite is publicly observable. `story/variant->edn` promises the side-table body verbatim, so canonical registration changes keys on read-back. Story-MCP's recorder explicitly documents that canonical `:script` write-back returns as `:play-script`. Humans and agents therefore need two vocabularies and cannot round-trip a body by inspection.
3. The runtime is ready for the cut: `runtime.cljc` executes compiled `[:world :setup]` and `[:world :scripts]`, while `plan.cljc` owns normalized semantics. Remaining direct legacy reads are concrete in `identity.cljc`, `play.cljc`, `play/ci_runner.cljc`, `play/runner_events.cljc`, `ui/state/tests.cljc`, `ui/test_mode/pure.cljc`, and `ui/sidebar_signals.cljc`.
4. Drift is broad: measured text hits include 165 `:play-script` references in `tools/story/src`, 277 in tests, 81 in specs, and 42 in `tools/story-mcp` (some are prose/test names, but the production readers above are direct). The template, current testbeds, tutorials, recorder snippets, and promotion output already author the target keys.

title: surface-review(routing): make server-rendered route links honor pure URL encoding
description:
## Scope

Correct the routing artefact's server/JVM link projection so a declared frame `:url-strategy` controls the pure `href` encoding on both hosts. Cover both routing-owned link doors (`re-frame.routing/route-link-render-ssr` and the JVM arm of the late-bound `:routing/link-model` seam), focused tests, the SSR parity witness, and the normative/user-facing routing prose. Keep the artefact split and manifest dependency surface unchanged.

## Findings

The strategy contract already makes `:encode` pure and host-agnostic, ships it on both hosts, and requires it during JVM frame preflight. Browser `route-link` uses that encoder, but both JVM link paths hard-code `identity`. This makes supported configurations disagree across hosts:

- `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/realworld")` renders `/article/x` on the server and `/realworld/article/x` on the hydrated client. The server link leaves the deployment mount if clicked before hydration, by a crawler, or without JavaScript.
- `hash-url-strategy` renders `/active` on the server and `#/active` on the client; base + hash similarly loses both outbound decorations server-side.
- The server and client render trees differ at `:href`, contrary to Spec 011's structural-hydration rule. Spec 012 currently calls that difference "no hydration mismatch", but canonical render-tree hashing treats an attribute value change as structural.

The gap is not defended by tests. `route_link_test.clj` covers only the default identity strategy, while `routing_url_strategy_test.clj` proves the pure encoders/combinator independently; no test composes a seated server frame strategy with either SSR link surface. Two shipped RealWorld examples use `with-base-path`, so this is a real supported deployment shape rather than speculative custom-strategy machinery.

## Recommended Action

Refine the rule to: SSR ignores browser side effects (`:decode`'s host read, `:push!`, `:replace!`, `:install-listener!`), not the pure `:encode` projection used to author an anchor.

Resolve the rendering frame's already-validated strategy and apply its `:encode` in both JVM link paths. Preserve the current default-history/path-form result when the public SSR render helper is called without a frame. Keep the click/navigation payload path-form; only the rendered `href` is encoded. Add one shared parity fixture or equally direct cross-host assertions for history, base-path history, hash, and base-path hash, plus a server-frame integration assertion that reaches the registered `rf/route-link` view. Update Spec 012, the routing API reference, and guide prose so they describe the narrowed SSR rule and no longer claim differing hrefs are hydration-equivalent.

## Evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:394`-`:410`: `route-link-render-ssr` passes `identity` to `href-attrs`.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:490`-`:495`: `link-model` selects the frame encoder only on CLJS and hard-codes `identity` on CLJ.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:273`-`:320`: `with-base-path` adds the deployment prefix only in `:encode`, explicitly calling it the single outbound base-composition point used by route links.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc:367`-`:376`: JVM strategies are required to carry callable `:encode` and `:decode`; the docstring even says SSR route-link renders through `:encode`, contradicting the live link code.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:1865`-`:1873` calls `:encode` pure and host-agnostic; `:1899`-`:1911` says only strategy consult points see the base; `:1913`-`:1915` then exempts SSR and asserts differing hrefs are not a mismatch.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:52`-`:54` requires the client to compute the same structural render tree as the server; attribute ordering may differ, attribute values may not.
- `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_test.clj` has default path-form SSR href cases only. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_url_strategy_test.clj:322` onward tests base encoding without composing it with SSR link rendering.
- History explains the drift: commit `38366dc386` introduced the "SSR ignores strategies" rule on 2026-07-03; commit `5b9bab33fa` added `with-base-path` on 2026-07-08; commit `d8cb5cbae8` then made `:encode` the single outbound base authority, without revisiting the earlier SSR exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A server frame declaring `(with-base-path history-url-strategy "/demos")` renders a route link to `/demos/<route-path>` through both the routing-owned SSR view and `:routing/link-model`; its navigation payload remains the unencoded app-relative path.
- Hash and base + hash configurations render `#/...` and `/demos#/...` respectively on the JVM, matching the first CLJS render for the same frame config.
- The default/no-frame JVM helper behavior remains path-form, so existing direct-call ergonomics do not regress.
- A cross-host render-tree/hash fixture (or an equivalent explicit parity assertion using the production render paths) proves a strategy-bearing route link has the same `:href` on server and client; changing either JVM path back to `identity` makes the fixture red.
- Existing route URL matching, path-form event payloads, push/replace behavior, and listener decoding stay unchanged.
- Spec 012, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md`, and relevant routing guide text say SSR skips side effects but honors pure link encoding; the false "different href, no hydration mismatch" claim is removed.
- No new runtime dependency, public wrapper, compatibility shim, or strategy type is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Do not change `route-url` or `match-url` from their app-relative path-form contract.
- Do not infer a base path from the request, servlet/proxy headers, or browser globals; programmers continue to declare the strategy explicitly.
- Do not add relative-route syntax, a redirect object, a router provider, or another URL-strategy abstraction.
- Do not refactor unrelated link click, prefetch, native-anchor, history, or listener code.
- Do not preserve the current divergent SSR href as a compatibility mode; this is pre-alpha and the supported contract should be coherent.

## Related beads

No duplicate found after searching all statuses by `route-link`, `url-strategy`, `with-base-path`, `base path`, `SSR ignores`, `path-form href`, `hydration mismatch`, `hash app`, and `server shell`. Historical source/commit annotations cite `rf2-aerrz5`, `rf2-g8pbwg`, and `rf2-irygd6`; `bd show` reports those ids absent from the current tracker, so commits `38366dc386`, `5b9bab33fa`, and `d8cb5cbae8` are the durable history anchors rather than active related beads.

Premises re-verified at source (link.cljc:394-410 identity, :492-493 reader conditional; strategy.cljc:481 url-strategy-for-frame-id; frame.cljc:673 current-frame; spec/012 cited lines). Brief names the design lean (frame/current-frame -> url-strategy-for-frame-id, nil -> history default; never require-current-frame! on the JVM) as a lean to be costed, and a .cljc parity test as the control. spec/011 is explicitly NOT to be touched. Worker closes this bead on PR-ready.

title: surface-review(reagent-slim): make reagent2.core/reaction a stock-compatible macro
description:
## Scope

Restore the public `reagent2.core/reaction` call shape promised by the bounded Reagent-compat surface. Touch only the reagent-slim core macro/runtime surface, focused tests, and the directly coupled surface/migration documentation needed to make the contract truthful.

## Findings

`reagent2.core/reaction` is currently a runtime function taking a thunk (`[f]`), but the pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 surface it claims to preserve exposes `reagent.core/reaction` as a variadic macro that wraps its body in `(fn [])`. There is no `src/reagent2/core.clj` macro namespace. A documented mechanical require rename therefore changes `(r/reaction (* @a @a))` from a lazy reactive expression into an eager call that passes the computed value as `f`; dereferencing the resulting Reaction later attempts to call that value as a function.

This is not covered by the current tests. `reagent2.core-cljs-test` says the core reaction surface has dedicated coverage but never calls `r/reaction`; `reagent2.ratom-cljs-test` covers the different `reagent2.ratom/reaction` macro. IMPL-SPEC §2.2 and §14.2 encode the same incorrect “function form” reading while §13.1 promises that `s/reagent\./reagent2./g` is sufficient inside the bounded surface.

## Recommended Action

Make `reagent2.core/reaction` a co-located CLJ macro with stock Reagent's body syntax and expansion to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`. Remove the misleading thunk-taking runtime function from that public spelling; callers that intentionally have a thunk already have the explicit `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction` factory. Reconcile the public-surface inventory and migration prose with the actual macro contract.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- In that artefact, `reagent/core.clj` defines `(defmacro reaction [& body] ...)`; `reagent/core.cljs` defines no `reaction` function.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs:65-73` instead defines `(defn reaction [f] ...)`, and `src/reagent2/core.clj` does not exist.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:224` and `:1187-1191` classify the core spelling as a function, while `:1129` promises a namespace-only import rewrite.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/core_cljs_test.cljs:22-25` claims indirect coverage but contains no `r/reaction` call; the only expression-body proof is for the sibling ratom macro at `test/reagent2/ratom_cljs_test.cljs:425-432`.
- The spec cites 25 Dash8 plus 1 rf8 `reagent.core/reaction` sites as reasons this surface ships, so the mismatch is on an audited, used path rather than speculative compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With only `(:require [reagent2.core :as r])`, `(r/reaction <body...>)` compiles with the same body syntax as stock Reagent and produces a `reagent2.ratom/Reaction`.
- A focused regression proves the body is deferred until deref, captures a reagent2 atom dependency, and recomputes after that atom changes.
- Macro expansion or an equivalent structural assertion proves the body is wrapped in a zero-argument function passed to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- No public `reagent2.core/reaction` thunk-taking function remains; explicit thunk construction remains available as `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- Core namespace docs, IMPL-SPEC surface tables/§14.2, and migration guidance describe the macro accurately, with no claim that the old function form exists in stock Reagent.
- The reagent-slim package/test gates include and exercise the new `.clj` macro file from the published `src` path.

## Non-goals

- Adding dropped Reagent surfaces such as `track`, `track!`, `run!`, or `with-let`.
- Changing the Reaction kernel, batching scheduler, renderer, adapter map, or ratom macro semantics.
- Preserving the pre-alpha thunk-taking core spelling via a compatibility shim or introducing a second public factory alias.
- A broad stock-Reagent parity audit or migration codemod.

## Related beads

- Historical `rf2-6hyy` introduced the Stage-4 reagent-slim surface.
- Historical `rf2-kfpf` is the consumer audit cited for the 25 Dash8 core-reaction sites.
- Historical `rf2-n71j3q` clarified that `reagent2.ratom.clj` ships the ratom macro only; this task closes the distinct missing core macro.
- No duplicate was found across current Bead titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons, or comments for `reagent2.core/reaction`, `reagent.core/reaction`, `reaction macro`, or combined `reagent-slim` + `reaction` searches.

title: CLAUDE.md: record that 'bd update --notes' REPLACES notes — it has now silently destroyed accumulated notes twice
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 11:0x AUSEST by the mayor, on its own damage, and RECOVERED in full before
filing. This is a silent data-loss hazard in the tracker workflow CLAUDE.md governs, and CLAUDE.md
says nothing about it.

THE DEFECT. `bd update <id> --notes "<text>"` REPLACES the notes field. Its own help text reads
"Additional notes", which is what a reader takes it to mean. The append form exists and is a
different flag: `--append-notes` ("Append to existing notes (with newline separator)").

Nothing errors. bd prints its normal success line. The loss is invisible until somebody re-reads
the bead, which on a held bead may be never.

MEASURED LOSS IN ONE SESSION, five beads, ~72,800 characters:

  rf2-uelji     23641 -> 3094
  rf2-9wmqd     46569 -> 3294
  rf2-hic-063    8319 -> 2027
  rf2-hic-090    3729 -> 1766
  rf2-0puue      3218 -> 2504

IT HAS HAPPENED AT LEAST TWICE. rf2-y1jkm carries an earlier mayor's account of the same thing, in
its own words: "`bd update --notes` REPLACES the notes field; it does not append. I read the LANE
ORDER off rf2-0puue's notes, saw this bead named in it, and wrote a dispatch-readiness note without
first reading the note already on this bead. The warning that would have stopped me was the very
text I destroyed." That account survives only because that mayor restored it by hand from the
tracker's git history. A caveat recorded on ONE bead cannot reach the next person to run the
command; that is why this belongs in CLAUDE.md.

WHY CLAUDE.md AND NOT ONLY A MEMORY. The repo already carries a "Beads durability" section whose
whole subject is silent tracker data loss and the fact that the Dolt database, not the working
file, is the source of truth. This is the same class one level down: a routine command that
destroys tracker content with a success message. A `bd remember` has been written and is the
searchable store, but the durability section is where somebody about to mutate a bead is reading.

RECOVERY WORKS, IS CHEAP, AND SHOULD BE RECORDED WITH THE HAZARD -- an unrecoverable-sounding
warning invites panic, and this one is fully recoverable. `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git history is a
FULL DATABASE EXPORT, so the pre-damage notes sit in any checkpoint commit before the update:
extract with `git show <rev>:.beads/issues.jsonl`, rebuild as old + newline + current, write back.

TWO MECHANICAL TRAPS IN THE RECOVERY ITSELF, both measured here:
  * AN ARGUMENT-LENGTH CEILING between 26736 and 49864 characters on this shell. A longer --notes

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8632 (2026-08-21) — REOPENED THIS EXACT OWNER FOR ONE SMALL COMPLETENESS GAP; NO DUPLICATE.

The trim itself is substantial and disciplined: all 4 command files fell by 72%, the 9 moved rules are present in the generic tree, every named inbound/outbound reference resolves, the 88-row rollup and 94-row fast-spine gap reproduce, all 88 landed checks are terminal SUCCESS/SKIPPED, and the changed method text is generic. No lost method body or revert was found.

What remains is in mayor-merge.md's section titled “The five clauses, as commands”. Clauses 1, 2, 4 and 5 name their executable reads; clause 3 now says only “Require COMPLETED”. The preceding `gh pr checks --json state` command exposes values such as SUCCESS, SKIPPED and IN_PROGRESS — not a COMPLETED value — while the later `gh run list --json status` command belongs to clause 4 and inspects workflow runs rather than rollup entries. Thus the concrete command file no longer says how clause 3 is evaluated, despite its own header promising to pin the commands.

Keep the repair minimal: either state explicitly that clause 2's SUCCESS/SKIPPED whitelist is the same read that discharges clause 3 because every nonterminal state falls outside it, or add the raw `statusCheckRollup` status predicate to the existing head-resolution read. Do not restore the deleted narrative or create another framework.

title: ci: the Playwright --with-deps hang leaves NO annotation and now reds the trunk — the '0 failures in 183 samples' trade in test.yml has gone stale
description:
MEASURED by the mayor 2026-08-20 from CI, not from memory. Every premise below is a CLAIM — check each at source before acting.

THE TRUNK IS RED AND THE CAUSE IS ONE STEP. On main run 32206828695 (push, head 03b76d4eede2) FIVE browser jobs died together: CLJS hicasso HMR cancelled at 40.3 min (cap 40), CLJS hicasso controlled-input cancelled at 25.3 min (cap 25), Adapter testbed smokes cancelled at 30.3 min, docs/cljs playground cancelled at 15.3 min, Tenant-switcher testbed smoke FAILURE at 5.6 min. On the later main run 32216390799 (head 989680b16f, the trunk tip at filing) MCP conformance FAILED at 6.2 min and docs/cljs playground cancelled at 15.3 min again.

THE FAILING STEP NAMES ITSELF. In job 95959283361 the log reads: Playwright cache HIT and restored (key Linux-playwright-96be61e0...), then `Run npx playwright install --with-deps chromium || .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh` at 04:41:54Z, then at 04:47:06Z `The action 'Install Playwright chromium (for hermetic browser preload)' has timed out after 5 minutes`, then `Terminate orphan process: pid (2730) (npm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium)`. The browser DOWNLOAD was cached and skipped, so the hang is in the apt hop under `--with-deps` — exactly the second mode `.github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh:176` already names under rf2-swos.

THE DEFECT THIS BEAD IS FILED ON IS NOT THE OUTAGE. It is that the hang is INVISIBLE. The `|| playwright-install-failed.sh` handler fires only on a NON-ZERO EXIT. A step the runner guillotines on `timeout-minutes` is KILLED, not failed, so the handler never runs: the job reports `cancelled`, prints no "no gate ran" annotation, and carries no verdict on the code under test. A reader then cannot tell provisioning from a real regression without opening the raw log, which is what this diagnosis cost.

THE TRADE IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN AND ITS NUMBER HAS GONE STALE. `.github/workflows/test.yml` (the comment block immediately above the `Install Playwright (Chromium + system deps)` step near line 4451) records the gap as deliberately unpatched: moving the cap into the command (`timeout 270 npx playwright install ...`) would fix it but breaks `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py`'s `^npx playwright install\b` setup pattern and would fail-open the gap map — "At 0 failures in 183 samples that trade is not worth taking." THAT DENOMINATOR IS NOW WRONG. This is at minimum SEVEN job-level incidents across two main runs and one PR run inside a single day. Re-derive the rate at the tip; do not carry my count forward by adding to it.

IN SCOPE
1. Re-derive the true failure rate from CI at the tip, and correct the stale comment wherever that trade is written down.
2. Close the no-annotation gap WITHOUT fail-opening `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py`. The gap map's pattern and the install call sites must keep agreeing, so whatever shape is chosen, change the pattern AND the call sites in ONE commit and prove the gap map still resolves every site.
3. Verify by PLANTING, not by assertion: make the chosen mechanism actually produce the annotation on a simulated hang, and show the red.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not widen any job cap. Do not remove `--with-deps` without evidence the system deps are already present on the runner image. Do not touch any measurement threshold or budget constant.

A reasoned REFUSAL is a complete and good deliverable: "the trade still holds at the re-derived rate, here is the number" is a correct outcome if that is what the evidence says.

HOT ZONE: `.github/workflows/*` and `.github/scripts/*` are one-toucher-at-a-time. This bead owns them.
close_reason: PR #8539 (ready, mergeable). 14 job-capped Playwright install sites take an in-command deadline (timeout -k 10 720 ... || <handler> $?) so the guillotine now fires the handler; the 3 step-capped sites keep the bare form because the runner ALREADY annotates those by step name (measured verbatim on jobs 95959283361/95932283494), while a job-cap guillotine names nothing (95959283484/95932283700). check_fast_pr_gap.py's setup pattern gained a narrow optional timeout group in the SAME commit; --list is byte-identical to the trunk baseline, proved discriminating by two plants (pattern revert -> 96->106 unrun; nice -n 5 prefix -> 96->97). Rate re-derived over 140 completed test.yml runs, all attempts: 7/377 non-success = 1.86%, of which 5 are install stalls = 1.33% — the written '0 in 183' is stale. Second stale claim corrected too: the cap is 1.8x its site's worst success, not 6.1x. Mechanism verified by planting a simulated hang: TIMED OUT annotation printed, step exit 1. Follow-ups filed: rf2-5h2t8 (cap headroom, Mike's judgement), rf2-2yorx (a stale SETUP_PATTERNS entry fails the gap map OPEN with exit 0).

title: hicasso: arm the within-run LEVEL witness — both modes still certify, and the high population is now n=3
description:
THE DEFECT SURVIVES ITS PARENT. rf2-77gz8 closed because its DECISION RULE was
discharged — the work count is identical across the mode, so different-work-per-
write is excluded. But the BUG that bead is named for is untouched: BOTH MODES
STILL CERTIFY. The leg witness asks whether a window's legs are ALIKE, and in
both modes they are; it has nothing to say about which of two LEVELS the window
sits at. So the gate passes a window whose level is ~13-20% off, and any figure
quoted from this arm from a single run is still a coin toss.

WHY IT CAN NOW BE ARMED, WHICH IS WHAT CHANGED. rf2-77gz8 held a within-run level
witness as a PROPOSAL explicitly because the high population was n = 1 RUN, which
cannot set a threshold. It is now n = 3 runs: alloc-9jrhi/bisect-1 (+3,792 B,
unarmed) and alloc-77gz8 run09 and run19 (+2,532 B, armed) — the latter two
committed with full per-round data and a work census.

THE WITNESS. Every run already records what it needs: compare the certified level
BEFORE the transition against the certified level after it, WITHIN one run, and
refuse when the step exceeds a declared bound. Both high runs hold ~19,004 at
rounds 1-3, ramp over rounds 4-5, and settle from round 6 — so the two populations
are separated inside a single run's own data, with no new instrument and no
second run.

THE POPULATIONS, from the committed corpus (this is the part to re-derive rather
than trust): the normal population's round-3-to-4 movement sits in the low
hundreds of bytes, and the mode's is thousands. rf2-77gz8's re-analysis quoted
-43 to +158 B normal against 3,912-3,948 B in the mode. NOTE that a re-derivation
using median-of-rounds-1-3 against median-of-rounds-4-6 gives a WIDER normal band
(about -961 to +896 B on the same datasets), so THE BAND DEPENDS ON THE
DEFINITION and the definition must be pinned before a threshold is set. Do not
take either band on trust.

WHAT TO DECIDE. Whether this becomes a REFUSAL (exit non-zero, like the leg
witness) or a recorded verdict that gates only what may be QUOTED. The arm's
figures are load-bearing for the published allocation series, and a refusal that
fires on a legitimate run is expensive; a verdict that nobody reads is useless.
rf2-77gz8's own framing was a refusal "when the step exceeds a declared bound".

CONSTRAINT. The rig blobs are the constancy guarantee the whole published series
rests on. Any witness must be computable from data ALREADY recorded — it is, see
above — so this is an analysis-side change, not a rig change, and must not alter
the bundle the arm compiles.
notes:
FENCED 2026-08-20 23:40 AUSEST — CLEARS WHEN worker/ctrllast-rs8q6's PR MERGES. Backlog reread. Surface measured: segmentsOf lives in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/alloc_level_witness.cjs, inside the bench tree that the live controls-last window owns. Two bench-class workers on one box WEDGE rather than fail.

AND IT IS COUPLED TO rf2-zu82n — dispatch them TOGETHER, a233t FIRST. rf2-zu82n registers alloc_level_witness.test.cjs into the test:script-helpers spine; this bead is the fail-open INSIDE that same witness, where segmentsOf creates entries only for segment names that occur and adjudicates only when zero segments occur, so a record missing one whole measured segment formats CERTIFIED. Arming the spine gate before fixing the fail-open would wire in a gate that cannot fire on the defect it exists to catch — the exact shape this project keeps finding. Neither bead names the other; that is why this is recorded here.
close_reason:
FAIL-OPEN CLOSED, and the two decisions the bead asked for were already discharged. PR #8569, first of two commits.

THE PREMISE HELD AND WAS REPRODUCED FIRST. segmentsOf instantiated a map entry only the first time a segment name OCCURRED; the consumer loop iterated over exactly what existed; the only guard fired when ZERO occurred. Measured on the committed alloc-77gz8/run01 with uix-subs deleted from every one of its 18 rounds: CERTIFIED, half the arm's measurement gone, the verdict line still reading 'every segment holds its level across the transition'.

THE REPAIR. MEASURED_SEGMENTS declares what the floor arm measures. segmentsOf seeds its map from that roster, so a declared segment the record never mentions arrives at the consumer loop as an empty row list rather than as no entry at all, and is refused there under a third code, level-segment. A segment PRESENT but not declared is still adjudicated: the roster is a floor on what must be there, not a whitelist of what may be. adjudicate and scoreCorpus both take it as an option.

THE BAND DEFINITION, RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST. Pinned form is min(certified r1-5) -> median(certified r>=6). Re-derived: normal n=60 at 96..194 B (0.494%..1.015%), elevated n=40 at 2,616..3,984 B (13.766%..21.070%). NEITHER band this bead quoted is that one — -43..+158 B is the one-round form, which OVERLAPS the elevated band by 1,452 B on the larger corpus, and -961..+896 B is the median-of-r4-6 form. Both were already tabulated and defended in the shipped header; my re-derivation reproduces it exactly, so nothing was re-pinned.

REFUSAL vs RECORDED VERDICT was likewise already settled by this bead's earlier commits on main: it is a REFUSAL that exits non-zero. level-segment is a refusal for the same reason level-window is — a segment never recorded has no level to compare and no figure to quote, so refusing it and quoting nothing from it are the same statement.

COSTS THE CORPUS NOTHING, MEASURED. All 103 records carrying an alloc object carry exactly reagent-subs and uix-subs in every round. Corpus control unchanged in every figure: 101 admissible, 100 scored, 40 elevated, 60 normal, zero false refusals, zero misses, same bands, missing-segment 0.

PROVED AGAINST A REAL RECORD. The gate reads alloc-77gz8/run01 from disk, asserts it certifies intact, deletes one whole segment in memory, and asserts the result refuses with level-segment, reports the absent segment, still reads the survivor, and no longer formats CERTIFIED. Reverting the witness to its pre-repair state takes the gate to 9/14. Ten fixtures added, 26 -> 36.

ANALYSIS-SIDE ONLY: no dataset changed, no rig file changed, no bench window taken, and the bundle the arm compiles is untouched.

title: hicasso: bisect F_old's surviving ~1-3.5 KB drop across 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13, on ONE instrument
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-nkeba, 2026-08-17, PR #8434, record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-controls-target-is-not-the-quantity-it-is-read-against.md

WHAT rf2-nkeba SETTLED, so this bead starts from the right place. V1's across-time clause failed by a published 16 - 20%. Most of that is a comparison artefact: the 2026-08-08 target is a round MEDIAN of rise/W taken on a pre-prime, pre-certificate instrument over an UNSELECTED population, while today's figures are per-window values on a CERTIFIED subset with the prime excluded. Three differences at once, none of them documented.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, and it is this bead's subject. Against the LOWEST of the six 2026-08-08 rounds with its largest step removed — the most generous like-for-like the surviving artefacts support — today's certified readings are still low by:

  reagent-subs   >= 982 B   (4.7% - 7.0%)
  uix-subs       >= 2,472 B (10.7% - 14.9%)

A gap at every cell. Smaller than published, and real.

WHAT IS ALREADY ELIMINATED, so this bead does not re-tread it:

- THE RESEEDED PAGE WIDTH — REFUTED on two independent grounds. `:p0/write-all` is byte-identical at 4a1537cb71 and 2e993181f8 and rebuilds `cells-n` = 300 regardless of the seed; the floor arm holds no subscription and the seed runs inside `prepare!` outside the measured region; and V1's own first clause reads F_old flat to <= 117 B over a 24x seeded-width range, i.e. <= ~351 B extrapolated to 300 cells.
- THE PRIME — accounted, and re-derived on the 2026-08-08 data itself at ~6,231 / ~6,267 B (1,038 / 1,045 per write), SMALLER than the pooled 6,966 the corpus subtracts.
- THE WORK UNIT — byte-identical at both revisions: same three statements, same drain split, same stride-2 sampling, same `write-all!` and `dispatch-sync!`.
- THE TOOLCHAIN — playwright 1.59.1, react/react-dom 19.2.0, shadow-cljs 3.4.10 at both revisions. CAVEAT: the 2026-08-08 dataset records no runtime version, so a resident-binary difference is neither ruled in nor out.

WHAT IS LEFT. Drift in the event pipeline. The drop was already present by 2026-08-13 (legMedian 19,781 / 20,446), so it happened inside 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13. Twenty-two commits landed under implementation/core/src in that interval and NONE was shown to be it.

WHAT THIS BEAD WOULD RUN. A bisection: the floor arm at B = 24 under write-all, at two or three revisions spanning that interval, on the CURRENT instrument at every point so the estimator is constant and only the substrate moves. That is the one design constraint that matters — a bisection that also moves the rig measures nothing.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN WINDOW rather than an extension of rf2-nkeba's. It needs a browser, it needs the rig frozen across several revisions, and Shape 6 forbids adding a rung or an arm inside a running window. rf2-nkeba added neither and launched no browser.

NOT ASSUMED: that the substrate is where it went. That is the surviving candidate, not an established one, and a bisection that comes back flat across the interval is a legitimate and informative result — it would push the question onto the runtime, which the pins cannot settle.
notes:
FENCED 2026-08-21 00:55 AUSEST — CLEARS WHEN worker/levelwit2-a233t's PR MERGES. Dispatch tick, and this fence is a COUPLING rather than a file conflict or a machine one.

THE MACHINE IS FREE. worker/recert-hic090 reported done, so the bench lane's one slot is open and this bead is the obvious P1 to take it. It is fenced anyway, for a reason that costs more than a slot.

WHY. This bead is a BISECT — many runs. rf2-a233t is in flight right now, arming a within-run LEVEL witness inside implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/alloc_level_witness.cjs, and deciding whether it becomes a REFUSAL (exit non-zero) or a recorded verdict. Until that lands, every run a bisect takes is adjudicated by the CURRENT witness, whose segmentsOf fail-open creates entries only for segment names that occur — so a record missing a whole measured segment formats CERTIFIED.

SO A BISECT TAKEN NOW WOULD BE CERTIFIED BY A GATE THAT CANNOT FAIL ON THE DEFECT IT EXISTS TO CATCH, and if a233t lands a refusal with a declared bound, some of those runs may be retrospectively inadmissible. title: hicasso: F_old no longer lands on its own 2026-08-08 figures — the allocation control's across-time clause fails by 16-20% on certified windows
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1/V2 re-run window, 2026-08-17 01:45-01:51 AUSEST, branch worker/v1v2-140 off 6a32dbf7e5. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md.

THE FINDING. V1's control has two clauses. The first (F_old flat in B) HOLDS and is now confirmed on CERTIFIED windows for the first time. The second — 'must land on the 2026-08-08 figures at B = 24 (24,108 / 24,730 B per write)' — is now ASSESSED for the first time, and it FAILS:

  segment        certified rise/W        2026-08-08 target   shortfall
  reagent-subs   19,349 / 19,650 / 19,816   24,108            17.8 - 19.7%
  uix-subs       19,712 / 20,696            24,730            16.3 - 20.3%

Five of twelve floor windows certified at B=24 under write-all (the comparable 2026-08-13 run certified NONE, which is why the clause could not be read before). Estimator: rise/W per certified window, prime leg excluded — the same quantity the 2026-08-08 figures are stated in (the-write-halfs-floor-is-the-pipeline.md:154 says so explicitly).

THE PRIME DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT. The 2026-08-08 windows predate rf2-oiy1, so their rise/W carried the first-leg excess spread over six writes: 6,966/6 = ~1,161 B. Subtracting it leaves pre-prime-equivalent targets near 22,947 and 23,569. The certified readings are still ~3.1 - 3.6 KB below THAT.

WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. F_old's stated job (allocation-instrument-rework.md:260-263) is to say the rig has not moved and thereby license comparison between the two writes.
  - The ACROSS-TIME half is NOT discharged: rows measured today may NOT be differenced against the 2026-08-08 rows. Every page that does so needs re-checking.
  - The WITHIN-RUN half is untouched: V2 compares two writes measured in the same sessions on the same build, and nothing in this failure bears on it.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This is NOT a claim that the 2026-08-08 figure was wrong. Three independent sessions since the prime landed — 2026-08-13 (legMedian 19,781 / 20,446), 2026-08-16 (19,256-23,132) and this one — agree on a floor near 19-20 KB, and the 2026-08-08 reading stands alone at 24.1-24.7 KB.
