DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

ROUTE (a) DISPATCHED AGAIN AND REFUSED AS ALREADY DISCHARGED — 2026-08-17 01:30 AUSEST,
worker "cheapwrite-140". NO WORKTREE WAS CREATED, no branch, no commit, no PR: there was no
honest change to make and I did not manufacture one. Status left OPEN and NOT claimed, so
the bead does not read in_progress with no live worker.

WHAT I WAS BRIEFED TO BUILD, VERBATIM FROM THE BRIEF: "route (a) only: a cheaper write on
the allocation bench, so the fixed per-write cost F stops consuming the masking budget",
quoting this bead's DESCRIPTION — "if the write could touch only the mounted boundaries, F
would fall with B and the whole squeeze relaxes."

THAT IS THIS BEAD'S OLDEST TEXT (2026-08-08, written BEFORE the work). Route (a) was built,
merged, structurally pinned and MEASURED nine days ago, and the measurement refutes the
premise. Verified at source this tick on origin/main @ e7bb5a3dfa, not from memory:

  - :p0/write-page EXISTS and is the allocation window's DEFAULT arm.
    p0_fixture.cljc:237 — (rf/reg-event :p0/write-page
      (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ v]] {:db (assoc db :cells (vec (repeat (count (:cells db)) v)))}))
    i.e. the width rebuilt is the db's own, not the compile-time 300.
  - THE WIDTH IS THE MOUNTED PAGE, threaded and unable to drift: seed-db takes grid-width,
    :p0/seed carries it (p0_arms.cljs:158 :initial-events [[:p0/seed (long grid-width)]]),
    enter-segment! and p0-heap/prepare! thread it from the driver (p0_heap.cljs:399,1252),
    :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db)), and the page is P0_ROOTS x P0_ALLOC_CELLS
    with P0_ALLOC_CELLS MANDATORY (p0_run.cjs:1196,1412).
  - p0_heap.cljs:1187-1200 — write-page! is the default arm, write-all! the else-arm of
    (= kind "write-all"); p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:1859-1892 pins exactly that,
    pins write-all! byte-identical with its literal cells-n, and pins write-all!
    reachable from exactly ONE place.
  - Landed in PR #7702 (worker/allocbuild-140), MERGED 2026-08-08T08:59:54Z.

THE PREMISE IS MEASURED FALSE: F DOES NOT SCALE WITH B, AND CANNOT BE MADE TO BY THIS ROUTE.
This bead's own V1 window (PR #8152, MERGED 2026-08-13T18:59:38Z) answered it with numbers:

  F_old - F_new = 1.1-1.9 KB per write, AT EVERY PAGE SIZE
  w = 3.6-7.3 B/cell, consistent across six independent readings
  F0 ~ 18-19.4 KB, i.e. OVER 90% OF F, and F_new is FLAT IN B for the same reason F_old is

The 300-element vector rebuild was never the dominant term. It was ~7% of F. The boundary-
proportional write works exactly as designed and removes exactly that 7%. The residue F0 is
THE EVENT PIPELINE, and that is recorded in-source at p0_run.cjs:1243 and p0_heap.cljs:305.

AND THE REMAINING 93% IS LOAD-BEARING, which is why route (a) has no second attempt in it.
The bench's own stated design (p0_fixture.cljc:211) is that both bulk writes go through
dispatch-sync "because in re-frame2 the commit IS the write clock and an arm that reached
past it — a bare reagent.core/atom, a direct app-db replace — would be skipping the event
pipeline and the signal graph that a real application pays for on every write." A write made
cheaper by removing F0 would stop measuring the thing HD-002's ladder claims to measure.
This is precisely the refusal condition the dispatch brief itself anticipated, and the
equivalence argument at p0_fixture.cljc:216-236 is why the 7% WAS safe to take: every
mounted key folds into db[:cells] under (mod k width), so the invalidation set is identical
and the old write's only extra was data no boundary read (276 of 300 cells at B=24).

TWO FURTHER PREMISES IN THAT BRIEF NO LONGER HOLD, both because route (b) landed in the
SAME PR #7702 rather than separately:

  1. "so F stops consuming the MASKING BUDGET" — THERE IS NO MASKING BUDGET. It is retired.
     ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B, ALLOC_B_PER_BOUNDARY_WRITE, predictedWindowB, headroom,
     maxBoundaries, floorBoundaries and maskable are all deleted, and
     p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:568-569 PINS their absence. Certification is now the leg
     rule (deviation from the cohort median beyond tau), the falls gate, and — since PR
     #8420 (rf2-4ctls, MERGED 2026-08-16T13:34:12Z) — allocIntraLegRefusals. The (W+1).perWrite
     charging rule the brief's whole squeeze table is computed from no longer certifies anything.
  2. "ROUTE (b) IS NOT YOURS. Do not build it, and do not blend the two." The 2026-08-08
     DELEGATED DECISION on this bead ruled the COMPOSED PACKAGE — "route (a) AND route (b),
     designed together in ONE brief. Not (a) alone, not (b) alone" — and both shipped
     together as criteria 2 and 3. A route-(a)-only dispatch contradicts this bead's own
     standing ruling.

THE THREE PROHIBITIONS WERE ALREADY HONOURED BY THE MERGED WORK, and I widened nothing and
touched nothing: ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B still 600,000, ALLOC_MIN_WRITES still 6, R=20 still
on the ladder, tau still the declared 0.25 placeholder. I took NO measurement window: no

SECOND CROSS-REFERENCE FROM THE BACKLOG REREAD, mayor 2026-08-18 11:45 AUSEST. This one bears on whether V2's residual can be ASSESSED at all, not just on how precisely.

rf2-irxrw, filed today by rf2-0gjqi's re-analysis and derived at source without taking a window, reports that THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT DRIVE BOTH WRITES IN ONE PROCESS. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (p0_run.cjs:1504), ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members and no paired option (:1490), and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). So one process drives ONE write, necessarily.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is structural rather than statistical: every write-all versus write-page comparison this instrument has ever produced differences TWO SEQUENTIAL PROCESS RUNS IN A FIXED ORDER. allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires those two writes to be compared as a same-page, same-run pair. They never have been.

WHY THIS TOUCHES THIS BEAD. V2's criterion is about the arm-floor residual, and the residual is exactly the quantity that comparison produces. Until a paired mode exists, V2's residual is UNASSESSED rather than small - and that is the merged-PR audit's own word, recorded on rf2-0gjqi on 2026-08-17.

WHAT THE RE-ANALYSIS ADDED to that audit, and it sharpens it considerably. The eight mid-rung sign comparisons that looked like 1-in-256 are EIGHT CELLS, ONE DRAW: they share one run order; the four reagent-subs cells difference against the SAME four certified floor windows; and rf2-77gz8's second floor mode moves both segments by exactly the same 3,792 B, which merges the segments too. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs, or 928 on uix-subs, reverses every sign - and three runs at one revision under one write span 3,852 / 3,912 B/write in certified floor median. Both exceed what it takes to flip the result.

WHAT IT DID NOT CLAIM, and the restraint is worth preserving: it did NOT adopt the mode account. A floor offset is additive and identical across a segment's arms, while the observed mid-rung offsets span 1,948 / 740 B/write and within an arm family the residual is closer to a constant proportion. Right magnitude, wrong shape - neither excluded nor supported. The cause is UNRESOLVED; only the inferential claim is refuted.

SO THE RULING ON THIS BEAD NOW HAS A PREREQUISITE THAT DID NOT EXIST YESTERDAY: rf2-irxrw's paired mode. Ruling before it lands would rule on a residual nobody can yet measure. That is not an argument for any particular disposition of the ladder - it is an argument about what evidence a defensible ruling can rest on, and it is the second such constraint recorded here today.

NOT DISPATCHED, NOTHING CHANGED HERE.

MAYOR RULING ON CRITERION 5, 2026-08-19 00:05 AUSEST, taken on Mike's standing delegation. This criterion has owed a ruling since the paired mode landed, and the 2026-08-18 re-read poses it cleanly enough to answer.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING ON. rf2-0gjqi's question — whether ~1-4% of non-cancellation is tolerable — is WITHDRAWN, and rightly: under matched within-round pairing the agreement half no longer shows a direction at all (page reads below all at 10 of 16 mid-rung cell medians, not 8 of 8, with the absolute median falling from 1.68% to 0.46%), and the sign that WAS there tracks which leg pass ran SECOND rather than which write it was. That is rf2-fk6pj's subject, not this one.

THE QUESTION AS IT NOW STANDS: is the instrument's residual non-cancellation acceptable, given that its R=0 NULL ARM — boundaries that read nothing, so arm minus floor must be exactly zero under either write — reads an absolute median of 1.5 B per boundary and a 90th percentile of 4.5, over 38 paired certified observations?

RULING: ACCEPT IT, AND PUBLISH IT AS A NAMED FLOOR RATHER THAN AS A TOLERANCE.

WHY ACCEPT. The null arm's reading is the instrument's own noise floor measured directly, which is the best possible way to have it: not inferred, not modelled, but read off an arm whose true value is known to be zero. And it is three orders of magnitude below the quantities the ladder publishes — the per-boundary terms this programme reports run 2,031 to 22,174 B per boundary per write, against which 1.5 B is roughly 0.07% and the p90 of 4.5 B is roughly 0.2%. An instrument does not need perfect cancellation; it needs a floor small against its signal and HONESTLY STATED.

WHY 'A NAMED FLOOR' RATHER THAN 'A TOLERANCE', and this is the part that matters. Ruling a PERCENTAGE tolerable would be the wrong shape: percentages travel, and a figure that is 0.07% of a 2,031 B term is 100% of a 1.5 B one. The number that is stable is the FLOOR ITSELF, in bytes per boundary, because that is what the null arm measures.

SO THE OBLIGATION THIS RULING CREATES, and it is one line of code and one of prose rather than new machinery:
  1. Record 1.5 B per boundary (median) and 4.5 B (p90) over 38 paired certified observations as the instrument's NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR, in the record beside the figures it qualifies.
  2. REFUSE, rather than publish, any per-boundary figure that is not comfortably above it. I set that bar at ten times the p90 — 45 B per boundary — because a figure within an order of magnitude of the noise floor is not a measurement, and the honest answer there is the same one rf2-2rtt6.139 reached about sizing: an instrument that says 'I cannot resolve this' is not a worse instrument.
Do NOT add a new gate, a new constant, or a rung parameter. The floor is a published number and a refusal the preflight can already express.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE. The floor-drop half stands as the re-read left it: 1,652 B (8.6%) on reagent-subs and 1,652-1,658 B (8.4%) on uix-subs, the same number on both segments to within 6 B across 21 paired certified rounds, against published unpaired figures of 1,769 / 1,765 B. Those published figures are now superseded by a within-round measurement and should be moved, with the change of basis stated — the same disclosure rule applied to S8 on rf2-6zc2q.

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN carrying that work. Re-derive every number here at the tip before acting; they are quoted from a report, not measured by me.

Three facts bear on it, measured first-hand from data/alloc-0gjqi/{paired-run1,paired-run2}.json at origin/main b524ba71ce. None of them decides it.

(a) THE BOUND REFUSES NOTHING THE CERTIFICATE ADMITS. At W = 6 the bound charges (W+1) x perWrite <= 300,000 B. (b) THE BOUND IS CHARGED ON A QUANTITY THAT CANNOT SEE A COLLECTION. Two identities hold over all 528 arm windows in the corpus, checked rather than asserted:
      perWrite == rise / writes                       0 mismatches of 528
      rise     == sum(max(leg,0)) + sum(max(gap,0))   0 mismatches of 528
rise sums POSITIVE deltas only, over legs and over the inter-leg gaps alike. A collection inside a window therefore makes that window's rise SMALLER, its perWrite smaller, and its charge against the masking bound smaller. The bound is loosest exactly where masking is worst. The 72 R20 refusals carry a median rise of 879,080 B against a would-be total of 1,035,036 B — charged on about 85% of what the window actually asked for.

title: hicasso: attack the interpreter-walk mount cost — the located deficit is 100% script, +1.06ms where uix pays +0.38ms on byte-identical DOM
description:
THE OPTIMISATION LANE'S PRIMARY TARGET, opened under the operator's 2026-08-02 directive ('keep going on the actual implementation, the optimisation can happen in parallel').

WHERE THE DEFICIT LIVES, from three independent measurements that agree:
  - rf2-0qj9w located it: the candidate pays +1.06 ms over its own floor where uix-subs — same spine, same adapter, same 300 reads, BYTE-IDENTICAL DOM — pays +0.38 ms. The runtime hiccup codec walking 901 elements.
  - rf2-emvod/rf2-yd52q: taskNet reads every gated pair 0.98-1.08 — the gap is ENTIRELY script, zero frame.
  - rf2-2rtt6.56 (census rows): typical census shape 1.16-1.22x vs UIx (instrument-limited at the 1.10 line); worst case 1.3053x on the ONE-BOUNDARY 1,202-element page — the pure interpreter-walk shape. The deficit scales with elements-per-boundary, not boundaries.
  - rf2-2rtt6.31 (HD-008 re-take): donor arms show the same ~10-13% interpreter cost over UIx at their shapes.

SO THE TARGET IS THE PER-ELEMENT COST OF THE HICCUP WALK: parse/classify/convert per element per mount. The one-boundary page (1,202 elements, one commit) is the acceptance shape — it currently FAILS the 1.10x line at 1.3053x [1.1044-1.4660] with an 18.7% margin clearing a 6.7% band; the census feed is the guard shape (it must not regress from 1.1646x).

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, to be costed not assumed — and the PRIOR-ART DIRECTIVE applies in full (mine Freehand, re-frame.ui, Replicant, Reagent, UIx; cite taken/declined):
  1. CACHE THE STATIC SKELETON: most census markup is static per view; Replicant and every compiled substrate exploit this. re-frame.ui's compiler shows what static extraction buys; the question is what a RUNTIME can cache keyed on the hiccup's identity without a compiler (fences: no compiler, no analyzer — but a value-keyed cache at the codec is neither).
  2. CHEAPEN THE PER-ELEMENT PATH: prop-map conversion, keyword->string, intent classification — profile first, the walk has never been profiled element-by-element.
  3. AMORTISE ACROSS COMMITS: the walk re-runs per render; the memo wrapper (HD-026, #7375 pending) already stops child re-walks — what remains is the FIRST walk, which is what mount prices.
  Reagent's own answer (interpret once into a render fn, cache on the component) and UIx's (macro-compile to createElement at build time — unavailable to us by fence) bracket the space.

FENCES, all standing: Surface B; no compiler, no analyzer, no candidate ledger, no ViewCell graph; <=2-hook shell; subscribe closes over the read set alone; Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's codec — a cache AROUND the codec is in scope, a fork OF it needs a ruling.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: the full instrument canon (raw TaskDuration, quiet box, absolutes+ratios, B/E/Q, bands, blob provenance, discarded-if-died, announced windows). Profile and optimise in the implementation lane; PUBLISHED rows only on the clock of record against same-run donors. An optimisation claiming X% must show it on the one-boundary acceptance shape AND show the feed did not regress.

AN HONEST NEGATIVE IS AN ANSWER: if the walk is irreducible within the fences, say so with the profile — that converts 'the interpreter is slow' into 'the interpreter costs exactly this, here', which is what a ship/kill decision needs.

title: [method] README and bootstrap say FIVE standing loops; loops.md has SIX, and the missing one is the drift-catcher
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 06:45 AUSEST from the MAYOR RETRO loop.

THE DEFECT. Both front-door documents undercount loops.md by one:
  - README.md:271  "the 5 standing loops"
  - bootstrap.md:78 "SET UP THE LOOPS. The five loops are in `loops.md`."
loops.md has SIX top-level loop sections: Merge, Dispatch, Backlog reread, Posture, Hygiene,
Method reread.

IT IS A LONG-STANDING STALE CONSTANT, NOT RECENT DRIFT, and that is the interesting part.
loops.md ALREADY held six at commit 9728d5cae6 (22 Aug), the commit where README.md was last
touched - so the count was wrong when it was last written, and seventy-four commits to that
tree since, plus every Method reread including several of mine tonight, passed over it. A count
written in prose reads as authoritative, and nothing was checking it against the headings.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS SELF-CONCEALING, which is what makes it worth more than a number fix. A mayor
following bootstrap.md literally codifies FIVE command files and never creates the sixth - and
the sixth is METHOD REREAD, the loop whose entire job is catching stale measured constants. The
omission removes the instrument that would have found the omission. Nothing errors; five loops
run perfectly well.

SHIPPED as PR #8974 (mayor/loop-count). The README takes the number. bootstrap takes the DURABLE
fix instead: enumerate the loops from that file's own section headings rather than from a count,
so the seventh does not reopen this - one sentence inside the step that already exists, replacing
a number that will go stale again with an instruction that will not.

BOUNDED IN CHANGE, NOT IN SEARCH: these are the only two numeric claims about loops in either
file, searched as digits AND as number-words. bootstrap.md's "five-clause criterion" is a
DIFFERENT count and is CORRECT - the merge criterion still has five clauses - which is why this
is two targeted edits rather than a replace.

GATE COVERAGE DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO FILES and only one is gated. The README line is ordinary

check_doc_slugs.py exit 1 naming README.md:271 and mkdocs --strict exit 1 "Aborted with 1

a70cc40d before and after. The bootstrap edit is INSIDE A FENCED BLOCK - it is a pasteable prompt

nothing about it; verified by hand instead (no link, no anchor, no heading, rewrap at <=85 chars
against a file maximum of 123).

REOPENED 2026-09-02 07:10 AUSEST — THE FINDING WAS FALSE AND PR #8974 WAS A REGRESSION. Revert
raised as PR #8975. Everything above this line about a "stale count" is wrong; it is kept rather
than deleted because the reasoning error is the useful part.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. loops.md declares FIVE loops in its cadence table - Merge + dispatch,
Backlog reread, Posture + stranded sweep, Hygiene, Method reread - and states the distinction
outright, twenty lines above where I was looking:

  "Five loops, six bodies. Merge and dispatch share one tick, but each is long enough to want a
   heading of its own, so they are written separately below. The numbering follows the bodies;
   the cadence follows the table."

So "the 5 standing loops" and "The five loops are in loops.md" were both CORRECT. My six was a
count of BODIES.

HOW I GOT THERE, because the shape is worth more than the fact. I ran `grep -c '^## [0-9]'`,
got six, and treated a heading count as a loop count - the classic wrong-question instrument.
The page pre-empts it in two consecutive sentences, one of them the paragraph quoted above and
the other "Some people prefer merge and dispatch as separate loops". I read neither, because I
was grepping the file rather than reading the section.

THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE WAS INSIDE MY OWN WORKING AND I INVERTED IT. I established that the count
was already "wrong" at the commit where README.md was last touched, and read that as proof of a
long-standing stale constant. The correct reading is that it was right then and is right now. A
number unchanged across seventy-four commits is far more likely correct than uniquely
overlooked - and I wrote the opposite into a close reason and a PR body.

I ALSO FABRICATED A CONSEQUENCE TO JUSTIFY IT. The "self-concealing" argument - that a mayor
would codify five command files and omit Method reread, the drift-catcher - has no referent:
Method reread IS loop 5 in the table. The argument felt strong precisely because it was
constructed to fit a conclusion already reached.

THE BOOTSTRAP HALF WAS WORSE THAN A WRONG NUMBER and had to be reverted on its own merits. It
instructed a mayor to enumerate the loops from section headings; followed literally that yields
six loops and six command files, contradicting the cadence table and splitting the single tick
that exists so a merge can refill the slot it frees. An instruction that manufactures a
structural error every time it is obeyed.

NOTHING IS ADDED BY THE REVERT. No new caution, no clarifying sentence. The document's own
"Five loops, six bodies" is complete and discriminating; it did not fail, I failed to read it,
and warning about a trap the page already names would repeat the mistake in the other direction.

title: [method] step 1 names one direction of the sequencing hazard; the inverse — a lift is narrower than the item — fails OPEN
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 04:11 AUSEST from the Method reread loop, about a near-miss I made in the
merge tick immediately before it.

WHAT THE DOC SAYS TODAY. dispatch-prompt-template.md step 1 (shipped an hour earlier as
rf2-ute0q) names two sequencing shapes and BOTH FAIL CLOSED: a generic fence restated over a
triage note that already named its predecessors "converts a satisfied precondition back into a
blocker - which either strands the work or ... costs the worker a justification round it should
not have had to write."

THE GAP. The inverse is unnamed and fails OPEN. A note LIFTING a fence names the fence it lifts,
not the item, so an item can carry a second sequencing the lift says nothing about; its newest
layer then reads "released" while a live precondition sits underneath. The failure is not
re-blocking clear work - it is dispatching into a surface somebody else holds, or one gated by a
decision nobody has made.

MEASURED LIVE, and I was one command from taking it. rf2-ov144: I lifted its api-manifest fence
at 03:22 on the holding worker's own explicit words, then at 04:05 - with tools/xray finally
free and the PR queue empty - went to dispatch it. Reading the WHOLE item rather than the note I
came for turned up an older 2026-08-30 21:55 note sequencing it behind rf2-ahjbc, which is OPEN
and is an operator call. Worse, the OTHER half of that same older note ("regenerates
spec/api-manifest.edn LAST, after rf2-v4xjh/rf2-93sxp land") HAD genuinely cleared - both read
CLOSED - which is precisely what made the note as a whole look discharged.

MEASUREMENT OF THE CLAIM, not assertion: probing the step-1 section flat for 'lift', 'lifted',
'release', 'released', 'more than one fence', 'second fence', 'several fences', 'other fences'
and 'narrower' returns ABSENT for all nine, while the controls 'sequencing', 'authorisation with
a precondition', 'hold' and 'predecessors' all return FOUND - so the instrument reads the section
and the direction is genuinely missing.

SHIPPED as PR #8973 (mayor/lift-is-narrower): one paragraph inside the existing step, naming the
inverse, its fail-open consequence, the measurement, and the durable remedy - encode a
precondition as a TRACKER EDGE rather than leaving it in prose, because a fence that exists only
in a note is re-derived every pass and eventually missed. The two existing shapes are untouched
and no mechanism is added.

MECHANICAL HALF ALREADY DONE, independently of the doc: rf2-ov144 now carries a real dependency
edge on rf2-ahjbc and no longer appears in bd ready. That is the third time tonight the same
repair was needed (rf2-rc0yh and rf2-k5r9t earlier), which is the argument for naming the remedy
in the document rather than re-deriving it each time.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus python -m mkdocs build --strict. Neither reads prose
- the added paragraph carries no link or anchor - so both greens are about the rest of the file
and the prose was verified by hand. Discrimination proved by planted anchor (exit 1 naming
dispatch-prompt-template.md:97); restore verified by blob hash c5c4c156 before and after.

CORRECTION 2026-09-02 04:52 AUSEST — THERE WAS NO REVERTED CLOSE. The re-close note above is
WRONG about the reason it was written, and it is corrected here rather than deleted so the
instrument failure stays on the record. The bead has been closed since 04:30:26 and was never
reopened.

THE TRUTH, read from the fields rather than the rendering: status = 'closed', closed_at =
2026-09-01T18:30:25Z, absent from `bd list --status open`. The history is three entries,
newest-first: 04:30:26 closed / 04:14:24 open / 04:11:22 open — an ordinary create, notes
update, close.

TWO INSTRUMENTS FAILED, AND THE SECOND APPEARED TO CONFIRM THE FIRST, which is what made it
convincing.

  (1) The status probe was `bd show <id> | head -1 | grep -oE 'OPEN|CLOSED' | head -1`. THIS
  BEAD'S OWN TITLE CONTAINS THE WORD "OPEN" — "...the inverse ... fails OPEN" — and the title
  precedes the status field on that line, so the probe returned the title's word. The bead was
  the only one of twenty in that sweep whose title could poison its own status read, and it is
  the one that flagged.

  (2) The corroborating check was a status-transition walk over `bd history --json`. It reported
  "closed -> open" at the newest index. The history is NEWEST-FIRST, so walking indices upward
  walks BACKWARDS in time: a pair reading closed-then-open forward-in-index is open-then-closed
  forward-in-TIME. The detector printed every transition reversed. On any bead that has ever been
  closed it would report a reopen.

WHAT THIS COST: a re-close that was a no-op, and a false finding written onto this bead claiming
a third revert this session. The WORK was never at risk — b22600c25a is an ancestor of
origin/main throughout.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, and it is the general form rather than this bead's specifics: read a STATUS
from the status FIELD, never by pattern-matching the rendered header, because an item's own text
can contain the words a status probe looks for. And before trusting a transition walk over a
history, establish which end is newest by reading the timestamps — the ordering is a property of
the tool, not something to assume, and an ordering error inverts every answer while producing
well-formed output.

title: [method] gate-artefact cleanup uses a variable-expanded rm, which stalls on a permission prompt
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 03:39 AUSEST from an OPERATOR REPORT (Mike, in chat), not from an audit.

THE FRICTION. Workers clean their gate artefacts with a variable-expanded deletion -
  rm -f "$SP"/*<worktree>*
- and a static permission check cannot evaluate $SP, so it must stop and ask. The ask lands
on an operator who may not be watching, and the worker stalls mid-turn with everything queued
behind it. Mike's words: "that results in the session locking up and asking me for permissions
to continue because the rm operation is potentially dangerous if $SP is blank."

THE HAZARD IS REAL, WHICH IS WHY THE CHECK IS RIGHT TO ASK. An unset or empty variable turns
"$SP"/*name* into a glob rooted at the top of the filesystem. So the repair removes the
AMBIGUITY, not the check.

SHIPPED as PR #8971 (mayor/rm-literal-path): one paragraph in the gate-mechanics block of
dispatch-prompt-template.md, beside the artefact-naming rule that generates this cleanup -
delete by the LITERAL path, never through a variable; and where a variable is genuinely
unavoidable, make the shell itself refuse an empty one ("${DIR:?}"), named as the FALLBACK
because it removes the hazard without removing the prompt.

A SECOND, STRUCTURAL OPTION WAS OFFERED TO MIKE AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE - it is his call, and
this bead is not authority for it. The template currently sends artefacts to the SESSION-shared
scratch directory, which is why the worktree-and-attempt naming rule exists and why a cleanup
command is needed at all. Writing them inside the worker's own worktree instead would let
scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh take them out on reap: no cleanup command, no glob, no
prompt, and the peer-collision half of the naming rule becomes unnecessary.

I MEASURED THE ONE THING THAT COULD HAVE BLOCKED THAT OPTION, so the decision is informed:
*.log is ALREADY gitignored repo-wide (.gitignore:14), so a gate-*.log written inside a
worktree is invisible to `git status --porcelain` (verified: clean tree with the file present)
and does not block removal (verified: the removal script's --dry-run accepted the tree). So the
structural option needs no tooling change - only a change to the instruction.

SCRIPT WART NOTED IN PASSING, not filed: remove-worker-worktree.sh --dry-run prints its
ordinary success line "OK: worktree removal complete." A reader could take that for a real
removal. It is inert - the worktree and branch were both verified intact afterwards - and not
worth a change on its own, but worth knowing before trusting that line.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8971, verified on main at d6e56e4d19 (docs(method): delete gate artefacts by literal path, never through a variable). Verified by MERGE, not by PR state. One paragraph in the gate-mechanics block of dispatch-prompt-template.md, beside the artefact-naming rule that generates this cleanup: delete by the LITERAL path, never through a variable, because a deletion whose target a static permission check cannot evaluate is one that check has to stop and ask about, and the ask lands on an operator who may not be watching - so the cleanup stalls mid-turn and the work queued behind it stalls with it. The hazard is stated as real rather than theoretical (an unset or empty variable turns the glob into one rooted at the top of the filesystem), and the shell-side guard is named as the FALLBACK because it removes the hazard without removing the prompt. Discrimination proved by planted broken anchor (slugs exit 1, naming dispatch-prompt-template.md:1066 and the planted target); edit committed BEFORE the plant so the restore target was the intended state; restore verified by blob hash eb917ee7 before and after, not by reading a diff. title: [method] route-vs-queue names one queue trigger and leaves the actual discriminator implied: is there an open change to land in?
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 02:10 AUSEST by the acting mayor, from the Method reread loop (loops.md
§6), about a decision I had made correctly twenty minutes earlier for a reason the document
does not give.

THE SECTION. loops.md §2, "Routing a finding onto a live worker's file". It offers two
moves. Route-and-note: "message the worker that holds the file, and the fix lands inside the
change that is already open". Queue-and-note: "Sometimes routing is the wrong move
altogether. It widens a deliberately bounded fence mid-flight, which is how a bounded repair
becomes an unbounded one."

THE GAP. The route branch's clause "the change that is already open" reads as DESCRIPTION of
the happy path, not as a PRECONDITION to test - and the queue branch names exactly one
trigger, fence-widening. So a mayor holding a finding whose surface is held by a live agent
WHOSE CHANGE HAS ALREADY MERGED finds neither branch obviously applicable, and the default
pull is to route, because routing is the section's headline move and the agent is right
there and messageable.

WHY THAT FAILS OPEN. Routing into an agent with no open change hands fresh work to a
transient owner with nothing to carry it - which is the precise shape the section's own next
paragraph says evaporates ("the message lives in one agent's transcript, so if that agent
dies, times out, or reasonably declines the extra item ... the finding evaporates"). The
section records that hazard against the AGENT (it may die or decline) and not against the
CHANGE, so a reader who has satisfied himself the agent is alive - which is easy, and which
I had done - reads the warning as discharged.

MEASURED TODAY, and this is what I want on the record because I nearly took the wrong
branch. rf2-7htk7 was reopened by the PR #8963 audit with two concrete findings. The agent
that wrote #8963 was STILL RUNNING and still holding tools/xray/, I had messaged it an hour
earlier, and its PR was MERGED. Route was the reflex; queue was correct. I reached queue by
reasoning from the clause rather than by reading a rule, which is exactly the situation §6
exists to catch.

APPLYING THE DOCUMENT'S OWN DISCHARGING TEST to this finding, since #8962 just installed it:
what would I expect to SEE that is different if this claim were false? A sentence in that
section naming a merged, closed or finished change as a queue trigger, or naming the absence
of an open change at all. Searched the section as a flat string: "already open" and "landed"
are present; "merged", "no open change", "has closed", "finished" and "not open" are all
absent. So the claim is not merely un-refuted, it has a positive check behind it.

PROPOSED - ONE CLAUSE, and it belongs inside the existing route paragraph rather than as a
third branch. Say that routing works BECAUSE there is an open change for the fix to land in,
so that is the thing to check first; where the holder's change has already landed, there is
nothing to route into and the queue branch is the one to take even though no fence is being
widened. Keep both existing branches and both existing reasons exactly as they are - this
adds a second trigger to the queue branch, it does not replace the first. Add no mechanism:
the section says outright that an owner plus one note "does not want to grow past that: no
routing registry, no tracking field, no script", and that binds this repair.

SEQUENCING. docs/the-mayor-method/ is SOLE-TOUCHER hot-zone. rf2-e9z2e is IN FLIGHT on
loops.md §5 right now. This finding is being ROUTED to that worker rather than dispatched -
see the routing note below - which is the section's own preferred move and is available here
precisely because that worker's change IS open, the condition this bead is about. If it does
not land there, this item dispatches on its own once that PR merges.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus python -m mkdocs build --strict (exclude_docs
does NOT hide the-mayor-method/). Run mkdocs as "python -m mkdocs" - bare mkdocs returns 127
here, which is NO VERDICT rather than a pass. Neither gate reads prose: verify by hand.

ROUTED 2026-09-02 02:12 AUSEST to the live rf2-e9z2e worker (worktree reaproute-e9z2e,
branch worker/reaproute-e9z2e), which holds docs/the-mayor-method/ under the sole-toucher
rule and whose change is OPEN - the condition this bead is about, which is what makes
routing available here rather than queueing.

WHAT WAS ROUTED: the one-clause repair described above, in full, with the proposed wording
constraints (inside the existing route paragraph, a second queue trigger rather than a
replacement, no mechanism).

WHAT HAPPENS IF IT DOES NOT LAND: the worker was told declining is a fine answer, because
taking it widens a deliberately bounded repair mid-flight. If it declines, or never answers,
or its PR merges without this clause, THIS ITEM DISPATCHES ON ITS OWN once the method
surface frees. The item is the durable owner; the message is not.

ROUTING DID NOT LAND, verified 2026-09-02 02:52 AUSEST at the published head of PR #8966
(worker/reaproute-e9z2e). The PR touches docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md only, and its 19 added
lines carry the rf2-e9z2e repair alone - probes for 'already open', 'landed', 'queue' and

title: test(websocket): integration fixture shadows the example registrations it claims to cover
description:
Audit finding from PR #8959 across completeness, correctness, and implementation quality.

The focused WebSocket integration fixture does not consistently exercise the runnable example registrations it claims to protect. `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs` calls `register-all!` for every test, and that function re-declares registrations from `examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs` inline. Because `reg-*` is last-write-wins, the fixture copies replace the example's own handlers before assertions run.

This is measured, not hypothetical: PR #8959 records that a fault planted in the example's `:ws.app/request-reply` handler body left the whole focused suite green. The same ownership split also weakens the boundary checks by construction: `inbound-boundary-structural-test` reads `handler-meta` only after `register-all!` has installed the fixture's copied `:schema` and `:rf.schema/at-boundary` metadata, so the suite can certify the copy while the runnable example drifts.

Completeness: machine/schema/mock vars are genuinely reused, but the source registration bodies and metadata are not. Correctness: a regression in the shipped example can remain green while its test-local twin behaves correctly. Implementation quality: the docstring now tells maintainers to mirror changes into both copies, preserving the drift mechanism instead of removing it.

Minimal outcome: make the example registrations re-invocable from one source of truth and have test setup call that source (or reuse named handler/metadata values directly). Add one focused mutation/control proving that changing the example's ingress handler or boundary metadata makes the suite red. Keep this local to the WebSocket example; do not build a generic registrar reload framework or broaden the public API.

Duplicate search covered all-status terms for `websocket register-all handler bodies`, `websocket test fixture mirrors example`, `request-reply body left suite green`, `websocket handler drift`, `websocket inbound boundary test`, `websocket at-boundary fixture`, and `websocket example registration test`; no existing owner was found.
acceptance_criteria: The WebSocket focused suite registers the example's handler bodies and boundary metadata from the same definitions the runnable example uses, with no independent test-local copy that can drift. A controlled fault in the example's `:ws.app/request-reply` body or removal of its `:rf.schema/at-boundary` metadata makes the focused suite red; the restored focused and adapter suites pass. The repair stays local and adds no generic reload framework.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8969, worker/wsfixture-idv1m) — finding CONFIRMED at source and repaired; premise held in full.

REPRODUCED BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING, both directions, on the pre-fix tree:
- gutting the example's :ws.app/request-reply body ({:db db}) -> focused suite exit 0, 29 tests / 240 assertions / 0 failures. Matches what PR #8959 recorded.
- deleting the example's :rf.schema/at-boundary from :ws.app/request-reply -> focused suite exit 0, 29 tests / 240 assertions / 0 failures. This second direction was NOT previously measured; it confirms the 'weakened by construction' half — inbound-boundary-structural-test was reading handler-meta back for metadata register-all! had installed moments earlier.

REPAIR (minimal outcome, first option): each example ns (websocket.schema / .connection / .messages / .core) now installs its registrations through a named re-invocable (defn register! ...), still called once at ns-load, so the production-app ns-load idiom and core/run are unchanged. Ignoring whitespace the diff to the four example files is exactly the wrapper — defn + docstring + one closing paren + (register!) — no registration content changed. The fixture's register-all! calls the four entry points and keeps no copy. Registered ids in the fixture: 30 -> 5 (four :ws.test/* reply-log targets it genuinely owns, plus the two framework :rf.machine/* runtime subs no example ns owns). Verified line-oriented AND over whitespace-collapsed text, with origin/main as the positive control. No generic registrar-reload framework, no public API change, nothing outside the WebSocket example.

The docstring instructing maintainers to mirror body changes into both copies is deleted with the mechanism it described.

CONTROL ADDED: websocket-example-registrations-are-live — three assertions, one per way the coupling can be lost: registered :doc (identity: which definition won the last write), registered :schema + :rf.schema/at-boundary read off the live registry, and the handler body driven through a real dispatch.

BOTH PLANTS REPLAYED ON THE REPAIRED TREE:
- body fault -> exit 1, 18 failures across 8 tests (new control among them)
- at-boundary removal -> exit 1, 2 failures (websocket-inbound-boundary-structural + new control)

GATES (implementation/, test:cljs split into its two phases; captured runner exit codes, all re-run after rebase onto the current base):
- compile-node-test.cjs node-test: exit 0, 1876 files, 0 warnings
- node out/node-test.js (full CLJS contract suite): exit 0, 11121 tests / 55163 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors
- node out/node-test.js --test=re-frame.websocket-cljs-test: exit 0, 30 tests / 245 assertions / 0 failures (was 29/240; +1 test, +5 assertions = the control)

Concurrency check: 4 open PRs at dispatch time, none touching implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs or examples/patterns/websocket/ (pattern control positive). No live change beside this one.

Acceptance criteria met in full. Left open for the mayor to close on merge.

The premise was REPRODUCED before anything changed, in BOTH directions: on the pre-fix tree, gutting the example's :ws.app/request-reply body left the focused suite at exit 0 (29 tests / 240 assertions, 0 failures), and deleting its :rf.schema/at-boundary did the same. title: [method] the reap route stops at the empty sink: an id keys TWO locations and the doc names only the expensive fallback
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 01:28 AUSEST by the acting mayor, from the Method reread loop (loops.md §6),
against a rule I had just spent a whole Hygiene loop enforcing. This is the §6 category
"hazards recorded without their discriminating test" — the hazard is on the page, the cheap
test that discharges it is not, and the doc jumps straight to the expensive fallback.

WHAT THE DOC SAYS TODAY. loops.md §5 Reaping records the empty-sink hazard correctly and at
length: "beware a per-agent scratch sink that merely shares the id"; "An empty file keyed by
the id says nothing whatever about whether a report exists - it is a fact about that file";
"the sink read empty for fifteen of seventeen worktrees, every one of those fifteen
transcripts sat complete elsewhere". It then says "the id names a FILE only once you know
which file is the agent's OWN; until then it names a directory to search", and the NEXT
paragraph - headed "When no id was recorded at all" - gives the path search: grep every
transcript for the worktree path, rank by hit count, confirm by the report's own claimed root.

THE GAP. Between "the sink is empty" and "grep 4.6 GB of transcripts" there is a step the doc
never names: TRY THE ID AT ITS OTHER LOCATION. An agent id is not one path. Here it keys both
a per-task scratch sink AND the real session transcript store, under different roots and a
different filename convention. The doc's own evidence already implies a second location exists
- "their real transcripts sat complete elsewhere" - but it never turns "elsewhere" into a step,
so a reader who has just been told the sink lies goes to the path search, which is two orders
of magnitude more expensive and, per the doc's own warning, many-to-one and misrankable.

MEASURED TODAY, one hygiene pass, 40 candidate worktrees.
  - 38 had a ledger id; 2 had no row at all.
  - Scratch sink keyed by id: NON-EMPTY for 9, exactly 0 bytes for 31. Consistent with the
    doc's "fifteen of seventeen", so the recorded constant is NOT stale - the remedy is
    incomplete.
  - Second id-keyed location: held a complete transcript for ALL 31 of the empty-sink ids.
    Zero misses. 29 of the 31 opened their final message with a quotable completion sentence;
    the other 2 (adapterswitch, twosmall) ended on interim status and were correctly REFUSED
    the reap - the route works in both directions, which is what makes it a test rather than
    a shortcut.
  - Path search was needed for exactly 2 of 40, both unindexed: timerincarn-jqvgp resolved
    cleanly (92 hits in the worker's own transcript against 1 in each peer, and its report's
    claimed root matched), and http-issuance did not (every hit was 1 - peers naming it and
    nothing else), so that tree stays.

So the expensive fallback earned its place once in forty, and the doc points at it thirty-one
times too often.

PROPOSED, small, and it belongs inside the existing Reaping paragraph that already warns about
the sink rather than as a new block. Say that an id can key MORE THAN ONE location; that an
empty one is a fact about THAT location and not about the id; and that the step between them is
to enumerate the id's other locations before falling back to the path search. Keep the path
search exactly where it is, as the route for an id that was never recorded - which is what it
is actually for.

GENERICITY. State it as "an agent id may key several locations" rather than naming this host's
directory layout. A transcript path the platform documents as an implementation detail is not a
contract - loops.md says so itself two paragraphs later - so the durable instruction is
"enumerate the id's locations", not "look in <path>".

SEQUENCING - MANDATORY. docs/the-mayor-method/ is SOLE-TOUCHER hot-zone. PR #8962
(worker/methodstep-ute0q, rf2-ute0q + rf2-f7fby) is OPEN against loops.md and
dispatch-prompt-template.md right now. DO NOT DISPATCH until #8962 merges.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus python -m mkdocs build --strict (exclude_docs
does NOT hide the-mayor-method/). Run mkdocs as "python -m mkdocs" - bare mkdocs returns 127
here, which is NO VERDICT rather than a pass. Neither gate reads prose, tables or rendering:
verify those by hand and say so in the PR body.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8966, verified on main at b99e95fefa (docs(method): name the id's other locations as the step between an empty sink and the path search). Verified by MERGE, not by PR state. The repair sits INSIDE the existing empty-sink paragraph in loops.md section 5 Reaping - an id may key several locations rather than one, an empty one is a fact about THAT location and not about the id, and the step between them is to enumerate the id's remaining locations before falling back to the path search, which is left verbatim and in place as the route for an id that was never recorded. Carries the forty-worktree measurement including the both-directions discrimination (29 quotable reports found, 2 correctly REFUSED on interim status). Written generically - 'an id may key several locations', no host directory layout - as the bead required, since the page itself says two paragraphs later that a platform-documented transcript path is not a contract. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0, test-fast-pr.sh exit 0, all re-run in full on the final base after rebase; both doc gates proved to read the worker's tree by planted fault (slugs exit 1 naming loops.md:1211; mkdocs exit 1 naming the-mayor-method/loops.md, which also re-confirms exclude_docs does not hide the directory), each restore verified by blob hash. THE BEAD'S OWN SEQUENCING NOTE WAS STALE and the worker said so: it read 'PR #8962 is OPEN - DO NOT DISPATCH until it merges', but #8958 and #8962 had both merged before dispatch and the merge base carried both. No harm - I dispatched after the merge - but the note outlived its condition. GATE MISFIRE WORTH KEEPING: one run chained behind git fetch with && lost a fetch race, so the gate never ran and the captured 1 was the FETCH's status; the ABSENT LOG FILE was the tell. Re-run standalone, green.

title: [method] the mayor briefs from the bead's oldest layer — make the newest-mutation read and hold-banner sweep a STEP, not a thing to remember
notes:
FILED 2026-09-02 by the acting mayor, against my own practice. This is at least the THIRD recorded instance of one failure class and the memories have not stopped it, which is the argument for a mechanical step.

THE PRIOR RECORD, found while filing this: bd memories 'mayor-brief' returns three keys, two of them predating today - mayor-brief-accuracy-stop-asserting-file-paths-i (2026-07-18, 'three times in one session') and mayor-brief-premises-must-be-verified-at-head (2026-08-17, whose own text says 'fifth instance'). Today added a third. A note that has been written three times and re-learned each time is not working as a control.

TODAY'S THREE, all the same shape - briefed from the bead's Scope/description rather than its newest text-bearing mutation, all three caught by the WORKER rather than by me:
- rf2-y8jjk: dispatched onto an unstruck '*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. ***' banner that WAS the newest text-bearing field. Worker refused, wrote nothing, opened no PR. A sweep then found ELEVEN of 27 open beads carrying a hold banner - I had been reporting two of them as dispatchable.
- rf2-9n43e: the newest note split the work into A (dispatchable) and B (sequenced behind two open beads sharing a test file). The brief asked for both; the worker did A only.
- rf2-i3og0: ruled from a skill page's prose without checking the owning spec or the history. Ruling was backwards. Worker refused and filed rf2-lspr9.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS WORTH A STEP: the dispatch preamble ALREADY orders the worker to read by tracker timestamps, at length, with the reasoning. The mayor writes that preamble and then does not do it. So the knowledge is present, written down, and pasted verbatim into every dispatch - what is missing is that nothing makes the mayor execute it before the brief exists. That is the same property the stash ban, the beads-boundary hook and the draft interlock all have and the reason they hold: enforced where it cannot be forgotten.

PROPOSED (small, and it belongs in the existing 'Write the brief in this order' section rather than as a new section): make step one of writing a brief a READ of the item's newest text-bearing mutation plus a fixed-string hold sweep - probes short enough to survive the ~76-column wrap ('NOT DISPATCHABLE', 'AWAITING MIKE', 'OPERATOR CALL'), exercised once against a bead known to carry one, because a zero from a wrong pattern reads exactly like a clean bead. State that a hold banner is the newest field often enough that the Scope section cannot be trusted to mention it.

SEQUENCING - MANDATORY. docs/the-mayor-method/ is SOLE-TOUCHER hot-zone per rf2-ttu8i, never parallel with another method-file bead. PR #8949 (mayor/one-rule-draft-interlock) is open against BOTH method pages right now. Do not dispatch until #8949 merges.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus python -m mkdocs build --strict (exclude_docs does NOT hide the-mayor-method/, verified by a planted-link red on #8949). Run mkdocs as 'python -m mkdocs' - bare mkdocs returns 127 here, which is NO VERDICT rather than a pass.
FIFTH INSTANCE, 2026-09-02, and a DIFFERENT SHAPE worth naming separately — a blanket fence in the brief that the bead had already lifted.

rf2-fmns2 (PR #8954). My brief said: 'Do not touch implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. If a new example build-id is genuinely required, that lives in the hot-zone top-level shadow-cljs.edn, so STOP and report rather than editing it.' The worker edited it anyway and was RIGHT to:

- the item's AC4 requires :examples/login-hicasso to exist and enrol automatically, which is only possible in that file;
- the bead's own TRIAGE NOTE had already anticipated the hot-zone touch and SEQUENCED this task behind rf2-3xq1v (shadow-cljs.edn) and rf2-39rc5 (package.json) - both closed and merged before dispatch;
- it checked every open PR first and found none touching either file.

I verified all three claims after the fact: rf2-3xq1v and rf2-39rc5 both read CLOSED, and a sweep of every open PR's file list found #8954 is the only one touching implementation/shadow-cljs.edn or top-level deps.edn.

WHY THIS SHAPE IS DISTINCT from the four already recorded. Those were the brief carrying STALE instructions - a hold banner not read, a work split not read, a ruling made without checking the owning spec. This one is the brief carrying a fence the mayor invented generically and correctly by default, which the ITEM had already discharged by naming the predecessors that had to land first. A blanket 'do not touch X, STOP and report' is the right default and is WRONG whenever the bead has already sequenced X - and the bead is where that sequencing lives, so the mayor cannot know it without reading the newest layer.

IMPLICATION FOR THE PROPOSED STEP: the newest-mutation read must look for SEQUENCING as well as for holds. A triage note that names predecessors is an authorisation with a precondition, and re-stating a fence over it converts a satisfied precondition back into a blocker - which either strands the work or, as here, costs the worker a justification round it should not have had to write.

Cost this time: nothing, because the worker read the item and overrode the brief. That is five for five on workers catching it, which is the safeguard working and not a reason to keep relying on it.
CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSED REMEDY, 2026-09-02 — the marker sweep I proposed has a FALSE-POSITIVE mode, and I hit it within hours of proposing it. Do not build the step as written.

WHAT HAPPENED. I ran the fixed-string sweep over dispatch candidates and it flagged THIS BEAD as held, carrying both 'AWAITING MIKE' and 'OPERATOR CALL'. I wrote this bead and put no banner on it. The probe was matching (a) my own note QUOTING rf2-y8jjk's banner, and (b) the proposed remedy's own list of probe strings. It also flagged rf2-6c12m, whose text says outright 'its AWAITING MIKE banner is struck, so it is DISPATCHABLE' - the opposite of held.

I then tried to discriminate automatically - active marker vs 'struck' nearby vs a banner attributed to another bead id - and THAT failed too, because the standing banner text itself ends 'WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT', so the word 'struck' appears in every ACTIVE banner as an instruction. rf2-y8jjk, which is definitely held, scored active=2 struck=2. A second instrument, same shape of failure.

THIS IS THE HAZARD THE METHOD ALREADY NAMES, and I walked into it while building a check meant to prevent a different error. loops.md Tracker mechanics: 'An instrument can be RIGHT and still answer a different question from the one you asked... a marker scan finding a banner read as this item is held.' It lists that exact instance. The scan answers 'does this text contain these characters'; the question is 'is this item currently held', and the gap is invisible in the answer.

CONSEQUENCE FOR MY EARLIER REPORT: I told the operator '11 of 27 open beads carry a hold banner'. That number is UNRELIABLE and at least two of the eleven (this bead, rf2-6c12m) are false. Do not carry it forward. The two I can stand behind are reads rather than scans: rf2-y8jjk (a worker read it, refused the dispatch, and quoted the unstruck banner) and rf2-zq34m (I read its banner and its diverged-blockers note directly).

WHAT THE STEP MUST BE INSTEAD. A marker scan is a CANDIDATE FILTER, never a verdict. It narrows 27 items to a handful; the hold is then established by READING each candidate - which is cheap at that size and is the only thing that distinguishes an active banner from one quoted, discussed, or struck. Write the step that way, and write beside it the question the scan actually answers, so the gap is on the page rather than in the reader's head. If a machine-checkable hold is wanted, the durable fix is a STRUCTURED FIELD on the item rather than a marker in prose - but that is a tracker change and a separate decision, not this bead's.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8962, verified on main at commit 2a018d54fd (docs(method): make the newest-mutation read a dispatch step...). Verified by MERGE, not by PR state. Built with the bead's own CORRECTION note governing, not its original proposal: the step reads the item's newest text-bearing mutation for a hold AND for sequencing, and a hold-marker sweep is written as a CANDIDATE FILTER with the hold established by reading each candidate - the question the scan answers stated beside the question being asked. The structured-field idea stayed out of scope. Worker pointed at loops.md Tracker mechanics rather than restating it, and correctly reported that #8958 had landed MORE there than my brief credited.

title: ci(story): the FULL Story feature-load gate is RED, and only arms on a direct-runner change so nothing sees it
notes:
DISCOVERED 2026-09-01 by the mayor, on PR #8941 (rf2-f9f3p).

WHAT HAPPENED. PR #8941 changes exactly two files - .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs - and touches nothing Story-related (verified: 'gh pr diff 8941 --name-only' returns those two paths and zero Story files). Because a change to the classifier script hits its mark_all arm, EVERY surface armed on that PR, including gates that are normally skipped. One of them failed:

  job 'Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)', step 'Run the FULL Story feature-load gate (direct-runner change, rf2-65ajl)'
  https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/actions/runs/33510451794/job/99865809057

The sibling steps in that same job PASSED - the Xray feature browser gate and the Story :script CI-as-test gate both green - so this is not an environment or Playwright-install failure. The step after it, the Story static-export gate, was skipped because this one failed.

THE INFERENCE, AND ITS LIMIT. #8941's diff cannot CAUSE a Story feature-load failure - it changes which gates get scheduled, not what Story does at runtime. So it can only have EXPOSED an existing one. What is NOT yet established is how long it has been red, because the step arms only on a 'direct-runner change' and therefore almost never runs. That is the part to measure rather than assume: find the last run of this step that passed, and what landed between.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE RED. This is the same shape as rf2-cl8mg - a lane whose green means 'did not run' rather than 'passed'. A gate that arms only on changes to the thing it guards cannot catch a regression introduced from anywhere else, and its silence is indistinguishable from success. The narrow arm is what made this invisible; widening it is a cost decision, not an obvious fix.

THE FIX THAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: narrowing the rf2-f9f3p classifier change so the Story gate stops arming. That would make #8941 green by re-hiding the red and would defeat the reverse-edge work outright. If #8941 needs to land before this is fixed, that is a sequencing decision for the mayor, not a reason to weaken the classifier.

At filing the CI run was still in_progress so the step's log was not yet retrievable ('logs will be available when it is complete'); the run also uploaded artefacts under 'Upload failed browser-gate run evidence (rf2-315cf)', which is the place to start.
CORROBORATED 2026-09-01, and the corroboration is decisive: a SECOND PR with a completely unrelated diff fails the identical step.

PR #8943 (worker/cilanes, beads rf2-cl8mg + rf2-ohfym) touches .github/workflows/test.yml, tools/testbed-support, implementation/http and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md - nothing Story. It fails:

  https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/actions/runs/33511492305/job/99869066434

The step listing is identical to #8941's, sibling for sibling: 'Run Xray feature browser gate (PR-smoke)' green, 'Run Story :script CI-as-test gate' green, THIS step red, 'Run the Story static-export gate' skipped because it failed.

WHY THIS SETTLES CAUSE. Both PRs arm every surface - #8941 because a classifier-script change hits mark_all, #8943 because it edits a workflow file - which is why a normally-skipped gate ran on each. But their diffs share no file and neither touches Story. A defect common to both cannot come from either. The gate is red independent of PR content, i.e. red on main-equivalent trees, and has been invisible because it only arms on a direct-runner change.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX WORKER: establishing pre-existence no longer needs a run against origin/main - two independent PRs have established it. Running the gate locally is still the way to get the ACTUAL failure text, which is the thing nobody has yet, because both CI runs were still in_progress when read and GitHub withholds step logs until a run completes ('logs will be available when it is complete'). The run also uploads artefacts under 'Upload failed browser-gate run evidence (rf2-315cf)'.

COST NOW: this single red blocks BOTH #8941 and #8943 from merging. It is no longer one PR's problem.
RESOLVED 2026-09-01 23:35 AUSEST by the rf2-f9f3p fix-worker. Root cause found, fix pushed on `worker/pairedges-f9f3p` (PR #8941, commit `ed141dc167`). The gate is GREEN locally: `npm run test:story-feature-load`, captured exit 1 before the fix, 0 after, same command, same checkout, one file changed between them.

THE FAILURE, verbatim from a local run of the actual gate command (the CI run was still `in_progress` when this bead was filed, so nobody had the text; the job log became retrievable via `gh api repos/day8/re-frame2/actions/jobs/99865809057/logs` even while the run was not):

  FAIL Story browser scenarios (rf2-dczqg): [story-browser-scenario=mid-tier-umbrella-helper-strong-rows-rf2-s75sy] failing-play detail missing source-coord (at <file>:<line>); got: reason: expected 999 at [:count] but got 1
  expected: 999
  actual:   1
  at <checkout>/tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs:438open
  ...
      at <checkout>/tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs:1860:15

  FAIL  Story browser scenarios (rf2-dczqg)

One scenario of one of the gate's two spec modules. Note what the "missing" coord actually is: it is PRESENT and correct — `at .../counter_with_stories/stories.cljs:438` — and the trailing `open` is the open-in-editor chip's own button text, which `innerText()` concatenates. Nothing is broken in the product.

ROOT CAUSE. `tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs:1860` asserted the coord by matching it from its LEADING EDGE:

  /at\s+counter_with_stories\/stories\.cljs:\d+/

That spelling held only while Story's macro emitted the reader's `:file` verbatim, which is the CLASSPATH-RELATIVE portion both compilation hosts hand a macro. `e1cbd089c4` (rf2-3xq1v, "Story's macro source stamp absolutises via core's canonical helper", merged 2026-09-01 21:42 AUSEST) routed `re-frame.story.macros/coords-form` through `re-frame.source-coords/coords-form`, which absolutises at macro-expansion time (rf2-wvsxg). `test_mode/view.cljs`'s detail-source renderer prints `(:file source)` verbatim, so the rendered line became an on-disk path whose prefix is per-machine. The regex's `at\s+` no longer abuts `counter_with_stories`, and it stopped matching. rf2-3xq1v updated the JVM/CLJS pins it knew about (its own commit body says the JVM net "previously PINNED the relative spelling ... and now pins ... absolute") and did not reach this browser-scenario pin, because nothing ran it.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT BRANCH-CAUSED. Confirmed three ways: (1) #8941's diff is two classifier files and zero Story files; (2) the breaking commit is an ancestor of #8941's merge base; (3) PR #8943, disjoint diff, fails the identical step (the mayor's corroboration — which is why no separate `origin/main` gate run was made; the question was already settled).

HOW LONG RED — a bounded answer, ~1.5 hours at the time of the #8941 run. The step last PASSED on PR #8794 (`660423bb74`, rf2-7dewo slice A), run `33344735738`, step conclusion `success`, 2026-08-31 00:37:18–00:42:28 UTC — the most recent PR before this one to touch any of the five paths in `is_story_full_gate_path`. Between that and the red, the only relevant landing is `e1cbd089c4` at 2026-09-01 11:42 UTC. So this is one PR's worth of rot, not a long-standing rotten lane.

THE FIX (one file, `tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs`). Match the classpath-relative TAIL instead of the leading edge:

  /\bat\s+\S*counter_with_stories[\\/]stories\.cljs:\d+/

The tail is what carries the signal the scenario exists to check — the coord names the play's own source file, with a line — and it is stable across hosts. `[\\/]` accepts the Windows separator; the leading `\S*` is optional so a host that cannot resolve a root (in-jar source, synthetic coord) still passes on the relative spelling that path ships verbatim. Exercised against controls, not only against the target: MATCH on the CI absolute, the Windows absolute (both separators) and the legacy relative spelling; NO MATCH on a detail with no coord, a coord with no line number, and a coord naming the wrong file. So the assertion keeps its discriminating power. The absoluteness of the coord is separately pinned by the JVM/CLJS tests rf2-3xq1v added; this scenario is not the place to re-pin it.

THE FENCE WAS HONOURED. The classifier change is untouched and unnarrowed. Verified on the pushed tip: `git diff origin/main...HEAD` on `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` removes exactly one line and replaces it with a strict SUPERSET (the same eight `implementation/{core,ssr,hicasso,adapters/reagent}/{src/*,deps.edn}` patterns plus six more for epoch/schemas/machines). #8903's four MIG-23 roots survive verbatim.

RELATED FAIL-OPEN, RECORDED NOT FIXED — the narrow arm is narrower than this bead says, and in a second place. rf2-3xq1v's three files armed NEITHER Story browser output. Measured with a control:

  tools/story/src/re_frame/story/macros.clj              story_full_gate=false  story_xray_browser=false
  tools/story/test/re_frame/story_open_in_editor_cljs_test.cljs  (both false)
  tools/story/test/re_frame/story_source_coords_test.clj         (both false)
  tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs  [control]  story_full_gate=true
  tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/view.cljs [control] story_xray_browser=true

Identical results from `origin/main`'s copy of the classifier, so this is not something #8941 introduced. The `story_full_gate` half is the narrow arm this bead already describes. The `story_xray_browser` half is a distinct hole: `is_story_xray_runtime_path` guards `tools/{story,xray}/src/**` on extension (`.cljs|.cljc|.js|.cjs|.css|.scss|.html`), which excludes `.clj` — but `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/macros.clj` is the MACRO PRODUCER whose expansion is what the browser renders, and its two sibling predicates `is_story_xray_node_test_path` and `is_story_xray_dom_test_path` BOTH carry a named `macros.clj` exception for exactly that reason (rf2-eyyd2, whose own comment says "Same reasoning arms it on the browser predicate below"). The third predicate did not get it. So a Story macro change fires no Story browser gate of any kind, cheap or full — which is precisely how a change to the source-coord stamp reached main without any browser seeing the pane that renders it. Adding `macros.clj` to `is_story_xray_runtime_path` would be the rf2-eyyd2-shaped completion; left unbuilt here because it is a cost decision on the gate matrix, which this bead already reserves.

The classifier half is complete for the Pair fixture's five declared direct local roots and preserves the pre-existing per-artefact routing. The Story repair, however, still assumes the machine-specific absolute prefix contains no whitespace:
