blob 2ae92d2e08a1b3b198f195a9932eda91ae909d53.
CLJS red: public added to the cljs arm, probe exit 1 naming
re-frame.hicasso/planted-control-public, 113 files recompiled as positive evidence the
runtime saw the plant, restore blob 03ba4a6d8411ff8ac21801fa62f39ded7761b1f0, recompiled
and re-run green.

GATES (runner exit codes, captured on the same command line, re-run on the final rebased
base): gen --check 0 (493 vars); api-md-check 0; story-spec-check 0; xray-spec-check 0;
skills-check 0; doc-guide-check 0; doc-api-check 0 (171 eligible vars have page+member);
clojure -M:test 0 (74 tests, 156 assertions); full CLJS node-test 0 (11149 tests, 54867
assertions); focused probe 0 (4 tests, 44 assertions); check_doc_slugs 0;
check_readme_links --ci 0; mkdocs build --strict 0; check_guide_samples 0.

SCOPE EXPANSION FOR THE MAYOR TO NOTE. Enrolment gave doc-api-check an opinion it never
had: every manifest var at an eligible tier needs a docs/api/NAMESPACE.md page plus a
member heading, and the door had neither. Added docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md as a terse
var index pointing at the existing 631-line docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md rather than
duplicating it, plus an mkdocs nav entry. The :doc-api-coverage-exempt hatch was
deliberately NOT used: it is for a var documented only as a facade pointer elsewhere, and
misusing it would have recreated the exact fail-open shape this item exists to close.

A STALE DISPOSITION OVERTURNED. docs/api/README.md said the door carries no api-manifest
rows and that this is deliberate rather than an oversight. That was rf2-wf1ey of
2026-08-16; this item names rf2-wf1ey and rules past it, so the paragraph described the
opposite of the tree. Rewritten: the DOOR is tracked on both hosts, its OPTIONAL MODULES
still are not.

CURATED AXES, worth a maintainer glance since the item did not rule them: :tier :advanced
throughout (restrictive-by-default per API.md Tier taxonomy, since Hicasso is an opt-in
substrate whose door is not the front-porch set the Guide loads); :owner 004C for the four
root-lifecycle verbs (Roots-and-Mount names this door impl/mount.cljs as its in-tree
realisation) and 006 for the rest.

INCIDENTAL FINDING. docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md said the door has Fifteen names
while its own code block listed fourteen. The manifest now MEASURES it - full completeness
in both directions reconciles against exactly 14 - so the prose was corrected. The
separate Fifteen names at re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted is a different namespace this work
did not measure and was left alone.

ALSO OBSERVED, NOT ACTIONED: gen.clj namespaces-under is a roster-completeness gate with
no consumer anywhere in the repo (dead code since it was written).

No spec/*.md normative document touched. No new CI job. No runtime behaviour change.

title: Xray Trace drops every real FX argument by reading nonexistent singular tags
description:
## Scope

Repair the Dynamic Trace panel's FX target/detail projection in tools/xray. Scope is the raw-trace-to-row seam in day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers and its focused dual-target test. Reconcile the fixture with the framework's shipped FX vocabulary; do not redesign the panel.

## Findings

Correctness finding: target-detail reads :rf.fx/arg and :rf.fx/value, but the framework emits FX arguments under canonical :rf.fx/args. Every real :rf.fx/handled row therefore projects only its fx id, dropping the argument from the main target/detail column and hover title. The existing test is green because it fabricates the nonexistent singular :rf.fx/arg key.

## Evidence

- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:575-579 reads :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1234-1239 emits successful :rf.fx/handled rows with :rf.fx/id and :rf.fx/args. Exception, skipped-platform, and no-such-fx rows use the same plural key at lines 1455-1463, 1583-1601, 1617-1626, and 1651-1660.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_collector.cljs:207-228 snapshots framework rings without renaming tag keys.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:853-884 writes target-detail directly to :target; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:632-639 renders it in the target/detail column and hover title.
- tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:305-309 asserts the promised output using :rf.fx/arg, a shape no framework producer emits.
- tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md:45-51 and line 264 promise fx-id -> arg in that column.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register :app/audit and return {:app/audit {:message "saved"}} from an event handler.
2. Dispatch the event and open Xray's Dynamic Trace panel on that event bundle.
3. Inspect the :rf.fx/handled row. The framework trace carries {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}}, but the target/detail cell and hover title show only :app/audit.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The payload distinguishing one effect invocation from another is absent from the primary diagnostic unless the operator expands raw EDN. When an FX trace row contains canonical :rf.fx/args, projected :target must include that exact value after pr-str-safe; when the key is absent, the row stays id-only. Key presence, not truthiness, is the distinction because false and nil are valid effect arguments.

## Recommended Action

Make the FX branch read canonical :rf.fx/args and distinguish an absent key from present false/nil with contains? or an equivalent sentinel. Replace the singular-key fixture with producer-shaped tags. Keep the id-only fallback for rows that genuinely omit arguments.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused test passes a producer-shaped :rf.fx/handled event with {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}} through target-detail or project-row and asserts :app/audit -> {:message "saved"}. The fixture explicitly contains neither singular key; this non-vacuity check fails on the current implementation.
2. The same table proves present false and present nil render as -> false and -> nil, while a control row with no :rf.fx/args renders only :app/audit. This pins key presence rather than a truthiness shortcut.
3. No production Xray code or focused test relies on the nonexistent singular FX argument tags.
4. From tools/xray, clojure -M:test -n day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers-cljs-test passes, and the CLJS node-test lane containing the same .cljc namespace passes.

## Non-goals

- No Trace layout, expansion, filtering, stage, or colour changes.
- No framework trace-schema change and no compatibility aliases for invented singular keys.
- No broad audit of other op families or historical fixture cleanup.
- No work on the separate Xray runtime retirement tracked by rf2-7htk7.

## Related / duplicate search

title: flows: tag output-path write failures instead of blaming :derive
description:
## Scope

The flow evaluation boundary in `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc`, plus the router's consumer-side error record and focused CLJ/CLJS tests. This is about attribution of an actual pre-install failure, not broader output-path validation.

## Correctness finding

`evaluate-flow!` catches the whole recompute/install block as though it were the application `:derive` callback. A derive function can return normally and the later `assoc-in` can throw because the pending app-db has a container incompatible with the declared output path. The runtime then emits `:rf.flow/failed` and `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` with the actionable message "a flow's :derive fn threw" and "Fix the :derive fn". That attribution is false: the framework output write failed after derive completed.

The error contract must distinguish the phase that failed. Otherwise local diagnostics and the always-on production error record send a programmer to working code and conceal the output-path/container mismatch that caused the event to abort.

## Evidence

- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:172` opens one `try` before `(apply (:derive flow) new-inputs)` at line 174.
- The same `try` covers `(assoc-in db (:output-path flow) new-output)` at line 184, the dirty-cache write, debug trace construction, and output-schema observation through line 208.
- Its catch at lines 209-236 unconditionally emits `:rf.flow/failed`, throws `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception`, says the `:derive` function threw, and tells the programmer to fix it.
- Registration validates only that `:output-path` is a non-empty vector of legal concrete segments (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:269-272,315-326`). Correctly, it cannot prove the shape of a future pending app-db container.
- The public contract describes `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` and `:rf.flow/failed` as derive-throw signals (`docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:249,271`; `spec/013-Flows.md` failure semantics). No focused flow test drives a successful derive followed by an output install throw.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a frame at `{:source 1 :items []}`.
2. Register flow `:flow/output-write` with input `[:source]`, output path `[:items :total]`, and a derive function that records its call and returns `42`.
3. Dispatch one event so the first flow pass runs.
4. Observe that derive returned, then Clojure/ClojureScript `assoc-in` attempts to associate keyword `:total` into the vector at `:items` and throws.
5. Observe that the event correctly aborts, but the emitted failure says the derive function threw and instructs the programmer to fix derive.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The declaration passes path validation because every segment is legal. Atomicity is preserved (the event does not commit), but both the dev trace and production error surface blame the completed derive callback and omit the failing output-write phase.

Invariant: every typed failure and recovery instruction must name the component/phase that actually threw. A framework output installation failure must not be represented as an application derive throw.

## Recommended minimal fix

Split the authored callback invocation from framework output installation in `evaluate-flow!`. Keep the existing derive-throw behavior, but classify/tag an `assoc-in` failure as `:output-write` (with flow id and declared output path) and give it an honest reason. Thread that structural phase through `:rf.flow/failed` and the router's always-on record. Reuse `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` if it remains the aggregate flow-evaluation category; a new public error id is not required if the phase and message are unambiguous. Preserve the existing exact-owner fence and pass-level dirty-cache/vacation rollback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused CLJ test and its CLJS counterpart install `{:source 1 :items []}`, register the `[:items :total]` flow above, and dispatch one drain. A non-vacuity counter proves derive ran exactly once and returned before failure. The committed app-db remains unchanged.
- The captured `:rf.flow/failed` trace and always-on error record identify flow `:flow/output-write`, identify phase `:output-write`, and do not claim or advise that `:derive` threw. The structural output path is available in the thrown diagnostic or dev trace.
- A negative control makes derive itself throw before output installation. It still produces the existing `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` contract with phase `:derive`, flow attribution, atomic abort, and no output-write attribution.
- A positive control uses the same derive and `[:items :total]` output path with `:items {}`. It commits `42`, advances dirty-check state, and emits no failure.
- The tests assert the always-on record, not only a debug trace, so production attribution cannot silently remain wrong; the existing flow atomicity/conformance tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not reject legal output paths at registration based on the current app-db shape; that shape can change before evaluation.
- Do not change event atomicity, retry/dirty-cache behavior, path segment grammar, schema observation, or output vacation semantics.
- Do not add defensive validation for arbitrary application data or redesign the flow error catalogue.
- Do not address dynamic registration/clear settling; `rf2-kh73v` already owns that distinct lifecycle behavior.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all statuses by title and full tracker text for `flow`, `flow-eval`, `derive throw`, `assoc-in`, `output write`, and `output path`. No issue owns output-write failure attribution. `rf2-kh73v` is the open dynamic-toggle settling task and is distinct. Other matches concern unrelated schema, CI, Hicasso, or trace-catalogue work. Source history/tests cover derive throws and vector-index vacation, but not this successful-derive/output-install failure boundary.
notes:
## Implemented — PR #8863 (2026-09-01 12:40:52 AUSEST)

Premise verified at source before building: `evaluate-flow!` really did open ONE `try` before the derive call and close it after the install (line numbers had drifted ~4 from the bead's — the try is at 176, not 172 — but the structure is exactly as described). A fixed-string census for `output-write` across the tracked tree returned only the bead's own row in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, so no repair already existed at tip; the census was run once against a string known to be present as a control.

### The split
Structural, not message inspection. The authored `:derive` call sits in its own `try` returning a one-key marker map (`::output` / `::thrown`); the framework install — `assoc-in`, the `last-inputs` write, the `:rf.flow/computed` trace, schema observation — sits in a second `try`. An install failure is therefore unreachable from the derive handler. A new private `flow-eval-failure!` takes the phase as an argument and threads it to:

- `:rf.flow/failed` trace tags: `:phase` + `:path` (the declared output path; `:path` is the spelling `:rf.flow/computed` already uses)
- thrown ex-data: `:rf.flow/failed-phase`, `:rf.flow/output-path` (beside the existing `:rf.flow/failed-id` / `:cause`)
- the always-on error record: top-level `:phase`, lifted off the ex-data by the router's `emit-flow-eval-exception!`

`:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` stays the aggregate category — no new public error id. The derive-throw message is preserved verbatim; the exact-owner fence, pass-level dirty-cache rollback, path grammar, schema observation and event atomicity are untouched. Nothing was added to registration-time validation (bead non-goal).

### Acceptance criteria
All five met. New `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_output_write_attribution_cljs_test.cljc` — one `.cljc` so the JVM runner and the shadow `:node-test` build (ns-regexp `cljs-test$`) both run it, giving the CLJ test and its CLJS counterpart in one file. Three tests: the repro (derive-call counter proves derive ran once and RETURNED; app-db unchanged; `:phase :output-write` on trace, on the always-on record, on that record with `:exception` dissoc'd, and on the ex-data; message neither claims nor advises `:derive`), the derive-throw negative control (`:phase :derive`, wording preserved verbatim, no output-write attribution), and the legal-write positive control (`:items {}` commits 42 and a second value-equal drain skips, proving dirty-check state advanced).

### No test pinned the wrong attribution
Searched: none exists — every other `:rf.flow/failed` test throws from inside `:derive`, and `flows_vector_parent_vacation_test.clj` covers vector INDICES, which are a legal write. So nothing was flipped or renamed. One test was EXTENDED: `flows-trace-test/flow-eval-exception-routes-through-error-emit-substrate` pins the always-on record's exact key set tree-wide (the only such pin), which now gains `:phase`; its scenario is a genuine derive throw so it asserts `:phase :derive`.

### Gates
`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`, foreground, exit captured in the same shell:
- green on the committed bytes: 244 tests / 6087 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0
- RED against the pre-repair sources (both files at merge base `d2688dd381`, tests kept): same 244/6087, 14 failures, 0 errors, exit 1 — the red is also what proves the gate read the worker worktree, since the test file exists nowhere else
- RED on a one-line revert (`:output-write` → `:derive` at the install catch's call site): 7 failures, exit 1, controls still green
- both restores verified by git BLOB hash against the committed objects, not by reading a diff
- both `.cljc` files reader-checked under `#{:clj}` and `#{:cljs}`, exit 0; the reader-check exercised once against an unclosed `#?(:cljs` form, which returned exit 1

CLJS lane reliance declared in the PR body: the `cljs-*` node-test jobs in `.github/workflows/test.yml` cover `implementation/flows/{src,test}`.

### Out of scope, filed
`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/013-Flows.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md` and `docs/core/flows.md` still describe both signals as derive-throw signals. `spec/` is hot-zone and outside this bead's stated scope, so nothing there was edited — filed as **rf2-ywdvp** (P2, dispatch alone).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8863 (branch worker/flows-attrib-gpj9r, head 38b499c0a529e82fa2b61be846267921a4819ba6). evaluate-flow! now splits the authored :derive call and the framework output install into separate try forms, so an assoc-in write failure is structurally unreachable from the derive handler; the failing phase (:derive / :output-write) rides the :rf.flow/failed trace, the thrown ex-data (:rf.flow/failed-phase, :rf.flow/output-path) and the always-on error record's :phase slot. New flows_output_write_attribution_cljs_test.cljc covers the repro plus derive-throw and legal-write controls on both hosts; flows JVM suite 244 tests / 6087 assertions green (exit 0), red 14 against pre-repair sources and red 7 on a one-line revert. Spec/docs catalogue rows are hot-zone and out of this bead's scope — filed as rf2-ywdvp.

title: http: abort during body preparation can still issue the JVM request
description:
## Scope

The managed HTTP request lifecycle in `implementation/http`, specifically the boundary from body-thunk realization / encoding to the JVM `HttpClient.sendAsync` call. Cover the shared CLJC lifecycle only as needed to keep its cancellation semantics coherent; keep the public API unchanged.

## Correctness finding

An abort can win while `run-attempt!` is blocked in the managed request-preparation phase, deliver the canonical cancelled reply, and clear the in-flight registry, yet the same attempt proceeds to call `jvm-fetch` after preparation returns. On the real JVM adapter that call invokes `HttpClient.sendAsync`, so a side-effecting request can begin after the framework has told the app it was cancelled.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1810-1825` checks `@finalised?` only before `prepare-body!`; a body thunk may block inside that call. The successful-preparation branch then enters the host transport with no second cancellation check (`cljs-fetch` at 1827; `jvm-fetch` at 1884).
- The abort closure at `transport.cljc:1658-1718` flips `aborted?`, wins `finalised?`, clears the registry, and dispatches the aborted outcome. During preparation the JVM `cf-holder` is still nil, so it has no future to cancel.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:285-290` calls `HttpClient.sendAsync` synchronously inside `jvm-fetch`; the returned future is not published to `cf-holder` until `transport.cljc:1911`, after the request has already been issued.
- Deterministic no-network probe at `dba7835137e7`: run `run-attempt!` on a future with a body thunk held by a promise; wait for thunk entry; call `registry/abort-in-flight!`; then release the thunk while `jvm-fetch` is redefined to increment a counter. Observed `:registered-before-abort true`, `:abort-result true`, `:fetch-calls 1`, `:registered-after false` (process exit 0). The cancellation succeeded observably, but transport issuance still followed it.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_body_prep_failure_test.clj` covers prep throws, encoding failures, and prep retry, but no abort during preparation. `http_abort_retry_race_test.clj` covers retry/backoff handoffs, not the preparation-to-send handoff.
- Spec 014 says body realization is a managed phase that respects abort precedence (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:218`) and that a cancelled request must not issue a fresh attempt (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:491-499`). The user guide calls manual abort an explicit “stop now” (`docs/async/http.md:306-316`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a JVM `run-attempt!` context with a stable `:request-id` and a `:body` thunk that signals entry, then waits on a latch/promise.
2. Start the attempt on another thread and wait for the thunk-entry signal, proving preparation is in progress and the handle is registered.
3. Call `registry/abort-in-flight!` for that id and require it to return true; verify the registry slot is gone.
4. Release the thunk. Instrument or redefine `transport-jvm/jvm-fetch` with a call counter.
5. Current result: the counter becomes 1 even though abort completed before body preparation returned. As a non-vacuity control, omit the abort and observe the same harness call the transport once.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A JVM/SSR app lazily materializes a large upload or signed POST body in a thunk. While that work is running, the user cancels, a resource owner releases, an actor is destroyed, or the frame is torn down. The app receives cancellation (or stale suppression) and the registry reports no live work, but the POST starts afterward and may commit server-side.

Invariant: once an abort has completed before host transport issuance begins, that attempt must never subsequently call the host transport. If issuance wins first, the future must be published before the abort returns so the abort path can cancel it. Exactly one terminal outcome remains observable.

## Recommended minimal fix

Extend the existing cancellation-safe handoff through request preparation and JVM future publication. Re-check the shared `aborted?` / `finalised?` state immediately after successful preparation and skip host transport when cancellation already won. On the JVM, serialize the tiny check → `sendAsync` → `cf-holder` publication region with the abort path (or an equivalent one-cell phase CAS) so there is no residual check-to-send window: abort-before-send suppresses issuance; send-before-abort publishes the cancellable future before abort completes. Apply the shared post-prep guard to CLJS as well for a re-entrant external abort fired by body realization. Reuse the current abort closure, reply CAS, registry cleanup, and reply shapes; add no public surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic JVM regression test uses latches/promises, not timing sleeps, to hold a body thunk in preparation; an abort that returns true before release yields zero `jvm-fetch` / `sendAsync` calls, exactly one canonical `:status :cancelled` reply for manual abort (or the existing suppression outcome for lifecycle abort), and an empty registry.
- The same test fails against the pre-fix implementation by observing one host-transport call after abort.
- Non-vacuity control: the identical harness without abort invokes the host transport exactly once and completes normally, proving the test did not merely disable the send branch or fail before preparation.
- A deterministic handoff control covers the opposite ordering: when JVM issuance wins, the future is published/cancellable before abort completes; abort cancels it and still produces no double reply.
- A focused CLJS regression covers a synchronously/re-entrantly fired external signal during body-thunk realization, or the implementation demonstrates why the shared post-prep guard is host-neutral; no Fetch call occurs after that abort.
- Existing body-preparation failure/retry tests, abort-precedence tests, and abort/retry handoff tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Interrupting or forcibly terminating arbitrary user body-thunk code already running.
- Expanding `:timeout-ms` semantics to govern body-preparation duration.
- Undoing a request after the server has already received it, stronger delivery guarantees, or transactional HTTP.
- New cancellation APIs, new failure categories, compatibility aliases, or broader transport refactoring.

## Related / duplicate search

Scanned all 1,109 current all-status beads via `bd list --all -n 0`, then searched titles, descriptions, and notes for HTTP, managed abort, body thunk, request preparation / `request-prep`, abort precedence, `jvm-fetch`, cancelled request, and fresh attempt. No bead covers this preparation-to-send cancellation hole. The only current HTTP surface-review bead, `rf2-lddbk`, concerns successful response metadata and is distinct. The sole in-progress bead, `rf2-jui1c`, is an unrelated prose sweep and remains untouched. Historical source/test references `rf2-065xo` (managed prep failures) and `rf2-6nczv9` (retry/backoff cancellation handoffs); neither current tracker record exists, and their shipped tests do not cover abort during body preparation.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8842 (2026-09-01): The post-body-prep gate fixes the named held-thunk ordering, but the required JVM issuance handoff remains incorrect. transport.cljc:1909 CASes issue-phase to :issued before any host side effect; the test seam at :issue/before-send (1910) can then run abort synchronously. That abort returns true, wins finalised?, dispatches the canonical cancelled reply, and clears the registry while cf-holder is still nil. Execution then continues to jvm-fetch/sendAsync at 1969 and only publishes/cancels the future at 1996-2012. A cancel after sendAsync cannot prevent a side-effecting POST from reaching the server, so the framework can still issue the request after abort completed and told the app it was cancelled. The new residual-window test codifies the defect by requiring fetch-calls = 1; it contradicts this bead's invariant/acceptance that, when issuance wins, the cancellable future is published before abort returns. Narrow fix: handshake or serialize actual host entry + future publication with abort (or let an abort before the actual call win and suppress it), and make the deterministic test prove no send occurs after abort completion rather than blessing post-abort send-then-cancel.
AUDIT RESIDUAL REPAIRED — PR #8859 (2026-09-01 12:1x AUSEST). The audit's structural claim held at trunk tip f902e800cc, re-verified in the worktree: the CAS to :issued sat ~60 lines above the jvm-fetch/sendAsync call and ~90 above the cf-holder publication, so an abort in that window lost the cell (could not suppress the send), found cf-holder nil (had nothing to cancel), and completed anyway — registry cleared and canonical cancelled reply delivered — after which the request was issued.

Design chosen: the audit's FIRST shape (serialize host entry + future publication with abort), not the second. The second shape alone — let an abort before the actual call win and suppress it — only shrinks the window: moving the CAS adjacent to the call still leaves a concurrent abort losing the CAS with nothing published to cancel, which is the same defect one step smaller. The bead's invariant ('if issuance wins first, the future must be published before the abort returns') is a mutual-exclusion statement, and only a handshake can make it true. So: the commit CAS is now the first act inside each host's own entry region, and on the JVM that region — CAS, jvm-fetch, reset! cf-holder — is held under a new per-attempt monitor issue-lock that the abort closure's cancel step also takes. Abort-first wins the cell and nothing is sent; abort-during cannot complete (it parks before its cancel step, so registry clear and reply follow the region) and finds the future published. The dead post-publication residual re-check is removed. No app code runs inside the monitor: .whenComplete, clear-in-flight! and dispatch-aborted! are all outside it.

CLJS production semantics are unchanged and need no monitor — single-threaded host, CAS immediately before cljs-fetch, so the only interleaving that host can produce (re-entrant external abort during body realization) is still ordered by the cell; the existing test (3) drives that ordering through the JVM's copy. No public API change, no spec edit: Spec 014 :218/:414/:493-497 already mandate the fixed behaviour and nowhere bless send-then-cancel (checked at source).

The defect-blessing test was FLIPPED and RENAMED, not deleted: abort-in-residual-publish-window-still-cancels-future (asserted fetch-calls = 1 after a completed abort) is now abort-completing-at-issuance-boundary-issues-no-request (asserts ZERO fetch calls and that no future was ever created). New sibling concurrent-abort-cannot-complete-while-host-call-is-in-flight covers the opposite ordering as a live handshake: the jvm-fetch stub runs inside the region, starts a competing abort, observes it reach BLOCKED on the monitor, and samples registry+replies while it is parked (both prove the abort had not completed).

Gates from implementation/http, foreground, exit captured in the same shell: full clojure -M:test exit 0, 508 tests / 3881 assertions, 0 failures. Non-vacuity control — the same namespace against the pre-fix transport.cljc restored from the merge base — exit 1 with exactly the audit's four failures (fetch-calls 1 not 0; a CompletableFuture completed exceptionally by CancellationException where none should exist; observed-blocked false; registry ALREADY EMPTY while sendAsync ran). Source restored from HEAD and verified by git blob hash e19f173c53f4da288efcde8142758bc23ede7710 against the committed object, git status clean. Heavy CLJS/browser lanes are CI's; the file was reader-checked under both :clj and :cljs feature sets.
(Correction to the note above: the placeholder '12:1x AUSEST' should read 2026-09-01 12:11 AUSEST, the time PR #8859 was opened. Timestamp only; nothing else in that note changes.)
close_reason: Audit residual repaired in PR #8859 (branch worker/http-issuance-rsv2n), which builds on the original fix in PR #8842. The premature issuance commit is gone: the issue-phase CAS is now the first act inside each host's own entry region, and on the JVM that region — CAS, jvm-fetch/sendAsync, cf-holder publication — is serialized against the abort closure's cancel step by a per-attempt monitor, so an abort either wins the cell before any host call (nothing is sent) or cannot complete until the future it will cancel has been published. The dead post-publication residual re-check is removed. The test that codified the defect by requiring fetch-calls = 1 after a completed abort was flipped and renamed (abort-in-residual-publish-window-still-cancels-future -> abort-completing-at-issuance-boundary-issues-no-request, now asserting zero host calls), with a new concurrent handshake control proving the abort blocks. Full implementation/http JVM suite exit 0 at 508 tests / 3881 assertions; the flipped pair fails 4 assertions against the pre-fix source. No public API change and no spec edit — Spec 014 already mandates the fixed behaviour.

title: surface-review(routing): make component URL encoding host-identical
description:
## Scope

Correct component emission in `implementation/routing` so the pure `route-url` prism and every consumer of it produce one canonical URL on JVM and CLJS. Cover the encoder plus focused cross-host route/link tests; keep routing grammar and URL strategies unchanged.

## Correctness finding

`re-frame.routing.url/url-encode` promises `encodeURIComponent` semantics on both hosts, but its JVM implementation is `java.net.URLEncoder` with only the space-to-`%20` difference repaired. `URLEncoder` also escapes `!`, apostrophe, `(`, `)`, and `~`; JavaScript `encodeURIComponent` leaves those characters literal. Thus identical valid route data produces different URL bytes on server and browser.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `implementation/routing`, evaluate production `url-encode` on the JVM for character codes 33, 39, 40, 41, and 126; it returns `%21 %27 %28 %29 %7E`. Evaluate JavaScript `encodeURIComponent` for those same characters (the exact function called by the CLJS arm); it returns the literal characters. Then register `:probe` at `/p/:slug` and call production `route-url` with `{:to :probe :params {:slug "~"} :query {"!" "()"} :fragment "~!"}`: JVM returns `/p/%7E?%21=%28%29#%7E%21`, while the CLJS implementation emits `/p/~?!=()#~!`.

## Evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url.cljc:36-43` documents `encodeURIComponent` semantics, then uses `URLEncoder` plus only `+` -> `%20` on CLJ and native `encodeURIComponent` on CLJS.
- The executable probes above exercise production code, not a reimplementation.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1477-1480,2240-2245,2251-2271` routes ordinary path captures, query keys/values, and fragments through this encoder. `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:142,511-513` makes both route-link doors consume that `route-url` result.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:724-725` requires component-wise `encodeURIComponent` emission and a pure host-symmetric route prism. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc:66-88` uses only `x` and `comments`, so its shared JVM/CLJS table does not exercise the divergent boundary characters.
- `docs/ssr/head.md:26` shows `route-url` as the canonical-link source, making the host-dependent bytes visible beyond click handling.

## Failure scenario / invariant

For a legitimate article slug such as `draft~1`, SSR emits `/articles/draft%7E1` while the hydrated client emits `/articles/draft~1`. Route-link's `:href`, canonical head links, copied URLs, cache keys, and snapshots therefore depend on the rendering host; the first client tree can also disagree with the server tree at the href attribute. Both spellings may decode to the same route, but that does not satisfy the stronger promised invariant: identical route data has one host-independent canonical URL byte string.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the CLJ arm implement the exact unescaped character set of `encodeURIComponent`. A small normalization of the five additional `URLEncoder` escapes (`%21`, `%27`, `%28`, `%29`, `%7E`) is sufficient; `*`, `-`, `.`, and `_` already agree. Pin the boundary with one shared CLJC character table and extend the existing production route-link parity table with a punctuation-bearing address. Keep decode behavior and the literal-`+` rule intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A shared CLJC test asserts identical literal outputs for the complete `encodeURIComponent` unescaped boundary, including `! * apostrophe ( ) - . _ ~`, on JVM and CLJS.
- The same test includes controls that must remain escaped: space as `%20`, `/` as `%2F`, and `%` as `%25`; it cannot pass by disabling encoding.
- A production `route-url` case exercises punctuation in an ordinary path param, query key, query value, and fragment and asserts the same literal expected URL on both hosts, plus exact `match-url(route-url(address))` recovery.
- The existing cross-host route-link parity suite includes a punctuation-bearing address and proves the JVM SSR render and first CLJS render emit the same `:href` under the default strategy.
- Reverting the CLJ encoder to `URLEncoder` plus only the `+`/`%20` swap makes at least the JVM boundary case and production URL/link parity case red while the escaped-character controls remain meaningful.
- Focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to route patterns, matching/ranking, schemas/coercion, URL-strategy composition, history effects, or decoding.
- No dual canonical spelling, compatibility mode, new public API, general URI abstraction, or broad encoder dependency.
- No speculative normalization of inbound URLs; this fixes deterministic emission only.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched all tracker statuses for `encodeURIComponent`, `URLEncoder`, `percent encoding`, `percent-encoding`, `host parity`, `hydration href`, `canonical URL`, `punctuation`, and `url-encode`; no matching open or in-progress issue exists. The sole in-progress bead is unrelated. Closed `rf2-skr1c` fixed whether server link rendering consults a frame's pure URL-strategy encoder and explicitly left `route-url` unchanged; this finding is the lower-level component encoder and reproduces under the default strategy, so it is not a duplicate.

title: SSR Form-2 arity parity still diverges for missing arguments
description:
## Scope Correct the JVM Form-2 callable-head invocation in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc`, with focused coverage for both public consumers of the shared helper: synchronous `emit-element` / `render-to-string` and `re-frame.ssr.streaming/render-shell`. Keep the supported Form-2 surface and its CLJS argument semantics; no renderer redesign. ## Correctness finding `invoke-form-2-render-fn` uses `try (apply inner args) (catch ArityException _ (inner))` as arity detection. That catch encloses execution of programmer code, so it cannot distinguish an invocation-arity mismatch from an `ArityException` raised inside a correctly-invoked inner render. It therefore invokes that inner a second time and replaces the original failure. The fallback also handles only zero args: an inner that accepts a non-zero prefix of the outer props is valid under the CLJS/JavaScript extra-argument semantics the helper explicitly promises, but JVM SSR tries all args and then zero, rejecting it. Both the synchronous emitter and streaming shell walker call `resolve-component-head`, so the defect affects both server paths. ## Evidence - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:380-394` states that lower-arity Form-2 inners are tolerated, but catches every `clojure.lang.ArityException` from the full invocation and blindly retries at arity zero. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:396-435` routes every fn-returning-fn component through that helper. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:502-517` reuses `resolve-component-head`, so streaming inherits the same behavior. - `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_emit_test.clj:862-878` covers only the two endpoints (same arity and zero arity); it has no partial-arity row and no inner-body `ArityException` control. - An in-memory JVM probe against the current artefact produced: :same-control

kept

:zero-control

kept

:partial-error clojure.lang.ArityException Wrong number of args (0) passed to: .../partial.../fn... :internal-error clojure.lang.ArityException Wrong number of args (0) passed to: .../internal.../fn... :inner-calls 2 The partial case used an outer `(fn [kept ignored] ...)` returning `(fn [kept] [:p kept])`. The internal-error case used a valid zero-arity inner with an invocation counter and a nested wrong-arity call; the counter reached 2, proving the catch re-entered programmer code. Same-arity and zero-arity controls prove the probe reached the live Form-2 path. ## Failure scenario/invariant A shared `.cljc` Form-2 component accepts two props in its outer function but its inner render needs only the first. The client calls the one-argument inner with two JavaScript arguments and ignores the extra prop. JVM SSR first calls it with two arguments, catches that call-site mismatch, then calls it with zero and throws. The same application consequently renders in the browser but fails both synchronous and streaming SSR. Separately, a correctly-invoked inner render can encounter an ordinary wrong-arity bug in a helper it calls. JVM SSR catches that user-body exception as though the renderer selected the wrong arity, invokes the render body again, duplicates its work, and surfaces the retry's exception rather than the original failure. Invariant: Form-2 arity adaptation chooses a compatible call shape before programmer code runs. One render attempt invokes the inner exactly once; any exception raised after entry propagates unchanged. JVM SSR accepts the same fixed-arity-prefix behavior as the client, and sync/streaming agree because they share one resolver. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Require `re-frame.ssr.emit` and define `(fn [kept ignored] (fn [kept] [:p kept]))`. 2. Call `emit-element` on `[component "kept" "ignored"]`; observe an `ArityException` reporting the zero-argument retry instead of `

kept

`. 3. Define a zero-arity inner that increments an atom and then makes a nested wrong-arity call. 4. Render it once; observe the atom is 2, proving the renderer caught the body exception and invoked programmer code again. 5. Run the same component through `re-frame.ssr.streaming/render-shell`; it reaches the same shared resolver and reproduces both outcomes. ## Recommended minimal fix Replace exception-driven probing with one explicit JVM arity-selection step in the shared helper. Select the compatible fixed/variadic invocation shape before calling the inner (full args when accepted; otherwise the longest accepted prefix, including the established zero-arity closure form), then invoke exactly once. Do not catch `ArityException` around the render body. Keep the CLJS branch and the single Form-2 unwrap unchanged. Add the missing focused rows to the existing emitter test block; the streaming assertions should exercise the same shared helper rather than introduce a second adaptation implementation. ## Acceptance Criteria - A fixed-arity regression defines a two-argument outer returning a one-argument inner, renders `[component "kept" "ignored"]`, and asserts `

kept

` through both `emit/emit-element` and `streaming/render-shell`. - Non-vacuity: that one-argument-inner regression is fixed-arity (not variadic) and is demonstrated red on the current implementation, whose zero-arity retry throws. It must assert the exact rendered bytes on both paths so skipping component resolution cannot pass. - An inner-body regression increments a counter and then triggers an `ArityException` from a nested helper call. Each sync and streaming invocation propagates the original body failure and leaves its per-invocation counter at exactly 1; the current implementation reaches 2 for a zero-arity inner, so the control detects the old catch-and-retry behavior. - Existing same-arity and zero-arity Form-2 controls remain green through both sync and streaming paths. - A variadic inner receives the complete original argument sequence once, preserving ordinary Reagent/CLJS semantics. - `resolve-component-head` retains one Form-2 unwrap and the existing `:rf.error/ssr-nonrenderable-component` failure for a still-function result. - The focused SSR JVM test namespace and the artefact's normal SSR test gate pass. ## Non-goals - Form-3 lifecycle support or client-adapter changes. - Multiple recursive Form-2 unwraps. - Catching, translating, or recovering from exceptions thrown by programmer render code. - A new component protocol, renderer registry, or compatibility layer. - Preserving the accidental double-invocation behavior. ## Related/duplicate search Searched all bead states by `Form-2`, `arity`, `ArityException`, `inner render`, `invoke-form-2-render-fn`, `ssr-nonrenderable-component`, `invoked twice`, `partial-arity`, and `SSR emitter`. No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead owns this finding. - The source/tests cite historical `rf2-dtza9a` for adding the single Form-2 unwrap, but that id is not present in the current tracker and the landed tests cover only same-arity and zero-arity success; they do not cover this arity-selection defect. - `rf2-08hx1` is the distinct open reagent-slim Form-3 lifecycle argument-forwarding bug; it does not touch SSR, Form-2, or this helper. - `rf2-8arzr` is the distinct open Node-renderer-to-Ring integration feature; it does not own JVM callable-head semantics.

- Cross-host coverage includes a single fixed-arity inner invoked with fewer args and a fixed+variadic inner invoked below its required count.
- The supported Form-2 arity contract is stated truthfully and consistently in helper docs/tests; it does not claim full CLJS parity while these calls differ.
- If shared `.cljc` Form-2 parity remains the contract, both cases have the same observable render/rejection outcome on JVM and real CLJS, while exact, excess-argument, single-invocation, and exception-propagation controls remain green.
- The repair stays inside the existing arity helper/test surface; no renderer abstraction or compatibility layer.

## Verdict (rf2-mocn3) — PR #8883 FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, both defects, and fixed. Line citations held exactly at tip 77d6ecbbaa: invoke-form-2-render-fn at emit.cljc:380-394, resolve-component-head at :396, streaming reuse at streaming.cljc:513/517. Only the test citation drifted — the Form-2 block is 867-897, not 862-878. REPAIR. Detect arity, do not catch it. A compiled JVM fn's accepted arities are inspectable: one `invoke` method per declared FIXED arity off (.getDeclaredMethods (class f)), plus clojure.lang.RestFn/getRequiredArity for a VARIADIC tail. Selection is then the full arg count when accepted, else the longest accepted prefix (zero included), invoked exactly once. No programmer code runs inside a catch. Where the inner declares no compatible arity there is no shape to choose, so (apply inner args) lets the inner's own ArityException report the REAL call — strictly better than the old fabricated zero-arity retry, and it widens nothing. ARITY INSPECTION VERIFIED FOR EVERY SHAPE THIS HELPER RECEIVES, by probe before committing to the approach. Fixed, multi-arity and prefix shapes read exactly. Both halves of the inspection are load-bearing: (fn [& xs] ...) declares NO invoke method (fixed=#{}, required=0), and (fn [a & xs] ...) reports required=1 — so "accepts any arity" is correctly never read as "accepts zero", which is the precise confusion that let the old zero-arity retry SUCCEED on a variadic inner. Mixed (fn ([a] ...) ([a b & r] ...)) reads fixed=#{1} + required=2, the correct union. VARS NEVER REACH THE HELPER, and this matters more than it looks. resolve-component-head guards on (fn? resolved); (fn? #'v) is FALSE (a Var is ifn?, not fn?), as are keywords, maps, sets, vectors and multimethods. So the helper only ever sees clojure.lang.Fn. Load-bearing because clojure.lang.Var declares invoke for arities 0-21 regardless of what it holds — inspecting one would answer "yes" to every arity. Documented on accepts-arity? so the guard is not silently removed later. BOTH PUBLIC CONSUMERS COVERED. emit/emit-element and streaming/render-shell share one resolver, so every new row asserts through BOTH, on exact rendered bytes where it renders. DOUBLE INVOCATION MADE OBSERVABLE by a counting inner — the exception is identical with and without the retry, so only the count discriminates. THE SABOTAGE RUN CAUGHT A DEFECT IN THE CONTROL ITSELF, which is the main thing worth carrying forward. The first double-invocation row used a zero-arity inner under a ONE-arg component: the old (apply inner args) threw on the INVOCATION before ever entering the render body, the catch then re-invoked at arity zero, the body ran for the FIRST time, and the counter finished at 1. The row was green against exactly the defect it existed to detect, and it would have shipped as proof. For the catch-and-retry to bite, the inner's arity must MATCH ON THE FIRST CALL so the body is genuinely re-entered. Reshaped to a zero-arity inner with zero args (unrepaired helper reaches 2), plus a companion same-arity row discriminating on the arg count in the message, which is what the counter cannot express. GATES. Covering gate derived from .github/workflows/test.yml job `jvm-ssr` (clojure -M:test, working-directory implementation/ssr, gated on implementation_jvm); ssr's JVM-lane tests are .clj, and the change is inside the #?(:clj) arm, so the CLJS arm is untouched. Captured exit codes: run 3 fix + controls exit 0 603 tests / 2943 assertions run 4 SABOTAGE (helper reverted) exit 1 6 failures, 2 errors run 5 final rebased base exit 0 603 tests / 2943 assertions Sabotage red on all three defect rows, both paths each: partial-arity threw "Wrong number of args (0) passed to: ...form2-partial.../fn..." (reproducing the finding's :partial-error verbatim in shape); the counter read (not (= 1 2)) (the finding's :inner-calls 2); the variadic row returned HTML where the render had FAILED (actual: nil for thrown?). Namespace/assertion counts identical across green and sabotage (603/2943), so the plant failed rows rather than crashing a lane. Plant applied and reverted by git BLOB hash: 4098f07bf9799b30c7eba719d60c4178c2d0f923 before, 72b406e69fee7c41446b8a201f46b634f7c91710 planted, restored equal to the committed object. Re-run after the rebase rather than resting on the pre-rebase green — implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc landed in the interval and this suite loads it. No reflection warnings. NO SPEC EDIT. This is a JVM implementation bug against semantics spec/011-SSR.md already promises; the hot-zone file is untouched. FOLLOW-ON, NOT DONE HERE (deliberately, per the no-widening stance). The CLJS arm still relies on JS arity leniency while the JVM arm now decides explicitly; the two agree on every shape tested, but they agree by construction rather than by a shared rule. Converging them is a renderer question, not this bug's. ## Addendum (post-close) — the merged test block tripped clj-kondo; PR #8883 kept green The close above stands unchanged: both defects confirmed, repaired, controls bite. What follows is a lint interaction discovered after it, repaired in the same PR without touching emit.cljc or altering what any test does. CI's `clj-kondo (fail on errors, warnings informational)` job went red on the new test block, taking the `Lint required` aggregate with it (every other check passed; clj-kondo was green on main, so it was this change's own). Three errors, all `needs-two is called with 1 arg but expects 2`, at implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_emit_test.clj lines 965, 993 and 1020. WHAT THOSE SITES ARE, because the natural reading is wrong. They are NOT the partial-arity fixture. `form2-partial` is never called directly — the renderer selects its arity at run time — so clj-kondo sees no call site there and flagged none of it. The three flagged sites are `needs-two`, a plain two-arity test helper deliberately called with ONE argument INSIDE the Form-2 inner's render body. That wrong call is the fixture payload: it is how the double-invocation and variadic rows obtain "an ArityException raised from a nested helper call", which is the acceptance criterion those rows are built on. So clj-kondo is CORRECT about the code it can see, and the test is also correct; the mismatch is the test input. Correcting the arity to satisfy the linter would have deleted the failure the rows exist to observe and left a green PR that no longer tested its own subject. SUPPRESSION SCOPE — the narrowest of three. A per-form `#_{:clj-kondo/ignore [:invalid-arity]}` at each of the three call sites, each with a one-line reason so a later reader does not delete it as noise. Rejected: one ignore over the enclosing fixture (blinds :invalid-arity across a whole `let` body that also holds the calls under test), and a `.clj-kondo/config.edn` entry (weakens arity checking repository-wide to serve three lines in one test file). `.clj-kondo/config.edn` is NOT touched, so this is not a one-toucher on shared lint config, and :invalid-arity stays live everywhere else including the rest of this file. THE SHAPE DOES NOT RECUR. All three occurrences were flagged and all three are fixed; the fourth Form-2 row (emit-passes-form-2-variadic-inner-the-whole-arg-seq) carries no deliberate mismatch, and clj-kondo reports zero errors across the whole lint surface. GATES. Run locally as the CI job runs it — the `--lint` path list and `--fail-level error` read off .github/workflows/lint.yml, at the version CI pins (clj-kondo v2026.04.15 from the same pinned release URL; the locally installed v2025.10.23 was not used). Captured exit codes: run 1 before, reproducing CI exit 3 errors: 3, warnings: 2078 run 2 after the three ignores exit 0 errors: 0, warnings: 2078 run 3 SABOTAGE, one ignore removed exit 3 errors: 1, warnings: 2078 Scope verified by set-differencing the complete finding lists of runs 1 and 2: the three error lines vanish and NOTHING else does — the warning total is unchanged and the only other movement is one pre-existing `unused binding x` warning shifting four lines down where the comment was inserted. The sabotage run is the control: removing a single ignore reds the gate at that exact call site and nowhere else, establishing that the ignore is load-bearing, that the green is not vacuous, and that the run read this branch's tree (`needs-two` is absent on the merge base, so the same gate against any other checkout returns zero errors). Planted and restored by git BLOB hash: 96004999cfa52decf11b67f702682b66b79e2ea4 committed, 76b066c4c1bcfa147e4a18e3a6af1754a72c8b26 planted, restored equal to the committed object. The SSR suite was re-run on the final base to confirm the ignore is inert (the reader discards `#_`, but "inert" is a claim like any other): captured exit 0, 603 tests / 2943 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors — the same counts as the close's runs 3 and 5. CI agrees: clj-kondo and `Lint required` both pass, and `JVM ssr (clojure -M:test)` passes, on head d1711c57cf. AUDIT PR #8883: REOPENED. Exception-driven probing is gone and programmer failures now propagate once, but the replacement does not actually preserve CLJS arity semantics for multi-arity inners. `form-2-invocation-arity` walks every declared fixed arity downward and picks the longest prefix. A CLJS single-arity fn does ignore extra JavaScript arguments, but a compiled multi-arity fn dispatches on `arguments.length` and throws when no exact/variadic arm exists. Executable CLJS probe: `(fn [x] ...)` applied to 3 args returns normally, while `(fn ([x] ...) ([x y] ...))` at 3 args and `(fn ([] ...) ([x] ...))` at 2 args both report `Invalid arity`. The JVM helper instead selects 2 and 1 respectively and returns `[1 2]` / `1`. A shared `.cljc` Form-2 can therefore render successfully during SSR but fail on the client/hydration path—the parity this repair is meant to establish. Minimal completion: model the compiled CLJS dispatch shape: exact fixed arms; full args for a satisfied variadic arm; prefix truncation only for a non-variadic function with one fixed arity (the raw-JS lenient shape). Add paired JVM and real CLJS multi-arity controls. Preserve the single invocation and exception propagation; no renderer abstraction. ## Verdict (rf2-mocn3, audit reopen) — PR #8918 AUDIT FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE ON BOTH HOSTS, BY EXECUTABLE PROBE, BEFORE ANY EDIT. The audit's probe reproduces exactly. Real CLJS (compiled by ClojureScript 1.12.145, run on node, invoked through cljs.core/apply — precisely what the :cljs branch of invoke-form-2-render-fn calls): (fn [x] ...) at 3 args -> returns, extra args dropped (fn ([x] ...) ([x y] ...)) at 3 args -> throws "Invalid arity: 3" (fn ([] ...) ([x] ...)) at 2 args -> throws "Invalid arity: 2" The same shapes through emit/emit-element on the JVM at the reopened tip returned

[:m2 1 2]

and

[:m1 1]

— the prefix walk selecting 2 and 1, exactly as the audit stated. A shared .cljc Form-2 component could therefore render on the server and throw on hydration. WHY THE PREFIX WALK IS WRONG. Only a fn with a SINGLE fixed arity and no variadic tail compiles to a bare JavaScript function, and only a bare JavaScript function drops extra arguments. Anything with more than one arm compiles to a dispatcher that switches on arguments.length and throws when no arm matches. "CLJS ignores extra args" is true of one shape and false of the rest, and the walk generalised it to all of them. DISPATCH MODEL IMPLEMENTED, mapping one-to-one onto the three branches the compiled dispatcher has: (1) an exact fixed arm for n; (2) a satisfied variadic arm, handed the WHOLE arg list; (3) prefix truncation ONLY for a non-variadic fn with exactly one fixed arity. Otherwise there is no shape CLJS would accept either, and (apply inner args) lets the JVM's own ArityException report the real call. Rule 3 stayed narrow deliberately: it models the runtime, and a tidier rule would be a different behaviour wearing the same name. THE WIDER CASE WAS REPRODUCED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN. CLJS is also lenient in the "too few args" direction — a single-arity-2 inner at 1 arg returns with undefined, and a fixed+variadic inner below its required count routes to the variadic arm with undefineds (both measured on node). The JVM raises there and still does. Fabricating nil props on the server is the class of silent divergence this helper exists to prevent, and the prior repair had already taken that position; nothing here widens it. accepts-arity? is replaced by declared-fixed-arities plus variadic-required-arity. Both things the old docstring was right to insist on are carried forward: the reflection is only ever applied to a fn? value, because clojure.lang.Var declares invoke for arities 0-21 regardless of what it holds; and a variadic tail is never read as "accepts zero". SINGLE INVOCATION AND EXCEPTION PROPAGATION PRESERVED — no user code runs inside a catch, the inner is invoked exactly once, and the prior repair's counting-inner rows still pin both. No renderer abstraction, no new protocol, no spec edit; edits confined to implementation/ssr. TESTS. A new cross-host .cljc table (re-frame.ssr.form2-arity-cljs-test) asserts the SAME expectation on both hosts — exact rendered bytes, or an arity rejection — twelve rows, because a JVM-only proof cannot see this defect at all. Its rejection predicate is narrow and host-specific (ArityException on the JVM, an "Invalid arity" js/Error on CLJS) and anything else propagates, so no row can pass on the wrong failure. Beside the existing Form-2 block, emit-form-2-multi-arity-inner-refuses-what-cljs-refuses covers the second public consumer: emit-element and render-shell share one resolver, so every row asserts through both. Non-vacuity is structural — the same multi-arity inners must still render through every arm they DO declare, so the rejection rows cannot be satisfied by a blanket refusal of multi-arity inners. GATES, captured exit codes, on the final rebased base (951c44ba92): clojure -M:test from implementation/ssr exit 0 605 tests / 2969 assertions, 0/0 npm run test:cljs (node-test, real CLJS) exit 0 11127 tests / 54980 assertions, 0/0 clj-kondo v2026.04.15, lint.yml's exact --lint list and --fail-level error exit 0 errors 0, warnings 2078 (unchanged) JVM baseline before the change was 603 / 2943; the new rows add exactly +2 tests and +26 assertions (14 JVM deftest, 12 cross-host table). SABOTAGE. Restoring the prefix walk: JVM exit 1, 6 failures — both cross-host rejection rows and all four JVM multi-arity rejection rows (sync and streaming); counts unchanged at 605/2969, so the plant failed rows rather than crashing a lane. Restoring the ORIGINAL exception-driven probing: JVM exit 1, 10 failures + 2 errors — every one of PR #8883's defect-detecting rows goes red (emit-renders-form-2-partial-arity-inner, both emit-form-2-inner-body-arity-exception-propagates-once blocks, emit-form-2-variadic-inner-body-failure-is-not-swallowed). So this change did NOT defang them. The one #8883 row that stays green under that plant is emit-passes-form-2-variadic-inner-the-whole-arg-seq, correctly: it is an acceptance row, not a catch-detector, and the old probe's first apply already succeeded for a variadic inner at two args. TREE-READ CONTROLS. The CLJS lane prints its shadow-cljs.edn path, and it named this worktree. Flipping one expectation in the new .cljc reds the node run at that exact line with actual :arity-rejected, which is also the direct real-CLJS evidence that the runtime refuses the multi-arity call. One planted str/join arity error reds clj-kondo (exit 3, errors 1) at exactly that line with the warning total unchanged. Every plant was applied and reverted by git blob hash, each restored file verified byte-equal to its committed object. AUDIT PR #8918: REOPENED. The repaired dispatcher now matches CLJS for excess arguments, but knowingly diverges for missing arguments while its public/source contract still says it models what the same compiled CLJS inner accepts and that the server fails where the client fails. The PR's own Node probes establish two omitted cases: a single-fixed-arity-2 inner called with one arg renders with `undefined`, and a fixed+variadic inner called below its required count routes to the variadic arm with missing `undefined` slots; the JVM still throws in both. The new cross-host table contains neither case despite describing host agreement as the contract. A legal shared `.cljc` Form-2 can therefore render in the browser and fail during SSR. Keep the completion small: pin both cases on both hosts, choose and state one honest supported contract, and—if parity remains the promise—model missing JS arguments on the JVM with the corresponding nil slots. Preserve single invocation/exception propagation; no renderer abstraction. MAYOR RULING 2026-09-01 21:38 AUSEST — NARROW THE PROMISE; DO NOT FABRICATE NIL SLOTS. The audit offers two exits: model missing JS arguments on the JVM with nil slots, or state one honest contract. TAKE THE SECOND. WHY. CLJS supplying undefined for a missing argument is an accident of the JavaScript calling convention, not a designed affordance. Emulating it on the JVM means SSR silently renders a component with nil props where the author has made an arity mistake — a defect that ships as production HTML instead of failing where it can be seen. Failing loud on the server is the better half of the divergence, and PR #8883 already took that position for the same reason; reversing it is a larger change than this item's own 'keep the completion small' allows, and the stance rejects that kind of gold-plating. SO THE DEFECT IS THE CONTRACT TEXT, AND THE AUDIT IS RIGHT ABOUT IT. The public and source wording promises that the helper models what the same compiled CLJS inner accepts and that the server fails where the client fails. That is FALSE for missing arguments, and a promise that is false is worse than a narrower promise that is true — it is what makes a legal shared .cljc Form-2 look safe. RULED, three parts, all small: 1. PIN BOTH OMITTED CASES ON BOTH HOSTS in the existing cross-host table — a single-fixed-arity-2 inner called with one argument, and a fixed+variadic inner called below its required count. Record the ACTUAL behaviour on each host, divergence included. A table that describes host agreement as its contract must show where agreement stops, or it is advertising the same false promise the prose does. 2. CORRECT THE CONTRACT WORDING to the honest, narrower claim: the helper matches CLJS on arity SELECTION and on EXCESS arguments, and deliberately REFUSES where CLJS would silently supply undefined for a missing one. State the reason in one clause — a fabricated nil prop is a worse outcome than a loud failure — so the next reader does not read the divergence as an oversight and 'fix' it. 3. Preserve single invocation and unmodified exception propagation. No renderer abstraction, no options map, no public API change. NOT WANTED: filling missing arguments with nil on the JVM; any flag or opt-in that selects between the two behaviours; widening into the wider leniency class beyond the two cases named. ## Verdict (rf2-mocn3, second audit reopen) — PR #8935 RULING FOLLOWED, NOT THE AUDIT'S FIRST EXIT. The mayor ruling of 2026-09-01 21:38 AUSEST was confirmed as the newest text on this bead before any work: the history walk newest-first found the last text-bearing change at 21:39:49 (hudke6b0), a notes append of +2354 characters carrying the ruling, and it is a suffix append rather than a rewrite. No child beads, no comments. So: narrow the promise, do not fabricate nil slots. PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT TIP BEFORE ANY EDIT, four probes, two per host, measured rather than taken from PR #8918's report. Real compiled CLJS (ClojureScript 1.12.145, node v24.13.0), through emit/emit-element — the same public entry point the cross-host table uses: single fixed-arity-2 inner @ 1 arg -> renders

fixed2|a|

fixed+variadic (required 2) inner @ 1 arg -> renders

fv|a||

(variadic arm, missing slot) JVM, through the same emit/emit-element at tip: single fixed-arity-2 inner @ 1 arg -> clojure.lang.ArityException "Wrong number of args (1) passed to: …" fixed+variadic (required 2) inner @ 1 arg -> clojure.lang.ArityException "Wrong number of args (1) passed to: …" Controls on both hosts at every count the same inners DO accept rendered identical bytes, so the probes reached the live Form-2 path rather than short-circuiting. The divergence is real and present at tip; the contract text still promised parity. HOW undefined WAS TOLD APART FROM nil, AND BOTH FROM A THROW — this task turns on it. The rendered strings cannot do it: (str x) is "" for both nil and undefined, and nil? answers true for BOTH because it compiles to `== null`. The discriminator is undefined?, which is `===` against `void 0`; measured directly, (nil? js/undefined) is true while (undefined? nil) is false. A spy fn captured (undefined? a) / (undefined? b) at the call site: the argument that WAS passed read false, the one that was NOT read true. A throw is a third, unambiguous outcome — the exception class was printed, never inferred from output. THE DEFECT REPAIRED IS THE CONTRACT TEXT. emit.cljc's edits are docstrings ONLY. Single invocation and unmodified exception propagation are untouched; no flag, no options map, no renderer abstraction, no public API change, no nil-filling. Every site that stated the promise was corrected: • form-2-invocation-arity — its nil return no longer means "CLJS would reject the call too". It means "no declared arm fits n", and the TWO situations that produces are enumerated: too many args for every arm of a multi-arm inner (both hosts refuse) versus too few args (CLJS does NOT refuse; the JVM refuses deliberately). • invoke-form-2-render-fn — a new THE SUPPORTED CONTRACT paragraph. Before, the closing sentence read "… rather than a fabricated retry — the server fails where the client fails." After: the helper matches compiled CLJS on arity SELECTION and on EXCESS arguments, and deliberately DIVERGES on MISSING ones, where the server is STRICTER than the client, so a legal shared .cljc Form-2 can render in the browser and fail during SSR. The reason is one clause — supplying undefined is an accident of the JavaScript calling convention, and emulating it would ship an author's arity mistake as production HTML with nil props instead of failing where it can be seen — followed by an explicit "do NOT fix this by filling the missing slots with nil", so the next reader does not read it as an oversight. • resolve-component-head — "arity-tolerantly" became "at the arity its declared arms select, and tolerating EXCESS args only". • the cross-host table's ns docstring — the flat claim "the JVM agrees with CLJS" is replaced by the true one. • ssr_emit_test.clj's section comment — "the cross-host table proves the AGREEMENT on both hosts" now also names where agreement stops. BOTH OMITTED CASES PINNED ON BOTH HOSTS, in the existing cross-host table, as rows carrying a PER-HOST expectation that records the actual behaviour rather than an agreement the code does not hold. Three non-vacuity controls assert host agreement at every count those same two inners DO accept, so the divergence rows cannot be satisfied by a JVM that has simply stopped rendering these shapes. One CLJS-only block pins that the missing slot is genuinely js/undefined and not a fabricated nil — the word is load-bearing in the new contract wording and the rendered bytes cannot carry it. SPEC UNTOUCHED, AND NO HOT-ZONE SEQUENCING NEEDED. spec/011-SSR.md carries no Form-2 arity contract at all. Checked line-oriented and again over the whitespace-flattened text, because a wrapped phrase is invisible to a line-oriented search: Form-2, form-2, "inner render" and invoke-form-2 all count 0. The contract lives only in source and tests, which is the fence this worker owns. STREAMING NOT RE-ASSERTED FOR THESE TWO CASES, deliberately. emit-element and render-shell share one resolver and that is already pinned by many rows; the refusal is pre-existing behaviour now being documented, not new behaviour. Adding rows there would have been widening without evidence, and the ruling named the cross-host table. GATES, captured exit codes, on the final rebased base (de33d639e7). Each captured with the redirect and the echo of the runner's own exit on ONE command line, in one shell, and it is that number quoted — not one the harness reported about the run. clojure -M:test from implementation/ssr exit 0 610 tests / 2995 assertions, 0/0 npm run test:cljs (node-test, real CLJS) exit 0 11153 tests / 55172 assertions, 0/0 compile 1874 files, 0 warnings clj-kondo v2026.04.15, lint.yml's exact --lint list and --fail-level error exit 0 errors 0, warnings 2081 Both suites re-run AFTER the rebase rather than resting on the pre-rebase green: nine commits landed in the interval, three under implementation/core/src/re_frame/ (events.cljc, fx.cljc, router.cljc) which this suite loads. JVM baseline on the same base was 609 / 2990; the new deftest adds exactly +1 test and +5 assertions on the JVM, +8 on CLJS (the extra three being the CLJS-only undefined? pin). TREE-READ CONTROLS. The CLJS lane prints its config path and the line named this worktree's implementation/shadow-cljs.edn on both runs. clj-kondo prints no root, so the proof is a planted fault: one str/join arity error at the fixture line this change adds reddened it, captured exit 3, errors 1 at exactly that file and line, warning total unchanged at 76 for the scoped surface, and set-differencing the complete finding lists of the clean and planted runs moves exactly one line and nothing else. The fault existed only in this worktree, so a run that had wandered into a sibling checkout would have come back green. THE ROW-FLIP CONTROL, which is the deliverable's own control and has a shape the usual one does not. These two rows RECORD a divergence rather than asserting a fix, so "revert the fix and watch it red" does not apply — there is no fix to revert. Instead each row's expected value was flipped to the OTHER host's behaviour and the run checked for red on the host it is then wrong about: both :clj expectations -> the CLJS render JVM exit 1 2 failures, one per row, at their own lines, actual: ::arity-rejected both :cljs expectations -> ::arity-rejected node exit 1 2 failures, one per row, actual: "

fixed2|a|

" and "

fv|a||

" So neither row would pass if its host behaved the other way, which is the whole question for a row whose content is "these hosts disagree". title: machines: restored mixed-prefix actors violate reverse-creation teardown
description:
## Scope

Correct restored/hydrated spawned-actor disposal ordering in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc` and the spawn/teardown bookkeeping it consumes. Add focused coverage in `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj` and update the machine runtime-db schema/spec commentary needed for any new durable ordering fact.

## Correctness finding

`teardown-on-frame-destroy!` promises reverse creation order even after epoch restore or SSR hydration has repopulated durable snapshots without the process-side `spawn-order` atom. Its fallback sorts actor IDs by the trailing `#<n>` parsed by `creation-rank`. That suffix is only a per-`id-prefix` sequence, not a frame-global creation sequence. It therefore cannot order actors created under different machine types/prefixes, and IDs supplied through `:fixed-actor-id` carry no rank at all. The implementation is attempting to reconstruct information that the durable state does not contain.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From `implementation/machines`, use the existing plain-atom/reset-runtime fixture, create one frame, and register two child machine types `:probe/a` and `:probe/b`; each child appends its stamped `:rf/self-id` to an atom from its active state's `:exit` action.
2. Register a boot machine whose action emits three `:rf.machine/spawn` effects in order: A, A, B. Dispatch it and verify `spawn-order/frame-order` is `[:probe/a#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/b#1]`.
3. Call `spawn-order/reset-all!` while leaving runtime-db snapshots intact. This is the existing test suite's model of epoch restore/SSR hydration, where durable state survives and the process-side atom does not.
4. Call `rf/destroy-frame!` and inspect the exit log. Current main produces `[:probe/a#2 :probe/a#1 :probe/b#1]`; exact reverse creation order is `[:probe/b#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/a#1]`.

## Evidence

- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:34-40` pins frame disposal to leaf-to-root exit cascades in reverse creation order, with the most recently spawned instance disposing first.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc:91-113` parses only the numeric suffix; lines 168-177 and 209-220 claim that descending suffix order reconstructs the durable creation order.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:60-75` increments `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-counter <machine-id>]`; lines 909-914 select `(or :id-prefix :machine-id)` as that counter key. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2711-2718,4471` likewise defines the allocator as per-prefix.
- The existing restore regression at `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj:321-366` creates three actors of the same `:rs/child` prefix, so suffix rank happens to be a valid total order and the mixed-prefix defect is invisible.
- The JVM public-surface probe above exited 0 with:

```clojure
{:recorded   [:probe/a#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/b#1]
 :exit-order [:probe/a#2 :probe/a#1 :probe/b#1]
 :expected   [:probe/b#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/a#1]}
```

The wrong first exit is forced, not a map-order flake: rank 2 sorts ahead of rank 1 even though `:probe/b#1` was created last.

## Failure scenario / invariant

An SSR-hydrated or epoch-restored frame contains actors of two worker types. The application created `a#1`, then `a#2`, then `b#1`; their exit actions release dependent resources or emit ordered cleanup effects. The transient atom is absent after the round trip. `destroy-frame!` exits `a#2` before the newer `b#1`, and may place the equal-rank `a#1` before `b#1` as well. This violates the pinned stack-discipline invariant and exposes cleanup effects in an order the application did not create.

Invariant: every supported frame-state round trip must preserve one total oldest-to-newest order for live spawned actors, independent of actor-id spelling, type, prefix, or fixed-id allocation. Frame destruction consumes its exact reverse.

## Recommended minimal fix

Persist the total live-spawn order in the durable machine runtime-db instead of deriving it from actor IDs. The smallest shape is an oldest-to-newest vector sibling under `:rf.runtime/machines` (for example `:spawn-order`): append exactly once in the same exact-owner write that successfully installs a spawned snapshot, remove the actor in every successful teardown projection, and have frame destruction read that durable vector. Epoch restore already replaces runtime-db wholesale, and the SSR projector already carries machine bookkeeping siblings verbatim, so the same fact then survives both paths without a restore callback.

The current process-side atom may be removed or retained only as a derived cache; it must not remain the source of truth after a round trip. Remove or explicitly demote the suffix parser: per-prefix ranks can be a deterministic last-resort walk for malformed/fixture-only state, but cannot satisfy or be described as satisfying reverse creation order. Keep the public actor-id format and per-prefix counters unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a red-first focused test that spawns at least `a#1`, `a#2`, then `b#1` through the public machine/fx path. Before simulating the round trip, it asserts the exact live order `[:a#1 :a#2 :b#1]` and that all three spawned snapshots exist; these are non-vacuity controls.
- Simulate the real loss boundary (wipe only transient bookkeeping or round-trip/replace the frame runtime-db) while retaining the new durable order. Then `rf/destroy-frame!` must run child exit actions exactly `[:b#1 :a#2 :a#1]`, once each. The test must fail on current main with the measured `a#2`-first result.
- The durable ordering fact round-trips through EDN and the SSR machine-runtime projection unchanged; no function, atom, host handle, or process-local token enters runtime-db.
- Successful explicit destroy/finalization removes the actor from the durable live order; a later frame destroy neither exits it twice nor leaves an unbounded stale entry. Existing system-id release, snapshot cleanup, and silent-idempotent destroy assertions remain green.
- The existing same-prefix restore control (`child#3`, `child#2`, `child#1`) remains green, demonstrating that the fix preserves the ordinary path while the new mixed-prefix case is the discriminator.
- Schema/spec/source prose names the durable total-order authority and no longer claims that a per-prefix `#<n>` suffix reconstructs global creation order.
- Negative control: removing/bypassing the new durable-order append or reverting frame destroy to suffix sorting makes the mixed-prefix assertion red while its pre-destroy liveness/order controls still pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to public actor IDs, the per-prefix spawn counters, `:system-id`, join semantics, or callback APIs.
- No compatibility layer for historical pre-alpha payloads, global wall-clock timestamp, UUID ordering, or process-wide actor registry.
- No redesign of singleton teardown, frame incarnation fencing, timer cancellation, HTTP abort, classification, or general SSR/epoch machinery.
- No claim that arbitrary hand-edited runtime-db lacking the new durable fact can reveal an order it never recorded.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses with title and description terms `reverse-creation`, `reverse creation`, `spawn-order`, `spawn order`, `frame destroy`, `frame-destroy`, `restored spawned`, `restored actor`, `creation-rank`, `newest-first`, `newest first`, `straggler`, `disposal order`, `mixed-prefix`, and `per-prefix`; no issue owns this invariant. Open `rf2-cq0yi` concerns core's unrelated `frame-generation-pool` teardown leak, not machine actor ordering. The sole in-progress bead at filing time, `rf2-jui1c`, is an unrelated prose sweep and was left untouched.
