title: surface-review(examples-substrates): make login the runnable three-view-layer comparison
description:
## Scope

Make the existing login feature the canonical runnable comparison of re-frame2's three active browser view languages: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso. Keep `examples/core/login/` as the Reagent arm and `examples/substrates/uix/login/` as the UIx arm; add one Hicasso arm under `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` that requires the same substrate-free `login.model` and owns only its view/root code. Add a concise `examples/substrates/README.md` that explains which comparison to read, wire the new arm through the existing example build/runner/compile path, and extend the existing login bundle-isolation proof. Correct only directly coupled catalogue and TESTING prose.

This is one worked-example outcome, not a demo framework or a substrate selector.

## Findings

- The substrate tree has UIx counter/login/dashboard and reagent-slim counter, but no landing page and no human-facing Hicasso example. `examples/README.md` still describes the family as UIx plus reagent-slim even though Hicasso now ships its own canonical view adapter.
- Hicasso already has a complete installation counter in `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` and a Story/Xray-owned counter testbed under `tools/story/testbeds/hicasso_counter/`. Another counter would duplicate the beginner sample or send learners into tool scaffolding; neither shows a realistic model/view boundary.
- Login is already the right comparison seam. Commit `2644f42b72` (`rf2-ppbvav`) extracted roughly 19 schemas/effects/machine/events/subscriptions and `frame-config` into one substrate-free `login.model`, leaving only views and mount code in the Reagent/UIx/Helix entries. Commit `e1f38e5ddf` (`rf2-d6epb`) removed Helix, so that deliberate three-view example became a two-view pair.
- The removal left observable drift: `examples/TESTING.md` still says counter and login "triplet", "three reactive substrates", and "three login examples" although only Reagent and UIx login builds remain. `login.model` also still speaks of "three mounts". Fixing those words alone would be minutiae; supplying the current third view language restores the useful product shape they once described.
- The three small counter files deliberately repeat their tiny event/sub dataflow so each remains readable top to bottom. Extracting a counter model would weaken the smallest-app lesson for little gain. The substantial login model already amortises sharing and has model-level tests.
- Hicasso's native root door is compatible without an API change, but the boot shape must be honest. `h/mount!` accepts only `:frame`, `:initial-events`, and `:identifier-prefix`; the login demo also needs `model/frame-config`'s `:fx-overrides`. The Hicasso entry should therefore install `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, create the frame once with the existing config, and mount into that frame. Hot reload should re-render the retained Hicasso root rather than recreate the frame.
- The existing harness already supplies the needed mechanics. A normal `:examples/login-hicasso` build whose init namespace and `index.html` live under `examples/` is discovered by `serve-example.cjs`, staged with `_shared`, and swept by `check-examples-compile.cjs`; no registry or special runner branch is needed.
- Examples are intentionally test-free. The shared login behavior is already exercised outside the tree, while `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` proves the shared model does not pull a foreign view runtime. That checker currently has only Reagent and UIx arms even though the general isolation gate already owns live Hicasso sentinels and a positive-control module.

## Recommended Action

Add `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` as a direct third view over `login.model`. Keep the same fields, messages, test ids, canned success/failure flow, and shared visual assets as the existing pair. Author the view in native Hicasso idioms (`h/defview`, `h/sub`, event vectors where they fit); preserve the password event's classified map payload rather than flattening the secret into a positional intent. Use a small `h/event` callback where constructing that map requires the DOM value.

Declare `:examples/login-hicasso` beside the two current login builds, with the standard `out/examples/login-hicasso` output. Let the existing manifest-derived runner and compile checker enroll it. Add the exact repository-local run command to the new example README, while linking the Hicasso installation chapter for dependency setup and truthfully noting that the Maven coordinate is not published yet.

Make `examples/substrates/README.md` a short decision/comparison surface with two explicit tracks:

1. Same Reagent authoring language, different adapter/package: stock counter versus reagent-slim counter.
2. One substrate-free model, different view language/root: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso login.

Link directly to the model and three thin entry points so a programmer or coding agent can compare source, not prose excerpts. Point the root catalogue at this page and reconcile the stale parity section in `examples/TESTING.md` and directly coupled login comments/READMEs.

Extend `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` and `test:bundle-isolation` to release and inspect the Hicasso login. Reuse the existing Hicasso sentinels and positive control: each login bundle must contain its own view runtime and exclude the other two. Keep compile coverage plus this structural proof; do not add a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- `examples/README.md:9,55-61` lists only UIx and reagent-slim under Substrates; `examples/substrates/README.md` does not exist.
- `examples/TESTING.md:82-118` calls two current pairs triplets and claims three login examples while naming only two login bundles.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljs:42-57,722-742` documents the substrate-free owner and shared frame config; only `examples/core/login/core.cljs` and `examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs` require it today.
- `implementation/scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs:3-45,85-103,179-235` explicitly implements a two-bundle Reagent/UIx proof.
- `implementation/package.json:41-42,53` releases only the two login builds for bundle isolation and exposes the existing compile and `dev:example` doors.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1611-1644` declares the current login pair; `:examples/hicasso-counter` at lines 1950-1959 points to the tool-owned Story testbed instead of `examples/`.
- `node ../examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs --list` includes `examples/login` and `examples/login-uix` but not the tool-owned Hicasso counter. `node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` does include that tool build, demonstrating why compile inventory alone is not a human learning catalogue.
- `docs/core/hicasso/index.md:3-6` defines Hicasso as re-frame2's native view layer. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2130-2138` lists Hicasso's own adapter in the canonical shipped inventory.
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:549-605` and `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:115-155` bound `h/mount!` to the three root keys and show that it joins a frame already created through `rf/make-frame`.
- `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:300-332,742-746` already defines non-dev Hicasso sentinels (`hicassoBoundary`, `rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector`) and proves them present in a dedicated positive-control module.
- History establishes the sequence: shared login model on 2026-07-11 (`2644f42b72`), Helix removal on 2026-07-22 (`e1f38e5ddf`), Hicasso's own adapter on 2026-08-18 (`4cb9e16951`), and canonical adapter registration on 2026-08-19 (`5d1fd88c3f`). The examples never gained a human Hicasso arm after that change.
- Current tag and installation evidence says the example must stay repository-local for now: `git tag --list 'v*'` is empty and `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:18-40,125` says the coordinate is unpublished and uses `:local/root`.
- Fresh open/closed title and description searches for the exact prefix, Hicasso login, login-hicasso, three-view-layer, cross-substrate, `login.model`, and `examples/substrates/hicasso` found no duplicate. The adjacent launch-command tasks `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` are distinct and explicitly remain separate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` contains a readable Hicasso entry, host page, and concise README. It imports `login.model` and contains no duplicate auth schemas, effects, machine, events, or subscriptions.
2. The Hicasso view uses native `h/defview`/`h/sub`/intent idioms and matches the Reagent/UIx pair's visible login behavior and stable test ids. Email edits remain positional; password edits still dispatch the classified `[:auth.login/edit-password {:value ...}]` shape, and submit/success/failure behavior remains owned by the shared model.
3. Boot installs `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, constructs the frame once from `model/frame-config` so the canned HTTP effect override and initial event are honored, mounts Hicasso into that frame, and retains/re-renders one root on hot reload. No expansion or compatibility shim is added to `h/mount!`.
4. `:examples/login-hicasso` emits to the standard example output root and appears automatically in both `npm run dev:example -- --list` and `npm run test:examples-compile` inventory. Its host/shared assets are resolved by the existing staging code with no hard-coded build-to-folder entry.
5. `examples/substrates/README.md` gives the two-track comparison above and links the exact model/view/root files. `examples/README.md`, `examples/TESTING.md`, `login.model`, and the three login READMEs no longer describe deleted Helix arms or incorrect triplet counts.
6. The new README gives one truthful repository-local launch path and points greenfield setup to the Hicasso installation guide; it does not advertise an unresolved Maven version or duplicate a project template.
7. `test:bundle-isolation` releases all three login builds. The existing login checker proves own-runtime presence plus foreign-runtime absence for Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso, using a non-vacuous Hicasso positive control. The Hicasso login carries no Reagent or UIx fingerprint, and the other two carry no Hicasso fingerprint.
8. `npm run test:examples-compile`, `npm run test:bundle-isolation`, the existing example staging/runner tests, and relevant docs-link gates pass. A clean repository-local launch paints the form and exercises one validation failure plus the canned successful login; no new per-example browser gate is introduced.

## Non-goals

- No runtime view-layer switcher, multi-adapter bundle, mode flag, gallery shell, code generator, or new example manifest/framework.
- No extraction of the tiny counter registrations, sharing of view code, or conversion of every example to every view layer.
- No Hicasso variant in `tools/template`, no publication workaround, and no invented compatibility coordinate while the artifact is unpublished.
- No change to Hicasso root/adapter APIs, login business behavior, or the substrate contract.
- No promotion or relocation of the Story/Xray Hicasso counter testbed; tool testbeds remain tool-owned.
- No Hicasso SSR/Node example; `rf2-8arzr` owns that separate path.
- No sweep standardizing existing substrate README launch commands; `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` own the adjacent catalogue command policy. This task only documents the new arm and follows whichever shared wording lands.
- No per-example browser-test matrix; examples stay human learning surfaces and adapter smokes stay adapter-owned.

## Related beads

- `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` - adjacent core/capability launch-command work; not duplicated here.
- `rf2-9hcyf` - executable UIx component-testing recipe; distinct from the human example comparison.
- `rf2-8urba` - deferred Hicasso template variant, gated on publication; this task does not scaffold consumers.
- `rf2-8arzr` - native-Hicasso SSR/Node reference path; explicitly outside this browser example.
- `rf2-auiy5` and `rf2-hvr5h` - established Hicasso's canonical native adapter.
- Historical `rf2-ppbvav` / commit `2644f42b72` - created the shared login model and original three-view comparison.
- Historical `rf2-d6epb` / commit `e1f38e5ddf` - removed Helix and its example arms.
- `rf2-5czki` - added Hicasso Story support and the tool-owned testbed; this task supplies the intentionally separate human surface.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-31 00:56:58 AUSEST (read-only agent at 5d35356469): premises HOLD (TESTING.md hits drifted to :98-103; h/mount! has NO :fx-overrides; substrate.cljs is .cljs-only; mount.cljs ensure-frame! creates-if-missing else joins, so the plan is valid; discovery is prefix-derived with no exclusion list and no hicasso pin at _examples-staging.test.cjs:224). SEQUENCED: after the ujdn0/iacw2 cluster merges (examples READMEs) and serialised on implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (HOT; rf2-3xq1v) and implementation/package.json:41 (rf2-39rc5). Trim: no spec/006 wording change; no staging-test pin unless needed; extend only check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs, reusing the sentinel literals from check-bundle-isolation.cjs:329-332.
AUDIT 2026-09-02 — PR #8954 correctness/completeness finding (reopened).

implementation/scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs now claims the shared login.model is free of every foreign view library OR adapter and exports COVERS_RUNTIMES including hicasso, but its HICASSO_SENTINELS cover only the Hicasso codec: hicassoBoundary and :rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector are both defined solely in re-frame.hicasso.impl.codec. The standalone adapter used by the new arm, re-frame.hicasso.substrate, requires React plus core spine/context/frame/boundary and does not require the codec or public Hicasso door; its own adapter fingerprints are the rf-hic-sub- / rf-hic-use-sub- prefixes.

That leaves a real false-green: a reachable adapter-only dependency from login.model can put the foreign Hicasso adapter into the Reagent and UIx login bundles while both chosen Hicasso sentinels remain absent. The own-Hicasso positive still passes because hicasso.login.core separately requires the codec, so it cannot reveal this gap. This contradicts the gate's stated substrate-free proof and its checker-owned hicasso contract.

Minimal remedy: add a production-stable adapter-owned Hicasso marker to the existing own/foreign sentinel proof (the Hicasso spine prefixes are the direct analogue of the UIx markers already used) and demonstrate that an adapter-only leak into the shared model turns the gate red. title: surface-review(skill-reagent-migration): teach only Hicasso's live read and navigation doors
description:
## Scope

Update skills/reagent-migration/** so the published skill teaches only the current post-dead-weight Hicasso authoring vocabulary at the two seams changed by rf2-6c12m.15:

- h/sub is the sole public subscription-read door.
- navigation is authored through h/route-link or ordinary routing events; the navigate intent head is implementation-owned and is not written as ::h/navigate.

Cover the distributable SKILL/references and the authoring-time spec/eval material that can reintroduce the old forms. Keep this a skill-only change.

## Findings

1. The skill violates its own cardinal rule 6 (“emit only what has shipped; read the door”). Current re-frame.hicasso exports h/sub and no h/use-subs, but references/mental-model.md and references/catalog-mechanical.md still teach h/use-subs as a deliberate control, while spec/inputs.md still rosters it as public.

2. The public navigate spelling also moved. rf2-6c12m.15 demoted the navigate head to re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate; h/route-link mints that internal value. references/gotchas.md still calls ::h/navigate one of two public reserved heads and says the draft guide is incomplete without it, while spec/authoring-prompt.md preserves that claim for the next reauthor. An authored ::h/navigate now resolves to a different keyword from the internal head and is not the shipped navigation contract.

3. This is high-friction in the failure direction. An AI following the read leaf can emit an unresolved h/use-subs call; one following the gotcha can emit a vector the current intent lowering does not recognize as its navigation head. The programmer is asked to choose between doors that no longer exist instead of using the single simple path Hicasso intentionally kept.

4. Progressive disclosure currently hides, rather than contains, the drift: the top-level router says “read the door,” but the false advice appears only when the relevant read/gotcha leaf is loaded. The eval corpus has no expectation that rejects either retired form, so its behavioural fixtures do not expose the contradiction.

5. This is recent history, not a request to redesign Hicasso. Commit 4c9fa03def (rf2-6c12m.15) removed h/use-subs as below the ergonomics bar and internalised navigation as part of the open dead-weight programme. Other same-wave skill updates carried hframe, native and defhost changes, but these six live teaching references remained.

## Recommended Action

Carry rf2-6c12m.15 into this skill directly:

- Teach repeated, conditional and looped reads as ordinary h/sub calls. Remove the grouped-read alternative rather than replacing it with another abstraction.
- Remove ::h/navigate from the author-facing marker/reserved-head vocabulary. Where navigation is relevant, point to h/route-link or a normal routing event; do not expose the internal intent value.
- Correct spec/inputs.md and spec/authoring-prompt.md so a future reauthor cannot resurrect either form.
- Add or amend one focused behavioural eval that grades the live outcome: h/sub is the only read emitted, and neither h/use-subs nor ::h/navigate is proposed.

Keep the explanation short. The outcome is fewer concepts and code that compiles against the current door, not a new compatibility story.

## Evidence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc: the current public door aliases h/sub and has no use-subs export.
- docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md, “Reads”: the complete current roster contains h/sub only.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:284: navigate-head is namespaced to the implementation.
- docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:68-80: route-link owns and mints that head; application authors do not.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/mental-model.md:84 and references/catalog-mechanical.md:61 still teach h/use-subs.
- skills/reagent-migration/spec/inputs.md:17 still lists use-subs on the door.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:108,204 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:23 still teach ::h/navigate as public.
- git commit 4c9fa03def: “hicasso: drop h/use-subs, the grouped read control (rf2-6c12m.15)”.
- skills/reagent-migration/README.md says the skill is pre-alpha and has not been exercised end to end; the static eval set contains no retired-read/navigation control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No live instruction, source-of-truth roster, reauthoring prompt or eval expectation under skills/reagent-migration/** presents h/use-subs as callable or ::h/navigate as author-written.
- The read guidance has one direct answer: use h/sub at each read site, including conditional/loop/helper cases.
- Navigation guidance, if retained in this migration skill, uses only h/route-link or ordinary routing events and clearly leaves the opaque navigate head to Hicasso.
- A focused behavioural eval would fail an answer that emits h/use-subs or ::h/navigate and pass one that stays on the live public doors.
- Existing M/D/R routing, whole-view coherence, reporter/census workflow, compile/test verification and programmer-owned render check remain intact.
- JSON parses, skill/package structural checks pass, and the relevant markdown link/anchor gate passes. The handoff names the current public-door source that was checked.

## Non-goals

- No Hicasso runtime or public API change.
- No compatibility alias or shim for h/use-subs or ::h/navigate.
- No automated view rewrite engine, new linter, surface-sync gate or defensive policy.
- No broad API audit, catalogue expansion, reporter change, migration of application dataflow, or redesign of route-link.
- No unrelated polish or exhaustive wording sweep.

## Related beads

- rf2-6c12m.15 — exact landed facade-hygiene change this skill missed.
- rf2-6c12m — open Hicasso dead-weight epic; establishes the minimum-ceremony/trust-the-programmer direction.
- rf2-r3r00 — current complementary surface review reducing Hicasso’s clj-kondo export to useful macro-shape analysis; no dependency or overlap.
- rf2-r4j91 — original Reagent-migration retarget to Hicasso.
- rf2-0jl8s, rf2-6c12m.24, rf2-6c12m.30 and rf2-6c12m.13 — prior API changes successfully carried into this skill, useful history for the same bounded update pattern.

title: surface-review(skill-re-frame-migration): make one explicit migration request run end to end
description:
## Scope

Make the published re-frame v1→v2 migration skill complete the ordinary work an explicit invoker asked it to do. Cover `skills/re-frame-migration/**`, its `allowed-tools`, the verification-posture row in `skills/README.md`, and the migration corpus Part 2 only where needed to keep the execution contract singular and consistent.

The outcome is one uninterrupted default path: inspect the app, apply authorized Type-A changes, run the app's discovered noninteractive install/compile/test gates, batch genuine Type-B decisions, and report observed results. Keep interactive or visual runtime verification with the programmer only when no connected runtime is available.

## Findings

- The skill calls Type A automatic, but cardinal rule 4 still pauses before every multi-file sweep for an acknowledgement. An explicit “migrate this repo” request therefore does not authorize the migration it requested.
- Cardinal rule 5 then guarantees a paste loop: after M-0, inventory commands, compile, tests, and every re-verification step are printed for the programmer to run and paste back. The frontmatter permits `rg` and three read-only git forms but excludes the routine `npm` / `npx` / `clojure` / `shadow-cljs` commands required to learn whether the agent's edits work.
- The bespoke boundary contradicts both nearby authorities. `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` Part 2 tells the performing agent to compile, test, and run the app. `skills/README.md` says published skills “trust the explicit invoker” and explicitly permits those routine command wildcards. The sibling `reagent-migration` skill already uses the useful split: the agent runs discovered noninteractive compile/test gates; the programmer owns genuinely interactive visual confirmation.
- The delegated/CI exception proves the commands are already considered valid migration work, but makes execution depend on where the same agent is labelled as running. That distinction adds prose and stalls without reducing the risk of the command itself; the host agent's normal permission/sandbox controls already own that boundary.
- This posture is repeated across 15 files (42 matching instruction lines for author-runs / paste / arbitrary-code / mass-rewrite language). It consumes the router and leaf budget with policy explanation instead of migration action, weakening progressive disclosure.
- `evals/evals.json` is trigger-only. Nothing grades whether the skill proceeds after M-0, runs verification, avoids redundant approval gates, batches Type-B questions, or refuses to claim completion when only the interactive smoke remains. Its last change predates much of the skill's correction history.
- Human-facing status is also unsynchronised: `README.md` says the skill has never been exercised end to end, while `spec/improving.md` records a substantial real migration and its runtime findings. That makes the published maturity signal untrustworthy.

## Recommended Action

Adopt the repository's existing trust-the-explicit-invoker posture for this migration skill.

Treat an explicit request to migrate the current project as authorization for the planned Type-A source edits and for the project's own discovered, noninteractive install/compile/test commands. Announce a Type-A sweep as a concise progress update with rule id, scope, and diff shape, then proceed; do not wait for an extra acknowledgement. Preserve the smallest-diff rule and batch all unresolved Type-B choices into one checkpoint, as `sequencing.md` already recommends.

Use the same verification split as `reagent-migration`: the agent runs noninteractive gates and records exact command + result; it drives the boot smoke through a connected runtime when one is present; otherwise it hands the programmer one concise interactive smoke checklist and reports that item as pending rather than claiming completion. Normal platform permissions and sandboxing continue to govern command execution—do not recreate them as skill-local ceremony.

Make one normal-operation document own this posture and have the router/leaves point to it briefly. Delete the repeated author-runs/paste-loop and sandbox-exception prose. Add small behavioural evals that grade the outcome, not a codemod: a Type-A app proceeds through edit + compile/test without asking for pasted output, and a mixed Type-A/Type-B app runs the safe work then pauses once on the unresolved semantic decision.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:56-61` says Type A is automatic, then adds a blocking sweep acknowledgement and a blanket author-only execution rule plus a sandbox exception.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:75,96-100` stops after the dependency edit and delegates compile/test/smoke back to the programmer.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:7-21` requires a real abort window before every multi-file Type-A sweep.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/kickoff-prompt.md:30`, `references/sequencing.md:178-187`, `references/setup.md:20,121`, and `references/runtime-smoke-test.md:46` repeat the paste-loop contract.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md` frontmatter permits search/provenance only; compare `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:31-43`, which permits and explains `npm`, `npx`, `clojure`, and `shadow-cljs`.
- `skills/README.md:191-205` records the inconsistent verification postures; `skills/README.md:261-270` explicitly says to trust the invoker and blesses the routine command wildcards.
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:3157-3200` assigns compile, tests, and application smoke to the agent performing the migration.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/evals/evals.json:1-27` contains 19 routing fixtures and no behavioural fixture. `skills/reagent-migration/evals/evals.json` demonstrates the existing trigger + behavioural convention.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/README.md:48` says no real end-to-end run; `spec/improving.md:53` says one substantial real migration produced roughly two dozen generic findings.
- History locates the accretion: `84f2e0489c` introduced the blanket no-execution rule; `6cc38547ae` added the orchestrated exception; later commits repeatedly repaired API and runtime guidance without adding an end-to-end behavioural check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An explicit request to migrate the current repo authorizes Type-A edits without a second acknowledgement. Progress still names the rule, matched scope, and representative diff shape before or as the sweep begins.
- The skill discovers and runs the nearest project-owned noninteractive install/compile/test gates under the host agent's normal permission model. Its frontmatter permits the routine commands needed for the supported project shapes.
- The skill does not ask the programmer to copy/paste output that the agent can obtain directly. Exact commands, exits, and relevant results appear in the migration report.
- Type-B rewrites remain ask-first. The agent inventories them, performs independent Type-A work, and presents unresolved decisions in one batch rather than interrupting per site.
- A connected live runtime may be driven for the prescribed state/trace smoke. Without one, the report clearly says the interactive smoke is pending and gives one compact checklist; it does not claim migration complete.
- The execution posture has one normal-operation owner. `SKILL.md`, kickoff, setup, sequencing, runtime-smoke, output format, `skills/README.md`, and the skill meta-docs agree without restating a sandbox taxonomy.
- Behavioural evals cover at least: (1) a Type-A-only migration that proceeds through verification without a paste loop; (2) a mixed migration that pauses only for a real Type-B choice; and (3) no false completion when interactive runtime evidence is unavailable.
- Published status text is reconciled with the recorded real migration evidence.
- Existing API/rule citation and package/eval structural gates remain green, with focused regression coverage for the changed execution contract.

## Non-goals

- No compatibility shim, deprecated-v1 runtime path, or change to re-frame2 semantics.
- No codemod, `migrate.bb`, generated rewrite engine, or bespoke migration harness.
- No weakening of Type-B review, smallest-diff discipline, or opt-in O-rule boundaries.
- No execution of destructive, privileged, deployment, or unrelated commands; this concerns routine project-owned migration gates only.
- No requirement to automate a browser/visual smoke when no connected runtime exists.
- No new exhaustive prose or per-tool policy matrix.

## Related beads

No duplicate was found in all-status searches over `surface-review`, `re-frame-migration`, `author runs`, `arbitrary-code execution`, `mass rewrite`, `trigger-only`, `end-to-end`, and `Q14`.

`rf2-r4j91` (closed) concerns the separate Reagent→Hicasso migration surface; it is adjacent only because that sibling skill now demonstrates the recommended noninteractive-gates / programmer-visual split.

title: surface-review(examples-real-apps): make offline Conduit writes survive the refetch they cause
description:
## Scope

Make both RealWorld examples honest end-to-end offline SPAs by turning the existing shared in-process Conduit demo backend into a small deterministic stateful model for the API routes the apps already use. Cover `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs`, the two thin app-local managed-HTTP override seams, the external RealWorld test wrappers, and the two READMEs where they describe offline behavior. Keep the managed-HTTP and Resources application architectures separate and directly readable; the shared backend remains the only comparison seam.

## Findings

The applications themselves exercise a credible breadth of SPA composition: boot and frame scope, URL-owned routing and guards, auth/session restore, schemas, machines, flows, managed HTTP, resources/mutations, pagination, optimistic writes, comments, profiles, settings, editor navigation, and SSR payload policy. They compile as standalone builds and have large headless integration wrappers outside the test-free examples tree.

The production demo backend does not preserve any write. `payload-for-request` is a one-request lookup over immutable `articles`, `favorited`, and `user` values. POST/PUT/DELETE branches manufacture valid response envelopes but never produce a new backend state. Subsequent GETs always read the seed corpus:

- create returns a derived slug but never inserts it; GET of an unknown slug silently falls back to the first article, so create-then-navigate can render `hello-conduit` at the new URL;
- update and delete do not change later detail or list reads;
- post-comment returns a random-id comment while GET comments is always `[]`, and delete changes nothing;
- favorite/unfavorite echo the requested flag but later article/list reads use the original articles and the Favorited tab is a fixed `take-nth` subset;
- follow/unfollow echo a flag but later profile reads always return `following false`, while the feed is permanently empty;
- settings PUT returns the original static user, and tag/author list query params do not filter the corpus.

This is most damaging in the Resources sibling because its headline is the automatic `read -> write -> invalidate -> refetch` loop. Post-comment deliberately does not populate a partial list; it invalidates comments and trusts the refetch as authoritative. The shipped offline backend answers that refetch with `[]`, so a successful comment disappears. Favorite explicitly refetches lists/feed "to truth", but the backend's truth is the pre-write seed. Fixing the client to suppress those refetches would hide the evidence rather than repair it.

The test surface misses the contradiction. `realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs` calls the pure router once per assertion and checks envelope shape, never write-then-read state. The resources integration wrapper replaces `:rf.http/managed` with a request-capture function and manually supplies every reply; its comment test asserts that a refetch starts but never settles that refetch from the production demo backend. The HTTP wrapper likewise installs bespoke canned stubs. Compile coverage proves buildability, not this user journey, and no current example wrapper mounts the DOM.

History explains the false confidence. Commit `02e6630851` consolidated two drifting fake backends and correctly fixed request routing and response envelopes, but its claim that create/update/delete/favorite/follow/settings "now actually work" was only pinned one request at a time. The shared backend is the right ownership boundary; it needs temporal semantics, not another copy or another abstraction.

## Recommended Action

Keep one shared backend, but express it as ordinary pure data plus one pure transition: seeded backend state + managed-request args -> next state + success/failure reply. Let each launched demo own an explicit, resettable instance of that state and keep `respond` as the thin adapter into the existing canned-success/canned-failure effects and 20 ms deferred reply path. Use deterministic counters/timestamps instead of `rand-int`, and make test/app reset boundaries explicit so hot reload, a fresh mount, and separate frames/tests cannot inherit accidental state.

Implement only the Conduit subset already called by these apps: login/session restore/settings, article CRUD, comments, favorite membership/counts, follow relationships/feed, profiles, tags, current-state list filtering, and limit/offset pagination. Missing article/comment routes should return an explicit Conduit-shaped 4xx failure rather than a plausible first record. Preserve the existing wire schemas, classification, bearer interceptor, frame routing, and offline/no-network default.

Replace the backend's one-shot contract tests with sequential transition tests, then add a focused full-frame receipt for each app-local fx seam using the production demo backend rather than a bespoke canned reply. The Resources receipt should prove a real mutation settles, invalidates, automatically refetches, and leaves the resource at the new server truth. The managed-HTTP receipt should perform the corresponding write and later load through its normal public events. Keep all tests outside `examples/` per repository policy.

Refresh the README claims and give readers one short try-it journey whose result survives refetch/navigation. Do not turn the backend into an example framework; the simple state transition is part of this example's evidence.

## Evidence

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/README.md:3,11-13` calls this a complete working blog and names `read -> write -> invalidate -> refetch` as the one idea the example exists to prove.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:106-126` defines immutable article/favorite/user data and makes unknown slugs fall back to the first article.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:128-134` uses `rand-int` for comment IDs; the same file's POST branches at 190-237 return envelopes without updating any store.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:239-255` makes feed/comments fixed empty responses, serves Favorited from a static subset, sends tag/author queries through the full article vector, and always reads profiles as not-following.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:163-202` says favorite reconciliation refetches lists/feed to truth; lines 243-271 intentionally make comment writes invalidate and refetch rather than populate a partial collection.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:90-98,183-186` replaces the live transport with request capture. Its comment case at 1264-1300 hand-injects the write reply and only asserts that refetch began.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs:20-31` explicitly treats the backend as a pure URL/method-to-payload function. Lines 88-139 assert isolated favorite/comment/list envelopes, not any later read.
- `examples/TESTING.md:5,18-23` records the test-free source-tree policy, external headless wrappers, and the distinction between compile coverage and browser behavior.
- Commit `02e6630851` is the backend's entire path history: it centralized the correct seam and added one-shot shape tests, but no state sequence.
- Full title/description searches across open and closed beads for demo/stateful/offline backend, `payload-for-request`, write persistence, mutation refetch, comment disappearance, and favorite reversion found no matching task.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The offline backend has a deterministic seeded state and one canonical transition used by both app-local fx ids; identical fresh-state request sequences produce identical replies and state in both variants.
- Article create -> GET-by-new-slug/list/author-filter, update -> later GET, and delete -> later GET/list are covered sequentially. Unknown/deleted slugs fail explicitly and never return the first seed article.
- Comment POST -> GET includes the exact saved comment and deterministic id; DELETE -> GET removes it. A Resources full-frame test uses the real demo fx and proves the invalidation-triggered comments refetch settles with that new collection.
- Favorite/unfavorite persist through detail, global/tag/author lists, and the acting user's Favorited list with correct counts. Follow/unfollow persist through profile reads and affect the demo feed consistently. Settings changes survive later user/profile reads, and a saved valid demo token can restore the session while invalid/missing credentials fail predictably.
- Tag, author, favorited, feed, limit, and offset query semantics are applied to current backend state, and each `articlesCount` describes the filtered set rather than the seed corpus or page size.
- Backend instances/reset are explicit and isolated for fresh launches and tests; generated values are deterministic; no raw timer replaces the existing `:dispatch-later`-backed canned reply path.
- At least one automated full-frame path per app variant uses its production demo override rather than a bespoke response stub and proves a write remains observable after a later normal read. Tests remain outside `examples/` and include a negative control that fails if the transition result is discarded or reads consult the seed constants.
- Both RealWorld builds compile warning-free, the focused CLJS suites pass, and README claims/try-it steps describe only behavior the served offline apps now retain across refetch and navigation.

## Non-goals

- No full Conduit server, database, network listener, service worker, persistence across browser reload beyond the existing demo-token contract, multi-user authorization system, or production backend replacement.
- No generic mock-server library, request-fixture DSL, compatibility layer, generated client, example framework, or new framework runtime API.
- No sharing of routes, handlers, subscriptions, views, app-db slices, or feature namespaces between the managed-HTTP and Resources variants; their architectural comparison stays explicit.
- No weakening/bypassing resource invalidation, pinning stale optimistic data, or changing cache semantics to accommodate a stateless backend.
- No broad visual redesign, route-id rename, source-layout reorganization, or exhaustive per-page browser suite.
- No duplicate `dev:example` launch-command standardization; the adjacent examples-core/capabilities tasks own that documentation family and this task is about temporal app behavior.

## Related beads

- `rf2-y8jjk` (open) makes active-route resource replanning authoritative; it is complementary. That task repairs which reads are planned after identity changes, while this task makes the backend truth those reads receive reflect prior writes.
- `rf2-8cevm` (closed) established the test-free examples policy; sequential and full-frame receipts stay in the external adapter test tree.
- `rf2-czvc` (closed) fixed RealWorld editor settle races through external production-source wrappers; it is the precedent for testing a real example flow rather than a copied miniature.
- `rf2-0vav5.1` (closed) supplies derived compile coverage for every declared example build; compile remains necessary but cannot prove write/read causality.
- `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` (open) standardize one-command launch documentation for adjacent example families; they do not cover backend state or this outcome.

Negative control: one deftest that mutates, then asserts the seed vector is unchanged AND the read differs. Do not touch auth.cljs / routing.cljs (y8jjk files). A is DISPATCHABLE now.

Each app seam holds its own defonce'd instance, so the two demos never share a world and fresh-state is the explicit reset boundary. The architectures stay separate: the backend is still the only seam, and nothing moved across it.

HOW THE WRITE-SURVIVES-REFETCH BEHAVIOUR WAS DEMONSTRATED (a compile pass is not that proof):

1. Sequential tests, not shape assertions. The one-shot contract suite in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs is replaced by 15 tests / 115 assertions that each WRITE and then READ BACK through a separate, normal request. The headline test posts a comment and asserts the exact saved comment (id, body, timestamps) is in the collection the next GET returns, and favourites an article and asserts the detail read AND the global list read both still say favourited with the count the write produced -- the two reads that used to revert it. Also covered sequentially: create -> GET-by-new-slug/list/author-filter/tags, update -> later GET, delete -> later GET/list with the deleted slug 404ing, comment DELETE -> GET, favourite through detail/global/tag/author/Favorited-tab with counts, follow -> profile read + feed, settings -> later user/profile reads including a username change moving the byline, and session restore succeeding only for a token that world issued.

Both app fx ids call this one transition, so pinning it pins both.

5. Every reply is Malli-validated against the shared wire schemas, since the canned-success fx never runs :decode and nothing else would catch drift off the Conduit contract.

title: surface-review(machines-viz): make registered topology one-click copyable as Mermaid
description:
## Scope

Complete the existing Mermaid workflow from tools/machines-viz's pure `day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.mermaid/emit` function to Xray's existing Static Machines definition-detail header. Add one accessible, direct "Copy Mermaid" action for the currently selected registered machine, focused integration coverage, and the small documentation update that makes the workflow discoverable. Keep `MachineChart` presentation-only: the Xray host already owns the selected definition and owns the user gesture.

## Findings

Machines-Viz has a mature producer but no reachable workflow. `mermaid/emit` accepts the normalised definition and returns a fenced `stateDiagram-v2` block; its dedicated corpus covers grammar, validation, parallel/compound topology, and lossy-semantics warnings. `export/copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` also exists, but its DOM-element contract is an exporter convenience rather than a host-level action.

The repository has no production call site for either `mermaid/emit` or `copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` outside Machines-Viz itself. Xray's own machine-inspector spec still labels "Copy machine as PNG / SVG / Mermaid" as "Not built". Consequently a capability explicitly described for README files, pull requests, design docs, and AI-pair chat is available only to someone who writes CLJS around the library API.

The lowest-friction host is already present. Xray's Static Machines surface is the event-independent browse of every registered machine; its definition-detail view already subscribes to the selected machine's exact definition and renders a compact header containing its id, source coordinate, state count, and live count. Mermaid is static topology, so this is a better fit than the Dynamic Machine panel's deliberately narrow three-part forensic view.

The other shipped routes do not close this gap. The share viewer is an inbound, read-only URL consumer; it must be built and self-hosted, and share encoding requires an explicit host because there is no Day8 deployment. The manifests expose tests and a viewer build but no end-user command or standalone launch path. Xray's panel gallery and machine-epochs testbed provide rich visual fixtures, yet neither exposes the Mermaid exporter.

History makes the disconnect explicit: rf2-deo2i shipped the emitter, rf2-sqhqu moved ownership into Machines-Viz, and rf2-8d7w1 shipped the export/viewer primitives. rf2-nugvv later removed Xray's heavy Share modal and URL/session-posture machinery, leaving the copy formats recorded as unbuilt. Reintroducing that modal would repeat the wrong abstraction; a single explicit copy action needs none of it.

Exact tracker searches for "machines-viz", "Copy machine", "Mermaid export", "machine mermaid", "machine topology", "standalone viewer", and related terms found no existing bead for this outcome.

## Recommended Action

Add one "Copy Mermaid" control to the selected machine's Static Machines detail header. On activation, pass the selected definition directly to `mermaid/emit` and copy that exact fenced string through a small, testable clipboard effect. Do not make the renderer rediscover registry state and do not require a rendered chart DOM node.

Make the gesture immediate: no confirmation modal and no format chooser. Give it a clear accessible name and a minimal non-modal success/failure status so a rejected or unavailable clipboard does not look successful. Omit or disable the action when no valid definition is available.

Use an existing representative Static Machines/panel-gallery fixture for the integration proof. Assert the clipboard payload equals `(mermaid/emit definition)`; the emitter's existing corpus remains the authority for diagram semantics.

Update the Machines-Viz and Xray documentation just enough to name this as the normal path for copying a registered topology into Markdown or an AI conversation, and replace the stale "Not built" statement for Mermaid only.

## Evidence

- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid.cljc:946` defines the pure `emit` API and its fenced Markdown contract.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/export.cljs:561-589` defines the chart-element wrapper and clipboard helper.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2078-2099` says Mermaid output is for GitHub, PRs, Notion, and other Mermaid-aware consumers and identifies `mermaid/emit` as the load-bearing pure function.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/000-Vision.md:284-300` explicitly names README and AI-pair chat replies as the static Mermaid surface.
- A repository-wide source search finds no production use of `mermaid/emit`, `chart-as-mermaid`, or `copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` outside Machines-Viz; references elsewhere are documentation only.
- `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1829-1842` explicitly marks the copy-as formats "Not built".
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/definition_detail.cljs:52-90` is the existing selected-machine header, and lines 209-254 already hold the selected definition in the host view.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/panel.cljs:110-161` composes registered ids, definitions, snapshots, and selection for that surface; no new registry query is needed.

title: surface-review(testbed-support): retire checkout-root plumbing now the endpoint resolves source files
description:
## Scope

Retire the repository-internal browser-side checkout-root pipeline from `tools/testbed-support/**` and its direct Xray, Story, example, launcher, Shadow, and documentation consumers. Make the already-wired JVM `POST /__rf-open-in-editor` endpoint the one source-file resolver for repository-owned dev testbeds, and return `re-frame.testbed.story-host` to its single job: live-app / Story-shell React-root handoff and hash routing.

Keep the generic public `:rf.story/project-root` / `:rf.xray/project-root` options and the client URI fallback available to external/non-shadow hosts. This is a removal of redundant repository testbed setup, not a redesign of the shipped open-in-editor contract.

## Findings

1. The surface carries two complete paths for the same repository dev workflow. `re-frame.testbed.config` derives an absolute source root in the browser from `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT` or `?checkout-root=`, while `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server` resolves the original relative coordinate against the live JVM classpath at request time. The endpoint is already attached to every dev-http port used by all twelve builds that seed the checkout-root define.
2. The older path makes each new testbed coordinate the same fact in several places: a literal source subdirectory in the CLJS consumer, a per-build Closure define in `shadow-cljs.edn`, the launcher environment export, and related docs/tests. Current consumers repeat seven Xray resolver/configure calls and five Story `:source-subdir` calls even though endpoint resolution needs none of them.
3. The cost is material for a private helper. `config.cljs` is 97 lines and its 41-test suite is 519 lines: 616 of `tools/testbed-support`'s 2,346 tracked lines (26%), before counting Story-host option tests, twelve Closure-define blocks, launcher/static-export checks, and prose across twenty tracked reference files.
4. No live caller was found for the query escape hatch. Repository-wide tracked searches for `checkout-root` find only the resolver, tests, configuration, and explanatory prose; no script emits a `?checkout-root=` URL and no runtime outside this internal support path reads it.
5. This is not a compatibility surface. `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` and the README explicitly say the tool is dev-only and not published, and `spec/api-manifest.edn` / `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` contain no `re-frame.testbed.*` row. The private two-arity Story-host option can be deleted rather than shimmed.
6. History explains the overlap. Commit `3b4aed8b4e` (`rf2-5dphw`, 2026-05-31) introduced browser checkout-root plumbing to replace hardcoded personal paths; commit `bc895415b8` (`rf2-wn3bh`, 2026-06-14) later added the zero-config runtime endpoint and wired every testbed port, but did not retire the first mechanism. Five later commits still touched the config source/tests, including malformed-override repair, while endpoint behavior was unaffected.
7. The endpoint suite already owns classpath resolution, cwd fallback, query handling, launch behavior, JSON, and the loopback/method/origin boundary. The useful missing proof is consumer-shaped: real relative Story and Xray coordinates should resolve through that endpoint with both tool project-root atoms unset.

## Recommended Action

- Delete `re-frame.testbed.config` and `config_cljs_test.cljs` outright.
- Remove source-root configuration from `re-frame.testbed.story-host`; keep one `mount-with-hash-routing!` call shape taking only the live root view, and migrate all repository consumers to it without an alias or compatibility arity.
- Remove testbed-only `resolve-source-root` helpers and `xray-config/configure! {:rf.xray/project-root ...}` boot writes from the seven Xray consumers.
- Stop `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs` from deriving/exporting `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, and remove the twelve matching Closure defines plus now-vacuous static-export sentinel checks/prose. Preserve the launcher's explicit-build, de-duplication, process, and URL-printing behavior.
- Keep every affected dev-http entry wired to `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler`. Add one bounded consumer-shaped witness using representative real Story and Xray relative coordinates, with launch stubbed so no editor opens.
- Rewrite the support README around the two remaining responsibilities and show the minimal new-testbed path: wire the handler, call the one-arity host when Story routing is needed, and launch the build. Do not introduce a replacement config layer.

## Evidence

- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/config.cljs`: 97-line query/define/path resolver whose only public operation is `resolve-source-root`.
- `tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/config_cljs_test.cljs`: 519 lines / 41 tests, including private parser and slash-normalisation contracts.
- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs:52-77`: optional `:source-subdir` exists only to invoke the config resolver before mounting.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:479-628`: fourteen dev-http entries already use the JVM endpoint handler; lines 1317-1958 separately repeat twelve checkout-root Closure defines for the affected builds.
- `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs:7-18,261-283`: the launcher exports the root solely for that define; its independently useful build/URL manifest does not need the value.
- `tools/xray/testbeds/{two_frame_isolation,standard_epochs,routes_epochs,machine_epochs,edn_inspector,managed_http,panel_gallery}/core.cljs`: seven identical resolver/configuration gestures.
- `tools/story/testbeds/{counter_with_stories,login_form,hicasso_counter}/core.cljs` and the login/nine-states example hosts: five literal `:source-subdir` options.
- `tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server_test.clj:17-54`: the server already proves relative classpath files resolve to real on-disk paths; the remainder covers the endpoint boundary and launch result shapes.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` open-in-editor launch modes: the endpoint is the preferred zero-config runtime resolver; project-root composition belongs to the generic URI fallback.
- `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` plus the absent API-manifest rows: local dev/test support, not a published facade.
- Exact current/closed tracker title searches and issue-record scans for testbed-support, checkout-root, `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, `resolve-source-root`, source-root resolver, and open-in-editor endpoint found no outcome bead owning this retirement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No tracked source, build config, script, test, or current documentation references `re-frame.testbed.config`, `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, `?checkout-root=`, or the deleted checkout-root Closure define. The config namespace and its dedicated test namespace are gone.
2. `mount-with-hash-routing!` has one repository-internal call shape and owns only listener/root handoff plus hash selection. All Story/example consumers call it without source-root options; all Xray testbeds boot without testbed-support project-root resolution.
3. `npm run dev -- <build-id>` retains explicit build forwarding, order-preserving de-duplication, URL reporting, cwd, signal, and exit semantics, but no longer computes or exports an absolute checkout path.
4. All twelve formerly seeded builds remain served by dev-http entries using `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler`. With Story and Xray project-root config unset, one real relative Story coordinate and one real relative Xray coordinate reach the handler and resolve to the intended existing file; the test stubs `launch!` and proves the resolved argument without opening an editor.
5. The generic Story/Xray project-root configuration APIs, endpoint-preferred/URI-fallback client rule, endpoint path/query/method/security contract, and `launch-editor` behavior are unchanged. No public facade symbol or API-manifest row is added.
6. The focused testbed-support JVM, Node, and DOM suites plus the launcher/static-build checks pass after deleting the obsolete assertions. A negative witness demonstrates that removing the dev-http handler (not removing checkout-root plumbing) breaks the representative relative-coordinate path.
7. The README and direct consumer comments teach the endpoint-backed one-command workflow and contain no replacement root-discovery convention, generated manifest, compatibility note, or manual absolute-path recipe.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning the endpoint, its loopback security boundary, query grammar, process timeout/drain logic, editor vocabulary, or `launch-editor` dependency.
- Removing or changing the generic `:rf.story/project-root`, `:rf.xray/project-root`, custom editor URI, or URI fallback APIs for external/static/non-shadow hosts.
- Auto-discovering source roots, scanning namespaces, generating Shadow config, or creating a new testbed registry/config DSL.
- Adding a facade namespace, deprecated alias, compatibility arity, environment-variable fallback, warning, or migration mode for this unpublished helper.
- Refactoring unrelated frame boot, testbed application code, port allocation, build IDs, or the `DEV_HTTP` URL manifest.
- Enabling local-editor links in published static Story exports.

## Related beads

- `rf2-in6c4` (closed) owns compile-gate coverage for testbed builds; it does not own developer setup or source resolution.
- `rf2-7dewo` (open) owns Story variant vocabulary convergence; no overlap with Story-host mounting or open-in-editor setup.
- Historical commit-linked `rf2-5dphw` introduced the checkout-root path and `rf2-wn3bh` introduced the endpoint that superseded its repository-dev purpose; neither is present as a current tracker record.
- No matching open, in-progress, deferred, or closed outcome bead was found.

title: surface-review(examples-core): make every documented core run command launch a real page
description:
## Scope

Make the primary examples/core learning path genuinely one-command runnable from the instructions programmers and coding agents actually encounter. Scope is the core catalogue landing copy in examples/README.md, the seven core README carriers (counter, flows, login, managed_http_counter, notebook, todomvc, and seven_guis), and the existing npm run dev:example runner/manifest tests only as needed to pin that documented contract.

The outcome is not a new runner. The repository already has the right one. The outcome is that every default core run recipe invokes it and reaches a real page with the required host assets.

## Findings

The application code is broadly coherent and current: the 12 core builds use the reg-event / reg-sub / reg-view idiom, explicit frame scope, the init! plus lazy frame-root mount shape (with the intentional pre-created-frame exception for frame-local flows), namespaced registrations, and external headless wrappers where behavior needs coverage. test:examples-compile derives every declared :examples/* build and rejects compile errors and warnings.

The first-contact run path is the material gap. examples/README.md says any example runs with shadow-cljs watch BUILD-ID, and every core README repeats a bare shadow-cljs watch examples/... command. Those commands compile to implementation/out/examples/ID but do not stage the colocated index.html, copy _shared, copy per-example assets, or serve that output on a discoverable URL. The core builds also have no matching generic :dev-http roots. Consequently:

- opening a source index.html cannot find its relative main.js;
- opening an output directory has no host page unless the user manually copies it;
- TodoMVC additionally misses base.css and index.css from node_modules;
- managed-http-counter additionally misses api/inc.json, so its headline success request becomes a 404;
- phrases such as "open the served page" and "open index.html against the watch build" describe a page the documented command did not assemble.

This is inconsistent inside the same catalogue. The UIx READMEs already teach npm run dev:example -- examples/ID, which cleans and stages the selected output, starts the watch, serves it on a free loopback port, and prints the URL.

History explains the split. Commit a4636f853f (rf2-pdo5mx) introduced serve-example.cjs, the npm entry point, manifest derivation, staging tests, and migrated the UIx docs. The later concept reorganisation at 210f812fe2 installed the raw-watch sentence in the new catalogue/core READMEs and lost the complete staging-and-serving recipe. Subsequent runner work made the canonical path stronger, not obsolete: 1d62730eb1 added the clean-stage boundary, 8365a4f32e centralised asset exceptions, and the current staging tests explicitly pin TodoMVC CSS and managed-http-counter's JSON fixture.

## Recommended Action

Bless one default command for the core family:

    npm run dev:example -- examples/BUILD-ID

Run it from implementation/. Put one concise explanation on the catalogue landing page: it watches, stages the host/assets, serves on a free port, and prints the URL. Give each core README its exact copy-paste command; the 7GUIs README can show one command and say to substitute the other listed build ids. Use the same runner for the login Story build if it is documented as a default runnable path.

Keep raw shadow-cljs watch only in one clearly labelled advanced/manual note if it still earns a place, and state the full copy/stage/serve obligation there. Do not repeat that troubleshooting ceremony in every example.

Extend the existing listStandaloneExamples staging test just enough to pin that all 12 documented core build ids resolve to a host page. Reuse the existing runner, manifest, and script-policy lane; do not add another wrapper or a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- examples/README.md:11 advertises raw watch for every example.
- Bare raw-watch recipes remain in examples/core/counter/README.md:115, flows/README.md:61, login/README.md:84, managed_http_counter/README.md:50, notebook/README.md:159, todomvc/README.md:71, and seven_guis/README.md:59.
- Every core host page loads relative main.js; the build outputs are separately declared under implementation/out/examples/* in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.
- implementation/package.json already exposes dev:example.
- examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs documents and implements clean, stage, watch, serve, and URL reporting.
- examples/scripts/examples-asset-manifest.cjs records the two core-only staging obligations: TodoMVC CSS and managed-http-counter api/inc.json.
- implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs pins clean-before-stage, manifest projection, and those special assets, but its runnable-manifest assertion currently names only the three UIx examples.
- npm run dev:example -- --list currently returns all core ids: counter, flows, login, managed-http-counter, notebook, todomvc, temperature, flight-booker, timer, crud, circle-drawer, and cells.
- examples/TESTING.md confirms compile coverage is not a served-page smoke; examples remain test-free and behavior wrappers live outside the tree.
- Searches across open and closed bead titles/descriptions for serve-example, dev:example, core example run commands, and surface-review(examples-core) found no live duplicate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From implementation/, each documented core command uses npm run dev:example -- examples/ID and is copy-pasteable without an unstated copy, staging, or server step.
2. examples/README.md names that command as the default route and explains it once, tersely. Each core README points to the exact build id; all six non-counter 7GUIs ids are discoverable from its README.
3. No bare shadow-cljs watch examples/... remains in the scoped core docs as the default run recipe. Any retained raw-watch form is explicitly advanced/manual and names the missing staging and serving work.
4. The existing staging/runner test suite asserts that all 12 documented core builds appear in listStandaloneExamples() with an existing host page. The assertion has a non-vacuous failure if one core build falls out of the runner.
5. A clean run of the documented counter command serves the current page and main.js on the printed URL; minus and plus update the displayed count.
6. Existing staging tests prove TodoMVC's two CSS assets and managed-http-counter's api/inc.json land under their clean output roots. npm run test:script-policy, the relevant docs link/slug gates, and npm run dev:example -- --list pass.
7. The final change stays documentation-and-existing-runner focused; it does not introduce a second launcher or per-example browser matrix.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the example applications, their API idioms, or their tutorial narratives.
- Adding a browser smoke for every core example or reversing the test-free-examples policy.
- Turning gallery examples into independent greenfield project templates; tools/template remains that path.
- Abstracting the intentionally visible mount code into a shared helper.
- Sweeping the individual READMEs under capabilities, patterns, real-apps, or substrates in this task, beyond correcting the shared catalogue entry.

## Related beads

- rf2-pdo5mx - introduced the one-command example runner and migrated the UIx learning path.
- rf2-rg2tze - made the runner clean the selected output before staging.
- rf2-cq6va5 / rf2-phpbo8 - pinned and centralised per-example runtime assets.
- rf2-8cevm - established the test-free examples policy; this task preserves it.
- rf2-0vav5.1 - introduced derived compile coverage for declared example builds; compile coverage remains complementary to, not a replacement for, a runnable documented page.

Four occurrences fixed.

It now pins 12 core + 8 capability + the 3 substrate ids to a resolvable host page, plus a non-vacuity test on the three roster lengths. TEETH PROVEN: replacing one roster id with a non-existent build gives captured exit 1 naming it and the exact documented command, PASS count 27 to 26 (scoped, no suite crash). title: surface-review(examples-capabilities): make every capability README launch the real one-command app
description:
## Scope

Make the capabilities catalogue and all eight examples/capabilities/** README launch recipes copyable from a clean checkout. Cover machines/state_machine_walkthrough, routing/routing, resources/{resources,infinite_feed,linearlite}, ssr/{ssr,resources_ssr,ssr_streaming}, and the capabilities entry point in examples/README.md. Keep the existing examples and the existing runner; this is an executable-documentation correction, not a new example framework.

## Findings

- Every capability README still leads with raw "shadow-cljs watch examples/<id>" and then asks the reader to serve or open some combination of source and build output. The root catalogue makes the same blanket claim for every example.
- That is not a complete runnable recipe. Each source index.html references both main.js and _shared assets, while the browser builds emit main.js under implementation/out/examples/<id>. Seven of these examples have no dedicated dev-http root that composes those trees. Linearlite is the lone special case with a hard-coded 8044 dev-http entry, so its README works differently from every sibling.
- The repository already has the canonical solution: "npm run dev:example -- examples/<id>". The runner cleans the selected output, stages that example's real index.html and shared assets, starts watch/compile, serves loopback on a free port, and prints the exact URL.
- The runner derives its standalone-build list from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Its current --list output includes all eight capability build ids, and the independent compile gate derives and sweeps the same eight builds.
- History explains the drift. Commit a4636f853f (rf2-pdo5mx, 2026-06-09) introduced the one-command runner and migrated the then-UIx READMEs only. The concept-layout move in 210f812fe2 (2026-06-28) and later capability README rewrites retained the older recipes. The runtime code, mount idioms, and build declarations are already consistent; the learning front door is the stale part.

## Recommended Action

Replace each capability README's primary How to run recipe with the exact npm dev:example command for its declared build id, run from implementation/. Say that the command stages the page, watches it, selects a free local port, and prints the URL; for the three SSR examples, make explicit that the runner stages the checked-in baked SSR index rather than requiring the reader to manually combine it with the bundle. Remove the hard-coded Linearlite-only 8044 path from the primary flow.

Update examples/README.md so its generic launch instruction names the same runner. Raw shadow-cljs watch may remain only as an explicitly advanced compiler-only path that does not pretend to stage or serve a page. Reuse the runner and its manifest derivation as-is unless an actual failing capability build proves a small runner defect.

- All eight index.html files reference main.js and _shared/css/style.css plus _shared/img/favicon.svg.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1557-1784 declares all eight builds and emits each to implementation/out/examples/<id>; only the top-level dev-http map at lines 603-611 gives Linearlite a composed source/output server.
- implementation/package.json:53 exposes dev:example.

- examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:222-347 derives build id, output directory, init namespace, source folder, index page, and staged assets from shadow-cljs.edn.
- "node ../examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs --list" currently lists examples/state-machine-walkthrough, examples/routing, examples/resources, examples/infinite-feed, examples/linearlite, examples/ssr, examples/resources-ssr, and examples/ssr-streaming.
- "node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list" independently lists the same eight builds, and examples/TESTING.md documents the all-build compile and asset-policy gates.
- Git history for serve-example.cjs begins at a4636f853f with the explicit outcome "one-command runnable"; that commit touched only the old UIx README slice, not these capability READMEs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the eight capability README files has one primary, copy-paste command of the form "npm run dev:example -- examples/<correct-build-id>" from implementation/.
- Each recipe tells the reader to open the URL printed by the runner; none leaves them to infer how to combine source index.html, output main.js, and _shared assets, and Linearlite no longer needs special knowledge of port 8044.
- examples/README.md teaches the same canonical command and keeps its per-row build ids consistent with it.
- "npm run dev:example -- --list" includes all eight capability ids, and a representative launch from each family (machines, routing, resources, SSR) serves HTTP 200 for index.html, main.js, and the shared stylesheet from one printed origin.
- "npm run test:examples-compile" and the existing example staging/script-policy tests remain green; README links pass the existing documentation link check.
- The capability narratives, source code, build ids, baked SSR payloads, and test-free examples policy are unchanged.
- No new launcher, hard-coded capability roster, README generator, or CI job is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Refactoring machine, resource, routing, SSR, mount, or hydration code.
- Adding examples, turning the catalogue into an exhaustive showcase, or sharing application code between examples.
- Adding per-example Playwright specs or changing the external-wrapper testing policy.
- Allocating a fixed dev-http port to every example.
- Replacing the manifest-derived runner with a framework, template system, or second build registry.
