title: surface-review(mcp-base): return the pair-only epoch diff codec to Pair-MCP
description:
## Scope

Restore tools/mcp-base to its documented role as the small library of primitives shared by the shipped MCP servers. Move the epoch :db-after diff codec and its section-grouping helper, specs, tests, Closure define, and conformance ownership from re-frame.mcp-base into tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. Preserve Pair-MCP's tool names, arguments, result shapes, :rf.mcp/diff-from wire representation, defaults, ordering, and errors.

## Findings

- The base contract says it contains genuinely cross-cutting primitives consumed by every MCP server and explicitly says a primitive stays consumer-side until a second consumer needs it.
- Current production imports contradict that boundary: Pair-MCP alone requires re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode; Story-MCP has no source reference. section-grouping is referenced only by diff-encode.
- These namespaces are substantial: 1,324 of 4,633 physical base source lines (28.6%), plus 1,276 focused test lines, two spec pages, Malli-specific validation/test setup, and Pair/global Closure-define wiring.
- The conformance suite's use of the builder is test evidence for Pair's wire shape, not an independent runtime consumer.
- History confirms this was never a stable cross-server seam: c4abf7f799 moved Pair's diff block into the new base, while neither Story-MCP nor the former Causa-MCP ever imported the namespace; the later section-grouping surface likewise serves only Pair epoch responses.
- Keeping a single-consumer codec in the common jar enlarges the API downstream MCP authors must understand, makes Pair's epoch representation look like a cross-MCP obligation, and violates the package's own admission rule.

## Recommended Action

Rehome the two pure .cljc namespaces under Pair-MCP with Pair-owned names, carrying their JVM/CLJS tests and specs with them. Retarget Pair production calls, its Closure define, and the wire-vocabulary conformance witness to that implementation. Remove the namespaces, Malli-only diff setup, focused tests, and index rows from mcp-base. Keep the existing :rf.mcp/diff-from vocabulary and observable wire shape stable; vocabulary constants intentionally reserved across MCP tools may remain shared.

Do not introduce a generic codec protocol, registry abstraction, forwarding namespace, or compatibility alias. The implementation remains useful; its truthful owner is the only server that emits it.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md:4 calls the library genuinely cross-cutting primitives consumed by every MCP server; lines 107-111 require a second consumer before lifting.
- Only tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs and wire_pipeline.cljs call base-diff functions; no Story-MCP production source imports diff-encode.
- tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc is 911 lines and section_grouping.cljc is 413; their focused JVM tests total 1,276 lines.
- tools/mcp-base/spec/diff-encode.md defines epoch :db-after encoding; section-grouping.md identifies diff-encode as its consumer.
- tools/mcp-base/deps.edn carries Malli for the diff validation suite; Pair/global Shadow configs carry the re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode/validate-patches? production define.
- tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab invokes the builder only to validate Pair's marker schema.
- History: c4abf7f799 introduced mcp-base and moved Pair's implementation; git log -S searches show no Story-MCP or Causa-MCP consumer. Commit 6191a6b316 later removed Causa-MCP.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. day8/re-frame2-mcp-base no longer publishes or documents diff-encode or section-grouping; its source/spec index and test/dependency configuration contain only genuinely shared surfaces.
2. Pair-MCP owns equivalent .cljc encode/decode and section-grouping namespaces. Its production pipeline, default epochs-mode, :rf.mcp/diff-from body, section ordering/classification, error ids, and full-mode pass-through remain unchanged.
3. The complete relocated corpus runs on JVM and CLJS, including map/vector/set round trips, malformed-marker failures, Malli-present validation, Malli-absent or Closure-disabled production behavior, and section losslessness/order.
4. The wire-vocabulary conformance gate exercises the Pair-owned canonical emitter and existing fixtures/schemas without changing the marker's observable wire shape.
5. Pair's local and root Shadow builds use the new Closure-define symbol; no tracked production, test, spec, generated-manifest, or conformance file requires the removed base namespaces.
6. mcp-base JVM/CLJS gates and Pair focused/descriptor/conformance gates pass non-vacuously; a package-content check proves the base jar excludes the pair-only namespaces.
7. No forwarding namespace or deprecated alias preserves the old internal API; current pre-alpha consumers migrate in the same change.

## Non-goals

- Removing diff encoding from Pair-MCP, changing its default, or redesigning the patch/section grammar.
- Renaming :rf.mcp/diff-from, changing epoch records, or changing any tool schema/result.
- Moving genuinely shared args, cursor, cap, dedup, egress, envelope, privacy, vocabulary, or descriptor-manifest primitives out of mcp-base.
- Unifying handler arities, registries, transports, or result-envelope representations.
- Adding a general plugin/codec framework, external runtime dependency, or automated two-consumers policy engine.
- Solving the separate Clojars group-verification/publish blocker.

## Related beads

- rf2-ahjbc is an adjacent open Pair-MCP simplification touching parts of the same tool surface; coordinate file ownership if both are implemented concurrently, but neither blocks the other.
- rf2-uelji is the deferred Clojars first-publish blocker; this task improves package ownership independently.
- Exact current and closed tracker searches for surface-review(mcp-base), epoch diff, pair-only, section grouping, mcp base, diff, and related descriptions found no duplicate outcome.
close_reason: REJECTED AS GOLD-PLATING by the mayor 2026-08-30 22:10:05 AUSEST under the stance, on the read-only triage at d0aabeb73a (premises HOLD; one extra real require found at tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/.../wire_vocab_test.clj:102 plus a 742-line CLJS test the bead did not mention). The boundary argument is true, but the move's hidden cost is disproportionate: the 1,276-line test corpus is JVM .clj with Malli, and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp has NO JVM test lane (its :test alias is a shadow compile), so relocating means a new JVM alias + Malli dep in a CLJS-only npm artefact, a new test.yml job (hot zone), scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh roster + check_jvm_lane_rosters.py bijection edits, and wire-vocab's :local/root switching to Pair (dragging shadow-cljs/js-interop onto its JVM classpath). Cheap alternative, filed as the disposition: one sentence in tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md:107-111 recording diff-encode/section-grouping as a Pair-owned codec hosted in base for its JVM+Malli lane — fold into any later mcp-base prose PR. Mike may override; reopen if so.

title: surface-review(mcp-conformance): make one command explain and run the live compatibility profile
description:
## Scope

Turn the existing repository-level `test:mcp-conformance` runner into the one documented front door for understanding and running MCP compatibility. Preserve its current medium-cost default run, add one explicit opt-in mode that chains the existing hermetic live Pair suite, and make every terminal verdict state which profile actually ran. Limit implementation to the existing runner, its small regression surface, and the MCP testing docs/package entry points needed to make the command copyable; keep the split CI jobs and focused per-suite commands.

## Findings

- The compatibility corpus already has strong teeth. The Node workflows use the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client, SDK-call every advertised tool, validate descriptor classifications and result envelopes, and run real Story and degraded Pair workflows. The JVM wire suite auto-discovers its focused namespaces and combines canonical schemas, fixtures, reachable builders, source pins, near-miss rejection, and cross-encoding checks. The high-leverage need is not another protocol checklist or host matrix.
- There is already a single repository operator command: `npm run test:mcp-conformance` from `implementation/`. It installs/builds prerequisites and chains Story JVM/stdio, Pair compile/tests, the conformance Node inventory, and wire-vocab. Commit `7f1f93234a` created it specifically because the prior workflow required reading CI and invoking commands across four directories.
- The command is not the front door of the artefact it verifies. `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md` still teaches dependency installation plus separate unit, Pair compile/e2e, Story, hermetic-live, and wire-vocab recipes, and never names the existing single command. A reader or coding agent arriving at the conformance package has to reconstruct which recipe means “compatibility”.
- The default command's final verdict loses a load-bearing distinction. `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs` correctly records live rows as `SKIP` when no nREPL port is supplied and explains that the hermetic suite did not run. One level up, `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs` reduces that whole child run to one status row and unconditionally ends with `ALL MCP-CONFORMANCE GATES GREEN`.
- The outer runner's own header says it chains the six PR-time MCP gates, while the same header explicitly excludes the hermetic live suite. CI's Pair conformance job does include that suite after the SDK/degraded rows. The omission is an intentional cost profile, not a missing test, but the terminal success line makes the default profile look complete.
- `TESTING.md` knows the real split: `test:mcp-conformance` is the medium command and `test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite` is a separate expensive command. That distinction lives in a large repository testing catalogue rather than in the command's help/output or the conformance README.
- Existing inventory ownership is sufficient: `scripts/test-all.cjs` owns Node rows, `scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs` owns live rows, and the JVM runner discovers `*_test.clj`. A new manifest, report schema, compliance database, or duplicated roster would add drift without improving compatibility feedback.
- Exact current/closed tracker searches for `surface-review(mcp-conformance)`, `test:mcp-conformance`, `single entry`, `hermetic live`, `SKIP`, and the current all-green sentinel found no bead owning this outcome.

## Recommended Action

Extend the existing `implementation` runner, rather than creating a second orchestrator:

1. Keep the no-argument command as today's medium profile. Its final summary must identify the server/unit + SDK/degraded + wire-vocab layers that passed and show the existing hermetic live Pair suite as `NOT RUN`, with the exact opt-in command beside it. It must not print an unqualified “all MCP conformance gates green” verdict.
2. Add one explicit `--live` mode that runs the same default steps and then invokes the existing `test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite` entry point. A full-green verdict is available only after the hermetic runner observes every registered live sentinel and proves cleanup, preserving its existing exit-code distinction between conformance and orchestration failure.
3. Add side-effect-free `--help` output that names both modes, their prerequisites/cost boundary, what `npm test` inside `tools/mcp-conformance` does, and which mode proves live runtime behavior.
4. Front-load the two copyable repository-root commands in `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md`; keep focused scripts below them for diagnosis. Align `TESTING.md` wording if necessary, but retain one canonical project command rather than adding aliases in several packages.

Reuse the existing Node and live inventories and the wire-vocab test discovery. The improvement is an honest, executable profile boundary, not a new compliance framework.

## Evidence

- `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:3-47` describes the six-gate operator runner, says the hermetic suite is intentionally excluded, and points to a second manual command.
- `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:186-245` declares the current prep and six gate steps; lines 303-318 collapse their result to the unqualified all-green sentinel.
- `implementation/package.json` exposes the runner only as `test:mcp-conformance` from the implementation package.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md:101-148` gives five separate run recipes, uses `npm install` despite the committed lock/reproducible `npm ci` posture, and describes `npm test` as the Node inventory without pointing to the repository-level runner.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs:13-18,87-96,130-156` derives the live rows, marks them `SKIP`, and prints the coverage caveat that the outer runner later loses.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs:6-41` is the one live roster; the hermetic runner derives `INNER_TESTS` from it.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:1266-1302,1361-1378` refuses skipped/missing sentinels and emits green only after cleanup grading.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/package.json` exposes focused Node/server/live scripts but no project compatibility profile or CLI help.
- `TESTING.md:32-34` separately lists the medium conformance command and expensive live command.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml:5345-5423,5488-5500,5562-5566` shows the actual CI split and that the Pair job includes the hermetic suite.
- History: `7f1f93234a` introduced the single runner; `ddb3ec91f3` made its installs reproducible. The current package README was rewritten later in `deb03d1d01` and still exposes only the multi-command route.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From the repository root, one documented command runs the current medium compatibility profile; its terminal summary explicitly marks the hermetic live Pair profile `NOT RUN` and prints the exact `--live` invocation. No unqualified all-green sentence is emitted for that partial profile.
2. The same command with `--live` invokes the existing hermetic suite after the default steps. It reports full compatibility green only when every live row from `LIVE_TESTS` ran to its sentinel and the hermetic cleanup grade is clean; inner exit 1 and orchestration/cleanup exit 2 continue to propagate distinctly.
3. `--help` exits zero before installs, compiles, or server boots and concisely explains default versus live coverage, prerequisites, expected relative cost, and the narrower meaning of `tools/mcp-conformance/npm test`. Unknown options fail before any setup mutation.
4. A lightweight runner regression test exercises default, `--live`, help, and unknown-option selection without launching Clojure, shadow-cljs, Chromium, or either MCP server, and proves the live step is absent/present in the corresponding planned summary.
5. `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md` starts its run guidance with the two repository-root commands and a small included/omitted profile table. Focused unit, per-server, wire-vocab, and direct hermetic commands remain available as diagnostic recipes and agree with package scripts.
6. The implementation reuses `TESTS`, `LIVE_TESTS`, the current hermetic entry point, and JVM test discovery; it introduces no second test roster, copied tool catalogue, new result/report format, or new CI job.
7. Existing CI jobs, changed-surface scheduling, default medium cost, server behavior, tool descriptors, and wire schemas remain unchanged. The existing focused suites and runner policy tests pass.

## Non-goals

- No MCP certification product, compatibility score, persisted report, dashboard, badge, or release-compliance database.
- No matrix across MCP hosts, SDK languages/versions, protocol versions, transports, operating systems, or published-package combinations.
- No new protocol assertions, tool semantics, wire markers, schemas, vocabulary rules, or server launch flags.
- No consolidation of the three CI jobs, no changed-only scheduler, and no default-on Chromium/hermetic cost.
- No replacement or broad refactor of the mature Node/JVM corpus, hermetic orchestrator, source-pin strategy, or server-owned manifests.
- No second package-level “all” runner that can drift from `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs`.

## Related beads

- `rf2-gt4pf` (historical; commit `7f1f93234a`) created the current single operator entry point and deliberately kept rich reporting, changed-only mode, and CI consolidation out of scope. This task preserves that minimum-scope posture while making the existing profile boundary explicit.
- `rf2-vtp2er` (historical; commit `ddb3ec91f3`) made the runner's installs reproducible; keep its lockfile-exact/skip-if-present policy.
- `rf2-ahjbc` (open) proposes removing Pair progress streaming and its live conformance row. It is not a dependency: this task must derive the live profile from `LIVE_TESTS`, so either inventory state is handled without a copied list; coordinate only if both edit the live runner concurrently.
- `rf2-cfq8a` (open) adds a consumer-shaped Story bootstrap workflow to the existing Story end-to-end path. It is adjacent, not blocking; the project runner should pick up that workflow through the existing Node inventory without naming it separately.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead matching this execution/verdict outcome was found.

DISPATCHABLE solo, TRIMMED: extend _mcp-conformance-install-policy.test.cjs (no new *.test.cjs — the package.json chain belongs to rf2-39rc5); fence OUT implementation/package.json and TESTING.md (rf2-39rc5/rf2-qxg24). --live just spawns the hermetic suite and propagates its exit; summary prints the six rows + the NOT RUN line; rename the sentinel (verify 0 greps outside the runner); README npm install -> npm ci.

Run: npm --prefix implementation run test:mcp-conformance -- --live', above an explicit '[NOT RUN ] hermetic live Pair conformance suite (shadow-cljs fixture + Chromium; 6 live rows)' row carrying that same opt-in command. LIVE, captured exit 0: 'MCP-CONFORMANCE LIVE PROFILE GREEN - 7/7 gates, hermetic live Pair suite INCLUDED (6 live rows)', preceded by the hermetic runner's own 'RE-FRAME2-PAIR-MCP live hermetic conformance passed (6 inner tests).' which it emits only after every inner row hits its sentinel and the teardown grades clean. --help captured exit 0 on a checkout with NO node_modules anywhere (nothing installed); an unknown option captured exit 64 (EX_USAGE, deliberately clear of the 1/2 gate codes) with all three tool node_modules still absent afterwards. --live is one extra step delegating to the existing test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite entry point, so its 1-vs-2 exit distinction passes through; LIVE_TESTS is read from scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs, no second roster. title: surface-review(implementation-build): let Node discover the script test suite
description:
## Scope

Replace the hand-maintained file rosters behind `implementation/package.json`'s `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` with one canonical implementation-level JavaScript harness command. Cover the 42 conventionally named `implementation/scripts/*.test.cjs` files, the two intended out-of-tree `.test.cjs` support tests currently in the helpers chain, and the native-IME verdict self-test. Update the fast-PR, CI, documentation, and policy consumers that currently know the two-command spelling. Preserve each test file's behaviour, process isolation, and failure signal.

## Findings

The suite already has a complete naming convention but does not use it. `implementation/scripts/` contains 42 `*.test.cjs` files. `test:script-policy` names 34 of them one by one; `test:script-helpers` names the other 8, plus two out-of-tree `.test.cjs` files and one CLI `--self-test`. That is 45 literal `node` invocations across two 2,218-character package-script values. Every new conventional test needs a second registration edit to one contested JSON line.

The split has user-visible cost without an execution boundary. The fast spine and CI always chain both commands. `TESTING.md` records that running only the second half has already let a red through. `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` therefore pins the exact two-command string, and `implementation/scripts/_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs` parses `package.json` to assert that its own filename appears in the roster. These are guards around manual registration rather than product or test semantics.

History shows the mechanism repeatedly failing in the dark direction. Closed beads `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` each existed to append tests or self-tests that had landed but ran in no spine; their notes also record guaranteed conflicts because each insertion rewrote the same long `package.json` line. The recent bench retirement removed most exceptional flag-driven readers, leaving only one such CLI self-test in the current helpers command, so this is now a small simplification rather than a framework project.

CI pins Node 24. Node 24's built-in test runner discovers quoted `*.test.cjs` glob patterns, runs each matching file in an isolated child process, and treats the child's exit code as the file verdict; files are explicitly not required to use `node:test` internally. The existing standalone harness files can therefore retain their current code and output. `--test-concurrency=1` can preserve today's serial host-load posture.

## Recommended Action

Create one obvious command, `npm run test:scripts`, that uses the Node 24 test runner with quoted, repository-scoped glob patterns for the conventional `.test.cjs` populations and `--test-concurrency=1`. Keep `scripts/run-hicasso-native-ime-witness.cjs --self-test` as the one explicit prelude, or expose that verdict control through a tiny conventional `.test.cjs` wrapper; do not build a custom discovery runner.

Delete `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` rather than retain forwarding aliases. Point the fast spine, the `js-harness-self-tests` CI job, `TESTING.md`, and `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` at the single command. Remove self-enrolment assertions and comments that tell authors to edit `package.json`; adding a correctly named test file should be the registration act.

## Evidence

- `implementation/package.json:60-61` contains the two literal rosters: 34 policy files and 11 helper invocations.
- `rg --files implementation/scripts -g '*.test.cjs'` returns 42 files; all 42 occur exactly once across those two package scripts. The helper command separately names `core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache_wiring.test.cjs`, `hicasso/scripts/check_modules_compile.test.cjs`, and the native-IME `--self-test`.
- `TESTING.md:20` presents both names as one JS-harness tier; `TESTING.md:181-183` says they must be chained and records that running only the second let a red through.
- `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1489-1490` and `.github/workflows/test.yml:3131` duplicate the chained spelling; `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py:297` pins it as an exact regular expression.
- `implementation/scripts/_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs:203-208` checks its own textual enrolment in `test:script-policy`.
- Closed registration beads `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` document tests that existed but were not executed, plus contention on the one-line roster.
- Node 24 documentation lists `**/*.test.cjs` as a default discovery shape, recommends quoted globs for portability, and states that isolated test files are judged by process exit code without needing to use `node:test`: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/test.html#running-tests-from-the-command-line
- Exact tracker searches for `node --test`, `auto-discover`, `test:script-policy`, `test:script-helpers`, `hand-register`, and `surface-review(implementation-build)` found no open, in-progress, or deferred bead owning this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From `implementation/`, one documented `npm run test:scripts` command runs the same 44 `.test.cjs` files and the same native-IME verdict self-test that the two old commands run today, each exactly once.
- The command uses Node's built-in discovery over explicit repository-scoped globs, with process isolation and concurrency 1; it adds no dependency and no custom file-inventory runner.
- A temporary failing `implementation/scripts/*-negative-control.test.cjs` is discovered without editing `package.json`, makes the command exit non-zero, and is named in the failure output; removing it restores green. Record the red/green control in the PR.
- Baseline and replacement runs agree on the executed file population and preserve actionable stdout/stderr from a deliberately failing existing fixture or equivalent scoped mutation.
- `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` are removed, not retained as aliases. The fast spine, `js-harness-self-tests` CI job, `TESTING.md`, and fast-PR gap check all use the one canonical command.
- The self-enrolment assertion in `_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs` and stale comments telling authors to wire individual `.test.cjs` files into `package.json` are deleted or rewritten to describe convention-based discovery.
- The focused command passes on Windows and in the Node 24 Linux CI job without increasing test-file concurrency or introducing shared-fixture collisions.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the 44 standalone test files to the `node:test` API or changing their assertion harnesses.
- Parallelising test files, changing their internal order, suppressing their diagnostics, or weakening exit-code handling.

title: pair-mcp: retire the progress-stream subsystem (33 -> 29 tools)
description:
## Scope

Make live observation fit an ordinary programmer+AI tool turn. Retire Pair-MCP's progress-notification streaming subsystem: the public `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` tools; their server/runtime queue, polling, accounting, and launch-control machinery; and their schema, manifest, test, spec, skill, and conformance carriers. Establish the already-shipped result-returning tools as the one supported live-app observation workflow. Cover the smallest coherent cross-repo seam under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**`, the companion `re-frame2-pair.runtime` preload and Pair skill, and the MCP conformance fixtures that pin the public catalogue.

## Findings

- The source catalogue exposes 33 tools. Four are one push-streaming subsystem, and four environment/launch controls exist only to bound that subsystem (`MAX_STREAMS`, event rate, abuse threshold, abuse window). This is a large public and configuration tax for an optional observation route.
- `subscribe` does not return observations as the tool result. It holds `tools/call` open until cancellation/cap/termination, emits useful data through `notifications/progress`, then returns only a terminal summary. Pair-MCP's own live conformance witness must keep a `subscribePromise` open and issue `dispatch` concurrently to exercise it. That is a valid custom MCP-client pattern, but not the natural sequential turn shape of a coding agent; out-of-band `unsubscribe` has the same second-concurrent-call assumption.
- Every normal pairing outcome already has a turn-shaped route: `dispatch` returns its consequence or settled epoch; `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` read bounded history; `watch-until` blocks to a data predicate and returns the sample; `record` + `read-recording` cover human/intermittent interaction; and `tail-build` waits for hot reload. The rare need for a bespoke live listener remains expressible through the default-enabled `eval-cljs` escape hatch and does not justify four permanent public tools.
- Eight dedicated Pair-MCP source/test files (`subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, `get-stream-controls`, `resource-controls`, and their three largest focused suites) already total 3,056 lines / 156,022 bytes, before `resource_controls_test.cljs`, the preload's subscription queues/listener fan-out, server/config plumbing, the long catalogue sections, skill prose, and the dedicated live conformance script are counted.
- The complexity is not passive. The stream needs dual event/byte queue caps, drop-oldest accounting, a token bucket, an abuse window, dead-connection retry/termination, cancellation and out-of-band teardown, per-tick cap/dedup/elision, and two diagnostic tools to explain the controls. History records repeated follow-on repairs for lost events, uncapped progress frames, dead drain loops, privacy projection, frame scoping, and control observability.
- The generated descriptor manifest is already 88,930 bytes for the full catalogue. Removing four host-specialized tools reduces the always-advertised surface as well as implementation weight; retaining them as aliases would preserve the cost and defeat the pre-alpha simplification.

## Recommended Action

Delete `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` from the registry and remove the streaming-only server/runtime implementation: runtime subscription queues and drain API, polling controller, progress payloads, concurrent-slot/rate/abuse controls, their flags/environment variables, diagnostics, and teardown state. Do not add a generic replacement, deprecated aliases, tombstones, or a compatibility mode.

Rewrite the Pair routing guidance around returned-result workflows:

1. Use `dispatch` consequence/settle for an action the agent initiated.
2. Use `watch-epochs` or `trace-window` for retained event/trace history.
3. Use `watch-until` for a known asynchronous condition.
4. Use `record` + `read-recording` while a human or the browser drives the app.
5. Use `tail-build` for code reload.

Keep `list-subscriptions`: it reads the app's reactive subscription cache and is unrelated to MCP progress streams. Preserve the retained tools' existing privacy projection, elision, wire caps, and explicit time bounds; do not replace deleted stream controls with another permission or resource-control layer.

## Evidence

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/registry.cljs` registers the four tools as a distinct streaming/diagnostic family.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/subscribe.cljs` is 864 lines. Its contract says the call runs until abort/unsubscribe and carries observations in `notifications/progress`; the final result is a summary. `resource_controls.cljs` adds another 479 lines.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-subscribe.cjs` explicitly starts `client.callTool(subscribe)` without awaiting it, fires `dispatch` concurrently, accumulates `onprogress` callbacks, and only later awaits the terminal subscription result. The test demonstrates the concurrency contract rather than a normal one-call/one-result agent workflow.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/package.json`, `spec/API.md`, and `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` expose the stream configuration, progress wire shape, caps, filters, diagnostics, and five termination paths.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` owns the streaming queue/listener fan-out (`subscribe!`, `drain-subscription!`, `unsubscribe!`, `subscription-info`) in addition to the retained history and recorder surfaces.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn` reports 33 tools and is 88,930 bytes; the streaming family consumes four names and their always-loaded descriptions/schemas.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs` already presents `watch-until`, `record`, `subscribe`, and `tail-build` as alternate waiting routes, confirming overlap at the routing layer.
- Source/commit history identifies the additive lineage and its repair tail: rf2-hq49 (push subscribe/unsubscribe), rf2-ho4ve (byte budget), rf2-uvfph (rate-limit event preservation), rf2-a0kxsb / rf2-3ijbl (controls and observability), and rf2-ajhwbm (dead drain-loop termination).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` are absent from `registry/tools`, `tools/list`, the canonical tool-name fixture, generated descriptor manifest, conformance corpus, package README/API/catalogue, Pair skill allow-list/routing, and current capability/status docs. No alias, deprecated descriptor, or unknown-tool special case preserves them.
2. Streaming-only Pair-MCP files and code paths are removed. The server has no progress-notification emitter, stream slot/token-bucket/abuse-window state, stream-specific launch flags or environment variables, or stream cleanup branch. The preload has no Pair-owned stream registry, bounded event queue, drain loop API, or stream-only listener fan-out. Shared framework trace/epoch facilities used by retained reads remain intact.
3. `list-subscriptions` remains and is documented/tested as the reactive app subscription-cache read, with no streaming terminology or dependency.
4. A live end-to-end witness proves the retained turn-shaped workflow without concurrent MCP calls: dispatch an event, observe its returned consequence and retained epoch/trace; a focused `watch-until` test returns a matching asynchronous sample; and the existing recorder path still captures and returns a browser/human-driven change. Each observation reaches the agent in a completed tool result, not a progress callback.
5. Tool annotations, schemas, `tool-descriptors.edn`, the stdio catalogue snapshot, and cross-server MCP conformance agree with the reduced surface. The Pair package tests, descriptor-drift check, stdio round trip, and relevant live fixture/conformance lanes pass non-vacuously.
6. Current docs state one observation decision tree using the five retained routes above. Historical design notes may record that push streaming once existed, but no current setup, recipe, status table, or diagnostic ladder instructs an agent to use it.
7. No new public tool, compatibility shim, permission gate, scheduler, queue, or background service is introduced to replace the deleted subsystem.

## Non-goals

- Removing or weakening `read-sub` / `list-subscriptions`, framework trace/epoch listeners, epoch retention, privacy projection, elision, or the ordinary per-response wire cap.
- Redesigning the remaining 29-tool catalogue, globally rewriting descriptor prose, or combining unrelated tools in this change.
- Changing MCP itself, adding a different streaming transport, or supporting dashboard/telemetry clients whose primary workload is continuous event consumption.
- Preserving compatibility for the four removed pre-alpha names, migration aliases, deprecation windows, or launch-flag no-ops.
- Tightening eval/write permissions or adding safety confirmations. The installed local Pair-MCP and explicit invoker remain the trust boundary.

## Related beads

No open or in-progress duplicate was found after title and full-description searches for `subscribe`, `stream`, `notifications/progress`, `push-mode`, `list-streams`, and `resource-control`.

- `rf2-wyza` (closed) removed the duplicated 33-entry onboarding catalogue in favor of routing rules after measuring the permanent tools/list context tax; this is the same pre-alpha/trust-the-agent posture applied to a redundant runtime subsystem.
- `rf2-ov144` (open) is an adjacent Pair-MCP catalogue change for replay-by-epoch-id. It is not a dependency; coordinate registry/manifest edits if both land concurrently.
- Historical implementation lineage retained in source/commits: rf2-hq49, rf2-ho4ve, rf2-uvfph, rf2-a0kxsb, rf2-3ijbl, and rf2-ajhwbm.

title: surface-review(story-mcp): make project stories reachable on first launch
description:
## Scope

Make the published headless Story-MCP server expose a consumer project's JVM-loadable Story registry on its first MCP connection. Add one explicit launch-time namespace-loading seam, document one copyable consumer-project/MCP-host configuration, and prove the path end to end against a project-owned story. Preserve the settled boundary that live browser/CLJS stories are reached through re-frame2-pair.

## Findings

Story-MCP is a same-JVM adapter: every catalogue read, run, and write operates on the process-local Story registry. That makes loading the consumer's registration namespaces a prerequisite, not optional setup polish.

The only canonical launch is `clojure -M -m re-frame.story-mcp.server` from the tool directory. The README adds one sentence saying the launch “must preload” registry-populating JVM namespaces, but supplies no argument, alias, wrapper, MCP-host config, ordering rule, or executable example that does so. The server CLI accepts only the two gate flags and ignores every other flag; `boot!` installs canonical vocabulary and immediately enters the stdio loop. A normal launch therefore has tags/assertions but no project stories.

The integration corpus proves protocol and synthetic in-memory behavior, not the consumer workflow. `stdio-roundtrip.js` uses the bare canonical command and deliberately probes missing stories/variants. The SDK conformance harness starts the same command with `--allow-writes`, creates a synthetic variant only after connecting, and explicitly notes that a successful story read would need a registered story. No test starts the published server from a consuming project, preloads a project namespace, then discovers and runs that already-authored story.

This is the first-use bottleneck for the whole 20-tool catalogue: until a project registry is present, the documented `list-stories -> get-story/get-variant -> run/refine` workflow cannot begin. More protocol hardening or another tool would not fix it.

## Recommended Action

Add one repeatable explicit startup option, for example `--require app.stories.login`, whose values are trusted namespace names from the invoking project's classpath. In `boot!`, install Story's canonical vocabulary first, then `require` the supplied namespaces, then start the MCP loop. Let an ordinary require failure abort startup loudly; do not add namespace scanning, a custom discovery protocol, allowlists, or redundant name validation.

Document a single golden consumer path: a `deps.edn` alias that depends on `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp`, a project-root MCP-host command using that alias plus the explicit namespace option, and the write-gate flag only when the author/refine loop is wanted. State plainly that the namespace must be CLJ/CLJC-loadable in this headless JVM; a running browser's CLJS registry remains the pair's one live door.

Back the path with one consumer-shaped fixture driven through the official MCP SDK: launch from the fixture project, load its story namespace at boot, and immediately discover/read/run its pre-authored story without first calling `register-variant`.

## Evidence

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:37-51` shows the bare tool-directory command and only the unimplemented “must preload” sentence.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:337-365` parses only `--allow-writes` and `--allow-sensitive-reads`; unknown flags are logged and ignored.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:368-384` applies gates and installs canonical vocabulary but has no consumer-namespace load step.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:17,74-80` and `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:35-55` make registrations/runs process-local and define Story-MCP as the headless same-JVM host.
- `tools/story-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js:45-51,247-281` calls the bare launch and verifies only missing-variant plus gated-write behavior.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-story.cjs:27,134,342-369` launches with `--allow-writes`, says a story hit needs a registered story, then synthesizes only a variant after connection.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md:15` documents the complementary browser path: Story-MCP cannot see a tab's registry; pair `eval-cljs` is the live door.
- History: initial commit `65c05d67c5` introduced the current bare command; `4cfdf55f61` added the preload caveat two months later, but no launch mechanism or consumer integration witness followed. There are 185 commits touching `tools/story-mcp`; the missing consumer bootstrap is not an unimplemented handler detail.
- Exact tracker searches across current and closed issues for `story-mcp`, project stories, JVM namespaces, preload namespace, empty registry, same-JVM registry, launch, setup, and bootstrap found no matching outcome bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consuming project's documented `deps.edn` alias and MCP-host configuration start the published Story-MCP main from the project root without repository-local source paths or a user-written wrapper namespace.
- One repeatable explicit namespace option loads named CLJ/CLJC registration namespaces after canonical vocabulary installation and before the server accepts MCP requests; multiple supplied namespaces preserve command order.
- An official-SDK end-to-end fixture launches through that consumer path and, before any MCP write, proves `list-stories` finds the fixture story, `get-story` or `get-variant` reads it, and `run-variant` executes its fixture variant.
- A missing or throwing supplied namespace terminates startup with a useful stderr diagnostic/non-zero exit rather than continuing with a misleading empty project registry. The implementation relies on ordinary `require` failure; it does not invent a second validation layer.
- README/spec guidance clearly distinguishes JVM-loadable project namespaces from the running browser's CLJS registry and routes the latter to re-frame2-pair.
- Existing no-namespace launches, gate semantics, the MCP method set, tool names, tool input/output schemas, and Story's public registration API remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Adding nREPL, a JVM-to-browser bridge, or a second live-app transport.
- Auto-discovering namespaces by scanning source roots, classpaths, files, manifests, or naming conventions.
- Hot reload, namespace watching, runtime load/unload tools, or persistence of registrations to source files.
- Adding a new MCP tool, a new Story registration primitive, or extra env/sysprop aliases/config DSLs for the same bootstrap.
- Redesigning the 20-tool catalogue, token budgeting, privacy egress, cursor protocol, or JSON-RPC lifecycle.
- Making CLJS-only story namespaces JVM-loadable.

## Related beads

- `rf2-tgci` (closed) introduced the separate-jar Story-MCP server and its canonical bare launch.
- `rf2-3fc89f.21` (closed) made browser-only reads fail as capability-unavailable rather than false-empty; this task preserves that truthfulness.
- `rf2-3fc89f.22` (closed) ruled the pair as the one live-browser Story host; this task is only the explicit headless-JVM bootstrap.
- `rf2-s99lw4` (closed) documented the pair-side browser recipe through `eval-cljs`; it is the complementary path, not a duplicate.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead matching this project-namespace bootstrap outcome was found.

title: surface-review(conformance-security): stop security-tier edits from arming production and browser gates
description:
## Scope

Correct PR changed-surface routing for the four source-less, cross-artefact test partitions under implementation/security, implementation/reply-conformance, implementation/derivation-conformance, and implementation/event-conformance. The implementation change should be confined to the classifier and its executable policy tests/comments unless a directly coupled testing-policy sentence must move with them.

## Findings

- All four partitions are test-only: each deps.edn has :paths [] and :deps {}, none has a src/ tree, and none publishes production code. Their responsibilities are substantial and distinct: reply vocabulary/egress across managed-async families; derivation algebra across five graph contributors; the event facade/runtime/isolation boundary; and adversarial security properties over schema, SSR, reply, profile, error-slot, and MCP egress.
- The suites deliberately complement artefact-local tests rather than replace them. Derivation composes family projections; event tests adversarial public seams after core-owned duplicates were removed; reply tests own cross-family vocabulary while family tests own lowering; security adds generated/sentinel/fail-closed coverage beyond fixed local pins. A broad semantic dedupe would trade away confidence for little benefit.
- CLJS already has the right shape: every namespace matches the consolidated :node-test build's cljs-test$ selector, and the focused test:security build is only a local-iteration subset. JVM CI likewise keeps four required clojure -M:test jobs. Current successful run 33307155376 reports security 92 tests/698 assertions, derivation 22/522, event 49/209, and reply 27/533.
- The changed-surface classifier treats the three *-conformance trees as source-less and sets only implementation_jvm=true plus cljs_node_test=true. The same probe on an actual security test currently also sets cljs_browser=true, examples_compile=true, cljs_prod=true, and bundle_isolation=true.
- Those four extra gates cannot observe a security-tier-only edit: :browser-test selects only *-dom-cljs-test namespaces; production and bundle-isolation builds do not require the test tree; and the all-examples compiler has no edge to it. implementation/security/deps.edn is also test-only.
- This is drift from recorded intent, not a new coverage trade. Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 says adding implementation/security/* was needed specifically to fire implementation_jvm and cljs_node_test, but placed it in a generic feature-artefact arm that sets five outputs. The later src-less conformance arm at report-changed-surfaces.sh:1202-1220 explicitly says security is the precedent for omitting browser/prod/bundle gates, while the earlier executable arm contradicts it.
- The examples-compile policy test reinforces the mistake with implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc, a path that does not exist in this intentionally src-less partition, and asserts that this imaginary file can change an example closure.
- The toll is material. Security-only commit d1fa5ff493 changed deps/test commentary and its tests workflow run 29096118890 executed the relevant JVM/Node suites plus the all-examples job (10m24s), browser, two production browser builds, and bundle isolation. The all-examples job was the critical path; current direct classifier output still arms the same unrelated surfaces.
- Search across all tracker statuses and title/description/notes for conformance, security classifier/surface/tier, src-less, examples_compile, bundle_isolation, cljs_browser, and over-classification found no issue owning this exact mismatch.

## Recommended Action

Move implementation/security/* out of both the shipped-feature classifier arm and the examples_compile input arm, and classify it alongside reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance as a source-less cross-artefact tier: implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true only.

Update the classifier's executable mirror using real tracked security paths. Preserve the jvm-security required job, the local JVM roster entry, the consolidated Node inclusion, and the focused test:security command. Keep production artefact routing unchanged, so changes to core/schemas/machines/routing/flows/SSR still run their existing production/browser/bundle gates and continue to trigger the broad JVM and Node suites.

## Evidence

- implementation/security/deps.edn and the three *-conformance/deps.edn files: empty production paths/deps, test-only aliases.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:208-287 and 650-655: all four test roots feed the shared cljs-test$ Node build; security's focused selector is at 769-790.
- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:574 includes security in examples compilation; 973-997 includes it in the full feature fan-out; 1202-1220 gives the three sibling tiers the intended narrow routing and states that security has the same posture.
- implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1983-2011 asserts examples compilation from the nonexistent implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc; 3283-3311 already pins the narrow sibling-tier contract.
- .github/workflows/test.yml:2149-2198 and 2482-2610: required JVM jobs; 6026 and 6040-6042: aggregator membership.
- scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh:46-90: all four JVM lanes remain in the rigorous local roster.
- Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 and workflow runs 29096118890 / 33307155376 provide the intent, observed toll, and current suite tallies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Classifying both implementation/security/deps.edn and at least one real tracked implementation/security/test/** file sets implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true, while examples_compile, cljs_browser, cljs_prod, and bundle_isolation are false.
2. Representative real files under reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance retain the same two-output routing.
3. The classifier policy test removes the imaginary implementation/security/src/** positive fixture, uses tracked paths for the security tier, and explicitly locks the four negative outputs so the broad arm cannot silently return.
4. jvm-security remains conditional on implementation_jvm, remains in all-required-passed, and still runs clojure -M:test from implementation/security. The local JVM roster entry, shadow :node-test root, and npm test:security focused command remain intact.
