title: surface-review(http): expose successful response metadata to :after middleware and reply handlers
description:
## Scope

Close the managed-HTTP completion gap from a host-normalized 2xx response through decode/accept, canonical reply construction, the per-frame `:after` chain, and app reply delivery. Cover the JVM and CLJS transports plus HTTP test support, Spec 014, async/API documentation, and the managed-HTTP skill/example material that describes response middleware.

## Verified Findings

- Both host transports feed `handle-response!` a normalized map containing `:status`, `:status-text`, and `:headers`. The 4xx/5xx branches retain these facts, but the successful 2xx branch calls `finalise-success!` with only the accepted body value.
- `success-reply` accepts only ctx plus value and builds a canonical success reply without HTTP response metadata. Therefore neither `:after` nor `:reply-to` / `:on-success` can observe status or headers for a successful request.
- Spec 014 and `docs/async/http-going-further.md` explicitly present rate-limit-header and Cache-Control parsing as `:after` use cases.
- The two motivating JVM tests do not verify that contract: their servers emit `X-RateLimit-*` and `Cache-Control`, while the interceptors hard-code `37`, `100`, and `600` after comments acknowledge that headers do not ride on the reply. The tests pass even if the emitted headers change or disappear.
- Searches of all current beads for response headers, success headers, rate-limit, HTTP metadata, ETag, Location, Cache-Control, and after-interceptor headers found no matching task.

## Recommended Action

Thread a minimal, documented successful-response metadata value through decode/accept and success finalization into the canonical reply's existing `:meta` family-extension slot. It should contain the actual numeric status, status text, and the transport's already-normalized header map; keep `:value` as the decoded-and-accepted application payload. Run `:after` over that canonical reply and deliver its result unchanged to the selected app target.

Use the existing cross-host header normalization and existing core reply `:meta` trace-elision path. Before trace egress, apply managed HTTP's immutable and app-declared sensitive-header carrier policy so exposing useful headers to app code does not expose `Set-Cookie`, auth tokens, or custom secret headers in traces. Let canned/route stubs opt into the same metadata shape without inventing metadata when it is omitted.

Rewrite the motivating middleware tests so they parse the headers actually emitted by the local server; do not retain hard-coded stand-ins.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1310-1450`: normalized response facts enter `handle-response!`; the success tail passes only `(:accepted outcome)` to `finalise-success!`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:507-511` and `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:181-189`: success construction takes only the accepted value.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:1191-1239`: the server emits rate-limit headers, lines 1213-1214 admit headers are absent, and lines 1221-1224 hard-code the alleged parse result.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:1280-1313`: the Cache-Control server value is likewise replaced by a hard-coded map at line 1300.
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:768,809-814` and `docs/async/http-going-further.md:38-40`: the public contract promises response-header parsing in `:after`.
- Commit `264dc7b352` introduced `:after` and both motivating tests together; blame/history show the stand-ins have not subsequently been replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful live JVM request and a successful live CLJS request expose the actual response status, status text, and normalized headers at one documented location in the canonical reply seen by both `:after` and the app reply target; `:value` remains the accepted payload.
- The rate-limit and Cache-Control motivating tests read and parse the local server's real header values. Their assertions fail if those response headers are removed or changed without changing the expected parse.
- Cross-host tests pin the chosen normalized header shape, including a multi-valued header case, rather than introducing a second header representation.
- HTTP canned success and route-map stubs may supply optional response metadata so header-dependent `:after` code is testable without a network; absence remains minimal and does not fabricate lifecycle facts.
- Completion traces continue to use the shared canonical-reply elider, and tests prove built-in `Set-Cookie` plus an app-declared sensitive response-header carrier are redacted while ordinary response headers remain useful on-box. Per-call `:sensitive?` still redacts wire-bearing metadata as specified.
- Spec 014, async/API docs, and managed-HTTP skill/example material document the exact reply shape with one working header-parsing example. Manifest/conformance data is updated only if implementation introduces a new public var (the recommended shape needs none).
- Existing success decode/accept behavior, failure classification, retry, cancellation, frame routing, stale suppression, and reply-target semantics remain green on JVM and CLJS.

## Non-goals

- A Fetch/HttpClient response wrapper or host object in app state.
- New response-header parsing helpers, middleware registries, global mutable policy, or compatibility aliases.
- Upload/download progress, streaming bodies, cookie-jar behavior, or a fully realistic HTTP simulator.
- Duplicating body data or inventing status/headers for stub replies that did not supply them.

## Related beads

No matching current bead was found. Historical source/comments reference `rf2-uheqq` (the `:after` middleware work) and `rf2-ibksxg` (minimal canonical canned replies), but neither ID resolves in the current tracker; they are context, not dependencies.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-30 21:39:08 AUSEST (read-only agent, premises at e159c96fbf): every cited line HOLDS except one — 'managed-HTTP skill/example material' does not exist (git grep reg-http-interceptor -- skills examples: 0). Drop that surface. Dispatchable solo; owns spec/014 as its hot-zone file.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8818: successful-response metadata ({:status :status-text :headers} — the transport's normalized shape) threads from handle-response!'s 2xx branch onto the canonical reply's :meta family-extension slot, visible to :after middleware and the app reply target; :value unchanged. Trace egress redacts [:meta :headers] denylist ∪ app carriers (new privacy/redact-response-meta); per-call :sensitive? force-redacts :meta wholesale via the existing wire-slot walker. Canned-success + route-map stubs take optional :meta (absent = omitted, never fabricated). Motivating rate-limit/Cache-Control tests now parse the server's real headers. Cross-host shape pinned (set-cookie parity .cljc + live JVM multi-valued test + full-pipeline CLJS test). Spec 014 §Successful-response metadata + async docs updated with a working header-parsing example. No new public var — manifest untouched. Per TRIAGE note, the nonexistent managed-HTTP skill/example surface was dropped. Gates: implementation/http clojure -M:test exit 0 (502 tests / 3827 assertions) on the final rebased base; check_doc_slugs exit 0; both controls went red under planted faults and restores verified by blob hash.

title: surface-review(flows): make dynamic flow toggles settle automatically
description:
## Scope

Change the runtime semantics of the existing `:rf.fx/reg-flow` and `:rf.fx/clear-flow` effects so their app-db consequences settle automatically on the dispatching frame. Keep the existing effect ids and 3-slot registration payload. This includes the flows runtime, the core fx/router integration it uses, focused tests/conformance, Spec 013, the API/core guides, and the shipped cart example.

## Verified Findings

- The reserved flow effects run after the event's flow transform. A flow registered by an event therefore has no output until another event drains; a flow cleared by an event leaves its old output in app-db until another event drains.
- The clear case is observably incoherent at the dispatch boundary: the registry row is already gone while the derived value it owned is still present.
- The documented solution makes every caller invent and dispatch a no-op event. The shipped cart defines `:cart/touch` solely for this purpose and emits it after both apply and remove. This is ceremony in the event catalogue, trace stream, tests, docs, and generated code, not application behavior.
- The current tracker contains no open, in-progress, deferred, or closed issue that owns automatic settling for flow lifecycle effects. Spec 013 itself labels synchronous re-walk as an untracked note.

## Recommended Action

After a successful `:rf.fx/reg-flow` or `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, have the runtime request one private, same-frame settling drain for the parent event. Reuse the existing run-to-completion queue and ordinary flow pass: this is the framework performing the exact follow-up drain it currently tells every application to hand-write. Keep one app-db install per individual event; do not re-run flows inline in the original fx walk. The private transport must not become an application-facing event or option.

Make this the only default. Delete the lag workaround contract instead of adding a synchronous variant, a `:settle?` flag, or compatibility behavior.

## Concrete Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:858` through `:869` calls the lag the least-obvious behavior and instructs callers to dispatch a follow-up no-op event.
- `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1148` through `:1184` proves clear removes the registry entry while leaving `[:wizard :result]` stale until `:touch`; `:1186` through `:1220` locks the registration lag and workaround.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:149` through `:191` spends a full handler plus two extra `:dispatch` pairs on `:cart/touch`, whose only purpose is to cause another flow walk.
- `docs/core/flows.md:299` through `:321`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:153`, `spec/013-Flows.md` under "Sequencing"/"Open questions", and `spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-toggle-via-fx.edn` all publish or pin the same lag.
- Git history shows the behavior was documented rather than removed: `256e6693aa` (rf2-1smwp) added the mid-event signpost, and `16bbd2f349` (rf2-2qd9wp) extended the lag to in-drain clear semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dispatching one event whose only lifecycle action is `:rf.fx/reg-flow` leaves the flow registered and its initial output materialized once the synchronous/run-to-completion dispatch settles, without an app-authored follow-up event.
- Dispatching one event with `:rf.fx/clear-flow` leaves the flow absent, its output path vacated, and existing dependent flows recomputed against that absence by the same settle boundary. The cart's apply/remove actions update `:cart/discount-rate` and `:cart/total` after one user dispatch.
- Automatic settling is frame-correct, uses the normal topo/dirty-check pass, and preserves the one-app-db-install-per-event invariant and existing derive-failure reporting.
- The public effect ids and payloads do not change, and no public settle event, flag, alternate effect, or new lifecycle API is added.
- Focused CLJ and CLJS tests fail under the old lag behavior and pass under the new default. The conformance fixture is flipped from "next app event" to automatic settle.
- The cart deletes `:cart/touch` and both manual settle dispatches. Spec 013, API/core docs, comments, and tests no longer teach or assert a user-authored no-op workaround.

## Non-goals

- Do not perform a second app-db install inside the original event.
- Do not add fixed-point iteration, conditional/liveness policies, a general scheduler abstraction, or a public "run flows now" command.
- Do not redesign the 3-slot `reg-flow` grammar, static boot registration, the optional-artifact boundary, tooling projections, classification, or exact-incarnation machinery in this task.
- Do not preserve the lag behind a compatibility switch; this is pre-alpha.

## Related beads

- No duplicate owner exists in the current 1,060-issue tracker corpus (all statuses searched across title, description, notes, and close reason for the effect ids, lag, no-op follow-up, dynamic toggle, and settle terms).
- Historical rf2-1smwp documented the registration lag; historical rf2-2qd9wp made in-drain clear preserve the same next-drain behavior. They explain the current contract but do not own removing the application workaround.
- Spec 013 "Synchronous re-walk after `:rf.fx/reg-flow`" is explicitly marked post-v1 and untracked. This task takes the smaller route: automate the already-supported follow-up drain rather than re-walk inline.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-30 21:44:09 AUSEST (read-only agent at e159c96fbf, premises all HOLD). See the mayor's dispatch note when it comes; queued behind a free slot.
VERDICT 2026-09-01 AUSEST (worker, PR #8893). NOTE-START-MARKER-KH73V.

PREMISES ALL HOLD, re-verified at source. Every cited line number in the item
was still exact after today's `implementation/flows` merge — zero drift:
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:858-869` is the ONE-EVENT LAG comment
verbatim; `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1148-1184` is
`fx-reg-flow-and-clear-flow-round-trip` (its lag pin is the `(= 9 ...)` at
:1179) and `:1186-1220` is
`fx-reg-flow-mid-event-lag-and-followup-dispatch-workaround` (its pin is the
`(nil? ...)` at :1213); `examples/core/flows/core.cljs` carried `:cart/touch`
at :192-195 with dispatches at :175 and :184.

WHAT THE POST-TRANSFORM ORDERING WAS PROTECTING. Exactly one `app-db` install
per event (Spec 013 Drain integration property 4), and with it the
pending-effect-transform model and the atomic-commit contract. The old fx.cljc
comment, the Spec 013 Sequencing section and the Open-questions entry all say
the same thing and all make the same assumption: that closing the lag requires
a SECOND INSTALL inside the registering event. A second EVENT closes it
instead. The `:fx` walk now enqueues one framework-private `[:rf/settle-flows]`
on the dispatching frame, which drains in the same run-to-completion pass. Each
event still installs once; nothing re-runs the transform after `:fx`.

The separation buys a second property the item did not ask for and that an
inline re-walk would have LOST: the failure boundary. A newly registered flow
whose `:derive` throws now aborts the SETTLE, not the registering event, whose
own `:db` write has already committed. An inline re-walk would have made a bad
`:derive` retroactively abort the registration.

SETTLE-TIME DERIVE FAILURES USE THE EXISTING PATH, no new one. A settle is an
ordinary event, so a throw goes through `flows-after-interceptor`'s existing
catch, is stashed under `:rf/flow-error`, and surfaces via
`emit-flow-eval-exception!` as `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` carrying the
structural `:phase` discriminator (`:derive` vs `:output-write`) that
`flows.cljc/evaluate-flow!` assigns by which `try` caught it. No code was added
on that path.

DESIGN CHOICE WORTH RECORDING: `:rf/settle-flows` is NEVER REGISTERED. Not into
the registrar, not into the EP-0023 image standard registry. It resolves through
the router unresolved-handler seam (new `router/framework-private-handler-metas`,
consulted ahead of the machines actor resolver in `resolve-unhandled`). The
alternative was the `:rf/set-db` template, a private `registrar/register!`, and
it was rejected for the reason the item itself gives: registering it would put a
row into every app event catalogue, tooling projection and generated code, which
merely MOVES the ceremony from the app into the framework instead of deleting
it. The seam also removes the need for an image-standard registration, since a
generation-routed `registrar/lookup` returns nil for an unregistered id and
falls through to it. It is still listed in `events/reserved-event-ids`, for a
different reason than `:rf/set-db` is: the registrar is consulted BEFORE the
seam, so an app `(reg-event :rf/settle-flows ...)` would silently shadow the
settle and strand every lifecycle effect.

NOTE-MIDDLE-MARKER-KH73V.

FENCED CORE FILES: neither needed. The change is `fx.cljc`, `router.cljc` and
`events.cljc`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc` and
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (held by rf2-cq0yi) were not
touched — confirmed by name against the merge-base diff, not by memory.

SPEC 013 TAKEN. Sequencing rewritten from "the one-event lag" to "settling on
the dispatching frame" with the boundary stated as normative; the
"Synchronous re-walk after :rf.fx/reg-flow" open question RESOLVED and moved to
Resolved decisions; the Dynamic-toggle table rows corrected. Also corrected
where the retired lag was asserted as fact outside Spec 013:
`spec/Derivations.md`, `spec/AI-Audit.md`, `docs/EP/EP-0014`,
`skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/flows.md`, and two
`examples/real-apps` comments — one of which justified an `{:optional true}`
schema key by a lag that no longer exists.

THE CART NO-OP IS GONE. `:cart/touch` and both manual settle dispatches are
deleted from `examples/core/flows/core.cljs`. One consequence the item did not
anticipate and that a grep for the example alone would have missed:
`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/flows_example_cljs_test.cljs:119`
had borrowed `:cart/touch` as a drain nudge while probing the hot-reload seam.
It now registers its own local no-op, since it is testing the reload seam and
not a lifecycle effect. That is a browser lane and was NOT run locally.

CONFORMANCE. `flow-toggle-via-fx.edn` gained `:flow-recompute-counts
{:step-2/computed 2}`, which is what actually pins the new contract: its
`:final-app-db` is a SUBMAP matcher and is therefore blind both to a stale
output the clear failed to vacate and to whether the registering dispatch
computed at all — the fixture passed unchanged under the new runtime, which is
why the count had to be added rather than the app-db expectation edited.
`flow-frame-scoped.edn` went 2 to 4 for the same reason it should: each frame
registration now computes on its own dispatch.

GATES, captured exit codes, all re-run on the final base after rebasing
8378fa7c90 -> 8451531aed (trunk moved mid-work; its six changed files had zero
overlap with this diff):
  JVM flows  `clojure -M:test` in implementation/flows  -> 0 (247 tests, 6096 assertions)
  JVM core   `clojure -M:test` in implementation/core   -> 0 (2170 tests, 11105 assertions)
  doc gate   `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`        -> 0
  README     `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci`-> 0

NOT COVERED BY ANY LANE RUN HERE, stated rather than implied: the CLJS
examples-compile job for `examples/core/flows/core.cljs`; the reagent browser
lane carrying the example behaviour test; and all markdown prose, tables and
rendering, which nothing anywhere validates (the two doc gates check link
targets and anchors only, and neither looks inside a fenced block). Table
column counts and the rewritten prose were checked by hand.

CONTROL. New file
`implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_settle_on_dispatch_test.clj`. Both
arms red against the unchanged runtime (captured exit 1, five failing
assertions) and green after (exit 0) — no plant or restore involved, since the
property was genuinely absent when the control first ran. Mid-change the full
flows suite showed exactly the three expected reds and nothing else across 247
tests. Separately, the CORE lane does not print its root, so it was
discriminated by a planted unresolved symbol in `fx.cljc`
(`rf2-planted-fault-kh73v`), which took it to exit 1 naming the plant; restore
verified by git BLOB hash 42ee7cca6f859b8285d5fa246a39249ae526ba29 against the
committed object. The flows lane needed no plant — its classpath prints this
worktree.

FILED, not taken: rf2-z529y — `spec/Conventions.md` reserved `:rf/*` roster
does not name `:rf/settle-flows`. Conventions is a hot-zone one-toucher outside
this item's enumerated scope. The bead records that the roster entry is NOT
simply a second `:rf/set-db`, because this id is reserved but never registered.

NOTE-END-MARKER-KH73V.
AUDIT PR #8893: REOPENED. The lifecycle mutation is correct, but the private settle is appended only after the whole :fx walk via ordinary child-dispatch!, so any :dispatch effect from that same handler is already ahead of it in the FIFO. Those child handlers run inside the originating run-to-completion pass while app-db still reflects the pre-registration/pre-clear state, and can persist a wrong decision even though the later settle repairs the final derived slot. Production probe: register-flow + [:dispatch [:read-after-register]] leaves {:seen-after-register nil, :derived 3}; clear-flow + [:dispatch [:read-after-clear]] leaves {:seen-after-clear 3} after :derived is removed. Thus a continuation after register cannot read the new output, and a continuation after clear reads the stale one. This defeats ergonomic composition of the new automatic contract with ordinary follow-up work. Minimal completion: after the completed fx walk, prioritize the one private settle ahead of already queued continuations (still one ordinary internal event, same frame, no public knob), and pin both register/read and clear/read ordering. Preserve the one-install-per-event and existing failure path.

AUDIT-FIX 2026-09-01 21:35 AUSEST (worker, PR #8929). ORDER-NOTE-START-KH73V.

HISTORY WALK. bd history rf2-kh73v --json, 775 snapshots, adjacent pairs walked
newest-first over description/notes/acceptance/design/title. Newest
text-bearing change is the notes append at 2026-09-01T18:21:40 (7477 -> 8674
chars) - the AUDIT note that reopened this - with the status flip closed->open
at 18:21:33 just behind it. Nothing text-bearing after it; the 100-odd later
entries are checkpoint no-ops. Description unchanged since creation, so the
brief's reading is right: the description scopes work that already merged as
PR #8893, and the audit note is the live instruction. No comments (bd comments
--json returns []). No new child beads.

PROBE REPRODUCED AT TIP, exactly the audit's values.
  register: reg-flow + [:dispatch [:read-after-register]]
    -> {:wizard {:foo 1, :bar 2}, :seen-after-register nil, :derived 3}
  clear:    clear-flow + [:dispatch [:read-after-clear]]
    -> {:wizard {:foo 1, :bar 2}, :seen-after-clear 3}  (:derived gone)
A third shape, not in the audit and worth recording because it shows the bug is
not simply "the settle is last": a handler emitting [:dispatch [:read-a]],
reg-flow, [:dispatch [:read-b]] read [[:a nil] [:b 3]] - :read-b saw the value
because :read-a's OWN flow transform had already computed it. So the pre-fix
damage is confined to the FIRST continuation, which is exactly why it reads as
a boundary that mostly works.

ONE TRAP WORTH THE NEXT WORKER'S TIME. The first cut of the regression file
omitted (:require [re-frame.flows]) - the namespace whose load publishes the
:flows/reg-flow / :flows/clear-flow late-bind hooks. Without it the reserved fx
find no hook and NO-OP SILENTLY, so every assertion goes red with :derived
absent, which reads exactly like the lagging runtime and would have been
reported as a worse bug than the one that exists. Caught by running the audit's
probe in a throwaway namespace that DID require it and getting a different
answer. The require is now in the file with a comment saying why.

MECHANISM CHOSEN: an envelope flag the router head-inserts on.
:rf.flow/settle? rides the envelope (set by fx/settle-flows-if-requested!
through the existing child-dispatch! seam, carried by build-envelope on the
same unconditional terms as :rf.machine/internal?), and router/insert-envelope
places it at the ABSOLUTE HEAD. Still one ordinary internal event, same frame,
no public knob.

Two alternatives, and why each is worse:
  * REUSE front-insert-machine-internal's boundary splice. It splices AFTER the
    machine-internal prefix because it is called once per sibling and must keep
    siblings in source order. The settle has no siblings - at most one per :fx
    walk, enqueued at the very end of it - so there is nothing for a splice to
    preserve, and a settle behind the machine-internal prefix leaves the machine
    case broken: machine continuations are "already queued continuations" too.
  * RUN THE SETTLE SYNCHRONOUSLY inside do-fx's terminal branch. Worse on both
    counts the audit tells us to protect: it re-enters the drain outside
    run-to-completion, and it puts settle-time :derive throws back inside the
    registering event, which is the failure boundary PR #8893 deliberately moved
    out.

WHY SETTLING EARLY IS FREE, since PR #8893's own docstring argued the opposite
("the back is the one that settles ONCE over everything the cascade did"). The
flow transform runs on EVERY event, so each continuation settles its own writes
on its own drain. One late settle was never needed to cover the cascade; it only
ever needed to cover the case where NO further event runs.

INCIDENTAL SIMPLIFICATION, not scope creep. The queue-ordering rule was written
out twice - inline in ensure-drain-scheduled! and again in enqueue-envelope! -
so adding a second exception would have meant adding it twice. Both now read one
insert-envelope. head-insert is a separate one-liner beside
front-insert-machine-internal.

KNOWN-DISPATCH-OPTS. :rf.flow/settle? had to join
router.diagnostics/known-dispatch-opts or the no-silent-swallow diagnostic would
fire :rf.warning/unknown-dispatch-opt on the framework's own settle. That set is
pinned by an equality assertion in
implementation/core/test/re_frame/unknown_dispatch_opts_warn_test.clj, updated
with it. No spec file enumerates the set (009 references it by name only), and
neither Spec-Schemas' :rf/dispatch-opts nor :rf/dispatch-envelope lists
:rf.machine/internal? either - checked with a control grep that bit (4 hits for
rf/dispatch-opts, 0 for the flag).

NO SPEC CHANGE, and the reason is on the page: Spec 013 Sequencing already says
applications must not depend on the settling event's id, its trace presence, OR
ITS POSITION IN THE QUEUE. This moves the position inside that stated contract.
:rf.flow/* (singular) is the rostered flows sub-namespace in Conventions line
71, so the flag needs no roster row - and the precedent is exact:
:rf.machine/internal? is not in the :rf.machine/* row either. NOTE the first
draft used :rf.flows/settle? and was corrected: :rf.flows/* is not a rostered
root and would have invented a second flows namespace.

rf2-z529y (Conventions roster for :rf/settle-flows) IS ALREADY DONE at tip -
spec/Conventions.md line 46 names :rf/settle-flows at length, including the
reserved-but-never-registered distinction. Not taken here, and appears to need
nothing further; worth a look before it is dispatched again.

GATES, captured exit codes, all re-run on the final base after rebasing onto
current origin/main (8951a73642; trunk's only source movement in the interval
was implementation/ssr/**, zero overlap):
  JVM flows  clojure -M:test in implementation/flows -> 0 (250 tests, 6102 assertions)
  JVM core   clojure -M:test in implementation/core  -> 0 (2174 tests, 11130 assertions)
  CLJS node  npm run test:cljs from implementation   -> 0 (11149 tests, 55134 assertions)
No markdown in the diff, so neither doc-link gate is nominated.

ORDER-NOTE-MIDDLE-KH73V.

CONTROL, and its shape is the deliverable. Reverting only the ordering (the
settle's :rf.flow/settle? set false, so the envelope falls back to conj - the
pre-change back-of-queue behaviour) took the FULL flows lane to captured exit 1
with exactly 3 failures across the SAME 250 tests / 6102 assertions:
  RED   settle-precedes-continuations-queued-by-the-registering-handler
        (the :seen-after-register assertion, line 65)
  RED   settle-precedes-continuations-queued-by-the-clearing-handler
        (the :seen-after-clear assertion, line 93)
  RED   settle-precedes-a-whole-run-of-queued-continuations
        ([[:a nil] [:b 3]] for [[:a 3] [:b 3]], line 117)
  GREEN all 247 pre-existing flows tests, INCLUDING all three of
        flows_settle_on_dispatch_test's settle-boundary tests, AND the three
        preconditions inside the new tests themselves (each new deftest asserts
        the PR #8893 boundary before it asserts the ordering, and those held).
Identical namespace and assertion counts between control and green run, so
nothing was skipped. That asymmetry is the finding: the pre-existing lane passes
under the buggy ordering, which is why the audit had to find this by hand.

WORKTREE DISCRIMINATION. The CLJS lane prints its config path and it named this
checkout. The core JVM lane prints no root, so it was discriminated by a planted
unresolved symbol in router.cljc, which took it to captured exit 1 naming the
plant. The flows lane needed no plant of its own - the ordering revert above was
planted in core's fx.cljc and reddened the flows lane, which is positive evidence
that lane read this checkout's core source.

Both plants restored and verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object
(line endings are translated here, so a byte digest of the working file is not
sound): fx.cljc back to 76b0e3746a2b0b5dcb6a94f100fc32623690b069, router.cljc
back to 8b381fdea89bd4a056413b6672396c04568e34cd, tree clean after each. Worth
recording that the FIRST plant attempt silently no-opped - a perl substitution
whose pattern escaped the slashes inside a quotemeta block - and was caught only
because the post-plant blob hash was IDENTICAL to the pre-plant one. Had the hash
not been read, that plant would have produced a green sabotage run and an
inverted conclusion.

FILES: implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc, router.cljc, events.cljc,
implementation/core/src/re_frame/router/diagnostics.cljc,
implementation/core/test/re_frame/unknown_dispatch_opts_warn_test.clj,
implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_settle_ordering_test.clj (new).
Neither live_frame.cljc nor frame.cljc (held by rf2-cq0yi) was touched -
confirmed by name against the merge-base diff. No flows SOURCE change was
needed: the defect was entirely in core's queue ordering.

ORDER-NOTE-END-KH73V.

The audit's back-of-queue settle is fixed: the one framework-private [:rf/settle-flows] now head-inserts ahead of the continuations the same handler queued. title: surface-review(hicasso): reduce the clj-kondo export to macro-shape analysis
description:
## Scope

Reduce Hicasso's shipped clj-kondo integration to the part that materially improves ordinary authoring: correct analysis of `h/defview`, `h/event`, and `h/defhost` as macro shapes. The scope is the export under `implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2-hicasso/`, its fixtures/checker under `implementation/hicasso/`, the `test:hicasso-lint` scheduling references, and live package/user/example prose that promises the six custom findings.

Preserve the export's classpath/package delivery. Do not change Hicasso runtime semantics or the public authoring API.

## Findings

The useful editor contract and the accidental apparatus are currently fused in one 847-line hook. The three rewrites make normal clj-kondo analysis understand view names, destructured props, callback bindings/arity, and host option references. That is high-value, general-purpose assistance.

The other half is a bespoke behavioral linter: two custom errors and four custom warnings, plus Hiccup walkers, symbol resolution, a hand-maintained lexical-scope grammar, exact-row fixture matrices, and a mutation-testing gate. Across the hook, README, config, two fixtures, and checker this surface is 2,400 lines. It also owns a required CI lane and a fast-PR step.

That analyzer has already demonstrated the wrong maintenance shape for a trust-the-programmer library. The ERROR-level `direct-view-call` rule repeatedly blocked valid code because a hook has no scope table: parameters and `let` bindings, multi-arity `letfn`, six more binding forms, `areduce`/`amap`, and method-spec grammar each required repair. The same shadowing blindness then spread to the read warnings. The current hook documents a finite roster and still tells authors to rename a legal local or disable the rule for forms outside it.

The payoff remains intrinsically narrow. The direct-call check can see only a view calling itself, not the ordinary cross-view mistake. The function-head check can see literals, not symbols. The key rule deliberately misses the common dynamic-props spelling. The a11y rule cannot see tree-level naming. The deferred-read warning explicitly admits legal synchronous callbacks can trigger it. These limits are honest, but they mean substantial custom machinery protects a small, non-authoritative slice while the actual runtime, React, and Hicasso test kit already own the relevant behavior.

For a pre-alpha surface, carrying this analyzer is worse than teaching the small set of authoring laws clearly and keeping the real failures loud at their execution boundary. It increases contributor and AI context, creates a second grammar that must track Clojure/CLJS binding forms, and turns lint maintenance into product work without making the core SPA API more expressive.

## Recommended Action

Keep the published clj-kondo export, but reduce it to the shortest honest implementation of these three shapes:

- `defview` is analyzed as a definition with its one props vector and body;
- `event` is analyzed as a function with its argument vector and body;
- `defhost` defines its name and analyzes the component/options expressions.

Delete the six `:re-frame.hicasso/*` behavioral findings, their Hiccup/scope walkers, the positive/negative behavioral matrices, and the mutation framework built to keep that custom analyzer correct. Replace the dedicated behavioral gate with one small consumer smoke, preferably folded into an existing package/lint lane, that imports the export through the artifact classpath and proves ordinary clj-kondo analysis sees the three macro shapes. Remove stale live claims and scheduling apparatus. Do not replace the deleted checks with compiler analysis, cache-backed namespace analysis, a new warning framework, or a compatibility layer.

## Evidence

- Current measured surface: hook 847 lines; export README 236; config 46; positive fixture 245; negative fixture 542; checker 484 — 2,400 lines total.
- `hooks/re_frame/hicasso.clj:7-12` describes the valuable macro-shape job; `:14-25` introduces the separate six-finding engine. `config.edn:31-46` couples both jobs.
- The hand-built scope model occupies the `bound-symbols`/`locals-bound-by`/`self-call-nodes` path through `check-direct-view-call!`; its own comments say the binding roster is the price of having no scope table.
- `README.md:48-109` says `direct-view-call` cannot see another view, enumerates the finite binding roster, and asks authors using an unrecognized form to rename the local or switch the check off. `:125-175`, `:188-217`, and `:225-233` document similar blind spots for the warnings and other desired checks.
- `check_lint_export.py:273-455` is a mutation harness largely preserving regressions in that custom grammar. It is scheduled by `implementation/package.json:45`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml:464`, and `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1547-1548`.
- The repair history is concrete: `rf2-hic-022` was repeatedly reopened for valid-code false errors; `rf2-ka4d` records the finite binding roster and later method/array-macro defects; `rf2-c6t6` records the same shadowing defect in the read rules. Commits from 2026-08-10 through 2026-08-11 repeatedly repaired the hook before the API had a first tagged release.
- Authoritative downstream behavior remains: bad heads refuse in `impl/codec.cljs`; out-of-render reads refuse in `impl/collector.cljs`; boundary-crossing deferrals refuse in `impl/codec.cljs`; React reports general missing keys; `ht/unnamed-controls` performs tree-level accessibility inspection. Live user docs already teach the corresponding recovery routes.
- Active-bead searches for `clj-kondo`, `lint export`, `direct-view-call`, the hook path, and `check_lint_export.py` found no task owning this reduction. `rf2-6c12m` is the broad dead-weight epic, but none of its children targets this residual.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A consumer importing Hicasso's clj-kondo export from the artifact classpath gets correct ordinary analysis for all documented `defview`, `event`, and `defhost` declaration shapes, including optional docstrings and destructuring.
2. The shipped export defines no `:re-frame.hicasso/*` custom behavioral linters, calls no `api/reg-finding!`, and contains no bespoke Hiccup walker or lexical binding-form roster.
3. The six-finding positive/negative fixture matrices and their mutation machinery are removed. Any remaining gate is a compact packaging/macro-shape consumer smoke, not a second static analyzer.
4. Package scripts, required workflow/fast-PR scheduling, export README, core docs, and live example comments no longer promise or schedule the removed findings. Historical design records need not be rewritten merely to erase history.
5. The normal repository clj-kondo lane remains green on Hicasso code, and a negative control proves the macro-shape smoke fails when one of the three rewrites is unavailable.
6. Runtime behavior, runtime refusal contracts, React behavior, the test-kit accessibility surface, and Hicasso's public API are unchanged.
7. The resulting diff is a material net deletion with no replacement analyzer, compatibility shim, or new dependency.

## Non-goals

- Adding whole-program, cache-backed, compiler, or cross-namespace analysis.
- Recreating any removed finding at warning level or in another tool.
- Weakening or expanding runtime validation and diagnostics.
- Removing ordinary clj-kondo analysis or the artifact's exported macro configuration.
- Changing `defview`, `event`, `defhost`, Hiccup, routing, accessibility, or subscription semantics.
- Broad CI restructuring unrelated to retiring this dedicated behavioral gate.

## Related beads

- `rf2-6c12m` — active Hicasso dead-weight epic; this is a de-duplicated residual not owned by an existing child.
- `rf2-hic-022` — introduced the six bounded findings and records repeated false-ERROR reopenings.
- `rf2-ka4d` — repaired missing binding forms, array macros, and method grammar in `direct-view-call`.
- `rf2-c6t6` — repaired the same lexical-shadowing blindness in the read rules.
- `rf2-zzdg` — repaired drift in the dedicated lint workflow's mutation-count prose.

Triage note: keeping the npm script NAME test:hicasso-lint and its lint.yml step means lint.yml, test-fast-pr.sh and check_fast_pr_gap.py need no edit — hot-zone touch drops to zero; brief will say so. Also delete .clj-kondo/config.edn:49-56 per-namespace :off overrides for the retired findings.
Chronological merged-PR audit (#8808): the reduced macro-shape export is correct, but its shipped README overstates the replacement contract. It says every mistake seen by the six retired checks is now refused at execution with a named :rf.error/hicasso-* id. That is false for at least unkeyed mapped children (React warning), nameless interactive elements (test-kit/tree-level accessibility inspection), and parked reads (documented programmer judgment/undefined conduct); the bead's own evidence distinguishes those owners. Correct this one paragraph to name the split authority without restoring lint checks, changing runtime behavior, sweeping historical records, or adding a gate.

Audit residual fixed by PR #8823: the shipped README's replacement paragraph now names the split authority (runtime :rf.error/hicasso-* refusals for bad heads/out-of-render reads/boundary-crossing deferrals; React's missing-key warning for unkeyed mapped children; test-kit ht/unnamed-controls for nameless interactive elements; parked reads documented judgment, nothing polices). Gates on final base, captured exits: check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 (planted broken link in the edited file went exit 1 naming file+line, restore blob-hash-verified); npm run test:hicasso-lint exit 0 (self-test PASS incl. behavioral-linter-rides-back-in negative control). No runtime change, no gate added.

title: surface-review(schemas): elide Malli's dev-only humanizer from production bundles
description:
## Scope

Review and tighten the production bundle boundary of the shipped `implementation/schemas` artifact: its Malli adapter, late-bind integration with core, advanced-build A/B gate, JVM/CLJS diagnostic tests, package manifest, spec/API/how-to text, and examples that intentionally use Malli directly.

## Verified Findings

- Loading the public `re-frame.schemas` facade transitively loads `re-frame.schemas.malli`. That adapter unconditionally requires `malli.error` and publishes `malli.error/humanize` under `:schemas/humanize-explain!`, alongside the always-needed Malli validate/explain hooks.
- The humanizer has no production runtime consumer in the shipped schemas/core path. `validate.cljc` consults it only to enrich `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` dev traces with `:explain-humanized`; those emit paths are behind `interop/debug-enabled?` and are DCE-elided for advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` builds. The always-on production boundary record is deliberately structural-only and omits Malli explanation/humanization.
- The matched advanced A/B bundle report records a 41,570-byte gzip schemas margin (40.6 KB) and attributes 12.0 KB of post-Closure optimized code to `malli.error` (about 6 KB gzip in the spec's dependency guidance). Spec 010 explicitly calls this a measured exception to its own dev/test-only guidance for `malli.error`.
- Existing JVM tests pin useful development behavior, including real `:explain-humanized` payloads and symmetric redaction for sensitive values. The bundle gate bounds total margin but does not assert that the dev-only humanizer is unreachable in production.
- `implementation/schemas/deps.edn` correctly keeps Malli as the artifact's default validator dependency; this finding is about separating Malli core validation from Malli error presentation, not removing the default validator.
- The login example directly requires and calls `malli.error` for application form UX. That explicit consumer should continue paying for it; it does not justify making every schemas consumer pay through the adapter's dev-only hook.

## Recommended Action

Make publication/reachability of `:schemas/humanize-explain!` debug-only and Closure-DCE-safe in the Malli adapter while leaving `malli.core/validate` and `malli.core/explain` wired automatically in every build. Keep the public require/API unchanged. Extend the matched production build proof so it demonstrates that `malli.error` is absent from the schemas probe unless application code directly requires/uses it, then remeasure and update the two-sided bundle budget and documentation from that result.

## Evidence

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/malli.cljc:34,54` — unconditional `malli.error` require and ns-load publication.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:305-322,548-554,839-859` — the only in-artifact humanizer reads feed dev diagnostic tags.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` — always-on boundary validation/rejection does not require a humanized payload; production reporting is structural.
- `implementation/scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs:36-57,126` — matched advanced control/probe, current 41,570-byte gzip margin, and `malli.error` attribution.
- `spec/010-Schemas.md:279-291,723-745` — humanization is documented as production-elided while `malli.error` is simultaneously recorded as production-reachable.
- `docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:236` and `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:272` — development diagnostic and redaction contracts.
- `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_sensitive_test.clj:1652-1770` — humanized-payload and privacy coverage to preserve.
- `implementation/schemas/deps.edn:32-34` — package boundary and default Malli dependency.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljs` — deliberate direct application use of `malli.error`, which remains outside adapter elision.
- Relevant history: `0702449fe7`, `967fd3de95`, and `81e5b2051c` established/attributed the current matched bundle budget rather than removing this reachability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Requiring `re-frame.schemas` still installs the default Malli validate/explain behavior without an extra application require in development and production; schema-implies-validation and core production-boundary behavior remain green.
- Development JVM and CLJS coverage proves failures still carry useful `:explain-humanized` data, and sensitive failures still redact raw and humanized explanations symmetrically.
- An advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` matched control/probe build proves the schemas adapter no longer retains `malli.error`; an application probe that directly uses `malli.error/humanize` still retains and works with it.
- The matched gzip margin drops measurably from the recorded 41,570 bytes. The checked-in baseline/two-sided band is re-derived from clean repeated measurements and retains its non-vacuity controls.
- Public namespace/import ergonomics and schema registration/validation semantics do not change.
- Spec 010, API/how-to material, adapter docstrings, and bundle attribution describe the resulting dev-versus-production boundary consistently.

## Non-goals

- Removing Malli or making users manually install the default validator.
- Changing schema registration, validation, recovery, privacy, or production boundary semantics.
- Preventing applications from directly requiring/using `malli.error` for product UI.
- Adding a dynamic loader, a new public configuration switch, compatibility aliases, or speculative runtime guards.
- Broadly optimizing Malli internals or unrelated schemas code.

## Related beads

- Historical/landed context: `rf2-v96fh` (schema implies validation), `rf2-kybsf` / `rf2-v4o7e` (schemas bundle attribution/gate), `rf2-2ek7t` / `rf2-qhq3f` (humanized diagnostics and redaction).
- Live tracker duplicate search on 2026-08-30 for schemas bundle, `malli.error`, `humanize-explain`, and production humanization found no owning issue.

Premises verified at source before dispatch; the brief names the wave's other four surfaces as the fence. Worker closes this bead on PR-ready with the PR URL.
VERDICT (worker, 2026-08-31, PR #8788). The humanizer publication in re-frame.schemas.malli now sits behind interop/debug-enabled? (goog.DEBUG); malli.core validate/explain stay published in every build; public require/API unchanged; login example untouched.

MEASURED on the matched schemas-bundle A/B (gzipped, control 86851 B): unconditional publication (trunk) margin 41595 B (40.6 KB) -> gated 40885 B (39.9 KB), -0.7 KB. The :schemas/humanize-explain! keyword and the humanize code leave the probe (keyword count 1 -> 0; malli/error.cljc 12.0 -> 10.5 KB optimized). Counterfactual with the adapter's [malli.error] require deleted: 38333 B (37.4 KB), -3.3 KB, every malli.error literal gone.

title: surface-review(machines): make pure transition results self-describing
description:
## Scope

Redesign the application-facing result contract of re-frame.machines/machine-transition, together with its normative spec, generated API projection, guides, executable examples, manifest coverage, and focused JVM/CLJS tests. Keep runtime transition semantics and the event/effect model unchanged.

## Findings

machine-transition is presented as the simple, pure way to test a machine, but the facade currently aliases the engine function directly and leaks the re-frame.machines.result representation. Callers must require a second namespace, learn either result/ok?, result/snap, result/fx, and result/info or opaque namespaced keys (::tag, ::snap, ::fx, ::info), and reconcile documentation that calls those keys public with a namespace docstring that calls the namespace internal. This makes the most important testing seam less obvious to programmers and harder for AI tools to infer or generate correctly.

The public API manifest inventories re-frame.machines/machine-transition but does not inventory re-frame.machines.result, while the tutorial, inspection guide, API page, normative spec, and executable walkthrough all require that omitted namespace. The result representation is therefore public in practice but private-looking and absent from the authoritative public surface.

## Recommended Action

Make a clean pre-alpha break: have the public re-frame.machines/machine-transition return one transparent, self-describing ordinary map owned by the facade. A suitable contract is success {:status :ok, :snapshot snapshot, :fx [...]} and engine-reported failure {:status :error, :error diagnostic}; settle the exact spellings once in the normative spec and use them everywhere. Application code and tests should need only re-frame.machines.

Remove re-frame.machines.result from application-facing docs and examples. Delete it if the engine no longer needs it, or keep an internal representation genuinely private and normalize only at the facade boundary. Do not retain aliases, tombstones, dual shapes, or compatibility adapters.

## Evidence

- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:103 exports machine-transition as a direct alias of engine/machine-transition, so the engine representation becomes the public representation.
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/result.cljc:6-20 defines the ::tag/::snap/::fx/::info map and labels three keys public, while lines 43-45 describe the namespace as internal to the machines artefact.
- docs/machines/tutorial.md:320-348 and docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md:128-166 teach a second re-frame.machines.result require plus accessors solely to inspect a pure transition.
- docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:143-164 and spec/API.md:936 name re-frame.machines.result/Result as the public return type.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj:867-888 imports re-frame.machines.result and destructures ::result/snap and ::result/fx in the executable public walkthrough.
- spec/api-manifest.edn contains the machine-transition row but no re-frame.machines.result rows; implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:88-111 introspects re-frame.machines but not the result namespace.
- A repository-wide search finds 45 files requiring re-frame.machines.result and 43 files consuming its accessors or namespaced keys, so this is established cross-cutting friction rather than a single stale example.
- History introduced the Result ADT and accessors in commits 964e08dc16 and 742e30bd97 on 2026-05-14. The source comment records public-key churn as the reason not to use a record; in the current pre-alpha phase that compatibility concern should not dictate a permanently awkward public seam.
- Exact tracker searches for machine-transition, re-frame.machines.result, transition result, result ADT, pure transition, machine testing, state machine testing, and machines API found no existing issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The normative machine spec defines one exact, self-describing public return shape for successful and engine-reported failed pure transitions, including snapshot, ordered effects, and diagnostic data.
- re-frame.machines/machine-transition implements that contract without requiring consumers to know an internal namespace or qualified implementation keys.
- Existing semantics remain covered: successful snapshots and effect order are unchanged; thrown action/guard failures and depth-abort failures remain atomic and diagnostic; programmer-input errors that intentionally throw have a clearly documented boundary.
- Focused JVM and CLJS machine tests, conformance fixtures, and executable examples assert the public shape through re-frame.machines only.
- Spec 005, spec/API.md, docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, the tutorial, inspection guide, and state-machine walkthrough all use the same contract and no longer teach re-frame.machines.result.
- The API manifest/generator and drift checks accurately describe the resulting public surface; no public namespace used by the docs is omitted from that surface.
- The old application-facing Result accessors and key shape are removed in the same change, with no compatibility layer.

## Non-goals

- Changing statechart syntax, transition selection, hierarchy, action execution, effect ordering, dispatch, timers, actor ownership, or spawn semantics.
- Designing a model-based testing DSL, matcher library, or new helper namespace.
- Redesigning the broader exception taxonomy beyond documenting the existing programmer-error boundary.
- Solving eager singleton startup or synthetic start-event ergonomics.
- Preserving the old Result shape for compatibility.

- rf2-npgc (closed) restructured the machines guide and added inspecting-machines.md; it is documentation context, not duplicate implementation work.
- rf2-cnij (closed) improved facade docstrings and API notes; it did not cover the pure transition result contract.

title: surface-review(core): remove implementation-only constructors from re-frame.core
description:
## Scope

Make the `re-frame.core` facade expose the supported authoring surfaces, not the implementation-only lowering constructors behind them. Remove `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`, `re-frame.core/->interceptor`, and `re-frame.core/->interceptor*` from the public facade; relocate or delete their lowering entry points as appropriate, and update the macro/runtime consumers that legitimately need them. Keep `re-frame.core/capture-frame` and `re-frame.core/reg-interceptor` as the app-facing paths.

## Independently verified Findings

- The accepted pre-alpha facade rule says internalising an export must remove it from the facade, manifest, and current API projection; a docstring saying “internal” while `:facade? true` remains is named as the precise failure mode (`spec/Conventions.md`, “Removing or demoting a facade export — delete, don't demote”).
- That exact failure is live. `make-capture-frame` and `->interceptor` are `:tier :implementation` plus `:facade? true`; `->interceptor*` is `:tier :advanced` plus `:facade? true` even though its status and docs say “internal lowering only”. All three appear in generated `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`.
- The exposure is plumbing, not an app capability. `reg-view` expands through `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`; the interceptor macro expands through `re-frame.core/->interceptor*`; the owned runtime constructor already exists as `re-frame.interceptor/->interceptor*`. A compiler-visible Var need not live on the user facade.
- SCI copies every public runtime Var from `re-frame.core`, so the accidental surface is also presented to playground users and AI-generated examples.
- The earlier API-shrink commit `ca1fa564da` declared `capture-frame` the one public carry primitive but retiered `make-capture-frame` instead of removing it. The same repository conventions explicitly reject annotation as removal.
- The conventions say a public-facade manifest-hygiene CI check enforces this disposition, but `.github/workflows/lint.yml` records that the old check was retired. Current manifest generation accepts the contradictory rows, so the same drift can recur.

## Recommended Action

Move the capture-frame and interceptor lowering seams behind explicitly non-facade implementation namespaces (or delete a wrapper where the owning constructor already suffices). Repoint `reg-view` and interceptor macro expansion, internal/test consumers, and SCI bindings to those owned seams. Remove the three facade Vars and their manifest/API entries without compatibility aliases. Add a small generic manifest invariant that rejects implementation-only rows exported with `:facade? true`, so an internal docstring/status cannot masquerade as surface removal again.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1369` — `make-capture-frame` says it is internal and public only for macro expansion; `capture-frame` begins at line 1453.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2137` — `->interceptor` says it is an internal lowering constructor and directs apps to `reg-interceptor`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:187` — emitted code calls `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_call_site_macros.cljc:173-179` — emitted code calls `re-frame.core/->interceptor*`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:23` — the owned `->interceptor*` constructor already exists.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn:69-70,74,118` — the three internal constructors are facade rows beside the front-porch `capture-frame` row.
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:635-668` — metadata acknowledges the internal-only dispositions while retaining facade placement.
- `spec/Conventions.md:1235-1250` — pre-alpha delete-not-demote rule and its stated manifest guardrail.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:1471` — `capture-frame` is the one public carry primitive and `make-capture-frame` is not app API.
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:475-483,556-571` — generated public API publishes the internal constructors.
- `docs/tools/playground/sci/src/rf2_playground/sci.cljs:156,165-188` — SCI macro expansion names `make-capture-frame` and `copy-ns` exposes all public core runtime Vars.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/reg_view_injection_test.clj:298` and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/interceptor_runtime_complete_cljs_test.cljc` — tests currently pin the facade plumbing rather than its absence.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml:627-637` — manifest checks remain, but the former facade-hygiene check is explicitly retired.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `re-frame.core` no longer resolves or documents `make-capture-frame`, `->interceptor`, or `->interceptor*` in either CLJ or CLJS, and none has a `:facade? true` manifest row.
2. `reg-view` expansion and internal interceptor construction use owned non-facade symbols; compilation, source-coordinate stamping/elision, and advanced-build behavior remain intact.
3. `capture-frame` remains the single supported carry primitive, preserving frame-incarnation fencing and injected dispatch/subscribe behavior; `reg-interceptor` remains the supported interceptor authoring form.
4. Playground SCI still supports `reg-view`, `capture-frame`, and registered interceptors without copying the removed runtime aliases into `re-frame.core`.
5. Focused tests assert both behavioral preservation and facade absence in CLJ/CLJS. Generated API/manifest projections and affected specs/docs agree with the resulting surface.
6. A generic automated check fails on a planted manifest row that combines an implementation-only disposition with `:facade? true`, and passes after the plant is removed.

## Non-goals

- No broad reclassification of the rest of `re-frame.core`, Story, or Xray.
- No redesign of capture-frame lifecycle semantics, interceptor descriptors, registration, or source-coordinate diagnostics.
- No compatibility aliases, deprecation tier, tombstones, or new public sugar; this is pre-alpha surface correction.
- No change to the public names or signatures of `capture-frame` or `reg-interceptor`.

## Related existing beads

- `rf2-2hpxo` (P3, deferred) is the broad retrospective facade-export classification sweep for external-alpha prep. This task does not duplicate it: these three exports are already classified and documented as implementation-only; the work here is to execute those settled dispositions and restore a regression check.

title: surface-review(uix-adapter): make a real UIx component test copy-pasteable and executable
description:
## Scope

Make the consumer-facing UIx component-testing path runnable from the public docs and easy to copy into a real app. Use the adapter's existing UIx/React primitives; cover the smallest honest real-DOM loop (mount a hook component under `frame-root`, drive an event, settle with `flush-views!`, assert the DOM, and tear everything down). Keep the executable witness close enough to the docs or generated scaffold that drift is caught.

## Verified Findings

- The UIx runtime surface is already substantial and well covered: `spec/api-manifest.edn:60-68` rows all nine public adapter Vars, and the adapter forwards a large shared React regression suite. This is not a request to redesign `use-subscribe`, `use-frame`, or frame scoping.
- The main view-testing guide is not substrate-neutral in practice. `docs/core/testing/views.md:5` says a view is a callable pure function returning hiccup and builds the whole recipe around JVM tree walking. A UIx `defui` that calls `use-subscribe` / `use-frame` is a React hook component and cannot use that recipe. The page's only UIx-relevant escape at line 93 says to use a real DOM and `flush-views!`, but supplies no mount, fixture, event, assertion, or cleanup shape.
- UIx's own public docs stop at the settling primitive: `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`, `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`, and `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:17` show `flush-views!` but no complete component test.
- The generated UIx app does not fill the gap. `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309` emits only `events_test.cljs`; `_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24` explicitly runs DOM-free against a headless adapter. That is good dataflow coverage, but it teaches nothing about testing the UIx view the scaffold just generated.
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128` explicitly makes Test-React local-only, React-free, DOM-free, opaque-tree, and non-reconciling. It therefore cannot execute UIx hooks and is not a missing consumer test kit to point at.
- The desired flow already exists as framework evidence: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` plus `testbed/spec.cjs` prove frame-root mount -> use-subscribe -> click/dispatch -> DOM rerender in a real browser. Commit `2d2f4aff53` introduced the per-adapter testbed; commit `b924dca1af` introduced the current hiccup-centric Test-a-view recipe. The missing work is to turn those two disconnected bodies of knowledge into one consumer-shaped, executable UIx recipe.

## Recommended Action

Publish one canonical, copy-complete UIx component test using existing APIs only. Put the explanation where a test author looks (`docs/core/testing/views.md` and the UIx adapter docs), point the generated UIx README at it, and back the exact shape with a focused browser-lane test or other named executable witness. Prefer a small fixture/helper local to the example over a new framework abstraction. The recipe should make lifecycle ownership obvious: one mount node/root, `frame-root` (or an explicitly created/scoped frame), a real DOM interaction, `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, an assertion, and guaranteed unmount/runtime cleanup.

## Concrete Evidence

- `docs/core/testing/views.md:5,93`
- `spec/008-Testing.md:36-48,107` (defines `flush-views!` and marks real React mounting CLJS-only, but illustrates only the Reagent call)
- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309`
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24`
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128`
- `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` and `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/spec.cjs`
- History: `2d2f4aff53` (adapter testbeds), `b924dca1af` (Test-a-view recipe), `9cf8f2e54c` (generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A copy-complete CLJS UIx test mounts a `defui` that uses `use-subscribe` and/or `use-frame` under a valid frame boundary, drives a real DOM event, settles through `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, observes the updated DOM, and guarantees unmount plus frame/adapter cleanup.
2. The published command for that test runs successfully in a named browser/DOM-capable lane; a focused executable test protects the recipe from API or lifecycle drift.
3. `docs/core/testing/views.md` explicitly distinguishes its fast hiccup-walk path from UIx hook components and links the runnable UIx recipe rather than implying the hiccup recipe applies.
4. The UIx adapter README/API and generated UIx project README make the first component-test path discoverable; the scaffold's existing DOM-free event/sub tests remain the recommended default for business logic.
5. The solution uses current public primitives. No new public helper namespace/API is added unless implementing the executable recipe demonstrates unavoidable repeated lifecycle machinery.

## Non-goals

- Do not publish or expand the internal Test-React adapter; it deliberately models class-3 lifecycle without React and cannot be made into UIx by adding shims.
- Do not build a Testing Library clone, add speculative compatibility layers, or create a full per-adapter test matrix.
- Do not change UIx hook signatures, frame semantics, adapter installation semantics, or the substrate contract.
- Do not require every generated project to run a browser suite by default if a documented, executable opt-in recipe gives the same low-friction path.

## Related beads

- `rf2-0c23j` (closed): ruled the `flush-views!` test door and documented its render-phase constraint.
- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed): repaired the generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle; its one-root/after-load shape is the right lifecycle donor.
- `rf2-60aoj` (closed): established that Test-React intentionally omits React render flushing and is a different capability, not the UIx test path.

No matching open or closed bead was found by title searches for UIx testing/component tests and description searches across `uix`, `test-react`, `flush-views!`, `real DOM`, and `component test`.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, copy-complete UIx browser component test mounts a hook component under a frame boundary, drives a real event, settles with `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, asserts updated DOM, and guarantees cleanup; the exact recipe is executable in a named gate, is linked from the UIx adapter and generated-project docs, and the generic view-testing guide clearly routes UIx hook components to it. Existing public primitives are used unless the executable proof shows a helper is truly necessary.

Both successful paths finish with the flag forced to true; the async path also forces it false during polling. In a copied test suite this changes React act-warning/flush behaviour for later tests according to execution order, contradicting the page's copy-complete and unconditional-teardown promise. The shared React suite already demonstrates the bounded discipline at react_shared_suite.cljs:3280-3351: capture the previous value, use the required temporary state, restore it in guaranteed final cleanup. Apply that discipline locally to this recipe and its pinned docs block, preserving the false polling window and unconditional unmount; no public helper, abstraction, or broader test-harness redesign is owed. Completeness otherwise passes: browser execution, page/file byte pin, adapter/template pointers, fixture ownership, real click, bounded settle, and named gates are present.

AUDIT PR #8798 (2026-08-31): REOPENED. The success-path value restoration works, but it is not failure-safe. mount! sets the global before flush-views! and returns cleanup ownership only afterward; if render or act throws, no mounted token exists and the prior flag is lost. unmount! restores only after flush-views! and node.remove, so an unmount or effect-cleanup throw skips the flag restore and, in the async .finally callback, done. This contradicts the copy-complete unconditional-teardown and exactly-as-found contract and does not carry the donor final-cleanup discipline. Keep the correction local and surgical: restore and remove through try/finally or catch around mount and unmount, ensure async done executes even when cleanup throws, and commit one sentinel pre-value regression so the check does not depend on the ambient runner already being non-true. Do not create a shared fixture or pursue rf2-3t2nq broad consolidation.

title: hicasso defhost: infer the callback contract by position, keep :callbacks as a 2-value override, delete :handler (executes ruling rf2-6c12m.2)
description:

This description is the condensed DO.

THE RULE: a defhost or [:>] callback contract is inferred from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (intent.cljs:1200-1210 position-contract; intent.cljs:1212-1228 lower-prop): on*-spelled -> :event, any other walked prop -> :render, :ref -> React's, declared :slots -> markup. :callbacks survives ONLY as an optional override {<prop> :event|:render} written where inference is wrong (on*-named render props: Fluent onRenderItem/onRenderCell, Ant onRow/onCell/onFilter); a declared contract outranks the spelling. :handler is DELETED (a plain fn is the handler contract and already crosses untouched at every position - intent.cljs:1225,1228; codec.cljs:2865). A vector or map at a render position (inferred or overridden) crosses as data via host-prop-value, as at a native tag. An h/event at a declared :slots position stays refused.

CODE: host-entry (codec.cljs:3040-3111) :else arm -> reuse intent/lower-prop for the event/render inference, then host-prop-value; NO second classifier, warning, or compat layer. lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1255-1302) keeps :event and :render arms, drops :handler; non-callback values at :render route through host-prop-value. (intent.cljs:1230-1253), the false branch of refuse-unclaimed-host-callback! (:2899-2954, call site :3105-3106; KEEP the node-slot? branch, :3079-3080). title: RULING: src is 71% prose - docstring = contract plus one sentence of why; the essays move to docs/design/hicasso
description:
src/ is 17,113 lines of which ~12,000 are docstrings and comments (approx: codec.cljs 67%, collector.cljs 74%, controlled.cljs 78%, hicasso.cljc 87%, mount.cljs 76%). impl/ alone: 11,693 lines = 2,788 code + 7,207 docstring + 1,219 comment (72% prose). collector.cljs opens with a 393-line docstring before its first require; controlled.cljs is 688 doc lines for 155 of code; generation.cljs 102 doc lines for 26 of code. Docstrings cross-reference three others, so editing one mechanism means re-reading the essay on all of them, and finding flush! means scrolling ~1,000 lines. This is the shape problem underneath the rest of the review: nothing is short enough to be seen whole, which is why the dead weight survived, and it is why every rename is a multi-file multi-paragraph edit. docs/design/hicasso (146 files) already exists and is where HD-numbered rulings, measurement tables and rejected alternatives belong.

RECOMMENDATION: per file, docstring = what it is/returns, the contract, and one sentence of why (with a link to the design record for the argument); move measurement tables, rejected designs and ruling citations to docs/design/hicasso. Target roughly 1:1 prose:code. Best done per file alongside the cut tasks in this epic so the prose is trimmed once, after the code it describes has settled. This reverses the direction of PR #8736 (which polished the prose in place); that PR is not wasted - the survivors will be the timeless versions - but Mike should rule before a second prose pass starts.
