title: hic: the classifier pair still describes the hicasso contract documents as docs/** — stale premise, fails GREEN
description:
FOUND BY rf2-ps7ia STEP (a) (PR for worker/hicspec-ps7ia). NOT FIXED THERE, deliberately: the two files move in ONE commit by construction (CLAUDE.md's one-toucher pair) and a live peer held .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh at the time.

THE FACT THAT CHANGED. rf2-ps7ia moved five machine-gated documents out of docs/design/hicasso/product/ and into implementation/hicasso/spec/: dispositions.md, complaints.md, invariants.md, naming-ledger.md, budgets.md. Measured at the classifier rather than assumed — the NEW paths return cljs_node_test=true (plus cljs_browser, migration_hicasso_codemod, hicasso_controlled, hicasso_hmr), and the OLD paths returned every output false.

FINDING 1 — A STALE PINNED PREMISE THAT STILL PASSES.
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, the test named 'the complaint catalogue reads three families that arm NO expensive tier (rf2-hic-021)', asserts that docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md does not arm cljs_node_test. That file no longer exists. The assertion still PASSES, because the classifier is a lexical path function and does not care whether a path exists — so this is fail-green staleness rather than a break, which is why it is filed rather than urgent. Its ~10-line comment block above it ("reads FOUR file families ... exactly ONE arms cljs_node_test") is now false in the understating direction: the register family arms it now too. The row should either be re-pointed at implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md and INVERTED (it now arms), or dropped with the comment rewritten to say the hole closed. The two SIBLING rows in the same test — spec/009-Instrumentation.md and docs/core/hicasso/02-views-and-reads.md — were re-probed and are STILL false, so they are correct as written and must stay.

FINDING 2 — OVER-ARMING, A JUDGEMENT CALL RATHER THAN A DEFECT.
A markdown-only edit under implementation/hicasso/spec/ now arms cljs_browser, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr as well as cljs_node_test, because the classifier's implementation/hicasso/* arm does not discriminate .md. That is a Chromium lane queued for a prose edit. TESTING.md's standing rule is 'when in doubt, over-classify', and the test.yml comment block above the very test in finding 1 says in terms that arming a ~10-minute CLJS compile for a Markdown edit is the trade the placement table exists to refuse — so the two principles point opposite ways here and this is a call, not a bug. A narrowing arm would be implementation/hicasso/spec/*.md -> cljs_node_test only (the invariants chain is pure Python and is what these documents actually gate). Note the five documents ALSO have unconditional test.yml jobs of their own, so cljs_node_test is not the only thing standing behind them.

WHY ONE BEAD. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs are the one-toucher pair: the test pins the script's outputs, so a change to either alone lands a tree where the suite contradicts the script. Both findings touch that pair, so they are one dispatch.
notes:

MAYOR BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-21, tip c77fa75aa5. THE REOPEN IS SOUND — verified at source, not accepted on the audit's word — AND IT IS NOW FENCED.

THE AUDIT'S CLAIM HOLDS, both halves measured:

test's NAME overstates. The repair is a rename to the precise property (e.g. 'do not arm the
CLJS node-test tier'). NO CLASSIFIER BEHAVIOUR CHANGES.

along. That rule exists because the test pins the script's OUTPUTS; a test rename pins nothing

_changed-surfaces.test.cjs carries 28 freehand mentions, so the sweep may edit this exact file.

title: hicasso: aggregate randomisation band breaks the declared paired two-session assignment
description:
PR #8634's aggregate band samples each of the eight run schedules independently from the 48 per-run admissible schedules (48^8). That is not the assignment support the PR designed or executed: alloc_pass_design.cjs selects two distinct non-complement schedules A/B, adds their exact complements, and pre-registration repeats [A,B,~A,~B] verbatim in session B. The complementary pairing is load-bearing because it is what cancels every round-index nuisance; the cross-session repeat is load-bearing because the page calls the session the independent unit.

Reproduction against the committed eight runs: exhaustively enumerate the ordered design-preserving support [A,B,~A,~B,A,B,~A,~B], B != A and B != ~A. There are 48*46 = 2,208 configurations. The mid-rung result is 6/2208, p=0.002717 (not the published 1/20001 = 0.00005); the null control is 268/2208, p=0.121377 (not 0.0934). Outcome 1 remains at alpha 0.05, but the reported p-values, minimum attainable p, reference quantiles, and claim that the reference uses schedules the design would equally admit are wrong.

Repair the corpus reference so every draw preserves the declared complement pairing and cross-session repeat, add a test pinning that joint support rather than only each run's 48 marginal schedules, and re-adjudicate the published page without rewriting historical provenance pins. If a different reference is intended, state and justify that assignment mechanism without calling it the executed design's randomisation distribution.

title: mayor method: no rule says WHICH CLOCK dates a historical commit in prose, and the liveness rule reads as though it does
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-21, step 2 (checking the rules being ENFORCED against what the tree does). It cost a wrong flag to a live worker the same session.

THE GAP. Both layers state the author-versus-committer distinction, and all FOUR mentions are scoped to LIVENESS — is this worker alive? Measured with a grep over .claude/commands/*.md and docs/the-mayor-method/*.md:

  .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:12   liveness (tip SHA vs ahead count vs %aI/%cI)
  .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:30   liveness (same discriminator, stranded sweep)
  docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:613-616 liveness (generic form of the same)

NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS WHICH CLOCK TO READ WHEN **DATING** A COMMIT IN PROSE. That is a different question with the OPPOSITE answer, and the liveness rule actively misleads on it.

WHY THE TWO ANSWERS DIVERGE, and it is not a nuance. This repository rebase-merges, so %aI and %cI differ on essentially every merged commit.
  - For LIVENESS, the committer date is right: a rebase rewrites it, so it moves when the worker moves. The author date is replayed unchanged and reads as death.
  - For DATING A HISTORICAL COMMIT IN PROSE, the AUTHOR date is right: it is when the work was actually written. The committer date is an artefact of when the trunk happened to replay it, which is not a fact about the change at all.

A reader who has only ever met the liveness rule has been taught that %aI is the untrustworthy one, and will 'correct' a correct author date to a committer date.

THE MEASURED INSTANCE. A worker dated a set of deletions 2026-08-15 in a design record. The mayor flagged it against CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-16 and had to retract to the operator. Both dates are right and they are different clocks: commit ef3131f4a2 reads author=2026-08-15T20:07:56, committer=2026-08-16T13:29:40. The worker had used the correct clock; the mayor applied the liveness rule to a dating question.

WHERE THE FIX GOES — TWO LAYERS, KEPT APART.
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, beside the existing liveness passage at 613-616: the GENERIC rule. Which clock answers which question, and why they diverge under rebase. No repository names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths or tool names — that is the method tree's standing constraint.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md and .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md: the EXECUTING layer, where the concrete command may be named. One clause each, pointing at the generic rule rather than restating it, so the two copies cannot drift.

The point is not to add prose. It is that BOTH questions are now answerable from the same passage, so a reader meeting one cannot mistake it for the other.

title: hicasso: the published non-cancellation floor does not describe the corpus the allocation instrument produces now — 23.2% of the null arm sits above the 45 B/boundary bar
description:
MEASURED by rf2-fk6pj's phase-3 window, 2026-08-21, on 164 null-arm cells. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-design-control-comes-before-the-window.md, section D. Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-passterm/.

THE OBSERVATION. The R = 0 null arm reads nothing, so arm minus floor must be zero under either write; it is the only allocation population whose true value is known in advance, and rf2-2rtt6.140 published it as the instrument's NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR — 1.5 B/boundary median, 4.5 B p90 — setting a REFUSAL BAR of 45 B/boundary at ten times the p90. The fraction of that zero-signal population sitting ABOVE that bar has risen across three windows:

  rf2-0gjqi (parity, 2 x 6 rounds)   2 of 38   =  5.3%   p90  4.5
  phase 2   (seeded, 2 x 6 rounds)   4 of 40   = 10.0%   p90 56.5
  phase 3   (seeded, 4 x 12 rounds) 38 of 164  = 23.2%   p90 61

PHASE 2'S EXPLANATION IS REFUTED, and that is the point of filing this. Phase 2 saw its own p90 jump from 4.5 to 56.5 and wrote that it was AN ARTEFACT OF THE COUNT — four outliers in forty putting one exactly at the 90th-percentile index where two in thirty-eight did not. At n = 164 that no longer holds: a quarter of the population above the bar is a distribution, not an index. The full quantile ladder is p50 = 3, p75 = 19.5, p80 = 54.5, p85 = 59.5, p90 = 61, p95 = 64, max 135.5.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, so it is not over-read. The MEDIAN is 0 in every one of the four runs and the ABSOLUTE MEDIAN holds at 3 B/boundary against the published 1.5. The instrument still cancels in the centre. What has changed is the TAIL, and the tail is what the published bar was derived from.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every allocation window's licence to read its mid-rung figures is the null arm reading flat. The mid-rung figures are thousands of bytes per boundary and are unaffected. What IS affected is any statistic of the same order as the tail — and rf2-fk6pj's phase-3 window is exactly that case: its pre-registered band, built at ten times its own null-arm p90, came out at 610 B/boundary and refused a term whose implied delta was 37.8.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED.
* NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED and none is excluded. The 12-round runs, the seeded pass order, the session length and the box are all confounded with the corpus date.
* IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THE PUBLISHED BAR IS WRONG. The bar refuses nothing the ladder publishes and nothing here moves it. What is established is that the DISTRIBUTION it was derived from is not the distribution the instrument produces now.

THE CONTRADICTION IS IN THE LANDED RECORD ITSELF. `the-window-total-is-the-ceiling.md` says the 884,280 B figure is the highest certified observation, that 168,036 B above it is unsampled, and that this “ceiling is bounded from below by an observation and from above by nothing.” That is the correct evidential status: the largest observed success is a LOWER bound on any real maximum certifiable total, not an upper bound.

Zero certified windows above an observed maximum in this finite B=4 corpus cannot exclude a future certifying window above it, especially when the record says the entire 884,280–1,028,670 B interval is unsampled and `t` is a one-point linear fit. The 36 refusals below the figure prove only that it is not sufficient; they do not turn it into a necessary cap.

That conditional projection may be useful, but it cannot reverse the old impossibility claim as a live necessary result.

CHEAPEST CORRECT DISCHARGE: restate B <= 3 everywhere (page, reader output/comments/self-test, README/close record as applicable) as a model-conditioned projection, not a necessary condition. Preserve the empirical B=4 rung result. If a real page-size necessity is wanted, it needs evidence at another B; the page already says that window is unmeasured. title: ci: a stale SETUP_PATTERNS entry fails check_fast_pr_gap.py OPEN with exit 0 — nothing in CI catches it
description:
MEASURED BY PLANTING under rf2-mul6w (PR #8539). Every premise is reproducible.

WHAT WAS PLANTED. In a worktree carrying the 14 prefixed Playwright call sites (`timeout -k 10 720 npx playwright install ...`), the SETUP_PATTERNS entry was reverted to its pre-fix form `^npx playwright install\b` — i.e. exactly the drift this bead is about: a setup pattern that no longer matches the call sites it covers.

WHAT HAPPENED. `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` (the default --check mode) EXITED 0 and printed 'fast-PR gap map clean'. The only visible effect was the headline count moving from 'REQUIRED CHECKS THIS SPINE DOES NOT RUN (96)' to (106), with 10 toolchain-setup steps silently reclassified as unrun GATES — each listed with its own reproduce command telling a reader to run `npx playwright install` locally.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG DIRECTION. The file's own docstring states the safe direction — 'a new CI job or a new step inside an existing one is reported as UNRUN until somebody teaches this file otherwise' — and that is true for the LANES. It is not true for SETUP_PATTERNS, where the same drift inflates the gap map with false entries and no exit code changes. The header of .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh calls this 'a fail-open in the very map the merge criterion consults', which is precisely right, and nothing detects it.

THE DRIFT RATCHET DOES NOT COVER THIS. `--check`'s ratchet fires when a SPINE_LANES signature stops matching any required gate step. A SETUP_PATTERNS entry that stops matching has no equivalent: it produces MORE unrun entries, which reads as normal.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not prescriptive). A floor per setup pattern — 'this entry must match at least one required step' — would catch it the same way MIN_REQUIRED_JOBS and MIN_SPINE_CHECKERS catch an empty parse, and in the same spirit. title: ci: the 300s Playwright step cap is now 1.8x its worst observed success, not 6.1x — a judgement for Mike
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-mul6w (PR #8539), which was fenced OUT of changing any cap. Filing rather than acting.

MEASURED 2026-08-20 over the 140 most recent completed test.yml runs (window 2026-08-18T05:11Z .. 2026-08-20T10:13Z, ALL attempts, every step named 'Install Playwright*'): 377 non-skipped samples, 370 successes.

THE POPULATION THE CAP NOTE DESCRIBES IS GONE. rf2-g3lv's note above the cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation install step recorded 'p50 13s, p90 21s, max 49s. The 300s cap is 6.1x the observed worst case.' Re-derived: p50 14s and p90 34s still, but p95 113s, p99 424s, MAX 621s. FOUR of the 370 successes finished ABOVE 300s (424s, 556s, 589s, 621s).

Across the three step-capped sites (cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation, tenant-switcher-testbed-smoke, mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair) the worst success is 164s over 80 samples, so the 300s cap is 1.8x its own site's worst case. WHY IT MIGHT BE ONE. Two of the five install stalls measured on 2026-08-19 were at step-capped sites and died at 312s and 313s (jobs 95959283361, 95932283494) — i.e. AT the cap. Given four uncapped-site successes ran past 300s in the same window, those two are consistent with installs that would have completed given more time, which would make them cap-induced reds rather than genuine outages. Not established either way; distinguishing them needs the raw apt/download timings from those two logs.

Raising it re-widens exactly that window. So this is a trade between two real costs, not a bug with a fix. rf2-mul6w corrected the stale numbers in the comment and left the cap untouched.

PR #8539 already: re-derived the rate, corrected both stale claims in test.yml's comment block, and closed the no-annotation gap at the 14 job-capped sites.

title: hicasso: the floor arm's mode RATE is not a property of the revision — 0%, 10% and 53% at 4a1537cb71
description:
MEASURED by rf2-c4hhk's seventy-run window (PR #8531), record docs/design/hicasso/studio/does-arming-the-census-move-the-high-level.md, 70 datasets under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-c4hhk/. Filed rather than chased: rf2-c4hhk was sent to answer the armed/unarmed confound and did, and this is a second finding from the same data.

THE OBSERVATION. Three windows at the SAME revision (4a1537cb71), on the SAME instrument (no bench file has changed since 408dfb0aa8), with the SAME plan (floor, write-all, ROOTS=4, CELLS=6, ROUNDS=18) and the SAME estimator, produce three incompatible rates for the elevated mode:

  rf2-n1b9h    6 runs    0 high     0%
  rf2-77gz8   20 runs    2 high    10%
  rf2-c4hhk   69 runs   37 high    53%

WHY IT IS NOT AN ARMING EFFECT, which is the first thing to exclude and the one thing this data can exclude cleanly. rf2-c4hhk alternated armed and unarmed runs strictly, and BOTH ARMS MOVED TOGETHER: 52.9% armed (18 of 34) against 54.3% unarmed (19 of 35). An arming effect would have separated them; an environment effect moves both, and did. rf2-n1b9h's 0% was all-armed and rf2-77gz8's 10% was all-armed, so neither of those is an arming contrast either.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every measurement window on this arm SIZES ITS RUN COUNT against a prior rate, and a pre-declared count is the one thing in these windows that cannot be revised after the fact. rf2-77gz8 sized twenty runs against a re-derived 1-in-7 and got 2 of 20; rf2-c4hhk sized seventy against a re-derived 8.7% on the binding arm and got 53%, i.e. it took roughly four times the runs it needed. The error runs in the expensive direction here, but a window sized against 53% when the box happens to be in the 0% state would produce a null and report a refusal, and the refusal would be an artefact of the sizing rather than a fact about the arm. So this is a live risk to the METHOD, not only an oddity.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is most of it. Nothing here identifies what the rate depends on. The three windows differ in wall-clock date, in what else the box was doing, and in nothing that any dataset records. Candidates worth separating, none of them supported yet: machine load or thermal state at the time of the window; a resident-runtime difference (the Chromium binary is pinned by playwright but the datasets do not record its build); and a within-window ordering effect, since rf2-c4hhk's runs were back-to-back for ninety minutes where earlier corpora were not.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, or at least bound it. The cheap first move is to record what the datasets currently do not: the Chromium build string, the box's load at window open, and the elapsed time since the previous run, all of which ride free on an existing field the way rf2-n1b9h's census does. That converts the next window into evidence about the rate at no extra runner cost. A DELIBERATE variation — the same plan run cold, run hot, and run after an idle gap — is the confirming second move and should not be taken first.

NOTE this bead is about the RATE only. The LEVELS are settled: rf2-c4hhk established that arming moves neither, and the level values themselves reproduce to the byte across all three windows.

STATED AT ITS TRUE STRENGTH. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE 2026-08-21 03:21 TRIAGE.

(1) THE QUARTILE p IS BOUNDARY-SENSITIVE, and the boundary is a choice rather than a measurement. P(at most 5 high among the first k of 69 | 37 high) reads 0.0210 at k=17, 0.0109 at k=18, 0.0054 at k=19 and 0.0025 at k=20 -- an EIGHTFOLD move across a two-run choice -- and a first-half/second-half split gives 0.093. The triage's p = 0.0054 reproduces exactly at k=19 and should not be the figure a record leads with. The page therefore leads with a test that has NO cut point: Mann-Whitney on each run's position in its session, high against low, U = 763 against a null mean of 592, z = 2.058, ONE-TAIL p = 0.0198. The gradient is real at about p = 0.02, not p = 0.005. The reader's fixtures REQUIRE the sweep to move at least fourfold across the cut and require the boundary-free test to come out weaker than the best cut, so a change that made the quartile figure look robust reds them.

(2) THE BISECT'S HIGH RUN IS THE SECOND OF EIGHT, NOT THE THIRD. The triage's own ordered list shows pilot-rounds6 at +0.0 and bisect-1-a at +3.6; its prose beside that list said third. The direction of the bound is unaffected -- second is if anything earlier.

CONDITIONAL CONSISTENCY, stated as that and not as a test. Against the long session's own early rate (5 of 19 = 26.3%) the two short sessions are unremarkable: P(0 of 6) = 0.160 and P(<=2 of 20) = 0.072. Against its POOLED 53.6% they are 0.0099 and 5.89e-05. All four reproduce the triage exactly. The reference rate is taken from the same data the gradient was found in, so the second row is not an independent confirmation of the first; what it establishes is that ONE within-session gradient plus ordinary sampling accounts for all three observations, where three properties of three revisions is not needed.

THE HONEST BOUND, AND IT SURVIVED INTO THE RECORD IN THREE PLACES -- the page's summary, its body at length, and four reader fixtures that pin it as literals, because it is the half a write-up is most likely to lose. alloc-9jrhi's single high run sits at +3.6 min, SECOND of eight, in a 14.9-minute session. Under the within-c4hhk gradient (27.8% in the first quarter against 52.9-68.8% after) an early run is where a high is LEAST likely. So ELAPSED TIME DOES NOT EXPLAIN THIS RUN, and this bead does NOT discharge rf2-9jrhi's revision-dependence question. It would have, had the high run landed late; it landed early, so the RATE and the mode's REVISION-DEPENDENCE stay separate questions. Nothing here is to be cited as bearing on rf2-9jrhi.

One nuance worth keeping: the bisect's RATE (12.5% at 14.9 min) fits the duration ordering perfectly well. It is its INTERNAL ORDERING that does not fit the within-session gradient. Two different claims about the same eight runs, kept apart on the page.

NOT CONCLUDED: no mechanism (thermal, V8 tier accumulation, heap fragmentation all survive equally); across the three sessions duration is confounded with date and clock time; the whole gradient rests on ONE session; and the LEVELS were not reopened.

THE SECOND MOVE IS CARRIED OUT RATHER THAN DROPPED: filed as rf2-24o2z (record the Chromium build string, the box's load at window open and the inter-run gap). It is hermetic, needs no window, and is a p0_run.cjs change one-toucher with rf2-fk6pj / rf2-csca8 / rf2-onozm -- the mayor's to bundle.

title: [hic] TRIAGE ONLY: classify the 64 hicasso product files by KIND — the number rf2-ps7ia turns on
description:
REQUESTED BY MIKE, 2026-08-19 10:13 AUSEST. This is a MEASUREMENT bead. It moves nothing, edits nothing, and rules nothing. Its whole deliverable is a classification and a set of counts.

WHY IT EXISTS. rf2-ps7ia must decide where the hicasso normative set lives, and that decision reads very differently depending on how much of the set is actually normative. Nobody has counted. The mayor twice said 'roughly forty files' in chat; the measured figure is SIXTY-FOUR files and 17,044 lines under docs/design/hicasso/product/, with thirteen of those in the lanes/ subtree, against 131 files across the whole docs/design/hicasso/ tree. So the estimate was low by half, which is itself the argument for counting before deciding.

THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS: is the hicasso spec tree a four-file job or a thirty-file programme? If it is small, rf2-ps7ia is easy and can be executed in one pass. If it is large, it is a sequenced programme and needs to be planned as one.

=== WHAT TO DO ===

Classify EVERY file under docs/design/hicasso/product/ into exactly one of four kinds. Report the counts, and the per-file assignment as a table.

1. VIEW SPECIFICATION — normative statements about how a view is AUTHORED in hicasso. The thing a consumer must obey to write hicasso views correctly. This is the kind with no current home, which is what makes the count matter.
2. SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — normative statements about what a SUBSTRATE must provide. These already have a home in spec/ proper: 004B carries the structural render-tree ABI, 004C root identity and the mount grammar, 006 the substrate contract. If a file is this kind, name which of those it belongs beside.
3. READER-FACING ANSWER — content a hicasso user needs, which belongs stated on a guide page under docs/core/hicasso/ rather than in a design record. Precedent: rf2-75q3l, where three published pages routed readers into an excluded tree and the fix was to make the pages answer their own questions rather than relocate anything.
4. WORKING RECORD — provenance, measurement windows, budgets, decision history. These stay exactly where they are; docs/design is the right tree for them and their provenance pins are gated there.

A file may be MIXED. Say so explicitly rather than forcing it, and give the rough proportion — a 90% working record with one normative paragraph is a very different problem from a half-and-half file, and the mixed count is one of the numbers the decision turns on.

=== ESTABLISHED CONTEXT — verify each at source, do not inherit ===

MIKE'S DIRECTION, 2026-08-19: an artefact-local implementation/hicasso/spec/ folder IS the likely destination for kind 1, CONDITIONAL on spec/ not carrying view specification. THE CONDITION HOLDS: spec/README.md:66 states in terms 'There is no 004 view contract.' spec/004-Views.md and the S3/S4/S5 view-conformance profiles were deleted under rf2-h89ri (PR #8500), and the hole was DECLARED rather than papered over. What survives — 004B, 004C, 006 — is substrate-facing, not view-authoring.

THE PRECEDENT for an artefact-local spec tree is tools/: seven of them carry one (xray, story, template, machines-viz, mcp-base, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp). There is currently NO spec/ or design/ directory anywhere under implementation/ — this would be the first.

=== TWO RIDERS TO REPORT ON, NOT TO FIX ===

A. THE GATE GAP. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py has DEFAULT_ROOTS of docs, spec, skills, migration, plus an explicit special case for tools/<tool>/spec/**. implementation/** is in NEITHER, and check_readme_links.py reaches only READMEs beside source. So a normative tree at implementation/hicasso/spec/ would be UNGATED from day one — no link or anchor validation. Confirm that at source and say what the smallest correct fix looks like. DO NOT BUILD IT.

B. A POSSIBLE RULING COLLISION. rf2-h89ri deliberately wrote NO 'see hicasso' pointer into spec when it declared the hole, citing rf2-0yp7w.11. A reader hitting 'there is no 004 view contract' should eventually be told where the view spec lives. Read rf2-0yp7w.11 and say whether it forbids that pointer, or whether it only forbade re-aiming RETIRED freehand/ui material at hicasso. Those are different, and the mayor has not verified which.

=== SCOPE FENCE ===

NO MOVES. NO EDITS to any classified file. NO new spec tree. NO gate change. The deliverable is a report and, if it is useful, ONE new working document recording the classification.

Out of scope: the whole of docs/design/hicasso/ outside product/ (the other 67 files) unless your reading shows product/ cannot be classified without them — in which case say so and stop rather than widening.

DO NOT rule rf2-ps7ia. That decision is Mike's and this bead exists to inform it.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

1. Every one of the 64 files assigned a kind, or explicitly marked mixed with a proportion.
2. Counts per kind, and a line count per kind — a four-file kind carrying 6,000 lines is not small.
3. For kind 2, the spec/ document each file belongs beside.
4. The two riders reported with source citations.
5. A one-paragraph answer to the question that prompted this: is the view-specification set a small job or a programme?
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8522 (2026-08-20): reopen exact owner. The delivered census is internally inconsistent about the number of view-specification carriers. Its own per-file classification attributes VS content to 12 files (lanes/adversarial-risks, design-laws, ergonomics-api, hot-path-architecture, react-compatibility-notes, testing-xray, use-cases; plus specification, invariants, facade-freeze, dispositions, complaints), while the headline and conclusion say seven documents. The section titled 'What the seven view-specification carriers actually hold' contains eight rows summing about 1,001 VS lines and silently omits four classified carriers totaling about 135 more lines (adversarial-risks ~15, hot-path ~21, use-cases ~7, complaints ~92), which is how the headline total reaches ~1,136. Acceptance: distinguish the seven files whose PRIMARY kind is VS from all 12 files carrying attributed VS; reconcile the headline, carrier table, small-job conclusion, and owner summary; include or explicitly justify excluded carriers; recompute totals if any classification changes.
close_reason: RECONCILED. PR #8551 (draft->ready) closes the AUDIT-REOPEN #8522 finding. No classification changed; the page now states both file counts (7 primary VS, 12 carrying any VS), lists all twelve carriers so the table reconciles with the headline, and re-derives every count at commit 5858e9317a. Counts and both riders are recorded in full on the bead comment above so rf2-ps7ia can read them without opening the file. Answer unchanged and strengthened: a SMALL JOB (~1,138 normative lines, under 7%, three or four authored documents in one pass), NOT a thirty-file programme — but plan the reading against twelve carriers, not seven, and expect a rewrite in voice rather than a move.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RECONCILED, 2026-08-20. PR #8551 (draft) closes the AUDIT-REOPEN #8522 finding. The audit reproduces exactly: the delivered census attributed VS content to 12 files but titled its carrier section 'the seven', listed 8 rows in it (one of them dispositions.md, not a primary carrier), and omitted 4 carriers worth ~135 lines — so the table summed ~1,001 against a headline of ~1,136.

NO CLASSIFICATION CHANGED. Every file holds the kind and proportion first assigned. The fix is presentational + arithmetic: the headline table gains a 'Files (any share)' column beside 'Files (primary)', the carrier section lists all twelve and marks the seven primary, and the conclusion/bullets/closing note are reconciled to the same pair.

=== COUNTS, RE-DERIVED AT COMMIT 5858e9317a (not inherited) ===
Population:  64 files / 17,054 lines under docs/design/hicasso/product/
             13 files / 947 lines in lanes/; 5 files / 707 lines in pilots/;
             46 files / 15,400 lines at top level
Wider tree:  135 files across docs/design/hicasso/ (bead recorded 131)
DRIFT since the bead: lines 17,044 -> 17,054. All +10 inside two SINGLE-KIND
WORKING RECORDS (correction-ledger.md 131->133, release-scans.md 328->336).
No carrier of any normative kind changed length, so kinds 1/2/3 are unmoved
and only the kind-4 residual absorbed it. File count and classification stable.

=== PER-KIND ===
Kind                     Files(primary)  Files(any share)  Lines(attributed)  Share
1 View specification            7              12               ~1,138         6.7%
2 Substrate contract            0               3                  ~97         0.6%
3 Reader-facing answer          4               6                 ~608         3.6%
4 Working record               53              64              ~15,211        89.2%
TOTAL                          64               -              17,054          100%

THE TWO FILE COUNTS ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, and conflating them is what
the audit caught. 'Primary' sums to 64 and says how many documents are CHIEFLY
a kind. 'Any share' double-counts mixed files and says how many a graduation

The bead asked which of two things was wrong. Answer: NOTHING outside the port's own tests
consumes `re-frame.substrate.observation` in shipped source. Fork (a) — "hicasso reaches it
indirectly through re-frame.subs / re-frame.interop" — is FALSIFIED, and by a specific
counter-route rather than by an absent grep hit.

EVIDENCE

1. No src namespace anywhere requires the port. Every `:require` in the tree is a test ns
   (2 reagent-adapter tests, core bench/read_attribution.clj,
   observation_drain_elision_prod_test.cljs, observation_port_cljs_test.cljc). Every mention

2. The dependency runs the OTHER WAY, so no indirect route through subs can exist.
   implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2232 marks compute-sub-with-memo as an
   "observation-port internal entry point ... Two `^:no-doc` seams
   `re-frame.substrate.observation` consumes". The port consumes subs; subs does not consume
   the port.

3. Hicasso reaches AROUND the port, not through it. collector.cljs:1180 calls
   subs/compute-sub-with-memo directly — the same fn the port itself calls at
   observation.cljc:1691. So hicasso is a PEER consumer of the same core seam, not a consumer
   of the port. Its port mention at collector.cljs:234 is a lineage claim about following the
   port's cold-probe discipline, not a call.

4. Why the consumer went. `git log -S "[re-frame.substrate.observation"` over */src/ shows the
   real requirers were implementation/ui and implementation/freehand, deleted by the retirement
   commits ef3131f4a2 (ui) and c951808b47 (freehand). Hicasso never had the require, so this is
   not a regression in hicasso — it is the seam losing its only instances to rf2-0yp7w.

5. Consequence. port-abi-version / assert-port-abi-version! appear ONLY in the port itself and
   in core's own tests. The ABI boot guard that Conventions, Spec 006 and Spec 009 all describe
   a consumer asserting at load has no consumer side in any shipped build and cannot fire there.

   consumer.

WHAT LANDED (narrowest correction true under either disposition, per the fence)

spec/Conventions.md and spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md only. The consumer clauses become the
terms the category imposes on A consumer rather than assertions about a live edge, and both
pages carry an explicit rf2-63t1i-referenced flag that no shipped namespace requires the port
today. No implementation code touched, nothing deleted, no semantics changed. The port's
specified behaviour remains fully normative.

OPEN — NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION (deliberately not resolved here)

  (1) Give the port its consumer: have hicasso's collector read through the port instead of

MAYOR RULING, 2026-08-18 23:42 AUSEST — CONDITIONAL, WITH A SOURCE-CHECKABLE DISCRIMINATOR. Taken on Mike's standing delegation. The prose half landed in PR #8490; what remained was the disposition, and this settles it.

THE STATE OF PLAY, re-derived at origin/main 4852631958. re-frame.substrate.observation is live shipped core code whose only real requires are TEST namespaces — two reagent adapter tests, bench/read_attribution.clj, observation_drain_elision_prod_test.cljs and observation_port_cljs_test.cljc. Its original consumer went with re-frame.ui. Hicasso's collector.cljs was believed to consume it and does not; it reaches reactivity through re-frame.subs and re-frame.interop. So the port ships with no non-test consumer, and it carries a port-abi-version guard and a DEV-ONLY G-13 witness whose value depends on there being a real one.

RULING: RETIRE THE PORT — UNLESS spec/006 MANDATES IT AS A CONTRACT SURFACE. Establish that first; it decides the whole bead and it is a read, not a judgement.

WHY THE CONDITION IS NOT A FUDGE. The two answers are different KINDS of thing, and only a source read separates them. If spec/006 names the observation port as a seam a substrate MUST provide, the port is a contract with a currently-empty consumer set, and retiring it is a spec change requiring its own ruling — it is not dead code, it is an unexercised obligation. If spec/006 does not, it is an implementation detail whose consumer was deleted, and it is dead code wearing a guard.

WHY RETIRE IS THE DEFAULT AND NOT KEEP-PARKED. The stance is explicit: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, reject over-engineering. Parking is the 'preserve everything just in case' default, and a stance exists precisely to refuse it. The five test namespaces are not independent value — they test the port itself, so they cannot vote for its survival. And the port-abi-version guard and G-13 witness are the sharper argument FOR retirement rather than against it: a guard whose value depends on a consumer that does not exist is a hollow control, and this project's own rule is that a hollow control is REPLACED, not patched, because the next reader trusts it harder for having a history of being fixed. Keeping it parked keeps two controls that assert nothing while looking like coverage.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING: give-it-a-consumer is OUT, and it needs no investigation. Writing a consumer to justify shipped code is making work to preserve a decision nobody has defended, which is the clearest case of the gold-plating the stance rejects.

SCOPE FOR THIS PASS — DO NOT RETIRE THE PORT IN THIS PR. Establish the discriminator at source, record the answer on this bead with the evidence, and STOP. If spec/006 does not mandate it, the retirement is its own dispatch with its own fence: it deletes shipped core code, five test namespaces and two controls, and it deserves a worker whose whole context is that. If spec/006 DOES mandate it, say so and the bead becomes an operator ruling on the spec, which I will surface to Mike.

OUT-OF-FENCE RESIDUE ALREADY TRACKED, so it is not swept here: rf2-2n92u carries spec/Ownership.md:31 and spec/009:1985, which still name hicasso as the consumer.

This note is a CLAIM. Re-derive every require, line number and the spec/006 text at origin/main HEAD before acting.

ANSWER TO THE 2026-08-18 23:42 RULING'S DISCRIMINATOR. Re-derived at origin/main 57e45e3d29. INVESTIGATION ONLY -- no code, no tests, no spec/006 text touched, and the port is not retired here.

EVIDENCE, QUOTED.

1. spec/006:103-111, a blockquote inside the section that DEFINES the adapter contract:
   "**The internal observation port is not part of this contract.** A re-frame-native view substrate reads subscriptions through an adapter-internal observation port ... that lives **outside** this closed ten-fn map: no entry is added to the adapter spec map, no signature here changes, and existing adapters implement nothing new."
   The same blockquote already carries "though no shipped namespace requires the port today (see the scope section below)".

2. spec/006:1192-1193, the port section's own status block:
   "This port is INTERNAL -- it is NOT part of the public adapter API contract; see the scope statement below."

3. spec/006:1204, the scope heading, and 1206-1214 under it:
   "### Scope -- outside the closed public adapter contract, one named consumer"
   "The port is **adapter-internal**: a private surface between the core's sub-cache and a re-frame-native substrate's view runtime ... It is **not** an entry in the adapter spec map. The public adapter API contract remains exactly as [The adapter API contract] states it -- six required functions, three optional functions, one lifecycle function, plus the `:kind` discriminator (the 11-key adapter spec map) -- **closed for v1**. Existing adapters (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, plain-atom, SSR) implement none of the port's operations and are unchanged by this section. No feature predicate is added; a consumer cannot branch on the port's presence because the port is not consumable."

THE SENTENCE THAT SETTLES IT is "Existing adapters ... implement none of the port's operations". A seam a substrate MUST provide is one substrates implement. This one is implemented by CORE and consumed, in principle, by a view runtime -- the arrow points the other way. A substrate obligation it is not, and the spec closes the door twice more: the port is not in the spec map, and no feature predicate lets anything branch on it.

- "MUST provide" and "MUST implement" occur ZERO times in spec/006. Positive control on the same file: "MUST" 37 lines, "MUST NOT" 17 lines, so the search discriminates.

The port's SEMANTICS are normative: 006:1188 marks the section "Status: normative", and 006:1234-1243 -- a paragraph that already cites this bead -- ends "everything specified below states the semantics a consumer would meet, and remains normative for one." Normative-semantics-for-a-surface-that-exists is a different claim from a-seam-a-substrate-MUST-provide, and only the second would make retirement a spec change needing its own ruling. It is the second that is absent. But the retirement dispatch's fence must still include spec/006: it would remove a normative section running 1186-1980, the forward blockquote at 103-111, and the override cross-reference at 2502-2512. It is a code-plus-spec retirement, not a code-only one.

PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Every real :require of the port tree-wide is a test namespace -- exactly the five this bead names:
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_activates_ratom_node_cljs_test.cljs:59
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_watchable_host_cljs_test.cljs:75
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj:176
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_drain_elision_prod_test.cljs:29
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:84
Zero requires under any src/ tree. Every other mention of the port under a src/ tree is a docstring or comment.

The two controls are hollow exactly as the ruling describes. port-abi-version / assert-port-abi-version! occur ONLY in observation.cljc (11, 535-580) and in core's own tests -- no consumer side in any shipped build, so the load-time skew assert of rule 2 cannot fire there. And hicasso still reaches AROUND the port, not through it: collector.cljs calls subs/compute-sub-with-memo at :1109 and :1180 -- the same fn the port itself calls at observation.cljc:1691. Peer consumer of the core seam, not a consumer of this one. Its only mentions of the port (collector.cljs:234) are docstring lineage claims.

CONSEQUENCE UNDER THE RULING, NOT ACTED ON HERE. The condition fails, so the ruling's default stands: RETIRE. BLOCKER A — THE SIX FROZEN INVARIANTS. RULING: DO NOT RENUMBER, DO NOT EXTRACT. I verified 'invariant 6' appears four times in spec/006 alone, and the worker measured three of those inside the section I just rescued, as prose rather than links. Renumbering is therefore CATASTROPHIC AND INVISIBLE — it silently repoints every 'invariant N' citation in the corpus at the wrong invariant, and check_doc_slugs.py cannot see a prose ordinal any more than it can see a docstring citation.

THIS IS THE THIRD APPEARANCE OF ONE CLASS TONIGHT. spec/004-Views.md was cited by NUMBER as well as by filename — 102 hits across 55 files that three separate sweeps missed. The description says implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ and the 2026-08-18 06:35 comment says implementation/hicasso/examples/. The DESCRIPTION is right: implementation/hicasso/examples/ does not exist, and the eight witness applications (slice, editor, grid, ledger, forms, navigation, todo, typeahead) live under the test tree.

THE BLOCK WAS NEVER ONLY THE ESTIMATOR, AND THE SECOND HALF IS STRUCTURAL. lane/rounds! calls measure-one! and takes a NUMBER back, so an arm it can schedule is one whose whole window closes inside a synchronous call — and a window that ends at a PAINT cannot, because the browser produces the frame after the task returns and the only handle on it is a callback. Every arm this lane could schedule was therefore one bracketed by react-dom/flushSync. That is why both landed drivers measure a commit: it is the shape the only shared schedule allowed, not a coincidence of what got written. So the driver needed a schedule as well as an aim.

WHAT LANDED

1. lane/rounds-async! — rounds!'s schedule with the return type widened to a promise. Both loops now walk one private visit-plan, so the reflecting order, the warm-up boundary and observe!'s predecessor tagging cannot become two copies; lane_schedule_async_cljs_test runs one deterministic stub through both and asserts the samples, readings and true execution order are = at arm counts 2/4/5/7/8, that the visits stay serial, and that a plain value is accepted. lane_schedule_cljs_test is the regression net over the refactor and is green.

2. slice_echo_clock_app — the driver. It mounts the slice through h/mount! with the application's own :initial-events, differing only in which route it opens on, and its window runs from a real DOM event through requestAnimationFrame then setTimeout 0 — the first task after that frame's rendering lifecycle. The echo is read out of the DOM INSIDE the rAF callback, before style, layout and paint, and banks into lane/tally with assert-verified! refusing at N unverified of M. Every reading is published decomposed (:commit, :to-raf, :raf-to-paint). Four rows: :idle-frame (the floor), :keystroke (U1), :toggle (U2, the click/change path), :ctl-blocked (the control). U3 and U4 are named at source as NOT served, with what each would need.

3. NO HOT-ZONE EDIT, confirmed by building it that way: HICASSO_INIT_FN plus the existing :hicasso-bench id. shadow-cljs.edn untouched.

THE CONTROL IS INVISIBLE TO THE WINDOW IT REPLACES, which is what makes it the right one here rather than a generic sensitivity check. :ctl-blocked spends its injected 50 ms strictly BETWEEN the commit and the frame, on window!'s after-commit! seam, so a rig that had quietly reverted to a commit-bounded window would report a control that predicted 50 ms and measured nothing.

THE RISK THIS BEAD FLAGGED DOES NOT HOLD. The slice app compiles under :advanced through this driver — release build, zero warnings — and runs there. Budgeted for; it cost nothing.

THE FINDING THE RIG PRODUCED, AND THE REPAIR. The instrument's first run REFUSED, and not for load. A paint-bounded window is PREDECESSOR-DEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: its length is dominated by the wait for the browser's next rendering opportunity, those sit on a grid, and how long a sample waits depends on where in that grid the PREVIOUS sample left the clock. The arm-order guard measured exactly that — :idle-frame read a full rendering interval after :keystroke, which ends just after a paint, and zero after :ctl-blocked, which spans three intervals and ends with a frame already overdue, ranges disjoint; :toggle carried the same contrast. VERDICT: REFUSE.

THE GUARD'S TOLERANCE WAS NOT MOVED. The repair is in the ARM, one line in measure-one!: settle to a fresh frame OUTSIDE the reading so the clock always starts in the first task after a paint, making the grid phase a constant of the instrument rather than a property of whatever ran before it. With it the guard returns REPORTABLE on every arm by predecessor AND by phase, on a loud box.

TWO CONSEQUENCES STATED AT SOURCE rather than left to be found by the reading window: (a) a real interaction arrives at a uniformly random phase in the grid while this one always arrives at the phase with the LONGEST wait, so a reading here is the conservative end of the phase distribution — the end that cannot flatter the application, and the deliberately-randomised-phase alternative is named with its trigger and NOT built; (b) the injected block does not ADD to the wait the unblocked arm pays, it SUBSUMES it, so the control's difference reaches blocked-ms rounded to the grid rather than exactly, which is what control-slack's band is derived from.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT THIS BEAD'S. The READING. The instrument has never been read against a line and must not be: U1's one-60-Hz-frame clause, U2's 50 ms p95 / 100 ms p99 and U3's 100 ms appear nowhere in the code, and the only pass/fail the driver makes are the arm-order guard and the positive control, both instrument-integrity checks. rf2-85og2's gate 1 now needs a quiet-box window and nothing else structural. Three things that window should know before it starts:

- THE SCHEDULE KNOBS ARE DELIBERATELY SMALL. {:warmup 8 :samples 12} over 5 rounds is the lane's standard, and a p99 over 12 samples is mostly interpolation — lane/quantile's own docstring prices that. Raise both; the run's wall clock is roughly two frames per sample plus 50 ms per :ctl-blocked sample.
- U3 AND U4 STILL HAVE NO ROWS. U3 (operation latency for a broad operation — a route change, a reset, a save reply) needs per-arm preparation outside the window, because the route the editor rows type into is the route a navigation row would leave. U4 (per-frame latency under dragging or animation) is not one interaction through to one paint at all: it is a run of consecutive frames, and its estimator is a distribution over frame intervals rather than over window lengths. Both want another driver on window!'s mechanism. Neither is built and neither should be guessed at.
- THE FLOOR ROW IS THE ONE TO READ FIRST. :idle-frame is the wait for the next rendering opportunity with no application work at all, and a p95 at the floor and a p95 at twice it are different findings that the figure alone does not distinguish.

2. bank-aux! appends commit/to-rAF/rAF-to-paint values for warm-up and measured visits alike, while lane/rounds-async! returns readings/summary only for measured visits. The published :structure distributions therefore have a different population and n from the :summary they are documented to decompose (100 versus 60 values per arm with the current schedule). comments.text:
AUDIT GAPS 1 AND 2 CLOSED, PR #8589. NO READING TAKEN, no threshold, band, budget status or published figure moved, and budgets.md untouched — the refusal posture the audit asked to preserve is preserved. Three files, all in the bench tree: lane.cljs, slice_echo_clock_app.cljs, slice_echo_window_dom_cljs_test.cljs.

GAP 1 — THE REPAIR IS A DIFFERENT PLACE, NOT A DIFFERENT VALUE, and that is forced rather than chosen. per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test solves the accepted-verbatim problem by typing into a field whose model answers something ELSE (the editor's normalising :slug). THE SLICE HAS NO SUCH FIELD: ::events/edit takes what it is given, verbatim, and nothing on the article route normalises or refuses. Checked at source before designing around it.

So: React keeps a controlled input's committed value in TWO places, and only one of them is reachable by a scripted setup. The `value` PROPERTY is written by HTMLInputElement.prototype's setter and by a checkbox's native activation; the `value` CONTENT ATTRIBUTE (defaultValue) is written ONLY by React's own commit. Verified at source in react-dom 19.2.0 — updateInput ends every controlled-input update with setDefaultValue(element, type, value), unconditionally whenever a `value` prop is present — and the repo's own measured mutation trace in per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test carries the matching INPUT@value record. Every measured arm now blanks that mirror OUTSIDE the window and asks inside the frame whether the APPLICATION put the model's own title back.

THE CHECKBOX ARM READS THE SAME MIRROR, and that is the point of it rather than a convenience: ::toggle-published moves the draft, the editor's body re-runs, and React reconciles the title input beside the checkbox, so a restored title mirror is evidence the click reached the model and came back through a commit. defaultChecked would NOT have served, checked rather than assumed — the same updateInput writes it only for an element with no `checked` prop, and this one has.

THE SABOTAGE IS BUILT INTO THE DRIVER, not only into the suite. echo-discrimination! runs once at boot, performs the keystroke arm's setup mutation alone — no DOM event, so no handler, no dispatch, no state write, no commit — through the same window! and the same observation the arms use, and REFUSES to let anything be measured unless the check rejects it. A suite row is the right place to prove a repair; it is the wrong place to keep a driver honest, because the driver is what a quiet-box window runs and the suite is not.

title: hicasso: the allocation window's SECOND leg pass reads lower than its first — a within-round position term of 0.2–0.7%
description:
MEASURED by rf2-0gjqi's paired window, 2026-08-18. Record:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md (PR #8473).
Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/.

THE OBSERVATION. Under P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired the two write legs of every arm run
as two passes inside one round, and the rig alternates which leads on round
parity (p0_run.cjs:2418). Taking the round as the block and the median of
(page-all)/all over that round's certified mid-rung (R3, R7) cells as its
statistic, THE PASS THAT RAN SECOND READS LOWER IN 10 OF 12 BLOCKS -- 6 of 6 in
run 1, 4 of 6 in run 2 -- WHICHEVER WRITE OCCUPIED IT. Median second-minus-first
-0.59%.

Decomposed under an additive position model, the pass-order half-difference reads
+0.68% (run 1) and +0.21% (run 2), the same sign on both, while the order-free
write half-sum reads -0.33% and +0.24%, opposite signs.

WHY IT MATTERS. It is the class of term that manufactured this instrument's last
inferential finding. rf2-0gjqi's published 8-of-8 was taken with `all` as run 2
and `page` as run 3, so page was ALWAYS the later measurement; a position term of
this sign produces 8 of 8 in one direction with certainty. The paired mode
removes the confound and the unanimity goes with it -- but the term itself is
still in the instrument, and any future estimator that is not order-balanced will
pick it up again.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, so it is not rediscovered as new.

  - THE MAGNITUDE IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THE OLD EFFECT. This is a WITHIN-ROUND
    pass-position term; the old confound was between two PROCESSES. They are not
    the same quantity, and +0.21..0.68% is smaller than the published mid-rung
    absolute median of 1.68%. Right sign, wrong size, different estimand.
  - NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED and none is excluded.
  - LEG ORDER IS NOT SEPARATED FROM ROUND PARITY. The rig ties them: every
    page-first round is an even round. Any other even/odd property of a round
    acting differently on a first and a second pass would read the same way.
    Separating them needs a leg order that is not a function of round parity,
    which is a rig change and therefore its own window.
  - THE INDEPENDENT BLOCK COUNT IS 2, not 12. The twelve round blocks share a
    session inside each run. The nominal one-sided sign-test p over twelve is
    79/4096 = 0.019 and is quoted only as what the nominal test says.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT. A leg order drawn independently of round parity -- e.g.
seeded per round rather than parity-derived -- would separate the pass-position
term from every other even/odd round property in one window. That is a rig change
and must not be made inside a measurement window.

NOT A GATE PROBLEM. Nothing here is fixed by widening a tolerance, and the
existing gates behave correctly throughout: both runs' positive controls passed at
8.00 B/double differential and 0 unverified read-backs.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8596 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): exact open owner updated; no duplicate.

THE SEEDED MODE'S CLAIMED BALANCE DOES NOT HOLD AT THE ODD ROUND COUNTS THE NEW PREFLIGHT EXPLICITLY ADMITS. `allocPassFlips` chooses `floor(rounds / 2)` flipped rounds. Driving the exported functions gives n=3 as page/all lead counts 2/1 and n=5 as 3/2; only even n is exactly balanced. The structural pin includes n=5 but asserts only that the TRUE count is `floor(n/2)`, then calls that "balanced exactly as parity" without checking the other leg. The source, test, PR body, and bead update all say each leg leads exactly `floor(rounds/2)` times, which is mathematically impossible at odd n, while the preflight tells an operator that 3 rounds is sufficient.

THIS MATTERS ON THE CHANGE'S OWN DESIGN RULE: its rationale says an unbalanced schedule reintroduces the write/pass-position imbalance the alternation exists to remove. The intended phase-2 default of six rounds is safe, so the rig arm need not be reverted. Before advertising odd counts as admissible, either require an even seeded paired run (minimum 4), or explicitly define and justify near-balance at odd n and make the tests/prose state the unequal lead counts. Pin both legs, not only the flip count.

RELATED CONSISTENCY EDGE: the n<=2 seeded preflight refusal is unconditional, even for one-leg `page`/`all` selections that the new test and source call inert under both modes. Scope the refusal to a paired run or reject a meaningless seeded one-leg selection consistently. The phase-2 paired/default-six window remains the priority.

comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8601 (2026-08-21) — THE WINDOW CORRECTLY STAYS OPEN, BUT ITS CLAIM THAT RUN 2 “SEPARATED” PASS FROM PARITY IS FALSE, AND THE PRESCRIBED NEXT DESIGN REPEATS THE CONFOUND.

1. DIFFERENT MARGINAL MEDIANS ARE NOT IDENTIFIABILITY. Run 2's six-round schedule has parity·pass = -2, not 0. `decompose` computes two separate marginal median contrasts; it does not jointly fit the correlated columns. A direct synthetic control using the shipped `decompose` proves the failure:
- true PARITY only (even=+1, odd=-1; pass effect 0) reports PASS=-1 and PARITY=+1;
- true PASS only (page-first=+1, all-first=-1; parity effect 0) reports PASS=+1 and PARITY=-1.
Both use run 2's exact schedule `page,page,all,page,all,all`. So run 2's +0.64/-0.22 pair is not a separated pass/parity estimate. Its two numbers merely differ; each can contain the other term. Run 1 makes the same confound visible by returning identical medians, but run 2 does not remove it.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE LANDED RECORD. The “only run 2 separates,” “independent n=1,” and “four runs, four positive PASS terms” wording is too strong. Three of those four contrasts came from parity-tied or parity-correlated schedules and are page-first GROUPING contrasts, not pass-specific replications. The complementary two-run pooled design has dot=0 and is the only design-level contrast here that balances the columns; it is one paired design and still needs the nonlinear estimator qualified. The cautious terminal conclusion (“not established free of parity”) remains correct, so no shipped decision needs reversal.

THE SUCCESSOR PLAN WOULD REPEAT IT. “Both seeds at symmetric difference 4” gives dot=-2 in every six-round run. It reduces group overlap but does not make either marginal contrast identify its term; the synthetic control above remains maximally wrong. More runs merely replicate that confound. Before another expensive window, pre-register a design/estimator that passes synthetic pure-pass and pure-parity controls. Cheap routes include a round count and schedule with dot=0 WITHIN each run plus an estimator whose behavior is proved on those fixtures, or a joint model/paired contrast that estimates both columns rather than naming two correlated marginal medians. Do not treat “the medians came apart” as the control.

2. THE READER'S ARBITERS DO NOT ARBITRATE. `report()` prints `controlVerdict`, `verification.unverified`, `passOrder`, `parityTied`, and `scheduleDrove`, then unconditionally feeds every row to `blocks`, the headline, both decompositions, and `nullArm`. A copy of seeded-run1 with `controlVerdict.ok=false` still produces all blocks and the “PASS THAT RAN SECOND” headline; reversing round 0's driven legs makes `scheduleDrove=false` and still produces them. The source comments explicitly promise the opposite (“a failed control contributes no data”; disagreement means no figure may be read). Add one fail-closed admissibility boundary used by report/self-test, covering failed/absent control, nonzero/absent verification, wrong mode/seed/tied schedule, and schedule/drive mismatch; prove each rejection.

No duplicate Bead: this open issue already owns the estimator, the window, and its successor design. Keep it open after the terminology/reader repair until a genuinely identifying window exists.

comments.text:
WINDOW TAKEN as worker/passterm-fk6pj, PR #8615. rf2-fk6pj STAYS OPEN. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-design-control-comes-before-the-window.md. Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-passterm/ (four runs). No rig file edited.

WHAT THIS WINDOW DID NOT TAKE FROM THE BRIEF, AND WHY. The dispatch carried phase 2's own successor plan -- 'both seeds at symmetric difference 4' -- but the merged-PR audit of #8601 (this bead, 2026-08-20 20:43Z) had already refuted it, and the tree agrees: q.parity = 4a - R over R rounds with balanced legs, so it is NEVER zero at R = 6. Symmetric difference 4 is the -2 case. Taking the brief literally would have bought four more runs of the same confound. THE DESIGN WAS CHANGED INSTEAD, to twelve rounds where q.parity = 0 is reachable and is exactly the 2x2 balance.

THE CONTROL THE AUDIT ASKED FOR EXISTS AND RAN BEFORE THE WINDOW. alloc_pass_design.cjs (new, ~430 lines) drives the SHIPPED decompose over synthetic block sets whose true terms are known by construction. Positive: all four selected schedules recover pure PARITY, pure PASS and an unequal 1-and-3 mixture exactly. Negative, which is the half that matters: phase 2's run-2 schedule reports PASS -1 on a corpus with NO pass effect, and PARITY -1 on one with no parity effect; the parity schedule returns one number twice; and no balanced six-round schedule is admissible at all. Exit 0.

THE DESIGN: 12 rounds, 4 runs, seeds by an ENUMERATION RULE not a pick (fk6pj-9, fk6pj-11, fk6pj-2386, fk6pj-33), runs 3 and 4 the exact complements of 1 and 2. Three criteria per seed: not parity-tied, q.parity = 0 WITHIN the run, q.linear = 0 WITHIN the run. Complementing inverts the pass order at every round index, so each pair also balances the pass contrast against the round INDEX.

RESULT -- THE DESIGN IDENTIFIED AND THE PRE-REGISTERED BAND REFUSED.
* All four runs ADMITTED by a fail-closed boundary declared before the runs and proved in both directions (8 clauses broken one at a time, each must refuse; phase 2's own record refused on round count and q.parity). Controls 8.00 B/double, 0 unverified, schedule drove what it drew, all four.
* q.parity = 0 INSIDE EVERY RUN and 0 pooled. First allocation corpus that can say the first of those.
* PASS term +0.65, +0.64, +0.20, +0.29 -- four runs four positive -- pooling to +0.45% over 48 blocks.
* PARITY term -0.23, -0.06, +0.24, +0.34 -- two of each sign -- pooling to +0.02%. On the two COMPLEMENTARY PAIRS, the only contrasts balanced against the round index, it reads +0.01% and -0.00% while PASS reads +0.53% and +0.45%.
* Second-lower in 34 of 48, median -0.50%. Reported, not the headline.
* THE BAND REFUSES BOTH. Ten times this window's own null-arm p90 (61 B/boundary) is 610; the pass term's implied delta at the mid rungs is 37.8 B/boundary (21.4-77.0 over the d_all range). Outcome 3 under the pre-registration. THE PASS TERM IS NOT ESTABLISHED.

A DEFECT IN THIS WINDOW'S OWN PRE-REGISTERED BAND, RECORDED AND NOT REPAIRED. The band compares an AGGREGATE (a contrast of medians over 316 cells) against a PER-OBSERVATION noise scale (one cell's p90). It is too strict by roughly the square root of the count, and the 45 B/boundary bar it was modelled on was set for per-boundary cell MEDIANS. Repairing it after seeing the answer is the precise thing pre-registration exists to prevent, so it stands.

TWO FURTHER FINDINGS.
1. THE PUBLISHED NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS CORPUS, and phase 2's explanation of that is REFUTED at four times the sample size. Fraction of the zero-signal null arm above the published 45 B/boundary bar: rf2-0gjqi 5.3% (2/38), phase 2 10.0% (4/40), here 23.2% (38/164). Phase 2 called its 56.5 p90 'an artefact of the count'; at n=164 the p90 is 61 and a quarter of the population sits above the bar, which is a distribution and not an index. Median 0 and absolute median 3 B/boundary still hold. Filed as rf2-NULLFLOOR below.
2. A PER-ROUND-INDEX NUISANCE IS VISIBLE. Within each complementary pair the PASS term is larger in the original schedule than in its complement, by +0.22% and +0.17%. Complementing inverts q at every index, so that half-difference IS an index-tied term. It cancels in each pair and in the pool. No column is identified and no mechanism is proposed.

FOUR RUNS ARE ONE SESSION. runsInSession 1..4 against a single sessionStartedAt, fourteen minutes on one box. The session-level independent count is 1, which is this bead's own standing complaint applied to its own successor.

WHAT THE SUCCESSOR OWES, none of it a rig change:
1. A BAND ON THE AGGREGATE, declared before its runs -- the dispersion of the per-run terms, or a null-arm contrast pushed through the identical block-and-decompose pipeline so the noise scale and the signal scale are the same object. title: hicasso: V2's arm-floor does not cancel the write exactly — write-page reads below write-all at 8 of 8 mid-rung comparisons
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1/V2 re-run window, 2026-08-17. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md.

CONTEXT: V2's criterion became evaluable for the first time. The floor went from certifying 0 of 6 in BOTH 2026-08-13 runs on BOTH segments to 4-6 of 6, so (arm - floor) finally has a certified floor to subtract. The floor drops 1,769 B (9.1%) on reagent-subs and 1,765 B (8.9%) on uix-subs, which is the half of V2's criterion that HOLDS.

THE FINDING. (arm - floor)/B is meant to cancel the write's fixed cost F exactly, so the two writes must give the same per-boundary figure. Across the 13 comparable rungs they differ by -4.28% to +8.81%, absolute median 1.48%, and 10 of 13 certified per-round ranges overlap. That is close. But the RESIDUAL HAS A CONSISTENT SIGN:

  segment       arm       rung   all      page     page-all
  reagent-subs  hicasso   R3     6,984    6,687    -4.25%
  reagent-subs  hicasso   R7    14,447   13,829    -4.28%
  reagent-subs  reagent   R3     7,795    7,664    -1.67%
  reagent-subs  reagent   R7    15,408   15,180    -1.48%
  uix-subs      hicasso   R3     6,691    6,538    -2.28%
  uix-subs      hicasso   R7    13,752   13,520    -1.69%
  uix-subs      uix       R3     5,211    5,164    -0.90%
  uix-subs      uix       R7    11,405   11,347    -0.51%

Eight of eight in one direction, across both segments and both substrates. Under a null of random sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement. Estimator: (arm - floor)/B from each window's own leg median, then the MEDIAN across rounds where BOTH the arm and that segment's floor certified — not a mean, and not pooled beyond that median.

The two R=1 hicasso rungs carry the largest disagreements in the OTHER direction (+1.11%, +8.81%) and are also the noisiest cells on the page, with round-to-round spread of 22-35%. The sign consistency is in the mid rungs, whose spread is 1-7%.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. V2 exists to detect the case where 'the new write provokes different per-boundary work' (allocation-instrument-rework.md:217-220), for which the stated consequence is that the write half is WITHDRAWN rather than re-tuned. This residual is small — a few percent — and at most rungs does not exceed the round-to-round spread. So it is not obviously that case. But it is not obviously noise either, and 8-of-8 is the observation that says so.

THE DECISION NEEDED is whether ~1-4% of non-cancellation is tolerable for the equivalence argument, which is a RULING and not a measurement. The window deliberately did not make it.

SECOND ITEM, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN SEPARATELY: the R=20 rung still produced certified windows under both writes on only ONE of its four arm families (uix-subs | uix R20). reagent-subs|hicasso, reagent-subs|reagent and uix-subs|hicasso produced NO certified pair. That reproduces the 2026-08-13 window exactly, so it is structural rather than incidental, and V2's most informative rung remains unassessed on three quarters of the arms. DO NOT WIDEN A GATE TO ADMIT IT.

Direct parsing shows bisect-5-a-4a1537cb71-replicate.json has controlVerdict.ok=false (12.303 B/double direct; 15.039 differential), and its 19,236/19,736 medians are the middle entries in that three-run row; PR #8457 explicitly excluded this run’s figures. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RE-ANALYSIS, rf2-0gjqi, 2026-08-18. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md (PR #8458). NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN and no rig file was touched.

VERDICT. The CAUSE of the sign residual is UNRESOLVED and the committed corpus cannot decide it. The INFERENTIAL claim in this bead's description -- eight of eight in one direction, a 1-in-256 arrangement -- is REFUTED at source. The thirteen descriptive cells stand exactly as published; one sentence about eight of them does not.

WHY, and the third reason is new rather than the audit restated.

(1) MEASUREMENT ORDER, ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:1504), and ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members with no paired or interleaved option (:1490). One process therefore drives one write, and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). The two arms of every comparison are two sequential process runs. The record declares the order: all was run 2, page was run 3, brackets 01:48:27 / 01:50:09 / 01:51:44. Write and run-position are perfectly confounded across all eight cells. Within-run position is NOT a confound and that sharpens the point -- segment order alternates on round parity (:2269) and arm order is slot-order(n, round) (order_guard.cljc:149), a pure function, so both runs measured every arm at the same within-run position.

(2) ONE FLOOR PER SEGMENT PER WRITE. The estimator differences each arm window against that segment's floor window in the same round. The reagent-subs floor certified 4 of 6 under all, and all four of that segment's mid-rung cells report n = 4 under all, so those four cells difference against THE SAME FOUR FLOOR WINDOWS. A level term common to them shifts all four cell medians identically. Four cells, one draw.

(3) AND THAT TERM IS PAGE-GLOBAL, WHICH MERGES EVEN THOSE TWO. rf2-77gz8 measured the second floor mode moving reagent-subs and uix-subs by EXACTLY the same 3,792 B. So the segments do not draw separately either. Eight cells, ONE draw, probability 1 -- not 1/256.

MAGNITUDE, first-hand. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs and 928 B/write on uix-subs reverses all eight signs (B = 4, so eps = 4 x |delta|; largest mid-rung deltas are 618 and 232 B/boundary). Re-derived here from the eight committed alloc-9jrhi datasets -- population: the floor arm's certified windows; statistic: median of rise/W across certified rounds, per segment per run -- three runs at ONE revision (4a1537cb71) under ONE write span 3,852 B/write (reagent-subs) and 3,912 B/write (uix-subs). Both exceed what would flip every sign. Two runs at 88411ed803 span 1,645 B/write on uix-subs, which still exceeds that segment's 928.

BUT THE MODE ACCOUNT IS NOT ADOPTED. A shared floor offset is additive and identical across a segment's arms; the observed mid-rung offsets span 1,948 B/write within reagent-subs and 740 B/write within uix-subs, and within an arm family the residual is closer to a constant proportion (page/all reads 0.9575 and 0.9572, 0.9832 and 0.9852, 0.9771 and 0.9831, 0.9910 and 0.9949). So rf2-77gz8 is of sufficient magnitude and the WRONG SHAPE to be the whole of it. Not excluded, not supported.

WHY NO NEW WINDOW, verified at source rather than assumed. All EIGHT alloc-9jrhi datasets carry writeSelector "all", plan floor, B = 24 -- NO committed dataset carries write-page, and none carries a ladder rung under any write selector. The only committed full ladder (alloc-2rtt6-138/run1.json) predates the selector AND predates rf2-erre5, so it carries neither writeSelector nor samples. The V1/V2 re-run window COMMITTED NO DATASET AT ALL: there is no alloc-2rtt6-140 directory, so the eight disputed cells cannot be recomputed from anything in the tree. And a fresh window would reproduce the same confound at a new timestamp, because the rig can only drive one write per process.

LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY. The audit's obligation -- compare matched certified pairs after the paired mode lands -- is unmet, and closing would drop it. Filed rf2-irxrw as the work that would decide it. Two things it needs, stated so they are not rediscovered: the FLOOR must be paired too, because the floor is the dominant shared term; and rf2-77gz8 must be resolved alongside, because whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode is untested -- it was observed on a floor-plan run with no arms in it -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION SHOULD NO LONGER BE READ AS SAYING: "Under a null of random sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement." That null is not the one this design admits. Everything else in the description stands.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
THE PAIRED MODE HAS LANDED (rf2-irxrw, PR #8461). This bead stays OPEN: its audit obligation -- compare matched certified pairs -- is unmet until a window is taken through the new mode, and closing would drop it.

WHAT IS NOW POSSIBLE THAT WAS NOT. P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired drives :p0/write-page AND :p0/write-all at every arm inside every round, on the same page, in the same process. That is the same-page/same-run pair allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires and the instrument could not take, and it removes the confound this bead's re-analysis established at source: the two arms of every published comparison were two sequential PROCESS runs in a fixed order.

FOUR THINGS IT MAKES AVAILABLE TO A LATER WINDOW.

  1. MATCHED WITHIN-ROUND DIFFERENCES. Every recorded window names its own write and carries pairKey -- the arm key its legs share -- so an estimator groups a round's windows by that field and differences the two legs directly. It does not reconstruct a pair from two files, and it does not parse a key.

  2. A PAIRED FLOOR. The floor is an arm of the plan, so the leg pass takes it under both writes like every other arm. This bead's own note said the floor must be paired because it is the dominant shared term, and it is: (arm - floor) can now be formed within one round under each write, against a floor measured under that same write in that same round.

  3. THE WRITE IS NO LONGER CONFOUNDED WITH POSITION. The leg order alternates on round parity exactly as the segment order does, so over six rounds each write leads three times. A drift within a run no longer reads as a difference between the writes.

  4. rf2-77gz8's UNKNOWN BECOMES ASKABLE. The paired mode puts an arm window and a floor window under both writes in one round for the first time, which is what deciding whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode requires -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated so it is not assumed. The two legs of a pair are separated by one segment pass rather than being adjacent windows, so a mid-run transition of the kind rf2-77gz8 describes can still fall between them; that is a large improvement on a whole process but it is not zero. NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN and no figure moved -- the build carries no measurement, and the thirteen descriptive cells in this bead's description stand exactly as published.

SEQUENCING UNCHANGED: rf2-77gz8 should be resolved alongside or first.
