comments.text:
PAIRED WINDOW TAKEN, rf2-0gjqi, 2026-08-18 14:26-14:31 AUSEST. Record:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md (PR #8473).
Datasets committed: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/.
Built at 1f004b15ff. NO RIG FILE WAS EDITED and no gate, band, threshold or
tolerance was touched.

THE AUDIT OBLIGATION IS DISCHARGED. #8424 required matched certified pairs once
the paired mode landed, an independent-block count over run-pair/order blocks
rather than rungs, and a correction to the measurement page, the studio index and
this bead together. All three move in PR #8473; the block count is below.

DESIGN, FIXED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN. Two runs, P0_ALLOC_PLAN=full
P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired, B = 4, six rounds. Two were declared and
two were taken; none added after a result, none dropped. The estimator was
written down before the first run.

THE ESTIMATOR, NAMED FOR WHAT IT IS. Per round r, segment s, arm a:
  d_all  = (arm@all .legMedian - floor@all .legMedian) / B
  d_page = (arm@page.legMedian - floor@page.legMedian) / B
  Delta  = d_page - d_all
A round contributes ONLY IF ALL FOUR windows certified in that round. Cells are
reported twice because they are different statistics: RATIO-OF-MEDIANS (median of
d_page over the cell's rounds over median of d_all over the SAME rounds, less 1 --
the form comparable to the published table) and MEDIAN-OF-RATIOS. Neither is a
mean and neither is a run-mean.

THE RESIDUAL DISSOLVES.
  - Across the 16 mid-rung cell medians (8 cells x 2 runs), page reads below all
    at 10 OF 16 on ratio-of-medians and 9 of 16 on median-of-ratios. The
    published window read 8 OF 8.
  - Magnitudes: 0.06% - 2.98% absolute, absolute median 0.46%. Published: 0.51% -
    4.28%, absolute median 1.68% on the same eight cells.

AND THE SIGN IS SET BY MEASUREMENT ORDER, NOT BY THE WRITE. Block = the ROUND,
because within a round every arm of a segment differences against the same floor
pair and rf2-77gz8's term is page-global. Taking the median of Delta/d_all over
each round's certified mid-rung cells: THE LEG PASS THAT RAN SECOND READS LOWER
IN 10 OF 12 BLOCKS -- 6 of 6 in run 1, 4 of 6 in run 2 -- WHICHEVER WRITE
OCCUPIED IT. Decomposed under an additive position model, the pass-order term
reads +0.68% and +0.21% (same sign both runs) and the order-free WRITE term reads
-0.33% and +0.24% (OPPOSITE signs). Filed as rf2-fk6pj.

INDEPENDENT BLOCKS, COUNTED AS THE AUDIT ASKED. TWO independent process blocks.
The twelve round blocks share a session inside each run and are NOT twelve
independent trials; the nominal one-sided sign test over twelve gives
p = 79/4096 = 0.019 and is quoted only as what the nominal test says. The claim
that survives the stricter count is the weaker one: both process blocks put the
second pass lower.

V2's FLOOR-DROP HALF HOLDS, AND IS NOW WITHIN-ROUND. 1,652 B (8.6%) on
reagent-subs and 1,652-1,658 B (8.4%) on uix-subs, the same number on both
segments to within 6 B, spanning 1,644-1,664 B across 21 paired certified rounds.
Published unpaired: 1,769 / 1,765 B.

THE CONTROLS. Both runs' positive control passed -- differential 8.00 B/double
against a predicted 8, direct 8.08, 0 unverified read-backs. Both captured EXIT 1
on the falls gate (55 and 54 collections inside measured windows), so NO SLOPE IS
QUOTED from either. And a null arm the previous windows did not read: R = 0 mounts
boundaries that read nothing, so arm - floor must be zero under either write --
over 38 paired certified observations its Delta reads a median of 0 B/boundary,
absolute median 1.5, 90th percentile 4.5. That is what licenses reading mid-rung
differences of 5-198 B/boundary at all.

WHAT IS NOT CONCLUDED, and it is a long list on purpose.
  - THE TWO WRITES ARE NOT SHOWN TO BE EQUIVALENT. No interval is offered for the
    write term. Two process blocks give -0.33% and +0.24%: consistent with zero,
    and NOT a bound. Its magnitude is UNRESOLVED.
  - THE CAUSE OF THE PUBLISHED 8-OF-8 IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The measured pass-order
    term is of the right sign but SMALLER than the published 1.68% absolute
    median, and it is a within-round effect where the published confound was
    between two PROCESSES. Different estimand; right sign, wrong size.
  - rf2-77gz8 IS NOT RESOLVED. Its second mode did NOT appear here -- the
    certified floor spans 46-58 B over six rounds in all four (run, segment)
    cells under both writes, with no 3,792 B step -- but that is B = 4 on the
    `full` plan against its B = 24 on the `floor` plan, and absence in two runs is
    not absence. What DID change is that the estimator no longer turns on the
    answer: a page-global level present in a round enters all four of that
    round's windows and cancels. Its sequencing note ("resolve alongside or
    first") is therefore satisfied in the sense that mattered.
  - NO RULING IS MADE ON TOLERABILITY. The description's question -- whether
    ~1-4% of non-cancellation is acceptable -- was posed of a figure this window
    does not reproduce, so as posed it is MOOT. Whether anything is left to rule
    on is Mike's, not this window's.
  - LEG ORDER IS NOT SEPARATED FROM ROUND PARITY (the rig ties them), no

    one per run, reproducing across runs).
  - NO BOUND ON WITHIN-RUN QUIETNESS. Brackets are before-and-after only. The box
    was loaded (5.7-8.0% of 24 cores, 0 java at every bracket) and that is

  - THE INTRA-LEG GATE SCREENED NOTHING. Stride 2, so allocIntraLegRefusals
    returns [] by construction.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION SHOULD NO LONGER BE READ AS SAYING. The whole
paragraph beginning "THE FINDING" retains its thirteen descriptive cells, which
stand as published; but "Eight of eight in one direction", "Under a null of random
sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement", and "it is not obviously noise either" are
each now MEASURED not to hold under the pairing the design always required. The
DECISION NEEDED paragraph is moot as posed.

THE SECOND ITEM CARRIED OUT RATHER THAN DROPPED. R = 20 again certified on one of

NO FIGURE MOVED, and the reason is arithmetic rather than lucky: the refused run's medians are the MIDDLE entry of each row, so the two admissible runs were already the endpoints the 3,852 / 3,912 B/write spread was taken between. The page says so, and keeps the refused run on the page rather than deleting it -- the sub-finding is that the floor's between-run spread is LARGE, so an inadmissible run could only ever be argued to have inflated it, and dropping it changes nothing. One run in eight failing a control that predicts a constant 8 B/double is itself a fact about this instrument's between-run behaviour and is recorded as one.

THE ESTIMATOR IS NOW NAMED, which the triage asked for and which turned out to be checkable rather than declarative. The page's published figures are median(perWrite) = rise/W with W = the six NON-PRIME writes (writes, not windowWrites); that reproduces 22,984 / 19,236 / 19,132 and 23,468 / 19,736 / 19,556 to the digit. Taking legMedian over the same certified rounds instead gives 22,892 / 23,332 and 19,100 / 19,540, a spread of 3,792 / 3,792 B -- rf2-77gz8's figure to the byte, the same number on both segments, and the triage's own re-derivation reproduced. So the residual gap between this page and rf2-77gz8 is the estimator and not a third quantity. Added to the page as a cross-check.

GATES: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main exit 0, both re-run on the final base after rebasing past 11 landings, and both proven to reach the edited tree by a planted fault restored to an identical blob hash. mkdocs NOT nominated -- exclude_docs keeps docs/design/** out of the site.

title: [method] reopened-item shortcut revives the false description-is-stale rule
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 00:25 AUSEST on rf2-lo7uy, by the mayor making the mistake.

THE GAP. The timestamp-ordering rule exists in three places and none of them is the
one that was needed:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (4 mentions) — WORKER-FACING.
    It is the text the mayor PASTES INTO A BRIEF, so it instructs the worker.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-backlog-reread.md (1 mention) — mayor-facing, but scoped
    to the hourly BACKLOG REREAD loop.
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md (2 mentions).
mayor-dispatch.md, which governs writing a brief FROM a bead, says nothing about it.
Grepped for 'bd history|newest|created_at|timestamp|superseded|stale.*comment' — the
only hit is an unrelated routing paragraph.

WHAT IT COST. The mayor read rf2-lo7uy top-down, took a 03:02Z mayor triage comment
splitting the bead into an EDIT half and a WINDOW half as the newest text, and
dispatched the edit half. A 04:55:51Z comment titled 'RIG HALF LANDED — THIS BEAD IS
NOW WINDOW-ONLY' already recorded that PR #8384 had merged those exact arms at
05:12:23Z the previous day.

PROCEEDING WOULD HAVE BEEN DESTRUCTIVE, NOT MERELY WASTEFUL. 'n' is an input to
lane/slot-order on that instrument, so adding two more nulls takes n from 11 to 13 and
moves EVERY arm's position footprint including the nine published ones — discarding
#8384's layout and starting a third series, on the very rig whose slot-sensitivity the
bead exists to measure.

THE WORKER CAUGHT IT. It walked 'bd history --json' newest-first across adjacent pairs,
found the 04:55:51Z comment, verified #8384 MERGED at source rather than from the
comment, wrote no code, and correctly declined to run a spine or quote an exit code for
a tree it had not changed.

THE FIX — one sentence-group appended to the 'Find + group' paragraph (line 19), whose
neighbours are already the same class of pre-dispatch verification ('A COUNT IS A CLAIM
TOO, AND THE GREP THAT CHECKS IT IS A DIFFERENT ONE'). Proposed text, to append after
'...treat a parent's remainder table as stale until re-derived.':

  **AND ESTABLISH WHICH TEXT ON THE BEAD IS NEWEST BEFORE YOU BRIEF FROM IT — by
  TIMESTAMP, never by position.** Every brief this file sends already tells the WORKER
  to do this, and mayor-backlog-reread.md tells the mayor to do it when rereading the
  backlog; the gap was here, at the one moment a brief is actually written from a bead.
  Comments do not render in timestamp order relative to notes appended into the
  description block, so the visually-last text is routinely not the newest:
  'bd comments <id> --json' sorted by created_at descending, and 'bd history <id> --json'
  walked newest-first to the first change in a text-bearing field, are the only two
  reads that answer it. **The mayor's OWN earlier note is the most dangerous stale
  source**, because it reads as authoritative and you recognise your own words.
  [then the rf2-lo7uy incident as above, and:] That is the 'where the item and this
  brief disagree, the ITEM governs' clause doing the work it is there for — but it
  should not have had to.

WORD IT YOURSELF IF YOU CAN DO IT BETTER; the above is a draft, not a specification.
Keep it PROPORTIONATE — the anti-gold-plating clause applies. Do NOT add a checklist,
a script, or a tracking field, and do NOT restate the reasoning that
dispatch-prompt-template.md already owns; this file's own line 23 warns that a second
copy of the template's text is 'the same drift one level down'.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the pre-commit hook refused, exactly as designed —
'.claude/commands/' is a worker-tracked surface and the mayor checkout cannot commit to
it. Attempted at 00:47, refused, reverted, filed here.

CONTROLS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so do not re-derive them: 'scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci'
covers '.claude/commands/*.md' via COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC and was proved to bite on THIS
FILE by a planted broken link — exit 1, naming '.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md:29'.
It is SILENT ON SUCCESS, so a green run alone proves nothing. 'check_doc_slugs.py' also
exits 0 on this file. One caution learned the hard way: the mayor planted its control on
an UNCOMMITTED edit and restored with 'git checkout --', which discarded the edit along
with the plant — commit first, then plant, and verify the restore by content hash rather
than by reading a diff.
acceptance_criteria: The dispatch template treats closed-to-open as an attention signal, not proof: it never infers that closure means merged/shipped or that a reopened item's description is necessarily stale. The existing timestamp-ordered history walk and tree check remain the authority. Prose-only correction; no new mechanism.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8906 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

The new closed-to-open probe is useful, but its evidence does not support its categorical wording. Completeness: three stale reopened descriptions plus one never-closed control establish a high-signal heuristic, not that every reopened description is stale; there is no reopened/current-description control. Correctness: the text says a reopened description is stale "by construction" because "the work that closed it has shipped" and the live instruction is whatever note reopened it. In this repository closure does not entail shipment (current concrete counterexample: rf2-lzrza is closed while its PR #8912 remains open/unmerged), and an issue can be reopened because the same defect regressed, leaving the original description accurate. This revives the field-based slogan this owner's prior audit deliberately removed.

Minimal completion: keep closed-to-open as a strong signal to do the already-required timestamp history walk; remove "guaranteed", "certainty", "by construction", and the inference that close means shipped or that a note necessarily supersedes the description. State that history plus the tree decides what is current. No script, checklist, tracker field, or new method layer.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8922 (merged 2026-09-01). The closed-to-open shortcut is retained as a strong signal but no longer stated as a verdict: 'guaranteed', 'certainty' and 'by construction' are gone, and the two false inferences riding on it are named explicitly — closed does not mean shipped (items here close when a PR opens, so a closed item's work may be unmerged), and a reopening does not always supersede (an item reopened on a regression has an accurate description). History and the tree decide currency. No checklist, script, tracker field or new layer, per the item. Note the item's own DESCRIPTION was stale — it targets .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, under a directory that no longer exists — while its audit note was live, which is the corrected wording working as described. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_readme_links.py --ci 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict 0; sabotage exit 1 naming loops.md:582 and the planted anchor, restore verified by git blob hash ed4a0b832723ac2ba5a9833731b467889638f427 on both sides.

MAYOR 2026-08-17 01:45 AUSEST — SCOPE CORRECTION FROM A FOURTH INSTANCE, WHICH HAPPENED AFTER THIS BEAD WAS FILED. The fix as drafted would NOT have prevented it.

THIS BEAD AS FILED describes the defect as 'the mayor does not establish which TEXT on the
bead is newest before briefing'. That is true and it is not the whole shape. Instance four
shows why.

INSTANCE FOUR, rf2-2rtt6.140, 2026-08-17 01:25. I DID order by timestamp — for the
SCHEDULING question. I read the comments newest-first, established that all four tracker
dependencies had closed and that the same-surface collision had cleared, and dispatched on a
correct decision. Then I took the CONTENT of the brief — 'the two routes left', the
(W+1).perWrite squeeze table, the rung figures — straight from the DESCRIPTION, which is the
bead's OLDEST text, written 2026-08-08.

Route (a) had shipped NINE DAYS EARLIER in PR #7702: ':p0/write-page' is already the
window's DEFAULT arm and rebuilds at '(count (:cells db))', the mounted width. Route (b)
landed in the SAME PR, DELETING the masking budget — and its absence is MACHINE-PINNED at
p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:568, 'lacks(/const ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B/, the budget constant is
deleted)'. So the entire squeeze arithmetic the brief was built on came from a rule that no
longer exists. My fence 'route (b) is not yours' also contradicted the bead's standing
ruling, which is the composed package: 'route (a) AND route (b)... Not (a) alone, not (b)
alone.'

The worker checked at source, refused, wrote no code, and named it exactly: 'the dispatch
DECISION was correct — fence and neighbour both cleared; only its CONTENT was nine days
stale.'

SO THE RULE NEEDS BOTH HALVES:
  (1) Establish which TEXT is newest — 'bd comments --json' by created_at DESC,
      'bd history --json' walked newest-first to the first text-bearing change.
  (2) THEN VERIFY EVERY TECHNICAL CLAIM THE BRIEF WILL CARRY AT origin/main HEAD — not
      only the blockers. A route, a constant, a file path, a threshold, a prohibition and
      a table are each a claim, and a bead saying 'the two routes left' was written when
      two routes were left.

THE COMPRESSIBLE FORM, which may serve better than the incident: **A BEAD'S DESCRIPTION IS A
HISTORICAL DOCUMENT. ITS COMMENTS ARE THE CURRENT STATE.** The description records what was
true when the bead was filed and is never rewritten as the work lands; that is not a defect
in the tracker, it is what a description is for.

STILL KEEP IT PROPORTIONATE. This is one sentence-group in the 'Find + group' paragraph, not
a checklist, not a script, not a tracking field. mayor-dispatch.md's own line 23 warns that a
second copy of the template's text is 'the same drift one level down'.

RUNNING COST OF THE CLASS, so the fix can be sized honestly: four instances in one night,
all mine, all failed SAFE — one refused by a tracker guard ('bd close' blocked by
rf2-0moc4), two refused by workers who walked the history themselves, one caught by the
pre-commit hook. Two full dispatches were spent on refusals. The 'where the item and this
brief disagree, the ITEM governs' clause is what caught the two worker cases, and it should
not have had to.

MAYOR — THE TWO FILES IN THIS BEAD'S CLOSING QUESTION HAVE OPPOSITE PROFILES, SO IT IS TWO RULINGS AND NOT ONE. Measured at source 2026-08-22 04:0x AUSEST, tip b15b38aad2. Nothing here rules anything.

THE CLOSING QUESTION groups specification.md (506 lines) and facade-freeze.md (247) together as carrying view specification while falling into no category the ruling enumerated. Grouped, they look like one decision. Counted, they do not.

CITATION CENSUS, tracked files, .beads excluded because it is tracker prose rather than a reference:

    specification.md      16 citers
    facade-freeze.md       2 citers

  CONTROL — the five that step (a) MOVED to implementation/hicasso/spec/:
    dispositions.md  29 · budgets.md  31 · invariants.md  20 · naming-ledger.md  19 · complaints.md  14

So specification.md sits squarely inside the band of the five that were ruled normative and moved. facade-freeze.md is an order of magnitude below all six, and its only two citers are docs/design/hicasso/product-kind-census.md — the census that classified it — and dispositions.md.

AND THE COUNT UNDERSTATES specification.md, because WHO cites it decides this more than HOW MANY:

  * A GATE READS IT AND ASSERTS ON ITS CONTENTS. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_facade_inventory.py:890
    builds the path REPO_ROOT/docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md and opens it; :894 raises
    "specification.md now names `{}`. The Source column's reach has ..." — the checker fails when the
    page changes. That is the strongest test of normativity this repo has: a page a gate reads is
    contract by construction, whatever tree it happens to sit in.
  * PRODUCTION SOURCE NAMES IT THE NORMATIVE OWNER, in those words:
    implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/evidence.cljs:100 — "Normative owner:
    `docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md` §10"; tool.cljs:119 — the same, §10.
  * .github/workflows/test.yml:1212 cites it as a live premise.
  * THREE OF THE FIVE FILES THAT ALREADY MOVED cite it — budgets.md, dispositions.md, invariants.md.
    The normative set points AT it from its new address while it stays behind.
  * The checker's own comment at :131 records that it "did NOT move", so the split is already
    visible to the code and being worked around.

facade-freeze.md's two citers include NO gate, NO workflow and NO production source.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It does not decide either file — whether category 2's list was exhaustive is the operator's, and I am not answering it. What it does is make the two questions separable and give each one evidence: specification.md is cited like the five that moved and is read by a gate and named "Normative owner" by shipping source; facade-freeze.md is cited like a working record. A ruling that treats them as one thing is deciding the second on the first's evidence, or the first on the second's.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not read either file's CONTENT to judge whether it reads as specification. The census on this already exists (docs/design/hicasso/product-kind-census.md, which the bead quotes at VS 55% for both) and I did not re-derive it. This note is about consumers, which is a different axis and the one nobody had measured.

A SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE IF specification.md MOVES: check_facade_inventory.py:890 hardcodes the old path and would need re-pointing in the same commit, exactly as step (a)'s gate re-pointing did. And the new address is under implementation/hicasso/spec/, which is rf2-7rzg's Chromium-toll surface — so the two operator calls touch each other here as well.
SCOPING PASS ON STEP (b), 2026-08-22 18:0x AUSEST, at origin/main tip 112310ddbc. THE BRIEF'S PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD: STEP (b) IS ALREADY MERGED. I was dispatched to establish the teaching set and scope the migration. There is nothing to scope. PR #8668 is state MERGED, mergedAt 2026-08-21T13:29:59Z, merge commit f53dd7c17e, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor f53dd7c17e HEAD` confirms it is an ancestor of a checkout whose HEAD equals origin/main exactly. Six files: 05-forms.md, 06-lists-and-collections.md, product/README.md, forms-recipes.md, virtualizer-recipe.md, check_guide_samples.py. I edited no file and dispatched nothing.

Ordering verified as instructed rather than read top-down. `bd history --json` walked newest-first over 2504 snapshots: the newest text-bearing change is 2026-08-22T04:04:02 (the notes growing 9023 -> 12609, i.e. the "two files, opposite profiles" note). Today's 17:06 and 16:xx entries are checkpoint no-ops. So the newest instruction on the bead is that note, and the description's "AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE" header is discharged exactly as the brief said. Governing text is the comment "OPERATOR RULING - THE SPLIT" at 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z. Both fences the brief named are clear: rf2-wppza closed, its PR #8667 merged, and it was #8668's own base.

Below is what the brief actually asked for, delivered as an AUDIT of the merged set rather than a scope of unstarted work. I re-derived rather than trusted, and one finding closes a hole nobody had checked.

THE TEACHING SET, as established and executed - all six carriers verified by me at source. The set is the kind-3 "reader-facing answer" roster of docs/design/hicasso/product-kind-census.md, taken at ANY share rather than primary-only, which is precisely the trap the bead warned about for the contract set. Arithmetic reconciles: 237+51+71+86+31+132 = 608 against the census's stated ~608 (the per-file line attributions are the census's figures; the reconciliation is mine).

1. release-policy.md, RF 70%, ~237 lines - ALREADY PUBLISHED, not migrated. Its own :168-172 states the consumer-facing abridgement lives at docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md #supported-versions; that heading is real at 00-installation.md:111, and Sec 5.1's "An upgrade may cost you a rename. It should not cost you a rethink." stands near-verbatim at 00-installation.md:137 as "Upgrades before 1.0 may cost you a rename, and should not cost you a rethink", with the complaint-id stability promise beside it.
2. async-routing-recipes.md, RF 60%, ~86 - ALREADY PUBLISHED. Its :148 claims 08-async-resources.md and 07-routing-and-navigation.md "teach these three shapes already". I did not take the file's word for it: settle-merge -> 08 Sec "Merge a settled reply into the current draft" (:9); per-instance mutation status with optimistic plan -> 08 Sec "Track writes per instance" (:86) and Sec "Optimistic updates and rollback" (:122); dirty-navigation guard -> 07 Sec "Guard unsaved changes" (:221), with Sec "Deep links, Back, and Forward" (:287) carrying the Back-button half. All three published.
3. virtualizer-recipe.md, RF 60%, ~71 - GENUINE GAP, MIGRATED. 06-lists-and-collections.md gained Sec "Keep the focused row mounted" (:233), Sec "Announce the model's count, not the DOM's" (:262), Sec "Screen a virtualizer before adopting it" (:279).
4. forms-recipes.md, RF 55%, ~51 - GENUINE GAP, MIGRATED, and it is a DEFECT repair rather than an absence. 05-forms.md disabled the submit button on (not can-submit?) while :submit-attempted? is set only by a rejected submit, so the attempt that would set it was the one the disabled button prevented and the chapter's own display gate was dead code. Fixed by splitting the two kinds of unavailable - :disabled for in-flight, :aria-disabled for invalid - with the accessibility rationale and a new troubleshooting row. Verified in the merged diff.
5. per-keystroke.md Sec 6, RF 20%, ~132 - ALREADY PUBLISHED. 19-performance.md:15 carries the echo budget row ("the visible echo arrives within one 60 Hz frame at p95"); the keystroke trace's step 6 (:189, "React commits and Hicasso converges value and caret before the event turn ends") and step 7 (:190, the paint) carry the finding.
6. lanes/hot-path-architecture.md, RF 30%, ~31 - ALREADY PUBLISHED, and the published form is a superset. Its five-rung performance ladder is escape-ladder.md, a dedicated 214-line page that adds per-rung costs, how to take an escape, and climbing back; 19-performance.md:58 mirrors the ladder. Its Sec "Read-topology guidance" bullets map one-for-one onto 06-lists-and-collections.md: fine row reads -> Sec Fine-grained rows (:70), coarse view-model -> Sec Coarse display model (:108), chunked/windowed -> Sec Chunk the comparison sweep (:151) and Sec Window the DOM (:187), oscillating read sets -> Sec Avoid large oscillating read sets (:295).

So: four of six already answered on a published page, two real gaps closed. Nothing was duplicated, which is the right call - a duplicate in a published guide is worse than an absence.
THREE AUDIT FINDINGS FROM THE SAME PASS. Every count below carries a control.

FINDING 1 - LEXICAL PROBES CANNOT DISCRIMINATE TEACHING CONTENT IN THIS CORPUS, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. This validates the structural discriminator #8668 used as the correct instrument rather than a convenience. I checked the second-person probe that worker discarded and his control holds: 06-lists-and-collections.md, an unambiguous teaching page, contains ZERO occurrences of "you" (control: 00-installation.md 8, index.md 3, 05-forms.md 1). I then built an independent instrument - imperative density at line/bullet start over 22 verbs, normalised per 1000 lines - and it failed its control too: forms-recipes.md, virtualizer-recipe.md and release-policy.md, three of the FOUR RF-PRIMARY carriers, all score EXACTLY ZERO. The census records the cause at its own :390 - the corpus states its laws in the indicative and returns exactly one RFC-2119 keyword across all 64 files. Anyone re-opening this must read, not grep, and the bead's "do not grep for recipe" instruction generalises further than it says.

FINDING 2 - THE CENSUS HAS ONE COVERAGE GAP, AND IT IS BENIGN. product-kind-census.md classifies 59 of the 60 tracked files under product/. Measured: tracked files 60; census names 59 distinct product/ targets plus the 5 step (a) moved to implementation/hicasso/spec/ (budgets, complaints, dispositions, invariants, naming-ledger), whose links it re-pointed. CONTROL: whole design/hicasso tree 146 files, docs/core/hicasso 29, docs/core 64, and a nonsense pathspec returns 0. The unclassified file is post-rename-recertification-2026-08-20.md, 448 lines, which post-dates the census. I read it rather than inferring from its siblings: it is 100% working record - a dated fourth results record whose own header says every figure is a counter or a byte count and none is a clock reading, with Sec 7 "The controls - which gates were shown to still bite". No teaching content, so the gap does not touch the set. Recorded because the census is the instrument every downstream decision here rests on.

FINDING 3 - THE CENSUS'S KIND-3 ROSTER IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE GUIDE COVERS THE SHORTFALL ANYWAY. This is the finding of the pass, and it CLOSES rather than opens. I refused to take the census's RF roster on trust and ran two independent read-passes over 13 files it scored at 0% RF, picked as the likeliest misclassifications. Five carry material meeting a teaching criterion (addressee is an application author; the claim is standing rather than true-as-of a measurement; it is instruction rather than a gate-read row or a decision rationale): lanes/ergonomics-api.md (census VS 95%) - the n/$ grammar bullets and worked hot-row example; lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md (census VS 75%) - the Suspense/Activity retain-versus-release asymmetry; authoring-report-todo.md (census WR 100%) - N1 key map, N2/N3 reg-state placement, N4 :ref stability, N5 on-submit auto-prevent; authoring-report-slice.md (census WR 100%) - the ::h/value event-vector shape and the ::h/revision reset test; lanes/testing-xray.md (census VS 60%) - the testing ladder and its refusal rule.

BUT EVERY ONE OF THOSE ITEMS IS ALREADY PUBLISHED, each verified at page and heading:
- selector shorthand / class and id as props -> 10-native-tier.md:87
- Suspense retains where Activity releases -> 21-code-splitting.md Sec "A committed sibling keeps its reads while the fallback is up" (:229), which states it MORE sharply than the design source: "a slow chunk costs you a fallback, not a resubscribe - and if you want the opposite, hiding a pane and releasing what it holds, that is Activity's job rather than Suspense's"
- :ref must be a stable function -> 09-interop.md:353, "A top-level function keeps ref identity stable and avoids reattaching on every render", with the hoisted attach-map form shown
- key map {"Enter" ...} -> 03-events-as-data.md:194, 13-overlays-and-focus.md:252, cookbook.md:139, glossary.md:343
- ::h/value -> taught from 01-getting-started.md:60 onward; full reserved vocabulary at 03-events-as-data.md:42
- ::h/revision reset -> 04-controlled-inputs.md Sec "Reset with ::h/revision" (:127-190), including the anti-pattern warning against a view-body random-uuid or render counter, plus two troubleshooting rows
- :on-submit auto-prevent -> 05-forms.md:341 and 03-events-as-data.md:281
- testing ladder and refusal -> 15-testing.md Sec "The testing ladder" (:67), L0-L4 with Sec "L2 refuses React-only behaviour" (:267) and Sec "Use L3 for React claims" (:372)
NET: the census under-counted kind 3, and the guide over-delivers against it. The teaching migration has no residue. The set was established from an imperfect instrument and still landed complete. One item has no Hicasso guide home and correctly so - where a reg-state concern is DECLARED (todo N2/N3) is a re-frame2 application code-organisation convention, not Hicasso view authoring, and is out of this guide's scope.

THE GATE SURFACE, established rather than guessed.
(a) PUBLICATION. mkdocs.yml:14 docs_dir: docs; exclude_docs at :32 lists design/hicasso/, and "design/hicasso" matches exactly ONE line in the whole file - that exclusion, never a nav entry. Nav :265 carries "Hicasso: the view layer". Destination half built and published, source half excluded. CONFIRMED.
(b) YES, FENCED BLOCKS UNDER docs/core/hicasso/ ARE DIGEST-PINNED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING GATE FACT. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py carries a ROSTER pinning 223 fenced blocks across ALL 29 docs/core/hicasso pages by 12-hex digest. Editing any fenced block in a guide page is therefore a TWO-FILE change - the page plus its roster digest - exactly the class of the docs/core/freehand pin. #8668's sixth file is precisely that: a +1/-1 to the roster, 05-forms.md block 8, 51950e9321d2 -> 103b4f580107. It runs unconditionally in .github/workflows/test.yml (:1321 --self-test, :1328 live) and inside npm run test:hicasso-invariants. Any future guide-editing dispatch must be briefed with this or it lands red.
(c) LINK GATES, per half. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DEFAULT_ROOTS = (docs, spec, skills, migration) at :94, so it covers BOTH halves for link targets and heading anchors. scripts/check_provenance_pins.py DEFAULT_ROOT = "docs/design/hicasso" at :247, blocking via --changed-since, so it covers the SOURCE half only. Net: design/hicasso gets both gates; core/hicasso gets check_doc_slugs plus the digest gate.
(d) THE FENCE ASYMMETRY RUNS IN THE LOSING DIRECTION FOR THIS MIGRATION. Confirmed at the constant: check_doc_slugs.py:1708 FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES = ("docs/design/hicasso", "docs/the-mayor-method"). Fenced content moving design -> core therefore leaves a tree where doc links inside fences ARE validated and lands in one where they are NOT, so a markdown link inside a migrated fence silently stops being checked. Narrow in practice - fences in these pages are Clojure and in-fence doc links are rare - and offset on a different axis, since content arriving in docs/core GAINS digest pinning it did not have. It did not bite #8668, whose two migrations added prose sections and edited one fence, but it should be stated in any future hicasso design -> core move.

PHASE 2 SHAPE: THERE IS NO PHASE 2. Zero files, zero lines, no dispatch. Step (b) is merged and I found no teaching residue after independently testing the roster it was built from.

OPERATOR: I FOUND NO SECOND QUESTION. The only live one is the one already on this bead - specification.md and facade-freeze.md still carrying view specification in product/ while falling outside both category 2's closed list and category 4's - which the 2026-08-22 04:04 note already separated into TWO rulings on a citation census. That is bucket (2)'s question, not step (b)'s, and I have not answered it.

BEAD STATE: (a) merged #8661, (b) merged #8668. The ruling closes this bead when both have merged AND product/ carries no operative contract or unmigrated teaching content. THE TEACHING HALF OF THAT CONDITION IS NOW DISCHARGED AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The operative-contract half remains the open specification.md / facade-freeze.md ruling. I did not close the bead.

ONE OBSERVATION, OFFERED AS SUCH AND RECOMMENDING NO ACTION: 03-events-as-data.md:246 writes an inline :ref (fn [node] ...) closure while 09-interop.md:353 teaches that a top-level function is what keeps ref identity stable. 03's subject is rf/capture-frame composition at a foreign edge and 09 is the chapter that owns refs, so I read this as a simplification serving a different lesson rather than a defect. Recorded only so the judgement is on record.
MAYOR 2026-08-22, tip 112310ddbc — I DISPATCHED A SCOPING PASS FOR WORK THAT HAD ALREADY MERGED,
and the worker refuted the premise instead of doing the job. The refusal is the deliverable and it
was correct. Recording my own error here rather than in a transcript, and then the state.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I read this bead's note "STEP (b) IS THE ONLY THING BETWEEN THIS BEAD AND
CLOSING", confirmed its fence had cleared (rf2-wppza closed, PR #8667 merged), and dispatched.
Step (b) was already done: PR #8668, "docs(hicasso): merge the teaching set into the guide
(rf2-ps7ia step b)", MERGED 2026-08-21T13:29:59Z as f53dd7c17e, verified by me at source after the
worker reported it — state MERGED, merge commit an ancestor of origin/main, six files.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS EXACT AND IT IS EMBARRASSING. My brief pasted this sentence verbatim: "AND THE
CHEAPEST GUARD IS THE TREE, NOT THE ITEM: before you brief or build X, check whether X ALREADY
EXISTS AT TIP — one directory listing would have ended the dispatch that produced this rule." I
verified the fence, the guide's arrival, the file census, the classifier surface and the gate
coverage. I did not check whether the work itself had landed. I pasted the rule and did not apply
it, which is a more useful thing to know about briefs than any of the premises I did check.

WHY THE BEAD DID NOT SAVE ME: the note declaring step (b) outstanding and the merge that discharged
it fall on the SAME DAY, and nothing wrote the merge back onto this bead. A note that says "X is
the only thing remaining" is a claim with a shelf life, and this one expired within hours.

WHAT THE PASS DELIVERED ANYWAY, all of it worth more than the scope I asked for.

  1. THE GATE FACT, and it generalises well beyond this bead:
     implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py DIGEST-PINS 223 FENCED BLOCKS ACROSS
     ALL 29 docs/core/hicasso PAGES, and runs unconditionally in CI. EDITING ANY FENCED BLOCK IN
     THE HICASSO GUIDE IS A TWO-FILE CHANGE — the page and the roster. PR #8668's sixth file is
     exactly that roster bump, which is the pattern rather than an exception. Any future guide
     dispatch must carry this or it lands red.

  2. THE FENCE-LINK ASYMMETRY RUNS THE LOSING WAY for design->core moves: doc links inside fenced
     blocks ARE validated under docs/design/hicasso and are NOT under docs/core. So moving a fenced
     block from design into the guide moves it from checked to unchecked, and a broken link inside
     it stops being reported. Worth knowing before the next migration, not after.

  3. THE KIND-3 CENSUS ROSTER IS INCOMPLETE, and the worker flagged the instrument rather than
     letting the next reader inherit it as sound: five files scored at 0% RF do carry teaching
     material. Every item in them is nonetheless already published, each verified at page and
     heading — so the set was built from an imperfect instrument and still landed complete. That
     is luck worth naming as luck.

  4. LEXICAL PROBES CANNOT DISCRIMINATE TEACHING CONTENT IN THIS CORPUS, in either direction. The
     worker confirmed the discarded second-person control AND had its own imperative probe fail on
     three of the four primary carriers: this corpus writes in the indicative.

  5. One census file was unclassified (post-rename-recertification-2026-08-20.md). Read: pure
     working record, benign.

WHERE THIS BEAD NOW STANDS. THE TEACHING HALF — bucket (1) — IS DISCHARGED and independently
verified. What remains is the OPERATIVE-CONTRACT half and the one live operator question already on
this bead: whether specification.md and facade-freeze.md move, which is bucket (2)'s and which
nobody below the operator has answered. The worker did not answer it and neither do I.

*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-24 05:14 AUSEST, tip f4a61bc074, by the
backlog-reread loop. This bead ALREADY CONTAINED the phrase three times and was counted as marked by
the 2026-08-23 census. It should not have been, and the reason is worth more than the banner.

WHY THE MARKER CENSUS PASSED THIS BEAD WRONGLY. All three prior occurrences of "NOT DISPATCHABLE" in
these notes are the phrase being RETIRED, not asserted:

  @~1000  a pre-ruling note explaining why the bead was not dispatchable BEFORE the split ruling;
  @~2500  the ruling comment's own summary: "The description's 'AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE'
          header is DISCHARGED; dispatch per the execution shape in the ruling comment.";
  @~13650 a worker re-confirming the same: "the description's 'AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE'
          header is discharged exactly as the brief said."

Two of the three say DISCHARGED in the same sentence as the phrase. A substring scan cannot tell an
assertion from its own retraction, so the census scored this bead marked while its LIVE hold - which
sits at the very end of the notes, 27,000 characters past the newest of those three - carried no
marker at all. The failure runs in the direction that HIDES a hold rather than manufacturing one,
which is the worse direction for this particular scan.

THE HOLD THAT IS ACTUALLY LIVE, quoted from this bead's own newest note rather than re-derived:
"THE TEACHING HALF - bucket (1) - IS DISCHARGED and independently verified. What remains is the
OPERATIVE-CONTRACT half and the one live operator question already on this bead: whether
specification.md and facade-freeze.md move, which is bucket (2)'s and which nobody below the
operator has answered. The worker did not answer it and neither do I."

SO THE BEAD IS HELD, AND ON A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE ONE THE OLD HEADER NAMED. The old header
asked for the split ruling; that ruling landed on 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z and the header is correctly
discharged. What is open now is downstream of that ruling: bucket (2)'s destination for two named
files. Reading either of the "discharged" sentences as "this bead is released" is the misread this
banner exists to stop, and this pass made it before correcting it at the tail.

ORDERING, verified rather than assumed this pass: notes last changed 2026-08-22T08:22:53Z; the newest
comment carrying any instruction is the ruling at 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z, which is OLDER. The notes tail
is therefore the governing text, and it is what is quoted above.

NOTHING IS QUEUED BEHIND THIS BEAD: dependency_count 0, dependent_count 0, and it appears in neither
the blocked list nor any other bead's manifest. What the hold costs is that two files stay at an
address this bead's own description calls interim custody.

Whatever of the normative set is teaching content merges INTO those guide pages rather than moving as separate files.

Moves there: the facade inventory (dispositions.md operative rows §2.1/§2.2), complaints.md (the complaint catalogue), invariants.md, the naming outcomes (ledger's operative residue), and budgets.md — ruled operative contract, since it is the artefact's live performance ledger. The classifier needs no new predicate: implementation/hicasso/** already arms the hicasso lanes — but verify with a probe in the PR body per the rf2-6ng7 pin-your-arming codicil.

3. FRAMEWORK-LEVEL TOUCHPOINTS — root spec/ ONLY via fresh authored text, on demand, where the re-frame2 pattern itself is affected (004-Views/006/011 touchpoints). NOTHING relocates into root spec/: the 004D precedent stands — product prose is never re-aimed into pattern specification. Root spec/ remains the pattern's tree; hicasso product prose does not enter it.

4. GOVERNANCE AND EVIDENCE — decision-brief.md, the kill table/validation.md, phase records, lanes/, pilots/, and the whole studio/ tree: WORKING DESIGN RECORDS, address unchanged for now. Studio is evidence whose history is the content (append-only in spirit, freezes like the freehand studio did); it cannot graduate and must not be rewritten. PLANNING FACTS carried from rf2-g0vdg's census: the normative set is ~1,138 lines across the corpus (<7%), heavily transcribed between carriers; read against 12 files (7 primary + 5 partial carriers), write against 3-4 de-duplicated documents, plausibly <1,000 lines. title: [method] workers open PRs before they are done and the mayor merges them green — use draft PRs as the interlock
description:
THE MERGE LOOP AND THE DISPATCH BRIEF CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE MAYOR IS THE ONE WHO WROTE BOTH. Twice in one session a PR was merged while its author was still working on it.

THE TWO RULES, both of them mine, both individually right:
  DISPATCH BRIEF: "PUSH AS YOU GO, not at the end — pushed commits are the only durable worker state ... OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist; a PR is not a claim of green."
  MERGE LOOP: merge on the five-clause criterion the moment it is met, and never block on CI.

Put together they say: workers publish PRs before they are finished, and the mayor merges them the moment CI goes green. **The gap between "CI is green" and "the author is done" is where both incidents happened.**

INCIDENT 1, 2026-08-15 ~11:55. #8323 merged while worker/hicaudit-5zmul was live. GitHub's delete_branch_on_merge removed its branch server-side; the worker's next push recreated it against a main that already carried its commits, producing DUPLICATE PR #8325 with a byte-identical three-file diff. Closed by hand after verifying the duplication rather than assuming it.

INCIDENT 2, 2026-08-16 ~01:33. #8333 merged while worker/w-lane-est was still running gates. Its own words: "#8333 — MERGED by the mayor while gates were still running; full gate table posted as a comment on it." It recovered well — cherry-picked the one wording fix the merge had not carried onto current main as #8339, and re-ran the doc gates on that branch — but that is a whole extra PR and an extra review cycle for work that would have ridden the first one.

NEITHER MERGE VIOLATED THE CRITERION. Both PRs were genuinely green on all five clauses when merged. The criterion is not the defect; the missing coordination is.

*** THE FIX, and it uses a mechanism that already exists rather than inventing a rule to remember. *** Brief workers to open the PR as a DRAFT and mark it ready for review as their last act before reporting done. `gh pr merge` REFUSES a draft, so the interlock is enforced by the host rather than by anyone's memory — which is the property the stash ban and the beads-boundary hook both have and the reason they hold. It preserves everything the push-as-you-go rule buys: commits are still pushed continuously and still survive a worker's death, and the mayor can still read the diff and the gate output at any time.

WHAT TO CHANGE:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md — the push-as-you-go clause gains "open it as a DRAFT; mark it ready as your last act before reporting done."
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 1 — the merge criterion gains a line noting a draft PR is not a merge candidate, and WHY: the five clauses test the CHANGE, not whether its author has finished with it.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — the same line, concretely: skip drafts in the sweep.

THE ALTERNATIVE, rejected: have the mayor check worker liveness before every merge. It works, but it is a rule that must be remembered on every merge forever, and it re-introduces exactly the worktree-activity sweep the merge loop deliberately does not do. The draft flag costs one command at the end of a worker's run and cannot be forgotten by the mayor at all.

SCOPE FENCE: those three files. HOT ZONE method surface — SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead. Note rf2-4228y also targets loops.md; SEQUENCE the two, do not run them together.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Run mkdocs as `python -m mkdocs` — bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH, and 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass. No fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8944: REOPENED exact draft-interlock owner; no duplicate. Completeness: the new finished-draft exception landed only in loops.md. dispatch-prompt-template.md's canonical Publishing the change section still says never flip the flag on an inference, permits only the agent's report or an operator stop, and says that until one arrives the finished change waits stranded. loops.md now gives the opposite executable instruction when the worker's tracker items are closed: verify, publish, and retire. Correctness: the added block also says the earlier third-local-gate worker separates cleanly because it had not reached close, then seven lines later says that same third-gate worker would present with closed items. That contradiction makes the claimed discriminator unclear. Implementation quality: this restores the two-source drift the draft interlock was created to prevent. Minimal completion: state one rule consistently in both method pages (and any surviving concrete merge command); if closed tracker records are the new positive signal, define the required ownership/all-items-closed check in both and preserve the full section-1 merge verification. Replace the contradictory third-gate reference with the actual residual case—an author who closed, then discovered further work. No new liveness system or broader rewrite.
MAYOR, 2026-09-01: PR #8949 opened to answer this audit. Both findings accepted as stated; neither is disputed.

The repair REMOVES what PR #8944 added rather than extending it. #8944 invented 'closed tracker items' as a new positive signal licensing the mayor to set the publish flag. That was unnecessary - dispatch-prompt-template.md already carried a sufficient authorisation, 'the operator's decision to stop that agent, which settles liveness by making it false'. loops.md now routes to that instead, so there is one rule, stated on the template page and deferred to from the loop page. The self-contradiction the audit names (third-gate worker 'separates cleanly' vs 'would present this way too') disappears with the discriminator it belonged to.

What both pages gain is the ORDER, which is where the real error was and which neither page stated: STOP, THEN MERGE. Merging first and stopping second reaches the same end state by the forbidden route, and leaves an identical record afterwards - a merged change beside a stopped agent - so nothing later can tell the two apart. That is why the rule is 'stop, then merge' rather than 'make sure the agent ends up stopped'.

Residual risk restated as the audit asked, and re-attributed: an author who closed its items and then found further work presents identically, and the act that can destroy unpushed work is the STOP, not the merge. Bounded by merging the published head CI graded.

The bead's third file, .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, no longer exists - that directory has been removed. Nothing to change there; the bead's WHAT TO CHANGE list is stale in that one respect.

Gates on #8949: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0, each proven against this worktree by a planted fault going red and naming it, both restores verified by git blob hash. exclude_docs does NOT hide the-mayor-method/, so the strict build genuinely covers these pages - confirmed by the planted red rather than assumed.
close_reason:
FIXED and on main. PR #8949 merged (mayor/one-rule-draft-interlock), answering the audit that reopened this bead against PR #8944.

Both audit findings were accepted and both are fixed by REMOVING what #8944 added rather than extending it:

1. TWO-SOURCE DRIFT. #8944's finished-draft exception landed only in loops.md, while dispatch-prompt-template.md's Publishing the change section still said never flip the flag on an inference and that the change waits stranded. That is exactly the drift the draft interlock exists to prevent, reintroduced by the repair.
2. SELF-CONTRADICTION. #8944 claimed the third-local-gate worker 'separates cleanly because it had not reached close', then seven lines later named as residual risk that the same worker would present with closed items. The caveat falsified the claim and the claim was left standing.

THE FIX DROPPED THE INVENTED DISCRIMINATOR. #8944 introduced 'closed tracker items' as a new positive signal licensing the mayor to set the publish flag. Unnecessary: the template already carried a sufficient authorisation - 'the agent's own report, or the operator's decision to stop that agent, which settles liveness by making it false'. loops.md now routes to that. A stopped agent cannot be working, so the question the four clocks could not answer stops being asked, and the self-contradiction disappears with the discriminator it belonged to.

WHAT BOTH PAGES GAINED, and it is what neither said before: the ORDER. STOP, THEN MERGE. Merging first and stopping second reaches the same end state by the forbidden route, and leaves an identical record - a merged change beside a stopped agent - so nothing later can tell the two apart. That is why the rule is 'stop, then merge' rather than 'make sure the agent ends up stopped'.

Residual risk restated as the audit asked and re-attributed: an author who closed its items then found further work presents identically, and the act that can destroy unpushed work is the STOP, not the merge. Bounded by merging the published head CI graded.

STALE ITEM DETAIL, for the record: this bead's WHAT TO CHANGE list names .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md as a third file. That directory no longer exists, so there was nothing to change there.

GATES on #8949: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0, each proven against the authoring worktree by a planted fault going red and naming it, both restores verified by git blob hash. Verified merged and on main before closing.

title: [method] added-line triage still says it settles the common case
description:
FOUND BY rf2-cyt80's WORKER, which declined to widen its own scope and flagged this instead — correctly. The mayor's bead text is the defect here, not the worker's reading of it.

WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-cyt80's drift 3 OBSERVED that "neither mayor-hygiene.md nor loops.md section 5 contains the words cherry, patch-id or patch-equivalent". Its FIX clause then named only mayor-hygiene.md. The worker implemented exactly what the fix clause said and reported the gap rather than quietly extending its fence. So the concrete command file now carries the containment test and THE GENERIC PUBLISHED METHOD STILL DOES NOT.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 5 ("Branches") says to delete merged branches and never one whose change is not verifiably merged. It says nothing about HOW to establish containment — and under rebase-merge the obvious test is wrong in both directions.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE GENERIC DOC SPECIFICALLY. loops.md is the method as published for other repositories, and rebase-merge is not a local quirk. A reader adopting the method there gets the rule and not the trap. Measured here on 2026-08-15 over 63 worktrees: 60 branches read "ahead of main by 1 to 3 commits" and 58 of them were FULLY MERGED, because a rebase gives every merged commit a new SHA so it never becomes an ancestor of the trunk. Deleting on ancestry would have kept all 58 forever; ignoring the reading would have destroyed worker/receipts-hic081's 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits. `git cherry <trunk> <branch>` settled both directions in one command — `-` means an equivalent patch is already upstream, `+` means genuinely new.

WHAT TO WRITE, keeping loops.md's register — GENERIC, no bd commands, no repo paths, no PowerShell, no bead ids:
  - ancestry and the ahead-count are both useless for containment when the project merges by rebase, and they fail in OPPOSITE directions;
  - the test is patch-equivalence (`git cherry`), which answers both directions at once;
  - the measured warrant, stated without repo-specific identifiers: 60 branches read ahead, 58 were merged, 1 was not, one command separated them.

Cross-reference rather than restate: loops.md section 4 and the command files already explain why the ahead count misleads for LIVENESS. This is the same trap on a different question — containment, not liveness — and saying so is cheaper and more durable than a second copy of the reasoning.

SCOPE FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md ONLY. mayor-hygiene.md already has its half from rf2-cyt80; do not touch it again. This is a hot-zone method file, so SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Note that bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH — 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass; run it as `python -m mkdocs`. No fenced code blocks are added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.
acceptance_criteria: loops.md consistently describes the added-line scan as a non-conclusive triage hint; no sentence says it settles or proves containment. Conclusions still require the whole-patch comparison, and the delete-only-on-minus rule remains unchanged.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8901 — REOPENED EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE.

COMPLETENESS: The PR correctly fixes the asymmetric meaning of git cherry: '-' proves patch-equivalent containment, while '+' only says that equivalence was not found. Its new one-step "discriminating test" is still incomplete, however: searching only for the commit's added lines ignores file/path and location, multiplicity, order, and every deletion. A generic added line may already exist elsewhere at the tip while the branch's actual change is wholly absent, so "all present means the content landed" is false. Conversely, upstream can preserve the change after a rename, formatting edit, or follow-on rewrite while an exact added line is absent, so "any absent means genuinely outstanding" is also false.

CORRECTNESS: Keep the safe deletion rule (delete only on '-'), but do not present added-line presence as a containment verdict. It is at most a cheap triage hint. Before concluding either landed or outstanding, inspect the full patch against the current tip at the intended paths/locations, including deletions and replacements; a three-way comparison from the branch parent is sufficient. This matters even though the prose forbids using the test to delete: the current wording can still dismiss real unmerged work as a phantom.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / NARROW REMEDY: Amend only the new paragraph in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md. Downgrade the added-line scan to a heuristic and name the full-patch review needed for a conclusion, or remove the purported one-step discriminator. Do not build a containment framework or change the conservative '-' deletion criterion.
AUDIT PR #8920: reopened exact owner. The repair correctly labels the added-line scan triage and explains both false directions, but the preceding sentence still says to run it first because "it settles the common case." That directly contradicts the next sentence ("triage, not a verdict") and the PR body's claim that the scan is no longer described as settling anything. A heuristic that cannot conclude either landed or outstanding does not settle even its common case; that word is the behavioral instruction likely to make a mayor stop before the required whole-patch comparison.

Minimal correction only: say the scan is cheap and useful for prioritising/starting the common investigation, without claiming settlement. Keep the full-patch conclusion and delete-only-on-minus rule unchanged; no new containment machinery or broader method edit.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8928 (merged 2026-09-01). The added-line scan no longer claims to settle anything: 'run it first because it settles the common case' becomes 'run it first because it costs seconds and tells you where to point the real check — never because it finishes one', removing the contradiction with 'triage, not a verdict' two sentences later. The full-patch conclusion and the delete-only-on-minus criterion are unchanged, per the audit's minimal correction.

title: hicasso: the-cold-read-mount-term's commit-half decomposition needs a whole re-take, not a two-cell restatement
description:
FOUND BY rf2-d360z's measurement window (2026-08-15). rf2-d360z was scoped to
re-take two absolutes and restate the share columns, on rf2-gttif's finding
that only rf2-aqgr2's keyword mint had moved under the table. THAT PREMISE IS
INCOMPLETE. Two further changes have landed under the same table, both AFTER
rf2-gttif and rf2-d360z were written on 2026-08-03, and neither is accounted
for anywhere on the page. Verified by reading the tree, not inferred:

1. rf2-dabt3 (383ba2d645, authored 2026-08-03 20:51) RETIRED THE SUB-INDEX
   INTO THE CELL TABLE. front/sub_index.cljs is DELETED. The shipping commit
   half no longer performs an index/mount! plus a whole-set record-reads!; it
   pushes one reader slot per key ((.push (.-readers cell) reg)). The same
   commit replaced read_profile_app.cljs's c-noindex arm with c-noreaders.

   CONSEQUENCE: the-cold-read-mount-term.md section 1 publishes
   '| - index write (c-local - c-noindex) | 0.0750 | 8.7% |'
   which PRICES A STRUCTURE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, through an arm that no
   longer exists. Section 4 quotes the same term as its 5.6% share.

2. rf2-lzpfj (04bb0fa73a) ADDED interop/activate-derived-value! to
   commit-local! so the copy matches wire-cell!'s shape. c-local now performs
   work it was NOT performing when the published 0.8625 denominator was taken.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE FIXED BY RE-MEASURING TWO CELLS. Every share in that table
divides by c-local. c-local has since LOST the index write, LOST the mint, and
GAINED the activation, so it is not the arm that produced 0.8625. Dividing
2026-08-02 numerators by a 2026-08-15 denominator is arithmetic across two
instruments -- the precise thing this page's discipline exists to prevent. The
share column therefore cannot be repaired by re-taking its denominator, which
is why rf2-d360z declined to restate it and marked the row instead.

WHAT IS OWED: a single phase-B run that takes EVERY arm at ONE commit and
republishes the whole commit-half decomposition -- absolutes, deltas and
shares together -- with the c-noindex row retired and c-noreaders in its place.

BLOCKED BY rf2-3l6hf. Phase B currently cannot resolve three of the four terms
that must be positive (they read negative on at least one run of three), so a
re-decomposition taken today would publish noise. Fix the window first.

SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: this is a clock estimand, so it needs the
quiet box and Shape 6 in full. rf2-d360z's window measured the dispersion that
makes this bead necessary: the commit arm moved 0.4500-0.5500 across three
runs of one binary in one session, four grid steps, nothing changing between
them.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8327 COMPLETENESS (2026-08-16): this existing whole-re-take owner must also sweep the live narrative derived from the retired sub-index; no duplicate Bead was created. In docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md, the “Reading it” conclusion still states that the index write is 8.7% and that batching it was declined. In docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-in-page-mount-term-decomposed.md, the conclusion still proposes batching the index write. Both read as current even though rf2-dabt3 deleted that structure. Retire or qualify those statements when this decomposition is republished.

Evidence caveat: this Bead's “nothing changing between them” wording is stronger than the window record. Queue length was 0 on 82/85 samples; two non-zero samples may have overlapped run 3. Preserve the re-take requirement, but do not attribute all observed dispersion solely to the instrument.
rf2-3l6hf's measurement window has run (2026-08-16, blob e1701c41af, PR
#8328). THE BLOCKER IS PARTIALLY LIFTED, and the part that is not lifted
is now bounded rather than unknown.

THE WINDOW. 4 frames -> 32 frames/window, 24 -> 64 samples. Grid falls
0.0125 -> 0.0015625 ms/commit. Three runs, exit 0, positive control
passing on each, residue gate never firing.

WHAT YOU CAN NOW DECOMPOSE (three runs, one sign each):

  reaction build + cache insert   0.4734 / 0.5016 / 0.4578
  watch wiring                    0.0687 / 0.0563 / 0.0672   <- recovered
  cell-map insert                 0.0375 / 0.0375 / 0.0469   <- recovered

WHAT YOU STILL CANNOT, AND ITS BOUND:

  reader membership              -0.0000 / -0.0062 / -0.0000

Still at or below zero at 8x the resolution. Its floor is measured by
arithmetic impossibility (the term must be positive), giving the
instrument a floor of about +/-0.006 ms/commit. So quote the fused
reverse edge as **< 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit half** — a
bound, not a figure. Do not quote a number for it.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU IF YOU DO NOT READ THEM FIRST.

1. **`c-noactivate` is NOT the noise floor the file says it is** — see
   rf2-tcffa, and rf2-19usn for the shipping cost behind it. It reads
   0.0406 / 0.0250 / 0.0406, LARGER than the cell-map insert in two runs
   of three, because `get-fn-cached` cannot cache a nil resolution and
   the React-hook spine never publishes that hook. If you read it as
   noise you will wrongly condemn a window that works. It is a real term
   and belongs in the decomposition as one.

2. **The shares are NOT window-size-invariant.** Reaction build is 56% of
   `c-local` at 4 frames, 62% at 4 frames on a same-day control run, and
   66.9-68.4% at 32 frames. Take every arm at ONE window shape and STATE
   the shape beside the table. Shares from different shapes do not
   compose, which is the same class of error the page's discipline
   already forbids across commits.

NOT CONCLUDED, and left to you or to a later window: whether ~128-256
frames would bring reader membership clear. The floor fell by about the
factor the window widened (0.04-0.05 -> 0.006 for 8x), which suggests it
is still window-limited rather than dispersion-limited, so a further
4-8x is the estimate. That is a PREDICTION from two floor readings, not
a measurement, and it was deliberately not attempted mid-window.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8328 CORRECTION (2026-08-16): supersedes this Bead's instruction to quote reader membership as “< 0.006 ms/commit, under 1%”. The c-noreaders arm removes real work with unknown positive cost; observing -0.0062 does not calibrate a symmetric ±0.0062 floor and cannot upper-bound the true cost. The old/new “floor scaled 8x” comparison also selects different positive-cost arms. Treat reader membership as unresolved, not bounded, and remain blocked by reopened rf2-3l6hf until a genuine null/control or valid direct bound exists. The recovered watch-wiring and cell-map observations remain useful.
MEASUREMENT WINDOW RUN 2026-08-16, PR #8329, commit a43aa8609f, instrument
blob 6d2b67b5b0. THE RE-TAKE RAN AND DECLINES TO PUBLISH. Bead stays OPEN
and BLOCKED.

THE WINDOW SHAPE, chosen once before the first run and held for every arm
of every run: 32 frames/window, 8x(2+8) = 64 kept samples per arm, grid
0.0015625 ms/commit — rf2-3l6hf's widened shape exactly as it landed. No
gate, tolerance or knob moved; instrument blob identical before and after.
Three runs, exit 0 each, both arm-order guards reportable on every run,
phase-A positive control passing on every run, phase-B residue gate never
firing. Every arm of a run taken in ONE process, interleaved.

ARMS (ms per 141-key commit, p50):

  arm             run 1     run 2     run 3
  commit          0.6953    0.7516    0.7203
  c-local         0.6594    0.6969    0.6875
  c-noactivate    0.6172    0.6484    0.6313
  c-nowatch       0.5875    0.6313    0.6094
  c-nosub         0.2156    0.2250    0.2188
  c-noreaders     0.6547    0.7109    0.6750
  c-nomap         0.6156    0.6703    0.6375
  b-build         0.4938    0.5688    0.5406
  c-local/commit  0.9483    0.9272    0.9544

TERMS (c-local minus arm):

  reaction build + cache insert   0.4437 / 0.4719 / 0.4688
  watch wiring                    0.0719 / 0.0656 / 0.0781
  activation capture              0.0422 / 0.0484 / 0.0562
  cell-map insert                 0.0437 / 0.0266 / 0.0500
  reader membership              +0.0047 / -0.0141 / +0.0125   <- STRADDLES ZERO

WHY IT DOES NOT PUBLISH. Four of five terms resolve with one sign on every
run. Reader membership does not: it straddles zero across three runs of one
binary in one session, and a negative delta is arithmetically impossible
when c-noreaders does strictly less work than c-local. A decomposition that
cannot see one of its terms is not one — this bead's own founding argument,
now applied to its own re-take. Nothing in section 1's table or section 4
is restated, and NO SHARE IS COMPUTED.

THE "< 0.006 ms/commit" BOUND IS WITHDRAWN, NOT PUBLISHED, on two
independent grounds. (1) A most-negative reading cannot bound a positive
quantity: if an observed delta is an unknown positive cost plus estimator
error, -0.0062 shows only that one negative excursion exceeded 0.0062 PLUS
that cost; it neither calibrates a symmetric floor nor caps the cost, and
comparing most-negative readings at two window widths cannot demonstrate an
8x floor scaling. (2) Run 2 read -0.0141 on this box — more than twice the
figure that was to be published. Agrees with the merged-PR audit of #8328.
THE WINDOW WAS NOT WIDENED to chase the term: whether 128-256 frames would
recover it is a prediction, not a measurement, and a rung added between runs
makes the series two instruments.

c-noactivate CORROBORATED AS A TERM, NOT A FLOOR (rf2-tcffa, independently
reproduced): 0.0422 / 0.0484 / 0.0562, one sign on every run, LARGER than
the cell-map insert in two runs of three. It cannot arbitrate whether a
window is wide enough, which is the job read_profile_app.cljs's docstring
and rf2-3l6hf's commit message both give it.

STILL OWED BY THIS BEAD, untouched by this window: the index write row still

MAYOR 2026-08-16 00:35 — I PROPAGATED A REFUTED BOUND INTO A LIVE WORKER'S BRIEF, AND THE AUDIT CAUGHT IT BEFORE THE WORKER PUBLISHED. Recording the error and the correction.

WHAT I DID. rf2-3l6hf's window recovered two of three terms and reported the third, reader membership, as "bounded: < 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit half". I read that as a finding, wrote it into rf2-07rnj's dispatch brief as guidance — "quote the BOUND, not a figure ... Publish that bound" — and reported it to the operator the same way.

WHY IT IS WRONG, per the merged-PR audit of #8328, whose reasoning I have checked and accept. Let an observed delta y equal an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e. A reading of y = -0.0062 proves only that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t. It does NOT establish that +/-0.0062 is a calibrated, symmetric floor, and it CANNOT upper-bound t. A most-negative observation is a statement about the error term, not about the quantity.

THE SECOND HALF, same shape: comparing the most-negative readings from DIFFERENT positive-cost arms at 4 frames and 32 frames cannot prove an 8x floor scaling. Two error excursions from two different arms are not two measurements of one floor.

SO READER MEMBERSHIP IS UNRESOLVED, NOT BOUNDED, until a genuine null/control arm exists or another valid bound is derived. And rf2-07rnj stays BLOCKED: rf2-3l6hf owned resolving the decomposition, one of its original terms still does not resolve, and a decomposition with an unresolved term is not one - which is rf2-07rnj's own founding argument turned on itself.

*** THE GENERAL RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO CARRY. *** An impossible reading tells you the instrument's error reached at least that far. It does not calibrate the error, and it does not bound the thing being measured. Treating "the worst negative I saw" as "the floor" is the same move as treating "no test failed" as "the code is correct" - it converts an absence into a guarantee. Whenever a worker reports a bound derived from readings that should have been positive, ASK WHAT NULL ARM PRODUCED IT. If the answer is "the impossible readings themselves", it is not a bound.

HOW IT REACHED A WORKER, and this is the process failure rather than the arithmetic one. The premises-are-claims sentence was in rf2-07rnj's brief, and it did not protect against this, because I passed the bound as GUIDANCE ("publish that bound") rather than as a premise to check. That is exactly the failure mode docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md already names for a LEAN: a worker reads guidance as instruction and a premise as a claim, so anything phrased as guidance bypasses the check. A NUMBER I ASSERT IS A LEAN TOO. Demand the evidence that produced it before writing it into a brief - here, one question would have caught it: what null arm produced that bound?

RECOVERY: the live worker was messaged the moment the audit was read, before it published. It was told to keep every measurement it had taken, publish no bound, not chase the term by widening the window, report, and leave rf2-07rnj open and blocked.

title: docs(method): equal export row counts are not tracker-state equality
description:

Before advancing the cursor, the merged main ledger at 43dcd2440a22a42e77d6ab773fb8df2a43a6a5a6 and the Dolt remote each contained 1,938 issues but different facts. DO: before checkpoint overwrites .beads/issues.jsonl, compare HEAD's issue IDs/updated_at/status to the fresh Dolt export. Either import newer/missing Git issue rows timestamp-safely then re-export, or refuse with exact IDs/fields. Keep the existing row-count floor, but do not treat equal counts as equality.   no quantum, and there overlap is not merely weaker but ABSENT: under the loose rule one
  round at 0 B beside five good ones PASSES, which is the exact failure the control exists to
  catch.

WHAT REMAINS IS HALF (b) AND IT IS MIKE'S: are the published P0 rows re-adjudicated, or does
the change apply only from the next run? The bead's own instruction was to record that on
rf2-2rtt6.1, which is CLOSED and is the operator-owned STANDARD.

records with no window run, the widest excursion across ten published heap-control figures is
4,690,838 B, 0.195% below a plus-or-minus-25 percent band.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS (2026-07-30, paths superseded above) ---

Found while consolidating HD-008 onto the lane (rf2-f5roa, PR #7267).

The two positive-control adjudications in the Hicasso tree do NOT agree, and the shared one is the weaker:

  lane/control-verdict           ok? = (and (<= min hi) (>= max lo))
                                 i.e. the measured RANGE need only OVERLAP the +/- slack band.
  hd8-rows/positive-control!     :within? = (and (>= lo (* p (- 1 tol))) (<= hi (* p (+ 1 tol))))
                                 i.e. EVERY round must be INSIDE the band.

HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule explicitly: 'a control whose worst round is wrong has caught something, and letting a good round vouch for a bad one is how an instrument stops being one.' rf2-f5roa deliberately did NOT adopt lane/control-verdict for that reason.

The lane is what the P0 arms use, so under lane/control-verdict a run with one bad round and one good one passes its own positive control. That is the shape of thing this programme keeps finding: a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything.

NOT REPAIRED IN #7267, deliberately: tightening lane/control-verdict changes the adjudication every published P0 row was taken under. Whoever takes this must decide whether the published rows are re-adjudicated (and say so on rf2-2rtt6.1) or whether the change applies only from the next run.
