title: Reconcile the 23 Spec 009 Tags-column rows the keys-set arm reds on (blocks rf2-6tags)
description:
BLOCKS rf2-6tags. The Tags-column keys-set arm is designed, measured and proven non-vacuous, but it CANNOT BE ARMED until these rows are reconciled, because it reds on them.

MEASUREMENT (worker/gate-detectors, PR #7027, against origin/main 5026a73078). The arm pairs a catalogue category to its schema by PascalCasing the name (:rf.error/resource-route-plan -> ResourceRoutePlanTags), diffs the schema's key set against the row's :tags column, and excludes exactly the two envelope slots the catalogue's own rule at spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1948 names ("Two envelope-level slots are therefore deliberately absent from every row" — :recovery and :category). That rule also says the column "lists the keys that genuinely ride under :tags on the wire — nothing else", so every finding below is a row the catalogue's own contract requires to change.

  pre-fix ded86cff64 (parent of the rf2-wsopx fix): 90 paired rows, 24 findings, INCLUDING :rf.error/resource-route-plan -> missing :contributor, :plan-cause
  main    5026a73078:                               90 paired rows, 23 findings, resource-route-plan absent (fixed)

So the arm reds on exactly its motivating defect and greens on the fix. The residual 23 are pre-existing instances of the same class — 44 undocumented schema keys.

THE 23 ROWS (schema keys the Tags column omits):
  :rf.error/coeffect-exception        (CoeffectExceptionTags)      :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception-message
  :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded      (DrainDepthExceededTags)     :frame
  :rf.error/effect-handler-bad-return (EffectHandlerBadReturnTags) :event-id :event
  :rf.error/flow-eval-exception       (FlowEvalExceptionTags)      :event
  :rf.error/fx-handler-exception      (FxHandlerExceptionTags)     :failing-id :frame
  :rf.error/handler-exception         (HandlerExceptionTags)       :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception
  :rf.error/interceptor-exception     (InterceptorExceptionTags)   :reason :event :event-id :frame :exception
  :rf.error/machine-action-exception  (MachineActionExceptionTags) :event :handler-id :frame
  :rf.error/machine-grammar-not-in-v1 (MachineGrammarNotInV1Tags)  :substitute
  :rf.error/malformed-schema          (MalformedSchemaTags)        :failing-id :frame
  :rf.error/no-such-sub               (NoSuchSubTags)              :frame
  :rf.error/override-fallthrough      (OverrideFallthroughTags)    :failing-id
  :rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args          (RegSubBadArgsTags)          :frame
  :rf.error/sanitised-on-projection   (SanitisedOnProjectionTags)  :exception-message :returned :reason
  :rf.error/sub-exception             (SubExceptionTags)           :failing-id
  :rf.error/sub-input-fn-bad-return   (SubInputFnBadReturnTags)    :frame
  :rf.error/sub-input-fn-exception    (SubInputFnExceptionTags)    :frame
  :rf.error/system-id-collision       (SystemIdCollisionTags)      :reason
  :rf.http/stale-suppressed           (StaleSuppressedTags)        :carried-token :current-token :event-id
  :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed(StaleSuppressedTags)        :event-id
  :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch          (HydrationMismatchTags)      :first-diff-path
  :rf.warning/multiple-redirects      (MultipleRedirectsTags)      :frame
  :rf.warning/multiple-status-set     (MultipleStatusSetTags)      :frame

THE ADJUDICATION NEEDED. Not all 23 are necessarily row-side. Several are ALIAS divergences: the schema declares :event / :event-id where the row documents :rf.event/v / :rf.trace/event-id. The 009 frame-destroyed row itself states the distinction ("The bare :event spelling is the ERROR-tag spelling ... :rf.event/v is the dispatch-PIPELINE spelling"), so for those the SCHEMA may be the side that is wrong. The rest (:frame on nine rows, :reason on four, :failing-id on four) look like plain row omissions. Each needs a one-line call: fix the row, or fix the schema.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN PR #7027. The dispatch fenced spec/009-Instrumentation.md's row content with an explicit instruction: "you are building the checker, not editing rows; if a row genuinely must change, STOP and tell me". Twenty-three rows genuinely must change. Reporting rather than editing.

ALSO MEASURED, against the ruling's premise. Spec-Schemas.md defines 111 *Tags schemas; the error/warning catalogue has 489 rows, not one schema per row. 89 schemas pair by name derivation, 22 do not (FxHandledTags, MachineUnhandledNoOpTags, SchemaValidationTags, NoSuchCofxTags, RoutePrefetchedTags, InvalidResourceSpecTags, BadAppSchemasArgTags, LargeValueUnschemadTags, ArtefactMissingTags, HttpInterceptorClearedTags, HttpInterceptorRegisteredTags, FxSkippedOnPlatformTags, DbReplacedTags, DecodeDefaultedTags, HeadMismatchTags, EpochCbSilencedOnFrameDestroyTags, InterceptorsInMetadataMapTags, InvalidMutationSpecTags, MachineActionRanTags, MachineGuardEvaluatedTags, MachineTimerCancelledTags, UnwrapBadEventShapeTags). Explicit in-row `Spec-Schemas §`XxxTags`` citations exist on only 3 of 489 rows, so citation is not a usable pairing key either. Closing those 22 needs either row edits or an alias table — and an alias table is the hand-maintained roster the rf2-6tags ruling forbids. Worth a second ruling alongside the 23.

REJECTED VARIANTS, for the record. Restricting the diff to non-optional schema keys gives 13 findings on BOTH the pre-fix and post-fix trees — VACUOUS on the motivating defect, because :contributor and :plan-cause are both {:optional true}. Widening the containment test from the Tags cell to the whole row changes nothing (24/23). Row->schema as the direction cannot catch the defect at all: the pre-fix row was a strict subset of its schema, which a subset check satisfies.

(A) REFUSED AT SOURCE — the premise does not hold. The #7030 audit's claim that the :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch Tags cell still spells :first-diff-path? is FALSE at branch base fd06174823. Commit 0eeab48748 ('name the literal :first-diff-path in the hydration-mismatch Tags cell and empty the Tags-column baseline (rf2-zk1xu)') is an ancestor of main; the cell names the literal key with optionality in prose, and tags-column-shrink-only-baseline is #{} with a paragraph recording this row as its last entry. Positive control: git log -S':first-diff-path?' returns that very commit, so the search could find the string it reports absent. No change made.

(B) IMPLEMENTED. HydrationMismatchTags is now a two-arm :or, one arm per emit tier, with required/optional keys and the category/envelope convention modelled per arm (:category present on the hiccup :error arm, absent on the adoption :warning arm). The hiccup arm also declares the keys the emitter genuinely puts on the wire and the schema omitted: :rf.error/id (payload shared with the :on-mismatch :hard-error throw), :where, :frame, :failing-id, :reason. The 009 row's Tags cell lists them, splits the arms, and DROPS the false :head-id (head) claim - verify-hydration! destructures only :first-diff-path / :failing-id / :server-hash and merges nothing else, so no :head-id can reach this category's payload; the head sub-arm is discriminated by :failing-id alone. #8544's no-:root-id rule, two-envelope explanation and retired-tier wording are preserved.

THE PROOF is over EMITTED EVENTS, not a reverse key diff. A cell -> schema diff is not mechanisable here: the cell states a NEGATIVE as part of its contract ('no :root-id, because a React-element root has none') that a cell-key harvest reads as a listing. So the new deftest drives the SHIPPED emitters - the hiccup tier for real through re-frame.ssr.hydrate/verify-hydration! (ssr is a test-only dep of core), the two .cljs adoption emitters by reading their payload maps out of source as data (each site's own :where symbol included) and driving them through the real trace/emit! - then closes both directions: every wire key is declared by some arm AND named in the cell. The pre-fix single-map schema rides inline as a control that must keep rejecting the real adoption event.

The gate's schema reader now unions a schema's top-level [:map ...] ARMS instead of taking the first found; a first-arm-only reading of a two-arm schema loses half its keys from the diff in silence.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8562 (2026-08-21 AUSEST) — REOPENED ONLY FOR THE BOUNDED `HeadMismatchTags` remainder this issue already identified; the new `HydrationMismatchTags` two-arm model itself is complete, and no duplicate is needed.

But adjacent `HeadMismatchTags` remains canonical-looking schema prose for `:category` / hashes / optional `:head-id` while no catalogue category, emitter, or other spec consumer claims it. At the merged tree, the only `HeadMismatchTags` occurrences are its definition and #8562's new comment saying it is not this category's schema; the “head-model channel of its own” named there has no corresponding contract or producer.

comments.text:
WORKER rf2-zk1xu (PR #8573, draft): the HeadMismatchTags remainder is DISCHARGED by RETIREMENT, and the audit's second option is refused at source with a reason.

THE PREMISE HOLDS, and the history explains it. The row went; the schema did not. So it is orphaned residue of a deleted row, NOT a forward declaration of anything — and #8562's own comment calling it 'a head-model channel of its own' was the misreading the audit caught.

NO PRODUCER CAN BE NAMED, now or after the deferred work. A head mismatch reaches the trace through verify-hydration! — host-attributed today via the generic :failing-id seam, runtime-attributed IF the post-v1 follow-on lands (011 §Mismatch detection — head; 011's deferred table records runtime-side head attribution as :post-v1, an untracked note). That is why 'document the real channel' was not available: documenting it would mean inventing a producer.

THE CHANGE is spec/Spec-Schemas.md only, 20 insertions / 8 deletions. The def is replaced by a RETIRED (rf2-zk1xu) note in this file's established house form (PlainFnUnderNonDefaultFrameOnceTags, DispatchFromAsyncCallbackFellThroughTags), and #8562's now-dangling parenthetical inside HydrationMismatchTags is re-pointed at it. :head-id is NOT put back on :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch; #8562's emitted-shape correction stands untouched.

NO 009 EDIT WAS REQUIRED and none was made — 009 never cited the schema, and its row already says there is no :head-id tag on this category. Census: git grep -F HeadMismatchTags -- :!.beads returned 2 hits before (def + #8562 comment), 1 after (the retirement note naming its own subject). The *Tags corpus goes 111 -> 110; paired-count is unchanged because the retired schema was one of the UNPAIRED ones, so tags-column-paired-floor (93) needed no edit.

GATE FINDING, worth carrying forward. title: skills: six of nine SKILL.md descriptions exceed the Agent Skills 1,024-char description cap — verify runtime truncation and trim so the tail disqualifier survives
description:
CLAIM. The Agent Skills spec caps the frontmatter description at 1,024 characters. Measured at tip: re-frame2-xray 1,712; reagent-migration 1,486; re-frame2 1,243; re-frame2-improver 1,149; re-frame2-pair-retro 1,137; re-frame2-setup 1,062. No repo gate checks it.
IMPACT. If the loader truncates, the clause at the END of each description is what is cut — in xray that tail is the Xray-vs-pair disqualifier the family README treats as the routing rule; in setup it is the greenfield-only disqualifier.
FIX SHAPE. First verify (do not assume) whether Claude Code truncates or refuses; then either trim the six descriptions to the cap with the disqualifier moved to the front, or record in skills/README.md that the cap does not apply and why. Do not add a gate unless truncation is confirmed.

That is a path inside the source checkout: the codemod is not in .github/workflows/release.yml's deploy DAG (a grep for codemod there returns nothing), and its deps.edn puts `../../../implementation/hicasso/src` on `:paths` so the tool and the runtime share ONE slot-rule implementation (rf2-ani6y / rf2-r4j91 — a deliberate design; keep the sharing). docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md records this as gap G2 and says "No bead filed: it is the same root cause as G1 and is expected to move with it". It will NOT move with it: rf2-kmqx3 publishes the Hicasso jar, not the reporter. After the tag, a counted pilot following the public page still cannot run step 1 without a re-frame2 checkout beside its project — which is exactly the contamination the artefact gate exists to remove — or must skip the reporter and lose the "what the migration report said before the port" evidence outcome 2 requires.

THE FIX — the least thing that makes the printed command true without a checkout. Trust the programmer; do NOT build a "released tool" or a second coordinate. Candidates, cheapest first: (1) a one-line `clojure -Sdeps` / `-T` invocation resolving the codemod as a git dep of the tagged release (`:git/tag` + `:git/sha` + `:deps/root "migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod"`), with the shared slot rule reached through the published `io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso` jar rather than the relative `:paths` entry; (2) if the relative entry must stay for the in-repo `identical?` pin (shared_rule_test.clj), an alias that swaps it for the jar when run outside the repo. Whichever is chosen, chapter 20 step 1 prints the exact public command.

ACCEPTANCE. The command printed on the public page runs the reporter against a sample source directory from an EMPTY directory with no re-frame2 checkout anywhere beside it and an isolated Maven cache (`:mvn/local-repo`); chapter 20 updated; pilots/README.md's G2 row transitions to closed under that page's own protocol; the codemod's `clojure -M:test` still green.

GATES. The codemod's `clojure -M:test` (migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod); scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for the docs/core/ page and scripts/check_provenance_pins.py for the pilots README; mkdocs build --strict for chapter 20 (inside docs_dir, not excluded). title: hic: PRE-PILOT rehearsal — both ratified pilots on :local/root from the prep package; NOT §13 evidence
description:
FILED 2026-09-02 by the delegated ruling on rf2-hic-063 (the RULING note of that date on that bead is the authority — read it first). Tip b26c5ad33e. Depends on rf2-xkhul (runnable baselines in the workspace).

(a) Each workspace is built per workspace.md, after rf2-xkhul lands, and the operator's boot check and baseline run pass BEFORE the agent is dispatched. The pilot's gates run in its own workspace only; the pilot opens no PR against this repository and reads nothing under it beyond what the published pages tell it to execute.

title: release: post-publish consumer artefact-install gate in release.yml — cold-repo resolution of io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso (+core, +ssr) after every v* tag
description:
FILED 2026-09-02 10:15 AUSEST by the delegated ruling on rf2-kmqx3 (tip b26c5ad33e). This bead is the REPEATABLE form of rf2-kmqx3's artefact-install proof: a post-publish job in release.yml that resolves the just-published set from Clojars into a cold Maven local repo and compiles a minimal consumer. It publishes nothing and gates nothing irreversible; it observes.

BLOCKED ON rf2-kmqx3, and the block is structural: this job resolves a PUBLISHED artefact, so it cannot be authored, run or exercised before io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso 0.0.1.alpha exists on Clojars and the one-off proof on rf2-kmqx3 has passed. Do not dispatch before rf2-kmqx3 closes. rf2-fo4ng (the 19-coordinate rename) is upstream of rf2-kmqx3 and will have merged by then.

HOT ZONE — .github/workflows/release.yml. One workflow toucher at a time: at dispatch, re-measure `bd list --status=open --limit 0 --desc-contains ".github/workflows"` and sequence behind any live one. At filing time rf2-zq34m, rf2-4a0c and rf2-8arzr named .github/workflows in their descriptions; do not trust that list.

## Deliverable

1. One new job `verify-consumer-install` in .github/workflows/release.yml with `needs: [github-release]` (runs on the same tag run, after the whole publish DAG and the GitHub Release). No deploy job's `needs` changes. No second trigger on release.yml — the v* glob at lines 162-165 stays the only one; the DAG policy test pins that shape.

2. A script .github/scripts/verify-consumer-install.sh (POSIX sh, CI-only, runnable under Git Bash locally) taking VERSION as its argument, so the worker can run it against the already-published 0.0.1.alpha — the exercised half of acceptance, because a tag-only workflow cannot be run on a PR. The job passes `${{ needs.deploy-core.outputs.version }}` (the value the release body at ~926-939 already uses).

3. What the script does, in order:
   a. `mktemp -d` a scratch directory OUTSIDE $GITHUB_WORKSPACE; never read the repo's deps.edn.
   b. Write deps.edn: `{:paths ["src"] :deps {io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:mvn/version "<VERSION>"}} :mvn/local-repo "<fresh empty dir>"}`. Do NOT declare core or ssr — they must arrive transitively through the published pom; that transitivity working is the proof.
   c. `clojure -Srepro -P` with a bounded retry for Clojars propagation lag (e.g. up to ~10 minutes, 30s apart) before failing. `-Srepro` ignores ~/.clojure/deps.edn so no mirror or local-repo override leaks in. Never use an actions/cache-warmed ~/.m2 as the resolution source; the fresh :mvn/local-repo is what makes the gate honest even when a cache action is present.
   d. `clojure -Srepro -Stree` captured to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and asserted: io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso, io.github.day8/re-frame2 and io.github.day8/re-frame2-ssr all present at exactly VERSION, and ZERO old-group `day8/` coordinates anywhere in the tree (an old-group dependency surviving in a pom is the rename campaign's miss, and this is where it shows).
   e. Minimal compile: `npm i react@19.2 react-dom@19.2 shadow-cljs@3.4.10` in the scratch dir (npm, not the repo's node_modules); a shadow-cljs.edn with `:deps true` and one :browser build whose single namespace requires re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso; `npx shadow-cljs compile app` exits 0. This catches a jar that resolves but is missing packed content (hicasso's :src-dirs are ["src" "resources" "test_kit/src"], implementation/hicasso/deps.edn 169-176). Versions per the compatibility matrix in docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md.

4. SCOPE: hicasso is the mandatory entry point because it exercises the deepest transitive chain (core + ssr). Extending to all 14 framework coordinates is RECOMMENDED if it is one loop and the list is DERIVED — from .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh's ARTEFACTS inventory (line 139 at filing) or from the workflow's own matrix — never a hand roster in the new job or script. A roster cannot report what it does not list (the lesson recorded at the top of preflight-tool-package.sh). If the 14-loop is included, the compile step stays hicasso-only; resolution runs per coordinate.

5. Policy test: implementation/scripts/_release-dag-policy.test.cjs asserts exactly 14 publishers (line ~282) and the ordering edges. The new job publishes nothing and must not be discovered as a publisher. Add a negative-control case asserting (i) `verify-consumer-install` is not in the publisher set, (ii) no deploy job lists it in `needs`, (iii) publisher count is still 14.

6. Failure semantics, written as the job's header comment AND as one paragraph in docs/release-process.md (under §Topological deploy DAG or a short new §Post-publish consumer gate): the job is post-publish and can un-publish nothing. Red from propagation lag → re-run the failed job only (`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`); NEVER re-push the tag (deploy-core 409s on the duplicate upload; docs/release-process.md §Recovery). Red from an unresolvable pom or missing packed content → bump-and-supersede per §Recovery (0.0.1.alpha → 0.0.1.alpha-1).

## Acceptance

- release.yml carries the one new job with `needs: [github-release]`; `git diff` shows no change to any deploy job's `needs`, matrix or steps, and no new trigger.
- The DAG policy test passes with the new negative-control case; publisher count 14.
- The script, run locally by the worker from a fresh :mvn/local-repo against the published 0.0.1.alpha, exits 0; its -Stree output is pasted in the PR body and shows the three coordinates at 0.0.1.alpha and no day8/* coordinate.
- The same script against a deliberately absent version (e.g. 9.9.9) exits non-zero after its bounded retry — the gate has teeth.
- No hand-rostered coordinate list beyond the hicasso entry point; if the 14-loop is included it derives from the lockstep inventory or the workflow.
- docs/release-process.md paragraph landed; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py green; verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test green; fast-PR spine green; actionlint if the repo runs it. Gates foreground, to completion, never backgrounded or piped through a filter.
- First real CI exercise is the NEXT v* tag (0.0.1.alpha-1 or 0.0.2.alpha); say so in the PR body rather than claiming the YAML ran.

## Traps

Warm ~/.m2 or a cache action = a green that asked Clojars nothing; Clojars propagation lag after publish is minutes — retry, do not conclude; no yank exists; same-tag re-run 409s; no :local/root, no :git/url, no `clein install` anywhere in the proof (clein install is a pre-tag pom REHEARSAL, never the proof); do not touch the deploy DAG; hot-zone sequencing; the worker is on Windows-capable Git Bash locally but the script targets ubuntu-latest — keep it POSIX sh.

## Provenance

Ruled on rf2-kmqx3 (RULING 2026-09-02, delegated by Mike). The one-off proof that precedes this bead is defined there and on docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md's compatibility matrix; the release DAG facts are release.yml 162-165, 176-902 and docs/release-process.md 15-19, 128-160, 198-225 at tip b26c5ad33e.

title: test(ssr): four more fixtures nest :config so their frames are never platform-tagged
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-umi1w (PR #8934), which fixed the same defect in multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc and deliberately did NOT sweep the rest — a general audit was out of scope there.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): `rf/make-frame` opts are FLAT — `:platform` is a top-level record-config key, per make-frame's own docstring. These four sites pass `{:id fid :config {:platform :client}}`, which nests as `:config {:config {...}}`, so the frames are never platform-tagged at all:

  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc  (lines 89 and 298)
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs  (line 45)
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs  (line 42)

Line numbers are as measured on 2026-09-01 and should be re-derived at tip.

WHY IT MATTERS: harmless TODAY only because the runtime falls back to the host-wide platform marker — `(or (-> rec :config :platform) (interop/active-platform))` — and that marker is already `:client` on CLJS. So each fixture gets the platform it meant by accident, and no assertion in these files discriminates a tagged frame from an untagged one.

THE FIX, mirroring rf2-umi1w: flatten the opts to `{:id fid :platform :client}`, and add ONE assertion per fixture reading the tag back through `rf/frame-meta`. That accessor is `(merge (:config f) (:lifecycle f) {:id (:id f)})` — it flattens the frame's OWN config and does NOT fall back to the host-wide marker, which is what makes it discriminating. Verified on rf2-umi1w: restoring the nesting turns such an assertion red with `actual: (not (= :client nil))`.

NOTE the two `_dom_cljs_test.cljs` files are browser-gated, not covered by the ssr JVM suite or the consolidated node-test — gate them accordingly.

PRECEDENT: machine_after_rearm_cljs_test.cljc and multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc both now use the flat form and carry a docstring warning about the trap.

SURFACE: test-only, implementation/ssr/test/.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8945 (2026-09-02) — REOPENED FOR THE UNGUARDED FOURTH CALL SITE.

The merged code correctly flattens all four `make-frame` opts maps. The new regression proof, however, reaches only three sites: each `the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged` test calls that file's `fresh-frame!` helper. The fourth corrected site is the direct teardown/rebuild call in `failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc` (`rf/make-frame {:id fid :platform :client}` inside `a-root-whose-seed-does-not-land-releases-its-claim`), which bypasses `fresh-frame!` and has no `frame-meta` assertion.

That gap is discriminating, not hypothetical. Returning only this rebuild to `{:config {:platform :client}}` leaves all three new tests green because they exercise the still-flat helpers. The rebuild test then checks only that hydration lands; the PR's own red-before established that the pre-existing behavioral tests pass when the tag is absent because runtime platform lookup falls back to the host marker. Thus the exact silent defect can recur at one of the four audited sites with the whole suite green, contrary to the close note's claim that one gate covers all four.

Completeness: four sites were fixed but only three are guarded. Correctness: the rebuilt frame can again carry `:platform nil` without a failure. Implementation quality: the repeated prose says the rebuilt frame "must carry" the tag, but the executable contract never reads it.

Minimal outcome: immediately assert the rebuilt frame's `rf/frame-meta` platform at that existing call site (or route both constructions through one equally small checked helper). No broader sweep, new fixture, or abstraction is needed.

Duplicate search: `rf2-33lfn` owns this exact four-site SSR fixture sweep, so it is reopened rather than duplicated.
close_reason:
Second pass (audit reopen of PR #8945). Addressed the UNGUARDED FOURTH CALL SITE: the direct teardown/rebuild (rf/make-frame {:id fid :platform :client}) inside a-root-whose-seed-does-not-land-releases-its-claim in failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc, which bypasses fresh-frame! and so was never reached by the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged. PR #8956 adds ONE assertion there reading the tag through rf/frame-meta (merge of :config/:lifecycle/:id — no fallback to the host-wide platform marker, which is what makes it discriminate).

Code premise re-verified at tip: all four opts maps are already flat; two sweeps (line-oriented AND whitespace-collapsed) over implementation/ssr/test/** found no surviving nested {:config {:platform ...}}. So the merged code was correct and only the proof fell short, exactly as the audit stated.

DISCRIMINATING CONTROL (the point of this bead, since a green run proves nothing here): reverting ONLY the fourth site to {:config {:platform :client}} and recompiling reds exactly one assertion -- the new one -- with 'expected: (= :client (:platform (rf/frame-meta fid))) / actual: (not (= :client nil))', while the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged and the other 14 tests stay GREEN. Test/assertion counts identical to the clean run (15 tests / 125 assertions), so the plant was scoped. That single result proves both that the new assertion bites and that the previous pass's proof did not reach this site.

Gates, captured exit codes: consolidated CLJS node-test split into its two phases. compile=0 (1877 files, 0 warnings); focused clean run=0 (15 tests/125 assertions/0 failures); planted control run=1 (1 failure, the new assertion only); full suite after restore=0 (11196 tests/55469 assertions/0 failures). shadow-cljs printed its config path as the worker worktree's own implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Plant reverted and restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object (ce58c88a8c), not by reading a diff. Diff is a pure addition (7 insertions, 0 deletions vs merge base), confined to implementation/ssr/test/**, so nothing from PR #8945 is reverted.

title: ci(testbed-support): the jvm lane installs no node deps, so the real-node launch probes self-skip
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-1i1ec (PR #8932), reported by that worker as an observation it deliberately did not fix.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): CI's `jvm-tools-testbed-support` job runs no `npm ci`, so `launch-editor-installed?` is false and every node-backed block in the suite self-skips. The job reports **42 tests / 229 assertions** where a local run with the dependency present reports **42 / 260**.

WHY IT MATTERS: the exit code cannot distinguish a run from a skip. The suite is green either way, so the real-node launch probes — including the column-only refusal that PR #8932 added precisely because no existing test could reach that path — are exercised only on a developer's machine and never in CI. The 31-assertion delta is the only signal that the block ran at all, and nothing checks it.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: this is a pre-existing property of the lane, not something #8932 introduced, and the remedy is a CI decision rather than a test fix. Two shapes are available and they differ in cost: install the node dependency in that job so the blocks run, or assert the expected assertion count so a silent skip fails loudly. The second is cheap and catches the regression; the first is what actually buys the coverage.

SURFACE: `.github/workflows/` is HOT-ZONE and one-toucher — sequence this against any other workflow work. Adjacent: rf2-ohfym is the sibling observation for the http lane (no solo-namespace ordering), also workflow-touching; consider whether one dispatch should take both.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-01: install the node dependency in the jvm-tools-testbed-support job so the probes actually run. The assertion-count assert is the FALLBACK, not the answer.

The bead states the trade exactly: the count assert is cheap and catches the regression; installing the dependency is what buys the coverage. Take the coverage. PR #8932 added the column-only refusal precisely because no existing test could reach that path - a test written to cover an otherwise-unreachable refusal, which then never runs in CI, is dead weight, and dead weight is what the stance is against. Asserting the count converts silent non-coverage into loud non-coverage; that is an improvement over today but it is a guard on the hole rather than the fix, and it would leave the 31 assertions permanently unexercised outside a developer's machine.

FALLBACK WITH A MEASURABLE DISCRIMINATOR: if arming that job drags the whole implementation dependency tree in for one small package, the cost is disproportionate and the count assert is then correct. Decide it by measuring, not by estimating - check whether the launch-editor dependency can be installed on its own, and report the added wall-clock either way. If you take the fallback, say what you measured and why it crossed the line.

Either way the job must stop being able to report green on a run that skipped every node-backed block. That is the acceptance.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8943 (branch worker/cilanes). Took the RULING'S PRIMARY BRANCH — install the node dependency — not the assertion-count fallback, and decided it by measuring as the ruling required.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both directions, before any edit: tools/testbed-support 'clojure -M:test' with implementation/node_modules absent captured exit 0 at 'Ran 42 tests containing 229 assertions'; with launch-editor present, exit 0 at 42 / 260. The 229-vs-260 claim and the 31-assertion delta hold exactly.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE BRANCH. The fallback was to be taken only if arming the job dragged the whole implementation dependency tree in for one small package. It does not. launch-editor@2.14.1 is a devDependency of implementation/package.json, so it comes from the same lockfile; 'npm ci' there installs 110 packages and fetches NO browsers (nothing in that lockfile carries an install script on Linux — only fsevents, macOS-only; playwright is not flagged hasInstallScript). Locally 10.9s cold-ish and 2.9s warm. On the runner it was better still: the PR's own job shows 'added 110 packages, and audited 111 packages in 2s', and the added wall clock from the run's step timings is 5 SECONDS (setup-node 2s + npm ci 3s) against a 23s whole-job time and a timeout-minutes: 10 budget. Nowhere near disproportionate, so the coverage branch is correct and the count assert is not needed.

CI EVIDENCE ON THE PR HEAD: 'JVM tools/testbed-support (clojure -M:test)' conclusion success, 'Ran 42 tests containing 260 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' — 260, not 229. The launch-editor probes ran in CI for the first time, including the column-only refusal PR #8932 added because no existing test could reach that path.

THE ACCEPTANCE ('the job must stop being able to report green on a run that skipped every node-backed block') NEEDED MORE THAN THE INSTALL. Installing makes the blocks run today but leaves the self-skip in place, so the job could go green on a skip again tomorrow (the step breaking, a package rename, a classifier change). RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES now turns each self-skip into a FAILURE naming the missing prerequisite (skip-or-fail), and the job sets it; a node-less developer box, which sets nothing, still skips exactly as before, and it is one assertion either way so the suite's count does not move with the skip. All four combinations exercised locally with captured exits: deps absent + flag unset = 0 (42/229, developer box preserved); deps present + flag unset = 0 (42/260); deps present + flag set = 0 (42/260, the CI shape); deps ABSENT + flag SET = 1 (42/229, 2 failures naming the prerequisite). That last row is the acceptance.

SURFACE: .github/workflows/test.yml only (hot-zone, one-toucher, sole workflow change in the diff) plus the test namespace. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and its mirror were READ, never edited — rf2-f9f3p's worker holds that pair.

title: test(ssr): multi_root_hydration fixture nests :config so its frames are never platform-tagged
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-jqvgp (PR #8915), reported by that worker as an incidental finding it deliberately did not fix.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): `rf/make-frame` opts are FLAT, but the fixture in `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc` passes `{:id fid :config {:platform :client}}`, which nests as `:config {:config {...}}`. The frames are therefore never platform-tagged at all.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is harmless TODAY only because CLJS defaults to `:client`, so the fixture gets the platform it meant by accident. The defect is that the assertion no longer discriminates — a JVM platform assertion added to this fixture would pass for the wrong reason, and so would a regression that broke platform tagging outright.

MINIMAL COMPLETION: flatten the opts to the shape `make-frame` actually reads, and add one assertion that the constructed frame's platform is what the fixture asked for, so the fixture cannot silently stop tagging again. Do not redesign the fixture or widen into the hydration contract.

SURFACE: test-only, `implementation/ssr/test/`. Gate: ssr JVM `clojure -M:test` plus the CLJS consolidated node-test.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-01 22:10 AUSEST — FIXED and landed in PR #8934 (draft at time of writing), commit 30055a3db5.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP. Verified at source rather than taken from the brief: make-frame's own docstring in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc is explicit that opts are FLAT — 'EVERY OTHER key is RECORD-CONFIG, honoured in the same call: :initial-events ..., :fx-overrides, :platform, :ssr, :doc, :preset, :tags ...'. The nested form was still present at tip on line 71.

WHAT CHANGED (test-only, hydration contract untouched):
  1. fresh-frame! now passes {:id fid :platform :client} instead of {:id fid :config {:platform :client}}, plus a docstring naming the trap.
  2. A new one-assertion deftest, the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged, reads the tag back through rf/frame-meta.

WHY frame-meta IS THE DISCRIMINATING ACCESSOR — this is the part worth keeping. frame-meta is (merge (:config f) (:lifecycle f) {:id (:id f)}): it flattens the frame's OWN config and performs NO platform defaulting. The RUNTIME path is different — fx/platform-for-frame-record is (or (-> rec :config :platform) (interop/active-platform)) — and that fallback to the host-wide marker is precisely why the defect was invisible: on CLJS the marker is already :client, so every hydration test passed either way. Asserting through frame-meta reads what the fixture ASKED FOR rather than what the runtime resolves, which is what makes the assertion bite.

CONTROL — THE PLANT DISCRIMINATED (this was the specified stop-and-report risk, and it did not materialise). Restoring the nested :config with the fix's assertion in place: captured exit 1, exactly ONE failure — the new test — reporting 'actual: (not (= :client nil))'. The platform read as nil, which is the 'never platform-tagged at all' claim demonstrated directly rather than argued. Test/assertion totals were identical to the clean run (608 tests / 2965 assertions at that point), so the plant crashed no namespace. Restored and verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (line endings are translated in this checkout, so a byte digest of the working file is not sound); RESTORE: MATCH.

POSITIVE EVIDENCE THE CLJS RUNTIME SAW THE CHANGE, not just the source: out/node-test.js is only the 156K loader, so a zero count there means nothing. The compiled per-namespace file .shadow-cljs/builds/node-test/dev/out/cljs-runtime/re_frame.ssr.multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.js contains the_fixture_frames_are_actually_platform_tagged (8 occurrences) and frame_meta (3). Confirmed independently by shadow-cljs.edn: 'ssr/test' is on the :node-test classpath and :ns-regexp is 'cljs-test$', which this namespace matches.

GATES, all on the final rebased base cdb9652c0f, exit codes captured on one command line and quoted from the captured file:
  ssr JVM clojure -M:test        exit 0   610 tests / 2991 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  CLJS node-test compile         exit 0   1874 files, 0 warnings
  CLJS node-test run             exit 0   11150 tests / 55135 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  (core exit 0 and machines exit 0 also re-run green on the same base)
The CLJS lane prints its config path and it named this worker's worktree — the worktree check for that gate.

PRECEDENT ALIGNED: machine_after_rearm_cljs_test.cljc had already been corrected the same way by rf2-jqvgp (the same PR that reported this finding) and carries the same docstring warning. This fixture now matches it.

INCIDENTAL, NOT SWEPT (a general audit was out of scope): the identical nesting is live at four more sites — failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc lines 89 and 298, failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs line 45, and multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs line 42 (the DOM sibling of this very fixture). Filed as rf2-33lfn with the fix recipe and the frame-meta rationale.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8934 (commit 30055a3db5). Premise held at tip: make-frame opts are flat and the nesting was still present. fresh-frame! now passes {:id fid :platform :client}, plus one assertion reading the tag back through rf/frame-meta, which does no platform defaulting and so discriminates where the hydration tests cannot. The control bit decisively: restoring the nesting turned that assertion red alone with 'actual: (not (= :client nil))'. ssr JVM 610/2991 exit 0; CLJS node-test 11150/55135 exit 0. Four more sites carrying the same nesting filed as rf2-33lfn.

title: ci(pair fixture): three local roots do not arm the shipped-preload test
description:
## Scope

Complete the reverse dependency into the existing `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure` CI job. Keep the current fixture, workflow, and changed-surface vocabulary; this is classifier reachability only.

## Merged-PR audit finding (#8903)

PR #8903 correctly adds the four local-root reverse edges for the MIG-23 fixture. Because both fixture jobs are gated solely on `skills_structural`, that dispatch incidentally fixes the Pair fixture for the two roots they share, core and the stock Reagent adapter. The Pair fixture has three additional direct `:local/root` inputs that remain unarmed: epoch, schemas, and machines.

`skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/deps.edn` directly resolves all five in-repo artefacts because the shipped preload requires their public surfaces. At #8903, production classifier probes report `skills_structural=false` for both `src/*` and `deps.edn` under:

- `implementation/epoch`
- `implementation/schemas`
- `implementation/machines`

The `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure` job is therefore accepted as skipped on a change to three fifths of its in-repo classpath. Epoch happens to arm a different MCP-live gate, but schemas and machines arm neither Pair fixture; none of those substitutions makes this job's shipped-preload compile and pure-function contract run.

## Three lenses

Completeness: the new reverse-edge comment and mirror enumerate only the MIG-23 roots, while the incidental Pair claim stops after the two shared roots and leaves the rest of that fixture's declared local-root roster uncovered.

Correctness: an owned-namespace API or behavior change in schemas/machines/epoch can break `re_frame2_pair.pure` or its runtime preload while the one job that compiles/tests that shipped source is skipped; a skipped required job is an accepted result.

Implementation quality / narrow direction: extend the existing `skills_structural` reverse-edge shape to the remaining Pair local roots at `src/*` plus `deps.edn`, accepting the same small over-fire trade #8903 already chose for ssr/hicasso. Do not add a workflow, fixture, generic dependency engine, or a 29th output.

## Duplicate search

All-status searches covered pair fixture, shipped-preload pure, reverse edge, local root, `skills_structural`, epoch, schemas, and machines. No exact owner exists. `rf2-bbe91` owns the MIG-23 fixture's four roots and is correctly closed; this is its sibling Pair fixture rather than unfinished MIG-23 work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Changes under `src/*` or `deps.edn` for all five Pair fixture local roots (core, Reagent adapter, epoch, schemas, machines) schedule `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure`; the two already-covered roots remain covered.
- Mirror tests pin the complete five-root positive roster from tracked paths, at least one unrelated negative, and preservation of each artefact's existing outputs.
- The existing changed-surfaces suite and `npm run test:pure` fixture pass; a focused control proves one remaining local-root edit can break the fixture and is now scheduled.
- No new job, fixture, output, or dependency-graph mechanism.
close_reason:
PR #8941 (open, ready for review). Premise VERIFIED at tip before any change, via the production classifier, with same-shape positive controls beside the negatives.

THE THREE PROBES (both entry shapes each, all six false):
  implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc        skills_structural=false
  implementation/epoch/deps.edn                       skills_structural=false
  implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc    skills_structural=false
  implementation/schemas/deps.edn                     skills_structural=false
  implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc  skills_structural=false
  implementation/machines/deps.edn                    skills_structural=false

POSITIVE CONTROLS (the instrument was exercised against inputs it should flag, at BOTH shapes, because a classifier that never understood the question answers false in the same voice as one that considered the path and said no):
  implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs                skills_structural=true
  implementation/core/deps.edn                                         skills_structural=true
  implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs    skills_structural=true
  implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn                             skills_structural=true
  skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/deps.edn                         skills_structural=true
  negative control: README.md                                          skills_structural=false

CHANGE: extended the existing rf2-bbe91 reverse-edge dispatch in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh to the UNION of both fixtures' classpaths (added epoch, schemas, machines at src/* plus deps.edn). One dispatch rather than a second case beside it: the two fixtures gate the identical output, so two rosters setting one variable is a distinction with no behavioural difference. No new job, fixture, output or dependency-graph mechanism.

AFTER: all ten Pair roots arm; every prior output preserved (epoch keeps mcp_conformance/mcp_live, schemas keeps template_expensive, machines keeps tools_jvm_machines_viz/tools_cljs_machines_viz/playground).

MIRROR moved in the SAME COMMIT, and had to: it pinned implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc as a NEGATIVE under the MIG-23 roster and that path is now a POSITIVE under the Pair one. Added the ten-path five-root positive roster (all paths checked with git ls-files, not transcribed), three per-artefact non-narrowing tests, a job-gating pin for re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure, and widened the negative half to five paths covering both fixtures (schemas/test and epoch/test now pin the src+deps.edn scope from the side the new arms could most plausibly over-reach).

GATE: implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs run directly with node on the final rebased base — captured exit 0, 330 tests passed. Tree-read proof by planted fault: breaking the machines arm produced captured exit 1 with exactly one failure naming the planted edge, in a test that exists only on this branch. Restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object.

SCOPE NOTE for the mayor: re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure's cache key in .github/workflows/test.yml hashes only three of the fixture's five deps.edn files (core, reagent, epoch — not schemas or machines), so a schemas/machines dependency bump restores a stale classpath cache. Out of this bead's fence and in a file another worker holds; flagged, not touched.

title: core_machines.cljc emits :where (quote rf/reg-machine*) for a var that is :facade? false
description:
Surfaced by rf2-lzrza (PR #8912) while correcting source-file prose, and deliberately NOT changed there because it is an error-payload behaviour change rather than a prose fix.

implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc lines 137 and 139:

  (reg-machine-impl (quote rf/reg-machine*) machine-id machine)

The :where symbol names the re-frame.core facade spelling. But reg-machine* is :facade? false in spec/api-manifest.edn and is NOT a facade export - core.cljc line 391 says so explicitly (front-porch shrink, rf2-wad2fl): reach it through re-frame.machines/reg-machine*. So an error raised from this path tells the programmer to look at a var that is not on the namespace the message names.

The docstring at line 146 describes this faithfully and was left intact by PR #8912 for exactly that reason - it is TRUE about what the code emits. Line 149, which was caller GUIDANCE rather than a description of behaviour, was corrected to rf.machines/reg-machine*.

The sibling reg-machine (lines 157/159) emits (quote rf/reg-machine), which IS correct - that macro is a real facade export.

Decide whether the :where symbol should become rf.machines/reg-machine*. If it changes, the docstring at line 146 changes with it in the same commit.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-01 20:47 AUSEST — YES, CHANGE IT to rf.machines/reg-machine*.

The :where symbol exists to tell a programmer where to look. reg-machine* is :facade? false in spec/api-manifest.edn and core.cljc states outright that it is not a facade export (front-porch shrink, rf2-wad2fl), so an error raised from this path currently names a var that does not exist on the namespace the message implies. That is a worse failure than an unhelpful message: it sends the reader to a namespace, they find nothing, and the natural conclusion is that their build is broken rather than that the message is wrong. Naming the reachable spelling costs nothing and the pre-alpha posture has no back-compat claim on an error payload.

SCOPE: lines 137 and 139 of implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc, and the line 146 docstring in the SAME commit — that docstring is currently TRUE about what the code emits, which is exactly why PR #8912 left it alone, so it becomes false the moment the emission changes. Line 149 was already corrected by #8912 and needs nothing.

DO NOT TOUCH the sibling reg-machine at lines 157/159: it emits (quote rf/reg-machine) and that IS correct, because reg-machine is a real facade export. Changing it would introduce the defect this bead is closing.

CHECK FOR TEST PINS before editing: any test asserting the error payload's :where will pin the old symbol and must move in the same commit. Search for the literal both line-oriented and flattened.

NOT WANTED: a general audit of every :where symbol in the tree, a lint rule tying :where symbols to the facade manifest, or any change to the error's shape.
VERDICT 2026-09-01 22:11 AUSEST — RULING IMPLEMENTED as written. PR #8934 (draft at time of writing), commit 3c8541797b.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP, verified at source: spec/api-manifest.edn carries {:namespace "re-frame.machines", :var "reg-machine*", :tier :advanced, :kind :fn, :owner "005", :status "v1", :facade? false, ...}, and the sibling is {:namespace "re-frame.core", :var "reg-machine", :kind :macro, ..., :facade? true, ...}. So the ruling's two halves are both grounded: reg-machine* is not reachable as rf/reg-machine*, and reg-machine genuinely is rf/reg-machine.

LINE NUMBERS RE-DERIVED AT TIP rather than trusted (PR #8912 had moved lines in this file): emissions at 137 and 139, docstring at 144-146, sibling at 157/159 — all five matched the ruling exactly. After the edit the docstring block grows from 3 lines to 5, so the UNTOUCHED sibling now sits at 159/161. Line 149 was already rf.machines/reg-machine* from #8912 and needed nothing, as the ruling said.

WHAT CHANGED: lines 137/139 now emit 'rf.machines/reg-machine*, and the 144-146 docstring moved with them in the SAME commit — it had described the old emission truthfully, which is why #8912 left it alone, so it would have gone false the instant the emission changed. The sibling reg-machine at 159/161 still emits 'rf/reg-machine, untouched.

TEST PINS: NONE existed, so nothing had to move. Searched for the literal both ways as instructed. Line-oriented found 3 sites, whitespace-flattened found 4 — the discrepancy is line 146 carrying two occurrences, reconciled by counting occurrences per line rather than counting lines, not a line-broken pin. The control term 'rf/reg-machine' returned 1440 line hits / 1443 flattened, so the search was live rather than silently matching nothing. All hits were in core_machines.cljc itself; no test anywhere pins this symbol. The two :where pins that DO exist are on the sibling — machines/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:75-76 and machine_pure_error_contract_test.clj:389 — and late_bind_missing_test.clj:24 states in prose that it covers reg-machine only.

CONTROLS — TWO, because the specified one cannot bite, and the reason is itself the finding. Reverting the symbol on line 137 and re-running the machines suite came back GREEN (captured exit 0, 1220 tests / 4289 assertions, 0 failures). That is not a broken control: it is the measured explanation for how this defect survived, and it agrees exactly with the pin search above.

Because a green run proves nothing about WHICH TREE the gate read, a second and COVERED fault was planted at a line adjacent to the edit — the sibling's 'rf/reg-machine replaced with 'rf/BOGUS-SENTINEL-UUQEK. title: spec/005-StateMachines.md:4100 is the last bare :as machines call spelling in the corpus (residue of rf2-qt7au)
description:
rf2-qt7au (PR #8912) moved every published bare machines/<helper> call spelling to the canonical rf.machines/ alias that Conventions section Require-alias dialect makes normative - 18 sites across six documents. One site was out of that dispatch fence and remains:

  spec/005-StateMachines.md line 4100:  (machines/machine-transition definition snapshot event)

It sits inside a clojure code fence with NO require beside it, so a reader copying the fence gets an alias that is never introduced. PR #8905 corrected the rf/-prefixed spellings in that file and did not touch bare-alias ones, which is why it survived both passes.

This is the LAST of the class: a census over every tracked markdown file under docs/, spec/, migration/ and skills/ at PR #8912 tip returns exactly this one hit and nothing else.

One line. Needs a dispatch that is allowed to touch spec/005-StateMachines.md.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-ur6kh) -- PR #8916, one line in spec/005-StateMachines.md.

THE FIX. Line 4100 now reads (rf.machines/machine-transition definition snapshot
event) instead of the bare-alias spelling. That is the whole diff: one file, one
insertion, one deletion, confirmed by a three-dot diff against the merge base
before push, which showed nothing else and in particular nothing reverted.

NO REQUIRE CLAUSE ADDED, AND THE REASON CORRECTS THE DESCRIPTION. The description
reads the site as a fence "with no require beside it, so a reader copying the
fence gets an alias that is never introduced". That is right about the defect and
is why the bare spelling had to go, but it is not right that the document leaves
the canonical alias uninstroduced. spec/005-StateMachines.md line 3932 already
introduces it once for the whole file: it tells the reader to require it under
the conventional dotted alias re-frame.machines :as rf.machines, cites Conventions
Require-alias dialect, and says in terms that the rf.machines/ spellings BELOW
assume exactly that alias. The corrected line is 168 lines below that sentence, so
it is covered verbatim. Two further facts point the same way: 44 other rf.machines/
call spellings already live in this file (PR #8905's work) and not one carries a
local require, line 3932 being the file's single deliberate introduction; and the
sibling Level 2 fence eleven lines below already spells
rf.machines/make-machine-handler bare of any require. A require here alone would
have contradicted the document's own design. So: rename only.

CENSUS, RE-DERIVED. Class = the bare alias token machines qualifying a PUBLISHED
re-frame.machines helper. The 23-name helper roster was DERIVED from the
"### re-frame.machines/<name>" headings of docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, not
hardcoded. Scope: all 974 tracked markdown files, wider than the description's
docs/ spec/ migration/ skills/. Total and per-file rows come from ONE command.

  BEFORE  24 hits in 7 files:
    14  docs/api/re-frame.machines.md
     4  docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md
     2  docs/machines/tutorial.md
     1  docs/machines/concepts.md
     1  spec/008-Testing.md
     1  spec/Construction-Prompts.md
     1  spec/005-StateMachines.md   <- this PR
  AFTER   23 hits in 6 files; the 005 row is gone, every other row unchanged.

"LAST OF THE CLASS" -- CORRECT BUT CONDITIONAL, AND NOT YET TRUE OF MAIN. 23 of
those 24 are PR #8912's fence, and PR #8912 has NOT merged: state OPEN, head
c50fb15a86, on branch worker/machnames-lzrza. The description's census was taken
at #8912's tip, so the claim holds conditional on #8912 landing; on main today the
class is 24 sites, not one. This PR touches only the site outside that fence, so
the two do not conflict, and #8912 remains the PR that actually closes the class.
That is the one premise of the brief that did not hold as stated.

THE TWO CENSUS TRAPS, HANDLED. (1) Keyword form excluded deliberately: a
fixed-string search for machines/ also matches the leading-colon keyword spelling
of the same name, so a leading colon sits in the negative lookbehind character
class, dropping 27 keyword occurrences that are not call sites; the same lookbehind
(dot and hyphen) also excludes rf.machines/, re-frame.machines/ and
day8.re-frame2-machines/. (2) The census ran TWICE, line-oriented and
whitespace-spanning, the latter tolerating whitespace including newlines inside the
machines / helper token, because a line-oriented search cannot see a target broken
across two lines and a matched control is invisible identically. Both passes
returned 24 before and 23 after, with an empty delta in both directions. A broad
tier over bare machines/<anything> returned 76 with every off-roster token listed
so nothing was dropped silently; the extra 53 are file paths, MCP op names and
prose slashes, none of them alias call spellings. Non-vacuity control: the
canonical rf.machines/ spelling occurs 112 times across tracked markdown, 44 of
them in this file. That control was itself caught vacuous on first measurement --
an empty Python negative lookbehind always fails, so it read 0 even after the fix
added one -- diagnosed, fixed and re-measured before being quoted.

OUT OF SCOPE, DELIBERATELY. Live :as machines require aliases in implementation/
and tools/ SOURCE are untouched, consistent with rf2-qt7au: a compile surface
across roughly 124 files, and rf2-qt7au left open whether Conventions should

GATE. spec is in scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DEFAULT_ROOTS, verified at source
rather than by job name; that is the gate. Run to completion with the exit code

BY GIT BLOB HASH against the committed object (78457e35d2, match) rather than by

NO GATE COVERED THE FENCED EDIT, STATED PLAINLY. Neither documentation gate reads

both the alias line 3932 introduces and the 44 other call sites in this file.

NOTHING ELSE FILED. No other defect was found in the fence or its section that
would warrant a follow-up bead.

title: [uix] adapter/wrap-view is also consulted at registration, so a pre-init registration misses the substrate wrap
description:
## Scope

The :adapter/wrap-view (rf2-00li) consultation in views/apply-adapter-wrap-view, on the same registration pipeline rf2-oz7wr fixed one layer above.

## Finding

Found while fixing rf2-oz7wr and deliberately left out of that PR (#8909) rather than widening it.

:adapter/wrap-view is published through substrate-adapter/route-hook!, so like :adapter/componentize-view it answers only while ITS adapter is the rf/init!-installed one. views/apply-adapter-wrap-view consults it at REGISTRATION. Under the canonical boot order in docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md the registration namespaces load first and run calls rf/init! afterwards, so under UIx a top-level reg-view* gets nil back, wrap-applied? is false, and build-frame-aware-view falls through to the inline hiccup walk (source-coord/inject-source-coord-attr).

That walk exists for Reagent hiccup. On UIx the render-fn output is a React element, which is precisely why the UIx adapter publishes wrap-view at all — its own cloneElement path. The docstring on apply-adapter-wrap-view says the inline walk mis-classifies such a root and skips annotation.

## Severity, and why it is P3 rather than P2

Dev-only degradation, not a mount failure: the affected surface is the data-rf2-source-coord attribute (click-to-source in Xray and re-frame2-pair), which is elided from production builds anyway. Nothing throws and nothing renders wrongly. Contrast rf2-oz7wr, where the same routing/ordering mismatch made the advertised mount impossible.

## Suggested repair

rf2-oz7wr's fix moved the componentize step to lookup and memoized it on (wrapper identity x adapter spec) in views/view-head. wrap-view cannot simply move there — it is composed BELOW the frame-aware wrapper, so re-deriving it means rebuilding the wrapper, which changes the wrapper's object identity and therefore the cached head's. That is workable (re-derive the whole pipeline from the original render-fn, keyed the same way) but it is a bigger change than rf2-oz7wr's, and it needs its own check on what depends on wrapper identity across a re-derivation.

## Verification

Confirm before building: plant a top-level reg-view* under UIx, mount it, and read the rendered root for data-rf2-source-coord. Assert the attribute is ABSENT pre-fix and PRESENT post-fix, in a browser row (the annotation is a real-DOM fact).
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8919)

Dev-only classification: HOLDS at source, but the extent is wider than the description states. The spine's wrap-view body sits entirely inside (if interop/debug-enabled? ... user-fn), so :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false collapses it to the bare user-fn either way -- nothing throws, nothing renders wrongly, no production behaviour differs. P3 is right. But declining the wrap costs FOUR things, not one:
  1. data-rf2-source-coord -- the annotation the description names.
  2. data-rf-view -- Spec 006 view tagging contract, the view-hierarchy fallback when Fiber inspection is unavailable.
  3. the React-hook unmount sentinel (rf2-te71r), so :rf.view/unmounted never fires for that view. interop/make-reaction returns nil on a React-hook substrate, so the phase-A reaction-dispose hook cannot cover for it.
  4. a one-shot console.warn asserting the root element is not a DOM root -- about a view whose root is an ordinary span. The only one of the four that is actively misleading rather than merely missing.

Mechanism: REUSED #8909's lookup-time mechanism rather than building a second one, by generalising it. The description is right that wrap-view cannot simply move to view-head as-is: it composes BELOW the frame-aware wrapper where the shell composes ABOVE it, so re-deriving the wrap means rebuilding the wrapper, and rebuilding the wrapper means re-deriving the shell. That is an argument for ONE derivation, not for a parallel one. compose-view runs apply-adapter-wrap-view, view-coord-attr, build-frame-aware-view and apply-adapter-componentize-view against the adapter installed at call time; reg-view* runs it once to seed, view-head re-runs it when the seed was taken against a different substrate.

Two consequences the description's what-depends-on-wrapper-identity question asked for:
  - The cache key moved. #8909 matched the slot's handler-fn against either face of the entry (wrapper or head) because its re-derivation KEPT the wrapper object. This one rebuilds it, which would fail that check on every lookup and mint a fresh component type each render. The entry now records :registered, the exact object registration stored in the slot, and matches identity against that. One key instead of two faces.
  - Reagent keeps its object. A re-derivation whose wrap answer was nil before and is nil now has identical inputs to build-frame-aware-view, so it reuses the previous wrapper outright. Reagent publishes neither hook, so it takes that branch in every ordering and (rf/view id) hands back the very object registration built. Reagent behaviour unchanged; the Reagent adapter was not touched.
The registrar slot is still not rewritten on the lazy upgrade -- registrar/register! emits :rf.registry/handler-replaced on every call, and a phantom hot-reload on the first lookup after boot would be worse than the bug.

Evidence: new browser file implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs, three rows, asserting on the OUTPUT. reg-time-composition-is-unwrapped-while-the-lookup-is-not is the ABSENT half on the same registration (registration runs at ns-load with no adapter, premise asserted; the value registration stored is still readable and invoking it directly yields a root with NO data-rf2-source-coord, while the head (rf/view id) hands back post-init yields an annotated one). boot-order-registration-annotates-the-mounted-root is the PRESENT half as a real-DOM fact -- mounted through the documented route and read back off the committed node with getAttribute, plus a console check that the false non-DOM-root warning is gone. post-init-control-annotates-the-mounted-root is the non-vacuity control.

Gates, captured exit codes, on the rebased base: node-test compile 0 (1870 files, 0 warnings); node out/node-test.js 0 (11129 tests / 54979 assertions, 0 failures); shadow-cljs compile browser-test 0 (1012 files, 0 warnings); serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs 0 (760 tests / 4168 assertions, 0 failures); clojure -M:test -n re-frame.late-bind-drift-test 0 (8 tests / 686 assertions). No markdown changed, so neither check_doc_slugs.py nor check_readme_links.py has a surface here.

Controls, both red: (a) planting the pre-fix behaviour -- always reuse the reg-time wrapper, which is #8909's shape -- gave exit 1, 5 failures, ALL in the two boot-order rows, with both attributes nil off the committed node and the false warning back verbatim naming a span root; the post-init control and every #8909 row stayed green. (b) restoring #8909's own defect under the new structure gave exit 1, 11 failures and 1 error, with boot-order-registration-yields-a-mountable-head-after-init contributing 9 -- the same count #8909's own plant produced, so this change has not defanged it. Both plants recompiled 314 files; both restores verified by git blob hash against the committed object.

Two stale prose spots found and deliberately LEFT (both outside the fence, neither load-bearing for any assertion): implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/view_alias_registry_cljs_test.cljs says core consults :adapter/wrap-view AT REGISTRATION TIME, now registration-and-lookup; and the late-bind directory lists re-frame.hicasso.substrate as a :adapter/wrap-view producer, which is true only transitively (hicasso reaches it through spine/make-react-adapter, not by its own route-hook! call).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8919. compose-view now runs the WHOLE registration pipeline against the adapter installed at call time; reg-view* seeds it, views/view-head re-runs it when the seed was taken against a different substrate, and memoizes. One derivation serves both routed hooks rather than a second parallel mechanism.

title: implementation/machines: line-broken rf/machine-by-system-id survived the prefix sweep
description:
Residue deliberately left out of scope by rf2-wrzfb (PR #8905), which corrected the
105 in-scope markdown sites. Census instrument and full breakdown are on that PR.

Three separate remainders, all measured at the same tip:

1. FIFTY-NINE hits inside SOURCE-FILE docstrings, comments and test-name strings
   (implementation/**, tools/**, and skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/**.cljs).
   Every one was inspected during rf2-wrzfb: they are all prose, never a live
   call -- the calls themselves already use the machines/... alias and compile.
   Touching source files is a gate-bearing change (check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py
   guards the skills preload), so it was left rather than bundled into a
   documentation PR. Note these files use the BARE leaf alias :as machines,
   which Conventions reserves for APPLICATION namespaces -- so a proper pass here
   is an alias question as well as a prefix one.

2. migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md section O-9 was MISSED by PR #8902.
   That PR corrected lines 1356 and 2335 to rf.machines/, but O-9 still teaches
   (rf/machine-by-system-id sid) at three sites (approx lines 2944, 2948, 2950).
   Worse, the same section teaches (rf/dispatch-to-system sid event) -- and there
   is NO dispatch-to-system var in spec/api-manifest.edn under any namespace.
   Only dispatch-to-system-fx exists (row 217, :facade? false). So that call
   resolves under no prefix at all. The action-side surface is the reserved
   [:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system [system-id event]] fx tuple.
   Out of rf2-wrzfb's fence because PR #8902 had just landed in that file.

3. spec/Conventions.md carries two sites -- line 517 ((rf/machines) in the
   reserved-metadata-keys table) and line 612 (rf/machine-by-system-id prose in
   the reserved runtime-db slot table). Out of rf2-wrzfb's fence for the same
   reason: Conventions was the authority it followed, not a file it edited.

SEPARATELY, one shape contradiction found in passing and NOT fixed, because
resolving it needs a ruling rather than a spelling change:
tools/xray/spec/API.md line 454 documents (machines) as 0-ary returning a SEQ of
machine-ids, while line 873 of the same file describes the get-machine-list MCP
tool source as a MAP keyed by machine-id. The implementation settles the fn --
re-frame.machines/machines returns a vector (machines.cljc line 174), and the
pair runtime's machines-list wraps it in vec -- so line 873 is either describing
an xray-side projection or is simply wrong. rf2-wrzfb corrected the prefix on
both lines and left the shape claim untouched.
acceptance_criteria: The query-API comment names rf.machines/machine-by-system-id; a whitespace-spanning census that handles Clojure comment leaders finds no unintended rf/-prefixed machines-helper references, while preserving the deliberate fixture/emitted-symbol exclusions.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8912: reopened after completeness/correctness review. implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc still describes the third query helper as (rf/machine-by- on one comment line and system-id sid) on the next. That is the same non-facade rf/machine-by-system-id spelling this Bead owned, split by a Clojure comment leader. It survives at the merged PR head and on current main even though the PR says all 56 intended source-prose sites were corrected and says its whitespace-spanning census found no extra sites. The nearby machines and machine-meta references were corrected, making the leftover especially misleading. Minimal fix: spell the split reference rf.machines/machine-by-system-id and re-run the class census with comment leaders/newlines represented so the three documented deliberate exclusions remain the only old-prefix hits; no new checker or API work is needed.
VERDICT rf2-lzrza (PR #8939) — CONFIRMED and FIXED. Both deliverables landed.

SITE, re-derived at tip (line numbers drift; these were read, not carried over).
implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc lines 168-169 before the fix:

  ;; id)` returns the registered machine's spec map; `(rf/machine-by-
  ;; system-id sid)` resolves the spawned-machine id currently bound to

Literal on disk: `rf/machine-by-` + newline + `;; ` + `system-id`. No
line-oriented search can see it at all — not with a better pattern, because a
line is the wrong unit.

WHY IT WAS WRONG, not merely non-canonical. spec/api-manifest.edn row 220 carries
machine-by-system-id on re-frame.machines with :facade? false, and re-frame.core
re-exports no such var. Its two siblings in the same paragraph had already been
corrected, so a reader met three references to one namespace with one of them
naming a namespace the var is not on.

FIX. Reflowed the query-API comment block so all three references read
`rf.machines/...` and none is split at a line boundary. `(rf.machines/machine-meta
id)` was already spelled correctly but was broken at the same kind of boundary —
that is the blind spot rather than the error, and leaving it split would leave the
next census the same hole. Comment-only; no API, behaviour or code change.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT (the real deliverable). Two passes, because neither result is a
superset of the other. LINE: each physical line on its own (what ripgrep sees).
FLAT: per file, each line's comment leader stripped (`;` `//` `#` `*` `>`, applied
repeatedly so `> ;; ` nests), lines joined with a single space, pattern tolerant of
whitespace at the `/` and at EVERY hyphen.

That last clause is the whole point, and it is where the pre-dispatch attempt went
wrong: stripping the leader and joining still leaves a SPACE between `by-` and
`system-id`, so a flattened search for the fixed literal still reports a clean
zero. The pattern is therefore built from the var name with \s*-\s* at each hyphen
rather than as a fixed string. Line-end hyphen, break at the `/`, and break at a
non-final hyphen are all covered. Class = the 23 vars read from
spec/api-manifest.edn at the tip being censused, not a hardcoded list.

TWO INSTRUMENT FAULTS, both caught by the control rather than by inspection:
(1) the first draft's character class ended `...'-` and then had `:/` appended,
turning `'-:` into a RANGE (0x27-0x3A) covering `(`, `)`, `,` and every digit — so
`(rf/machines)` was excluded by its own opening paren and the census read a clean
zero, with the control reading zero too. That zero-control is the only reason it
was caught, and it is a direct instance of the brief's own warning.
(2) the report CRASHED mid-listing on a non-cp1252 character, truncating output and
under-reporting while exiting non-zero into a log nobody re-reads.

CONTROL FIXTURE (outside the repo, never committed): six positive shapes, four
negatives. Reads LINE 2 / FLAT 6 both before and after; all four negatives
correctly rejected (`:rf/machine?` reserved metadata key, `[:rf.runtime/machines
...]`, the already-canonical spelling, `rf/machines-and-more`). Four of the six
positives are visible ONLY to the flattened pass.

BEFORE / AFTER, whole tree:
  LINE-oriented   before 3   after 3
  FLAT            before 4   after 3
  seen only by FLAT   before: machines.cljc machine-by-system-id   after: none
The single flat-only hit is exactly the target site. After the fix both passes
agree at 3, and those 3 are the deliberate exclusions.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS — re-derived independently, DELTA FROM THE BRIEF'S LIST IS
ZERO. All three read, not assumed:
  1. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/re_frame/api_manifest/doc_api_check_test.clj:44
     live fixture in `live-manifest-var-resolves-anywhere`, asserting
     doc-api-check's cross-namespace bare-name latitude.
  2. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/doc_guide_check.clj:94
     the comment explaining that latitude and why docs/core/api/** is excluded.
  3. implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc:146
     prose describing the literal :where symbol the code really emits
     ('rf/reg-machine*, emitted at lines 137/139). HELD by rf2-uuqek — read, not
     edited. If uuqek changes that emitted symbol the hit count drops to 2; the
     exclusion is correct either way.

LOOSE-BOUNDARY VARIANT, run to prove nothing hides behind the `:` and `'`
exclusions: 71 flat hits, essentially all `:rf/machines` / `:rf/machine-meta`
KEYWORD forms (reserved app-db slots and metadata keys), plus one line-broken
`[:rf/machines :login/flow :data :attempts]` app-db path in
tools/story/test/story_browser_scenarios.cjs:1158-1159. None is a var reference,
so the strict boundary is classifying rather than hiding work. No follow-up bead.

GATES (captured exit codes, redirect + echo $? on one command line — never a
harness report):
  clojure -M:test (implementation/machines), final base ..... 1233 tests /
      4379 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors ................. exit 0
  same, SABOTAGE ........... 1 failure, same 1233/4379 (bounded) ... exit 1
  clj-kondo --lint on the changed file, final base ... 0 errors/0 warnings . exit 0
  same, SABOTAGE ........... Unresolved symbol .................... exit 2
  census control fixture, final base ... LINE 2 / FLAT 6 .......... exit 0
  census whole tree, final base ........ LINE 3 / FLAT 3 .......... exit 0

WORKTREE-READ PROOF: planted fault. Neither gate prints its root, so the proof is
the red — the fault existed only in this checkout, so a run that had wandered into
a sibling's would have come back green. Both restores verified by GIT BLOB HASH
against the committed object (identical before and after), not by reading a diff.
The plant used a mid-line anchor whose match count was read as exactly 1 before
each run, so a CRLF-translated line ending could not silently no-op it.

GATES CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT NOMINATED. doc-api-check and doc-guide-check DO
NOT cover this file: both resolve only *.md (markdown-files /
require-markdown-files) and neither ever opens a .clj/.cljc/.cljs source file.
Worth recording because two of the three deliberate exclusions live inside those
very checkers, which makes it look as though they read this class of reference —

title: docs(api/machines): canonical API doc teaches the bare :as machines alias Conventions reserves for application namespaces
description:

  A **bare** leaf alias (:as routing, :as machines, :as schemas) is
  **reserved for application namespaces**.

It names :as machines specifically as the form the framework yields to apps.

The published API doc teaches the opposite. docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:7

different code, and the API doc's form is the one Conventions reserves for the
app's own myapp.machines.

Conventions' dialect rule is the standard and the docs plus (over time) the
