change — and merged GREEN at 88/88 with every check terminal. The suite did not contradict the
script. Verified just now: gh pr view 8664 reports state=MERGED, files=1.

WHY THE UNIVERSAL FORM IS WRONG, and the distinction is the whole repair. The rule assumes every
change to one half CREATES a contradiction. A change can also REMOVE one. #8664's test carried a
pin naming docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, an address that ceased to exist when
PR #8661 moved the contract; the script's behaviour was never wrong and needed nothing. Its
worker put it exactly right: 'This change runs the other way: the test contradicted the script's
ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR, and now agrees with it.'

The same shape is queued again on rf2-xomo's reopen: the audit asks for a test NAME rename with
no classifier behaviour change. Under the rule as written a mayor would force a pointless
two-file diff, or block a legitimate one-file fix.

THE REPAIR — narrow the claim to what is true, do not delete it. The pair must move together when
the change alters WHAT THE CLASSIFIER OUTPUTS, or what the test PINS about those outputs. A change
that only corrects the test to match the script's existing, unchanged behaviour — a stale pin, an
overstated test name — is legitimately one file, and saying so is what keeps the rule credible.
The 'two workers in that pair conflict every time' half STANDS and must be kept: that is about
concurrency, not about diff shape, and it is what the dispatch fences rely on.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY FIXED: CLAUDE.md is currently held by PR #8666 (worker fhsweep, rf2-wppza),
unmerged. Editing it now would plant a conflict in exactly the file this rule is about. DO IT
AFTER #8666 MERGES.

EVIDENCE IN THE TREE, all measured rather than recalled:
  #8664 — test half only, 1 file, merged green 88/88.
  #8666 — both halves, comments only, one commit (afe06a9145).
  rf2-xomo reopen — a test-name rename, no behaviour change, one file.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-21. DISPATCHED to worker pairhonesty (branch worker/pairhonesty-0tkx), CLUSTERED with rf2-xomo — different files, no collision, both about the classifier pair telling the truth about itself.

WHY THIS IS A WORKER DISPATCH AND NOT A MAYOR EDIT, recorded because I got it wrong first. I said
on this bead that I would make the one-sentence change myself, since it is method work. I tried,
and THE MAYOR CHECKOUT'S PRE-COMMIT HOOK REFUSED IT:

    Staged files in refused zones: CLAUDE.md
    Permitted in mayor commits: .beads/issues.jsonl, MEMORY.md

That guard is right and I was wrong. 'One sentence' and 'method work' are not exemptions —
orchestration, not implementation, is the rule, and the hook is the backstop that catches a mayor
reasoning its way past it. I reverted the working-copy edit and verified the blob matches HEAD
before dispatching.

My draft replacement wording is on the bead and in the brief, given to the worker as a STARTING
POINT rather than as text to paste unexamined.
PR #8667 AUDIT RESIDUAL (completeness / correctness / implementation quality). The repaired one-toucher rule in CLAUDE.md:91 remains internally inconsistent. Its bold lead says the pair must move together for any change that alters what the test PINS about classifier outputs. The later sentence then exempts this stale-pin repair, contradicting the lead that operators skim. Action: define the joint-edit trigger as a classifier-behaviour change that requires corresponding expectations (or a proposed expectation change that requires new behaviour), while explicitly excluding a test-only repair that brings stale expectations to the script's already-existing behaviour. Reopened the exact owner rather than creating a duplicate.

THE REOPEN WAS A STATUS-ONLY REVERT, and I checked that before deciding rather than assuming
either way. bd history --json shows NO text-bearing change in the newest 20 snapshots — no note,

'MERGED-PR AUDIT #8666 — CORRECTNESS FINDING' note and a real defect. Reading the notes before
re-closing is what separates the two; re-closing rf2-wppza then would have destroyed a live

VERIFIED AT SOURCE AT TIP, three ways:
  - The old universal claim 'a change to either alone lands a tree...' -> 0 occurrences. Removed.
  - The concurrency clause 'two workers in that pair conflict every time' -> 1 occurrence. Kept,

THE WORKER IMPROVED ON MY DRAFT AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING. I had put the narrowing two

title: hic: remaining SSR prose still calls hand-rolled renderToString the package's only server path
description:
## Owner: found while auditing rf2-s52w. This stale sentence is what PRODUCED that bead's false root cause.

`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66`, under the
header section *## What is deliberately NOT here*, still reads:

> **A Hicasso server entry.** There is none, and none is needed: the consumer calls
> `react-dom/server` and the policy is honoured by rendering. The harness here is
> `renderToString` called by hand, which is the only server path in the package.

Both halves are false at trunk tip.

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs` — 452 lines, `re-frame.hicasso.server/render`
— landed in commit `30317bfe0e` on 2026-08-14 21:28 +1000 (`feat(hicasso):
re-frame.hicasso.server/render, and h/hydrate! on the door (rf2-b6jkj)`, PR #8236). It is a real
product door, not a stub: `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs:50-58`
names it as one of the TWO minters of the adoption window — "once per REQUEST, closed in that
door's `finally`" — and records that because both doors call `impl.mount/tree` "the fork is
decided once for both sides of the wire". So it is neither absent nor a second server path
beside the hand-rolled harness; it is THE server path, and the hand-rolled `renderToString` in
this file is the harness beside it.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

Checkpoint 3 cited THIS FILE, by name and "in terms", as the evidence for a root cause it then
wrote into rf2-s52w: *"THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY. Every server witness in the package
calls react-dom/server's renderToString by hand — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in
terms."* From there it propagated into `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md:89`,
into `checkpoint-3-native.md`, and finally into a mayor note of 2026-08-21 that raised
"Does Hicasso ship a server entry?" as an open decision for Mike — a week after it shipped.

One stale docstring, four downstream records, one moot operator question. That is the cost, and
it is why this is a bead rather than a shrug.

## It is an omission, not a convention

The bullet DIRECTLY ABOVE it in the same section was amended in place when its own condition
changed: "When this file was written the prefix was UNSPELLABLE ... The operator then ruled a
thin pass-through, so `:identifier-prefix` is now an option on both root doors and the clause is
reachable; what has not changed is that it is not a NATIVE-tier claim, which is why it is still
not here." So the file's convention is to amend and keep the reason. The server-entry bullet was
simply missed — including by the 2026-08-20 sweep that touched this file twice (`7a65ab11d7`,
`53df56d29b`).

## The repair

Amend the bullet in place, in the same shape as its neighbour: the file's own harness is still a
hand-rolled `renderToString` and that is still deliberate (these are NATIVE-tier claims and the
product door is dispositioned elsewhere), but say that `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` exists
and is the package's server path, so the sentence cannot be re-read as a fact about the package.
Keep it a *deliberately not here* bullet; do not turn it into a claim this file does not measure.

While there: check the other bullets in that section against the current tree, since this one
survived two sweeps.

## Fences and gates

- Test-file docstring only. No behaviour change; no assertion touched.
- `implementation/**` is OUTSIDE `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots — a markdown link planted
  there returns that gate GREEN. `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the gate for markdown
  beside source, and since rf2-i4nb2 its third roster covers non-README tracked markdown — but a
  CLJS docstring is neither, so NO link gate reaches this text. If the amendment adds or changes
  a link, check it by hand and say so in the PR body.
- `verdictlbl` (rf2-egdaq) holds `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/` — a
  different directory. Re-check holders before editing; the fence is a dispatch-time claim.
acceptance_criteria: native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs's 'A Hicasso server entry' bullet no longer asserts that none exists or that the hand-rolled renderToString is the package's only server path; it names re-frame.hicasso.server/render and keeps its 'deliberately not here' framing with the reason. The section's other bullets re-checked against the current tree. No assertion changed.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #8645 (2026-08-21): REOPENED. PR #8645 accurately fixes the two carriers in native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, but a repo-wide exact-claim sweep finds seven live carriers of the same now-false present-tense architecture statement across five other source/test files: identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:24, :93-94 and :204; core_view_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:10; client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:153; facade_roster_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:211; and impl/mount.cljs:182. Each still calls a hand-rolled react-dom/server renderToString the only server path the package has, although re-frame.hicasso.server/render is the shipped product server door and itself accepts :identifier-prefix. This is the exact stale-server-path owner, so reopen it rather than create a duplicate. Repair by applying #8645's distinction consistently: these are deliberately minimal harnesses beside the product door, not the package's only server path. Re-sweep the exact phrases and compile/gate every touched source namespace. correction-ledger.md, checkpoint-3-native.md and the dispositions rows remain rf2-s52w/ledger-keeper territory and are not added to this owner's scope.
close_reason:
Swept by PR #8650 (branch worker/ssrsweep-981ka), opened against the audit note that reopened this bead — NOT the original DESCRIPTION/acceptance-criteria block, which describes the already-shipped PR #8645 work.

DELTA against the audit's 'seven carriers across five files': all seven were still live at tip (none pre-fixed, none phantom), and a re-derived sweep found FOUR more the list did not have, across two additional files — impl/overlay.cljs:253, native.cljc:1082, core_view_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:27 and facade_roster_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:54. Corrected figure: ELEVEN carriers across SEVEN files. The extras wear different words for the same claim ('the package's server path', 'this package's only server path'), and native.cljc carried the second half of the very sentence #8645 deleted from the test file, still standing in production source.

Discriminator applied: a line is a carrier only if it asserts the hand-rolled harness is the package's ONLY server path (or that no product server entry exists). Five matching lines were read and deliberately LEFT because they already draw the distinction — impl/mount.cljs:504-515 (indefinite article, and it names server/render two paragraphs later, which is what made carrier :182 an internal contradiction in the same file), impl/roots.cljs:58, presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test.cljs:18 and :99, and facade_roster_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:176.

No assertion touched, no behaviour changed. Eleven per-region sabotage plants all read exit 1 with per-file attribution and blob-hash-verified restores; control counts identical before and after.

OUT OF SCOPE, reported for routing: the same claim stands in docs/design/hicasso/product/ at checkpoint-3-native.md:203, correction-ledger.md:89 and dispositions.md:282/:283/:301 — ledger-keeper / rf2-s52w territory per this bead's own note.

title: hic: scope row 5's 'mismatch attribution' required result to roots a re-frame2 door opens (rf2-s52w's last acceptance clause)
description:
## Owner: this is rf2-s52w's remaining acceptance clause, not a new finding

rf2-s52w's acceptance option B has three clauses. Two are discharged:

- the source-located statement + measured witness landed in PR #8302 (`473ff5e330`) —
  `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs:30-52` header,
  measured row at `:920`, pointer from `native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:38-46`;
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md:290`'s HS-21 row was amended 2026-08-20 by
  rf2-vwo53 (PR #8559).

The third — *row 5's required-result sentence amended to scope "mismatch attribution" to roots
the package itself adopts* — is still owing, and no open bead owned it before this one.
A later audit re-finding it should recognise it as rf2-s52w's clause, not a second finding.

## The obligation and where it actually lives

Two homes, and it is the SECOND that creates the obligation:

1. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md:49` — the native tier's only
   release checklist ("A red row blocks publication of the native namespace"). Row 5's
   *Required result* reads "...including server bytes or source refusal, matching hydration,
   **mismatch attribution** and multiple roots".

2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md:34` — the canonical matrix
   row 5 is measured against. Its per-row hydration column for *Root/frame provider and
   outward bridge* (`:24`) does NOT list mismatch attribution. But the blanket sentence at
   `:34` — "Every Render row runs the common hydration states: matching content, **deliberate
   mismatch with source attribution**, two simultaneous roots with stable `identifierPrefix`,
   and unmount cleanup" — puts it back on every Render row, that one included. So the row's
   omission is not a carve-out and the blanket sentence is what has to be scoped.

## What the scope IS, normatively

`spec/011-SSR.md:825` already states it in as many words: the framework reporter rides the
package's own hydrate path, and "hydrating via the substrate-native renderer directly
(`uix.dom/hydrate-root`, react-dom `hydrateRoot`) bypasses the reporter and falls back to
React's default (silent) handling". `onRecoverableError` is an option of an INDIVIDUAL root
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs:20-27`), so a root the package
did not open takes none of the package's options.

**Scope it by WHO OPENED THE ROOT, not by which surface.** There are two re-frame2 doors that
install the reporter on a React-element root — `h/hydrate!`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:546`) and the Spec 006 client
mount entry `(re-frame.substrate.adapter/render tree mount {:hydrate? true})`
(`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1107`, whose docstring at `:1191-1204`
names itself the only native mount route that installs it). The outward bridge is not special:
any surface under a root the consumer opened with raw `react-dom/client` is equally outside the
channel. Wording that singles out the outward bridge invites a door for the outward bridge,
which is the wrong remedy.

## Why this is worth one small edit rather than leaving it

The release checklist is a publication gate. As written, row 5 can never go green for a reason
everyone already agrees is correct and normative, so every checkpoint re-derives the same
"unmet" and pays a dispatch to refute it —
`docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-3-native.md:194` records the finding,
`checkpoint-4-coverage.md:384` and `correction-ledger.md:89` both record that Checkpoint 4's
conjunct B keeps scoring HS-21 until the sentence is amended. This edit REMOVES a clause; it
adds no gate, no diagnostic and no ceremony.

## Fences

- DO NOT touch `correction-ledger.md` — fenced out by rf2-s52w and by this bead.
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-3-native.md` is a dated checkpoint record. Whether it
  gets an in-place amendment is the ledger keeper's convention; the two lane pages above are
  the live surface and are enough to discharge the clause.
- Re-check holders before editing: rf2-hic-090 (`recertdup`) holds a `docs/design/hicasso/`
  recertification results page, and PR #8634 holds `docs/design/hicasso/studio/**`. Neither is
  a lane page, but the fence is a dispatch-time claim and can go stale.
- Gate: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers `docs/`. `mkdocs build --strict` does NOT cover

title: hicasso: fail-closed gaps in alloc_pass_position.cjs's boundary and session reporting
description:
FOUND by rf2-fk6pj's phase-4 window (PR #8634) and deliberately NOT repaired
there, because an estimator must not change between a pre-registration and the
runs it will be read on. Neither affects any figure that window published;
both are recorded on its page under "Two defects found and deliberately NOT
repaired".

1. THE BOUNDARY CHECKS THE DRAWN SCHEDULE'S BALANCE, NOT THE REALISED ONE.
   admissibleRun verifies q*parity = 0 and q*linear = 0 on passSchedule.flips,
   and separately that the drive covers every scheduled round. It does NOT
   check the balance of the block set that actually CARRIED DATA. A round whose
   four windows all failed to certify yields no block, so the realised
   labelling can be short and unbalanced while the drawn one is neither -- and
   the design's identification is a property of the realised labelling, not of
   the draw. It did not bite in phase 4 (96 blocks of a possible 96, realised
   q*parity 0 in all eight runs, verified by hand and stated on the page), but
   the check belongs in the boundary rather than in a paragraph.

   THE REPAIR: compute the realised block set inside admissibleRun and refuse
   when its round set is incomplete or its q*parity / q*linear are non-zero.
   Negative controls: a record with one round's mid-rung cells stripped of
   certification must refuse, and the intact corpus must still admit.

2. THE READER'S SESSION LINE IS WRONG FOR A SINGLE-SESSION CORPUS. report()
   computes `agree` as sessions.size > 1 && all signs equal, then prints "THE
   SESSIONS DO NOT AGREE IN SIGN, so a claim of this term is capped at a single
   session. With 1 sessions that is a sign agreement on 1 blocks and nothing
   stronger." For a one-session corpus the honest statement is that no
   cross-session comparison is possible at all, not that the sessions disagree.
   Reproduced when re-reading phase 3's four runs. Cosmetic in the sense that
   no figure moves, NOT cosmetic in the sense that it asserts something false
   about the evidence.

   THE REPAIR: branch the wording on sessions.size === 1 explicitly. Pin both
   branches in --self-test; the single-session branch is reachable from the
   committed phase-3 corpus via data/alloc-legorder/phase3-re-adjudication.json.

NOT A GATE PROBLEM and nothing here is a tolerance. Both are analysis-only:
no window, no browser, no bench slot. alloc_pass_position.cjs is registered in
test:script-helpers and that is the gate.

NOTE FOR THE BRIEF: that file's blob hash is a PUBLISHED PROVENANCE PIN, cited in two committed tables (the studio results page and the pre-registration). The corpus has a precedent for this exact situation — the phase-3 page carries a section headed 'THE RIG FILE MOVED UNDER THIS BRANCH AFTER THE LAST RUN', which KEEPS the measured pin, names the new blob and states the re-run evidence. Follow that shape. Never rewrite a pinned hash, and never amend the pre-registration after the runs.

Reproduction: replace all eight committed box.session.sessionStartedAt values with the same ID and call report(rows, declared); it returns refused=false, computes OUTCOME 1, and only later prints the already-owned one-session wording defect. Thus a corpus that did not take the declared two-session design is admitted as all eight declared runs. Extend this owner (rather than open a duplicate) to validate the declaration's session partition: runs declared A share one actual session, runs declared B share another, and A != B; add negative controls for collapsed and mispartitioned sessions. title: docs(hicasso): production-server-arm's capability table says 'shipped' about two deleted trees, and async-routing-recipes cites a fixture that matches nothing
description:
MEASURED AT origin/main 2de41e2252, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Surfaced by the worker that landed PR #8622 (rf2-wbdr7), which correctly declined to action either — both sit outside that bead's live-command scope.

THIS IS NOT THE REPOINTING CLASS, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. rf2-wbdr7 repointed instructions a reader is meant to RUN, where a live equivalent existed. Neither of these has a live equivalent, and neither is an instruction. They are ASSERTIONS OF FACT that are now false, which is why a path rewrite cannot fix them.

FINDING 1 — A TABLE SAYS "SHIPPED" ABOUT DELETED TREES.

docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md, the capability table:

  line 162 | A live two-sided emitter parity apparatus
           | implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/parity_fixtures.cljc (643 lines, 66 cases)
             + parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs + parity_html.cljc
           | STATE: "shipped and running"

  line 163 | An interpreted structural walk that runs on the JVM
           | implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/tree.cljc (678)
             + node.cljc (1,438) + conversion.cljc (906)
           | STATE: "shipped, cross-host"

Two more references to the same trees at :389 and :424, the second repeating the 643-line figure.

MEASURED: implementation/ui returns 0 tracked files and implementation/freehand returns 0. Positive control on the same command shape: implementation/hicasso returns 628. Both trees were deleted by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16.

So the table asserts, in its own State column, that a capability is SHIPPED AND RUNNING when the 643-line file it names does not exist. A reader assessing what Hicasso has today is misled in the most direct way a design record can mislead.

FINDING 2 — A LAW IS SAID TO "LIVE" AT A PATH THAT MATCHES NOTHING.

docs/design/hicasso/product/async-routing-recipes.md:132 says the R-C1 law "lives in two places, neither of them a witness that could be elevated", and names spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures/fh-ctrl-013.edn.

MEASURED: `git ls-files | grep fh-ctrl-013` returns 0. Positive control: spec/conformance/** returns 246 tracked files, so the tree is real and the pattern is live.

WHAT IS WANTED, AND WHY IT NEEDS JUDGEMENT RATHER THAN A SWEEP.

There is nothing to repoint to. Each row needs a decision about what it now asserts, and the two findings may not take the same answer:
  (a) the capability MOVED into implementation/hicasso, in which case name where and re-state the figures against the surviving artefact - do NOT carry the old line counts across, they described deleted files;
  (b) the capability WENT with the tree, in which case the State column must say so, and the row becomes a record of what the donor had rather than a claim about what ships;
  (c) it is genuinely unresolved, in which case say that plainly instead of leaving a false "shipped".

ESTABLISH WHICH BY READING THE TREE, not by choosing the tidier answer. A row rewritten to claim something equally unverified is worse than the one it replaced.

DO NOT MECHANICALLY REWRITE PROVENANCE. Where a figure is pinned to a revision at which the file did exist, that is a record and it stays. The discriminator is TENSE AND MOOD: a State column reading "shipped and running" is a present-tense claim about now; a sentence reporting what a donor arm had at a pinned revision is a record.

RELATED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED INTO THIS BEAD: rf2-wbdr7 covers live reproduce COMMANDS with dead paths and is separately tracked.

Consider whether the two spellings should be unified, which would make the census a single grep rather than a judgement call.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it needs a decision rather than a one-liner. ladder_band.cjs is a data-driven recompute, not a pure fixture reader like the alloc_* siblings. Its '--selftest' path needs checking for whether it can run in CI unattended: does it need a checked-in dataset, how long does it take, is data/ladder-ymi6j.json sufficient? If it runs clean and cheap, register it in test:script-helpers beside the alloc_* readers. title: method: the generic gate-nomination rule covers an exclusion but not an exclusion's own carve-out
description:
RAISED BY worker/fenceclause 2026-08-21 while landing PR #8600, the repo-specific half of this same defect. It deliberately left the generic tree untouched and referred the question up, which was correct.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md carries a bullet at roughly line 620: 'Never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface being edited... Read the exclusion config before naming the gate.' That covers ONE direction — a gate covering LESS than it appears, where nominating it returns a green that inspected nothing.

THE INVERSE IS NOT COVERED, and it is what just bit this project in eight consecutive dispatch briefs. An exclusion can have its OWN CARVE-OUT: a gate that normally skips a construct but reports it in named trees. Stating only the blind spot then UNDERSTATES coverage, and 'read the exclusion config' does not tell a reader to read the exclusion's own exceptions.

WHY THE UNDERSTATING DIRECTION IS NOT HARMLESS, which is the part the existing bullet's reasoning does not reach. A worker told a gate does not cover its edit will hand-check, which costs little, and then REPORT that the gate did not cover it — a false statement in a change body, and the same both-directions misreporting the fast-spine-gap rule already warns about. Worse, it can read a green as having inspected nothing, and go hunting a problem the gate already proved absent.

WHAT IS WANTED: ONE ABSTRACT SENTENCE beside the existing bullet. Nothing more — this is a generic rule in a generic document and the stance's second half applies. Something to the effect that an exclusion may itself carry exceptions, so read the exclusion's carve-outs too, and that understating coverage misreports as surely as overstating it.

KEEP THE LAYERS APART, and this is the whole reason the bead exists rather than the worker just doing it. docs/the-mayor-method/** carries NO repository names, script names, constant names, paths, bead ids or PR numbers. The concrete instance lives in .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, landed by PR #8600. Do not name it here.

title: hic: U4 needs a per-frame driver on the LEDGER witness — the slice has no continuous interaction to measure
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-9wmqd, 2026-08-21, when that bead's donor-arm half landed as PR #8599. Edit-shaped and loud-box-safe: it needs NO window and can be dispatched beside anything.

WHY U4 CANNOT BE SERVED WHERE U1-U3 ARE. budgets.md section 4 registers U4 as 'Dragging/animation stay inside frame budget', estimand PER-FRAME LATENCY, and section 9.4 governs it on a witness application under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/. Both landed clock drivers sit on the SLICE, and the slice publishes NO DRAG AND NO ANIMATION — every interaction it has is discrete (a keystroke, a click, a select). A per-frame estimator driven by repeating one of those once a frame would publish a scripted repetition of a DISCRETE interaction against a line written about a CONTINUOUS one, which is the same class of error rf2-xa8wo's driver exists to have stopped making (a p95 of a mount against a line about a paint). Adding a drag to the slice is not the repair either: it would move the population, and U1-U4 are governed on the application's own interactions rather than on interactions added to reach a row. PR #8599's driver states all of this in its own docstring rather than leaving it to be discovered.

WHERE IT IS REACHABLE. re-frame.hicasso.examples.ledger publishes a VIRTUALIZED 10,000-ROW LIST over a real scroll viewport — its virtualized_dom_cljs_test.cljs drives scrollTop and dispatches a real scroll event, and vendor.cljs's own note names 'host-local animation/drag state'. A scroll over a windowed list is a genuinely continuous interaction and is the population U4 is stated over.

WHAT IS WANTED. A third driver, on the ledger, on the SAME mechanism the two slice drivers share — slice_echo_clock_app's window! and after-paint, REQUIRED rather than transcribed, the way slice_broad_clock_app requires them — but with an ESTIMATOR OVER FRAME INTERVALS rather than over window lengths. A run of consecutive frames under a sustained scroll, publishing the distribution of intervals between them; a floor arm (the same rAF chain with no application work, which is the box's own frame grid); and a positive control whose prediction is a FLOOR rather than a band (a busy-wait of N ms inside each frame cannot produce an interval shorter than N).

Note that lane/rounds-async! schedules a sample as a promise of ONE NUMBER, and a frame run yields K-1 intervals, so the frame estimator does not fit that loop. Use lane/slot-order for the per-round arm ordering rather than hand-rolling one — visit-plan's docstring records what a second copy of the schedule has cost this lane twice.

THE PROHIBITIONS, carried over and not negotiable. DO NOT WIDEN A BAND OR GUESS A THRESHOLD. DO NOT BUILD A GATE: section 7 routes every distributional row to pinned evidence runs on P-DEV-1 and FORBIDS converting one into a PR threshold, section 9.1 says such a row may never name the first lane, and check_budget_ledger.py enforces it. Building an INSTRUMENT is in scope; building a GATE is not. MOVE NO LEDGER CELL — 49 rows / 31 MET / 5 BREACH / 3 UNRESOLVED / 10 UNPINNED, and U4 keeps UNPINNED whatever this bead builds.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING. Re-read the ledger example and its virtualized_dom_cljs_test at the tip and confirm the scroll viewport is still there and still real; re-read PR #8599's driver docstring for the row-set reasoning it already states. title: hicasso: the twenty-run window record states its realised rate over a control-refused run
description:
RAISED BY PR #8598 (rf2-6kxub/rf2-csca8/rf2-z2xir), which imposed ONE admissibility rule across both analysis readers, their pages and their fixtures: a failed positive control is not an observation. Two committed datasets carry alloc.controlVerdict.ok=false -- alloc-77gz8/run12-a4a1537cb71 and alloc-9jrhi/bisect-5-a-4a1537cb71-replicate -- and both were previously counted as low-mode readings.

THE RESIDUE, and it is OUTSIDE that PR's fence. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-second-mode-a-pre-registered-twenty-run-window.md:76 states 'The realised rate was 2 of 20 (10%)', and docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md:124 restates it in that page's index row ('THE MODE REPRODUCED in 2 of 20 runs at 4a1537cb71 (10%, against the 1-in-7 prior)'). run12 is one of those twenty. On the admissibility rule now applied everywhere else, the realised rate of admissible READINGS is 2 of 19 (10.5%).

WHY IT WAS NOT CHANGED THERE. The page is rf2-77gz8's record, not rf2-6kxub's, and README.md was fenced to another worker in the same wave. More substantively, THE CLAIM MAY BE CORRECT AS WRITTEN and this bead should test that before changing anything: '2 of 20' there is a statement about a PRE-REGISTERED DESIGN -- twenty runs were committed before the first was taken and twenty were taken -- rather than about an admissibility census. A pre-registered count is honoured by running the runs, and a run whose control later failed was still run. The README row's own words support that reading: it says the two HIGH runs both had 'a passing positive control', which is true and is the claim that actually matters there.

SO THE QUESTION IS NARROW. Does the page distinguish (a) the DESIGN's realised count, 2 of 20, from (b) the admissible READING rate, 2 of 19? If it conflates them -- in particular where it compares the realised rate against the '1 in 7' prior, which IS an inference about rates -- the comparison should be restated on 19. If it is only reporting that the pre-registered window completed as declared, it is right as it stands and this bead CLOSES with that finding recorded.

REJECT A MECHANICAL SWEEP. Do not rewrite every '2 of 20' in the tree. The correct outcome may well be one sentence distinguishing the two readings, or no change at all plus a note.

FENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md is a hot index file -- sequence rather than parallel against anything else touching it. NO WINDOW, BENCHMARK OR BROWSER RUN IS NEEDED; this is computable from the committed corpus. Do not move tau in either direction and do not reopen the LEVELS.
close_reason:
SETTLED by PR #8602 (analysis-only; computable from the committed corpus, no window taken).

THE CLAIM IS NOT CORRECT AS WRITTEN, and what settles it is the page itself rather than a matter of reading. The sentence does two jobs and only one is a design statement: the page derives a 1-in-7 prior, computes P(at least one high) over twenty runs, then says the realised rate is 'consistent with that prior' -- which is an INFERENCE ABOUT RATES. For that comparison a run whose positive control failed is not evidence the mode was absent; the instrument did not work on it, so it is evidence neither way.

DECISIVE: THE PAGE ALREADY DRAWS THIS LINE. Its own Admissibility section names run12's control failure (11.79 B/double direct, 14.19 differential against a predicted 8), excludes it from the LEVEL population, and confirms both high runs are admissible. So the page excludes run12 from one population and includes it in another, in the same document, without saying they are different populations. That is internal inconsistency, not interpretation.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Census of all twenty alloc.controlVerdict values: 19 ok, 1 refused (run12), 0 absent -- carried with a positive control showing raw.controlVerdict is undefined on all twenty, the fail-open a census on the wrong path returns as a clean zero.

THE REPAIR KEEPS BOTH TRUE FACTS. Design count stays 2 of 20 (twenty pre-registered, twenty run, honoured however their controls later read); the rate quoted against the prior becomes 2 of 19 (10.5%), with the twentieth named as control-refused.

ALSO FOUND, AND IT MOVES THE OTHER SIDE OF THE SAME COMPARISON. The prior's seven 18-round runs at 4a1537cb71 -- 3 from alloc-9jrhi, 4 from workcount-n1b9h, re-derived here -- include alloc-9jrhi/bisect-5-a-4a1537cb71-replicate, the tree's OTHER control-refused dataset. So over admissible readings the prior is 1 in 6 (~16.7%), not 1 in 7. Applying the rule to one side of a comparison and not the other would have been the same half-applied-rule defect.

NEITHER ACCOUNTING DISTURBS THE CONCLUSION: Binomial(19, 1/6) gives P(X <= 2) = 36.4% against an expected 3.17 high runs, where the figures as written give 44.0%. Consistent with the prior either way, so nothing downstream moves.

NOT SWEPT. The design-time paragraph keeps 1 in 7 and the ~95% power figure -- that is what the corpus showed when the series length was fixed, and rewriting it would falsify the design record. tau untouched; the LEVELS untouched.

ONE THING FLAGGED RATHER THAN CHANGED, for rf2-77gz8 to rule on: the 'Why twenty' table's second row reads 7 runs at other revisions where a census of 18-round runs finds 6, the 6-round pilot being the likely seventh. Resolving it means deciding whether the pilot counts, which is not this bead's call. The table was left untouched.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWES, and why it stays OPEN.

      publishes: a paint-bounded window is dominated by the frame grid, so :over-floor's
      :straddles-1? must be read on each measured arm BEFORE any :comparative range is quoted.
      If the shipped seed cannot separate the measured arms from an empty frame, the honest
      conclusion is that C3 needs a BROADER POPULATION than the slice's feed page -- a finding
      about the row, never a licence to widen a band.

GATES. npm run test:hicasso-compile is the gate covering this surface; it is heavyweight and was
NOT run locally (loud box), but it auto-covers new files by walking the lane directory and runs
on every PR in test.yml, so CI gates the compile. Locally: a Clojure-aware delimiter-balance check
and a qualified-reference resolution check (45 refs in the driver, 8 in the donor views, all
resolve), each with a planted-fault discrimination proof and a restore verified by blob hash.
U4's half is now filed separately as rf2-xc0bw (a per-frame driver on the LEDGER witness, edit-shaped and loud-box-safe). This bead keeps items (b) the suite-level self-test and (c) the quiet-box window for U3/C3/C4.
AUDIT OF PR #8599 (2026-08-21) — repair before the quiet-box U3/C3/C4 window.

Two measurement-fidelity defects belong to this existing owner; no duplicate bead was created.

1. DONOR FEED READ-SET IS LARGER ON THE SHIPPED POPULATION. slice_donor_views.cljs feed-page always calls use-subscribe for [::subs/t :feed/empty], while the Hicasso feed-page calls h/sub for that value only in its empty branch. The pinned seed is non-empty, so the donor locale arm carries an extra subscription/hook that the Hicasso locale arm does not. That adds work to the denominator and can flatter the C3 Hicasso/UIx ratio. Keep the branch-local read branch-local (for example via an empty-state child boundary) and make the suite self-test prove the relevant read roster, not only canonical DOM.

2. THE THEME ARMS RUN OVER DIFFERENT LOCALE-STATE MIXES. :locale and :ctl-blocked both toggle the shared Hicasso frame's locale, while only :donor-locale toggles the donor frame. Replaying the six-arm lane/slot-order at measured slots s=8..19 shows :theme runs in the non-seed locale on 4/12 visits per round, but :donor-theme does so on 8/12. Thus the comparative theme medians are drawn from different page-state populations; the seeded-only canonical parity gate cannot see the divergence after sampling begins. Isolate the control's state/root or deterministically establish each arm's pre-state, and add a schedule-level self-test that proves paired arms see the same governed state mix.
AUDIT REPAIRS 1 AND 2 PLUS ITEM (b) LANDED in PR #8606 (worker/echoself-9wmqd, 2026-08-21). NO WINDOW AND NO BENCH RUN WAS TAKEN; no ledger cell moves; no threshold, band or gate created. ITEM (c) IS UNTOUCHED and this bead stays OPEN on it.

BOTH PREMISES RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both held. slice_donor_views.cljs feed-page bound empty-label unconditionally in its let; slice/views.cljs feed-page reads [::subs/t :feed/empty] only inside its empty branch; the seed is seven articles at a page size of three, so the branch never renders.

THE 4/12 AND 8/12 COUNTS REPRODUCED EXACTLY, in every one of the five rounds. Replaying the six-arm lane/visit-plan (order_guard/slot-order rotate-then-reflect at k=6, indexed by the SAMPLE index, not by the round) at {:warmup 8 :samples 12} over 5 rounds: at measured slots s=8..19, :theme runs in the non-seed locale on 4/12 visits per round and :donor-theme on 8/12.

THE SAME REPLAY FOUND A SECOND DIVERGENCE THE AUDIT DID NOT NAME, in the other dimension and on the POSITIVE CONTROL'S pairing: :ctl-blocked runs in the non-seed THEME on 8/12 measured visits per round against :locale's 4/12, and control-per-round subtracts those two medians. Same mechanism, same class. Both are closed.

WHAT LANDED.
1. Repair 1 on the DONOR SIDE only (slice/views.cljs is a shipped example consumed by a11y/l0/l2 tests): an empty-state child boundary, feed-empty, which costs the measured population nothing because its branch never renders at the seed. The full read roster was then swept boundary by boundary and the result recorded in the donor namespace docstring: chrome 7/7, article-row 2/2, digest 5/5, digest-body/callout/unsupported 1/1 each, pager 5/5 at the seed, app 4 against 3. TWO other differences exist and neither is the same defect. The PAGER is a source-located REFUSAL: the same child-boundary repair would put an extra boundary on the MEASURED page (the seed always renders a pager), which is the same error in the same direction, larger and always on. The shell's missing [:rf.route/id] read runs in the DENOMINATOR'S favour.
2. Repair 2 by ESTABLISHING each arm's pre-state, not by isolating the control. Arms declare :side and :alternates; pre-state is a pure fn of the arm and its own visit index; establish-pre-state! moves the frame through the application's own events, outside every window, on parity-discrimination!'s door and settle. Paired arms then see identical mixes at EVERY schedule by construction.
   WHY THE OTHER CANDIDATE WAS REJECTED, on a replay rather than on taste: both isolating variants (control restores its locale / control on its own root) equalise the theme pair at {8,12} and STOP DOING SO at {8,13} and {8,20} -- the equality is an accident of how slot-order's rotation lands on twelve indices, and sampling's own docstring says the run reading this instrument will raise those counts. The own-root variant also leaves the control's own theme mix wrong (0/12 against 4/12).
3. Item (b): implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/slice_broad_window_dom_cljs_test.cljs, beside slice_broad_clock_app.cljs (the driver both repairs live in; the sibling slice_echo_clock_app already has its own suite). Ten rows.

WHAT THE SELF-TEST PROVES, beyond canonical DOM -- both first-class, each with its own negative control.
- READ ROSTER: both frames' subscription caches through subs.tooling/sub-cache-snapshot (the same per-frame cache BOTH substrates go through -- Hicasso's collector calls subs/subscribe for every h/sub edge, the UIx adapter for every hook). Asserts donor-minus-hicasso is EMPTY, [::subs/t :feed/empty] is in NEITHER, [:rf.route/id] is hicasso-only, with anti-vacuity first. NEGATIVE CONTROL re-plants exactly the removed read as a UIx boundary on the donor frame in its own root and requires the comparison to go from empty to naming exactly that read.
- GOVERNED STATE MIX: replays lane/visit-plan through the driver's own pre-state and asserts the three compared pairs are one population at five schedules including {8,13} and {8,20}. NEGATIVE CONTROL models the rig PR #8599 shipped and requires the same comparison to refuse, reproducing 4-against-8 on the locale dimension and 8-against-4 on the control's theme dimension INSIDE the suite, then shows the repaired model passing at the same schedule.
- AND A BRIDGE from the arithmetic to the instrument, because a pure replay proves a model rather than a driver: one DOM row calls establish-pre-state! for both parities on both frames and reads the result back through the driver's own echo checks; another runs a tiny schedule end to end and asserts each arm's visit counter advanced exactly once per planned visit.

NO SEVENTH IN-DRIVER CONTROL WAS ADDED. The driver already runs six and in-driver is the stronger place; what was missing was the browser-suite row.

WHAT THE SUITE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RE-ADJUDICATE, stated in the file: the canonical-DOM parity gate is a RELEASE gate by construction (data-rf2-source-coord makes the two arms' attributes differ under goog.DEBUG), so a dev-compiled row asserting that equality would either fail honestly or have to strip attributes until it passed.

GATES. npm run test:hicasso-compile covers this surface and auto-covers the new file by walking the lane directory; it was NOT run locally (a peer worker held a live allocation window on the box and two heavyweight runs wedge rather than fail), and CI gates the compile. No fast-PR spine, no shadow-cljs, no browser run. Locally: a Clojure-aware delimiter-balance check and a qualified-reference resolution check over all three files -- 98 distinct in-repo refs (45 driver / 20 donor views / 33 suite), 0 unresolved, 8 further refs external and reported as out of reach rather than counted. Three planted faults, one per file, each red naming what was planted, each restore verified by identical blob hash against the committed object. Re-run green on the final base after a rebase past twelve landings. implementation/package.json was NOT touched: -dom-cljs-test$ is discovered by ns-regexp and needs no registration.
CI CYCLE 2 on PR #8606 — the browser lane read the first cut as 14 failures, ONE CAUSE plus one contract bug. Now GREEN on browser-test, node-test and every other check, on a rebased base. No assertion was weakened; one was added.

THE CAUSE, source-located. collector/!cells is a PROCESS-GLOBAL table keyed by (frame, query), and its own comment states that isolation between roots is a property of that keying rather than anything React provides. invalidate-cell! is the repair for a cell whose reaction has been retired -- including, in its own words, 'across a same-id reincarnation' -- but that repair rides the reaction's DISPOSAL HOOK, and make-reset-runtime-fixture retires a frame by resetting frame/frames to {} rather than through it. A second mount on a used frame id therefore finds a live cell holding a dead reaction: subs/subscribe is never called again (empty sub-cache) and no watch is installed (no re-render). THE FIRST RENDER IS PERFECT, which is what makes it silent.

THE EVIDENCE FIT THAT SHAPE EXACTLY: the mount row (1st mount) PASSED and every row after it failed. hic roster #{} against the donor's 34; every Hicasso-side locale/theme pre-state stayed English/light; the tally read 9 unverified of 18 -- precisely the nine Hicasso-side windows, with all six donor-side ones verified.

THE ACT-ENVIRONMENT HYPOTHESIS WAS TESTED AND REJECTED rather than assumed: every 'not wrapped in act(...)' line in that log is timestamped +12.32s / +14.36s and this namespace ran at +28.58s. Neighbouring-suite noise.

THE FIX is the discipline slice-echo-window-dom-cljs-test already keeps. boot! takes the frame ids as an argument (hicasso-frame / donor-frame become documented DEFAULTS for the bench page's single mount); a new frames reader publishes the live pair; frame-for and parity-discrimination! resolve through it, because a caller that dispatched into the default while the page rendered from a fresh id would be writing to a frame nothing reads. The suite mints a fresh pair per row. Mechanism + measurement recorded at source in boot!'s new section MOUNTING TWICE, and in teardown!, which states that it cannot fix this and why.

A REAL CONTRACT BUG THE SUITE ALSO CAUGHT: visits published the last visit INDEX under a docstring promising a COUNT, so it read one short of lane/visit-plan's per-arm count. claim-visit! now banks the count and answers the index. The bridge row earned its place on its first run.

AND THE FIRST DIRECT MEASUREMENT OF THE DONOR'S READ ROSTER, handed over by the empty-Hicasso failure: 34 query vectors, every one of them also read by the Hicasso arm, the fifteen ::subs/t strings matching one for one against the boundary-by-boundary sweep. [::subs/t :feed/empty] is ABSENT -- repair 1 confirmed on the shipped population rather than argued. The roster also reaches a :<- sub's INPUTS and not only the values a body asks for ([:rf.route/query] and [:rf/route] arrive as [::subs/page]'s input chain), which makes the comparison stronger than claimed; the docstring now says so and a new assertion pins it.

THE GREEN IS NOT VACUOUS: the red and green runs both report 1044 tests, and assertions go 5937 -> 5938 -- exactly the one assertion added. Had the DOM rows collapsed to their off-browser skips the count would have dropped by roughly forty-five.

GATES. npm run test:hicasso-compile still NOT run locally (machine contention: a peer held an allocation window throughout), and CI decided it. Browser-test is now a gate that RAN rather than one that was cited: red 14, then green, then green again post-rebase. Local static checks re-run on the final base: 97 distinct in-repo refs, 0 unresolved, exit 0; two further planted faults on this round's own edited lines, each red naming the plant, each restored to an identical blob hash.

ITEM (c) REMAINS UNTOUCHED AND THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN ON IT. No window was run, no reading taken, no ledger cell moved, no threshold, band or gate created.

title: hicasso: the allocation datasets record nothing about the box, so the mode-rate's mechanism stays unnameable
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-6kxub when its ANALYSIS half was answered in PR #8593, record docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-mode-rate-tracks-elapsed-session-time.md. This is rf2-6kxub's own SECOND MOVE, carried out rather than dropped.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. The floor arm's high-mode RATE tracks elapsed time within a session: 0/6 at 8.2 min, 1/8 at 14.9, 2/20 at 19.7, 37/69 at 88.3, with a within-session gradient inside the long corpus at one-tail p = 0.0198 (Mann-Whitney on position-in-session, boundary-free). That locates the rate on elapsed-time-within-session and NAMES NO MECHANISM: thermal state, V8 tier accumulation and heap fragmentation over a long session all survive it equally. Across the sessions, duration is confounded with date and clock time (11:23, 13:52, 23:54 -- the last running past midnight).

THE CHEAP MOVE, which is this bead. Record what the datasets currently do not, all of which rides free on an existing field the way the work census does:

  - the Chromium build string (pinned by playwright, but NOT recorded in any dataset),
  - the box's load at window open,
  - the elapsed time since the previous run in the same session.

That converts the NEXT window into evidence about the rate at no extra runner cost. generatedAt is already recorded and is what made the analysis half answerable at all; these three are the same kind of free rider.

HERMETIC, AND NEEDS NO WINDOW. title: mayor-dispatch's fence-derivation rule names two bad sources and misses the third — 'what I briefed them to DO'
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 by the method-reread loop grading its own briefs, and it had already produced a wrong fence in TWO live dispatches when it was found.

WHAT HAPPENED. I wrote the file-ownership fence for worker/ladder-onozm and worker/modeconf-6kxub naming PR #8590's holdings as README.md, the-bisect-is-flat-and-the-floor-has-a-second-mode.md, and alloc_heap_trajectory.cjs. Measured with gh pr view 8590 --json files, the real list is README.md, the-bisect-is-flat..., and the-second-mode-is-per-write-and-the-controls-never-move.md. So the fence was wrong in BOTH directions at once: it named a file the PR does not hold, and OMITTED one it does — and the omitted one is the page a peer bead's findings bear on.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS A SOURCE THE RULE DOES NOT NAME. .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md says, correctly: 'DERIVE that enumeration at dispatch time from gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,files plus git worktree list, NEVER from your own memory of who you dispatched', and separately 'write each fence entry from the FILE LISTS, never from the branch names'. Two bad sources named. I used a THIRD: my memory of what I had BRIEFED that worker to do.

WHY THAT ONE IS THE MOST SEDUCTIVE OF THE THREE. Memory-of-who is obviously a guess. Branch-names is obviously a guess about files. But memory-of-what-I-briefed FEELS like file-level knowledge — it is a list of paths, I wrote it, and I wrote it deliberately. It is nonetheless a PREDICTION, and a worker that does its job well falsifies it: #8590's worker dropped alloc_heap_trajectory.cjs because it fixed the prose instead of the script, and picked up the-second-mode page because reconciling three places was the audit's actual instruction. A GOOD worker diverges from its brief's file list more than a bad one does.

THE FIX, and keep it to one clause: add the third source to the existing prohibition. Something of the shape 'never from your own memory of who you dispatched, from the branch names, or from what you BRIEFED them to touch — a brief is a prediction, and a worker doing its job well falsifies it.' Cite the measurement above.

DO NOT restructure the surrounding paragraph. It is long, dense, load-bearing and already correct; this adds one clause to a list that already has two members.

SURFACE: .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md ONLY. That is a repository-specific command file, so it may name PR numbers, bead ids, paths and tool names freely — do NOT put any of this in docs/the-mayor-method/**, which is the generic tree and carries none of those.

SHARED SURFACE: .claude/commands/** is single-toucher. Check for an open PR against it before starting.

GATE: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci carries an arm that resolves path-shaped REFERENCES in .claude/commands/*.md — bare or backticked alike. It validates no anchors or markdown links there (those files carry none), so a path you name must resolve. check_doc_slugs.py does NOT reach .claude/commands/ at all; do not nominate it. Nothing validates the PROSE — read it back by hand and say so.

CLOSING THIS AS MINUTIAE IS NOT THE RIGHT CALL unless the re-derivation shows the clause is already there. It cost a wrong fence in two live briefs the day it was measured, and the stale-NARROW direction — omitting a file a PR holds — is the one that puts two workers on one file.

One clause added to mayor-dispatch.md's first fence-derivation prohibition: '...never from your own memory of who you dispatched, and never from what you BRIEFED them to touch - a brief is a PREDICTION, and a worker doing its job well falsifies it, which is what makes it the most seductive of the three bad sources...', with the 2026-08-21 measurement cited inline (PR #8590's real file list re-verified with gh pr view 8590 --json files before editing: the bench script the fence named was never in it; the second-mode studio page it omitted was). Surrounding paragraph not restructured - word-diff shows exactly one deleted token, 'dispatched**', re-emitted inside the insertion. Nothing added to docs/the-mayor-method/. title: method: the gate block's plant-verification rule misses the CRLF class — an EOL-anchored plant matches nothing, silently, and the green reads as a passing control
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-ue4kv worker (PR #8584, 2026-08-21), which hit it and caught it, and propagated it deliberately: 'a plant silently failed to apply first time — an end-of-line-anchored regex against a CRLF file matched nothing, with no error. Caught only by checking the match count BEFORE running the gate. Had I not, the green sabotage would have read as "the control does not bite".'

WHERE IT BELONGS: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, section 'Quality gates — how a gate is run', in the four-caution list under 'Verify a restore by hashing the bytes, never by reading a diff.'

WHAT THAT LIST ALREADY SAYS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. The third caution is 'Anchor a patch to a single line. One worker's multi-line anchor matched nothing, with no error and no edit, and only the hash caught it.' That is the same FAILURE (a plant that no-ops) reached by a different MECHANISM (multi-line anchor) with a different DETECTOR (the hash, after the fact). The CRLF mechanism defeats a single-line anchor too, so the existing caution does not cover it — an EOL-anchored pattern against a CR-terminated line is exactly one line and still matches nothing.

TWO THINGS TO ADD, and the second is the more valuable:

1. The MECHANISM. core.autocrlf is true on this checkout, so every file .gitattributes does not pin carries a CR before each line ending. A pattern anchored at end-of-line — a trailing dollar in a regex, or a tool's own line-anchoring — therefore matches nothing. This is the SAME class the method-reread loop already documents for git grep censuses (rf2-woy7g, commit 89b315d213); the plant path is a second door onto it and the block does not name it.

2. The DETECTOR, which is cheaper and earlier than the hash: CHECK THE MATCH COUNT BEFORE RUNNING THE GATE. The hash catches a no-op plant only after a whole gate run has already been spent, and it catches it as an ambiguous signal the worker then has to interpret. A match count of zero, read before the run, is unambiguous and costs nothing.

DO NOT RESTATE THE CENSUS RULE HERE. The generic method tree carries no repository names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics — say it as 'a checkout whose line endings are translated', which is the register the first caution in that same list already uses ('On a checkout whose line endings are translated, use version control's own content hash...'). Match that voice.

SIZE: one caution, a few lines. Do not expand the section. Do not renumber or restructure the list beyond adding to it.

SURFACE: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md only. SHARED SURFACE — two concurrent editors conflict by construction, so this is a one-toucher.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py covers docs/ link targets and heading anchors. Note what it does NOT cover: a broken markdown link inside a FENCED CODE BLOCK is invisible to it EXCEPT in the two trees named by FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES in that script — and docs/the-mayor-method IS one of them, so a fenced doc link in this file IS reported. mkdocs build --strict does cover docs/the-mayor-method (it is not in mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs).
close_reason:
FIXED — PR #8585. The premise held: searched dispatch-prompt-template.md for `match count`, `carriage`, `line endings`, `anchor` and the only hits were the "a rewrite that flips line endings reads clean" paragraph, the hash caution, and the single-line-anchor caution. Neither the mechanism nor the detector was stated anywhere. The third caution does NOT cover this class, exactly as filed — an EOL-anchored pattern against a CR-terminated line is one line and still matches nothing.

Added as the fifth caution under "Verify a restore by hashing the bytes": the mechanism (a carriage return sits between the text and the line ending, so the anchor never reaches the text) and the detector (read the match count BEFORE running the gate; zero is unambiguous and free, where the hash convicts only after a whole gate run and convicts ambiguously). "Four cautions" -> "Five" because it is a count. Nothing else in the file touched; list not restructured.

Register held: no repo names, tracker ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics. Opens on the failure rather than repeating the first caution's opening clause verbatim.

GATE python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, exit codes captured by the worker (never harness-reported): control 0, sabotage 1, restored 0, re-run on the final base after rebase 0. The gate prints no root banner (its green log is empty), so tree-verification was by planted fault: a broken link target in the new bullet, match count read BEFORE the plant (1) and after (1), gate red naming exactly the planted target at :820. Restore verified by the identical blob hash 1ec99efaf6272451b793c5c4f242f7d19618fab4 against the committed object. Fast spine NOT run; check_fast_pr_gap.py --list reports 94 required checks it does not run. mkdocs build --strict not run — CI owns it.

The detector this caution documents was USED here: both of the PR's plants had their match count read before the gate ran.

title: method: the reread loop's duplicate-block check is a false zero — a $-anchored git grep never matches on this CRLF tree
description:
FOUND BY the method-reread loop, 2026-08-20 23:55 AUSEST, step 1 — the duplicate-block check that loop prescribes returned a false zero on its own surface.

THE DEFECT. `.claude/commands/mayor-method-reread.md` tells the mayor to diff the worktree-boundary and gate-mechanics blocks against any second copy rather than trusting that they match. Run as an anchored `git grep`, that check CANNOT FIND EITHER BLOCK, because on this checkout a `$` placed directly after literal text never matches.

MEASURED. `git grep -l "^WORKTREE BOUNDARY — MANDATORY$" -- ':!.beads'` returns EMPTY. The heading exists at docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:478. Unanchored, `git grep -c "WORKTREE BOUNDARY — MANDATORY"` returns exactly 1 file, which is the correct answer and also the reassuring one — so the false zero and the true answer look identical to a reader who does not already know there is one copy.

MECHANISM, pinned on .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:
  leading `^` only ......................... 1 hit
  `.*$` ..................................... 1 hit   (`.` matches the CR)
  full literal line + `$` ................... 0 hits  FALSE
  same literal line, no `$` ................. 1 hit
The files carry CRLF terminators, so a `\r` sits between the last literal character and end-of-line.

SPREAD — this is why it is worth a bead rather than a note. `file -b` reports CRLF for ALL of docs/the-mayor-method/{dispatch-prompt-template,loops,bootstrap}.md, ALL of .claude/commands/mayor-{merge,dispatch,posture,hygiene,method-reread}.md, and CLAUDE.md. dispatch-prompt-template.md is 900 of 900 lines CRLF. The whole surface this loop audits is affected, and so is any census the dispatch loop runs over these files.

NO DISPATCH WAS HARMED, and the fix must not disturb what works. The block EXTRACTION uses `sed`, and `sed` on this Git Bash strips the CR on read: `sed -n '/^WORKTREE BOUNDARY — MANDATORY$/,/^```$/p'` still returns its 51 lines and the extracted text is clean LF. Only the VERIFICATION path was blind. DO NOT change the extraction, and do not convert any file's line endings — a mass line-ending rewrite would touch every line of nine governing files for no benefit and is explicitly out of scope.

THE FIX, and it is small. Add to .claude/commands/mayor-method-reread.md, at the block-divergence bullet where it bit: never end a `git grep` pattern with a `$` straight after literal text on this repo — drop the `$` or use `.*$` — and run a positive control before believing any census zero. Repo/OS mechanics belong in the command file, NOT in docs/the-mayor-method/**, which by its own rule carries no OS mechanics or tool names. Consider whether the same caution earns a line in .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, where the census rules live; add it only if it is load-bearing there, since that file already carries the "a search returning zero is not a check that passed" rule in the pasted gate block.

Durable memory recorded under key `git-grep-dollar-anchor-false-zero-on-crlf`.

GATE: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci covers .claude/commands/*.md (it resolves path-shaped references there, bare or backticked). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py does NOT reach that path. Nominate by PATH, never by job name.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8561 (2026-08-21 AUSEST) — REOPENED AS THE EXACT METHOD OWNER; no duplicate filed.

The diagnosed CRLF false zero is real, but both prescribed remedies — “drop the `$`” and append `.*$` — are not semantics-preserving for an exact-line census. They turn an exact line into a prefix match, so the fix can exchange a false zero for a false-high count. This PR's own namespace example demonstrates it: on the current CRLF checkout, `git grep -E '^\(ns re-frame\.core'` returns 17 files because it also matches `re-frame.core-artefact`, `re-frame.core-http`, tests, and every other namespace sharing that prefix; the CR-aware exact query `git grep -P '^\(ns re-frame\.core\r?$'` returns the one actual `re-frame.core` namespace. Searching the tree object is cleaner still for the origin/main census this method already requires: the original `$`-anchored exact pattern against `origin/main` returns that one hit because committed blobs are LF.

The positive control prevents a constant zero, but it does not prove that the broadened query counts the intended population. Repair both command-file lines to prescribe an exact, CRLF-safe route — preferably search the explicit `origin/main` tree object when auditing origin/main, or use a tested optional-CR end anchor — and keep the non-zero control as the independent fail-open guard. Preserve the sound diagnosis and the untouched extraction/line-ending fences.
close_reason:
Corrected by PR #8570. The audit's finding is CONFIRMED by measurement, not merely accepted: on this CRLF checkout the namespace census reads 0 files ($-anchored, false zero), 17 files (broadened - the remedy #8561 landed, and the count that file presented as CORRECT), and 1 file by both exact routes - CR-aware -P '\r?$' against the working tree, and the original $-anchored pattern against the origin/main tree object where blobs are LF.

BOTH command files now rank two EXACT routes in place of the broadening one: (1) search the tree object, since both loops already census at origin/main HEAD and the $ anchor works unchanged there - not an extra step but the step already prescribed; (2) only where a working-tree search is genuinely needed, an optional-CR end anchor via -P; (3) never broaden. The 17-file exemplar in mayor-dispatch.md is corrected from 'the answer the fix recovers' to the over-count it is.

The audit's subtler half is addressed: the control is now TWO-DIRECTIONAL. A positive control rules out a dead pattern and nothing else - every broadened form passes it, so a positive control alone would have certified the seventeen. Both files now require reading the HIT LIST rather than its length and confirming prefix-sharing near-misses are absent. Demonstrated: re-frame.core-http is absent from the exact census and present in the broadened one, while both censuses are non-empty.

Diagnosis preserved verbatim - CRLF mechanism, measured spread, fails-OPEN framing, sed extraction fence, MSYS_NO_PATHCONV caution. No line endings converted. Layering respected: docs/the-mayor-method/** untouched.

Gate: check_readme_links.py --ci captured exit 0, with a planted broken reference proving it reached the edited tree (exit 1 naming .claude/commands/mayor-method-reread.md:14) and the restore verified by identical git blob hash. check_doc_slugs.py neither nominated nor cited - it does not reach .claude/commands/.

title: [retire] docs/api/re-frame.core.md carries freehand residue and is GENERATED — needs a regeneration through the api-manifest chain, not a hand-edit
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-0yp7w.9 configuration/root-markdown slice (PR #8552) and correctly REPORTED rather than reached for — the file is generated and the slice's fence said regenerate via its own chain or report.

MEASURED at origin/main 0c5833b9a9, .beads excluded: docs/api/re-frame.core.md carries 1 hit for the retired-substrate pattern. Re-derive before acting; a count is a claim.

WHY IT IS NOT A HAND-EDIT. docs/api/*.md are produced by the api-manifest chain. Hand-editing a generated artefact makes the file disagree with its generator, and the next regeneration silently reverts the fix. This repo has been bitten by committed generated artefacts before: they serial-bottleneck merges, because any change to the generator re-drifts them and a merge race leaves main stale.

WHAT TO DO. Find the generator, run it, and commit what it produces. If the regenerated output STILL carries the residue, that is a finding about the GENERATOR or its input, not about this page — say so and stop rather than editing the output. If the generator cannot be run cleanly in a worker worktree, report that; it is a legitimate refusal.

FENCE: docs/api/** only, plus whatever the generator itself reads if the residue proves to originate upstream. Check for any open PR touching docs/api/ or the manifest chain before dispatching.

GATE: docs/ is one of scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS, so that script covers link targets and anchors on the regenerated page. It cannot see a stale substrate name. Also check whether mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs reaches docs/api/ before nominating mkdocs build --strict — read the block at source, do not trust a prose list.
close_reason: PR #8557. REFUSAL, on two independent source-located grounds; no edit made. (1) THE FILE IS NOT GENERATED. Nothing in the api-manifest chain writes into docs/api/. The chain's only spit is gen.clj:430, which writes spec/api-manifest.edn. doc_api_check.clj READS docs/api/ as a projection to validate against that manifest - its scope table at line 84 lists docs/api/ as an input tree and its success line is 'OK: docs/api page+member coverage in sync'; lint.yml carries docs/api/** on a paths: filter for the same reason. So docs/api/*.md are hand-authored prose checked against a generated manifest, not output of it. There is no generator to run. (2) THE HIT IS NOT RESIDUE. title: CLAUDE.md's link-gate paragraph is stale: check_readme_links.py grew a THIRD roster in PR #8546 and the description still names two

THE CLAIM, verified at source at origin/main 63a7b71ebb.

CLAUDE.md:116 describes scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci as covering exactly: repo-root markdown (README.md, CLAUDE.md, TESTING.md, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, SKILL-REDIRECT.md), every README.md beside source code, and — as a separately-described third arm — .claude/commands/*.md for path-shaped references.

THAT IS NOW INCOMPLETE. PR #8546 (rf2-i4nb2) added a roster function named _iter_source_markdown and wired it into the roster loop at scripts/check_readme_links.py:412, which now iterates three rosters: _iter_readmes, _iter_root_markdown and _iter_source_markdown. The new one walks git-tracked markdown files that contain a slash in the path and are NOT named README.md, minus the exclusions and minus the command files. It exists to close the gap where implementation/SECURITY.md — cited from the root README — was covered by NEITHER gate: _iter_readmes never saw it because it is not named README.md, and _iter_root_markdown drops anything with a slash in its path. The module docstring at lines 39-56 sets this out, and the self-test asserts it at lines 1212-1213 and 1280.

The widening was deliberately NARROW: 8 navigated files plus one template payload, against 150 orphaned candidates, of which 137 are gate test fixtures under scripts/_test_fixtures/ and 4 are tools spec findings records carrying 33 stale targets. Those 141 were REFUSED with reasons and the refusal is correct. So the fix here is a DESCRIPTION, not a re-widening.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS. That paragraph exists to stop workers nominating the WRONG GATE. As written it implies the rosters cannot reach anything that is not a README or root markdown. A worker editing implementation/SECURITY.md or examples/TESTING.md would read CLAUDE.md, conclude neither gate covers it, then hand-verify and say so in the PR body — UNDERSTATING its coverage. That is the mirror of the rf2-8pb5k failure rather than a new class.

FIX: correct CLAUDE.md:116 so the gate's surface reads as three rosters plus the commands arm, naming the beside-source non-README roster and what it deliberately excludes. Keep it SHORT — that paragraph is already very long and the stance rejects gold-plating. Do not restate the 141 refusals; say only that the roster is narrow and deliberate.

ALSO CHECK, DO NOT ASSUME: AGENTS.md is an independent file, and CLAUDE.md's own closing note says substantive edits must be mirrored across both. If AGENTS.md carries the same paragraph, fix both in ONE commit or they drift immediately.

title: hicasso: a second ~1,050-1,224 B term at the SECOND-driven window, seen only under the fixed segment order
description:
OBSERVED but not chased by rf2-rs8q6's confound-breaker (PR #8545), record
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-rider-follows-the-position-not-the-substrate.md.
Filed rather than actioned: naming it was outside that bead's scope fence.

THE OBSERVATION. Under P0_ALLOC_SEG_ORDER=fixed, the SECOND-driven arm window of
a round — which under that mode is always uix-subs — carries a cluster of 8 of 38
collection-free windows whose worst leg sits at 1,050-1,224 B over the window's
own leg median. It is present in all three fixed runs separately (fixed-1: 1050,
1062; fixed-2: 1056, 1062, 1068, 1224; fixed-3: 1050, 1224).

IT IS NOT THE +748 B RIDER. It is outside that term's 700-800 B band, at a
different magnitude, and at the position the rider does not occupy — position 1
carries the rider once in those same 38 windows.

THE COMPARISON, which is what makes it worth a bead rather than noise. The
paired parity runs, taken in the same session on the same revision and box, read
1 of 23 in the same 1,000-1,300 B band at uix-subs/position-1 and 0 of 26 at
reagent-subs/position-1. The committed parity corpus is available for a wider
baseline and was not pooled for this.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and n is small so the first move is more data rather than a
mechanism hunt: replicate at higher n under both segment orders and check whether
the cluster tracks the SUBSTRATE (uix), the POSITION, or the segment ORDER mode
itself. Under fixed those three are confounded exactly as position and substrate
were before — position 1 is always uix — so a fixed-order run alone cannot
separate them, and the discriminator is a fixed run with the segment order
REVERSED (uix leading), which p0_run.cjs does not currently offer.

DO NOT DISCHARGE BY WIDENING tau. rf2-e9wr's refusal stands and rf2-rs8q6's fence
against widening is restated.

Explicitly: do NOT silently switch to a one-sided test after seeing the five discordances.
AUDIT #8619 DISCHARGED, PR #8633 (worker/paired-csca8), 2026-08-21 11:31 AUSEST. BEAD LEFT OPEN
DELIBERATELY -- see the disposition at the end. ANALYSIS-SIDE ONLY: no window taken, no bench

ALL SIX AUDIT POINTS VERIFIED AT origin/main AND ALL SIX HOLD. Nothing was refused.

  1. The paired census is exactly as the audit states: 0 both, 5 uix-only, 0 reagent-only,

  2. Post-hoc pooling: withdrawn.
  3. Pre-registration gap (no paired test, no sidedness, no threshold): recorded in its own

  4. POSITION deliberately CHANGED (uix|pos0 vs reagent|pos1), not held constant: corrected

  5. FIXTURE PIN REPLACED. fisherExactTwoSided(5,5,0,10) is no longer an invariant of the

  6. 'More runs were never going to settle it': RETRACTED, with arithmetic. With b
     discordant pairs all one way the smallest attainable two-sided p is 2/2^b; five
     discordant pairs cannot go below 0.0625 by construction. This window's OWN fixed arm,
     ten pairs of the SAME runs under the SAME test at the SAME band, reaches p = 0.0039 on
     nine discordant pairs -- pinned as MIRROR, a positive control on the paired test itself.

NO ONE-SIDED TEST WAS RETROFITTED. The fence is honoured and restated on the page and in
the reader.

BOTH READINGS STAY PINNED. This change adds a THIRD reading and deletes neither of the
first two: signed-furthest and any-leg are both computed, both printed, each now with a

FORK TAKEN: RETRACT, not continuation. No continuation is designed anywhere in this PR.

TWO FURTHER ERRORS FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, both corrected and both pinned. These are NOT in

  (a) The pooled '6 of 15 against 0 of 15, p = 0.0169' REPRODUCES UNDER NO READING AND

  (b) The STAYS run-level count was published as '10 of 10 runs against 1 of 10'. It is

STUDIO INDEX ROWS CORRECTED TOO. docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md rows 135-137 all

MEASUREMENT-LANE TRIAGE 2026-08-21 03:21 AUSEST. Read-only pass, no repository file touched.

ESTIMAND: ALLOCATION (bytes). The term is a leg excess in B over the window's own leg median. Exempt from the quiet box per rf2-ojehu's measured drained-vs-loaded result (39 of 72 certified drained against 41 of 72 loaded).

CENSUS RE-DERIVED at origin/main 3572d6e9a3 from `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/segorder-rs8q6/`. Collection-free floor windows (falls == 0), worst leg minus legMedian, band 1,000-1,300 B:

  fixed   reagent-subs pos0   0 / 43
  fixed   uix-subs     pos1   9 / 38     <- bead says 8 of 38
  parity  reagent-subs pos0   0 / 20
  parity  reagent-subs pos1   0 / 26
  parity  uix-subs     pos0   1 / 20
  parity  uix-subs     pos1   1 / 23

The DENOMINATOR 38 matches this bead exactly. The NUMERATOR is 9, not 8: fixed-2 carries FIVE in-band windows (rounds 4, 6, 10, 12, 14 at 1,056 / 1,224 / 1,068 / 1,062 / 1,056 B), and the bead's list gives four. Minor, and it does not change the direction.

THE THREE-WAY QUESTION IS TWO-THIRDS ANSWERED BY DATA ALREADY COMMITTED, and the bead's stated blocker is partly superseded. The bead says "the discriminator is a fixed run with the segment order REVERSED (uix leading), which p0_run.cjs does not currently offer". But PARITY mode already supplies uix at position 0 for 20 windows, because the segment order reverses on odd rounds — so the position arm exists in the corpus:

  POSITION is REFUTED as the carrier.  Within parity, at matched substrate: uix pos0 1/20 vs uix pos1 1/23. Fisher two-sided p = 1.0. No position effect at all.
  SUBSTRATE is CONFIRMED as necessary.  Pooling both modes: uix 11/81 vs reagent 0/89. Fisher p = 1.96e-04. Not one reagent window in 89 lands in the band.
  MODE is ASSOCIATED.  At matched substrate: fixed 9/38 vs parity 2/43. Fisher p = 0.0204.

So the term rides the uix substrate, is indifferent to position within a round, and appears about five times more often under `fixed` than under `parity` at matched substrate AND matched position. That is the three-way separation the bead wanted, minus one arm.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and I am not claiming it does. It does not separate the `fixed` MODE from anything else that co-varies with it in these three runs, and 9 versus 2 is small n on both sides. It names no mechanism. And "seen only under the fixed segment order" is strictly wrong as written — the term appears twice under parity, just at the lower rate.

RUN NEEDED? NOT for the substrate/position separation, which is done above. A replication at higher n would firm the mode contrast, and that is an allocation window: bench-slot-bound, not quiet-box-bound.

FILES: analysis — `data/segorder-rs8q6/`, a reader beside `alloc_position_confound.cjs` (which already exists for exactly this class of question and launches nothing), a page under `docs/design/hicasso/studio/`. Any reversed-fixed rig arm would touch `implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs` at ALLOC_SEG_ORDERS (line 1717) — shared with rf2-fk6pj and rf2-onozm, so one-toucher.

VERDICT: dispatchable TODAY, beside anything, as an ANALYSIS bead. Do not widen tau; nothing here asks for it.
