ANALYSIS DELIVERED, rf2-csca8, 2026-08-21. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cluster-follows-the-mode-and-the-third-arm-is-still-missing.md (PR #8593). NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN, no rig file edited, tau untouched. New reader alloc_cluster_carrier.cjs, self-test 30/30.

BEAD STAYS OPEN. Its central question is answered in two arms of three and REFUSED in the third, and the discriminating arm is still unbuilt. Closing would drop it.

RE-DERIVED ON THE FULL COMMITTED FLOOR CORPUS -- 118 runs, 3,308 collection-free windows, 3,140 in the position tables (controlSlot=first) -- rather than the three paired runs the 2026-08-21 03:21 triage used. Statistic: worst leg per window over its own leg median, falls===0. Test: Fisher exact two-sided, because several cells carry 0 or 1 successes where the neighbouring record's two-proportion z is undefined.

  POSITION   REFUTED, and now with power: parity uix 8/747 pos0 vs 3/724 pos1, p = 0.2254.
             The triage reached this from 1/20 vs 1/23, p = 1.0. It was right, on 2.9% of
             the available evidence.
  SUBSTRATE  ASSOCIATED but NOT NECESSARY: parity uix 11/1471 vs reagent 2/1588, p = 0.0102.
             The triage's 'not one reagent window in 89 lands in the band' does NOT survive
             widening -- reagent carries it twice in 1,588. On 89 windows the expected count
             was 0.11, so a zero there was the likeliest single outcome and bounded nothing.
  MODE       CONFIRMED and it is the only arm left: fixed uix pos1 8/38 vs parity uix pos1
             3/724, p = 2.67e-9. BUT the strictly matched same-session contrast -- against
             the three parity runs interleaved with the fixed ones -- is 8/38 vs 1/23,
             p = 0.1344. The triage's p = 0.0204 pools POSITIONS (2/43). Both stated on the
             page; neither dominates.

THE BEAD'S COUNT IS NOT WRONG. The '9 in-band, not 8' is an ESTIMATOR difference. fixed-2 round 4 uix-subs has leg excesses 0, -12, 0, -4324, +1056, 0. Read as the excess furthest from the cohort median (legWorstDeviation re-derived, the reading alloc_position_confound.cjs publishes) its worst leg is -4,324 B and is out of band; read as the largest excess above the median it is +1,056 B and is in. That reader has pinned BOTH since it was written. Neither count is an error; a record quoting one owes the reader which.

'SEEN ONLY UNDER THE FIXED SEGMENT ORDER' IS FALSE, confirmed -- 11 parity windows in band, not zero.

METHODOLOGICAL FINDING, and it bounds my own result as well as the triage's. The two bands this bead names do not answer the same question. The wider 1,000-1,300 B band admits a SECOND, DIFFERENT term: at parity position 0 its in-band legs sit at the LAST leg ordinal 43 times in 48, where the fixed cluster never lands there (0 of 11), and only 8 of those 45 windows sit inside 1,050-1,224. Under the wide band the POSITION verdict inverts to p = 8.82e-11 -- and that inversion is about the last-leg term, not the cluster. Both bands are reported; the bead's own 1,050-1,224 is primary. The last-leg term is described, not chased, and is nobody's yet.

THE RIG CHANGE IS STILL NEEDED, and the triage's reason for saying otherwise does not survive. Parity does supply uix at position 0 (747 windows), and that is what refutes POSITION -- but it supplies it UNDER PARITY, and the one arm that survived is the MODE. Inside fixed, uix is always position 1, so substrate and position stay perfectly confounded there in all 81 fixed windows: 8/38 is consistent with 'uix under fixed' and with 'second-driven under fixed', and no committed run separates them. A fixed run with the order REVERSED is the only arrangement that puts uix at position 0 while holding the mode constant.

SIZED, NOT MADE (p0_run.cjs was fenced off this dispatch and is one-toucher with rf2-fk6pj / rf2-onozm): THREE LINES -- one name in ALLOC_SEG_ORDERS (:1717), one branch in allocSegmentOrder (:1821-:1824), and NOTHING in the preflight (:2582-:2585), which already interpolates the roster. No reader, schema or record change: the record already carries segOrder per run and both readers group on that field rather than recomputing a parity rule.

ALSO RECORDED, NOT ACTED ON. That -4,324 B leg is a leg something REMOVED bytes from, and nothing in the work unit removes bytes -- the collector does. Its window carries falls===0, so the falls gate did not see it. That is a bound on the gate. NO GATE WAS WIDENED OR NARROWED and none is proposed.

ONE THING FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED, filed here rather than actioned. alloc_position_confound.cjs's synth() FIXTURE BUILDER (:849) recomputes the segment order as `segOrder === 'fixed' || r % 2 === 0`, so it cannot yet synthesise a fixed-reversed record. It is that reader's SELF-TEST INPUT and not a reader of real data -- real records are grouped on the recorded segOrder field (:196, :264), which handles the new arm correctly -- so nothing is broken today. But a self-test arm for fixed-reversed would need that ternary widened. The whole hicasso bench tree was fenced to worker/foldwin-nkeba this dispatch, so it was not touched. Small, and it belongs to whoever takes the window.

GATES: node core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs -- captured exit 0, 100 passed (96 on origin/main; one of the four new tests is THE REVERSED FIXED ARM). node hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/alloc_position_confound.cjs --self-test -- captured exit 0, 33/33, i.e. the neighbouring reader is unaffected. comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8593 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): exact open owner updated; no duplicate.

Two corrections are required before this analysis can support its headline verdicts.

1. THE CORPUS INCLUDES CONTROL-REFUSED RUNS. `alloc_cluster_carrier.cjs` filters for `plan=floor`, `falls===0`, and `controlSlot=first`, but never checks `controlVerdict.ok`. It therefore includes `alloc-77gz8/run12-a4a1537cb71` and `alloc-9jrhi/bisect-5-a-4a1537cb71-replicate`, both of which have `controlVerdict.ok=false`. The latter is the exact refused control this same PR correctly excludes on `the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md`. Filtering those two changes the claimed corpus from 118 runs / 3,308 collection-free / 3,140 positional windows to 116 / 3,258 / 3,090, and changes parity denominators (uix pos0 747→733, uix pos1 724→712, reagent pos0 675→666, reagent pos1 913→898). Primary-band numerators remain 8/3/2/0 and the qualitative descriptive pattern survives, but the reader, page, fixtures, and close/update record must use one admissibility rule consistently.

2. THE INFERENTIAL VERDICTS OUTRUN THE DESIGN. Fisher is applied to individual windows as though they were independent trials, although windows are repeated within runs and the `fixed` exposure consists of only three runs in one session. The page itself concedes the controlled same-session mode comparison is 8/38 vs 1/23 with p=0.1344 and the pooled p=2.67e-9 carries session/date/revision as uncontrolled terms. That supports a large pooled association worth the reversed-fixed arm, not the headline `MODE CONFIRMED` / `the MODE carries it`. Likewise 8/747 vs 3/724, p=0.2254 is failure to reject equality, not `POSITION REFUTED`; its window-level odds ratio is about 2.6 and no power/equivalence bound is supplied. Reword these as associated/unresolved unless a run/session-blocked analysis or the planned reversed-fixed matched arm establishes them.

The bead correctly stays open and already owns the discriminating rig arm. Preserve the valid estimator split, ordinal finding, and descriptive counts after admissibility repair; do not create a new statistics or rig bead.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8596 follow-through: exact open owner updated; no duplicate.

The fixed-reversed implementation is mechanically sound and remains the right matched discriminator, but this PR embeds PR #8593's already-audited statistical overclaims into shipping rig source and its structural test. `p0_run.cjs` now says 8/747 versus 3/724 "refuted POSITION" and leaves MODE as "the only surviving arm"; `p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs` repeats that PR #8593 refuted position on 3,140 windows. Those denominators include the two control-refused datasets already named on this bead (admissible parity denominators are 733/712), p=0.2254 is failure to reject rather than evidence of equivalence/refutation, and the fixed exposure is only three runs in one session. The strictly matched comparison remains 8/38 versus 1/23, p=0.1344.

Do not remove the new arm: its matched window is exactly the stronger evidence this unresolved design needs. Correct the source/test narrative to the existing audit framing (descriptive pooled association; position and mode unresolved pending admissible run/session-blocked evidence) when this owner is repaired, so future rig readers are not taught that a non-significant window-level Fisher test proved absence.

comments.text:
BOTH AUDIT CORRECTIONS LANDED, PR #8598 (worker/admissible-6kxub). BEAD STAYS OPEN -- the corrections are made, but the bead's central question is still owed a WINDOW, not an analysis. NO WINDOW, BENCHMARK OR BROWSER RUN WAS TAKEN; no rig file edited; tau untouched in either direction.

(1) ADMISSIBILITY. Re-derived first-hand and the audit's figures held to the digit. alloc_cluster_carrier.cjs now fails closed through admit()/partition(), which NAME every refusal rather than dropping it, and the report prints them. Corpus 118/3,308/3,140 -> 116/3,258/3,090. Parity denominators uix pos0 747->733, uix pos1 724->712, reagent pos0 675->666, reagent pos1 913->898. PRIMARY-BAND NUMERATORS UNCHANGED AT 8/3/2/0 -- neither refused run carried an in-band window, so nothing this record claims positively rested on them; only the denominators were computed over too many windows. bisect-5 is now refused here as the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md already refused it, so the tree no longer contradicts itself about one dataset.

ONE JUDGEMENT WORTH NOT REDISCOVERING. The READER CONTROL (the published 387/182/205, 101+11) is deliberately computed BEFORE admissibility. Its job is to detect drift in the window extraction by reproducing a figure an earlier record published over all fourteen runs; filtering it would compare against a number nobody ever published and turn a cross-check into a restatement of this reader's own output. The admissible reading (359/169/190, 92+10) is printed and pinned beside it, so neither has to be inferred.

(2) THE INFERENTIAL VERDICTS OUTRAN THE DESIGN, and they have been WEAKENED rather than recomputed. No test was swapped for a smaller p; the arithmetic is exactly what the first version computed, on a corrected corpus, and the claims came down to meet it.

  POSITION   REFUTED -> UNRESOLVED. p = 0.2253 is a failure to reject, and the point estimate is an ODDS RATIO OF ABOUT 2.6 in favour of position 0. Calling that refuted read a non-significant p as evidence of absence. No equivalence bound is offered because none is computable at a useful width on eleven in-band windows, and the page says so rather than implying one.
  MODE       CONFIRMED -> ASSOCIATED, NOT ESTABLISHED AT A MATCHED BASELINE. The pooled p = 3.02e-9 spans 107 runs across several sessions, dates and revisions. The matched same-session contrast is 8/38 against 1/23, p = 0.1344. And a third figure the record did not previously carry: AT RUN LEVEL the matched contrast is 3 of 3 fixed runs against 1 of 3 parity runs, p = 0.4. Three runs is the entire fixed exposure and no arithmetic on the windows inside them turns it into a controlled comparison.
  SUBSTRATE  unchanged, and now with its reason stated. Its non-necessity is the one refutation the design supports, because it rests on OBSERVING the thing claimed impossible rather than on failing to observe a difference.

A RUN-LEVEL CENSUS is now published beside every window-level one, and a new section bounds every p on the page. Notable in it: all three fixed runs carry the term (so it is not one anomalous run) but one supplies half the in-band windows, while every parity cell is at most ONE in-band window per run at the primary band -- so the repeated-measures problem bites hardest on precisely the arm the strongest claim rested on. NO cluster-robust or mixed-effects estimate is offered and none should be: with three clusters in one arm a variance component is not identifiable and a cluster-robust SE is badly biased. The right answer to three clusters is more clusters.

ALSO UPDATED, because PR #8596 merged while this was in flight: the reversed-fixed arm has LANDED. P0_ALLOC_SEG_ORDER=fixed-reversed is now one of three names in ALLOC_SEG_ORDERS and the branch is in allocSegmentOrder, verified on the landed tree. The page's three-line sizing held and is now recorded as spent rather than proposed. THE ARM EXISTING IS NOT THE ARM ANSWERING -- no dataset has been recorded through it, so nothing on the page is read against it.

WHAT KEEPS THIS BEAD OPEN, unchanged from the 2026-08-20 18:52 comment: a fixed-reversed run at adequate n, read against the fixed and parity arms already in the corpus, statistic worst-leg-per-collection-free-window over its own leg median with falls===0 and band 1,050-1,224 B primary. Bench-slot-bound, not quiet-box-bound. The strictly matched same-session contrast is what needs power, not the pooled one -- and after this correction that is doubly true, since the run-level version of it has none at all.

FIXTURES 30 -> 54. Synthetic pins for both refusal shapes plus one that proves the exclusion DISCRIMINATES (the refused synthetic record carries an in-band window, so a reader skipping the check would count it); corpus pins naming both real refusals; pins on the corrected denominators AND on the numerators being unchanged; and run-level pins including the 3-of-3-against-1-of-3 matched contrast.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
WINDOW TAKEN, PR #8611 (worker/revarm-csca8). BEAD STAYS OPEN. Record:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-reversed-fixed-arm-a-pre-registered-fifteen-run-window.md.
NO RIG FILE TOUCHED -- p0_run.cjs was frozen for the window and stayed frozen; the arm
was used exactly as PR #8596 shipped it. TAU UNTOUCHED in either direction.

WHAT WAS TAKEN. Fifteen runs, one session, one revision, one box, interleaved ONE AT A
TIME: five fixed-reversed, five fixed, five parity. Configuration identical to
segorder-rs8q6's six. PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUNNER RAN ONCE (commits fb93d522cb and
3f85e96ef7 on the branch): run count, interleave, statistic, worst-leg reading, band,
admissibility rule, level read and stopping rule all fixed in advance, Result section
committed deliberately empty. All fifteen taken, none dropped or re-rolled, all fifteen
control-certified. 540 arm windows, 430 collection-free. Every run exited 1 on the falls
gate (4-16 collections) and the leg-tolerance gate (9-24 windows) -- this row's normal
verdict and by construction outside a statistic defined over falls === 0.

THE ARM DRIVES CORRECTLY, pinned as a positive control: every round of every
fixed-reversed run drove uix-subs then reagent-subs; every fixed round drove reagent then
uix; parity alternated.

(1) THE SLOT HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. With reagent-subs in the second-driven slot the
cluster does not go with it: 1 of 82 windows against the same session's 8 of 63 at
fixed|uix-subs|pos1, p = 0.0105 -- and 1 of 82 against 10 of 63 on the masking-free
companion, p = 0.0011. That is the one arm this window closes.

(2) THE SUBSTRATE HYPOTHESIS IS NOT SETTLED, AND THE REASON IS A DEFECT IN THE
PRE-REGISTERED STATISTIC RATHER THAN A SHORTAGE OF RUNS. The statistic counts a window
only when the in-band leg is that window's WORST. fixed-reversed|uix-subs|pos0 has a
median |worst leg| of 1,488 B -- ABOVE the band top -- with 35 of its 68 windows worse
than 1,224 B. The competing term is already on the record: POSITION 0 IS WHERE THE ~748 B
RIDER LIVES, and the-rider-follows-the-position-not-the-substrate.md established it is
position-locked rather than substrate-locked. So the reversed arm's uix cell reads 1 of 68
on the pre-registered statistic largely because a bigger term wins the maximum.

A MASKING-FREE COMPANION -- windows carrying an in-band leg whether or not it is the worst
-- puts that cell at 7.4% in FOUR OF FIVE RUNS, against fixed's 20.8% and parity's 1.3% at
the same substrate and position. IT IS POST-HOC, written after the window was read, and it
is labelled post-hoc everywhere it appears in the reader and on the page. It carries no
verdict on its own and none is rested on it. Of the windows carrying an in-band leg, the
share where it IS the worst is 80% under fixed and 20% under fixed-reversed -- that is the
masking, as a number.

So the pre-registered branch taken is NEITHER; the companion says the cluster DOES follow
uix at about a third the rate. Both are published; neither is discarded and neither stands
alone.

(3) THE METHODOLOGICAL FINDING, AND IT WAS KNOWABLE IN ADVANCE. The discriminator's DESIGN
and its STATISTIC are in tension. The reversed arm exists to move uix to position 0;
position 0 is where the rider inflates the worst leg; the statistic is a per-window
MAXIMUM. A reversed-arm read was always going to under-count at uix, and the rider record
predates this window by days. RECORDED RATHER THAN REPAIRED: repairing it means
pre-registering a masking-free statistic and taking the window AGAIN, and choosing the
statistic after seeing which one gives the wanted answer is what pre-registration exists
to prevent.

(4) THE MATCHED MODE BASELINE NOW EXISTS, which is what the bead said had no power. This
window is 4 of 5 fixed runs against 0 of 5 parity runs at run level, p = 0.0476. With
segorder-rs8q6's 3 of 3 against 1 of 3 that is 7 of 8 against 1 of 8 across TWO matched
sessions, p = 0.0101 -- the first run-level separation the record has that controls
session, date and revision. BUT MODE NARROWS: fixed-reversed is exactly as non-alternating
as fixed and does not carry the term, so what separates from parity is THE FORWARD FIXED
ORDER SPECIFICALLY -- reagent-subs driven first and uix-subs second, every round -- and not
"a plan that does not alternate". The bead's own "seen only under the fixed segment order"
is now closer to true than the corpus suggested, but only for the forward order.

THE FLOOR READ, PUBLISHED BEFORE ANY COMPARATIVE, because worker/passwin-fk6pj had just
reported an unexplained ~20% floor excursion on this box. THERE IS NONE HERE. Three levels
appear and the THREE HIGH-MODE RUNS ARE ONE PER ARM, so level is not confounded with the
property under test. reversed-1 settled on the IDENTICAL reagent-subs level to
segorder-rs8q6/fixed-1 (21,844 B) and agrees to 6 B on uix-subs, across two sessions, two
dates and two segment-order modes. Null arm: 4,818 control legs, 0 in band.

NO CLUSTER-ROBUST OR MIXED-EFFECTS ESTIMATE IS OFFERED and none should be at five clusters
per arm. Every window-level p is published beside its run-level counterpart.

CORPUS after this window: 131 admissible floor runs / 3,688 collection-free / 3,520
positional, from 116 / 3,258 / 3,090. The two control-refused runs are still named and
still refused. Reader fixtures 54 -> 64, including a scoped set for this window that
pins the CARRIER contrast, the 4-of-5-against-0-of-5 matched run-level contrast, the
one-high-mode-run-per-arm level result and the arm's own positive control.

WHAT NOW KEEPS THIS BEAD OPEN, and it is a narrower question than before:
- The SLOT arm is closed. Do not re-run it.
- The SUBSTRATE arm needs ONE more window, under a MASKING-FREE statistic PRE-REGISTERED
  AS SUCH before the runner is invoked. The rig needs no change -- the arm exists and this
  window shows it drives correctly. What must change is the declared statistic.
- Do not widen tau. Nothing here asks for it and nothing here moved it.

ALSO NOTED, NOT ACTIONED. docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md's rf2-csca8 row is STALE
against PR #8598 -- it still reads POSITION REFUTED / MODE CONFIRMED over 118 runs /
3,140 windows, which that PR corrected to unresolved/associated over 116 / 3,090. The
README is another bead's and was not touched; a suggested replacement row plus this
correction are in PR #8611's body.

comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8619 (2026-08-21) — REOPENED THIS EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE BEAD.

CORRECTNESS. The page and reader correctly identify CARRIER as the only within-run contrast, but then discard that pairing at the decisive step. The ten paired runs contain 5 uix-only hits, 0 reagent-only hits, 5 neither, and 0 both. `alloc_cluster_carrier.cjs` nevertheless pins `fisherExactTwoSided(5, 5, 0, 10) = 0.0325`, which treats the two arm-level run censuses as independent. The corresponding two-sided exact McNemar/sign result is 2 / 2^5 = 0.0625. Therefore the new pre-registered window does NOT support the page's statements that the primary “survives at run level” or resolves the substrate arm. The window-level p=0.0017 cannot rescue that claim because the page itself correctly says those repeated windows are not independent. Pooling the older five pairs gives 6 discordances and a paired two-sided p=0.03125, but those older records informed selection of `any-leg` and are explicitly POST-HOC under this page's own pre-registration; they cannot turn the new window into confirmatory evidence.

COMPLETENESS. The pre-registration names the within-run contrast but no paired test, sidedness, or inferential decision threshold. The landed result retrofits a two-sided independent Fisher calculation. Add the paired run table and paired exact calculation to the reader/report and pin them; then retract the standalone resolution or take a properly pre-registered continuation. Do not silently switch to a one-sided test after seeing the five discordances.

A SECOND CLAIM NEEDS CORRECTION. The primary compares `uix-subs | pos0` with `reagent-subs | pos1`; POSITION is deliberately changed, not “held constant by construction.” The same run holds mode, session, revision, box, and level. The broader crossover evidence may still distinguish position, but this primary contrast alone cannot be described as holding it fixed.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY. The corpus fixture currently makes the independent-sample p-value an invariant, so the test suite protects the defect. Replace that pin with the actual paired table/test. Also retract “more runs were never going to settle this”: 3/136 versus 0/161 at n=10 does not establish that a persistent nonzero rate could never resolve at larger n; it establishes only that this window did not.

TWO DISPATCHES HAVE NOW RE-DERIVED THE SAME ERROR because a ruling lives only in the tracker.

rf2-0moc4 (closed 2026-08-18) ruled that docs/design/freehand/ is KEEP, after R6b refused an instruction to delete it. On 2026-08-20 a second worker was dispatched at the same tree and refused again, having measured the same consequence independently: deleting the 37 files takes scripts/check_doc_slugs.py to exit 1 with 4 broken targets, all of them inbound links from docs/design/hicasso/ (hd-002-adjudication.md:158 and :566 to ../freehand/studio/bulk-rerender-where-the-time-goes.md; product/requirements-mine.md:15 and :108 to ../../freehand/studio/fitness-harness.md).

rf2-0yp7w.9's description has now been corrected in place, which was that ruling's own Consequence A and was overdue. THIS BEAD IS THE OTHER HALF.

THE GAP. docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md is cited as 'the full survey' and 'the authority' for this retirement programme, but around L370 it still lists docs/design/freehand/ as in scope, and carries no record of the KEEP ruling. A reader consulting the named authority therefore gets the superseded answer, and the correct one is reachable only by finding a closed bead.

FIX: one short passage in docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md recording that docs/design/freehand/ is KEEP, with the deciding reason (the hicasso coupling) and the measurement. Verify the L370 line number at source before editing; it comes from a worker report, not from a fresh read.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING while there: docs/EP/EP-0036 cites the tree 17 times and already asserts it remains, so it may need nothing. Confirm rather than assume.

GATE: docs/ is one of scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS, so that script covers link targets and anchors. It cannot see a false disposition claim, so this is a read-and-judge fix. mkdocs.yml exclude_docs keeps docs/design/** out of the site, so mkdocs build --strict is NOT the gate here.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8550 (merge 8b3a5fb87abdc8a923b46c644b00e27951fae89d, 2026-08-20): REOPEN. The authority now records KEEP and the decisive coupling, but its operative R6 instruction is internally contradictory. The new list says docs/design/freehand/ is “in scope for editing”; the next paragraph says its 37 files remain “with their contents untouched”; the following sentence again says they “are edited for stale status like any other prose surface”; and the supporting EP language calls the tree a “durable, frozen supporting record.” A worker cannot tell whether KEEP means no deletion only, no content edits, or bounded status-only edits — exactly the ambiguity this authority-page repair was meant to prevent after two refusals. Bounded completion: without re-ruling rf2-0moc4, distinguish the null/no-deletion disposition from any permitted R6 prose edits, explicitly protect the frozen measurement/evidence surfaces, and leave one coherent imperative. Preserve the landed four-link measurement, lapsed-support correction, and EP/exclude_docs evidence.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8563 (2026-08-21 AUSEST) — REOPENED AS THE EXACT OWNER; no duplicate filed.

The PR correctly separates KEEP/no-deletion from bounded editing and gives `studio/` the narrower frozen rule. But the promised “one coherent imperative” silently drops half of the authority it has just called “the whole of R6's permission.” The preceding paragraph quotes EP-0036's four allowed corrections: stale status, broken links, factual errors, and contradictions with rulings. The final operative line permits only “stale status and broken links” outside `studio/`, then says “add nothing.” A worker is still left to decide whether correcting a factual error or ruling contradiction outside the studio is permitted — the same class of ambiguity this PR exists to remove.

Make the final imperative enumerate all four EP-0036 correction classes (or refer to that exact four-part bound unambiguously), while preserving the no-growth rule, the absolute `studio/` freeze, and no deletion anywhere. The rest of #8563's reconciliation and measurements hold.

title: docs-gate: 128 tracked markdown files are covered by NEITHER link gate — implementation/SECURITY.md is the instance that surfaced it
description:
MEASURED by the mayor 2026-08-20, prompted by a worker refuting my gate nomination on PR #8542. Every figure is a CLAIM — re-derive before acting.

HOW IT SURFACED. I briefed a worker that `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` covers `implementation/SECURITY.md`, citing CLAUDE.md's "every README.md beside source code, implementation/** included". The worker MEASURED it instead of trusting me: it planted a broken cross-file anchor, then a broken FILE target, and the gate returned exit 0 on both. Reading the source, `_iter_root_markdown` DROPS any entry containing "/", so that gate's roster is READMEs anywhere plus ROOT markdown only. `implementation/SECURITY.md` is not a README, so NO GATE COVERS IT. My nomination silently generalised "READMEs beside source" to "any markdown beside source". CLAUDE.md itself is accurate; I misread it.

THE GAP IS NOT ONE FILE. Partitioning all tracked markdown at the tip:
  * 977 tracked `.md` files.
  * `check_doc_slugs.py` covers 747 — its DEFAULT_ROOTS (docs, spec, skills, migration) plus the `tools/*/spec` tier `_iter_markdown` adds.
  * `check_readme_links.py --ci` covers 138 — READMEs anywhere plus root markdown.
  * **128 files are covered by NEITHER**, once the 7 `.claude/commands/*.md` are set aside.

CAVEAT ON THAT NUMBER, and it matters: `.claude/commands/*.md` ARE reached by `check_readme_links.py`'s third arm (rf2-1yy75), which resolves path-shaped REFERENCES rather than anchors. I excluded them above. They are therefore partially covered, not orphaned, and any fix must not double-cover them.

WHAT IS IN THE ORPHANED SET — a sample, not the roster:
  * examples/TESTING.md
  * implementation/SECURITY.md
  * implementation/adapters/TESTING.md
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/absolute_path_ok/docs/index.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/absolute_path_ok/docs/target.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/ai_findings_dir_link_flagged/docs/index.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/ai_findings_link_flagged/docs/index.md

Nothing validates link targets or heading anchors in any of them. A broken link there is invisible to CI forever.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A DECISION RATHER THAN AN AUTOMATIC FIX. The stance rejects gold-plating, and "every markdown file must be link-checked" may simply not be worth it for design rationales and internal notes that no reader navigates by link. The honest question is which of the 128 are NAVIGATED — cited from elsewhere, or carrying cross-references someone follows — and those are the ones that want covering. A blanket widening of either gate's roots is the over-engineered answer and would also change what those gates mean.

SO THE DELIVERABLE IS: classify the orphaned set, propose the narrowest widening that covers the navigated part, and say explicitly what is left uncovered and why that is acceptable. **A reasoned refusal — "these are all internal notes, leave them" — is a complete and good deliverable**, provided it names what it examined.

DO NOT widen a gate's roots without checking the CI arming: a root added to `check_doc_slugs.py` validates nothing if no PR-time job runs it on that surface. rf2-v7fui is the precedent — `skills` sat in DEFAULT_ROOTS for months while no PR job ran the script on a skills path.

HOT ZONE: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `scripts/check_readme_links.py` are one-toucher-at-a-time surfaces, and `.github/workflows/*` likewise. Sequence behind PR #8539, which is changing `.github/workflows/` right now.
close_reason: Delivered in PR #8546 as a classification plus a narrow widening. RE-DERIVED the counts and three of the four moved: 977 tracked .md CONFIRMED; check_doc_slugs.py covers 744 not 747 (four tools/*/spec/findings/ docs excluded by name); check_readme_links.py --ci scans 76 not 138 (the 138 counted every README, but 62 sit under the docs-gate roots and are deliberately excluded — the two rosters are DISJOINT by construction); so the orphaned set is 150, not 128. BUT 137 OF THE 150 ARE GATE TEST FIXTURES under scripts/_test_fixtures/ — deliberately-broken markdown the gates' own self-tests consume; covering them is wrong, not merely gold-plating, and _test_fixtures is already an exclusion in check_readme_links.py. Four more are tools/*/spec/findings/ design records: MEASURED, they carry 33 stale relative targets between them (../spec/012-Routing.md from inside tools/xray/spec/findings/ resolves to tools/xray/spec/spec/...), exactly the exploratory link rot the standing 'findings' exclusion exists to leave alone — covering them would red main on day one. REFUSED both, 141 files. That leaves 13, of which 8 are unambiguously NAVIGATED: implementation/SECURITY.md (root README cites it, 36 relative targets, cross-file anchors into spec/), examples/TESTING.md (14 inbound citations), implementation/adapters/TESTING.md, the reagent-slim design trio, and tools/mcp-conformance/{NAMING,TOKEN-BUDGETS}.md which spec/Conventions.md and spec/Tool-Pair.md cite NORMATIVELY. New _iter_source_markdown roster covers them and needs NO new exclusion — _is_excluded already refuses fixtures, docs-gate roots and tools/*/spec/. It takes one extra file, a template payload whose sibling this gate already walks under the same mustache guard. Zero findings today, so it lands green as a ratchet. ARMING CHECKED (the rf2-v7fui trap): verify-readme-links has no if: and no surface guard, test.yml's PR trigger is unfiltered, and the job is in all-required-passed's needs — which is why the roster went here and not in check_doc_slugs.py. Proven by planting: a broken target in implementation/SECURITY.md now reds this gate naming that line, where the PRE-CHANGE gate exited 0 on the identical fault and check_doc_slugs.py still does. Self-test asserts each REFUSAL, not only membership, and both refusals were confirmed to bite.

title: hic: rule whether inventory.cljs's :what DATA strings may carry bead ids — 5 sites survive rf2-ww5at's fence
description:
NEEDS A RULING, NOT A SWEEP. Raised by rf2-ww5at's worker as an owed follow-up (PR #8535, merged 2026-08-20) and left deliberately unactioned, correctly.

THE SITUATION. rf2-ww5at removed bead-id citations from comments and docstrings across `implementation/hicasso/src/`. It was fenced OUT of DATA strings, so the `:what` values in `impl/inventory.cljs` still carry bead ids. Those values are not narration in a docstring — they are the inventory table's own payload.

THE COUNT IS A CLAIM AND THE TWO READINGS DISAGREE. The worker reported 4 sites. My own census at the merged tip reads 5, at `impl/inventory.cljs` lines 59, 61, 65, 67 and 81 — citing rf2-dabt3 (twice), rf2-2rtt6.39 with rf2-2rtt6.72, rf2-2rtt6.52, and rf2-digtt. Re-derive at origin/main HEAD before acting; neither number is authoritative and mine may be counting a line the worker excluded on purpose.

WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT MINUTIAE. The ids here are doing real work. Read line 65: it tells a reader that the frame-fed variant does not hold this token, that a ladder reading the table must subtract it and add a props slot, and it cites where that was priced. Strip the id and the reader loses the route to the evidence. So the question is not "are bead ids untidy" — it is whether the inventory's `:what` values are INTERNAL PROSE, in which case dehistoricalising them is right, or a PROVENANCE-BEARING RECORD consumed by a tool or a ladder, in which case the citations are the point and removing them destroys the trail.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH BEFORE RULING — this is cheap and read-only:
  1. Who CONSUMES `:what`? Grep for readers of the inventory table across `implementation/` and `tools/`. If a test, a ladder or a tool renders those strings, they are a record.
  2. Do the cited beads resolve? On the src/ sweep, 72 ids were removed and only 2 resolved to open or deferred, both provenance. Run the same check on these 5.
  3. Does any other data table in this tree carry the same pattern? A one-file rule is a smell; a repo-wide convention is a decision.

THE STANCE APPLIES DIRECTLY. We reject over-engineering and CLOSE minutiae rather than actioning it. If the answer is "these are provenance and they stay", that is a complete deliverable and this bead closes with the reasoning recorded — no edit. A source-located refusal is the likeliest correct outcome here, and nobody should feel obliged to produce a diff.

DO NOT sweep these until the ruling exists.

title: [retire] dehistoricalise implementation/hicasso/test/ — the slice rf2-ww5at did not reach

title: hicasso: the restore-hash rule and check_provenance_pins.py collide on docs/design/hicasso/ pages
description:
TWO OF THIS PROJECT'S OWN RULES COLLIDE, and the collision will recur for every worker on a docs/design/hicasso/ page.

RULE ONE (the gate-mechanics brief, pasted into every dispatch): verify a planted-fault restore by HASHING THE BYTES, using version control's own content hash against the committed object — never by reading a diff, because a patch that never applied and a correct restore produce the same diff. Workers are told to record that hash as evidence.

RULE TWO (scripts/check_provenance_pins.py, gated by .github/workflows/docs.yml job 'Provenance pins'): every 40-hex token on a changed page under docs/design/hicasso/ is extracted and classified as a cited authored head unless its nearest left-context word says digest. An unclassifiable token is a FINDING by design — the gate fails toward refusal.

THE COLLISION. A restore-verification hash is a SHA-1 BLOB hash, and it is naturally written in commit-flavoured prose: 'compared against the committed object'. 'committed' is in _COMMIT_WORDS; 'hash' is in _DIGEST_WORDS but sits further left. Nearest wins, so the token is read as a pin, resolves to no commit, and reds the job.

CONCRETE INSTANCE. PR #8536, docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-level-witness-armed-within-one-run.md:292. Gate output: '1 page inspected, 14 cited pins — 13 landed, 0 stranded, 1 unresolvable ... (commit word `commit` nearest on the left)'. `git cat-file -t 3dd95e0c268db8b517c802142b2a37de0acbae67` returns `blob`. Worked around in that PR by naming the token a blob so the nearest-word rule classifies it as a digest — the gate's own designed escape, which WORKS and needs no gate change to be usable.

SO THIS IS NOT URGENT AND MAY BE A DOC FIX RATHER THAN A CODE FIX. The escape exists and is discoverable only by reading a 2,300-line script. Options, in ascending cost: (a) add one line to the gate-mechanics brief telling workers to write 'blob' beside a restore hash, which costs nothing and fixes it at the source; (b) note the same in scripts/git-hooks/README.md or beside the gate; (c) teach the gate a restore-verification idiom. (a) is probably the whole fix.

DO NOT bundle this with a hicasso measurement bead — scripts/ and the dispatch briefs are separate surfaces.
close_reason: PR #8547: option (a) taken — one caution added to the restore-hashing block in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md telling workers to call a restore hash a blob hash in the words immediately before the token. Premise verified at source: _DIGEST_WORDS matches blob|digest|sha-?256|fnv|checksum|hash, _COMMIT_WORDS matches committed, classify() takes the nearest left signal with ties going to PIN, and the three phrasings were driven directly against classify() — the commit-flavoured one returns is_pin=True with reason 'commit word commit nearest on the left', the blob-named ones return is_pin=False. scripts/check_provenance_pins.py untouched; _DIGEST_WORDS not widened.

title: dehistoricalise implementation/hicasso: comments and docstrings state the present contract, not the journey
description:
Ruled by Mike (19 August 2026, chat). Rewrite comments and docstrings across implementation/hicasso so they state the PRESENT contract rather than the story of how it got here. Git history and the tracker own the archaeology; the source should read as if the current design had always been the design.

TARGET REGISTER, by example:
  BEFORE: ;; rf2-hic-009 carved the copied 2,120-line runtime into six owned
  ;;       modules after audit #7743 reopened the false green (2026-08-10)...
  AFTER:  ;; Six owned modules; each call site names the module that answers
  ;;       for the var it uses.
Rules:
- present tense, contract first: what is true, what it guards, what breaks if violated. Keep any constraint the code cannot show.
- delete pure narrative: dates, PR numbers, audit blow-by-blow, 'used to', 'before/after', superseded designs, reopened-over stories.
- remove ALL bead references. A citation of a closed bead is history: delete it (git blame recovers it from the commit message). Keep an id only where the comment documents a live obligation and the bead is still open or deferred — verify with bd show before keeping it, and delete the citation if the bead has closed.
- shrink, never pad: if a comment block is pure history, delete it whole.
- docstrings: same rules; they are consumer-facing, so plain contract statements only.

HARD FENCES — check before editing each file:
1. Do NOT touch src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/slot.cljc — the freeze gate (hicasso/frozen-sources.edn + hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py) pins it byte-for-byte; any comment edit reds CI. Do NOT touch frozen-sources.edn — its retirement is a separate ruled change; if that retirement lands first, slot.cljc unfreezes and joins this sweep as a follow-up slice.
2. Do NOT touch implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/** — measured evidence; its history IS the content.
3. Machine-read text is law: rf2:builder-bypass-ok marker comments (checker input, not citations), every refusal/complaint string (the complaint-catalogue gate round-trips them), diagnostic ids, and anything a checker parses. Byte-identical.
4. Pinned prose: some tests assert regexes against the SOURCE TEXT of other files (example: clock_exit_path.test.cjs pins comment sentences in clock_readjudicate.cjs). Before rewriting any distinctive sentence, grep the repo for a fragment of it; if a test or checker references it, leave it and list it in the PR body instead.
5. Comments and docstrings ONLY. Zero code changes, zero string changes, zero whitespace churn inside code. The diff must show no behaviour surface at all.

PROCESS:
- worker worktree off origin/main; run sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh before editing and report WORKTREE_ROOT. Check open PRs touching implementation/hicasso first and avoid files a live worker holds.
- slice: src/ in one PR; test/ (minus bench) in a second if the first grows past review size. Small reviewable PRs beat one mega-diff. The mayor may split this bead at dispatch.
- gates before each PR, foreground to completion: npm run test:hicasso-invariants, npm run test:hicasso-lint, and the focused hicasso CLJS suites (or npx shadow-cljs compile :node-test).
- PR body declares: comments and docstrings only, no behaviour change; lists any sentence left because pinned; names files where whole history blocks were deleted.

ACCEPTANCE:
- no dates, PR numbers, audit narratives or closed-bead citations remain in implementation/hicasso comments/docstrings outside the fenced files and pinned sentences
- every kept bead id resolves to an open or deferred bead
- slot.cljc, frozen-sources.edn and bench/** byte-identical
- all listed gates green; diff is comment/docstring-only
acceptance_criteria:
1. The non-bench `implementation/hicasso/test/**` comments and docstrings state the present contract under the same rules as #8535; machine-read markers, test descriptions/assertions, refusal text, evidence records, and other runtime strings are classified and preserved unless separately authorised.
2. `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/**`, `impl/slot.cljc`, and measured/frozen sources remain outside the sweep.
3. The `impl/inventory.cljs` `retained-inventory :what` Bead references receive an explicit contract-surface ruling: either a separately verified runtime-string rewrite or a documented retained exception.
4. Code identity and runtime-string inventories are mechanically checked, relevant Hicasso gates pass, and the Bead closes only after both remaining obligations are resolved rather than merely noted.

THE DELIVERABLE, which is rf2-hic-061's original acceptance clause:

  2. Prove a consumer app installs Hicasso from the ARTEFACT rather than from the repo.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD RATHER THAN rf2-hic-061 STAYING OPEN. A bead whose acceptance is gated on a third-party account action a month away is a calendar entry, not open work. Keeping it inside hic-061 made a finished deliverable read as unfinished and — the part that cost something — kept rf2-v04s blocked on a bead whose documentary half had shipped.

  • deploy-hicasso present in release.yml.

(a) SHAPE OF THE FIRST RELEASE — the repo-wide v0.0.1.alpha tag, publishing all 14 framework artefacts as one DAG. There is no Hicasso-only route and none is to be built. Verified at tip b26c5ad33e: .github/workflows/release.yml has exactly one trigger, the v* glob at lines 162-165 (`v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*`); the first job hard-fails unless the tag equals `v` + the VERSION file (lines 183-194), and VERSION reads 0.0.1.alpha, so the first valid tag is v0.0.1.alpha by construction. Jobs at tip: verify-version-lockstep 176 → test 203 → deploy-core 343 → deploy-leaf 430 (11-value matrix, fail-fast: false at 436) → deploy-ssr-ring 661 and deploy-hicasso 802 in parallel → github-release 890 (needs all four deploy stages, 898-902; artefact roster in the release body 926-939). deploy-hicasso declares needs: [deploy-core, deploy-leaf] (804-806) because implementation/hicasso/deps.edn:93-94 publishes two in-repo deps (day8/re-frame2 via ../core, day8/re-frame2-ssr via ../ssr), both rewritten to :mvn/version at deploy time (release.yml 863-875), so Hicasso's published pom only resolves if core and ssr already reached Clojars. implementation/scripts/_release-dag-policy.test.cjs pins exactly this: 14 publishers (line 282), the ssr→hicasso ancestry (acceptance at 335), and a TEETH case rejecting the dropped edge (380-388). grep of `hicasso-v` across .github/workflows/ returns 0; the prefixes that exist (story-v*, xray-v*, machines-viz-v*, template-v*) are tools-tier and presuppose the framework tier already on Clojars (docs/release-process.md §Release order, lines 149-158). The minimum coherent bespoke train would be core → ssr → hicasso (the reviewer's sharper statement of the dossier's point), which is a second publish path with its own secrets, rewrites, pom checks, recovery and ordering tests, carved out of policy #3 (first publish = full set, docs/release-process.md:17) and #5 (lockstep, rf2-w05l) — to avoid publishing 11 siblings that pass the identical pre-release test job. WHAT THE FIRST v* TAG PUBLISHES (coordinates as they read AFTER rf2-fo4ng; at tip every :lib still reads day8/*, which is exactly why the tag waits for the campaign):

(b) WHAT "PROVE ARTEFACT-INSTALL" MEANS, and who does it. Definition (binding): from a directory OUTSIDE any re-frame2 checkout, with a COLD Maven local repo (`:mvn/local-repo` pointed at a fresh empty directory) and `-Srepro` (no user deps.edn), a deps.edn whose only re-frame2 dependency is io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:mvn/version "0.0.1.alpha"} resolves with `clojure -P` from Clojars; `clojure -Stree` then shows io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso, io.github.day8/re-frame2 and io.github.day8/re-frame2-ssr all at 0.0.1.alpha (the two siblings arriving TRANSITIVELY via the published pom — that transitivity working IS the proof) and no day8/* coordinate anywhere in the tree; and a minimal shadow-cljs browser build of one namespace requiring re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso compiles. A warm ~/.m2, a prior `clein install`, any :local/root, or any :git/url invalidates the proof. The release commit itself is NOT hot-zone (CHANGELOG.md + tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj), but its :rf2-tools-sha pin must survive the rebase-merge — see TRAPS.

(d) FILE THE PREFLIGHT BEAD NOW — yes, done: rf2-59bgn, P3 task, blocked on THIS bead (not on fo4ng: fo4ng merging is necessary but not sufficient — the artefact must exist and the one-off proof must have passed). MIKE'S ACTS, in order, ALL UNCLAIMED (none of these has happened; nothing here asserts otherwise):

M1. rf2-uelji act — create the empty public repo github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson, submit its URL at clojars.org/verify/group logged in as mikethompson, confirm the verified badge on clojars.org/groups/io.github.day8, record badge + time on rf2-uelji. ~10 minutes; publishes nothing. (The reviewer re-probed on 2026-09-02: both the Clojars group page and the GitHub repo still 404.)
M2. Deploy token — mint a Clojars deploy token scoped to io.github.day8. Cannot exist before M1: Clojars refuses to scope a token to a group that does not yet exist. Mint it when the tag is imminent, i.e. after rf2-fo4ng has merged green, not at M1.
M3. Repository secrets — set CLOJARS_USERNAME (mikethompson) and CLOJARS_PASSWORD (the token, per release.yml 150-153) on day8/re-frame2. Read at release.yml 386-387, 624-625, 769-770, 880-881 and in the three tool workflows.
M4. Merge the release commit (prepared by a worker per the checklist) — the first publish is manual by protocol, so Mike reviews release.yml on that commit before tagging.
M5. Tag — `git tag v0.0.1.alpha <release-commit> && git push origin v0.0.1.alpha`, then watch every deploy job and github-release to completion. If the train partially publishes: bump-and-supersede (0.0.1.alpha → 0.0.1.alpha-1) per docs/release-process.md §Recovery (210-225); NEVER re-run the same tag (deploy-core 409s on the duplicate upload) and never ask for a yank (there is none: release.yml 63, 122).

NO-TAG RULE, restated so it cannot be missed: no tag of any kind until (i) M1 is recorded on rf2-uelji AND (ii) rf2-fo4ng has merged green AND (iii) M2/M3 are in place. A tag on the present day8/* tree runs verify-version-lockstep and test green and then fails at deploy-core with Clojars' 403 (group not verified) — the day8/de-dupe failure of 2026-05-13 reproduced on this repo. title: hicasso: V2's R=20 rung certifies on 1 of its 4 arm families — reproduced in three sessions, so it is structural
description:
CARRIED OUT OF rf2-0gjqi, whose description held this as a "second item, recorded
here rather than separately". rf2-0gjqi closes on its own audit obligation; this
item is unresolved and would otherwise be dropped with it.

THE OBSERVATION, now reproduced THREE times in three independent sessions.
V2's top rung produces certified windows under both writes on ONE of its four arm
families, and only that one:

  reagent-subs | hicasso R20   none
  reagent-subs | reagent R20   none
  uix-subs     | hicasso R20   none
  uix-subs     | uix     R20   certifies

  2026-08-13  (rf2-2rtt6.140's first window)
  2026-08-17  docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md
  2026-08-18  docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md
              -- TWO paired runs, and in both, 0 of 6 rounds on each of the three
              refusing families under EACH write, against 6 of 6 under each write
              on uix-subs | uix.

Three sessions agreeing makes it STRUCTURAL rather than incidental, and V2's most
informative rung remains unassessed on three quarters of the arms.

WHAT THE REFUSALS LOOK LIKE, first-hand from the 2026-08-18 datasets
(implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/). They are
dominated by a SINGLE leg -- usually leg 5 or leg 6 of 6 -- reading approximately
-800,000 B against a cohort median near 170,000 B. That is a collection of about
800 KB landing inside the window, which the leg witness catches correctly: a leg
below its cohort is a leg something removed bytes from, and nothing in the work
unit removes bytes.

DO NOT WIDEN A GATE TO ADMIT IT. The refusal is correct. An R20 window at B = 4
allocates a rise large enough that a collection inside it is close to certain, and
a tolerance wide enough to admit a -800 KB leg would admit every masked window the
leg witness exists to refuse. rf2-2rtt6.140 retired the previous bound for exactly
that reason.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none preferred and none authorised here: fewer measured
writes per window at the top rung so the window's cumulative rise stays under the
first collection; a rung ladder that stops below 20; or accepting that R = 20 is
not measurable on this instrument and saying so in the validity witness rather
than carrying an unassessed rung. Each is a rig change and belongs in its own
window.

WHY uix-subs | uix SURVIVES AND THE OTHER THREE DO NOT is not established. It is
the cheapest of the four per boundary, which is consistent with the
window-size account above and is not evidence for it.

MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-21 05:45 AUSEST — I RE-CLOSED THIS BEAD TWICE AGAINST A LIVE AUDIT. BOTH RE-CLOSES WERE WRONG AND THE AUDIT WAS RIGHT.

WHAT I DID. Seeing this bead open after worker/ladder-onozm had closed it, I read the two-second status flip in bd history as the known JSONL-revert artefact, checked for an AUDIT-REOPEN marker, concluded there was none, and re-closed with a reason asserting 'No AUDIT-REOPEN marker, no unmet obligation, no outstanding acceptance criterion'. That assertion is FACTUALLY FALSE and the audit said so in terms.

WHY I MISSED IT, recorded because the mechanism is general. The audit's finding was left as a COMMENT, and I searched the NOTES. bd show renders notes and comments in different blocks, my grep ran over a truncated view of the former, and the single hit it did return I dismissed as a description match about a different bead. So my 'no marker' was a property of where I looked, not of the bead. The backlog-reread loop already prescribes the right instrument for exactly this — bd comments <id> --json ordered by created_at — and I did not run it here.

THE SECOND RE-CLOSE WAS WORSE THAN THE FIRST, because by then the audit had posted an explicit correction naming my error and saying 'do not close until the multi-negative-window overclaim is corrected in the landed record or substantively rebutted'. Re-closing past that is precisely the failure the method warns about: re-closing an audit reopen destroys a real finding while looking like tidiness.

THE AUDIT'S FINDING STANDS AND IS DISPATCHABLE. The valid census establishes that all 72 R20 refusals contain AT LEAST ONE negative leg; the landed page strengthens that into 'one collection of near-constant size', and the raw paired-run corpus disproves the singular claim in three windows — paired-run1 round 1 uix-subs|lad/hicasso@all with three negative legs and falls=3, round 4 reagent-subs|lad/hicasso@page with two and falls=2, round 5 reagent-subs|lad/hicasso@all with two and falls=3. The reader reports only the FIRST negative-leg position and takes only the MINIMUM leg per window for the magnitude summary, so its 39/31/1/1 position census and -803,634 B median CONCEAL those events and cannot establish exactly one collection.

WHAT REMAINS VALID and must not be re-litigated: the independently reproduced 528-window identities, the 884,280 B observed ceiling, 72/0 above it, 420/456 at-or-below it, and the 5-write arithmetic. NO NEW BENCHMARK WINDOW IS REQUIRED.

DISPATCHED as part of worker/ledgerclust, which owns docs/design/hicasso/studio/README.md this tick.

THE LESSON, and it is mine rather than the tracker's: a two-second status flip in bd history is NOT a signature that distinguishes a revert from an audit reopen, because the audit writes through the same mechanism. Only reading the comments distinguishes them, and the cost of not reading them is destroying a finding.
close_reason: DISCHARGED by PR #8609 (worker/ceilinf-2k3vo), commit 2. WINDOW TAKEN AND PUBLISHED — PR #8684, docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-authors-split-window-on-the-amp-merge-clock.md. NOT closed; the mayor's to close.

THE VERDICT IS A REFUSAL, under a rule committed at a85302095d before any reading existed: a ladder term is RESOLVED only if its magnitude exceeds the largest measured |null ns/field| in EVERY evidence invocation AND its sign agrees across them.

THE NULL, FIRST (rf2-adld3's standing instruction). Fifteen rounds, every one inside +/-6.74% of 1.0, straddling 1.0 in all three runs. The 1.4737 did NOT recur, now at nine arms. Resolution bound R = 875 ns/field -- identical to the nanosecond to rf2-adld3's over its own fifteen rounds; nothing arranged for that.

(1') and (3'), ns/field pooled p50 per run:
  (1') wrapper   helper-lean/expanded    125,  0,  0   NOT RESOLVED (below R; exactly zero in 2 of 3)
  (3') roundtrip merged/no-dissoc-lean   625, 250, 750 NOT RESOLVED (below R; sign agrees)
  :author        (1)+(3) derived        -125, 375, 125 NOT RESOLVED (below R; signs disagree)
  :author-clean  (1')+(3')               625, 250, 1000 NOT RESOLVED (below R)
  :split-residual                       -625, 125, -875 NOT RESOLVED; largest magnitude equals R exactly and does not exceed it, so the split route and the cancellation route are INDISTINGUISHABLE at this resolution -- which is the one place the refusal carries positive content.
RESOLVED: rung (2) codec's merge-caller 2250/1500/2500, and :whole 2500/2250/2625. Both are figures z143r already had; no status cell moves.

WHY EVERYTHING LANDS BELOW R. Every mount time this rig reports is a multiple of 0.05 ms, which over 400 fields is exactly 125 ns/field. R is seven quanta, and nothing finer than one quantum is representable. That bounds what any future window on this rig can say about the author's share WITHOUT A FINER CLOCK -- which is the actionable instrument fact this window bought.

REPORTED, NOT PROMOTED: (3) reads negative in all three runs and (3') positive in all three, sharing :merged as numerator -- the reversal the lean arm was built to look for, 3-for-3 both ways. Both below R; the rule was written in advance so exactly this could not be upgraded after the fact.

title: [retire] R6 — the prose sweep: ~237 files of spec, docs, skills and source comments (needs splitting at dispatch)
description:
Largest by count, lowest by risk, and the LAST phase. 237 of the 508 referencing files are prose. THIS BEAD IS TOO BIG FOR ONE WORKER and should be split by sub-surface when dispatched — spec is ONE TOUCHER, everything else parallelises.

THE SUB-SURFACES, with counts measured 2026-08-15 (rg -il --hidden over the union of 'freehand' and re-frame.ui spellings, the two trees excluded):
- docs/design/freehand/ - 37 files. **KEEP. DO NOT DELETE.** The word "Deletes." that stood here was an ERROR, ruled so by rf2-0moc4 (closed 2026-08-18) after R6b refused it; this line is that ruling's Consequence A, applied 2026-08-20 after a SECOND worker re-derived the same error from the uncorrected text. THE DECIDING REASON is the hicasso coupling: docs/design/hicasso/ carries 11 inbound links across 8 files, and deleting the tree takes scripts/check_doc_slugs.py to exit 1 with 4 broken targets, measured independently by R6b and again on 2026-08-20. docs/EP/EP-0036 cites it 17 times and asserts the tree remains. mkdocs.yml exclude_docs already hides it from the site, so keeping it costs the published docs nothing. (The ruling's point 5, 11 links from spec/004-Views.md, has lapsed because that file is deleted. Point 3 is the one that decides.)
- docs/api/*.md - 12 files. **NOT GENERATED  the word "GENERATED" that stood here was WRONG.** Established at source 2026-08-20 by the rf2-jzv5x worker: the api-manifest chain has exactly one spit, gen.clj:430, and it writes spec/api-manifest.edn  NOT these pages. doc_api_check.clj READS docs/api as a projection to VALIDATE against that manifest (scope table at :84; success line "OK: docs/api page+member coverage in sync"). So these are HAND-AUTHORED prose checked against a generated manifest, not output of it. The error propagated four hops before anyone checked it  this line, into a dispatch brief, into that worker's report, into bead rf2-jzv5x, into a second brief  and cost one dispatch. Edit them by hand like any other prose, and keep them in sync with spec/api-manifest.edn because doc_api_check.clj will red if they drift.
- skills/re-frame2-ui/ — 5 files, a whole skill dedicated to the retiring substrate. Deletes, including .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the generated references/ui-context.md. Also skills/README.md, skills/reagent-migration/* (4), skills/re-frame2-setup (2), skills/re-frame2 (2), skills/re-frame2-improver, re-frame2-implementor, re-frame2-xray, re-frame-migration.
- spec/ prose remainder — Conventions.md (the whole 'Freehand — one public namespace' section, the :rf.adapter/* row's freehand member, the :rf.ui/* and :rf.ui.compile/* and :rf.ui.evidence/* and :rf.ui.tool/* rows), 006-ReactiveSubstrate.md's adapter table row and §Adapter introspection list, API.md's rows, Ownership.md, 001, 002, 008, 011, 012, AI-Audit.md, Security.md, Privacy.md, README.md, Principles.md, Spec-Schemas.md, Tool-Pair.md, Cross-Spec-Interactions.md, the Pattern-* pages, 000-Vision.md. HOT ZONE — one toucher, sequenced.
- source comments and docstrings — ~27 lines in core/src, ~45 in core/src for re-frame.ui, 4 in ssr/src, 3 in ssr-ring/src, plus tools/xray/src (5 files), tools/story, tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp, implementation/routing/src, implementation/hicasso/src (9), implementation/adapters READMEs.
- mkdocs.yml nav; root README.md, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, TESTING.md; docs/AUTHORING.md, docs/release-process.md, docs/skills.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1 and migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod comments.

DO NOT DELETE, and this is a judgement rather than an oversight:
- docs/EP/EP-0030 through EP-0036 (10 files) are HISTORICAL PROGRAMME RECORDS. A withdrawn programme's EP is the reason the withdrawal is legible; deleting it leaves the retirement unexplained.
- docs/design/hicasso/ (65 files) cite Freehand as the substrate hicasso replaced. That is hicasso's record, not Freehand's. Leave it. docs/design/hicasso/product/tool-consumer-census.md in particular already carries ruled dispositions for the retiring adapter ids.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs's react-element-render-kinds set — see rf2-0yp7w.10; it stays on a deliberate defensive footing.

Full survey: docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md

SCRUBBING A NAME HIDES A LIVE DEFECT FROM THE REGEX HUNTING IT. Every slice here finds residue by grepping for a donor NAME. Where someone has already replaced the identifier with a phrase — 'the retired compiled tier' — and left the surrounding CLAIM standing, the census returns that file as clean, permanently. Correcting the pattern does not reach it; the population is invisible by construction.

THE INSTANCE, and it is not cosmetic: implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs declines to test prefetch on the ground that all three positions 'are driven with REAL DOM events in the retired compiled tier's route-link DOM suite'. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE REMAINING SLICES. A slice reporting 'census clean on my surface' is reporting the regex's answer, not the tree's. It does NOT mean the surface is free of donor residue. Where a slice's own reading turns up a sentence whose subject was clearly edited — a definite article standing where a name used to be, 'the retired X', 'the former Y' — read the argument around it rather than moving on. That is a human read and no pattern replaces it.

AND THE CORRECTED REGEX IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIRST MEASUREMENT SUGGESTED. On implementation/, bare 're-frame2-ui' matched ELEVEN files and 're-frame2-ui([^x]|$)' matched THREE — eight of the eleven were live UIx. On skills/ the same correction took ten to four. MAYOR 2026-08-18 — CORRECTION TO MY OWN CENSUS, FROM THE WORKER ON rf2-0yp7w.9.1 (PR #8464). THE PATTERN I MEASURED THIS BEAD'S REMAINDER WITH IS WRONG, AND IT INFLATES THE SCOPE BY ROUGHLY HALF. Recorded here rather than in chat because the next slice reads this bead, not my reply.

THE DEFECT IN MY PATTERN. I sized the remainder at 243 tracked files using

    git grep -E 're-frame\.(ui|freehand)|implementation/(ui|freehand)/|re-frame2-ui|re-frame2-freehand'

're-frame2-ui' IS A PREFIX OF 're-frame2-uix' — the coordinate of the LIVE, first-class UIx adapter. Every UIx mention matches. This is a substring failure of exactly the class this corpus keeps meeting, and docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md:89-91 ALREADY DOCUMENTS THIS TRAP. I reintroduced noise the survey had already priced.

THE MEASURED SIZE OF THE ERROR, on the 14-file slice: SEVEN OF FOURTEEN FILES WERE FALSE POSITIVES — they matched on nothing but '-uix'. The single largest entry, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md at 6 hits, needed NO EDIT: a positive control, grep -c -F 're-frame2-uix', returns exactly 6, accounting for 6 of 6. That file is HOT ZONE, so a bad pattern was about to spend the scarce single-toucher slot on a file with nothing wrong in it.

SO: TREAT THE 243 AS AN UPPER BOUND CONTAMINATED BY UIx, NOT AS A REMAINDER. Re-derive per slice with a word-bounded or fixed-string pattern that cannot match 'uix', and run a positive control both ways before believing any count.

THE PATTERN ALSO MISSED THINGS, IN THE OTHER DIRECTION. Going case-insensitive added 9 hits 're-frame\.freehand' could not see — bare 'Freehand' in prose. No NEW files appeared, so on that slice the true donor surface was a strict SUBSET: 7 files, not 14. Both widenings were worth making; neither can be skipped.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the bucket boundaries still hold, and the exclusions on this bead stand — docs/design/freehand/ (KEPT, rf2-0moc4), docs/design/hicasso/, docs/design/retirement/, docs/EP/EP-0032..0036, spec/004+004C+S3/S4/S5 (held on rf2-h89ri), .github/** (hot zone).

A SECOND DISCRIMINATOR THE SLICE ESTABLISHED, worth carrying into every remaining slice. The brief predicted skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md would hold a LEGITIMATE 'the surface was removed' hit. IT HOLDS NONE, and the absence is CORRECT: neither surface was ever PUBLISHED (CHANGELOG:71, .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:128, docs/release-process.md:17), so there is no breaking change to record. Do not let a later slice 'helpfully' add a breaking-changes entry for a library that never shipped.

ONE SMALL ITEM PARKED HERE RATHER THAN FILED, for whichever slice takes the codemod: migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/test/re_frame/migration/hicasso/shared_rule_test.clj carries a docstring saying 'Only one of them survives Freehand''s retirement' while a comment 15 lines below correctly records that the twin was re-homed and BOTH survive. A stale sub-clause inside an attributed historical record. It misdirects nobody and its gate is a JVM clojure -M:test that was deliberately not run under the measurement-window reservation. Fix it in passing when that surface is next open; it does not deserve a dispatch of its own.

MAYOR 2026-08-18 — SLICE 3 CLOSED (PR #8474). ONE FINDING THAT CHANGES EVERY REMAINING SLICE, AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT A SWEEPER WOULD ASSUME.

**:rf.ui/* IS NOT A RETIRED SPELLING. IT IS LIVE SURFACE.** spec/Conventions.md:104 records that the structural render-tree ABI namespace OUTLIVED the substrate that minted it. It is the live keyword family for re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree and the Hicasso test kit. A sweeper who adds ':rf.ui' to a donor-residue pattern will delete or rewrite working surface, and every gate would stay green while doing it, because the spelling is legitimately everywhere.

WHAT IS RETIRED, and only these: :rf.ui.compile/* and :rf.ui.tool/*, which are struck-through RETIRED tombstone rows in the Conventions table. Note the shape — the retired names are SUB-namespaces of a live parent, so a prefix match on ':rf.ui' catches the live one and a match on the full retired names catches neither by accident. This is the third distinct prefix trap in this bead's history, after 're-frame2-ui' matching 're-frame2-uix' and 'hang' matching 'change'.

THE WORKING PATTERN IS UNCHANGED and still the one to use, with both controls run before any count is believed:

    git grep -ciIP 'freehand|re-frame\.ui(?!x)|re-frame2-ui(?!x)|implementation/(ui|freehand)/|004D'

    negative control  README.md = 0
    positive control  docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md = 64

DO NOT ADD ':rf.ui' TO IT.

SECOND FINDING, ABOUT WHAT A GATE-SCRIPT SWEEP COSTS AND SAVES: of 58 hits across 11 scripts, 52 WERE CORRECT AND WERE LEFT UNTOUCHED. The 6 that were residue were all present-tense claims about deleted things — a docstring teaching a failure class from the deleted jvm-freehand job, a hand-kept 'twenty-three per-artefact JVM jobs' comment against a roster that now reads 21, two comments naming a donor grep that zero workflows use, an exemption justifying itself by contrast with a workflow that does not exist, and a paragraph quoting two cells of a Conventions row that is now a struck-through tombstone. Every other hit was a FORBID pattern, a self-test fixture proving a pattern fires, a refusal regex, or a dated record. **Narrowing any of those would have disarmed a gate**, and the gate would have gone on reporting green over the class it no longer covered.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN BEAD, recorded because it is the kind of thing that gets copied forward: rf2-0yp7w.9.3's TITLE said '12 scripts/ files' while its own table listed 11. Eleven is right. The worker resolved it in favour of the table and said so.

REMAINDER STILL OWED BY THIS BEAD, after slices 1 to 4: implementation/** (about 103 files of source comments, heavy gates, needs the box free), tools/xray/** (18 files — now unfenced, PR #8467 merged), examples/** (3 CLJS files, heavy gates), the 9 source and build-config files listed on slice 4, and .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:1223 which still names jvm-freehand and is HOT ZONE. rf2-0yp7w.9.5 carries slice 3's two stopped-on items.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.
