title: hic: outward-bridge hydration mismatch attribution is unreachable by construction (no Spec 011 reporter)
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 5 (Server and
hydration), §2 Correctness.

Row 5 requires every native surface to satisfy its row "including server bytes or
source refusal, matching hydration, MISMATCH ATTRIBUTION and multiple roots".

The native tier's own SSR rows are the best-evidenced part of the row: HS-24 to
HS-30 are witnessed through real react-dom/server bytes on BOTH policy arms by
native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and that file records the defect it was written
against — a Client-only island appearing in the server bytes because the recorded
:server policy was consulted by nothing (rf2-u9lk, rf2-ggnp) — as found and fixed.
Checkpoint 3 searched specifically for a semantic-tree claim standing in for
server bytes and found none anywhere.

MISMATCH ATTRIBUTION for the OUTWARD BRIDGE is a different matter, and it is not a
missing test — it is unsatisfiable without a door. HS-21's bytes half is proved
(native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:124, renderToStaticMarkup). But an outward-bridged root
is built by the CONSUMER'S own createElement, so impl.mount/hydrate-root! cannot
adopt it, and a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs no Spec 011 reporter. There is
therefore no path by which a mismatch inside a bridged subtree is attributed to
source.

Root cause, shared with two other open gaps: THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY.
Every server witness in the package calls react-dom/server's renderToString by
hand — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in terms ("There is no Hicasso server
entry... the only server path in the package"). Row 5 is therefore proved against
a hand-rolled harness rather than a shipped door.

## Not this bead's, and named so they are not duplicated

- HS-11/HS-14 (root/frame provider Client-only under a measured, unrepaired
  obstruction: the package's only server path emits no counterpart to the adoption
  closer, so a tree minting a useId hydrates into an id mismatch).
- HS-33 (motion/presence measured to satisfy NEITHER policy, repair decided and
  unlanded).
Both are outside the native tier and already carried. Checkpoint 3 files nothing
against them.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs and/or impl/roots.cljs
  (only if a door is the chosen route)
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_cljs_test.cljs
- docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md HS-21 row

DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

EITHER a hydration path for an outward-bridged root that installs the Spec 011
reporter, with a deliberate-mismatch row attributing to source; OR a source-located
statement on HS-21 that mismatch attribution is out of reach for a consumer-built
root, with row 5's required-result sentence amended to scope "mismatch attribution"
to roots the package itself adopts. The second is a defensible line — the consumer
owns that root — but it must be written down rather than left as an unmet clause.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-21 01:00 AUSEST — NOT DISPATCHED, AND THE REASON HAS CHANGED. The earlier note said "not dispatched this tick because six workers are live... dispatch on the next free slot". A slot is free now. I read the bead instead of taking it, and it splits into two halves that do not belong to the same person.

THE FENCE QUESTION IS SETTLED AND THE ANSWER IS PARALLEL-SAFE. That note asked whether spec/011 collides with spec/009 in the hot zone. Measured at CLAUDE.md:91 today: the hot-zone list is an ENUMERATION of eight named spec pages — 002-Frames, 005-StateMachines, 006-ReactiveSubstrate, 009-Instrumentation, API, Conventions, Spec-Schemas, Tool-Pair. spec/011-SSR.md is NOT among them, so this bead never needed to queue behind a spec/009 toucher. That fence was over-broad, not wrong, and it is now retired.

WHY IT STILL DOES NOT GO OUT. The bead's own surface fence says "implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs and/or impl/roots.cljs (ONLY IF A DOOR IS THE CHOSEN ROUTE)". Whether to ship a door is the question, not the work. The bead's stated root cause is THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY — every server witness in the package calls react-dom/server's renderToString by hand, and native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in terms. Adding a shipped server entry is a PUBLIC-SURFACE product decision for Mike, not a bounded fix, and dispatching a worker at an undecided design is how a migration gets performed on a false premise.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so the operator half is not overstated: the HS-21 half was handled by rf2-vwo53 (PR #8559). Its worker amended the dispositions.md row to STATE THE SCOPE AND ITS MEASURED WITNESS and deliberately did NOT upgrade it, because rf2-s52w's own close record confirmed the finding rather than repairing it. So the record is truthful today; what is missing is the capability, not the description of it.

FOR MIKE — THE DECISION AND ITS COST. Does Hicasso ship a server entry? Today mismatch attribution inside an outward-bridged subtree is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION: the consumer's own createElement builds the root, impl.mount/hydrate-root! cannot adopt it, and a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs no Spec 011 reporter. COST OF THE HOLD: Checkpoint 3's row 5 stays proved against a hand-rolled harness rather than a shipped door, and two other open gaps (HS-11/HS-14 and HS-33, both already carried elsewhere) share the same root cause. Nothing is broken while it waits and no other bead is blocked behind it.
AUDIT 2026-08-21 13:40 AUSEST (rf2-s52w audit pass, read-only). Filed rf2-0brem — the last undischarged clause of THIS bead's acceptance option B (row 5's required-result sentence). Verdict and the other premise corrections follow in the next note.
AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-21 13:45 AUSEST — read-only pass on origin/main@94f23109d2. LEFT OPEN
DELIBERATELY: the operator hold in the 2026-08-21 01:00 note stands, but the question it asks
is stale and is re-put below. THE FINDING IS REAL AND THREE OF THIS BEAD'S FOUR PREMISES ARE
WRONG AT THE CURRENT TIP. 0 correctness defects. Filed rf2-0brem and rf2-981ka.

P1 "no Spec 011 reporter" — FALSE AS WRITTEN. Spec 011 defines the reporter for exactly this
tier: spec/011-SSR.md:811 (Hydration-mismatch detection), :825 (the adoption channel for
React-element roots), :846-856 (the trace shape). Hicasso implements it —
impl/mount.cljs:363 emit-hydration-mismatch!, :380 hydration-reporter, :415
hydrate-root-options, installed at :546 inside hydrate-root!. What the BODY of this bead says
— "a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs NO Spec 011 reporter" — is the true statement, and it is
a statement about WHO OPENED THE ROOT. (correction-ledger.md:89 cites mount.cljs:427-447 and
hydrate-root!:560; those numbers have drifted to 380-412 and 546. Not filed — minutiae.)

P2 "attribution unreachable for a consumer-built root" — TRUE, AND MEASURED, AND THE WITNESS
SURVIVES THE ANTI-VACUITY TEST. onRecoverableError is an option of an INDIVIDUAL hydrateRoot
(impl/roots.cljs:20-27 builds the whole per-root design on that). native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs
:891 consumer-element (deliberately not reaching impl.mount/tree), :920 the deftest, :952 the
CONTROL run FIRST asserting exactly one diagnostic through the package's own door, :1013 the
measurement (= [] seen). I applied the mechanical test — delete the signal, keep the fault —
and it holds: removing the reporter install from hydrate-root! reddens :952, so the row cannot
stay green on a broken mechanism. The zero is additionally bounded below by three live readings
in its own arm (the server bytes really said "#7 server"; React really recovered to
"#7 client", awaited rather than assumed; the console really captured the complaint). AND the
listener is not shared — watch-mismatches! (roots_frames_support.cljs:424) mints a gensym key
per call, so the second watch is a fresh registration, which was the specific way this row
could have been vacuous. It is the good version of the pattern, not the bad one.

P3 "unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION" — OVERSTATED, AND THE OVERSTATEMENT IS WHAT KEEPS GENERATING
THE FINDING. The boundary is not the outward bridge; it is which renderer opened the root, and
the bridge is not special in it. TWO re-frame2 doors install a root-scoped Spec 011 reporter on
a React-element root: h/hydrate! (impl/mount.cljs:546) and the Spec 006 client mount entry
(re-frame.substrate.adapter/render tree mount {:hydrate? true}) at spine.cljs:1107, whose
docstring at :1191-1204 names itself the only native mount route that installs it and repeats
Spec 011's boundary sentence verbatim. onRecoverableError fires for recoverable errors ANYWHERE
in that root's tree, so a consumer whose app is mounted through the Spec 006 door with a
Hicasso view bridged in under mount/provider would get :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch for a text
divergence inside the bridged subtree — tagged :where re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render
rather than Hicasso's site, but emitted. REASONED FROM REACT'S ROOT-OPTION CONTRACT PLUS THE
TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS; NOT MEASURED FOR THE BRIDGED CASE, and not claimed as measured — no suite
renders Hicasso under a UIx parent at all (rf2-ap7w's subject). The accurate wording is the one
spec/011-SSR.md:825 already uses: attribution is scoped to roots a re-frame2 door opens.

P4 "root cause: THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY" — FALSE AT TIP, AND IRRELEVANT EVEN WHERE IT
WAS TRUE. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs (452 lines,
re-frame.hicasso.server/render) landed in commit 30317bfe0e on 2026-08-14 21:28 +1000
(rf2-b6jkj, PR #8236) — about seven hours after this bead was filed and a week before the
2026-08-21 note that repeats the claim. It is a real door: impl/roots.cljs:50-58 names it one
of the TWO minters of the adoption window, "once per REQUEST, closed in that door's finally",
the fork decided once for both sides of the wire. The rest of the tree already describes it as
shipped (naming-ledger.md rows 22 and 50, invariants.md:85, globals.md:192,
architecture-census.md:168, dispositions.md:336, docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md,
api-reference.md:376). AND THE PREMISE IS IRRELEVANT: a server entry produces BYTES; the
reporter is a CLIENT root option. No server door of any design can install an option on a root
the consumer opens on the client. The two facts were never causally linked. The stale sentence
that produced the claim is native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66 — filed as rf2-981ka.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS — option B is 2/3 discharged. (a) source-located statement plus measured
witness: DONE, PR #8302 / 473ff5e330. (b) dispositions.md:290 HS-21 row amended: DONE
2026-08-20 by rf2-vwo53 / PR #8559. (c) row 5's required-result sentence scoped: OWING, and no
bead owned it — now rf2-0brem. Its two homes are hot-path-architecture.md:49 (the native tier's
only release checklist) and, the one that actually creates the obligation,
react-compatibility-notes.md:34's blanket sentence "Every Render row runs the common hydration
states: matching content, deliberate mismatch with source attribution, ...". The matrix ROW for
Root/frame provider and outward bridge (:24) omits mismatch attribution, so that omission is
not a carve-out — the blanket sentence puts it back on every Render row.

THE OPERATOR QUESTION, RE-PUT. The 2026-08-21 note asks "Does Hicasso ship a server entry?" —
it does, since 2026-08-14, and it would not have helped. The live question is narrower: SHOULD
THE PACKAGE EXPOSE A WAY FOR A ROOT THE CONSUMER OPENED TO CARRY THE FRAMEWORK REPORTER?
RECOMMENDATION: NO. (1) A consumer who wants the diagnostic already has two doors — h/hydrate!,
or the Spec 006 adapter render with {:hydrate? true} if their app is React-rooted. Trusting the
programmer means letting them mount through a door rather than shipping a second mechanism for
not doing so. (2) It is not the one-liner it looks like: exporting hydration-reporter alone
would emit NOTHING, because the emit is gated on roots/adopting? and a consumer-built tree
carries no adoption window and no adoption-window-closer, so the flag reads closed —
impl/roots.cljs:59-64 states exactly this for a hand-rolled renderToString. A real door means
publishing the window, the closer and the option-builder, which naming-ledger.md row 50 already
flags as "a larger decision" (making impl.mount/tree and impl.roots/open-adoption-window!
public). (3) Nothing is broken: React still complains on its own channel and the divergence is
a deterministic bug either way; what is missing is a TRACE, on a root the framework does not
own. If Mike wants it anyway it is a public-surface programme, not a bounded fix. rf2-0brem
does NOT wait on this ruling — the doc clause is true under either answer.

DECLINED, and why: no PR (read-only brief, and both candidate edits are the ledger keeper's
surface — native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs:48-52 states the principle, "a witness may not amend
the row it witnesses", which binds an auditor the same way); no third bead for the door (the
stance rejects the remedy, so a bead filed to be refused costs more than this recommendation);
no edit to correction-ledger.md (fenced out by this bead); no edit to checkpoint-3-native.md (a
dated checkpoint record — whether it is amended in place is the ledger keeper's convention, not
an auditor's); no bead for the drifted line numbers in correction-ledger.md:89.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS BEAD: Mike ruling on the door question above. rf2-0brem then discharges
the last acceptance clause independently. Nothing else on this bead is owed.
FOLLOW-ONS FILED BY THIS AUDIT (both name rf2-s52w as owner, so a later audit re-finding either recognises it as this bead's clause rather than a second finding): rf2-0brem — scope row 5's 'mismatch attribution' required result to roots a re-frame2 door opens (this bead's last acceptance clause; react-compatibility-notes.md:34 and hot-path-architecture.md:49). rf2-981ka — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66 still says 'there is no Hicasso server entry', false since 2026-08-14, and it is the sentence Checkpoint 3 cited that seeded this bead's P4 root cause. NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S TITLE: '(no Spec 011 reporter)' is false as written — Spec 011 defines the reporter and Hicasso installs it on its own doors. Title left unchanged because several committed docs cite this bead by id beside that phrasing; the P1 paragraph above is the correction. Returning to open — no worker holds it.

Reopen only on real consumer demand; then it is a public-surface programme, not a fix.

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

# hic-088 — Requirements-mine consolidation

**Phase**: 4/6 · **Est.**: S · **Depends**: hic-004
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md` (the one consolidation owner)

## Goal
The mine must be current when the audits read it. This bead owns the updates hic-004 only seeded.

## Deliverables
Two consolidation passes recorded in the file: one before the coverage checkpoint (every row's witness link resolves; "owed by" rows re-pointed to landed evidence or open corrections) and one before the final audit (same, plus final-name updates after the sweep).

## Acceptance
At each pass: zero stale witness links; zero rows owing to closed beads without landed evidence; pass dates recorded in the file.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. DOC-SURFACE GATE: for an edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/, `mkdocs build --strict` is NOT the gate — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates its markdown link targets and heading anchors, and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/; nothing validates its tables, rendering or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch — they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Any other database-derived path likewise. The human-authored config — `.beads/README.md`, `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore`, `.beads/hooks/**` — IS fair game. CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files only if this bead flags them — and the hot zone INCLUDES the spec/*.md hot files (spec/004-Views.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md among others), not just implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and .github/workflows/*. CLAUDE.md's Workflow section carries the canonical list; read it there rather than treating this line as complete.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues AND a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md. The checkpoint's own report PR writes the `open` row; a CORRECTIVE PR never edits that file — every later transition is the ledger keeper's. Read the file's own stated protocol before touching it.

# hic-051 — Forms: recipes first, the buffered-draft field at its second consumer

**Phase**: 5 · **Wave**: F · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-020, hic-025
**Surface**: optional forms namespace/recipes + tests (new files)

## Goal
The highest-traffic optional product: the draft/validation patterns that kill the five hand-rolled trap classes (twin-atom stack, same-value blindness, commit flicker, arity-sniffed done-fn, re-minted ephemeral state).

## Deliverables
- The documented recipes: buffered draft (commit/cancel/blur incl. cancel-unmounts-then-blur), touched/submit-attempt validation gating, mutation status display — each with structural tests on the kit.
- The `draft-field` helper extracted **when the second consumer appears** (the slice app + the vendor screen may already be the two — if so, extract now); zero reachable production code when the namespace is unused (sentinel proof).

## Acceptance
Recipes runnable; trap-class regression tests green (each of the five traps has a witness proving this pattern avoids it); reachability proof green.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §4.2 tail, §7 forms row; the A1/A2 rows in the requirements mine.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7971 (merged 2026-08-12T07:12:16Z; completeness/correctness/implementation quality) — REOPENED. The recipes and their synchronous/model coverage are strong, but the two poll-until chains in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/forms/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs (the refused-submit marker wait and valid-submit transport wait) have only a fulfillment handler. If the bounded poll rejects, cljs.test done is never called and the live hm/mount! handle is never unmounted/asserted clean; the row hangs and can contaminate later browser tests. The sibling slice suite already has the bounded finish-after shape: report the rejection upstream, tear down on both arms, and keep exactly one trailing done. Apply that shape to both rows and add a deliberate rejected-poll control proving the following row sees no retained mount/residue. Keep the correction local; no runtime or forms API change.
PR #8668 AUDIT RESIDUAL (correctness / implementation quality; the teaching-set completeness work is otherwise sound). Reopened this exact forms-recipe owner because the rule promoted into the published guide contradicts the accessibility state it exposes. At merge, docs/core/hicasso/05-forms.md says an invalid submit button stays "focusable and activatable" and relies on that activation to set :submit-attempted?, while rendering :aria-disabled true; forms-recipes.md:53 and the shipped example view/tests pin the same pattern. WAI-ARIA 1.2 defines aria-disabled=true as perceivable but disabled, "so it is not editable or otherwise operable" (https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-disabled). The page therefore tells assistive technology the action is unavailable while the application requires the user to activate it to reveal errors; current DOM/L2 tests pin both halves without testing their semantic coherence. Repair the guide, recipe, example view and witnesses together: normally keep invalid submit genuinely enabled (omit aria-disabled), let submit validation reveal the error summary, and describe the errors with the appropriate relationship/live-region semantics; reserve disabled/aria-disabled for an action the handler really suppresses. Do not merely change the prose while leaving the example and tests contradictory.
close_reason: PR #8671 — the aria-disabled/activatable contradiction is repaired across every layer at once: guide chapter (prose, worked form, field sample, two troubleshooting rows), forms-recipes.md rule + dated correction note, the shipped example view/subs/db/events, and both witnesses. The invalid submit button now claims nothing — validity is carried by the fields as aria-invalid + aria-describedby + role=alert, and aria-disabled is reserved for controls the handler really suppresses. New L2 row and DOM assertions pin the semantic coherence that nothing tested before. Two consequent pins moved in the same commit: the guide-samples roster (blocks 5 and 8) and the pooled read-set census (dropping the gate read left save-button and save-failure on an identical one-key set; verdict unmoved). Gates captured green: hicasso-invariants 0, node lane 0 (11811 tests), browser lane 0 (1064 tests), doc-slugs 0, provenance-pins 0, mkdocs --strict 0; each lane also driven red from a planted fault and restored blob-hash-verified.

title: hicasso: the fused reader array costs 91-92 B/read — the largest term this page has attributed to a container rather than a value
description:
MEASURED, NOT SPECULATED. rf2-zei9w's ablation attributes 91 B/read (Reagent segment) / 92 (UIx) to the cell's fused reader array — the container itself, not the membership it holds. Per-round bands are disjoint across all six rounds, the R=0 shell does not move, and donors moved 0.05/0.19 B/read, so this is a per-KEY term and the attribution is solid. Published in docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md (2026-08-04 section), PR #7452.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. rf2-dabt3's fusion banked -60 B/read in both segments — real, and it won — but that is only ~40% of the ~151 B/read the old reverse edge cost, because the replacement array is ~2x what ONE PersistentHashSet membership costs (+46/+47 B/read, PR #7418 run D). The design predicted the surviving array would be cheap residue; it is not. It is now the largest single term this page has attributed to a CONTAINER rather than to a value.

THE OBVIOUS SHAPE, and it is only a sketch. At the fan-out this table actually sees, the overwhelmingly common case is ONE reader per key. A scalar slot that holds the single reader directly and promotes to an array on the SECOND reader would retain a pointer instead of a JSArray-plus-backing-store for that case. arm1/runtime.cljs's own section header already argues a JS array beats a persistent set here; this asks the next question down, which is whether a container is needed at all in the common case.

THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first, for three reasons:
• release-cell!'s .indexOf, arm-cell-reaper!'s alength and stats's alength all read .-readers directly, and cell-readers/stats are witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against — a polymorphic slot touches all of them.
• It is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm, and the stance is explicit that not every measured term needs actioning.
• The bill it would attack is +331 B/read against Reagent; 91 of that is this term. Worth knowing the size before deciding it is worth the branch in a hot path.

Precondition if it is ever taken: a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder 6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and the same ablation discipline rf2-zei9w used — attribute, do not infer.
notes:
FENCE recorded 2026-08-21 by the dispatch tick — EXCLUSIVE RESOURCE, CONTENDED. Not dispatchable while the fleet is loud. This bead's own newest note states the rule: 'that is exactly why one bench-class worker at a time is the rule and why a second allocation window is not admissible merely because the estimand is exempt.' title: Consolidate 73 ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore sites onto one shared fixture
description:
Carried over from rf2-76lhy step 2, which closed on PR #7190 having delivered step 1 (the capture-time profile). This half was never done and should not be lost with the parent.

73 test files set and restore the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT by hand, with no shared fixture. A test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace in the bundle - a cross-namespace coupling that no assertion can catch and that only shows up as unexplained slowness or flakiness later in the run.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT, so this is not over-sold. rf2-76lhy originally advanced the leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown. The per-namespace profile shipped in PR #7190 dissolved that: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points all sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.

So this is a HYGIENE bead, not a bug hunt. It retires a real hazard class on its own terms - one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally - and it is worth doing, but nothing is currently known to be broken by it. Size it accordingly and do not let it grow into an audit.

Fenced away from the PR #7190 runner work; this is implementation/**/test/** across many artefacts, so it wants its own dispatch.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, NOT DONE (PR #7193 worker, 2026-07-28). Recommendation: leave it, or do it per-artefact later. This is the honest 'not worth doing now'.

CENSUS IS BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAYS: 78 files, 175 `set!` sites, across NINE trees — freehand 43, ui 15, adapters 7, ssr 6, tools/story 2, tools/machines-viz 2, machines 1, core 1, scripts 1. Not 73, and not one artefact.

THERE IS NO SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION TO ADOPT. The nearest existing shared fixture is `re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!`, which already does exactly the right thing (reads the prior value, sets true, restores the PRIOR value — not `false` — after React settles). But it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, a published and EXPERIMENTAL artefact surface. Adopting it from freehand / ssr / adapters / machines test trees would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's. The alternative — mint a new shared test-support surface every artefact may require — is also a decision, not a sweep.

WHAT DOES EXIST is per-artefact convergence: freehand already has mount_support.cljs and bench/b6_harness.cljs; ssr has SIX files carrying byte-identical `disable-act-env!`/`restore-act-env!` pairs. So the tractable shape is PER-ARTEFACT, ONE PR EACH — freehand first (43 of the 78 files, landing spot already present), then ssr (6 files, pure duplication), then ui.

WHY NOT NOW. (1) The motivation is gone: PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and PR #7193 confirmed it on a second box — the whole gap was seven benchmark namespaces (71% of the browser lane's wall clock), and the CI factor is a uniform ~1.7x. There is still no observed instance of the leak. (2) A 78-file mechanical edit across nine trees is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open PR touching a mounted test. (3) Every one of those trees was outside PR #7193's fence, so it could not have been done there in any case.

If someone does pick it up: rule FIRST on whether re-frame.ui.test's act door may be the repo-wide answer, because that ruling decides whether this is one shared fixture or nine private ones.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — leave the sweep undone now; bead DEFERRED. No 78-file mechanical edit during the current mounted-test churn: the motivating CI-slowdown hypothesis was dissolved by measurement (seven benchmark namespaces + a uniform ~1.7x CI factor), and the sweep is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open mounted-test PR. Pick this up only when the high-conflict Freehand work settles AND either a real leak instance bites or an artefact's mounted tests are being reworked anyway — then land it artefact-sized, not repo-wide.

RECORD CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion; commits verified in this checkout): "no observed instance" is true of the PERFORMANCE theory only. Flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired — 43ce4cf9f6 and 1fff5b618b (shared-page act-discipline, ~361 warnings) and 0dd432b9ed (un-restored act boundary after a negative-control run, 755 warnings). The hazard class is real and observed; the slowdown attribution is what was disproved. P3 stands.

ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (binding — do not re-litigate):
1. DONOR DEPENDENCY FORBIDDEN. No artefact's tests may require re-frame.ui (src or test): F6e deletes the artefact, and re-frame.ui.test/act-operation! is a private defn- coupled to donor internals in any case. Its invariant is the SHAPE to copy, never the namespace to require: capture the incoming flag value and restore the PRIOR value — not a blanket false — on every exit path (synchronous throw, Promise fulfilment, Promise rejection).
2. ONE repo-private implementation, NOT nine per-artefact copies. Home: the existing lightweight dependency-free shared surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs (or a narrowly named sibling in the same core/test root). Verified: it is already required across an artefact boundary today (adapters/uix test) and sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath, so this mints no new architecture and survives F6e. Per-artefact is the DELIVERY boundary — artefact-sized PRs, freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs) — not the implementation boundary. Nine permanent copies would reproduce at repo scale exactly the drift ssr's six copies already demonstrate.
3. Design floor for whoever lands it (from Codex, ratified): the helper takes the desired mode — both true (act-disciplined renders) and false (timing discriminators, hydration, deliberate un-acted negative controls) are legitimate, so no runner-wide constant. One save/restore engine with thin sync-wrapping and async-map fixture adapters (cljs.test forbids mixing the two fixture kinds; async tests need the map form) plus a Promise-aware operation bracket for callbacks that reject before done; overlapping async scopes rejected or serialized. Leave re-frame.ui.test self-contained until F6e and skip migrating ui test files the deletion gate removes.

Disposition: deferred (was open P3). Reopen against the conditions above.

DECISION — CLOSE AS MINUTIAE. No fixture sweep, no hicasso-only dedupe, no publish on re-frame.test-support, no further deferral. Three findings carry it, each re-measured at tip b26c5ad33e rather than inherited from the bead's earlier numbers:

(1) The hazard the bead is written around — a throw between a set and a restore leaking the flag bundle-wide — has ONE candidate site in the whole repo, and it is not in hicasso. Repo-wide there are exactly two prior-value restores: implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3280/3351 (act-prev, restored under `finally`) and implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:218-223 (prev, restored by `teardown!` at :243, called from the async continuation at :306 — NOT under `finally`; see PREMISE CORRECTIONS). Every one of the 43 `set!` lines under implementation/hicasso sets `false`; zero restore anything. There is no restore in that tree for a throw to skip.

(2) What the flag does makes the residual "hazard" a warning-policy leak, not a scheduler or timing leak (Codex's semantic correction, accepted — see WEIGHING). A `false` left behind suppresses "not wrapped in act" warnings in later tests of the same browser build; it does not defer renders or change what a test measures. The three repaired incidents the 2026-07-28 ruling cited (43ce4cf9f6, 1fff5b618b, 0dd432b9ed) were warning-state repairs of a `true` leaking across the shared page, consistent with that reading.

(3) What is left is a two-line duplicated helper (`leave-act-environment!` at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and roots_frames_support.cljs:82) whose stated reason for existing twice — the freeze gate forbidding a `:require` of the bench helper — was retired by 8a10915ed8 on 2026-08-29, and whose 35 callers split 22/13 for structural reasons: 34 of the 35 use other functions from the same support namespace, and exactly one (state_dom_cljs_test.cljs) requires checkpoint-support solely for the setter. A dedupe would touch ~35 files in the repo's hottest test tree to remove one redundant require and one redundant defn, retiring no hazard. That is the trade that got the 2026-08-21 lift withdrawn, and the stance (pre-alpha, trust the programmer, do not drown in minutiae) says close it rather than action it.

The placement question that was held for Mike needs no ruling. The repo-private cross-artefact home implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs already exists, is dependency-free (requires only clojure.string), sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath beside hicasso/test (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:34 "core/test", :137 "hicasso/test"), and is required today from three places: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reg_view_devtools_dom_cljs_test.cljs, implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs and implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs. "Can hicasso's tests reach a core test-support namespace" is yes, today, without publishing anything. The 2026-07-28 ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (items 1-3: no donor dependency; one repo-private implementation in that home; the save/restore design floor) stands as the SHAPE for any act-environment fixture that is ever genuinely needed; nothing here overturns it. What this ruling adds is that no such fixture is needed now, and the trigger for one is a diagnostic-policy decision, not this bead.

HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED

Dossier author (sections "Summary" through "Evidence"; recommends A, close). Accepted on its main line: the census both ways, the disproven hazard, the drifted docstrings, the dead freeze gate, the existing home, and the rejection of C. Two of its facts are corrected at tip below: "both restore brackets are correct" (the ssr one restores the prior value but is not throw-safe) and "one parameterised on? helper" (there are two, one of them prose in docs). Its option B ("rule the home and dispatch a hicasso-only dedupe") is described as viable and it is, but its own cost line — a wide mechanical diff for zero hazard retired — is why it loses.

Codex ("Codex Recommendation"; also recommends close, and adds "do not dispatch a standalone hicasso dedupe as a substitute"). Weighed heavily on three points, each re-measured here rather than taken on trust. (a) The semantic correction: IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT is React's `isConcurrentActEnvironment()` predicate gating the "not wrapped in act" warnings, while the act queue is `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue`, controlled by `act()` itself. I did not re-read React's source; the citation (ReactFiberAct.js at the v19.2.0 tag, matching the installed react-dom 19.2.0) is specific and consistent with the three repaired incidents, and it changes the disposition in no direction, so it is recorded as Codex's reading, accepted. It DOES sharpen one thing the worker and the mayor both wrote: "a finally-restore would re-enter the act environment and change behaviour" overstates it — a restore would change later WARNING policy, not scheduling — but the conclusion survives, because the hicasso disable is a deliberate lane-wide policy with nothing anyone wants to restore to. (b) The caller split is structural, not arbitrary: verified at tip, 35 callers, 34 use other functions from their chosen support namespace, one (state_dom_cljs_test.cljs, alias `checkpoint`) does not. This overturns the worker's 2026-08-21 claim that native_abi_dom_cljs_test, foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test, imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test require the multi-root harness SOLELY for the setter: the first and fourth no longer exist under any tracked path, and the second and third use cell-keys / make-reset-runtime-fixture / skip! and census / poll-until / released / teardown-census! respectively. The "latent wart in the converted half" is one file, not a class. (c) The freeze-gate residue is wider than the two docstrings — nine lines across nine hicasso test files by `freeze gate|freeze-gate` at tip (Codex counted ten) — and is independent of where the setter bodies live. Codex's reframing of any future work as "warning-state isolation, not scheduler fixture" is adopted below as the reopening condition.

Where the two disagree: the dossier presents B as a live option that a later irritation could justify; Codex says a dedupe would "centralise the spelling of a global write without establishing a correct shared policy for that global" and must not be done as a substitute for the real question. Codex's position is the one recorded, with one preservation of the dossier's view: if somebody is ALREADY refactoring both support namespaces, folding the two defns into one is a free by-product and needs no bead (recipe below). It is not worth a dispatch on its own.

MAYOR 2026-08-18, BACKLOG REREAD — THIS IS A DEFERRAL WITH NO DATE AND NO STATED RELEASE CONDITION, WHICH IS THE ONE SHAPE THAT NEVER GETS RE-EXAMINED. Giving it a condition rather than a date, so a future tick can test it.

THE STATE I FOUND: status DEFERRED, defer_until NONE, untouched since 2026-07-28. Of ten deferred beads it is one of only two with no date at all; the other (rf2-2hpxo) has a real condition written into it — API-freeze. This one had neither.

THE BEAD IS HONEST ABOUT ITS OWN VALUE AND I AM NOT OVERRIDING THAT. It says so itself: rf2-76lhy originally advanced the flag leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown, and PR #7190's per-namespace profile DISSOLVED that — 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. 'There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.' It is a HYGIENE bead, and it says so.

SO WHY NOT CLOSE IT AS MINUTIAE. Because the hazard class is real and is exactly the kind this project takes seriously: a test that throws between the set and the restore leaks a process-global into every subsequent namespace in the bundle, and NO ASSERTION CAN CATCH IT — it surfaces later as unexplained slowness or flakiness, which is the hardest possible failure to attribute. The remedy is small and correct: one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally. Closing it would discard a real hazard on the grounds that it has not bitten yet.

THE RELEASE CONDITION, which is what was missing: DISPATCH THIS WHEN THE FLEET IS QUIET — no more than one other worker out, and no open PR touching implementation/ test namespaces. NOT because it is risky, but because 73 test files across the tree is the largest merge-conflict surface any single bead in this backlog carries, and a mechanical sweep that has to rebase past several landings will cost more in conflicts than the change is worth. Measured context for that: on 2026-08-18 the fleet ran 6 workers with 5 PRs open and the trunk moved 11 commits inside one worker's run.

SIZE IT WHEN IT GOES OUT: 73 files is above the single-dispatch comfort line here, so expect to split by artefact rather than send one worker at all of them.

NOT A NEW DEFERRAL DATE — deliberately. A date would fire on a day that may be just as busy. The condition is about fleet state, and the backlog-reread loop is the tick that can test it.

FOUR OF THE FIVE PREMISES DO NOT HOLD IN THIS TREE.

1. THERE ARE NO SET/RESTORE PAIRS. All 51 in-scope sites are
   `(set! (.-IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT js/globalThis) false)`. Zero set `true`; zero
   restore anything; zero `finally` within six lines of any site (checked per file by
   awk, and by a value histogram taken two independent ways). So the hazard the bead is
   written around — "a test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag"
   — HAS NO INSTANCE HERE. There is no restore for a throw to skip.

   Repo-wide the pattern is nearly as rare: of 90 raw `set!` lines, 66 set `false`, 22
   set `true`, and exactly TWO restore a captured prior value —
   implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3351 and
   implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:223. Both
   are outside hicasso. The set/restore bracket the bead describes is 2 of 90 sites
   repo-wide, in two files, in two other artefacts.

2. THE PACKAGE ALREADY HAS THE SHARED HELPER, AND MOST OF THE TREE ALREADY USES IT.
   `leave-act-environment!` is defined at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76, and 34 files / 38 call sites in this very tree already
   call it. Repo-wide there are 98 converted call sites — 59 in the bench tree, 38 in
   the hicasso package, 1 in core. The tree is roughly 43% consolidated already
   (38 converted vs 51 raw), not 0%.

3. THE CENSUS METHOD UNDERCOUNTS BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is the correction that
   reframes the bead. A CONVERTED site does not contain the literal
   `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` — it reads `(support/leave-act-environment!)`. So
   `git grep IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` measures the UNCONVERTED TAIL, never the
   population. The recorded "69 files / 100 sites, nine trees" is a remainder. The real
   population is that remainder plus 98 already-converted call sites, and the shape of
   the remaining work is "finish a migration already 50%+ done", not "introduce a
   fixture into a tree that has none".

4. THE SPECIFIED BAR CANNOT BE MET WITHOUT A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. "One shared fixture with
   the restore in a `finally`" would RE-ENTER the act environment after each test. Every
   docstring in the tree says the disable is deliberate and LANE-WIDE, not a bracket:
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76-85 — "React's `act` queue is not the browser's scheduler,
   and every reading in these suites is taken outside it — a commit measured here is the
   commit a user's page performs." A `finally`-restore would contradict that and would
   violate the dispatch's own "no behaviour change" requirement. The one restoring idiom
   in the repo (ssr) captures the PRIOR value rather than forcing `true`/`false`, which
   is right for a bracketed region and wrong for a lane.

   The fifth premise — that the population might be heterogeneous — is wrong in the safe
   direction: it is perfectly homogeneous. 51 of 51 set `false`.

WHY FINISHING THE MIGRATION IS NOT A SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION.

The two helper definitions are byte-identical and the 34 existing callers split between
them with no principle: 22 files take it from checkpoint-support (THE MICROTASK-CHECKPOINT
INSTRUMENT), 12 from roots-frames-support (THE MULTI-ROOT WITNESS HARNESS). Several
already require a heavyweight, purpose-specific harness namespace SOLELY to reach a
two-line flag setter — native_abi_dom_cljs_test, foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test,
imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test all require the multi-root
witness harness for exactly that. That is a latent wart in the converted half.

Of the 45 raw files, only 8 already require one of the two support namespaces (a free
one-line conversion). The other 37 would each GAIN a `:require` on a namespace whose
stated purpose is unrelated to theirs — deepening that wart 37 more times rather than
fixing it.

Doing it PROPERLY means minting one canonical act-env home, deleting both duplicate
definitions, re-pointing all 34 existing callers AND converting the 45 raw files: ~80
files in the tree, for ZERO hazard retired, against a tree with live peers. That is the
same maximal merge-conflict change with no motivating defect that got this bead deferred
in the first place, merely confined to one artefact. Per the stance — reject
over-engineering, close minutiae rather than actioning it — I am refusing it rather than
landing it.

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THE DISPATCH ASKED (reusable, or hicasso-specific?)

In SUBSTANCE the helper is not hicasso-specific at all — it is a two-line global setter
with a docstring. In PLACEMENT it is, and that is the whole difficulty. It lives in the
hicasso package TEST tree, which the other eight artefacts have no business importing
(and which the freeze gate already fences in the other direction:
frozen-sources.edn :forbidden-import-prefixes ["re-frame.bench." "re-frame.freehand."]).
A repo-wide answer therefore needs a shared home every test tree can reach. The only
existing candidate is `re-frame.test-support` — but that is
implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc, inside core's `:paths ["src"]`, i.e.
a PUBLISHED surface. Putting a test-only React flag setter there is exactly the
architectural decision PR #7193 flagged and left to Mike, and it is unchanged by the
re-frame.ui / re-frame.freehand retirement. So: NOT reusable as it stands, and making it
reusable is Mike's call, not hygiene.

REMAINING RAW `set!` CENSUS AT TIP (files / sites, .beads excluded)

  implementation/hicasso (package)   45 / 51   <- dispatched scope, refused above
  implementation/adapters             7 / 13
  implementation/core                 2 /  9
  implementation/ssr                  2 /  3
  tools/xray                          3 /  3
  implementation/routing              2 /  2
  implementation/machines             1 /  2
  tools/machines-viz                  2 /  2
  implementation/hicasso (bench)      2 /  2
  tools/story                         1 /  1
  implementation/hicasso (test_kit)   1 /  1
  implementation/hicasso (testbed)    1 /  1
                                     ---------
                                     69 / 90

  (90 raw `set!` lines. The recorded "100 sites" counts every LINE mentioning the
  literal, which includes ten that are not `set!` calls — docstring and comment prose
  explaining why the flag is set outright. In the dispatched scope the same split is
  54 mentions / 51 `set!` calls / 3 prose lines.)

RECOMMENDATION

Retire the bead's hazard framing rather than the sites. As written it describes a
set/restore leak that exists in 2 sites repo-wide, neither in hicasso. What actually
remains is a half-finished DRY migration with no defect behind it and no shared home
available without a published-surface ruling. Either close it as minutiae, or re-file the
narrow real item: "hicasso has two byte-identical `leave-act-environment!` definitions and
callers split arbitrarily between them" — which is a genuine wart, but a ~35-file
re-point, and still retires no hazard.

Gates: none run, and none needed — no file was modified. The box was also not free
(24 node processes, three started within the minute), so a heavyweight CLJS suite would
have been the wrong thing to start regardless.

MAYOR 2026-08-21 05:20 AUSEST — THE REFUSAL IS ACCEPTED AND THE ERROR WAS MINE. Recording the mayor-side half, because the worker's comment records the measurement and not what produced the bad brief.

MY CENSUS WAS WRONG BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE WORKER'S POINT 3 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. THAT IS A COUNT-IS-A-CLAIM FAILURE OF A SPECIFIC KIND WORTH NAMING: I checked that the number was CURRENT and never checked what the number MEASURED. Re-running a stale census correctly still gets you the wrong answer if the instrument was never right. A migration's own census must count BOTH forms — the converted call and the unconverted literal — or it cannot see its own denominator.

So the hazard this bead is built on — a throw between the set and the restore — HAS NO INSTANCE in that tree. And the bar I wrote (restore in a finally, no behaviour change) is self-contradictory: roots_frames_support.cljs:76-85 records the disable as lane-wide and DELIBERATE, so restoring would re-enter the act environment and change behaviour.

DISPOSITION. The scoped lift I recorded at 04:52 is WITHDRAWN; the bead returns to DEFERRED on its original grounds, which the worker's measurement strengthens rather than weakens. I also record the honest reason I lifted it: I was reaching for worker saturation, and the stance says close minutiae rather than action it. The authority I cited (PR #7193's 'do it per-artefact later') was real but it was not why I reached for it.

THE ONE GENUINE ITEM THE REFUSAL SURFACES, held for Mike rather than filed as work: two BYTE-IDENTICAL leave-act-environment! definitions (checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and roots_frames_support.cljs:76) with their 34 callers split arbitrarily between them, 22 and 12. title: Grow the 009 ratchet by a Tags-column keys-set diff (NOT a trace-op arm) — ruled after rf2-wsopx
description:
MAYOR RULING: YES, and only the Tags arm (2026-07-26). The rf2-wsopx worker recommended this and asked rather than filing it, per its brief. I am adopting its reasoning as filed.

WHY THIS IS WORTH BUILDING AT ALL: the 009 ratchet pins the Channel column and the error/warning emit sites — not trace ops and NOT the Tags column. That blind spot is why spec/009 never received the EP-0037 planner rows: :rf.route/prefetched appeared ZERO times in the catalogue while shipping, and :rf.error/resource-route-plan Tags column omitted both :plan-cause and :contributor while its narrative still taught partial planning against the ratified atomicity rule. A gate whose coverage never reaches the column where drift accumulates will keep reporting green over it.

THE RULED SHAPE — Tags-column keys-set diff, and nothing else: Spec-Schemas.md ALREADY defines one *Tags schema per catalogue row, and both files are ALREADY parsed by existing gates. So the arm is a keys-set comparison between the schema and the row, which the worker describes as "a parser away". It would have caught the Tags omission directly.

WHY NOT THE TRACE-OP ARM, which is the tempting other half: there is no per-op schema roster to diff against, so the only available check is "is every emitted op documented somewhere in 2500 lines of prose?" — a scan with a bad false-positive rate. That is the expensive half for the weaker signal, and this repo has already learned that a census whose pattern cannot distinguish a correction from a defect will fight every fix. Declined.

CONSTRAINTS: extend the EXISTING gate, do not add a new script. No new vocabulary. If the keys-set diff turns out to need a second source of truth to be meaningful, STOP and report — a gate needing a hand-maintained roster is the drift generator this repo keeps removing (see the derived evidence-producer roster that ended its class after going stale twice by hand-copying).

NON-VACUITY IS MANDATORY: prove the arm reds against the PRE-rf2-wsopx catalogue state, where :plan-cause and :contributor were genuinely missing from the row. An arm that cannot red on the defect that motivated it has not been tested — and this repo has shipped exactly that mistake before, where an audit method could not have caught its own motivating instance.
notes:
WORKER 2026-08-21 (PR #8583) — PREMISE CHECK FIRST, then the one outstanding obligation.

THE ARM WAS ALREADY BUILT. The dispatch brief asked for the Tags-column keys-set diff to be
constructed. It shipped at 6035062599 under this bead, and five later commits hardened it:
ee645d3263 (009 states the column is gated), 4f105c5707 (a key in link text is not a documented
key), 5655058e72 (SchemaValidationFailureTags pairing), a855f10384 (the paired-count floor),
0eeab48748 (baseline emptied). Nine Tags-column deftests ship today, INCLUDING the mandated
non-vacuity proof at tags-column-arm-reds-on-its-motivating-defect. Re-deriving it would have
duplicated it. The three earlier obligations on this bead — whole-:operation pairing, the #7207
SchemaValidationFailure pairing, and the #8562 parser repair — are all discharged.

THE ONE THAT WAS NOT: the #8562 audit ordered the repair "and pin the existing infinite-pagination
row as the positive fixture so the real Tags cell is observed". PR #8576 did the repair (negative
lookbehind) and pinned it IN PROSE ONLY — its commit message says "No existing assertion changes",
and reverting the lookbehind ran all 28 tests / 177 assertions GREEN. The reader deciding WHICH
COLUMN the arm adjudicates was itself unratcheted, which is this bead's thesis one level down.

DELIVERED, one deftest / +7 assertions (28/177 -> 29/184, exit 0 captured):
  1. the live escaped-pipe row's :tags cell must harvest :resource-id, :infinite;
  2. a column-alignment invariant over every active row, derived from the corpus via a new
     :field-count key on the EXISTING reader — no second parser, no column literal;
  3. a synthetic escaped-pipe row proved end to end through tags-column-findings' verdict.

PROOFS. Planted fault = the pre-repair reader recovered verbatim from `git show 7d2dad1e7a^`;
it reds exactly and only the new deftest, 4 of 7 assertions, other 28 tests green — which is
also the measurement showing the state was genuinely unpinned. Restore verified by the identical
blob hash 8ab3f25f65a929db8b810175bf074b0e0fdaac5f. Historical non-vacuity: the arm driven over
`git show 344c5f7e09^` spec/009 + Spec-Schemas reports 24 findings including
{:rf.error/resource-route-plan "ResourceRoutePlanTags" :missing [:contributor :plan-cause]},
and :rf.route/prefetched appears ZERO times in that catalogue — both bead claims confirmed.

Corpus re-derived at this base: header 6 columns / 8 fields, 513 active rows, all 513 at 8.
Fast spine NOT run — worker/bisect-9jrhi held the machine; check_fast_pr_gap.py --list = 94.
close_reason: Ruled arm shipped at 6035062599 and hardened since; the one outstanding obligation (the #8562 audit's positive fixture pinning the escaped-pipe row's real Tags cell) lands in PR #8583, with a column-alignment invariant generalising it. All four obligations on this bead now discharged.

title: http: re-frame.http-privacy-integration-test fails when run as a solo namespace (order-dependent fixture fragility, pre-existing)
description: Running the http artefact's privacy integration namespace ALONE — clojure -M:test -n re-frame.http-privacy-integration-test — fails 4 tests that are green in the full-suite ordering: response-body-decode-schema-sensitive-slot-redacted-in-replied-trace, response-body-whole-body-sensitive-decode-schema-redacts-all, response-body-large-slot-elided-in-replied-trace (ERROR), accept-failure-emits-category-trace-with-schema-classified-decoded. Measured 2026-08-31 during rf2-lddbk (PR #8818) on the UNTOUCHED base version of the file at trunk 95222a2c3d: solo run captured exit 1 (Ran 17 tests, 3 failures 1 error), full-suite run captured exit 0 (502 tests, 3827 assertions). The failures show schema-marked sensitive slots riding unredacted (e.g. bearer-secret at [:tags :value :token]), so some state a PRIOR namespace's load or fixture normally establishes is missing in the solo ordering — likely a registration (schemas artefact load? classification hook?) that make-reset-runtime-fixture does not itself establish. Not introduced by rf2-lddbk: reproduced byte-identically on the base file. Impact: low — CI runs the full suite — but it makes focused local iteration on that namespace read false-red and could mask real regressions behind expected noise. Fix shape: make the namespace self-sufficient (require/establish whatever the redaction path needs) or teach the fixture to establish it.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8889, branch worker/http-robust-o9e15): FIXED. Premise reproduced exactly at trunk 24b33a618a before any edit - solo exit 1 (20 tests, 3 failures, 1 error), full suite exit 0 (508 tests, 3881 assertions) - and the guess recorded in the description turned out RIGHT, now verified at source rather than guessed.

ROOT CAUSE - the missing establishment is the re-frame.schemas NAMESPACE LOAD. privacy-body/decode-schema-marks reaches the per-slot classifier through the late-bind hooks :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema and :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema, which re-frame.schemas publishes at the bottom of its facade ns (re_frame/schemas.cljc). privacy-body/extract-paths returns an EMPTY MAP when the hook is unbound, so an unloaded schemas artefact does not error - it silently classifies nothing, and every schema-marked secret rides verbatim. Probed directly under this namespace own require set: hook unbound, marks empty; after requiring re-frame.schemas the same schema yields the expected [:token] sensitive mark. In the full suite the alphabetically earlier re-frame.http-privacy-body-test - which ALREADY carries this require, commented load-bearing - binds the hooks first, which is the accidental establishment that made the full ordering green.

All four reported failures are that one cause. The ERROR on response-body-large-slot-elided-in-replied-trace is the same thing wearing a different face: contains? was called on the UNelided String and threw IllegalArgumentException.

REPAIR - declare the dependency in this namespace require, exactly as the sibling re-frame.http-privacy-body-test already does. NOT fixed in make-reset-runtime-fixture: that fixture lives in implementation/core, which must not load an optional artefact, since the whole point of the late-bind seam is that core does not depend on schemas. No assertion was weakened - these pin that secrets are redacted, and making them laxer would have converted a test-ordering defect into a silent privacy hole.

GATES on the final rebased base, captured exit codes: solo re-frame.http-privacy-integration-test exit 0 (20 tests, 49 assertions) - the red-to-green control; full suite exit 0 (508 tests, 3883 assertions) - unchanged green. The diagnostic probe was exercised in BOTH directions in one run (unbound hook yielding no marks, then bound hook yielding the expected mark), so its nothing-here answer was checked against an input it should flag.

WORTH KNOWING - CI only ever runs the full-suite ordering (jvm-http in test.yml runs a bare clojure -M:test), so no gate would have caught this, and none will catch the next namespace that acquires the same latent dependency. Related: rf2-o9e15 rode the same worker; the two turned out INDEPENDENT - shared shape, unrelated mechanisms.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8889 (commit 54cc3e9f3e, branch worker/http-robust-o9e15). The missing establishment was the re-frame.schemas namespace load, which publishes the :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema and :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema late-bind hooks; privacy-body/extract-paths returns an empty map when they are unbound, so classification silently did nothing and schema-marked secrets rode verbatim. Repaired by declaring that require in the test namespace, matching the sibling re-frame.http-privacy-body-test. Control: solo run exit 1 (3 failures, 1 error) before, exit 0 (20 tests, 49 assertions) after, with the full suite exit 0 (508 tests, 3883 assertions) throughout. No assertion weakened. Full verdict in the notes.

title: hic: tool.cljs unjoinable-intent branch (id-less trace bundle) — reachable per Spec 009, unexercised
description: From rf2-dr90's audit. tool.cljs's merge-fragments/intent-rows (~:566-577, :587) handle a ring bundle with no :dispatch-id: it keeps its own identity, sorts last, exports :unknown. Zero exercise anywhere. Spec 009 §Dispatch correlation explicitly admits trace events with NO :rf.trace/dispatch-id ('emitted outside any in-flight run — handler registration before any dispatch, REPL evals that don't dispatch — carry no dispatch-id'), so the branch is NOT dead defensive code; what is unestablished is whether such uncorrelated events can reach read-intents' window through trace-tooling/trace-buffer's bundling, or whether the buffer drops them before the tool sees one. Task: establish that reachability first; if reachable, add the row (assert identity kept, sorted last, :unknown exported); if the buffer provably cannot deliver one, record that as the finding on this bead and close without a test.
notes:
FENCE - SEQUENCED BEHIND PR #8737 (rf2-dr90's draft), recorded 2026-08-29 10:32 AUSEST by the merge+dispatch tick. Same hicasso test surface as the live dr90 worker. Dispatch after #8737 merges, off the post-merge trunk. PLANNED SHAPE: cluster with rf2-s2ta and rf2-xofa. Whoever dispatches strikes this fence line in the same act.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-08-29 11:12 AUSEST by the mayor, in the same act as dispatch: PR #8737 is MERGED (trunk 6eb0a2a402). Dispatched as the planned three-bead cluster (rf2-i011, rf2-s2ta, rf2-xofa in commit order) to worktree hic-browser-rows, branch worker/hic-browser-rows.
REACHABILITY VERDICT (2026-08-29, hic-browser-rows cluster worker, measured at source on worker/hic-browser-rows off trunk 6eb0a2a402): NOT REACHABLE through trace-tooling/trace-buffer's bundling — closing without a test, per this bead's own terms.

THE EVIDENCE, all four legs at source:
1. read-intents' window is exactly (trace-tooling/trace-buffer fid) per frame (tool.cljs:633; explain-render's window :795 is the same door). The per-frame ring is the ONLY supplier of bundles to intent-rows.
2. The ring cannot retain an id-less event. push-to-ring! guards (when (and dispatch-id frame-id) ...) — implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:251-259 — and its docstring names the rule: frameless emits stream live to listeners only and are never retained. That is Spec 009's B3 ruling verbatim: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:879 'frameless events SKIP the rings entirely ... NEVER retained in any ring', :881 'no shared uncorrelated bucket, no fallback slot', :965 'Frameless events bypass the ring'.
3. A bundle is minted ONLY from ring run-keys: frame-ring-event-bundles maps :run-order and event-bundle seeds :dispatch-id from that key (tooling.cljc:476-488, :414-420), so a bundle's :dispatch-id is non-nil by construction. The other trace-rings writers (set-frame-events-retained! ~:204, clear-trace-buffer! ~:563, clear-trace-rings! ~:582, the inherited-default retune ~:646) resize or empty rings and mint no run key.
4. The uncorrelated events Spec 009 SDispatch-correlation admits (registry-time emits, REPL evals — spec line 72) therefore exist on the LIVE listener stream only. The :ungrouped slot at spec :798 belongs to the flat-stream group-by-event PROJECTION, not to the ring, and read-intents does not consume it.

CONCLUSION: tool.cljs's unjoinable branch (:576-577 nil-id assoc; :581-582 sorts-last; :587 exports evidence/unknown) is defensive-in-depth against a shape the buffer provably cannot deliver. The branch STAYS — it also defends the sort/export against a hypothetical manual emit carrying a non-numeric :rf.trace/dispatch-id with a :frame tag (tooling.cljc:255-257 calls that 'extremely rare - a manual emit from outside any framework boundary'), and against any future ring-side change — but no test can honestly reach it through the public path, and fabricating a windows map to force intent-rows through it would pin nothing the runtime can produce. Grepped: ::unjoinable appears only at its definition site; zero exercise anywhere, as the audit said.

title: hicasso: standardize native benchmark self-test flag
description: PR #8610 audit finding. The native Hicasso benchmark drivers use two spellings for the same operator-facing self-test mode: clock_run.cjs, hd8_run.cjs, and ladder_band.cjs use --selftest while the surrounding helper fleet and package scripts predominantly use --self-test. The split already caused a plausible wrong census and left ladder_band's guard unregistered until #8610. Standardize these three direct CLIs and their usage/comments/callers on --self-test; preserve the existing direct fixture exports and do not add duplicate package registrations for clock/hd8, which clock_exit_path.test.cjs already reaches. Pre-alpha means no compatibility alias is required.
acceptance_criteria: All native benchmark driver self-test CLIs use --self-test; repository searches show no executable or operator-facing --selftest residue for the three drivers; the existing helper gate still reaches the same adjudicator fixtures and remains green.
notes:
## 2026-08-21 09:15 AUSEST — audit remainder discharged (PR #8621)

The #8616 audit's three asks, all taken.

1. NO ALIAS. Unchanged and deliberate: pre-alpha, and an alias for a spelling
   nothing depends on is a compatibility shim.

2. FAIL FAST — read as strict unknown-argument rejection, not a narrower guard,
   and the reason is that for these two drivers the strict rule IS the narrow
   one. `clock_run.cjs` and `hd8_run.cjs` take every knob they have from an
   `HCLOCK_*` / `HD8_*` environment variable and no positional argument at all,
   so their flag vocabulary is closed by construction at two entries and one.
   Writing that list down is the CLI's own surface, not an argument-validation
   framework: no parser, no generated help, no did-you-mean (which would be the
   nag this repo rejects). A list of dead tokens was rejected as the shim
   wearing a refusal's clothes — it would still swallow the next typo.
   `ladder_band.cjs` does take positionals, so its rule is scoped to the flag
   namespace; its previous refusal was incidental (ENOENT on a token it took
   for a filename) and said nothing to whoever typed it.

   Measured at 8d4672db2b under a child_process preload, so the heavyweight
   path was observed and not paid for: `--selftest` took `clock_run.cjs` to the
   shadow-cljs `:advanced` release spawn and `hd8_run.cjs` to `git rev-parse
   HEAD` in the provenance block, one line above `build()`. All three now exit
   2 before anything is built.

3. THE PIN, in the existing exit-path suite as asked. Four claims per driver:
   the argv definition itself, the closed vocabulary, that a token outside it
   is refused, and that the refusal is wired above every self-test, `build()`
   and `chromium` in the head of `main`. Proven by sabotage — reverting
   `clock_run.cjs`'s argv spelling reds the suite 2/383 naming both new tests;
   the earlier suite was green against that same mutation.

   `ladder_band.cjs` is deliberately NOT repeated there: `test:script-helpers`
   invokes it directly, and a second sabotage run confirmed that invocation
   catches the same mutation (gate exit 2 at that step).

No package registration added; `implementation/package.json` untouched, as
required by the fence around rf2-lr4id / rf2-0eu1s.

Gate: `npm run test:script-helpers` exit 0 pre-rebase, exit 2 sabotaged, exit 0
on the final rebased base. `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` exit 0. No
spine, no shadow-cljs, no browser, no JVM — an allocation window was live.

## 2026-08-21 10:05 AUSEST — the SECOND audit remainder, closed (PR #8627)

#8621's own merged-PR audit found the closed vocabulary held only on a PREFIX
of `ladder_band.cjs`'s argv. Its parser ran the self-test and returned from
INSIDE the loop, so no token after `--self-test` was ever read. Reproduced at
`origin/main` before touching anything, and the note above is where the gap
came from — it recorded that `test:script-helpers` invokes the driver directly,
which is true, but that invocation is `--self-test` alone: the PASSING case,
which says nothing about a refusal.

THE REPAIR separates PARSING from ACTING rather than adding a validating pass.
A second pass is where the care would have been needed, because `--emit` and
`--from` each consume the token AFTER them and a pass that did not know it
would read `--emit --from.json` as a flag. `parseArgv` is now pure and total:
one left-to-right read, each valued flag's value consumed as a value, returning
either the whole plan or the first reason there cannot be one. `main` is the
only thing that acts and cannot act before the parser reaches the end of argv,
so there is no prefix left to hide in. Exported, with the entry point behind
`require.main === module`, so the pin drives the rule instead of quoting it.

The flag-namespace scoping stays — this driver takes dataset filenames where

around PR #8620 respected. THE ORDER PAIR IS THE TEST: refused BEFORE

driven as real process exits, plus the valued-flag trap, plus a claim that
`parseArgv` may not call `selfTest()`, `readRun` or `process.exit`.

title: [bug] spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2392 has a stray pipe inside a cell, so the row parses as 9 fields and its RECOVERY column is read as :tags
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-zk1xu (twice — recorded as a sibling on that bead on 2026-08-20, then offered as a one-line PR by its worker on 2026-08-21) and deliberately NOT taken both times, because spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot zone and single-toucher and neither dispatch was going to grow its diff for it.

THE CLAIM, to re-derive at origin/main HEAD rather than trust: the row for :rf.error/infinite-missing-next-page-param at about line 2392 carries a stray | inside a cell, so parse-catalogue-tag-rows counts 9 fields instead of 8 and reads the row's RECOVERY column as its :tags cell.

WHY IT IS ONLY P4. It is harmless TODAY and the reason is specific rather than general: no InfiniteMissingNextPageParamTags schema exists to pair with the row, so the mis-read cell is never compared against anything. That is luck, not design — the day someone adds that schema the pairing arm compares a recovery string against a tag key set and reds for a reason that has nothing to do with the change in front of them.

THE FIX IS ONE CHARACTER, and the whole job is proving it is one character. Escape or remove the stray pipe so the row parses as 8 fields. Verify by running the catalogue conformance namespace before and after and showing the test and assertion counts are UNCHANGED — this must be a no-op for every existing assertion, and a count that moves means the row was load-bearing somewhere and the change is not the one-liner it looks like.

CLOSING THIS AS MINUTIAE IS AN ACCEPTABLE OUTCOME if the re-derivation shows the parse is already correct, or that the repair costs more than a hot-zone toucher slot is worth. Say so with the measurement rather than doing it silently.

SURFACE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md only. HOT ZONE — one toucher at a time. Cluster with rf2-zmpfn if that bead is still open at dispatch: both are catalogue-prose minutiae and the two together are still smaller than one ordinary bead.
close_reason:
PR #8588. Half 2 (the parity bug) fixed; half 1 (the missing assertion) was already on main at my base via PR #8583 / rf2-6tags, commit 4b9e029c88, and is NOT duplicated here.

THE RULE. parse-catalogue-tag-rows split on a one-character negative lookbehind, so it called every backslash-prefixed pipe escaped. Markdown decides by the PARITY of the backslash run before the pipe. The rule now lives in a named table-delimiter-re and is ZERO-WIDTH: the run is inspected, never consumed, so only where columns break changes and no cell loses a character.

THE AUDIT SAID FOUR CASES WERE WRONG; IT IS TWO. Re-derived against Python-Markdown 3.10's tables extension rather than taken on trust: the old lookbehind is right on the ODD runs by luck and wrong only on the EVEN ones. Which two matters, because the error hides a defect rather than manufacturing one -- an even run really has broken the row into an extra column, and a reader that swallows the delimiter hands rf2-6tags's column-alignment invariant a field count matching the row's siblings. Under-splitting DISARMS that guard.

FIXTURE. table-delimiter-honours-backslash-run-parity, a pure parser fixture over the existing catalogue-fixture helper. It must be constructed: Spec 009 carries eleven escaped pipes across nine lines, every one a run of exactly ONE, no even run anywhere, and only the infinite-missing-next-page-param row is in this reader's section -- so the even half of the rule is unreachable from the corpus.

NON-VACUITY. 29 tests / 184 assertions before, 30 / 194 after. Reverting to the old regex reds exactly 4 of the 10 new assertions (both at run 2, both at run 4) and nothing else; counts stayed 30/194 through the sabotage, so the plant was scoped. Restore verified against the committed object by an identical git blob hash.

The fast-PR spine was NOT run and was not required; the single targeted JVM namespace was the only gate run directly, exit codes captured by this worker. spec/009-Instrumentation.md untouched; rf2-zmpfn stays closed.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8576: Fixing the downstream reader rather than valid spec prose is correct, and rf2-zmpfn can remain closed. The parser half is incomplete in two coupled ways. First, no assertion pins the new behavior: the PR proves the old and new implementations both pass 28 tests / 177 assertions, because the motivating row has no paired schema, so reverting the fix stays green. Second, (?<!\\)\| checks only the immediately preceding character and treats every backslash-prefixed pipe as escaped. Markdown uses backslash-run parity: one or three backslashes escape the pipe, while two or four leave it as a column delimiter. A local Python-Markdown tables probe confirms that split, while this regex skips all four. Minimal completion: add a focused pure parser fixture covering a single escaped pipe and an even-backslash delimiter, then make the split parity-correct. Do not grow this into a general Markdown parser.

title: Spec-Schemas *Tags corpus counts in the catalogue conformance test's prose are stale (2 comments, 3 integers)
description:

  line 978: 'measured at the change, all 111 *Tags schemas but the one edited here are [:map-headed'
