(2) THE TRAP THAT ALMOST SHIPPED A DEAD GATE: the worker's first elision sentinel spelled its fully-qualified grep strings INSIDE that same docstring, so the grep found its own prose (2 hits) and would have false-failed forever — a check whose own text is the thing it detects. CORROBORATED FINDING: the reload machinery (rules.cljc reload-ledger? and everything behind it) is confirmed ABSENT from production builds. "THE PROGRAM DOES NOT READ X" IS NOT "THE DATA DOES NOT HAVE X" — and compressing the first into the second nearly stalled a P1 (2026-08-06).

WHAT I WROTE INTO THE regime-jcm3p BRIEF, as a blocking fact: "clock_readjudicate.cjs never reads census or kbShape - only ensemble ratios and the additive constant. If your restatement needs either, that route does not exist."

WHERE IT CAME FROM: a previous worker's report, and IT WAS RIGHT - about the PROGRAM. clock_readjudicate.cjs genuinely does not read those fields.

WHAT I TURNED IT INTO, which is false: "that route does not exist". THE DATASETS ON DISK CARRY eventTiming, census, kbShape AND A FULLY-RECONCILED kbWitness.perArm. The route existed; the program simply had not been extended to walk it. And rf2-swwud's own ruling directs the re-adjudication "from the two on-disk runs VIA clock_readjudicate.cjs" - so the bead was telling the worker to extend exactly the program I had declared a dead end.

THE COST IT NEARLY HAD, in the worker's own words: "Had I taken the brief literally I'd have stopped and asked for a new bead." That is a P1 that unblocks roughly twenty measurement beads, stalled for a round trip, by a sentence of mine.

THIS IS THE COMPRESSION ERROR AGAIN, second instance, same shape as "in the catalogued family" becoming "catalogued in". A careful statement about ONE artefact - a program, a namespace, a roster - became a statement about the WHOLE ROUTE. The qualifier that made it true looked like padding.

THE DISCRIMINATOR TO KEEP: when a report says a PROGRAM does not read something, ask separately whether the DATA carries it. Code and corpus are different artefacts and a claim about one is silent about the other. The same split applies to "the gate does not check X" (the fixture may still contain it) and "the spec does not say X" (the implementation may still do it) - both of which bit today in the opposite direction.

PROMOTING ex-data TO A WIRE SURFACE MAKES IT WIRE DATA — and one non-EDN value does not fail quietly. Found fixing pair-mcp relay 1 (rf2-qoih4): merging raw ex-data into the consumer-facing envelope broke it, because `emit-name`'s ex-data carried `:type (type n)` — a JS constructor that pr-strs to `#object[Function ...]`. The consumer then fails with 'No reader function for tag object' on the WHOLE envelope, so they lose the message too, not just the bad key. NET EFFECT: a change intended to give the consumer MORE information gives them none. RULE: before promoting any internal map onto a wire/MCP surface, audit every value for EDN round-trippability; prefer `(pr-str x)` for anything that is not plainly data, and drop keys that tell the reader nothing. Related: the sibling relay-2 fix (rf2-6tzm5) had a genuinely nil ripple, which is exactly why 'measure, do not inherit the sibling's conclusion' was the right instruction.

PROVE A COMMITTED TEST WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE ORIGINAL BUG — build a mutant of the broken version. Established by the rf2-fr5yx worker (#6414) closing out my own failure.

BACKGROUND: I commissioned the ai/ ratchet (rf2-lsp1i #6380), accepted a three-teeth proof, merged it, and told the operator his end-state ruling was enforced. It was a STATIC CEILING: 89->61 passed, then 61->62 ALSO passed. All three teeth were genuine; each tested a SINGLE TRANSITION from a pristine baseline. The defect lived only in the composition, and the proof lived only in a chat report, so nothing re-ran it.

WHAT #6414 DID, and what to copy: it did not merely commit the seven arms. It BUILT A FAITHFUL MUTANT OF THE ORIGINAL BROKEN GATE (stale root-commit ceiling + count comparison) and ran the new suite against it. Result: arms 3+4, 5, 6b and 7 FAILED while arms 1 and 2 still passed — and arm 3+4 failed on exactly the right assertion (decrease passed, then the increase also passed, 0 !== 1). That demonstrates the committed test CATCHES THE SHIPPED BUG, rather than merely passing on the fixed code. It also kept a second, lighter control: the old decision rule reproduced in-test and asserted to pass the arms it should pass.

THE RULE: when committing a regression test for a bug that already shipped, do not stop at "green on the fix". Reconstruct the broken behaviour and show the suite REDS against it, arm by arm. A suite that only ever ran against correct code has never been shown to discriminate. This is the same scepticism as the mutation-proof rule, applied to the proof itself — and it is how you find that a tooth is a passenger (rf2-kxork found a suffix rename still contained its sentinel; rf2-vxgfnd.195 arm 4 built a function-name oracle, measured that it could never go red, and DELETED it).

SAFE-FIXTURE TECHNIQUE for gates that inspect the repo: build a throwaway repo under os.tmpdir() and ASSERT IT IS NOT THIS REPOSITORY before writing any guarded path. #6414 used the temp-repo + script-on-stdin form (sh -s) from _changed-surfaces.test.cjs so it runs the REAL script bytes and sidesteps Windows path translation. Never `git add -f` under a guarded tree to test its guard — the fixed ratchet has no in-band escape hatch, so a test that actually tracked a file could not clean up without an operator policy exception.

PROVE "NOTHING CHANGED ON THE TRACKER SINCE MY LAST PASS" FROM THE EXPORT DIFF, NOT FROM MEMORY OR A RE-READ (2026-08-23).

THE PROBLEM. The backlog-reread loop fires hourly and says do NOT rely on memory. On a static board that reads as an instruction to re-read fourteen long beads every hour, which is exactly what the method's own reread loop calls spending context for nothing. But "I remember it was the same" is not evidence either.

THE INSTRUMENT, two halves that together cover the whole window:

1. COMMITTED MUTATIONS: git log --since=<last pass> -- .beads/issues.jsonl gives the checkpoint commits spanning the window; git diff <first>..<last> -- .beads/issues.jsonl shows exactly which records changed. Parse the +/- lines as JSON and collect the id field to get the changed BEAD IDS.
2. UNCOMMITTED MUTATIONS: git status --porcelain -- .beads/. bd AUTO-STAGES on every mutation but never commits, so a clean export proves no tracker write since the last checkpoint.

MEASURED THIS PASS: the window carried exactly ONE changed line, and parsing it returned id=None. That None was not a null to wave through -- inspecting it showed {"_type":"memory", ...}, my own bd remember record. So: ZERO bead mutations in the window, proven, and the deep re-read of all fourteen was genuinely null.

THE TRAP INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT: the export holds more than issues. Memory records share the file and carry no id, so an id-keyed parse reports None rather than nothing. Read what the None was before calling the diff empty -- a records-changed count of 1 with zero bead ids is a DIFFERENT fact from a diff of zero lines, and only one of them is "nothing happened".

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER. Two of the loop's four things depend on the WORLD changing rather than the bead: a fence clears when a PR merges or a worker dies, and neither touches the tracker. So pair the export diff with: HEAD == origin/main unchanged (no merges), and the worktree sweep. If the trunk has not moved and no bead has mutated, all four things are provably null.

PROVE WHAT THE GATE READS, NOT THE TEXT IT READS FROM (2026-08-14, rf2-46tt9 worker).

MY INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG FOR ITS CASE. I told three workers to prove a required gate's input was unaffected by extracting the gate-read sections from origin/main and from the branch and diffing them byte-for-byte. That worked for the first two, because they LEFT the fenced section alone. The third worker's edit was INSIDE that section, so the raw text NECESSARILY differed by one line. Its words: "Claiming byte-identity would have been false."

IT PROVED THE RIGHT THING INSTEAD: the DERIVED ROSTER — what the required job actually consumes. 43 ids, 21 surface spans, 0 problems, diff EXIT=0, and the gate's own stdout byte-identical at 15 names and 43 rows. AND IT BUILT THE EXTRACTOR BY IMPORTING THE GATE'S OWN SECTION PARSER, so the proof cannot drift from what CI runs.

THE GENERAL RULE: a gate consumes a DERIVED value, not a file. Prove the derived value is unchanged. Byte-identity of the SOURCE is a sufficient proof only when you did not touch the source — and in that case it is also the easy case. The interesting case is exactly the one where it cannot hold.

AND BUILD THE PROOF FROM THE GATE'S OWN CODE. An independently written extractor can drift from the gate and then prove something CI does not check.

A FORENSIC BONUS WORTH KEEPING. My quoted 42,767-byte figure and its measured 42,663 differ by EXACTLY 104 over 104 lines — one byte per line. The earlier extractor emitted CRLF, this one LF. THIS REPOSITORY'S DOCS ARE CRLF, which also silently no-ops newline-spanning regexes. A byte-count discrepancy that equals the line count is a line-ending difference, not a content difference.

check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since IS BLIND TO AN UNTRACKED FILE, so running it before committing a NEW page is a green over a file it never opened (2026-08-15 13:10 AUSEST).

MEASURED by worker/releasepol-hic061 while adding a new page under docs/design/hicasso/: the gate reported '1 page inspected' while its new file was untracked, and '2 pages inspected' after committing. Same command, same tree, one commit apart.

WHY IT HAPPENS AND WHY IT IS NOT A BUG: --changed-since derives its corpus from git's change detection against a ref. An untracked file is not a change against that ref; git has never heard of it. The gate is behaving correctly and reporting honestly -- it says how many pages it inspected. Nobody reads that number.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: the failure mode is a CONFIDENT GREEN over unexamined content, which is the same class as three other traps measured today -- a job-key regex that matched no job key, a gh pathspec whose loud refusal a pipeline laundered into zero, and an architecture census whose positive control seeded a name nothing else owned. In every case a check returned the expected answer having verified nothing. The pattern is now firm enough to state as a rule: A GATE THAT CANNOT SEE ITS SUBJECT RETURNS THE REASSURING ANSWER.

THE REMEDY IS PROCEDURAL AND COSTS NOTHING: COMMIT FIRST, THEN RUN THE SCOPED GATE. Or read the 'N pages inspected' line and check N covers what you changed -- the gate already prints the evidence that it examined nothing.

NOT FILED AS A BEAD, deliberately. The gate is correct by construction, the remedy is one habit rather than a code change, and the stance rejects nag-diagnostics and says to close minutiae rather than action it. This record is the durable form. If a worker ever ships a page whose provenance was never checked BECAUSE of this, that is the moment it earns a bead.

GENERALISES TO EVERY --changed-since / --since / diff-scoped gate in this repo, not just this one. A new file is invisible to all of them until it is tracked.

check_provenance_pins.py REFUSES SHA-LIKE AND DATE-LIKE TOKENS IN NEW docs/design/** PAGES, AND IT IS NOT IN THE DOC-BEAD GATE MENU (2026-08-09).

WHAT HAPPENED. Six hic-* Wave A doc beads shipped new pages under docs/design/hicasso/product/. TWO of the six went red on the same gate, for two DIFFERENT token shapes:
  - rf2-hic-003 / PR #7713: the token 20260807 at k1-price-acceptance.md line 23 -- the fixed bootstrap RNG SEED (verified in clock_readjudicate.cjs and asserted in clock_exit_path.test.cjs), NOT a date -- on a line whose nearest commit-word to the left was "PR #". Reported as "(commit word 'PR #' nearest on the left, uncoded)".
  - rf2-hic-073 / PR #7714: the token abc1234 at correction-ledger.md line 55 -- an ILLUSTRATIVE PLACEHOLDER SHA inside a worked dry-run example row. Reported as "(unclassified -- read as a pin (fail toward refusal))".
Both are false positives about tokens never meant as provenance citations. The checker fails toward refusal by design, which is correct behaviour.

THE SECOND RED CHECK IS A SHADOW, NOT A SECOND FAULT. "Docs required" is a docs.yml roll-up; its log reads "needs results: success, success, failure". It goes green the moment the pins job does. Read the LOGS, not the check names, or you dispatch two fix-workers for one bug.

WHY THE BRIEFS MISSED IT. CLAUDE.md names scripts/check_doc_slugs.py as the gate for docs/design/** (mkdocs --strict excludes that tree), so that is what went into the briefs and what every worker ran, green. check_provenance_pins.py ALSO gates that tree on changed pages, and nobody ran it locally. Every worker was honestly green on the gate it was told about. This is the "never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface" failure in its mirror form: the nominated gate was right but INCOMPLETE.

THE FIX FOR FUTURE DOC BRIEFS. Name BOTH gates:
  python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py
  git fetch --no-tags origin main; python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main --verbose
And warn the worker: write dates in ISO form 2026-08-07, never 20260807; never use a hex-looking placeholder such as abc1234 for an example commit -- use a clearly non-hex placeholder instead. The tool does NOT re-pin and states that a human decides each finding, so one false positive costs a full fix-worker round trip.

THE MAYOR'S OWN DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, AND THE WORKER CAUGHT IT. The fix brief asserted 20260807 was "almost certainly a DATE written without separators" and proposed rewriting it as ISO 2026-08-07. It is not a date. It is the fixed bootstrap RNG seed: literal "seed: 20260807" in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_readjudicate.cjs:383, asserted by assert.strictEqual(EFFECT.seed, 20260807) in clock_exit_path.test.cjs:4058, and written as "the fixed bootstrap seed 20260807" in the source studio page. Rewriting it as a date would have FALSIFIED A REPRODUCER VALUE while turning the gate green. The worker verified the token against the harness source instead of complying, and regrouped it to 20,260,807 -- value preserved, longest hex run now 3 characters, and robust against any future rewording of the line.

THE LESSON FOR BRIEFS: when handing a worker a diagnosis, mark it as a hypothesis to verify, never as a finding to implement. This brief did say "CONFIRM that by reading line 23 before you touch it", and that sentence is the only reason the record survived. Keep it in every CI-fix brief.

THE PROVENANCE-PIN PLANT HAS A TRAP THAT PRODUCES A FALSE NEGATIVE — found by the rf2-hic-048 worker on 2026-08-14.

WHAT HAPPENS. check_provenance_pins.py treats a stranded pin as PASSING when its own block carries a landed pin alongside it. So a worker who plants a stranded SHA in the natural place — beside an existing citation, where SHAs already live — gets exit 0 and concludes THE GATE DOES NOT REACH THIS FILE. It does. PRUNE GATE REFINEMENT: AN INTERIM REPORT THAT SAYS 'WAITING' IS NOT A TERMINAL REPORT (2026-07-25, third instance of the same class in one session).

I pruned worker/fh-event-site-facts's worktree and deleted its branches while it was mid-gate. My gate required (a) PR verifiably MERGED from that exact branch, (b) an agent report, (c) no TRACKED uncommitted work — and all three read as satisfied. The defect was in (b): the worker had sent SEVERAL reports, but each said in substance 'I am burning turns polling, I will stop and let the monitor wake me for the final spine result.' That is a worker announcing it is BLOCKED ON A WATCHER, not one announcing completion. Consequence: its final test-fast-pr.sh run died on a failed redirect into the deleted .gate-logs/, and the resulting exit 1 looked like a gate failure. It reported the row from the earlier base rather than claiming it twice, which is why nothing was lost.

THE DISTINCTION TO ENCODE: a terminal report SUMMARISES AND STOPS. An interim report NAMES SOMETHING IT IS STILL WAITING FOR — a monitor, an in-flight suite, a retry, a rebase it has not done yet. Phrases like 'waiting on', 'in flight', 'I will report its actual exit code', 'the retry is running' mean ALIVE, no matter how complete the rest of the report reads. The harness's completed status is also NOT terminality: a background agent notifies each time it stops with no live children, so the same task-id notifies repeatedly across one job.

SO THE GATE IS NOW FOUR CONDITIONS: (1) PR MERGED, head == the branch read from git worktree list --porcelain; (2) the agent's LAST report contains no outstanding-wait language; (3) no tracked uncommitted work (gitignored residue like .probe/ or .gate-logs/ is fine); (4) its beads closed or explicitly stated as deliberately open. If (2) is ambiguous, DO NOT PRUNE — message the worker and ask. A worktree costs disk; an early prune corrupts a gate run and emits log noise that reads as a real failure.

WHY THIS KEPT HAPPENING: the prune step lives in the merge sweep, so 'PR merged' is the signal in hand and terminality is a fact living in task notifications. Three times I let the available signal stand in for the required one. The fix is not more care — it is refusing to prune whenever terminality is inferred rather than read.

A FOURTH POST-MERGE PULL ABORT SHAPE, CAUSED BY CONCURRENT WORKERS SHARING FETCH_HEAD (2026-08-13).

MESSAGE: 'fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.' Exit 128, HEAD unmoved.

This is NOT any of the three shapes mayor-merge.md documents. It is not 'local changes would be overwritten' (uncommitted tracker state) and it is not 'Not possible to fast-forward' (genuine divergence), and BOTH of those remedies are inert against it. Clearing .beads does nothing - the tree was clean. Rebasing does nothing - there was nothing to rebase.

CAUSE: linked worktrees SHARE the primary checkout's .git, and therefore share ONE FETCH_HEAD file. Three background workers had just been dispatched and each ran git fetch in its own worktree. Their multi-ref FETCH_HEAD was what the mayor's 'git pull --ff-only origin main' then read, and a FETCH_HEAD naming several branches cannot be fast-forwarded to. The mayor's own command was correct; a peer overwrote the file between its fetch and its merge.

DISCRIMINATOR: git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main. It read '0 2' - zero ahead, two behind - which is a clean fast-forward, i.e. proof this is a race and not a divergence. The two documented aborts both show a non-zero LEFT number or a dirty tree.

REMEDY: bypass FETCH_HEAD entirely by merging the remote-tracking ref, which no peer can clobber:
  git fetch origin main
  git merge --ff-only origin/main
Then verify HEAD == origin/main and the divergence count reads 0 0.

EXPECT THIS TO GET MORE COMMON, NOT LESS: it scales with fleet size, and the merge loop's own advice to dispatch immediately after merging is what puts the fetches and the pull in the same seconds.

A post-merge pull that aborts is NOT always the uncommitted .beads/issues.jsonl — that diagnosis was wrong twice in one session (2026-08-07), and the documented remedy would have found nothing both times.

THE LOOP DOCS STATE IT AS THE CAUSE: bootstrap.md and mayor-merge both say 'If the pull aborts, an uncommitted .beads/issues.jsonl is the cause: run beads-checkpoint.sh, THEN git checkout HEAD -- .beads, THEN pull.' Treat that as ONE cause of three, not the cause.

FAILURE 1 — GENUINE DIVERGENCE, NOT THE TRACKER. 'git pull --ff-only' aborted with 'Not possible to fast-forward' on a CLEAN working tree. git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD showed 2/1: the repo's post-merge hook had committed 'chore(beads): audit merged PR NNNN' locally while the rebase-merge rewrote main remotely. The remedy is 'git pull --rebase' (or fetch + rebase origin/main). Running the checkpoint dance here finds nothing to fix and leaves the pull still aborting.

FAILURE 2 — STAGED, NOT MERELY UNCOMMITTED, AND THE DOCUMENTED CHECKOUT DOES NOT CLEAR IT. A later pull failed with 'cannot pull with rebase: Your index contains uncommitted changes'. .beads/issues.jsonl was STAGED with 3 insertions/2 deletions: bd auto-stages, and it had re-staged the file BETWEEN my 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' and the pull. 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' does not reliably leave the index clean when bd is re-staging behind you.

THE SEQUENCE THAT ACTUALLY WORKS, and it must stay in this order (checkpoint FIRST so the Dolt re-export is committed before anything reverts the working file):
  sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh
  git reset -q HEAD -- .beads
  git checkout -- .beads
  git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main

DIAGNOSE BEFORE APPLYING ANY OF IT: 'git status --short' plus 'git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD' distinguishes all three cases in one look — clean tree + divergence means rebase; staged .beads means reset-then-checkout; unstaged .beads means the documented remedy. NEVER git stash in any of them: stashes are repo-global and contaminate every worktree in flight.

A PYTHON SELF-TEST BUILT ON assert PROVES NOTHING UNDER -O, AND STILL PRINTS ITS SUCCESS LINE (2026-08-13, found by worker/fencecheck-t9kd).

`python -O` strips every `assert` statement. A self-test written as a run of asserts therefore executes zero checks under -O, falls through, and prints `self-test OK`. Exit 0. Nothing warns you.

WHERE IT WAS FOUND, WHICH IS THE POINT. The worker was dispatched to fix a fence checker that counted inert macro forms as live claims — a control that could not catch its own case. It then asked the generalising question of the file it was fixing and found the SAME defect class sitting in `--self-test`, i.e. in the control that was supposed to prove the fix. The instrument and the bug were the same shape.

It is family-wide here: all five hicasso sibling scripts exit 0 under -O. Filed as rf2-uyhh (P3, and the bead explicitly licenses a refusal — copying five lines into ~40 scripts may not be worth it) and rf2-df9b (P2, a related false-green in check_optional_module_reachability where `ns_of` takes the FIRST `(ns …)`, so a discarded `#_(ns …)` above the real form makes the scanner exempt the file).

THE FIX IS FIVE LINES: have `--self-test` REFUSE when assertions are disabled. Detect with `if not __debug__:` — it is False exactly when -O is in effect — and exit non-zero naming the cause. Do not try to re-enable assertions.

THE TRANSFERABLE RULE: ask of every control whether it is constructed so that it avoids the case it exists to catch. And when you fix one control, ask that question of its NEIGHBOURS in the same file before you leave — this worker found three live instances that way, and the sharpest one was in the file it had already opened.

Related: the hollow-gate test (delete the signal, keep the fault — if it stays green it was proving nothing). This is that test applied to the test harness itself.

MY PROVENANCE FIX WAS UNSOUND: RE-PINNING RESTORES THE PATCH, NOT THE TREE (2026-08-06, rf2-owq6p, PR #7616).

WHY IT IS WRONG AS A GENERAL RULE: it holds for the SSR spike, where the run was taken on an UNMODIFIED MAIN TREE. But MOST of this evidence corpus measures the workers OWN INSTRUMENT CHANGES — so the measured tree was never on main, and NO COMMIT CARRIES IT. The landed commit sits on a LATER BASE. Re-pinning therefore restores the PATCH, not the TREE that was measured.

THE FAILURE IT CAUSES IS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT: an unresolvable pin is VISIBLY broken. A re-pinned wrong one is RESOLVABLE AND WRONG — it fails silently, which is precisely what the bead exists to prevent. Measured: for 9 of 11 pins the rebase preserved every contributed blob and re-pinning was safe; for TWO it did not (one rebase resolved conflicts in three files on the measured path, another moved the file its decomposition turns on) and those were ANNOTATED rather than re-pinned.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, which belongs in the convention rather than in judgement: RE-PIN ONLY WHERE THE REBASE PRESERVED EVERY BLOB THE COMMIT CONTRIBUTED. Otherwise the page says so.

AND THE ENFORCEABLE RULE IS NOT MINE EITHER: not "no authored heads" and not "every SHA must be on main", because several pages deliberately RETAIN the authored head alongside a blob-table fallback and a must-be-on-main gate would red them for being careful. It is "EVERY CITED AUTHORED HEAD MUST BE ACCOMPANIED BY A RESOLVABLE LANDED SHA".

SCALE, so the shape is not mistaken for an edge case: 319 unique hex tokens under docs/design/hicasso/**, of which only 77 are commits — 188 are content digests and FNV hashes that must not be treated as pins at all. 44 stranded, 79 occurrences, 24 pages, ALL reachable from no remote ref.

(1) The recovery was VALIDATED BEFORE BEING TRUSTED, against three pages that already document authored->landed mappings as ground truth: stable patch-id is invariant across this repos rebase-merge, and 43/44 mapped exactly. (2) The worker caught its OWN first blob check comparing WHOLE TREES — which differ for every rebased pair, so it would have condemned everything; the correct check is the commits OWN CONTRIBUTED BLOBS.

REACT CAN SWALLOW A DOM EXCEPTION SO THAT NOTHING REACHES THE CALLER — a refusal is not optional there, it is the only signal (2026-08-14, rf2-h6qm7 worker).

WHAT WAS MEASURED. A :value on a file input throws InvalidStateError inside React's setInitialProperties during commit. The obvious assumption is that the author can catch it. THEY CANNOT: React caught it inside its own commit and re-reported it via reportError, so a thrown-by probe around the flushSync returned NIL — the probe printed four nils. The author had neither an error id nor an exception to catch, only a console entry naming React internals.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE BUG. When judging whether a source-located refusal is worth minting, the usual test is "does the platform already tell the author?" Here the platform DOES throw and the author still learns nothing, because the framework intercepts it. So "React throws" is not evidence that attribution exists. CHECK WHETHER THE THROW REACHES THE CALLER, not merely whether something throws.

THE PROBE THAT SETTLES IT: wrap the mount in flushSync and assert on what thrown-by returns. Nil means the exception was intercepted and the author is blind.

AND THE SAME PASS PROVED A NEGATIVE PROPERLY, which is the reusable technique. I asserted that a sibling code path shared the defect. The worker showed it did not — by MOUNTING A REAL INPUT with setAttribute type FILE and measuring the asymmetry: attribute FILE, IDL property file, .files present, refusal fires. That row passed in BOTH the red and green states, which is what makes it evidence rather than assertion. A test that passes only after the fix cannot prove a path was already immune.

A THROW INSIDE A REACT EVENT HANDLER DOES NOT FAIL cljs.test — THE ROW READS GREEN OVER A LIVE EXCEPTION (2026-08-03, rf2-fki5d).

React does not let an exception escape dispatchEvent; it routes it to reportError. So a cljs.test deftest that dispatches a real DOM event and asserts 'nothing threw' sees 0 failures / 0 errors EVEN WHEN THE HANDLER THREW. COROLLARY WORTH KEEPING: also tell the worker WHY the title may be stale (an audit reopen keeps the original title), so it knows to look for the divergence rather than assuming the brief and bead simply disagree.

REAGENT 2.0.1 SWALLOWS :on-recoverable-error — hydration error-capture harnesses built on reagent.dom.client/hydrate-root are VACUOUS. Found by the rf2-53lsj worker (#6407) on 2026-07-19, in its OWN test harness, before shipping. Reagent destructures :on-recoverable-error and NEVER PASSES IT to React hydrateRoot, so the callback fires for nothing: the harness captured NOTHING on either input and passed identically on broken and fixed HTML. Driving React hydrateRoot DIRECTLY, React 19 correctly reports the mismatch ("Hydration failed... + revenue / - :revenue").
RULE: to assert on hydration mismatches, call React hydrateRoot directly. Do not route through Reagent for error capture. And whatever harness you use, PROVE IT CAPTURES: feed it known-bad input and confirm it reports, before trusting a green on good input.
SECOND FINDING FROM THE SAME PR, easy to get backwards: Reagent renders a keyword/symbol child via (name x), which DROPS THE NAMESPACE — :a/b renders as "b", not "a/b". A JVM emitter fix that merely strips the leading colon would emit "a/b" and leave the hosts FURTHER apart while appearing closer. Namespaced symbols diverge identically. Always diff the actual BYTES against the client, never reason about the shape.

Reagent's get-react-key (reagent2.impl.template L407) only reads :key meta from VECTORS. ^{:key k} attached to a function-call list form (e.g. ^{:key g} (group-section g …)) is lost on evaluation — the meta lives on the source list at READ time, not on the returned value. Two fixes: (a) put ^{:key k} on the vector literal returned by the function, or (b) wrap the result in (with-meta result {:key k}). Found in views_view.cljs PR #1471 fixing rf2-gphsi; same anti-pattern exists across several other panels (audit bead rf2-?? filed). Tell future test authors: a test that asserts :key meta on the rendered child reproduces the bug.

REAPING ON 'PR MERGED + AGENT REPORTED' STILL CATCHES LIVE AGENTS — twice now, and the guard saved it both times (2026-08-02).

WHAT HAPPENS: an agent sends its final report, the mayor merges its PR and reaps the worktree — and the agent is STILL RUNNING. It keeps working after reporting: extra confirmatory reruns, a last gate, tidying. The worktree vanishes under its cwd and its background process dies.

INCIDENTS: the heap worker (reaped on PR-merge while alive; recorded then as 'reap only when merged AND reported'), and now proc-6tags-7uxkt — which HAD reported done, then set up a node_modules junction and started an extra test:cljs run. It found its worktree gone mid-run.

WHY IT HAS BEEN HARMLESS BOTH TIMES, and this is the load-bearing part: scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh disarms the node_modules junction BEFORE removing, so the junction-following hazard (which has emptied the mayor's real node_modules twice historically) did NOT fire. Canary held at 101 entries across both incidents. The worker's commits were pushed before reporting, so nothing was lost either time.

THE REFINEMENT, since 'reported done' is evidently not the same as 'finished': the cheap check before reaping a just-merged worktree is whether its agent is still live (a task notification arriving after the report is the tell; so is a recent mtime under the worktree). It costs one look. But the honest weighting is that the GUARD is the real protection and it works — this is a courtesy to the worker's last few minutes, not a safety issue. Do not build ceremony around it; do not skip the guard.

DO NOT force removal or bypass the guard when a reap refuses — a refusal means something still holds the tree, which is exactly when following a junction would be catastrophic.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-11 (rf2-j689 ruling) — REAP-FIRST IS NO LONGER A REASON FOR ANYTHING. THE ORPHANED BRANCH IS SOLVED AT THE SERVER, NOT BY ORDERING.

WHAT THIS MEMORY USED TO SAY, and it was measured, not guessed: `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch` lands the merge but cannot delete a branch that a worktree still holds, and gh abandons the REMOTE deletion along with the local one — so roughly twenty merges in one session each left an orphaned origin branch. Reaping the worktree first made the flag work completely, four for four (#7842, #7843, #7845, #7848), because the worktree pins the branch and nothing else does. The mechanism was real and the measurement stands.

WHY IT IS SUPERSEDED ANYWAY. The ordering only ever worked when the worker had already reported done — the three merges in that same session whose workers had NOT reported were correctly merged without a reap and orphaned their branches 3/3. So reap-first solved the orphan for the easy half of the cases and left the hard half untouched, while placing the reap immediately beside a merge: the exact structural condition of the catalogrows-vkle violation, where I reaped mid-gate holding the worker's own message saying it was not done. An efficiency that re-creates the shape of the worst mistake in the session is not a bargain.

THE FIX THAT REPLACED IT: `delete_branch_on_merge` is now ENABLED on day8/re-frame2, so GitHub deletes the head branch server-side the moment a merge lands, and the server does not care what a worktree is holding. Merge with `gh pr merge --rebase` — NO `--delete-branch`. Zero orphans by construction, for reported and unreported workers alike, with nothing to remember afterwards.

SO THE ORDERING IS MOOT, WHICH IS STRONGER THAN "DISCOURAGED". There is no orphan left to avoid, so reap-before-merge buys nothing and is not a reason to reap, to hurry, or to sequence anything. The never-pair rule in mayor-hygiene.md stands VERBATIM: never pair a merge with a reap, never put the reap in the merge loop. Reaping is a separate deliberate hygiene step.

THE AUTHORISATION IS UNCHANGED AND NON-NEGOTIABLE — only the agent's own report that it has FINISHED authorises a reap. Not merge state, not PR state, not elapsed time, not mtime, not cleanliness. The test is still: can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done? See reap-requires-a-finished-report-not-just-a-message, which cost a destroyed gate run to learn.

THE ONE REMAINING MANUAL DELETE: `git push origin --delete <branch>` is now ONLY the post-MERGED fallback for a remote ref that survives the merge — head-ref branch protection, or a cross-repo PR whose head lives in a fork the server will not touch. Verify MERGED, delete that ref, and nothing else. A surviving remote ref is never grounds to reap a worktree early.

MY INLINE REAP DELETED A WORKTREE WHILE ITS WORKER WAS STILL GATING, AND THE GATE FAILED FALSELY (2026-08-04).

WHAT HAPPENED. Earlier in the session I twice merged a PR and forgot to reap its worktree, so I folded the reap INTO the merge loop to make it unskippable. That fixed the leak and introduced a worse failure: a worker was still running the fast-PR spine in the worktree I deleted. PR #7469 merged at 02:24:42 UTC; the branch and worktree were removed; the worker's spine finished at 02:24:53, eleven seconds later, reading a directory that no longer existed. It reported FAIL implementation JS harness helpers with 11 reagent-slim policy failures, all of the form "Cannot find module", "missing workflow: .github/workflows/test.yml", "missing changed-surfaces script" -- files that are tracked in git and were present. The worker correctly discarded the result under the killed-gate rule and confirmed the CI counterpart was SUCCESS on main.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS BEYOND THE WASTED RUN. The failure LOOKS like a real policy regression naming real files. A worker with less discipline would have "fixed" the missing modules, or reported a red that does not exist. It is the mirror of the backgrounded-gate bug we fixed today, where a relative invocation graded ANOTHER worktree: same class, opposite direction -- the gate reads a tree that is not the one it thinks it is reading.

THE RULE: A MERGE DOES NOT MEAN THE WORKER HAS EXITED. The PR opening is the worker's LAST reported act, not its last act -- it may still be running gates, updating the PR body, or answering a message. Before reaping a worktree, confirm the worker is actually done: no live agent for that bead, or the worktree quiescent across a tick. When in doubt, leave the worktree; a stale directory costs disk, a deleted one costs a false red and possibly a spurious "fix".

THE CORRECTED SHAPE: keep the reap adjacent to the merge so it cannot be forgotten, but gate it on the worker being finished rather than on the PR being merged. Reaping on the NEXT tick after the merge is the cheap approximation and is what I should do by default.

RELATED, SAME SESSION: the same worker corrected two claims of mine. REAP A WORKER WORKTREE ONLY WHEN ITS AGENT REPORTS DONE — NOT WHEN ITS PR MERGES (2026-08-01, my error).

WHAT I DID: after merging PR #7337 I ran scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh against worker/heapaxis-2rtt6-34. The removal FAILED on a Windows file lock, but the guard had already done its first job and DISARMED THE node_modules JUNCTION. The agent was still alive. Its next shadow-cljs call failed with 'shadow-cljs not found' and it spent a tool round diagnosing before reporting 'my worktree junction has vanished... Recreating it'. It self-recovered and the mayor's real node_modules stayed intact at 101, so no damage — but I cost a live worker a pointless detour.

THE MISTAKE IS THE TRIGGER, NOT THE SCRIPT. A merged PR means the WORK landed; it does NOT mean the AGENT finished. Agents legitimately keep working after opening a PR: updating the PR body, re-running a gate, hardening a mutation proof, answering a resume message.

THE RULE: reap only when BOTH hold — (1) the PR is merged, AND (2) the agent has reported done or is confirmed dead. A reap that fails on a file lock is often a SIGNAL the tree is still in use: check whether the agent is alive before retrying, and never retry in a loop.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the guard is right to unlink the junction BEFORE removing (that is what stops git worktree remove following it into the mayor's real node_modules), and right to refuse rather than force when removal cannot complete. The defect was entirely in WHEN I invoked it.

I REAPED A WORKTREE MID-GATE, AND I HAD THE WORKER'S OWN WORDS SAYING IT WAS NOT DONE (2026-08-11, catalogrows-vkle / PR #7813).

WHAT HAPPENED. The worker sent two interim messages. The second said, verbatim: "Holding for the spine — not done yet, and I won't report a colour I don't have." Minutes later I merged #7813 and reaped its worktree in the same breath. Its spine was in the JVM tier. git worktree list stopped showing the tree, .git went, gate.log was deleted mid-write, and the run died. The worker found gate.exit = 1 afterwards and CORRECTLY REFUSED TO REPORT IT AS A FAILURE — that 1 was written by a script whose own checkout had been deleted underneath it. My cleanup manufactured a red.

WHY I DID IT, because the mechanism matters more than the apology: I batched the reap into the merge pass. The hygiene procedure forbids exactly this — "Never pair a merge with a reap in the same breath, and never put the reap in the merge loop." A merged PR is the moment a tree LOOKS finished, which is precisely why the pull is dangerous. I had also, without noticing, promoted "the agent sent me a message" to "the agent reported done". Those are not the same thing and the difference was written in the message I was reading.

SO THE REAP CONDITION IS NARROWER THAN I HAD IT: not "the agent has spoken", but "the agent has reported that it has FINISHED". An interim status, a progress note, a partial hand-off, a PR-opened announcement — none of these are completion. A BACKGROUND GATE STILL RUNNING IS THE WORKER STILL RUNNING, even though nothing in the branch, the tree or the PR shows it.

WHY IT LOOKED SAFE, and this is the trap for next time: every proxy agreed. PR merged, branch clean, commits pushed, no junction, worker had messaged recently. All six of the forbidden proxies pointed at "done" simultaneously. That is not evidence; that is what a disciplined worker mid-gate looks like BY DESIGN, since commit-and-push-as-you-go is what every brief demands.

WHAT SAVED IT: the work was committed and pushed incrementally, so only the RUN was lost, not the diff. And CI's 90/90 on the merged PR is strictly better evidence than a local spine anyway — which is worth remembering when tempted to wait on a local gate at all.

THE RULE I AM ADDING TO MY OWN LOOP: before any reap, re-read the LAST message from that agent and find the sentence where it says it is finished. If I cannot quote that sentence, the worktree does not get reaped. Cost of waiting: one stale directory.

REBASE conflict resolution: --ours/--theirs INVERT vs merge. In a rebase, --ours = the branch you are replaying ONTO (e.g. origin/main), --theirs = the commit being replayed (the worker's own branch). So to take MAIN's version of a generated file (e.g. docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js) during a rebase, use 'git checkout --ours <file>', NOT --theirs. My earlier dispatch instructions said --theirs for this and were WRONG (caught by the rf2-ywwpx worker on #6284, 2026-07-18, which verified empirically: stage2/--ours == origin/main, stage3/--theirs == its own stale commit). Harmless for a generated file that gets regenerated afterwards, but on a NON-generated conflict the same wording silently takes the wrong side and can revert main's work. ALWAYS instruct workers to verify which stage matches origin/main (git show :2:<file> / :3:<file> and compare digests) rather than trusting the label.

Rebase-merge makes a worker branch look UNMERGED to an ancestry check. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` returns N>0 and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails for a branch whose PR was merged with --rebase, because the rebase rewrote the SHAs. Judging 'abandoned, holds unmerged work' from that heuristic mislabelled 7 of 9 branches in one hygiene pass (their PRs #7096-#7107 were all merged). The authoritative test is PATCH-ID containment: `git cherry origin/main origin/<branch>` counting '^+' lines == 0 means fully merged. Confirm with `gh pr view --json state` == MERGED as the second signal.

A MERGE TIMESTAMP EARLIER THAN A RUN'S START DOES NOT MEAN THE RUN'S TREE CONTAINED THAT CHANGE — this repo rebase-merges (found 2026-08-07, rf2-jv36i).

WHAT HAPPENED. A bead assumed 'the codec change is on main by then' because PR #7390 merged at 18:06:11Z and the measurement windows ran 18:14:02Z-18:21:10Z. Eight minutes clear, in wall clock. But the run was taken from a worker branch based at b4144427ec, authored BEFORE the change landed and rebase-merged AFTER. The landed history orders the commits correctly; the measured tree never contained them.

WHY IT IS EASY TO GET WRONG. Under rebase-merge the branch tip that produced a measurement is not an ancestor of main at all, and its base can predate several landings that appear, in main's log, to sit before the run. Reading merge times off main and comparing them to a run's clock is exactly the wrong instrument.

HOW TO CHECK PROPERLY — any one of these settles it, and they should agree:
  - BLOB: the evidence page stamps the blob of the file under test; compare it to the change's before/after blobs. This is the strongest check because it names what was actually loaded.
  - ANCESTRY: 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <change-commit> <producing-commit>' — NO means the tree lacked it.
  - BASE: what commit the producing branch was cut from, and what that tree's relevant blob was.

RELATED, same root cause: a stranded authored head's patch-id may differ from its landed counterpart because the rebase resolved conflicts — so 'the patch landed' and 'this tree was measured' are separate questions, and provenance prose must not conflate them.

A PROVENANCE PIN NAMING AN AUTHORED SHA IS STRANDED BY REBASE-MERGE — THE PAGE LOOKS PINNED AND IS NOT (2026-08-06, rf2-zn7pj / PR #7610; scope filed as rf2-owq6p).

THE FINDING: the SSR spike witness pinned its evidence to 952a3f2024. That commit IS NOT AN ANCESTOR OF MAIN, and neither is its sibling 6f40304011. This repo REBASE-MERGES, which rewrites SHAs, so the authored head a page names is stranded the moment its PR merges. Verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` returning non-zero.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE STALE FIGURES IT WAS FILED FOR: stale figures under a RESOLVABLE pin are checkable and wrong, which is a normal defect. Figures under an UNRESOLVABLE pin are NOT CHECKABLE AT ALL — a reader cannot obtain the tree the measurement was taken on. The pages central verifiability claim fails SILENTLY, and it fails while looking rigorous. This is the evidence-corpus form of the fail-open class.

THE FIX THAT DISSOLVES IT: PIN TO A COMMIT ALREADY ON MAIN. The measurement happens upstream of the documenting edit, so no merge of the documenting PR can move it — main advanced eight commits during that pass and the pin never had to change. Do not pin to your own branch head.

AND THE REASONING THAT DECLINED A BLOB TABLE, which is the better half: a blob table pins the INSTRUMENT when the anchor cannot be pinned. Here the anchor CAN be pinned, and a resolvable whole-tree SHA pins strictly more. It would also PIN LESS THAN IT LOOKS — the clock pages magnitudes are a function of three driver files, whereas these figures are a SHA-256 over a whole document plus a boundary census, a function of corpus, entry, substrate, adapter and the pinned react-dom. A short blob table would ADVERTISE A CLOSURE IT DOES NOT HAVE. Ask what the artefact is actually a function of before choosing what to pin.

RELATED, ALREADY KNOWN: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` and `git cherry` disagree for the same reason — rebase-merge rewrites SHAs, so ancestry says "unmerged" for branches that are fully merged. Same mechanism, two different wrong conclusions: there it under-reports merge status, here it strands a citation.

A GATE CONFLATED "THE TEST FAILED" WITH "THE TEST NEVER RAN", AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WHETHER THE RUNNER PRINTED ITS OWN COUNT (2026-08-06, rf2-v8561, PR #7608).

THE REPORTED DEFECT: three CLJS namespaces failing per-namespace isolation. It did NOT reproduce — clean worktree, fresh npm ci, fresh compile, the beads own repro command twice, exit 0 both times, and all 17 roster namespaces green alone (196 tests / 731 assertions).

THE TELL THAT CRACKED IT, and it is the kind of thing only a fresh reading finds: THE THREE REPORTED NAMESPACES ARE THE LAST THREE ROSTER ENTRIES, CONSECUTIVELY. That is not three independent fixture defects — it is a CONTIGUOUS TAIL, the signature of something collapsing partway through a sweep that spawns one node process per namespace over 276 measured seconds.

THE CAUSE: compile-node-test.cjs UNLINKS out/node-test.js before every compile, deliberately, so a failed compile leaves nothing stale (rf2-6t03c). A compile starting mid-sweep pulls the bundle out from under every run still to come. Injecting exactly that at t=225s of a 276s sweep reds EXACTLY THOSE THREE NAMESPACES, namespace for namespace. Both recorded sightings were worktrees with other builds running.

THE STRUCTURAL DISCRIMINATOR, which is the reusable part: --test=<ns> is a RUNTIME selector over a bundle that links EVERY test namespace, so A MODULE-LOAD CRASH CANNOT SINGLE A NAMESPACE OUT. Therefore: A RED CARRYING "Ran N tests containing M assertions." IS A VERDICT ABOUT THAT NAMESPACE; A RED WITHOUT ONE NEVER WAS. Three causes reach a non-zero standalone exit and the gate was reporting all three as the first — ISOLATION (real leak, fixture remedy), ROSTER (stale curated list; 9dd9633d0b and d3969eb67b are both commits fixing that AFTER the gate blamed fixtures), ENVIRONMENT (bundle vanished; the sweep is INDETERMINATE, exit 2, and ITS GREENS ARE WORTH NO MORE THAN ITS REDS).

TWO RULES TO CARRY:
1. When a gate accuses several namespaces at once, CHECK WHETHER THEY ARE CONTIGUOUS IN ITS ROSTER. Adjacency is evidence of one external event, not of N independent defects. The old gate under an unlink at t=6s accused SIXTEEN namespaces of leaking, every one MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
2. A GREEN MUST ALSO CARRY A NON-ZERO TEST COUNT. This is the same floor as the long-standing "Ran 0 tests reads as green" family, arriving from the opposite direction: there the count was zero because nothing was selected, here because nothing could load.

SIBLING TO CHECK, filed as rf2-1wyyb: check-ui-adapter-isolation.cjs has the same --self-test shape and plausibly the same conflation. Not verified — a shared filename pattern is not evidence of a shared defect.

Redaction/privacy threat model for re-frame2 dev tools (Story/Xray/MCP/share): a local programmer can ALWAYS reach secrets programmatically (eval, direct app-db), so redacting sensitive values from the human USING the tool is futile and NOT the goal. Only two concerns: (1) maybe handing them to an AI/LLM (MCP/agent payloads) — a soft 'maybe', and largely already handled by the MCP servers' --allow-sensitive-reads gate (OFF by default, forces :rf/redacted elision); (2) firmer: stopping them being written to logs. Implication: human-facing egress (share URLs, static export, copied EDN, screenshots of the dev's own app) is NOT privacy-blocked — unblock it. Scope rf2-qarwq narrowly to the AI boundary + logs; do not gold-plate. REFINEMENT OF MY OWN FINDING FROM EARLIER TODAY — WELL-EVIDENCED CLOSES ALSO GET REOPENED, AND THAT IS A DIFFERENT PHENOMENON (2026-07-26).

EARLIER I MEASURED that gate/fixture beads closed on ARMING rather than on CATCHING are the largest category the merged-PR audit reopens, and concluded that a meaningful share of the reopen rate is my own close quality. That is true and the remediation stands.

BUT IT IS INCOMPLETE. Checking again a few hours later: FIVE beads I closed TODAY WITH FULL MUTATION EVIDENCE are open again — rf2-5o52l, rf2-12g5z, rf2-4hc9p, rf2-isp3i, rf2-lnecd — and every one carries NEW-RESIDUAL language rather than a restatement of the original defect. rf2-5o52l is the clearest: the emit-site privacy direction was accepted as correct, and the reopen names a DIFFERENT thing the SSR widening changed in the hydrate and restore :skews accumulators.

SO THERE ARE TWO DISTINCT REOPEN CLASSES AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT RESPONSES:
  (A) WEAK-CLOSE REOPENS — the close said the job was added / the roster widened / the suite is green, giving the audit nothing to verify against. The audit then does the verification I should have done. FIX: mutation proof in the close reason. Mine to prevent.
  (B) NEW-RESIDUAL REOPENS — the close was fully evidenced and ACCEPTED, and the audit found something ELSE by examining the merged code. This is the audit working as designed and is NOT a defect in my closing. Treating it as one would push me toward defensive over-closing, which is worse.

HOW TO TELL THEM APART IN ONE READ: does the reopen note ENGAGE WITH the close evidence and then name something new ("the emit-site direction is correct, BUT the SSR widening changed..."), or does it re-assert the original defect? The former is (B) and is fresh work. The latter is (A) and is my failure.

Half of it is; the other half is the audit finding genuinely new defects in freshly merged code, which is exactly what it is for and which no improvement in my close reasons will reduce. So the open count will NOT converge to zero while the audit runs, and that is a property of the system rather than a throughput failure. Report it that way.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is one I keep relearning: a measured finding is usually true of the subset I measured, not of the whole. My first pass looked only at gate beads and generalised. Checking a wider sample a few hours later split the finding in two. BEFORE ACTING ON A MEASURED PATTERN, ASK WHICH POPULATION IT WAS MEASURED OVER.
Refinements added to an IN_PROGRESS bead rarely reach the worker (they have already read the spec and are coding). File a NEW follow-up bead instead of noting the in-progress one. (Mike, 2026-05-31)

WHEN A GATE FAILED BECAUSE ITS PREDICATE WAS TOO NARROW, WIDENING THE PREDICATE REPEATS THE DEFECT (2026-08-11, rf2-hic-021 repair, PR #7813).

THE SETUP. The complaint-catalogue checker reads four file families. Its CI invocation sat inside a job gated on the changed-surface output cljs_node_test, which only implementation/hicasso/** sets true — so register-only, spec-only and guide-only edits all skipped the gate silently. The audit's bounded repair said: give it a CI path whose changed-surface inputs include every family it reads. My message to the worker repeated that framing.

THE WORKER DECLINED THE FRAMING, and it is right: "The defect being repaired IS an arm that failed to cover a checker's inputs, so A NEW ARM IS A FRESH CHANCE TO MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE and needs re-widening whenever the checker learns a new file." A widened predicate is correct exactly until the checker reads one more path — and nothing makes anyone revisit it then.

WHAT IT BUILT INSTEAD: an UNCONDITIONAL job — no needs:, no if: — listed in all-required-passed. That covers all four families and every future one BY CONSTRUCTION, with no predicate to keep in sync. It then drove all three previously-dead families red (R1, R3, R8 -> exits [1,1,1]), restored byte-identically, re-ran [0,0,0], AND drove the routing claim itself red by re-gating the job on cljs_node_test and watching the new scheduling test fail verbatim.

THE GENERAL RULE: a conditional that must be kept in sync with a growing input set is a standing liability, and the cheap fix (widen it) preserves the liability while looking like a repair. Prefer removing the condition when the job is cheap enough to always run. Ask "what makes someone update this predicate the next time the thing it guards changes?" — if the answer is "nothing", the predicate is the bug.

To tell my own checkout-race reverts apart from genuine reviewer reopens I grepped bead notes for "AUDIT-REOPEN|MERGED-PR AUDIT". rf2-zt65l carried a note spelled "AUDIT REOPEN (PR #6921 ...)" — SPACE, not hyphen — so my grep returned 0, I concluded "my race, not a reviewer", and re-closed a bead whose audit finding was still unmet. THE UNDERLYING LESSON, which recurs: a negative grep result is weak evidence. It proves your PATTERN did not match, never that the THING is absent. Same class as "grep -c beads <file> || echo NO HOOK" (grep exits 1 on zero count, not only on a missing file) and the "&& / ||" precedence bug that truncated issues.jsonl. RESUMING AN AGENT INVALIDATES ITS EARLIER COMPLETION REPORT — I REAPED A LIVE WORKER'S WORKTREE (2026-08-10).

WHAT I DID. rf2-hic-009's worker reported done. Later it turned out to have stalled waiting for a nonexistent notification, so I SendMessage-resumed it to finish its spine run. Then PR #7744 went green, I merged it, and I reaped the worktree on the hygiene rule "only its agent's own completion report authorises a reap". I had a report. It was from BEFORE the resume. The worker was live, with sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh running inside that tree, and I deleted the tree underneath it. It saw FAST_PR_EXIT=1 - its own checkout vanishing, not a defect in the diff.

THE RULE THE HYGIENE DOC IS MISSING. A completion report authorises a reap only until the agent is resumed. After a SendMessage resume, the earlier report is spent: the agent is live again and owes a NEW report. Treat resume as un-completing the worker.

WHY THIS IS EASY TO GET WRONG. Every other reap signal I distrust is a proxy - PR merged, elapsed time, mtime, clean tree. The completion report is the one signal the method says to trust, so it does not feel like a proxy. But it is a point-in-time statement, and resuming moves the point. The tell is simple: if I sent the agent a message after its report, the report is stale.

WHAT IT COST HERE, AND WHAT IT COULD HAVE COST. Nothing was lost: the PR had already merged, and the worker re-ran the spine against origin/main WITH the change in it - a stronger check than the pre-merge run, exit 0. But had the reap happened before the push, three commits would have gone with the directory. A sibling worker the same night held three unpushed commits for over an hour.

THE PRACTICAL CHECK BEFORE ANY REAP: (1) has this agent been resumed since its last report? (2) is there a process live in that tree? Neither is answered by the PR state. If in doubt, leave it - a stale directory is the entire cost of waiting, and the removal script's own husk path exists precisely because directories are cheap to leave and expensive to delete wrongly.

THE RETIRING SUBSTRATE'S NAME IS A PREFIX OF A FIRST-CLASS ADAPTER'S — an unanchored sweep can delete what you are keeping (2026-08-14, rf2-2og6s worker).

THE TRAP: `day8/re-frame2-ui` is the DONOR being retired. `day8/re-frame2-uix` is the UIx ADAPTER, which is FIRST-CLASS AND STAYING under Mike's ruling. The first is a substring of the second.

So any unanchored grep, count or sed for `re-frame2-ui` over the tree MATCHES THE UIX ADAPTER TOO. A count over-reports. A blanket removal would strip the coordinate of an adapter the architecture depends on.

This is the most dangerous member of a family that produced EIGHT measurement errors from me in one day, because the others produced wrong NUMBERS while this one would produce wrong EDITS — and the edit would look correct in review, since the line it deleted really does contain the retiring name.

THE RULE: when sweeping for a retiring artefact whose name prefixes a surviving one, ANCHOR THE PATTERN. Match the coordinate with its delimiter (`re-frame2-ui"`, `re-frame2-ui }`, end-of-token), or grep for the namespace form rather than the coordinate string, or enumerate the hits and read every one before acting. Never a bare substring.

AND THE SAME SHAPE EXISTS FOR NAMESPACES: `re-frame.ui` prefixes nothing today, but `re-frame.ui.tool` and `re-frame.uix.*` would collide the same way if the latter existed. Check the neighbourhood of any name you are about to sweep.

GENERAL FORM, worth applying beyond this retirement: before any bulk operation keyed on a name, list every OTHER name in the repository that contains it as a substring. If that list is non-empty, the operation needs anchoring or manual review.
