(b) THE TASTE QUESTION: STRIP BOTH. The default Reagent scaffold does NOT preload Xray (no git-pinned `day8/re-frame2-xray` coord, no `{{xray-preload}}` `:devtools/preloads` entry, no `[data-rf-xray-host]` aside or its CSS, no `@xyflow/react` / `elkjs` npm packages, no `{{rf2-tools-sha}}` plumbing), and there is NO `:include-story?` on-ramp. Both tools attach post-generation through their own documented recipes — Xray's four edits in docs/xray/01-installation.md, Story's dev-alias coord + require + mount in docs/story/index.md:101-129 — and the generated README's next-steps section links exactly those two pages. Do NOT replace either with an `:include-xray?` flag, a profile, a wizard or a second template; the option surface is the thing being deleted.

(c) THE AXIS SENTENCE FROM rf2-8urba IS FOLDED IN, in this form and only this form: `:substrate` is the template's ONE and ONLY selector, and any future substrate arrives as a VALUE on it — one substrate-registry entry, one `_<substrate>/` resource tree of three files, one `case` arm — never as a second key and never as an authoring-model selector orthogonal to it. That is acceptance criterion 1 restated as a design constraint on the collapse, so the worker builds the reduced registry to take a third value cheaply. WHETHER Hicasso is that third value, its gate (the repository's first `v*` tag) and the foreign-adapter pairing residue stay with rf2-8urba, which a sibling agent is ruling concurrently; this bead's non-goal "No Hicasso substrate addition" is unchanged.

(d) Reagent stays the default. Nothing here reopens that.

== 2. HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED ==

THE DOSSIER AUTHOR (§Recommendation): "Affirm the collapse and strip both." Grounds: pre-alpha, elegance over accumulation, trust the programmer; a starter's job is to be read, run and replaced in one sitting, and today's scaffold hands a newcomer a 719-line handbook and five installed decisions before their first edit; Xray and Story each have a copy-paste attach recipe surfaced from the README's next-steps and from the setup skill at the moment the user wants it. Option B was called "the only defensible keep", tipped against by mechanics rather than aesthetics: the preload drags in a sha-pinned monorepo git dep and two npm packages, keeps the substrates asymmetric, and couples the template to the tools' release cadence. Reversible: re-adding one preload line later is a smaller act than carrying the machinery meanwhile.

THE REVIEWER (§Codex Recommendation): AGREES on every point that matters — "Affirm the collapse and strip both the default Xray wiring and the `:include-story?` generator flag. Make `:substrate` the only template-specific choice" — and says it reached that "from the current resources, hooks, tests, tool dependency graphs, documentation, and git history rather than from the bead's findings." It ADDED four things the dossier did not carry, all adopted here: (i) the strongest keep-Xray argument named at source — tools/template/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §9 ("Xray on by default", rf2-y9zqc) treats immediate runtime feedback as part of the first-run experience, and a devtools preload never enters an advanced release — answered by "'no production bundle cost' is narrower than 'no scaffold cost'", with the scaffold cost itemised (git-pinned coordinate, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a preload, a layout host, CSS, CSP qualifications, README material, and the lockstep tests at version_lockstep_test.clj:227-251) and Xray's own dependency graph (tools/xray/deps.edn:15-100 reaches epoch, routing, flows, schemas, resources, machines, Hicasso, machines-viz, reagent-slim, Reagent, Editscript and zprint, and records that Xray cannot publish while Hicasso lacks a coordinate); (ii) Story is "even less suitable as the one surviving flag" — the flag selects a 123-line routing/lifecycle entry point, a separate 102-line deps.edn and a 76-line registration example, and Story hard-depends on Reagent, machines, HTTP and Xray (tools/story/deps.edn:14-75); (iii) an explicit warning, adopted verbatim as a non-goal: "Do not replace the removed Xray wiring with an `:include-xray?` flag: that would immediately recreate the option matrix this decision is trying to eliminate"; (iv) the concrete test shape — explicit ABSENCE assertions for Xray/Story coordinates, npm packages, preloads, hosts and variant files, and the README's Xray and Story links kept as TESTED escape hatches.

WHERE THEY DIFFERED, in the reviewer's own words: "The real tradeoff is discoverability. A new Reagent user will no longer see the project's most distinctive devtools automatically, and some users will never follow a next-steps link. That is a product-marketing loss, not a runtime correctness loss, and it should be acknowledged rather than hidden behind the word 'minimal'. If the desired front door is a showcase rather than a neutral starter, then keeping Xray only is the coherent fallback; keeping Story or adding more flags is not. I would revisit default-on Xray only after there is evidence from first-run testing that auto-opening the panel materially improves successful onboarding, preferably once it has a stable consumer coordinate and can mount on every supported default substrate." The dossier called the same loss "the one real ergonomic loss" and mitigated it by the next-steps link; the reviewer weighted it higher and named the fallback. This ruling sides with both on the outcome and ADOPTS THE REVIEWER'S REVISIT CONDITION AS THE RECORDED ONE: default-on Xray is reconsidered only on first-run evidence, only once Xray has a stable published coordinate (`xray-v*`), and only if it can mount on every default substrate — today it cannot mount on UIx (rf2-p6f6u; Xray's mount refuses that adapter kind by name), and its Reagent-only preload is exactly the asymmetry that would force AC2/AC3 here and rc0yh's AC3 to be reworded around an exception. The front door is a neutral starter, not a showcase; the showcase is the docs, the testbeds and the setup skill, each of which teaches the tool at the moment the reader wants it.

WHY THE RULING WENT THIS WAY, in one paragraph: everything in the bead except the taste question is machinery removal, and both opinions plus the 2026-08-30 triage and the 2026-09-01 backlog reread hold it settled. On the taste question the two opinions converge from different evidence bases; the only dissent is about how loudly to acknowledge a discoverability cost; and that cost is reversible in a one-line PR, while the machinery a keep would retain (a git-pinned monorepo coord in every newborn app, lockstep npm pins, `xray?` substitutions in four hook slots, a permanent manifest asymmetry, release-cadence coupling) is exactly the class of coupling this surface review exists to cut. Posture applies in full: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, trust the programmer to paste four lines when they want a panel.
== 3. PREMISE CORRECTIONS AT TIP (b26c5ad33e) — so the worker does not rediscover them ==

title: surface-review(resources): make active-route resource replanning a first-class causal command
description:
## Scope

Add one public event-vector command for rerunning the active route's Resources plan when an app-db-derived identity input (principal, tenant, permission set, locale, impersonation) changes without navigation. Cover the Resources↔Routing late-bound seam, exact route-owner reconciliation, durable plan/blocking/readiness state, conformance tests, Spec 012/016 and API/resource docs, and the RealWorld-on-resources receipt. Keep Resources optional and vector-first.

## Findings

Named `{:from-db ...}` subscriptions deliberately re-key when resolver inputs change, but remain passive. The newly selected scoped key is therefore `:idle` until some causal path ensures it. Navigation normally supplies that cause, but identical navigation is intentionally a no-op and there is no public command that reruns the current route's effective resource plan without changing the URL.

The flagship works around this gap with the 39-line `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` event. That app event reads leaf `rf/handler-meta`, invokes each entry itself, and dispatches independent ensures. It is not the route planner: it omits inherited parent resources, local `:after` ordering, identity collapse, atomic planning, exact plan ownership diff, blocking-slot replacement, and route readiness/error repair; it also calls `:when` with nil instead of the planner's reserved `{}` ctx. A cold restore on a composed route can therefore omit a parent-owned read, and a successful hand-ensure after the initial nil-scope planning failure leaves the durable route plan/readiness facts stale.

The runtime already computes the authoritative answer once: the route planner materializes contributor/local-id, canonical params, resolved scope, scoped key and byte key-id; collapses and orders the effective parent chain; diffs prior identities; and returns the exact identity/blocking maps Routing commits under the active nav-token. The missing piece is a public causal door back through that machinery.

## Recommended Action

Ship one public command, `[:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause <edn>}]`, implemented through the existing late-bound Resources↔Routing integration. It should read the current resolved route and nav-token, rerun the canonical effective parent-to-leaf resource planner against the current app-db, and atomically reconcile the standing plan under the same route activation:

- retain/adopt unchanged usable identities without a forced fetch;
- ensure added or changed identities with the existing route owner and caller cause;
- remove that owner only from identities the replanned route no longer requires;
- replace the durable `:resource-plan` and `:resource-blocking` slots and re-project route transition/error from the new plan;
- preserve route id/params/query/fragment/nav-token and do not run guards, `:on-match`, history or scroll effects.

Use the ordinary fail-closed planner boundary: no partial ensures on a failed plan, and document/test the exact prior-owner cleanup and route-error result. Reuse the existing `:rf.resource/route-plan` evidence with an explicit replan cause rather than inventing a parallel planner or helper-function API.

Replace RealWorld's app-side planner copy with this event. Make its personalized feed admission explicit in route data (for example, only when the following-feed query arm is active) so confirmed-anonymous home does not contradict the existing strict nil-scope planning rule. Teach the account/tenant-switch recipe as: resolve/clear the old scope causally, commit the new identity, then replan the active route.

## Evidence

- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:35-50,84-120` — a `{:from-db ...}` sub re-keys reactively and reads the new key as idle until a route/event ensures it; subscriptions never fetch.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:189-261` — `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` reconstructs the leaf route's declaration and dispatches per-entry ensures by hand.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs:54-89` — the public home route mixes viewer/session identities and currently claims a nil session feed is simply omitted, while no `:when` admits that distinction.
- `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc:198-208` — the shipped contract proves a nil named route scope is a whole-plan `:rf.error/resource-route-plan`, not a silent omission.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:700-867,1023-1260` — the canonical planner already materializes exact identities, composes/collapses the branch, applies plan diff, and returns identity/blocking maps.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:247-306` — Routing commits those maps beside `:current` under the active nav-token; the app workaround never updates them or readiness.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:1026-1139` — restore tests assert newly created entries but do not assert repaired route error/readiness, stored plan membership, or an inherited parent read.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:1386` — the spec explicitly reserves force reload as a separate named contract instead of overloading fragment/identical navigation.
- `implementation/resources/deps.edn` and `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:406-545,641-643` — Resources is optional and its event family/route behavior already installs through late binding, so the command belongs on that seam without a static Routing dependency.
- Commit `d8a0f670704abc008eb151067f13a1e7cc976c48` removed named read helpers because vectors are the semantic API identity; this command should likewise remain an event vector. `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1237-1271` has no need for a new facade function.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented public event replans the active route in the dispatching frame from its current registered effective parent chain and current app-db, while leaving URL, route address, fragment and nav-token byte-for-byte unchanged and firing no guard, `:on-match`, history or scroll work.
- Replan uses the same `:when`/ctx, params and scope resolution, schema/canonical identity, contributor attribution, `:after`, branch ordering, identity collapse, blocking and keep-previous semantics as ordinary route entry; there is one planner, not an app-visible approximation.
- A same-route scope change A→B is covered: unchanged identities are retained without a forced request, B identities are ensured and owned, A-only identities lose the route owner, and the durable plan/blocking maps equal the newly materialized plan.
- An initial unresolved-scope plan error followed by app-db resolution + replan is covered: no navigation occurs, route error/readiness is repaired, exact plan membership is stored, and required loads start. The inverse/failing replan proves no partial ensure and the documented prior-owner cleanup/error result.
- Parent-chain coverage proves a leaf replan restores an inherited parent resource; a regression that reads only leaf `handler-meta` must fail. Coverage also pins a conditional occurrence entering/leaving the plan.
- RealWorld deletes `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`'s planner reconstruction in favor of the public command and tests successful restore, failed restore/confirmed anonymous, and a composed-route deep link including route readiness and plan membership, not only cache-entry existence.
- Spec 012/016, the Resources API/reference/concepts or how-to docs, examples and test prose agree on the command, passive-sub boundary, nil-scope behavior and trace cause. API-manifest drift remains green; no named facade helper is added.
- Proportionate Resources/Routing/RealWorld test gates pass, with a negative control that fails when effective-parent composition or durable readiness/plan replacement is removed.

## Non-goals

- No subscription-driven fetch, committed-read demand, app-db watcher, or automatic replan on every resolver input write.
- No general route reload that reruns guards, `:on-match`, history, scroll, or arbitrary route metadata.
- No named helper-function sugar, compatibility alias/window, second query grammar, or duplicate planner.
- No silent global fallback and no global change making nil route scopes silently optional; conditional resources remain explicitly admitted.
- No refactor of ordinary explicit `:rf.resource/ensure`/`refetch` for non-route owners.

## Related beads

- `rf2-hic-050` — STOP verdict for committed-read resource demand; this proposal preserves that ruling by adding an explicit causal event.
- `rf2-hic-054` — blessed event/sub async-resource recipes; the proposed command removes a route-planner reconstruction those public primitives cannot faithfully express.
- `rf2-hic-044` — current-primitives resource-demand witness; no demand/runtime ownership model is reopened here.

A full title/description/notes scan of all existing beads found no active or closed task for current-route resource replanning, force reload, principal-switch replan, or `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`.

title: ssr-node crossing (C/6): render-state contract (project/restore, two partitions) + protocol v1 revision
description:
Slice C of the ssr-node crossing programme. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 (S3 and S4 especially) first; this description carries only C's own brief. This is the slice both reviewers agreed carries the real risk — reconstructing the SAME settled render state in Node — so it lands BEFORE the adapter (D) consumes it.

## Scope (fence)

- New `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc` (+ JVM test under `implementation/ssr/test/` and a CLJS test in the same tree — `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` ~:102 already lists `ssr/test`, so NO build change).
- `implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs`, `test/protocol.test.cjs`, `test/fixtures/**`, README section `### A gap this protocol does not paper over` (~:355-365; rewrite it — the door now exists, decided by the framework, not by the sidecar).
- NOT `implementation/ssr-ring` (D consumes this), NOT `implementation/hicasso` (E). Parallel with A and B; B edits different README sections — rebase, don't fight.

## Do

JVM side (`render-state/project`): given a frame-id and a `:render-state` policy, return the partition map `{:rf/app-db {...} :rf/runtime-db {...}}` — the SAME envelope shape the hydration payload already uses (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj` ~:5-13) under a DISTINCT policy. The policy is declared like `:payload`: a fail-closed allowlist per partition — top-level app-db keys, and top-level runtime-db keys (the route slice, machine snapshots) — plus a `(fn [frame-id] -> partition-map)` escape hatch for a projector the allowlist vocabulary cannot express. Absent policy = construction-time error (mirror `:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy`). Reuse `payload_policy.cljc`'s apply/project machinery, including derived sensitivity the way `project-runtime-db` already applies it. Also a per-key `pr-str` serialization helper producing the wire form (key text -> EDN text) for both partitions; the serialization DOMAIN is the payload's existing EDN domain — reuse it, do not invent a second one.

description:
Slice A of the ssr-node crossing programme. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 first; this description carries only A's own brief.

## Scope (fence)

`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/{pipeline.clj,lifecycle.clj,ring.clj}` and `implementation/ssr-ring/test/**`, plus ONE stanza each in `spec/011-SSR.md` (beside the one-handler-constructor contract at ~:401, and the streaming refusal list at ~:1695-1703) and `spec/API.md` (the `re-frame.ssr.ring` row, ~:30). Both spec files are HOT-ZONE: queue behind any in-flight spec toucher; touch nothing else in them. No ssr-node, no hicasso, no examples, no workflows.

## Do

Introduce the render-body seam exactly as the parent's S1 states:

- `ssr-handler` gains ONE construction opt, `:renderer` — a plain fn, no protocol, no registry, no multimethod: `(fn [{:keys [frame-id request opts]}] -> {:body-html <string> :render-hash <string-or-nil>})`. It is called by `build-full-response*` at today's hard call (`pipeline.clj` ~:564, `ssr/render-to-string`) INSIDE the existing `rf/with-frame` scope, AFTER `drain-blocking-resources!` and the boot-event drain, BEFORE head resolution and the payload build consume its result. Its input is the live post-drain frame (by id), the handler opts and the Ring request — never a JVM hiccup value.
- The DEFAULT renderer wraps today's `lifecycle/resolve-root-view` -> `lifecycle/render-document-hash` -> `ssr/render-to-string` unchanged. Extract it as a named fn (public `re-frame.ssr.ring/local-renderer` or private — the worker's call; the public surface added by this slice is the one `:renderer` opt).
- `build-full-response*` consumes `{:body-html :render-hash}`. A nil `:render-hash` means no `data-rf-render-hash` marker and no payload `:rf/render-hash` — exactly today's unresolved-root behaviour (rf2-q1b96). Keep the `(and emit-hash? (some? hash-str))` guard: `:emit-hash?` with no hash re-stamps a constant (rf2-atmvj).
- `lifecycle.clj` (~:361, `:rf.error/ssr-ring-missing-root-view`): `:root-view` is required iff no `:renderer` is supplied. With a custom renderer it is optional and ignored.
- `stream-handler` REFUSES a non-nil `:renderer` at construction with `:rf.error/ssr-streaming-unsupported-opt` (ex-data `:opt-key :renderer`, `:got`, `:recovery`) — the `:html-shell` fail-closed precedent. Streaming over a non-local renderer is a programme non-goal.

## Acceptance

1. The existing ssr-ring suite is green with NO fixture or expected-byte changes — the Jetty end-to-end tests pin bytes, so this is the byte-identical + error-identical floor for the default path.
2. One new test with a custom `:renderer` returning a fixed body and nil hash: body inserted verbatim into a complete JVM document; no `data-rf-render-hash`; no payload `:rf/render-hash`; head, `__rf_payload`, shell, status and headers JVM-built; `:root-view` omitted without error.
3. `stream-handler` refusal test for `:renderer`.
4. The two spec stanzas (011 + API.md) describe the opt, the fn shape and the streaming refusal.

`clojure -M:test` in `implementation/ssr-ring` is THE gate. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the spec edits. Verify anchors and table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.

title: mayor loop: sweep open nightly-red issues into beads each merge+dispatch tick (loops.md §2 Dispatch + CLAUDE.md Workflow; alerter unchanged)
description:
Split out of rf2-2ohy's third acceptance item, which asked whether the
rf2-6sg25 alerting failed to surface seven consecutive nightly reds.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 13:36 AUSEST, and the answer is that THE ALERT FIRED
CORRECTLY. Issue #8423 'Nightly `expensive tests` is red' was opened
2026-08-16T16:01:50Z — the first red night — labelled `nightly-red`,
assigned to mike-thompson-day8, and its body named the exact failing step:
`Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates -> Gate — production elision,
browser (test:browser-prod-elision)`. It was edited every night since and
last updated 2026-08-22T16:02:05Z carrying `reds=7 greens=0`. The
alerting self-test step passed on every one of those runs. So the first
disjunct in rf2-2ohy's premise — 'the alerting did not fire' — is FALSE.
Nothing in .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py is broken, and this
bead is NOT a request to change its signature logic.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is the second disjunct: the issue went unseen for
seven days, and the alerter's own body says why, in its own words:

  'It is edited in place — which notifies nobody — while the same steps
  keep failing, and comments only when a step that was not failing starts
  to.'

That is a deliberate anti-spam design and it is defensible. The observed
cost of it is that a red lane produces EXACTLY ONE notification, on night
one, and then six nights of silence — and the one notification competes
with normal PR traffic in the same inbox. Seven days later the redness was
found by a manual PR-activity sweep, not by the alert, and no bead existed
until that sweep filed rf2-2ohy.

THE GAP, stated narrowly: nothing escalates a `nightly-red` issue that
stays open, and nothing bridges a GitHub issue into the beads tracker,
which is where work is actually dispatched from in this repo. The alert
lands in a channel the working loop does not read.

NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least
three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker:
  (a) re-notify on an age threshold (comment, not edit, after N reds) —
      cheapest, stays inside the existing script;
  (b) have the mayor loop read open `nightly-red` issues each tick;
  (c) have the alerter file/refresh a bead directly, so nightly redness
      enters the same queue as everything else.
(a) risks the spam the current design avoids. (c) is the most useful and
the most machinery. Mike to rule.

EVIDENCE: gh issue view 8423; gh run list --workflow expensive-tests.yml;
.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml lines 558-616 (the 'Nightly result ->
tracking issue' job, which succeeded on all seven red runs).

ACCEPTANCE: a ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night
one, and if so which shape. If the ruling is 'leave it as is, the mayor
sweep is the backstop', close this — that is a legitimate outcome and the
evidence above is the record of what that choice costs.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE — NOT DISPATCHABLE. WHOLLY AN OPERATOR CALL. *** Fence recorded by the mayor's dispatch tick 2026-08-23 13:41 AUSEST at tip e1a1faf9c8, quoting this bead's own description rather than re-reasoning it.

WHY IT IS NOT DISPATCHABLE: the bead states it in terms — 'NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker.' A worker sent here would have to choose between (a) re-notify on an age threshold, (b) the mayor loop reads open nightly-red issues each tick, and (c) the alerter files or refreshes a bead directly. Those differ in cost and in how much machinery they add, which is a judgement rather than a task.

DISCHARGED BY: Mike ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night one, and if so which of the three shapes. 'Leave it as is, the mayor sweep is the backstop' is a legitimate ruling and closes this bead — the bead says so itself, and the evidence it carries then stands as the record of what that choice costs.

WHAT IT IS NOT, and this matters because the parent bead's premise said otherwise: the alerting is NOT broken. This bead REFUTED that premise with measurement — issue #8423 opened on the first red night, labelled, assigned, naming the exact failing step, edited every night since, with the alerting self-test passing on all seven runs. Do not dispatch anything at .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py's signature logic; nothing there is wrong.

THE COST OF THIS HOLD, priced rather than asserted: nothing is queued behind it and no bead is blocked by it. What it costs is the thing that already happened once — seven consecutive red nights on the superset backstop, found by a manual sweep on day seven rather than by the channel built to report it. That cost recurs at the same rate as nightly redness itself, which over the last nine nights was seven times in nine.

NO HOT-ZONE SEQUENCING IS NEEDED. I had expected to fence this behind rf2-2ohy's worker because a remedy would touch .github/workflows/*, which is hot-zone and currently that worker's. That fence is unnecessary: this bead cannot be dispatched at all until it is ruled, and by then that worker will be long finished.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-23 17:05 AUSEST, tip 69a464c76b. THE PRICE OF THIS HOLD HAS CHANGED SINCE IT WAS RECORDED, and the bead's evidence needs the update so the ruling is made on current facts rather than on the state that prompted the bead.

WHAT THE 13:41 FENCE PRICES: "That cost recurs at the same rate as nightly redness itself, which over the last nine nights was seven times in nine."

THAT RATE WAS MEASURED WHILE THE ROOT CAUSE WAS LIVE, AND IT IS NOT LIVE NOW. Verified at source this tick, one item at a time:

  rf2-2ohy                          CLOSED (the browser-prod-elision abort, fixed by PR #8724)
  expensive-tests on main, 04:11    workflow_dispatch, completed/SUCCESS
  expensive-tests on the fix branch completed/SUCCESS at 03:38
  last SCHEDULED run                2026-08-22T15:24, failure -- i.e. BEFORE the fix landed
  schedule, read from the workflow  cron "17 15 * * *" = 01:17 AUSEST

So the first SCHEDULED exercise of the fix has not happened yet; it is tonight. The lane is proven green on main by dispatch, and the 7-in-9 figure describes a condition that has been repaired.

AND THE ALERTER CARRIES A RECOVERY POLICY THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION DOES NOT MENTION. Issue #8423's body reads, at this tick, "reds=7 greens=1" and states: "This issue closes automatically after 3 consecutive green runs -- the gap exists so an intermittent gate that passes tonight does not close and reopen the issue every other night." The 04:11 dispatch already counted as the first green.

WHY THAT MATTERS TO THE RULING RATHER THAN CLOSING IT. The "edited in place, notifies nobody" characterisation is TRUE OF THE RED DIRECTION ONLY. Recovery is automatic, bounded and hysteresis-guarded; it is the escalation on SUSTAINED redness that is absent. That narrows the question rather than answering it, and narrowing is worth recording: the three shapes are still the three shapes, but option (a) -- re-notify on an age threshold -- is now visibly the mirror of a policy the alerter ALREADY implements in the other direction, which is an argument about symmetry rather than about adding machinery.

THE HOLD'S COST, RE-PRICED. Still nothing queued behind it, still no bead blocked by it. What it costs is no longer a 7-in-9 recurring toll; it is the next unrelated breakage going unreported for as many nights as it takes somebody to sweep manually. That is a lower expected cost and a WORSE-SHAPED one -- rarer, and silent exactly when nobody is looking for it, which is when it will next bite.

NOTHING TO DISPATCH AND NOTHING CHANGED ABOUT DISPATCHABILITY. This stays wholly an operator call on the same three shapes, and "leave it as is, the mayor sweep is the backstop" stays a legitimate closing ruling.

ONE THING TO WATCH RATHER THAN FILE: if tonight's scheduled run is green, #8423 goes to greens=2 and closes itself after the third. If it is red, the fix did not hold under the scheduled trigger and rf2-2ohy wants reopening -- but that is a question for the merge tick tomorrow, not a bead today.
MAYOR 2026-08-24 01:57 AUSEST — THE WATCH CONDITION ON THIS BEAD HAS FIRED, AND IT FIRED GREEN.

This bead recorded: 'if tonight's scheduled run is [red], the fix did not hold under the scheduled
trigger and rf2-2ohy wants reopening.' Measured at source rather than inferred:

  2026-08-23T15:25  schedule           completed/SUCCESS  d1c824098d   <- tonight, 01:25 AUSEST
  2026-08-23T04:11  workflow_dispatch  completed/success  249d6ba0e2
  2026-08-23T03:38  workflow_dispatch  completed/success  bef9873398
  2026-08-22T15:24  schedule           completed/FAILURE  8c118b7dc2   <- the last red, BEFORE the fix

So the first SCHEDULED exercise of PR #8724's cache-blocking fix passed. The lane is now proven green
under the trigger that was failing, not only under manual dispatch. rf2-2ohy STAYS CLOSED — no reopen.

THE TRACKING ISSUE HAS MOVED TOO, and its own counter is the evidence: issue #8423 now reads
'reds=7 greens=2' where it read 'reds=7 greens=1' before tonight. It auto-closes after THREE
consecutive greens, so it stays open one more night by design — the gap exists so an intermittent gate
does not close and reopen the issue. Expect it to close after tomorrow's scheduled run.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE: this bead's own subject, which is the ALERTING gap rather than the test
failure — seven reds produced one notification. That question is untouched by tonight's green and is
still wholly an operator call. The banner stands.
RULING 2026-09-02 10:21:52 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-02, dossier review; ai/decisions/rf2-4a0c.nightly-red-escalation.md folded here and deleted — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). Ruled at tip b26c5ad33e.
BANNER STRUCK — the *** AWAITING MIKE *** banner above is discharged by this ruling.

1. DECISION: (b). The mayor's short Merge + dispatch tick reads the open nightly-red issues and ensures each one has exactly one open bead. The alerter (.github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py) and expensive-tests.yml are NOT touched — signature logic, thresholds, channel, all unchanged. (a), (c) and (d) rejected; one-line reasons under REJECTED in §4.

THE MECHANISM, exactly:
- WHERE: the DISPATCH half of the short tick (loops.md cadence table: "Merge + dispatch", ~10–15 min, and "on most signals"), as the first read BEFORE `bd ready` — its output is a bead, and the same tick can then dispatch it.
- THE READ, one-shot and non-blocking: `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --label nightly-red --state open --limit 100 --json number,url,title,updatedAt,body`. Check the exit code of the gh call itself. Exit 0 with `[]` = nothing red, done — the normal tick (the dossier measured the label non-empty on 12 of the last 60 days; at ruling time it is empty). Non-zero exit = "the sweep did not run this tick", retried on the next signal — NEVER read a failed query as "no nightly red" (the reviewer's invariant, adopted).
- DEDUP KEY: the canonical issue URL (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/<n>), carried in the bead's `external_ref` field — a field the tracker already uses this way (15 beads carry PR URLs in it at tip) and which `bd list --json` exposes. NOT the bare number: "8423" also matches PR numbers, run counts and commit prefixes. The read: `bd list --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --limit 0 --json | jq -r --arg u "$url" '.[] | select(.external_ref==$u) | "\(.id)\t\(.status)"'` (confirm once that `--limit 0` is unbounded on this bd build, as it is for `bd ready`).
- THREE CASES per open issue:
  (i) a bead in open/in_progress/blocked carries the URL → do nothing. The issue stays the live counter and signature record; the bead is the dispatch edge; later ticks do nothing.
  (ii) no bead carries the URL → file one: `bd create "nightly red: <failing steps> (issue #<n>)" --type bug --priority 2 --external-ref <url> --description "<shape in §4>"`. P2 by default; raise with a stated reason when the failing gate warrants it.
  (iii) only CLOSED beads carry the URL → THE HYSTERESIS CASE, and the one the reviewer's draft rule ("reopen it or file a clearly linked follow-up") would get wrong. The issue closes only after THREE consecutive greens (`--close-after 3`, sized above the rf2-7jevo flake), so for two nights after every fix the expected state is "bead closed, issue still open" — that is recovery, not a new failure. Read the body's marker line `<!-- nightly-alert:v1 signature=... reds=N greens=M -->`: `decide()` (nightly_failure_alert.py:246-286) sets greens=0 on ANY red night and increments it on a green one, so `greens>=1` → recovering by design, do nothing; `greens=0` → the most recent nightly was red AFTER the bead closed — the fix did not hold, or a new step joined — so file a NEW bead per (ii) with `--deps discovered-from:<closed-id>`, citing the closed one. Never reopen the closed bead: its close reason is a normative record.
- DUPLICATE ISSUES: the label-index race can open two issues in the same minute (#7537/#7538 on 2026-08-05, recorded in `fetch_open_issues`' docstring and self-healed by `collapse_duplicates` on the next run). Two open nightly-red issues with the same title created within minutes are ONE alert: file against the lower number only.
- BINDING FROM NOW: the doctrine binds the mayor from this ruling; the doc PR is the record, not the trigger. At ruling time (`gh issue list --label nightly-red --state open`, 10:13 AUSEST) there are ZERO open nightly-red issues and the last five scheduled runs are green, so today's sweep is a no-op.

2. HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED
Two voices in the dossier: the AUTHOR (sections "Summary", "The problem, carefully and fully", "What is waiting on this", "Options", "Recommendation", "Evidence") and the REVIEWER ("Codex Recommendation": "Independent findings", "Why this option", "Implementation invariant, risks, and next decision"). Both recommend (b). The ruling follows them because their agreement is on the load-bearing FACT rather than on taste: the reviewer independently re-ran the self-test and replayed the 22 runs and got the same classification (open/touch/touch/change/change/touch/touch, then hold/hold/close) — three loud events reached the inbox before discovery, and a manual sweep still found the redness on day seven. That is a channel miss, and (a) is the only option that treats volume instead. The reviewer adds a fact the author did not have: GitHub's own contract subscribes an assignee and routes assignment/update reasons to the inbox, so the events were DELIVERED and still missed — which closes the last door for (a) as a first repair.

AGREEMENTS (author and reviewer): the one-notification premise is wrong (four, three before discovery); channel, not volume; alerter untouched; (c) costs a second credential (GITHUB_TOKEN is repository-scoped by contract; the beads remote is a second repository), bd/Dolt bootstrapped in CI, and a concurrent tracker writer, for no better delivered latency than (b); (d) is coherent only if unbounded discovery time is accepted for the system of record.

DISAGREEMENTS, and how each went:
- WHERE the doctrine lives. Author: one bullet in CLAUDE.md's Workflow section. Reviewer: "the active repository-specific short-loop instructions" (the same file, in this repo's terms). Ruling: BOTH files, per loops.md's own rule at its head ("everything below is the method; the values it needs belong in that repository's agent-instructions file"): the generic paragraph goes in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md §2 Dispatch, the concrete query/label/dedup in CLAUDE.md Workflow. No loop command files exist in-repo (`.claude/commands/` is gone), so those two files ARE the loop body.
- DEDUP KEY. Author: "no open bead citing that issue number". Reviewer: the canonical issue URL, "exactly one open bead". Ruling: the reviewer's key, carried in `external_ref` — the author's number is a weak grep and the URL is what the tracker already stores for PRs.
- THE CLOSED-BEAD CASE. Reviewer: "reopen it or file a clearly linked follow-up". Ruling: neither reflexively — the marker rule in §1(iii). As written, the reviewer's rule would re-file or reopen on EVERY recovery, because the three-green close delay makes "closed bead, open issue" the expected state for two nights after each fix; the author did not address the case at all. This is the one place the ruling goes beyond both.
- SESSION SCOPE. Reviewer: (b) guarantees discovery on the next live tick, not 24-hour paging; if Mike wants a wall-clock acknowledgement SLO independent of mayor activity, (b) is insufficient and an acknowledged on-call channel or a scoped cross-repo credential with an owner is needed. Author: the red week had live sessions every day (182/82/221/70/155/416/169 commits on main 08-16 to 08-22), so the floor is "next live session" under every bead-ending option anyway. Ruling: no SLO adopted — the posture trusts the operator and does not build paging; the reviewer's condition is recorded as a reassess trigger in §5.

DISSENT PRESERVED: (1) the 2026-08-23 17:05 mayor note's symmetry argument — (a) is the mirror of the recovery hysteresis the alerter already implements in the other direction. The ruling's answer: symmetry into a channel measured not to reach the loop buys appearance, not escalation; the argument is fair and (a) stays available. (2) The reviewer's condition for (a) later: if the bridge is working and acknowledgements STILL stall, periodic comments become justifiable. (3) The author's, and this bead's own, statement that (d) is legitimate — it is, and this note is the record of what it would have cost.
3. PREMISE CORRECTIONS AT TIP (b26c5ad33e, re-verified 2026-09-02 10:13 AUSEST, read-only):
- "Seven reds, one notification" (this bead's title and description) is FALSE for this run. Measured at source: FOUR — the issue-open 2026-08-16T16:01:50Z; two loud github-actions[bot] comments "A nightly step that was not failing is now failing" at 2026-08-19T16:27:11Z and 2026-08-20T16:04:11Z (the cancelled 08-19 night reads as a signature change under commit 2ae34316e3 "a cancelled nightly is not a green nightly", 2026-08-06, which PREDATES the run; the signature changed back on 08-20); and the close comment 08-24. Replay (`--replay 22`, run by the author and independently by the reviewer): open NOTIFY / touch / touch / change NOTIFY / change NOTIFY / touch / touch / hold / hold / close NOTIFY — 4 against a naive alert's 7. "Then six nights of silence" is true only of a STEADY signature (the July 13-night outage would have been one open and then silence).
- Issue #8423 is CLOSED, 2026-08-24T15:58:43Z (auto-closed after three greens). `gh issue list --label nightly-red --state all` today: #8423, #7710 (08-08 to 08-10), #7538 and #7537 (2026-08-05, the label-index-race duplicate pair) — all four closed; ZERO open.
- Nightly green streak: every scheduled expensive-tests.yml run 2026-08-23 through 2026-09-01 is success; the last five verified today: 33527310887 (09-01), 33408409622 (08-31), 33319462434 (08-30), 33260019889 (08-29), 33203611049 (08-28). title: surface-review(skill-setup): make one prompt produce one mounted SPA
description:
## Scope

Treat `skills/re-frame2-setup/**` as one installed product and make its unqualified greenfield request do one thing well: turn an empty directory into a running Reagent counter SPA in one pass. The default path owns the exact files, resolving dependency baseline, commands, verification, and handoff. Keep UIx and merge-into-an-empty-CLJS-project support only when the author explicitly asks for those routes. Align the emitted result with the reduced canonical scaffold owned by `rf2-zq34m`; do not maintain a second independent project template.

## Findings

1. The advertised six-step path is not a fast path. A brand-new Reagent run needs `SKILL.md` plus `deps-versions.md`, `shadow-cljs.md`, and `first-counter.md`: 75,697 bytes and about 9,942 words before the agent writes the project. If it follows the boot explanation pointer too, `entry-namespace.md` adds another 22,547 bytes. Four of the five reference leaves are over the family 16 KB ceiling, while `spec/design.md` says only `entry-namespace.md` is slightly over and that a typical session reads two leaves.
2. The default request is forced into an interview. `deps-versions.md` says the author must choose a pin and the skill must stop before editing if none was supplied. `SKILL.md` also forbids the skill from executing the repo's one-command generator and tells it to hand the command back to the author. Thus “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” cannot complete without a choice and a second actor.
3. The first-mount route carries decisions unrelated to mounting: schemas, Xray, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a right-side host column, CSP/production-hardening prose, publication-state branching, and substrate-specific devtools policy. Reagent is nominally the default, but UIx/Xray/Hicasso distinctions occupy cardinal rules, the main checklist, troubleshooting, and handoff before the default counter exists.
4. The copyable runtime code is currently sound: it uses the current `rf/init!` + explicit `frame-root` seed, frame-targeted schema attach, retained React root, and measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` mount path; the local-root compile cover exercises both Reagent and UIx. The gap is the product journey, not a need for more API explanation.
5. The strongest setup compile test does not materialise the documented dependency file. It synthesises a separate deps map with placeholder Maven versions, rewrites framework coordinates to monorepo `:local/root`, and proves only `compile app`. It neither proves that the exact default dependency command/coordinate resolves from an empty consumer project nor boots the page and clicks 0→1.
6. The 16 evals are explicitly trigger-only (`should_trigger`); none grades the response, resulting files, commands, no-question default, mounted DOM, or handoff. The 1,162-line structural suite instead locks Xray layout, CSP wording, publication branches, UIx routing, and the prohibition on executing the generator. It protects accumulated policy better than the outcome named by the skill.
7. History shows accretion. The initial skill commit shipped `SKILL.md` plus four references at 36,433 bytes and taught core + adapter as the day-one path. The current corresponding shipped corpus is 105,173 bytes after schema, Xray, UIx, CSP/release, troubleshooting, and parity rules accumulated. The useful hot-reload correction in `rf2-r0kk7` / `rf2-ms6r8` came from a real watch-and-browser measurement, demonstrating the kind of outcome proof this skill still lacks.

## Recommended Action

- Define a zero-interview default: an unqualified request in an empty directory chooses Reagent, a single reviewed resolving baseline appropriate to the current publication state, the conventional app namespace/build id/port, and the smallest runnable counter. A user-supplied pin or UIx request overrides the default; absence of either is not a reason to stop.
- Make the main skill a short executor and router. Put the entire default in one copy-complete shipped source (or an asset mechanically derived from the canonical reduced template) with exact filenames and commands. The skill should never reassemble one project from three large prose leaves or hand-maintain a second template.
- Execute the normal work under the explicit invocation: create the files, run `npm install`, run a terminating compile check, start the dev server, and report the URL. Broaden the routine command grants as needed; do not preserve the current user-run-generator prohibition as policy.
- Match `rf2-zq34m`'s small SPA contract. Keep only dependencies and source needed for the counter and selected adapter. Move schemas, Xray, Story, HTTP, production CSP/hosting, Pair, and other capabilities to a compact next-steps link instead of installing or explaining them on the default route.
- Keep explicit UIx and empty-project merge recipes as secondary leaves. They may share the substrate-neutral counter, but they must not introduce a wizard, option matrix, compatibility aliases, or questions into the default.
- Replace prose-lock emphasis with an exact-output behavioral contract: consume the same shipped source the skill uses, resolve its real deps, compile it, serve its real page, and assert the counter paints and advances 0→1. Keep small structural checks only where they prevent a false-green.
- End with a factual handoff: files created, command verified, URL, and the single next skill for application authoring. Mention optional tools only when requested.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:51-63` makes schemas/Xray and their npm dependencies day-one, carries the substrate/tool matrix, and makes the generator user-run only; lines 68-81 repeat route-specific checks and handoff text.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md:65-73` requires an author-selected pin and explicitly says to stop before editing; line 77 begins a long publication-state/manual coordinate branch.
- Current measured sizes: `SKILL.md` 16,439 B; `deps-versions.md` 21,457 B; `entry-namespace.md` 22,547 B; `first-counter.md` 18,660 B; `shadow-cljs.md` 19,141 B; `shared-dataflow.md` 6,929 B. `skills/README.md` sets a 16 KB leaf ceiling.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/spec/design.md:17,46` locks “the author runs the build; the skill doesn't”; line 109 claims the smaller progressive-disclosure shape that the current file sizes and happy-path routing contradict.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:4-22` is trigger-only despite prompts explicitly asking the skill to start from nothing and mount a counter.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:109-1153` contains 15 numbered structural locks (including Xray, CSP, publication state, and generator prohibition).
- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj:1204-1490` synthesises setup deps, rewrites them to local roots, and stops at compile.
- Git history: initial commit `1806995740`; measured hot-reload repairs `rf2-r0kk7` and `rf2-ms6r8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From an empty directory, the positive prompt “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” takes no clarification round, writes a deterministic Reagent project with no `<VERSION>`/`<SHA>` placeholders, and uses one resolving baseline stored in one source of truth.
2. The default route requires `SKILL.md` plus at most one one-level-deep leaf/asset. Shipped leaves meet the family size discipline or have a demonstrated per-session token-saving exception; no default-path leaf routes onward to another required leaf.
3. The default direct dependency/file manifest matches the reduced runnable SPA contract from `rf2-zq34m`: no schema/Xray/Story/SSR/HTTP coordinate, no `@xyflow/react` or `elkjs`, no Xray host, and no generated policy/toolchain bundle unless the author explicitly requested that capability.
4. The skill executes file creation, install, and a terminating compile verification itself. Its handoff names the successful command and the actual local URL; it does not claim the browser mounted from compile success alone.
5. A black-box setup fixture consumes the exact shipped default source in a fresh temp project, resolves the documented coordinates, compiles, starts the real generated page, asserts the heading and initial `0`, clicks `+1`, and observes `1`. A red witness proves that breaking the adapter/init/build wiring or click path fails the fixture.
6. An explicit UIx prompt and an explicit merge-into-empty-CLJS prompt still reach complete focused routes, but the unqualified route contains no substrate/version/devtools questionnaire, option matrix, or compatibility mode.
7. Evals cover both routing and outcome: at least the start-from-nothing/minimum-wiring prompts assert no clarification, expected manifest/commands, successful verification, and concise handoff. Trigger-only fixtures may remain but are not the sole evaluation.
8. Root instructions, README/plugin metadata, references, internal design notes, and tests describe the same one-pass contract. Stale locks that require user-run generation, Xray/schema day-one wiring, or prose minutiae are removed rather than wrapped in compatibility wording.

## Non-goals

- No setup wizard, interactive questionnaire, `:minimal?` flag, profile system, deprecated aliases, or old-shape compatibility scaffold.
- No re-frame2 runtime, adapter, schema, Xray, Story, Pair, HTTP, SSR, CSP, or deployment redesign.
- No second generator implementation. Reuse or mechanically derive from the canonical reduced template contract; do not duplicate its variant machinery in the skill.
- No Hicasso substrate addition and no widening beyond the existing explicit UIx route.
- No authoring guidance beyond the mounted counter and concise next-step link.
- No Clojars group verification, coordinate rename, tag, repo split, or publication work; those remain with their existing owners.

## Related beads

- `rf2-zq34m` (open): owns collapsing `tools/template/**` to one small runnable SPA contract. This skill should consume that contract, not duplicate or broaden it.
- `rf2-r0kk7` and `rf2-ms6r8` (closed): established and propagated the measured-correct hot-reload lifecycle; preserve the behavior while removing the surrounding ceremony.
- `rf2-uelji` and `rf2-fo4ng` (deferred): own public-coordinate verification and rename. This task must not bypass or absorb them.
- `rf2-k5r9t` (open): adapter-owned client-root work may later shorten boot code but is not a prerequisite for fixing this skill journey.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern resources — reg-resource-scope shown as a 2-slot {:inputs :resolve} map the runtime rejects; canonical form is 3-slot (id metadata resolve-fn)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md` §Named scope resolvers — `reg-resource-scope` (L104-107):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs  {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}    ;; declared inputs — names ↦ source descriptors
   :resolve (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]
              (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}]))})
```

L118 then describes the `{:inputs … :resolve …}` **form** as the canonical declaration ("The `{:inputs … :resolve …}` form **declares** which app facts decide identity") and offers the whole-db bare-fn as the sugar. `resources-mutations.md`, the mutation descriptors and every `{:from-db :session}` reference in both leaves build on this registration.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:15-23` — "## The `{:inputs …}` metadata + resolver-fn grammar (the ONE canonical form) … The 3-slot shape is `(scope-id metadata resolve-fn)`: the resolver is the THIRD (value) slot, not a `:resolve` key inside the metadata map." L289-300: the registration fn is `[scope-id metadata resolve-fn]`, throws `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` with the message "the :inputs / :doc reflection-config metadata map is the SECOND slot, the :resolve fn is the THIRD", and the comment at L299-300 is explicit: "A `:resolve` left INSIDE the metadata map is a mislocated key; reject it". `spec/016-Resources.md:169,586` states the same 3-slot grammar; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/scope.cljs:105+` registers `:realworld/viewer` / `:realworld/session` in the 3-slot form. The whole-db bare-fn sugar the leaf mentions (L118) does exist (`scope_registry.cljc:55-68`) — that part is right.

## IMPACT

The one registration the whole Resources scope story hangs on is written in a shape the runtime rejects loudly (2-slot with `:resolve` mislocated). An agent copying it gets `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` at boot; every `{:from-db :session}` downstream then fails closed (unresolved scope → `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` on subs, dropped targets on mutations). Loud rather than silent, but it is the leaf's headline snippet and it contradicts the spec, the implementation and the canonical example at once.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/resources.md` only)

Rewrite L104-107 to the 3-slot form (lift from `scope_registry.cljc:17-20` or `scope.cljs`):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}}     ;; metadata: declared inputs
  (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]                           ;; resolver: THIRD slot, first arg = resolved inputs map
    (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))
```

and reword L118 ("The `{:inputs …}` metadata + third-slot resolver …"). Optionally add the one-line "first arg is ALWAYS the resolved inputs map; the bare-fn sugar is the only form whose first arg is the whole db" since that is the trap the grammar exists to prevent (`scope_registry.cljc:26-33`).

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences; `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run. Verify by hand against `scope_registry.cljc` §grammar and `realworld_resources/scope.cljs`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

Every `reg-resource-scope` call in `skills/re-frame2/patterns/*.md` is 3-slot `(id metadata resolve-fn)` with no `:resolve` key in the metadata map; the prose names the resolver as the third slot.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern websocket — canonical declaration does not register (4 dangling action ids → :rf.error/machine-unresolved-action) and calls an undefined current-socket? helper
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md` §Canonical declaration (L68-176) is presented as copyable code ("the canonical declaration below is the leaf-level summary" L7; "Read the source first; the declaration above is the leaf-level summary" L231). Its `:actions` map (L95-118) declares eight ids: `:record-connection-opts :rotate-cred :on-socket-lost :fail-in-flight :on-fatal-error :on-connected :flush-queue :enqueue-message`. Its states reference four more that are never declared: `:send-auth` (L147 `:authenticating {:entry :send-auth …}`), `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` (L158-159), `:send-now` (L160). Its `:trusted-frame?` guard (L91-93) calls a bare fn `(current-socket? data source-socket-id)` that the leaf never defines — `:current-socket?` exists only as a guard KEY in the same `:guards` map (L81-87), and a guard keyword is not callable from another guard's body.

## TRUTH AT TIP

Machine registration resolves action refs eagerly: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1651,1812` — "`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` on dangling refs". So `(rf/reg-machine :ws/connection …)` as written throws at registration on `:send-auth` (the first dangling ref hit), before any state is entered. And `current-socket?` is an undeclared symbol — a CLJS compile warning / undefined var at load. The example the leaf calls ground truth already has both fixes: `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:110-118` defines the shared helper `from-live-socket?` and all three guards (`:current-socket?` L215, `:own-request-timeout?` L242, `:trusted-frame?` L266) call it; the four actions are defined at L355-364 (`:send-auth`), L404-409 (`:send-now`), and the receive/refuse pair (`:receive-message` L515+, `:refuse-frame` — note the example names it `:receive-message`, not `:route-message`).

While there, one drift worth lifting in the same edit: the example guards the lifecycle transitions too — `connection.cljs:42-46` "This covers the whole socket-sourced surface — the lifecycle transitions (`:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed`, `:ws/closed`) as much as `:ws/received`" — whereas the leaf's `:connecting {:on {:ws/opened {:target :authenticating}}}` (L146), `:authenticating` (L148-149) and the parent `:ws/closed` (L139) carry no `:current-socket?` guard, so a straggler `:ws/closed` from a torn-down socket would bounce the NEW connection into `:reconnecting`. The leaf's feature table (L26) claims the guard "rejects events from a torn-down prior socket" generally.

Everything else in the leaf checks out against the 2026-09-01/02 spec + example commits (`2ef4147f8f`, `510e758f7e`, `f552191c3d`, `3113303ff4`, `7fb6031db7`, `cc2d3e5d71`): request-reply is taught as app-level (`:origin :ws/server` / `:ws/local`, no envelope, L200), the registration-token rule is in the anti-patterns (L225-226), three doors out of `:active` settle `:in-flight` (L52-66, L139-141), and `:cred-ref` timing matches. The token / `:next-token` mechanics live in prose only, which the "example is ground truth" framing covers.

## IMPACT

The one code block an agent copies for a WebSocket machine fails at registration with `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` and a compile-time undefined symbol. The agent then either invents four action bodies and a helper (plausibly wrong — `:route-message` must clear the `:in-flight` slot by REGISTRATION token, which only the example shows) or abandons the leaf for the example, which is what the leaf should have handed it in the first place.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/websocket.md` only)

- Add a `(defn current-socket? [data source-socket-id] …)` helper above the machine (mirroring the example's `from-live-socket?`) and have both guards call it; or rename to `from-live-socket?` to match the example verbatim.
- Add the four missing actions in compact form — `:send-auth` and `:send-now` are two lines each (lift from `connection.cljs:355-364, 404-409`); `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` can be one-line stubs whose comment says "lifted in full from `connection.cljs` `:receive-message` / `:refuse-frame`" — or rename `:route-message` → `:receive-message` so the reader greps the right symbol.
- Guard `:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed` and the parent `:ws/closed` with `{:guard :current-socket? …}` as the example does.
- Keep the leaf's length in mind (it is already 29 KB — see the patterns leaf-size bead); prefer lifting over adding prose.

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences — `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run (both exit 0 today; both blind to this). Verify by hand: every `:action` / `:entry` id referenced in the declaration appears in `:actions`, every bare symbol the guards call is defined in the leaf, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

The canonical `:ws/connection` declaration references no action id absent from its own `:actions` map and no undefined symbol; lifecycle transitions carry `:current-socket?`; the leaf's `:in-flight` / token prose is unchanged.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern boot — :routing waits on :rf.route/resolved, an event nothing dispatches (spec Pattern-Boot shares the fiction)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/boot.md` §Canonical declaration (state-machine form), L233-234:

```clojure
:hydrating {:entry :phase-hydrate :on {:hydrate/done {:target :routing}}}
:routing   {:entry :enter-routing :on {:rf.route/resolved {:target :ready}}}
```

with `:enter-routing` (L194-197) dispatching `[:rf.route/handle-url-change (.. js/window -location -href)]`. The prose (L242) says the machine "self-initialises and starts working at birth", and `decision-trees/pick-a-pattern.md:74` names this state set (`… → :routing → :ready`) as "the canonical state set".

## TRUTH AT TIP

No framework surface dispatches `[:app/boot [:rf.route/resolved]]` — or any `:rf.route/resolved` at all: `grep -rF ":rf.route/resolved"` over `implementation/{core,routing,machines,resources,ssr,...}/src` returns 0 hits (every other `:rf.route/*` id the leaf uses resolves: `:rf.route/handle-url-change` 99 hits, `:rf.route/navigate` 84). `spec/012-Routing.md` does not define it either; the routing runtime's post-resolution surfaces are the `:rf.route/transitioned` runtime event (31 hits, dispatched top-level, never into an app machine) and the route's `:on-match` metadata, which `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:14-17` describes as "fire-and-forget `:on-match` dispatch … dispatches (in order, …) on a valid plan". `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:191` carries the identical `:rf.route/resolved` line — the leaf copied the spec faithfully; the spec is what drifted from the implementation (Cardinal rule 1: implementation wins).

`:hydrate/done` (L233) is fine — app-prefixed, the app dispatches it — but nothing in the leaf says so, and an agent reads the two lines as the same kind of thing.

## IMPACT

An agent copying the canonical boot machine gets one that boots, authenticates, loads the profile, hydrates, dispatches the URL-change, and then sits in `:routing` forever: `:ready` is unreachable, `:app.boot/state` never reads `:ready`, and the app's "boot complete" gate never opens. Silent — no error, no trace, the route slice does settle — so it presents as "the app loads but the boot spinner never goes away". Under `:rf/*` reservation the app cannot "just dispatch it" either (Cardinal rule 7).

## FIX SHAPE (one PR; touches the spec too, so it is hot-zone)

Replace the fictional event with the shipped seam: the initial route's `:on-match` (fire-and-forget, dispatched on a valid plan) sends an app-prefixed event into the boot machine, e.g. route metadata `{:on-match [:app/boot [:boot/route-resolved]]}` and `:routing {:entry :enter-routing :on {:boot/route-resolved {:target :ready}}}` — with one line naming `:on-match` as the producer and one line saying `:hydrate/done` is likewise app-dispatched (by the handler that finishes hydration). Make the same substitution in `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:191` (and its `:routing` prose at L450 if it names the event). Alternative if a route-plan-independent signal is wanted: a small `reg-event` that listens for the top-level `:rf.route/transitioned` and forwards — but `:on-match` is the documented hook and needs no forwarder. Update `pick-a-pattern.md:74` only if the state names change (they need not).

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (both read-only structural; neither compiles the fence). No gate compiles skill code fences — verify by hand that every `:on` key in the canonical machine is either app-prefixed and dispatched somewhere in the same snippet/prose, or a shipped `:rf.*` id present in `implementation/**`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`git grep -n "rf.route/resolved" -- skills spec` returns nothing; the canonical boot machine's `:routing` state exits on an event the leaf itself shows being produced (route `:on-match` or an app handler); `pick-a-pattern.md` and `boot.md` still agree on the state set.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern ssr-loaders — teaches the spec-RETIRED SSR fan-out (Pattern-SSR-Loaders retired 2026-07-04); reroute SSR data-load to Resources and fix the 14-pattern rosters
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/ssr-loaders.md` (142 lines, 11 KB) teaches Pattern-SSR-Loaders in full as a live pattern: a `:pdp/load` machine whose `:loading` state fans out three `:rf.http/managed` children via `:spawn-all` "during drain", joins on `:on-all-complete`, and is guarded by `:after {30000 :pdp/timed-out}` — "phase-level wall-clock guard — mandatory under SSR" (L67); §The deadline (L114-116): "If one fetch hangs past the deadline, `:after` exits `:loading` … no partial render"; anti-pattern L127 "**Omitting the deadline.** A loader with no `:after` can hang until the host's outer timeout fires"; L124 "each `:rf.http/managed` blocks the drain thread on the server JVM transport". Footer: "Derived from `spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md` (Convention, not Spec) @ main".

Routed from `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:104` ("SSR parallel data fetch before render (fan-out) → `patterns/ssr-loaders.md`") and named in the pattern rosters at `SKILL.md:9`, `skills/README.md:43`, `skills/re-frame2/README.md:7`, `docs/skills/re-frame2.md:17`; cross-linked from `patterns/form-action.md:15,225` ("on GET dispatch the page loader (Pattern-SSR-Loaders)"; "the GET-path sibling") and `references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:145,158` ("parallel data fetch via `:spawn-all` before render").

## TRUTH AT TIP

`spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md:1-4` — title "Pattern — SSR Loaders (RETIRED)", "**Status: RETIRED — do not implement.** This pattern was authored on two false premises and describes a render barrier that does not exist." Retired by commit `9f375386c3` (2026-07-04, rf2-exfavp). The two premises the leaf still teaches are both stated false there: (1) L12 "The managed-HTTP JVM transport is `java.net.http.HttpClient.sendAsync` … the drain reaches fixed point with the machine's children still in flight and renders the `:loading` skeleton"; (2) L13 "`:after` **no-ops under SSR** … The mandated server deadline is a dead remedy — it never fires. A machine that leans on it … simply hangs at `:loading`". L17 states the rule: "**Machines are synchronous-only under SSR.** Async machine work — a `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` whose children exist to drive async loads … is **outside the SSR allowed subset**. It is a programmer error". L19 names the pinning fixture `spec/conformance/fixtures/spawn-all-under-ssr-ring.edn` (`:rf.machine.timer/skipped-on-server`, snapshot stuck at `:loading`). §What to use instead (L21-31): route-owned blocking resources + `drain-blocking-resources!` (Spec 016 §SSR and hydration) — the one render barrier the runtime installs, with a real deadline that settles to `{:kind :rf.http/timeout :reason :ssr-blocking-timeout}`. L39: FormAction's "GET-path pointer to this pattern now resolves to resources-backed loading".

Independently of the retirement, the leaf's own snippet would not register: `:after {30000 :pdp/timed-out}` (L67) names `:pdp/timed-out` as an `:after` TARGET (a state), then treats it as an `:on` EVENT key (L71) — no state by that name exists, and `:after` values are state/transition targets (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:478-480` checks every `:after` target), so registration fails before the SSR question even arises.

The skill leaf has not been touched since the retirement (no commit on `skills/re-frame2/patterns/ssr-loaders.md` since 2026-07-04; the skill's SSR routing row, rosters and cross-links all predate it).

## IMPACT

title: ssr-node crossing (D/6): JVM->Node adapter re-frame.ssr.ring.node + JVM->Node->JVM CI witness on a fixture module
description:
Slice D of the ssr-node crossing programme. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 (S5, S6, S7 especially) first; this description carries only D's own brief. Depends on A, B and C being MERGED (not merely closed).

## Scope (fence)

- New `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj` (the adapter), `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn` (+ `org.clojure/data.json`; if `implementation/deps.edn` aliases must also see it, that file is HOT-ZONE — sequence), `implementation/ssr-ring/test/**` including a plain-JS fixture render module under `implementation/ssr-ring/test/fixtures/node/` (the eight-line `{protocol, buildId, entries, render}` shape ssr-node's own fixtures use — no React, no CLJS build).
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`: one new job (HOT-ZONE — queue behind any in-flight workflow toucher). The classifier pair (`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` + `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`) ONLY if a new output is genuinely needed, and then both halves in ONE commit; prefer composing the existing `ssr_node` and JVM-implementation outputs.
- `spec/011-SSR.md`: one stanza for the Node renderer's construction opts and error codes (HOT-ZONE).

## Do

`(re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer {:endpoint "http://127.0.0.1:8148" :entry "app/root" :args <edn> :build-id "..." :timeout-ms 1000 ...})` returns the fn slice A's `:renderer` opt expects. Per request, inside the frame scope: `render-state/project` on the live frame (slice C) -> per-key EDN text for both partitions -> `POST /render` with `protocol 1`, `entry`, `args`, `state`, the runtime partition (C's spelling), `buildId`, `timeoutMs`, `requestId` -> Node's body bytes returned as `:body-html`, `:render-hash nil` (a native root carries no structural hash — S1). Construction validation: entry, args, render-state policy, build id, endpoint and timeouts are required for the Node renderer; `:root-view` is not (A made it conditional).

Transport (S6): ONE `java.net.http.HttpClient` per renderer, built at construction and reused; EVERY request carries an explicit timeout = `timeoutMs` + the sidecar's admission budget + a wire margin, derived by the adapter (add a knob only if you find one necessary). JSON via `org.clojure/data.json` — accepted by the ruling as ssr-ring's one new dependency. Build skew: the sidecar already refuses on `buildId` mismatch; additionally compare `x-rf-ssr-build` on success defensively and throw a distinct code if it differs.

Errors (S5): a transport failure (connection refused, read timeout), a sidecar refusal (`x-rf-ssr-refusal` present; 4xx/503/504/500) and a sidecar render failure ALL throw at the render call site with a live frame, so ALL route through the EXISTING render-failure projection (`ssr/project-render-exception!` -> the `:error-view` side of spec/011's division, ~:1428-1450) as a projected 5xx — with DISTINCT codes (e.g. `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable`, `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused` carrying the refusal code in ex-data, `:rf.error/ssr-node-deadline`). NEVER copy the sidecar's HTTP status to the browser response. `:on-error` keeps its existing meaning. No partial success page is possible: the body render fails before any shell is assembled.

## The crossing witness (a new test.yml job, named for what it is: the JVM -> Node -> JVM crossing)

A dedicated ssr-ring test alias (`:crossing-test`, so the default `:test` alias stays Node-free) that: spawns slice B's `serve` launcher via `ProcessBuilder` with the fixture module on port 0, parses B's ready line, constructs `ssr-handler` with the Node renderer, and proves —
(a) the JVM drains `:initial-events` FIRST and the fixture receives the drained value through the state partition (the fixture echoes a state value into its markup);
(b) the response is a complete JVM-owned document — JVM head, `__rf_payload` built from the JVM app-db, JVM shell/status/headers — with Node's body bytes inserted verbatim;
(c) render-state != payload: a server-only key is rendered by the fixture and ABSENT from `__rf_payload`;
(d) ONE refusal-or-deadline arm: a fixture entry that sleeps past `timeoutMs` -> sidecar 504 -> projected 5xx through `:error-view`, distinct code, no partial page (a refusal arm — a key the entry does not allowlist — is an acceptable substitute if the deadline arm proves flaky under CI load);
(e) cleanup on success AND on failure: the JVM request frame is destroyed (frame registry empty) and the sidecar's `/health` shows no in-flight work;
(f) ONE observational complete-crossing timing printed to the job log — a number, not a threshold.
Kill the launcher in a `finally`. The job needs `setup-node` 24 and the JVM toolchain; copy the shape of the existing JVM jobs.

## Acceptance

Everything above; existing ssr-ring, ssr and ssr-node lanes green; the spec/011 stanza; and while in `test.yml`, correct the stale comment at ~:5123 ("73 rows across 7 suites" — 8 suites since before this programme; slice B raised it to 9).

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`clojure -M:test` AND `clojure -M:crossing-test` in `implementation/ssr-ring` (Node 24 on PATH). The new CI job is the gate for the witness — cite its green run by URL in the PR body.

## Traps

Pass the FULL 40-char head oid to `gh run list --commit` (from `gh pr view --json headRefOid`); job keys need TWO leading spaces in the merge-criterion grep; `.github/workflows/*` is hot-zone; never pipe a gate through `tail`; no `git stash`; worker worktree guard first, report `WORKTREE_ROOT`.

title: surface-review(xray): make Pair the single agent runtime and retire the duplicate Xray seam
description:
## Scope

Make the human/agent boundary around Xray explicit and singular for pre-alpha users:

- Xray's preload and public API own the in-app human panel.
- `re-frame2-pair.runtime` plus `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/` own out-of-process programmer/AI inspection and mutation.
- Retire the unused `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` agent contract, its sentinel, tests, manifest rows, and documentation.
- Preserve the small fail-closed egress projection that Xray itself needs when copying app-db snapshots and diff values, but keep it internal to the panel.

Review and update the affected Xray source, specs, docs, tests, testbeds/build wiring, and repository API manifests. The desired outcome is one honest setup story, not a new capability.

## Findings

1. Xray documents an agent integration that does not exist. `tools/xray/README.md` and `tools/xray/spec/API.md` say Pair MCP evaluates `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` and that Xray's preload installs the agent sentinel with no second preload. Pair MCP instead hard-codes `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, probes `js/globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime` before runtime-backed tools, and contains zero references to the Xray runtime namespace or sentinel.
2. The two seams are not interchangeable. The canonical Pair preload supplies the current coarse-grained workflow (`orient`, `snapshot`, event-bundle/cascade reads, dispatch consequence/dry-run, recording/watch, DOM/UI reads, restore/replace). Xray's older runtime still exposes a parallel catalogue of trace/epoch/app-db/registrar/resource/subscription/mutation calls and explicitly leaves event-bundle reads to a follow-on.
3. The duplication is substantial and already drifting: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs` is about 91 KB / 1,700 lines and its dedicated CLJS test is about 115 KB / 1,884 lines. The Pair preload is about 230 KB / 4,000 lines and has continued evolving after Xray runtime's last direct change on 2026-07-11.
4. Xray itself does not need that public agent catalogue. Within `tools/xray/src`, the only functional callers of the runtime namespace outside the preload are three calls to `runtime/egress-value` in the palette snapshot and app-db diff copy paths. The preload requires the whole namespace solely to install the second sentinel.
5. The contract contradicts Xray's own product boundary. `spec/Principles.md` says Xray is the human surface and AI belongs in the separate Pair MCP; `018-Event-Spine.md` says the agent reads raw instrumentation rather than a Xray-curated facade. Xray already has a large panel/tab information architecture, and its restraint principle explicitly argues for subtraction rather than another surface.
6. Four Xray runtime exports are nevertheless published as post-v1 tooling rows in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` / generated `spec/api-manifest.edn`, turning an unused pre-alpha seam into prospective compatibility cost.
7. Testbed wiring proves the real setup: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` explicitly loads `re-frame2-pair.runtime` alongside Xray in builds that Pair MCP drives, while Xray-only and Pair-only builds load their respective preloads independently.

## Recommended Action

Take a clean pre-alpha cut:

1. Remove `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` as a public/tooling namespace, including `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime`, its preload require, external accessor catalogue, mutation helpers, streaming state, dedicated runtime test bulk, and API-manifest rows.
2. Move or re-express only the panel-local `egress-value` behavior needed by palette snapshot and app-db diff copying in a small internal Xray namespace, preferably as a thin call to the canonical framework projection. Keep its current frame-owned, fail-closed sensitive/large-value behavior and focused tests.

THE FIX. workspace.md is the OPERATOR's page — the pilot never reads it — so in-tree knowledge is allowed here; it must not leak into the two briefs.
1. Give each workspace an app-owned behavioural baseline under `app/test/` that runs from the clean workspace: extract the subset of the two adapter suites that exercises the nominated screens (RealWorld: feed + article editor + the routing they need; LinearLite: the board's create / retitle / change-status optimistic patches, commit and rollback), standing on cljs.test plus whatever the workspace can resolve from the published route (the Hicasso test kit on its `:test` alias, core test support) — NOT on the in-repo harness. Both suites currently use `re-frame.test-support` snapshot/restore and canned-stub helpers that live in the adapter test tree; whatever the copied tests need travels with them. Scope to the named screens — the whole RealWorld suite is not required.
2. Add the test build to the copy-ready shadow-cljs.edn in workspace.md (a `:node-test` or `:browser-test` target) and the one-line test command, so "the test command and its captured exit code" exists.
3. Add a step 5b to the six-step setup: run the baseline with the app still on Reagent and record its exit code in the log header beside the pinned commit. A baseline that is not green before the pilot starts is the operator's problem, not the pilot's.
4. Update the per-pilot source manifest so a second operator can rebuild the workspace by following the page alone.

ACCEPTANCE. From a workspace built by following workspace.md alone, `app/` runs its baseline green on Reagent before any Hicasso change; the two briefs are unchanged, or changed only to name the test command — no in-tree path may appear in either brief (rf2-hic-069's fresh-reader fence).
