title: skill(re-frame2): xstate-translation.md has no row for three shipped transition-grammar features — :ns/* and :* wildcards, :reenter? self-transitions, cross-region :tags/:all-state guard ctx (the stateIn analog)
description:
CLAIM
- `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md:11-37` — the translation table; `reg-machine.md:20` calls it "The full 27-row translation key — every concept, convergence and divergence"; SKILL.md cardinal rule 3 names it the standing mental model ("think in xstate, then map onto re-frame2 … a handful re-frame2 renames or omits, and those divergences are the trap").
- `xstate-translation.md:7` lists `stateIn` among the v5 helper creators v6 "removes … which re-frame2 never had" — with no row saying what re-frame2 ships for the cross-region-coordination *concept*.
- `reg-machine.md:118-132` (§Transition shape): the `:on` value forms — bare target / map / guarded vector. Nothing on event-descriptor tiers.
- `reg-machine.md:153-155` (§Guard/action contract): "Every callback receives one context map — `{:keys [data event state meta] cofx :rf.cofx}` … the runtime always delivers the full context map".
- `regions.md` has no section on how one region's guard reads a sibling region's state.
- `git grep -nEi "reenter|wildcard|:ns/\*|all-state|stateIn" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/ skills/re-frame2/decision-trees/` hits only the L7 preamble above.

TRUTH AT TIP — three shipped transition-grammar features with no row and no leaf
1. Wildcard / partial event descriptors. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:289-330` (§Wildcard transitions, §Namespaced (partial) event descriptors — `:ns/*`): `:on` resolves three tiers, exact → `:ns/*` → `:*`, least-priority *enabled* candidate at each level. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:800` (`:event-key <matched :on key, else nil> ;; exact / :ns/* / :* key`). XState spelling: `'*'` and `'mouse.*'` wildcard keys — a v4/v5/v6 constant an xstate-trained agent will reach for.
2. `:reenter?` self-transitions. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:332-360` (§Self-transitions — internal default vs external `:reenter?`): four geometries — targetless (action only, children preserved), self/ancestor target without `:reenter?` (re-resolves descendants to `:initial`), descendant target from a compound (re-enters the child), `:reenter? true` (exit + entry, timers restart, `:spawn` children respawn). `transition.cljc:1512-1522` implements the opt-in. XState spelling: `reenter: true` (v5/v6), `internal: false` (v4).
3. Cross-region coordination — the `stateIn` analog. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1750-1836` (§Cross-region coordination — tags as `stateIn`): a guard/action running inside a parallel region gets two extra ctx keys, `:tags` (machine-wide tag union — "**the** documented `stateIn` equivalent") and `:all-state` (region-name → active-state map, `(= :valid (:form (:all-state ctx)))`), frozen at the start of the selection round; flat/compound ctx stays exactly `{:data :event :state :meta}`. `transition.cljc:284-333` (`callback-ctx`: "additionally receives `:tags` + `:all-state`" for region callbacks).

IMPACT
These are precisely the "xstate-trained intuition steers you wrong" cases the leaf exists for, and today each ends in a hand-roll: duplicating a transition per event id instead of `:mouse/*`; exiting-and-re-entering via an intermediate state to get `:after` timers to restart, or writing an action that resets `:data` because "self-transition re-resolves children" is unknown; coupling regions through shared `:data` flags because the guard contract paragraph says the ctx is *exactly* `{data event state meta}`. Item 3 is also a correctness bug in `reg-machine.md:153-155` as written for parallel machines.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, three files)
- `xstate-translation.md`: three rows — **wildcard transitions** (`'*'` / `'ns.*'` → `:*` / `:ns/*`, convergence, note the enabled-fallthrough rule); **`reenter`** (`reenter: true` → `:reenter? true`; default = xstate "internal" geometry; targetless = action-only); **`stateIn` / `In()`** (→ read `(:tags ctx)` or `(:all-state ctx)` inside a region guard; flat machines use their own `:state`). Fix L7 so `stateIn` points at its row rather than reading as "never had".
- `reg-machine.md` §Transition shape: one line naming the three descriptor tiers; §Guard/action contract: "flat / compound: exactly `{data event state meta}`; inside a parallel region also `:tags` and `:all-state` — see regions.md". Fix "27-row" to the real count (the table has 25 rows today; 28 after).
- `regions.md`: a short §Cross-region coordination (the `:submit`-guarded-on-sibling-validity example from spec §1772, ~10 lines) and one gotcha on the frozen-config rule.
Watch the byte ceiling: reg-machine.md is already 19.8 KB (separate size bead); keep the additions to one line each there.

GATE
No gate validates this prose. `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --verbose` must stay green. Verify the new fences by hand against spec/005 §289/§332/§1750 and `transition.cljc` `callback-ctx`, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
`git grep -nE ":ns/\*|:reenter\?|:all-state" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/` hits xstate-translation.md, reg-machine.md and regions.md; the row-count sentence in reg-machine.md matches `grep -c '^| ' xstate-translation.md` minus the two header rows; drift script exits 0.

title: skill(re-frame2): cancellation.md teaches one auto-released resource kind; the runtime releases three (:after timers, :rf.resource/* owners under [:machine actor-id])
description:
CLAIM
`skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md`:
- L5 (§When to load): "The cleanup is automatic; this leaf tells you what is guaranteed and what to add by hand for non-HTTP side effects."
- L11 (§The guarantee): "When the runtime destroys a spawned actor by **any** trigger, every in-flight `:rf.http/managed` request the actor had issued is aborted." — the only guarantee the leaf states.
- L57 (§Cooperative cleanup for non-HTTP side effects): "The framework's automatic abort hook covers `:rf.http/managed`. For anything else a child holds — a websocket, **a timer**, a subscription on an external stream — wire your own cleanup into the child's `:exit` action."
- L100-102 (§Why one mechanism, not two): restates the HTTP-only hook.

TRUTH AT TIP
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3607-3619` (§What auto-cancels on destroy — exactly three framework-managed resource kinds): "1. In-flight `:rf.http/managed` requests … 2. Armed `:after` timers the actor scheduled — cancelled by `cancel-actor-timers!` on the same destroy path … 3. `:rf.resource/*` owners the actor holds under its `[:machine <actor-id>]` owner — released by dispatching the existing `:rf.resource/release-owner` effect on the same destroy path … The release fires on every destroy trigger". Then: "Any other resource a child actor holds is NOT auto-released — a `setInterval` / raw `setTimeout` issued via a custom fx, a WebSocket subscription, …".
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resource_release.cljc` (ns docstring): machine teardown releases the actor's `[:machine actor-id]` resource owners by keyword-dispatching `:rf.resource/release-owner`, guarded by `release-owner-registered?` so it is a no-op without the resources artefact; "Together these cover EVERY destroy cause".
- `timer/cancel-actor-timers!` is called from `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:256` and `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:640`.

IMPACT
Two consumer-visible errors. (a) The leaf says "a timer" is the author's job — an agent reads that as "wire `:exit` cleanup for my `:after`", which the runtime already cancels; the correct scope is *raw* `setTimeout` / `setInterval` issued through a custom fx. (b) The resource-owner release is untaught anywhere in the skill: `patterns/resources.md` (partition D) teaches `[:rf.resource/ensure {… :owner …}]`, and a machine that `ensure`s under `:owner [:machine <actor-id>]` gets that owner released on destroy — the whole reason to mint machine-owned owners — but an agent following this leaf either hand-releases in `:exit` or, worse, never uses the machine owner key and leaks a polling owner past the actor's death. The leaf is the skill's only cancellation carrier.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, one file)
- §The guarantee: state the three kinds (HTTP requests, armed `:after` timers, `:rf.resource/*` owners under `[:machine <actor-id>]`), one line each, with the "fires on every destroy trigger" sentence covering all three.
- §Cooperative cleanup: retitle to "for resources the framework does not manage", drop "a timer", and list the spec's examples (raw `setTimeout` / `setInterval` via a custom fx, WebSocket, worker, third-party SDK subscription).
- Add one gotcha: "A resource `ensure`d under `:owner [:machine <actor-id>]` is released on destroy; a three-part `[:machine <id> <instance>]` owner is app-authoritative and is NOT (resource_release.cljc docstring)." Cross-link `../../patterns/resources.md` §owners.
- §Why one mechanism, not two: "the same hook" → "the same destroy path" and name the three.
Keep the leaf under 16 KB (it is 11,090 B now).

GATE
No gate — nothing validates this prose; `check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose` for the new relative link. Verify by hand against spec/005 §3607 and `resource_release.cljc`, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
`grep -c "release-owner\|\[:machine <actor-id>\]" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md` ≥ 1; `grep -n "a timer" cancellation.md` returns nothing in the cooperative-cleanup section; the three kinds appear in §The guarantee; `wc -c` ≤ 16384.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): README "Watch events as they fire" example starts a signal `record` (no signals, a required arg) to observe events — the route is a watch-epochs poll with event-id-prefix + since-id
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md:96-100, §Examples "Watch events as they fire":
> **You**: Tell me about every `:checkout/*` event as I click through.
> **Claude**: *(starts a recorder, then reads it back between your clicks — every observation arrives as a completed tool result)* — I'll `record` now; after each step I'll `read-recording` and pull the matching epochs with `watch-epochs` (pred `:event-id-prefix ":checkout"`, `since-id` from the last pull), narrating each one with its effect cascade.

This is the line the rf2-ahjbc purge rewrote (e1a95e7135 changed exactly one README line) to replace the retired `subscribe` example, and it replaced a push-stream with the wrong pull tool.

TRUTH AT TIP

- `record` observes SIGNALS, not events: its `signals` arg is REQUIRED (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn `:required ["signals"]`) and the SIGNAL vocabulary is `{:app-db [path]}` / `{:sub [q]}` / `{:dom "sel"}` / `{:focus true}` (references/ops.md §Signal recording). A `record` call "for every `:checkout/*` event" has no signal to name — issued as written it fails on the missing arg, and with any signal it records value changes, not event epochs.
- The event-observation route is `watch-epochs {pred: {"event-id-prefix": ":checkout/"}}` polled with the previous `:head-id` as `since-id` — references/ops.md §Live watch and references/recipes.md §"Watch for X while I interact" both teach exactly that, with no recorder in the loop. The server's own routing rule 5 (get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs:80-85) separates the two: `record` + `read-recording` "to sample while a human drives the UI", `watch-epochs` for "what already happened".
- README.md:165 (§How the connection works) states the correct route one screen later: "Live-watch is the pull-mode `watch-epochs` poll loop".

IMPACT

The README is the human-facing catalogue (skills/README.md names it "the shipped tool catalogue") and its Examples are what a developer pattern-matches their first prompts against. This one models a three-tool dance whose first call cannot succeed, for a gesture one tool answers. It is also the retired stream use-case's replacement example — the one place the purge should have shown the new route cleanly.

FIX SHAPE

One PR, one file, ~2 lines: rewrite the Claude reply as a `watch-epochs` poll — e.g. "*(polls between your clicks — every observation arrives as a completed tool result)* — after each step I'll call `watch-epochs` with pred `:event-id-prefix ":checkout/"` and the previous `:head-id` as `since-id`, narrating each new epoch with its effect cascade." Optionally keep a one-clause pointer that `record` + `read-recording` is the route when what you want is a VALUE (a path, a sub, a DOM node, focus) sampled while the human interacts.

GATE

No gate covers README prose — verify by hand; `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the README's link gate (repo-root and beside-source READMEs), run it if any link is touched.

ACCEPTANCE

The §"Watch events as they fire" example names `watch-epochs` (with `event-id-prefix` + `since-id`) as the tool that observes the events and does not start a `record` without a signal; `grep -n 'record' skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md` shows `record` only where a signal is named.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): errors.md names two reasons nothing emits (:ns-not-loaded, :handler-error) and omits the eval-cljs failure family (:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error / -threw / -timeout / -rejected / -disabled)
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md is the leaf SKILL.md:194 routes to for "Translate a structured `{:ok? false :reason ...}` to plain English; suggest the recovery". Two of the reasons it lists are emitted by nothing, and the failure family an agent hits most often in a pair session is absent from it entirely.

Phantom ids:
- errors.md:9 — "`:ns-not-loaded :missing :re-frame2` → re-frame2 isn't loaded; check the user's deps."
- errors.md:22 — "`:handler-error` inside an epoch → the user's handler threw; surface the `:rf.error/handler-exception` trace event ..."

Missing family — `eval-cljs` is the workhorse (SKILL.md:206) and its own failures are:
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error` (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs:330)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-threw` (grep `:reason` over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-timeout` (eval_cljs.cljs:190)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-rejected` (eval_cljs.cljs:183 — the nREPL session refused the form)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled` (eval_cljs.cljs:255 — server launched with `--no-eval`)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-mailbox-missing` / `-await-wrap-failed` (eval_cljs.cljs:198,203 — the `await: true` path)

TRUTH AT TIP

`grep -rhoE ':reason :[a-zA-Z0-9./?-]+' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload | sort -u` (~100 distinct ids) contains neither `:ns-not-loaded` nor `:handler-error`; a wider `grep -rn ns-not-loaded tools/ implementation/ skills/re-frame2-pair/preload` finds nothing at all. The re-frame2-not-loaded case cannot surface as its own reason: the preload namespace requires re-frame.core, so an app without re-frame2 never installs the marker and `discover-app` reports the ladder's `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` (errors.md:19 already covers it). `:rf.error/handler-exception` (errors.md:22's own body) is the real trace op; `:handler-error` is not a `:reason` any tool returns. Across the whole skill only two of the eval-cljs ids appear anywhere (`-timeout` and `-rejected`, once each, in references/ops.md:83); `-compile-error`, `-threw`, `-disabled` are taught nowhere (`grep -rn 'eval-cljs-(compile-error|threw|disabled)' skills/re-frame2-pair` is empty).

IMPACT

The compile-error case is the one an agent trips on first (a typo in a form, an unresolved alias such as `story/` — stories.md:28 warns there is no alias), and `-disabled` is the one that needs a specific operator action (relaunch without `--no-eval`), yet the "translate the reason" leaf says nothing, so the agent falls back to guessing. ## CLAIM (three wrong statements + one gap, all in `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/capabilities.md`)

**(a) :76** — Time-travel table, "Restore failure surfaces":
> `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer {:op-type :error})` carries the structured tags

**(b) :38** — Core runtime visibility, "Inspect handler + interceptor chain + source coords":
> `handler-meta {kind: "event", id}` over `rf/handler-meta` (returns `:ns` / `:line` / `:file` / `:column` / `:handler-fn`)

**(c) :42** — "Show effects fired for one epoch":
> off-box each row's `:args` egresses as `:rf/redacted` by default (`:include-fx-args?` opt-in)

**(d) gap** — the Debugging-recipes table (:99-111) has "Watch all `:foo/*` events while I click around | *done*" with no route named, and no row at all for record / read-recording / watch-until, although the skill now has exactly five returned-result observation routes and this file is the capability scorecard.

## TRUTH AT TIP

**(a)** The form is the exact footgun `SKILL.md:78` and `references/ops.md:98,303` warn against: `trace-buffer` takes the **frame-id first** — an opts map as the sole arg "silently returns `[]`" — and `:op-type` is a **`:flat-only`** filter (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:523-531`: `:flat true` returns raw events; `:operation` / `:op-type` / `:since` / `:severity` are `(:flat-only)`). Correct form, already in ops.md:303: `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer :rf/default {:flat true :op-type :error})`. An agent copying capabilities.md's form gets `[]` and concludes there was no failure trace.

**(b)** `:handler-fn` is **stripped**, not returned: `preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:720-751` (`registrar-describe` — `(dissoc m :handler-fn)`, `strip-fns` over the map, augments `:handler-fn-hash`); `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs:46,250-262` repeats the dissoc server-side. `tests/runtime/registrar_describe_test.clj` pins the dissoc (`registrar-describe-dissocs-handler-fn`) and that `:handler-fn-hash` survives. The returned keys are `:ns` / `:line` / `:column` / `:file` / `:doc` / `:tags` / `:handler-fn-hash` / `:rf.mcp/source-uri` (ops.md:38).

**(c)** The arg is `include-fx-args` (no `?`): `descriptors_data.cljs:601` (`:include-fx-args {:type "boolean" …}`), `tools/args.cljs:75`, `dispatch_dry_run.cljs:66`. It is a `dispatch-dry-run` arg (and gated under `--allow-sensitive-reads`); the row reads as if it were a generic epoch-egress knob.

**(d)** `STATUS.md:17` names the five routes as the one supported live-observation workflow: dispatch consequence, `watch-epochs` / `trace-window`, `watch-until`, `record` + `read-recording`, `tail-build`. `references/ops.md:205-247` documents them. capabilities.md — whose stated purpose (:3) is "tell a prospective user honestly what the skill will and won't help with" — names none of them as a set, and the "Watch … while I click around" row (the one row a prospective user would look at after PR #8815 removed push streaming) says only *done*.

## IMPACT

(a) is a wrong command that fails silently (returns `[]`) — the class this review prioritises; it sits in a maintainer-facing scorecard rather than an agent-loaded leaf, which is why this is P3 not P2. (b)/(c) are wrong return/arg names an implementer would copy. (d) is the completeness gap the review was asked to check; it matters because the scorecard is where "what happened to streaming?" gets answered for a reader who does not open STATUS.md.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR, one file:
- :76 → `(re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer <frame-id> {:flat true :op-type :error})` (or simply "see ops.md §Time-travel for the read form").
- :38 → drop `:handler-fn`, add `:handler-fn-hash` (and `:doc` / `:tags` / `:rf.mcp/source-uri` if the list is meant to be complete).
- :42 → `` `include-fx-args` `` and say it is a `dispatch-dry-run` arg under `--allow-sensitive-reads`.
- Recipes table: give the "Watch … while I click around" row its route (`watch-epochs` poll with `since-id`) and add one row "Record while I interact / wait until X" → `record` + `read-recording` / `watch-until`; optionally one sentence above the table listing the five returned-result routes, citing STATUS.md as the source.

## GATE

`bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` — `capabilities-uses-current-tool-names`, `render-key-recipe-uses-first-tuple-slot` (capabilities half) and `catalogue-count-matches-live-manifest` read this file and must stay green (do not reintroduce a retired op name or a stale count). Nothing validates the corrected forms — verify (a)–(c) by hand against the cited source lines and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

title: skill(re-frame-migration): corpus Part 2 'do not introduce new dependencies' (README.md:3208) contradicts the skill's forced floor-gate / toolchain / Xray bumps while the skill README says the corpus wins
description:
CLAIM (three texts the agent is told to obey at once)
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:3208` (Part 2 §What you must not do): "**Do not introduce new dependencies** beyond bumping re-frame to the v2 version."
- `skills/re-frame-migration/README.md:92`: "If the skill and the migration corpus disagree, the corpus wins."
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:153` (Anti-patterns): "**Don't bump *unrelated* dependencies** ... The **explicit exemption**: the Phase-0b GO-state edits ride into the M-0 pass — React → 19, Reagent → 2.x ..., floor-gate-approved component-lib bumps, the shadow-cljs (Check 4) bump, any explicit ClojureScript pin, plus the Xray npm peer-deps (`@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`) when the 10x→Xray swap fires." Same list in `kickoff-prompt.md:40` and the report line in `output-format.md:14` ("Dependencies changed (non-re-frame)").

TRUTH AT TIP
The skill's exemptions are forced, not optional: the adapters target React 19 (`implementation/package.json:19-21` pins react/react-dom 19.2.0, shadow-cljs 3.4.10), so a React-17/18 v1 app cannot land M-0 without the bump; `setup.md` Check 4 documents the `NoSuchFieldError` a stale shadow-cljs produces; the Xray swap adds `day8/re-frame2-xray` + two npm peers. None of that is "bumping re-frame". The corpus's Part 2 sentence predates the floor gate and the Xray deliverable and was never carved out; the skill's README then hands precedence to the corpus.

IMPACT
Read literally and in the stated precedence, the corpus forbids the very bumps Phase 0b / Phase 2 require, and an agent that honours "the corpus wins" has a licence to refuse the React-19 floor or to leave `--legacy-peer-deps` scaffolding in place. Today agents follow the skill (the evals assume so), so the harm is a contradiction between two normative texts rather than a live failure — but it is exactly the disagreement README.md:92 says to resolve the wrong way. P3.

FIX SHAPE (one PR; the corpus file is a CLAUDE.md hot-zone file — sequence behind any in-flight corpus PR)
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:3208`: carve out the forced set in one clause — "beyond bumping re-frame to the v2 version **and the bumps the migration itself forces: the React 19 / Reagent 2 floor and floor-gate-approved component libraries (Phase 0b), the shadow-cljs / ClojureScript / Clojure toolchain pins (Check 4), and the Xray dep + npm peers when replacing re-frame-10x** — record each with the gate that justified it".
- Optionally `SKILL.md:153`: after the exemption list add "(the corpus Part 2 rule carries the same carve-out)" so the two texts visibly agree.
No new rule id; no restating the floor gate in the corpus.

GATE
`python scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py --verbose` (it scans MIGRATION.md Part 2 wording under Rule 6 — must stay green) and `python scripts/check_skill_migration_cites.py --verbose`. Prose agreement is verified by hand: quote both sentences in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
Corpus Part 2's dependency rule and SKILL.md:153's exemption list name the same forced set; no text tells the agent to refuse a floor-gate bump; gates green.

title: routing/resources: a :url-bound? make-frame plans route resources AT CONSTRUCTION and a failed plan is never retried (NOT a live-frame reprojection bug — mechanism in the original title is refuted; needs ruling)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by rf2-xkhul (PR #8990) while running the pilot baselines from a clean external workspace built per docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md on the published :local/root route (Node 24, shadow-cljs 3.4.10, dev compile of a :node-test build, goog.DEBUG default).

SYMPTOM. implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs copied VERBATIM into app/test/ of the LinearLite workspace (deps: core, adapters/reagent, http, routing, resources, hicasso) fails 16 of 51 assertions across 7 of 10 tests, while the identical file is green on the in-repo consolidated :node-test bundle. Its init! (the fixture :init-fn) does (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}) FIRST and then registrar/register! the snapshotted :resource/:mutation rows, reg-fx :rf.http/managed (capture stub) and :rf.nav/push-url. In the workspace bundle the frame never sees anything registered after make-frame: :rf.route/navigate to :linearlite.app/board lands :transition :error with :rf.error/resource-route-plan / cause :rf.error/resource-not-registered ('no resource is registered under :linearlite/board') even though (registrar/lookup :resource :linearlite/board) is truthy at that moment; moving ONLY the resource re-registration before make-frame clears that error but the capture stub registered after make-frame is still not what the read lowers through (entry stays :loading, last-managed-args nil). Moving EVERY registration before make-frame (frame made last) -> 51/51 green. Probes confirmed the ns-load state is identical to in-repo (registrar and source store both hold the resource + 3 mutations; :routing/on-route-entry and :resources/reg-resource hooks live).

WHY IT MATTERS. re-frame.live-frame documents the sealed-generation freshener as a CORRECTNESS invariant with NO debug gate (rf2-9c2jf): make-frame installs a registration hook so a later reg-* marks the projection dirty and a read-time coalesced flush reprojects (EP-0026 / rf2-h1vqa4). In the consumer bundle that reprojection does not take effect for the make-frame -> reg-* -> dispatch sequence, which live_frame.cljc names as 'exactly the broken one'. Either the in-repo bundle carries something (a sibling suite, the test-quiet runner, an artefact only it loads) that arms the flush and a consumer never gets, or the flush is not reached on this path. Unknown which; not chased under rf2-xkhul (fence was pilots/** only).

REPRO (about 3 minutes). Build the LinearLite workspace per workspace.md at tip of PR #8990 (or main once merged); replace app/test/linearlite/baseline_test.cljs with the adapter suite verbatim (ns re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test also matches the -test$ regexp); npm test -> exit 1, 16 failures. Then in its init! move (rf/make-frame ...) to the end -> exit 0. The committed baseline under docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/linearlite/ already makes the frame last and is green; this bead is about the framework behaviour the verbatim suite exposes, and about whether any in-repo fixture is green only because the consolidated bundle masks it.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP. Reproduce with a minimal consumer test: make-frame, reg-event, dispatch-sync -> expect :rf.error/no-such-handler in the consumer bundle if the theory holds; then diff what re-frame.live-frame/ensure-reprojection-installed! and the :live-frame/flush-projection! consult do in each bundle.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 19:57:00 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2-xkhul worker with a 3-minute repro. This is a FRAMEWORK bug (core/live-frame), not a hicasso or pilots one, and it is the highest-priority thing filed this session by a worker — a registration made after make-frame being invisible to that frame in a :local/root consumer bundle would bite any consumer following the published route, and it was found the only way it could be: by building a workspace outside the repo. Not fenced by any live surface. Next solo dispatch when a slot frees.
DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 20:07:19 AUSEST by the mayor. SOLO, DIAGNOSIS-FIRST, fresh worktree worker/liveframe-ma8r off origin/main 07c76826c2. Premises verified at that tip: live_frame.cljc:1790 carries the 'exactly the broken one' sentence verbatim; ensure-reprojection-installed! is referenced ~:377 and ~:512; the linearlite adapter suite has 11 deftests; the committed pilot baseline that makes the frame LAST is on main. LEAD HYPOTHESIS handed over AS A HYPOTHESIS: live_frame.cljc ~:386 reaches the flush through (late-bind/get-fn-cached :live-frame/flush-projection!) inside a when-let, so a bundle where nothing registers that publisher falls through SILENTLY — no error, no warning, exactly the observed symptom shape. The competing reading this bead names (flush reached but ineffective on this path) must be EXCLUDED rather than argued away. Worker is told the diagnosis is the deliverable, that no code change may be warranted, and to leave this bead OPEN for a ruling if the honest answer needs one.

DIAGNOSIS 2026-09-02 20:31 AUSEST (rf2-ma8r worker, PR #9000). The bead's
numbers reproduce EXACTLY (16 failures across 7 of 10 tests, 51 assertions,
exit 1, in a LinearLite workspace built per pilots/workspace.md on the
published :local/root route) — but the MECHANISM in the description is
refuted, and so is the flush-publisher hypothesis. No live-frame defect is
involved. Nothing is invisible to the frame.

WHAT IS REFUTED (each measured, not argued).

1. "Registrations made AFTER make-frame are invisible to the frame in a
   :local/root consumer node-test bundle." REFUTED. A minimal probe —
   make-frame, then reg-event, then dispatch-sync — PASSES in the very
   consumer bundle where the suite fails 16/51 (exit 0). In that same
   bundle the frame's own reprojection is demonstrably live: an explicit
   flush-pending-reprojection! taken mid-suite returns
   :added #{[:resource :linearlite/board] [:mutation :linearlite/create-issue]
   [:mutation :linearlite/edit-title] [:mutation :linearlite/change-status]}
   and :changed #{[:fx :rf.http/managed] [:fx :rf.nav/push-url]} — i.e. the
   post-make-frame registrations ARE picked up and swapped onto the frame.

2. "A late-bound :live-frame/flush-projection! that nothing registers in a
   consumer bundle makes the when-let fall through silently." REFUTED twice.
   At source: make-frame calls ensure-reprojection-installed! UNCONDITIONALLY
   (live_frame.cljc:928), and late-bind/get-fn-cached does NOT cache nil
   resolutions, so there is no negative-cache variant either. Empirically:
   in the consumer bundle the probe prints flush-publisher-resolvable? true
   and mark-dirty-publisher-resolvable? true.

3. "Or the flush is not reached on this path." REFUTED. The failing lookup
   happens strictly BEFORE the registrations exist at all, not against a
   stale generation — see below.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — a construction-time route plan, in routing/resources.

A println planted in registry/require-resource-spec!'s miss branch shows the
failing lookup happening with the registrar genuinely EMPTY
(atom-has? false, lookup-direct? false, ids-in-scope []), and — the decisive
ordering datum — it fires BEFORE the end of init!:

    PRE-MAKE-FRAME  resource-ids []
    MA8R-PLANT miss :linearlite/board where rf.resource/route-entry
                    gen-bound? true atom-has? false ids-in-scope []
    POST-MAKE-FRAME routing-slice {... :transition :error
                    :error {:rf.error/id :rf.error/resource-route-plan ...}}
    INIT-END        resource-ids [:linearlite/board] atom-has? true

So the route entry runs INSIDE (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}).
A :url-bound? frame performs a synchronous initial URL sync at construction:
frame/upsert-frame!'s post-create hook fires routing's
:routing/on-frame-registered!, which reconciles the URL listener and "syncs
the current URL into the owner's slice" (routing/history.cljc). Under Node,
history/current-url is "/". The LinearLite example registers
:linearlite.app/board at path "/" (examples/.../linearlite/core.cljs:458-464)
and that route declares :resources [{:resource :linearlite/board :blocking? true}].
The construction-time sync therefore PLANS the board resource while the
suite's init! has not yet reinstated the :resource/:mutation rows the
fixture's reset hook cleared — init! re-registers them on the NEXT line —
and the plan fails :rf.error/resource-not-registered, recording
:transition :error on the slice.

The error is then STICKY. The test's own
(dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :linearlite.app/board}]) does not
re-plan: the planted probe fires EXACTLY ONCE per test, at construction, and
never again — including in a probe test where the resource was verified
present and visible inside the frame immediately beforehand. Every one of the
16 assertions then reads nil off the never-populated entry.

DECISIVE CONTROL. Changing ONLY the example's route path from "/" to "/board"
in the workspace copy takes the identical suite from 16 failures / exit 1 to
0 failures / exit 0, with the planted probe firing ZERO times. Nothing else
was touched.

WHY THE IN-REPO BUNDLE IS GREEN — and YES, THIS IS A FALSE GREEN.
This answers the bead's second question. re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test
is green in the consolidated bundle ONLY because a co-loaded sibling owns "/".
At least seven in-tree apps register a route at "/" (infinite_feed, linearlite,
resources, routing, todomvc, realworld_http, realworld_resources), plus many
test suites. In the consolidated bundle "/" resolves to some other app's route,
so linearlite's board resource is never planned at construction and the suite's
explicit navigate is a genuine transition performed with everything registered.
In a consumer bundle only linearlite's routes exist, so "/" matches its board.
The in-repo suite's colour therefore depends on which siblings happen to be
co-loaded — it is not evidence about its own subject.

WHAT THE HONEST REPAIR IS — A RULING, NOT A PATCH, so this bead stays OPEN.
Two candidate framework defects, and they are different calls:

  (A) A :url-bound? frame plans route resources at construction. Arguably
      CORRECT and the whole point of :url-bound? — an app must register its
      resources before constructing a URL-bound frame, which is exactly what
      the committed pilot baseline does and what the "frame last" workaround
      does. If this is ruled correct, the defect is documentation plus the
      false green above, not code.

  (B) A FAILED route plan is never retried. A same-route navigate does not
      re-plan, so an app that RECOVERS (registers the resource afterwards)
      stays wedged in :transition :error permanently with no retry short of
      navigating away and back. This is fail-open on recovery and is the more
      interesting of the two.

Both live in routing/resources, NOT in core/live_frame.cljc. No core change is
warranted and none was made. Nothing under spec/ was touched.

NOT CHASED (named rather than argued away): whether (B) is deliberate
same-route-navigation semantics or an oversight; and whether any OTHER in-repo
suite is likewise green only by co-load masking — the "/" census above is the
place to start, and the cheap test is to build each app's suite in a
single-app bundle.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: rf2-k4oe (P2 bug) — the false green this exposed. The in-repo
re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test is green only because a co-loaded sibling
owns "/"; its one-line repair (reinstate the registrar rows BEFORE the
:url-bound? make-frame, matching the committed pilot baseline) was NOT made here
because implementation/adapters/reagent/** is inside a live peer's fence
(worker/clientroot-k5r9t).

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN for the two framework rulings named above ((A) is a
construction-time route plan correct for a :url-bound? frame, and (B) should a
FAILED route plan ever be retried). PR #9000 was closed carrying NO code change:
the diagnosis is the deliverable, and the invariant the bead accused is already
pinned in both lanes (read-time-flush-makes-late-registration-visible-same-tick
in live_frame_reload_cljs_test.cljc, which disables the deferred tick so only the
read-time flush can pass it; and prod_gate_dispatch_jvm_test.clj).
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-09-02 20:41:11 AUSEST after the diagnosis landed: this bead is OPEN and correctly so, and it is now a RULING FOR MIKE rather than dispatchable work. The worker refuted three mechanisms by measurement — the bead's own headline (the minimal make-frame → reg-event → dispatch-sync probe PASSES in the very consumer bundle where the suite fails 16/51), the mayor's late-bind lead hypothesis (refuted at source AND empirically: make-frame calls ensure-reprojection-installed! unconditionally, get-fn-cached does not cache nil, and the publisher resolves in the consumer bundle), and the bead's own alternative (an explicit flush in that bundle returns the added rows, so reprojection works). The real mechanism: a :url-bound? frame performs its initial URL sync AT CONSTRUCTION, so a route registered at "/" with blocking resources has its plan run inside make-frame before the fixture's cleared registrar rows are reinstated — and the failure is STICKY, fired once and never re-planned. Decisive control: changing only the route path from "/" to "/board" takes the identical suite from 16 failures to 0. THE RULING MIKE OWES: should a FAILED route plan ever be retried? Today an app that recovers stays wedged in :transition :error permanently. The worker declined to add a fourth test pin because two already pin the invariant (read-time-flush-makes-late-registration-visible-same-tick and the JVM prod-gate test), which is the right call under the stance. No code shipped; PR #9000 closed with an empty diff.

title: skill(re-frame2-implementor): the harness fail-loud floors and derivation greps omit the top-level :fixture/* key set — 8 live keys are undocumented in the corpus README
description:
IMPLEMENTOR-REVIEW-7f2c-B4

CLAIM
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:28-33 — "Four fail-loud floors the harness owes": spec version, unknown capability, unknown op (handler-DSL or Mode-B `:call`), non-vacuous run.
- conformance.md:12-20 — "Derive, never transcribe" greps: fixture count, Mode-B call ops, one family's live tags, dynamic-host-only set, spec versions in play.
- conformance.md:26 — harness shape: "read every fixture; filter …; bootstrap the registry; realise handler bodies via the DSL; create the frame; run the dispatches or calls; capture observables and compare; report".
- conformance.md:3 — "the **full contract is [`spec/conformance/README.md`]** — fixture format, the handler-body DSL op table, capability tagging, versioning, the harness steps."

TRUTH AT TIP
- The 245 fixtures carry 20 distinct top-level `:fixture/*` keys (`grep -rhoE ':fixture/[a-z?-]+' spec/conformance/fixtures/ | sort | uniq -c`). Beyond the keys the README §Fixture format describes, live fixtures use: `:fixture/frames` (13 fixtures), `:fixture/interceptor-fired` (11), `:fixture/flow-bodies` (6), `:fixture/clear-interceptor` (5), `:fixture/wire-order` (2), `:fixture/render-after-hydrate` (2), `:fixture/runtime` (1), `:fixture/compute-subs` (1). None of those eight strings occurs anywhere in spec/conformance/README.md, nor in spec/Spec-Schemas.md §`:rf/fixture-file` (line 4476). `:fixture/classification-effects` (17 fixtures; 6 of them `:data-classification/*`, i.e. gate-1 v1-required) is documented in the README's harness-step section but not in Spec-Schemas. `:fixture/dynamic-host-only?` is likewise README-absent.
- The README's own contract for silent skips: "a harness that silently skips unknown capabilities is the shape the spec forbids" (§Capability tagging). No floor — in the README or the skill — extends that to an unknown top-level key.

IMPACT
The skill's derive-at-the-pin posture rests on "the README is the contract"; on the fixture-file shape the README demonstrably lags the fixtures by eight keys. A port harness built from README + skill supports registry / handlers / frame-config / dispatches / expect / calls and none of the four floors fires when a fixture arrives with `:fixture/interceptor-fired` or `:fixture/frames`: the setup or expectation is ignored and the fixture can pass vacuously (an interceptor-fired expectation never checked) — the exact silent-skip shape the floors exist to forbid. On `:data-classification/*` (gate 1) a harness that has not implemented the classification-effects step fails loudly, which is fine; the eight undocumented keys are the quiet ones.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill side)
1. conformance.md §The harness: add a fifth floor — "**Unknown fixture key.** A top-level `:fixture/*` key the harness does not implement fails the run naming it — the corpus adds setup/expectation keys ahead of the README."
2. conformance.md §Derive, never transcribe: add the key-enumeration grep above beside the existing five.
3. phase-2-impl-order.md:11 (Step 0) lists the fail-loud set ("unknown spec version, capability, DSL op, call op") — add the key. SKILL.md:36 and README.md:20 carry the same four-item list; keep them in step (the order guard does not pin this list — hand check).
Spec side (report, not this bead): document the eight keys in spec/conformance/README.md §Fixture format and in Spec-Schemas §`:rf/fixture-file`; that is a corpus README gap and belongs to spec/.

GATE
No gate — verify by hand: run the new grep at tip and confirm it lists 20 keys; check_skill_implementor_order.py --verbose stays green (it scans conformance.md for the family roots only).

ACCEPTANCE
conformance.md names five floors including unknown top-level fixture keys and ships the key-enumeration grep; phase-2 Step 0, SKILL.md and README.md list the same five.

DERIVED KEY SET (not transcribed): 247 fixtures at tip carry EIGHTEEN distinct top-level :fixture/* keys. Derived by two independent methods that agree exactly on membership and on every per-key count: (1) a bracket-depth scan of every fixture that skips strings and ';;' comments and counts a keyword only at depth 1; (2) a line-start heuristic. The eighteen: capabilities, doc, id, spec-version (247 each), registry 237, handlers 218, expect 150, dispatches 148, frame-config 120, calls 108, frames 9, classification-effects 8, dynamic-host-only? 7, flow-bodies 6, render-after-hydrate 2, wire-order 2, compute-subs 1, runtime 1. title: Retrospective facade-export classification sweep (re-frame.core, Story, Xray) for external-alpha prep
description:
The RETROSPECTIVE half of the facade-export classification audit has no bead. Surfaced 2026-07-25 while processing the rf2-fby7o api-freeze dossier; bd list across every status returned no owner for it.

## What it is

spec/Conventions.md:1198 defines the audit in two halves.

The FORWARD half is already running: every new facade export classifies and justifies itself at diff time (tier, owner, status, justification), which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn all carry their four fields. That half needs nothing.

The RETROSPECTIVE half is unowned. Conventions calls it "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export - and the manifest table it produces" and says it "stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep".

## Scope

A repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core - the grandfathered exceptions Conventions explicitly records - deciding keep / rename / move / internal-public for each, and producing the manifest table.

NOT a Freehand audit. Freehand's 38 members are already classified at diff time; six are :facade? true (mount, unmount!, hydrate-root, ->react, active-connections, command-log) and every one is a CLJS-only verb re-exported from the namespace that owns it, which is exactly the deliberate single-import re-export the Conventions ruling sanctions.

## Deadline

Conventions sets it itself: before re-frame2's first meaningful external alpha/beta release - explicitly NOT "before v1". The reasoning is that the moment real users copy examples, a namespace move becomes a breaking change.

## Relationship to rf2-fby7o

DECOUPLED. rf2-fby7o's release condition names this audit as half of its api-freeze gate. Two independent analyses concluded that coupling is a drafting accident rather than intent: gating a Freehand guide on a re-frame.core sweep that Conventions itself schedules for external-alpha prep does not make the guide more correct. See rf2-fby7o notes (2026-07-25 dossier fold) for the full reasoning. Mike rules on whether the coupling is struck.

## Acceptance

1. Every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core carries a keep / rename / move / internal-public disposition.
2. The manifest table Conventions describes exists.
3. Anything ruled rename or move is either executed or has a bead.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-07-25 (mayor), with an explicit release condition so it stops being re-triaged every dispatch tick.

WHY NOT NOW: the bead's own charter defers it. spec/Conventions.md:1198 says the retrospective half 'stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep', and the FORWARD half is already running (every new facade export classifies itself at diff time, which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn carry all four fields). So nothing is rotting while this waits.

THE DECISIVE REASON: it is a repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core, producing a manifest table. The alpha is gated on rf2-vxgfnd.99 (EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag), which by its own title REMOVES a substrate and will move exactly the surface this sweep would classify. Running the sweep before S7 means classifying exports that S7 then deletes or renames, and redoing the table afterwards. Sequencing it after S7 costs nothing and saves the whole second pass.

RELEASE CONDITION — reopen when EITHER holds:
  1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or
  2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly.

Not a rejection: the work is real and Conventions mandates it. This is a sequencing decision only.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22 04:0x AUSEST, tip 0fa90bd815. ONE PARAGRAPH OF THIS BEAD'S SCOPING IS VOID, AND THE DEFERRAL CONDITION IS INTACT. Measured at source; this is the smaller of the two corrections this loop found in the deferred set.

MAYOR, BACKLOG-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 21:52 AUSEST — STAYS DEFERRED. Its release condition READS as met and is NOT met, so I am recording the discrimination rather than leaving the next reread to re-derive it.

THE CONDITION, as written on this bead: "reopen when EITHER holds: 1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or 2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly."

CONDITION 1'S PROXY HAS FIRED. rf2-vxgfnd.99 is CLOSED — "EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag", closed 2026-07-31. A literal read of the condition releases this bead today.

*** DO NOT RELEASE IT ON THAT READING. *** The condition names "S7 + ALPHA TAG", and the alpha tag never happened. `git ls-remote --tags origin` returns ZERO tags at this tick — nothing has ever been published from this repository. The epic closed carrying the S7 half and not the tag half, so the proxy moved while the thing it was standing for did not.

AND THE TAG IS NOT MERELY LATE — IT IS BLOCKED. rf2-uelji records that Clojars' verified-group policy refuses the FIRST publish of every day8/re-frame2-* coordinate: a new project may not be created in an unverified group, and day8 is not reverse-domain so it cannot be verified. That is an operator-only action, and it gates all 13 implementation artefacts and 5 tool jars. So "published artefact" is still exactly the moving target this bead deferred itself against.

THIS IS THE INVERSE OF THE USUAL FINDING. The loop normally catches a dependency that outlived what it was enforcing — the blocker shipped and the bead stayed blocked. Here the blocker's RECORD closed while its SUBSTANCE did not ship, so the bead reads releasable and is not. Both cases are found the same way, by testing the substance rather than the status field.

THE OPERATIVE GATE IS THEREFORE NOW: rf2-uelji clearing (which yields the tag, satisfying condition 1 in substance), OR condition 2 — the operator calling api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly, which needs no tag at all and remains available at any time.

Not a rejection. Conventions mandates the work; this is sequencing only, unchanged from the original disposition.

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): boolean-discriminator-subs After view and eval 24 clean fixture are plain defn views with bare rf/ ops — raise :rf.error/no-frame-context under EP-0002
description:
CLAIM. `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/boolean-discriminator-subs.md:71-75` — the **After** (recommended rewrite) is a plain Reagent fn with a bare facade read:

```clojure
(defn article-page []
  (case @(rf/subscribe [:article/render]) ...))
```

The same plain-`defn` + bare `rf/` shape is the should-be-clean fixture in `evals/evals.json` #24 (`behav-neg-render-local-component-state`: `(defn search-box [] ... #(rf/dispatch [:search/query-changed ...]))`), whose expectations require the agent to "report the view as clean against the catalogue".

TRUTH AT TIP. Under EP-0002 there is no `:rf/default` floor; a plain `(defn ...)` view carries no `:contextType`, cannot read the surrounding `frame-provider`'s frame, and its ambient `rf/subscribe` / `rf/dispatch` raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/views.md:104`, `.../fundamentals/subs.md:86`, `.../fundamentals/frames.md:9,82`, `skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:30` (deferred callbacks fire on a fresh stack with no `*current-frame*`). Every shipped example view is `rf/reg-view` with the injected `subscribe` (`examples/core/todomvc/views.cljs:64-141`, `examples/core/counter/*.cljs:60-70`). The improver's own `references/view-side-hook-state.md:78` states exactly this: "A plain `(defn ...)` view with a bare `#(rf/dispatch ...)` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on click (EP-0002 — no `:rf/default` floor)."

IMPACT. Leaf 2's canonical rewrite — the thing the critique hands the programmer — throws at first render in a re-frame2 app. Leaf 6 and leaf 2 contradict each other inside one catalogue. Eval 24 grades as "clean" a snippet that is itself the plain-Reagent-fn trap, so a reviewer who correctly notes it is penalised as "inventing an unrelated anti-pattern" (expectation 4), while a reviewer who stays silent misses a real runtime defect. (The Before snippets in leaf 2 and in evals #18/#22/#27 are fine as v1-flavoured "before" code; the defect is in the After and in the clean fixture.)

FIX SHAPE. One PR, two files:
1. `references/boolean-discriminator-subs.md` After: `(rf/reg-view article-page [] (case @(subscribe [:article/render]) ...))` — injected `subscribe`, no `rf/` prefix — with the one-line reason leaf 6 already gives (or a cross-ref to it).
2. `evals/evals.json` #24: make the clean fixture idiomatic re-frame2 (a `reg-view` whose deferred handlers use the injected `dispatch`; keep the render-local `hovered?` atom the fixture exists to protect — the Reagent Form-2 closure shape may need `reg-view*` / `r/with-let` per views.md; the worker picks the smallest idiomatic spelling), so "clean" is true. Optionally add to #18's expectations: "the rewritten view is a `reg-view` (or otherwise carries its frame) — a plain defn with bare `rf/subscribe` is the EP-0002 trap".

GATE. `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --verbose`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose`, `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (all exit 0 at tip; must stay 0). title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): post-error trigger names 'red CI' while §Session evidence excludes CI runs, and never names the :ok? false / :reason envelopes and :rf.error/:rf.epoch traces the pair tools actually raise
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

Post-error trigger (b) is defined in four places with "red CI" as a firing condition:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:11-12` (frontmatter description): "**post-error within a re-frame2-pair session** — after a stack trace, failed dispatch, red CI, or a runtime error during live pair work"
- `SKILL.md:37`: "a stack trace, failed dispatch, red CI, or an `:rf.error/*` event fired during live re-frame2-pair work"
- `spec/design.md:106` and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:55` repeat "red CI".

But `SKILL.md:72` (§Session evidence): "**Exclude unrelated activity.** Background workers, CI runs, shell commands, code-review threads, and app-authoring edits are out of scope unless the user explicitly names one as pair-session friction."

## TRUTH AT TIP

A CI run is not something a pair tool raises, and the family disqualifier `skills/README.md:166` puts "post-mortems on shell sessions, IDE workflows, or test-suite runs" out of scope. What the pair tools DO raise, and what a post-error offer should recognise:

- `{:ok? false :reason <kw>}` envelopes — the discover-app ladder `:nrepl-unreachable` / `:build-not-running` / `:no-runtime-connected` / `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/probe.cljs:302-310`), `:ambiguous-frame` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:173`), `:restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`), `:reset-rejected` (`tools/replace_app_db.cljs:114`), `:missing-baseline` / `:baseline-without-probe` (`tools/tail_build.cljs:148,172`), `:debug-disabled` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:8`).
- Error trace ops — `:rf.error/*` (`errors.md:43-47`, e.g. `:rf.error/handler-exception`) and the seven `restore-epoch!` failure ops (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126`, six `:rf.epoch/restore-*` plus `:rf.error/no-such-handler` kind `:frame`).

The existing evals already model the boundary correctly (ids 4, 17, 18 positive; id 19 "wants it FIXED" negative) and none uses CI.

## IMPACT

The trigger admits an input (a red CI run) that the skill's own evidence rules then discard, so the offer fires with nothing to retro; and it gives the agent no vocabulary for the failures that SHOULD fire it — a refused write or a ladder miss looks like "ordinary pair operation" under the current wording, so the post-error offer under-fires exactly where pair friction is densest.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR: drop "red CI" from the four sites and define (b) in one clause — "a pair tool returned `:ok? false` with a `:reason`, or an `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/restore-*` trace fired, during live re-frame2-pair work" — without restating the reason catalogue (that is the pair skill's errors.md). Keep "stack trace" (a handler exception is a runtime error). No evals change required; re-score ids 4, 17, 18, 19 by reading.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py` (description edited; evals untouched) and `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` (SKILL.md re-read). Prose by hand.

## ACCEPTANCE

No occurrence of "red CI" under `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/`; trigger (b) names the `:ok? false`/`:reason` envelope and the `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/restore-*` trace families; §Session evidence :72 unchanged; both gates exit 0.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): known-frictions.md proposes as improvements five behaviours the 29-tool catalogue already ships (operating-frame trio, discover-app :debug-enabled?, restore-epoch refusal, stream prose, errors recipe)
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` — the on-demand leaf SKILL.md:81 tells the retro to consult so "a match raises the finding's priority" — lists, under "Typical improvements", behaviours the current 29-tool Pair-MCP catalogue already ships:

1. §Frame ambiguity :91-94 — "require an explicit `:frame` opt where ambiguity is possible, or surface the implicit choice prominently in the result" / "list `(rf/frame-ids)` and recently-active frames at session start".
2. §Wrong listener for the question :106 — "short prose in SKILL.md naming the two streams and when each wins".
3. §Time-travel restore failures :116-118 — "structured presentation of the seven named failure modes ... with a next-best-action per mode" / "preflight check before restore" / "surface `:history-size` and `:schema-digest-recorded`/`:current` in the tool's output".
4. §Production-elision confusion :130-131 — "preflight check that reads `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` and reports the answer" / "make 'I am attached to a production-elided build' a first-class result state".
5. §Error observability :147 — "prefer a recipe over a doc paragraph when the friction is 'I didn't know how to pull recent errors at the REPL'".

## TRUTH AT TIP

Registry: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs` — 29 `:name` entries, including `get-operating-frame`, `set-operating-frame`, `reset-operating-frame`, `discover-app`, `restore-epoch`, `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`.

1. Frame: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:169-173` — the four-tier operating-frame cascade; "every other frame-targeted op refuses with `:ambiguous-frame` rather than guess"; `discover-app` returns `:frames [...]` (descriptors_data.cljs:186). The "explicit `:frame` or surface the choice" improvement IS the shipped design.
2. Streams: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:216` — "Use the assembled epoch stream by default; reach for the raw trace stream when you need detail the projection drops." The prose already exists.
3. Restore: the dedicated `restore-epoch` tool returns a structured refusal `:reason :restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`); the seven failure ops and their `:tags` (`:history-size`, `:schema-digest-recorded`, `:schema-digest-current`) are pinned at `spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126`.
4. Elision: `tools/discover_app.cljs:191-194` — `discover-app` returns `:debug-enabled?` and a hint "re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? is false ..." (descriptors_data.cljs:186 shows `:debug-enabled? true` in the example result). The preflight exists.

## IMPACT

A retro that pattern-matches a session onto one of these classes is told to propose, as the "smallest credible product change", a surface that already ships — and §Issue drafts then emits a draft asking `day8/re-frame2` for it. That is the wrong owner AND the wrong finding: when the session had `discover-app`'s `:debug-enabled?` or the operating-frame trio available and did not reach for them, the friction is discoverability in the pair skill's wording/recipes (tool-shaped), not a missing surface. One PR against `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` only. Do not grow the leaf: it is 195 lines / 12.7 KB against the 250 / 16 KB ceiling.

No gate — verify by hand: every tool named must appear in the `descriptors_data.cljs` `:name` list; every pair-skill line cited must exist at the PR's merge-base. `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` (reads SKILL.md only) stays green as a smoke.

title: surface-review(reagent-adapter): give SPAs one reusable adapter-owned client root
description:
## Scope

The stock Reagent adapter's browser-root surface: `implementation/adapters/reagent/**`, the shared ratom-spine root machinery only where needed, the Spec 006/public API contract, and the Reagent boot paths in the canonical guide, adapter testbed, examples, and generated templates. Preserve the canonical-namespace parity promised by the published full and slim Reagent artefacts.

## Verified Findings

- `re-frame.adapter.reagent` exposes exactly `adapter`, `flush-views!`, and `set-hiccup-emitter!`; there is no app-facing mount/root lifecycle. Spec 006 nevertheless calls adapter `:render` the client-side mount entry point, and core implements it only at `re-frame.substrate.adapter/render`, not on the documented front porch.
- The ratom spine already does the hard work: first render can call `create-root` or `hydrate-root`, it tracks the resulting React Root, and adapter disposal drains tracked roots. But the operation returns only an unmount thunk. It cannot render a new tree through that same root, so it cannot express the ordinary Shadow hot-reload loop.
- Consequently, normal applications bypass the adapter lifecycle. The boot guide, generated Reagent templates, examples, and the adapter's own browser testbed each retain a raw React Root and call `reagent.dom.client` directly. Those roots are invisible to `destroy-adapter!`, and every caller must independently get create-once, hydrate-once, rerender, and teardown ordering right.
- The SSR template makes the missing operation especially clear: `init` chooses `hydrate-root` versus `create-root`, stores the raw root, and its `^:dev/after-load` hook later calls `rdc/render` on that root. The existing one-shot adapter entry cannot replace this correct hot-reload shape.
- Spec 006 requires the returned unmount function to be idempotent, but `track-active-root!` removes the root from its set and invokes the underlying unmount operation on every call; a second call reaches React again.

## Recommended Action

Give the canonical Reagent adapter namespace one small, explicit, reusable client-root lifecycle. A caller should be able to allocate an inert root handle at namespace load, render through it repeatedly, and unmount it explicitly:

1. the first render creates or hydrates exactly one React Root from the supplied mount point and options;
2. later renders update that same Root, which makes the same call usable from `^:dev/after-load` without caller-owned raw React state;
3. explicit unmount is idempotent, and `destroy-adapter!` releases a still-live root exactly once;
4. the raw React Root remains private to the adapter.

Back the handle with the existing active-root ownership rather than adding a second lifecycle. Keep the handle caller-owned and explicit; do not introduce a process-global mount-point registry. Name the operations plainly and document the tiny boot recipe. Full Reagent and the published slim variant must present the same canonical namespace surface.

Migrate the canonical guide, generated Reagent templates (including SSR), the adapter browser testbed, and ordinary Reagent example entrypoints to this lifecycle. After the sweep, direct `reagent.dom.client` root bookkeeping should remain only in the adapter implementation, focused lower-level DOM tests, or integrations that intentionally own a foreign React root.

## Evidence

- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.reagent.md` says requiring the namespace gives exactly three things and documents no mount operation.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:227-239` defines `(render render-tree mount-point opts) -> unmount-fn` as the client mount contract and requires idempotent unmount.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:605-613` implements the entry only in the substrate namespace; no `re-frame.core` export exists.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3432-3448` creates/hydrates and tracks a Root but exposes only the unmount thunk. `:987-1000` shows that thunk calls the underlying unmount on every invocation.
- `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:39-60` teaches `defonce react-root`, `rdc/create-root`, and `rdc/render`.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:41-49` repeats that bookkeeping. `_reagent/core_with_ssr.cljc:146-162,183-209` stores a raw hydrated/created root specifically so hot reload can rerender it.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/testbed/adapter_testbed_reagent/core.cljs:57-72` bypasses adapter `:render` in the adapter's own end-to-end mount smoke.
- A repository census finds 30 files under `examples/` and `tools/template/resources/` containing `rdc/create-root`.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn` deliberately keeps Reagent 2.0.1 in the adapter artefact and out of core, so the Reagent-specific handle belongs at the adapter boundary without adding a Reagent dependency to core.
- History shows the split accreting: `16ec884492` established the one-shot create-root/render/unmount adapter path; `cd6cf3ebf8` added adapter-owned root draining; `9cf8f2e54c` fixed generated-app hot reload by rerendering caller-owned raw roots instead of extending the adapter surface.
- Duplicate search: `bd search` over `reagent mount`, `client mount`, `root lifecycle`, `adapter-owned root`, `create-root`, `rerender root`, and `reusable root` found no matching open or closed task for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical Reagent adapter API provides a documented caller-owned client-root handle (or an equivalently small explicit lifecycle) that performs no DOM work when constructed.
- Browser contract tests prove: a cold first render calls `create-root` once; a hydrating first render calls `hydrate-root` once; two or more later renders reuse the identical Root and call neither constructor again; a hydrated root is updated with normal render rather than hydrated again.
- Calling explicit unmount more than once invokes the underlying React unmount once. Destroying the adapter releases every still-live handle once, while an already-unmounted handle is not released again.
- Normal boot requires no caller-owned raw React Root or create/hydrate branch. The core boot guide, adapter testbed, generated Reagent templates, and ordinary Reagent example entrypoints use the canonical lifecycle; the SSR template still hydrates exactly once and hot reload still rerenders without reseeding app state.
- The full and published slim Reagent variants expose the same canonical namespace API and behavior; public API docs and Spec 006 describe ownership, update, hydration, and teardown semantics.
- Focused low-level tests and deliberate foreign-root integrations may keep direct `reagent.dom.client` calls, but remaining occurrences are reviewed and explicitly outside the normal app boot path.

## Non-goals

- No implicit default adapter, implicit frame creation, automatic DOM-id lookup, or auto-mount on namespace load.
- No process-global root registry and no exposure of the substrate's raw React Root.
- No Reagent 1 or React 17/18 compatibility path.
- No redesign of `reg-view`, Form-3 component authoring, subscriptions, or render-flush helpers.
- No requirement to rewrite focused DOM tests whose subject is raw React/Reagent behavior.

## Related beads

- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed) fixed Shadow hot reload by adding `^:dev/after-load` rerenders; this task keeps that behavior while moving root ownership behind the adapter.
