title: Clojars verified-group policy blocks the FIRST publish of every day8/re-frame2-* tool coordinate
description:
Surfaced by rf2-2ii52 (ruling caveat, deliberately not solved inside the vendoring PR).

Vendoring day8/de-dupe fixed the DEPENDENCY GRAPH for day8/re-frame2-mcp-base and
day8/re-frame2-story-mcp — both now generate a complete pom, and PR #7169 wires their
deploy jobs onto the existing story-v* glob. It did NOT make the coordinates CLAIMABLE.

THE POLICY. Clojars requires NEW projects to live in a *verified* group, and verification
requires a reverse-domain group name. `day8` is not reverse-domain, so it cannot be
verified. Existing projects in an old group may publish new versions; a NEW project may
not be created. This is not theoretical: day8/de-dupe's own tag-triggered publish workflow
ran on 2026-05-13 and received a 403 — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new
projects". That 403 is the reason route (a) (publish de-dupe) was ruled out.

THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TWO NEW JARS. The same rule applies to EVERY day8/re-frame2-*
coordinate that has never been published — which, as far as anyone has checked, is all of
them: the thirteen implementation/ artefacts as well as the five tool jars. If the day8
group cannot take new projects, then no v* tag can cut a first release either, and the
whole release pipeline is gated on this rather than on any code.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING (Mike's, not a worker's):
  1. Does day8's Clojars standing permit new projects today? (An older group may have been
     grandfathered, or the account may hold a verified group already — VERIFY against
     Clojars rather than inferring from the 2026-05-13 403, which was a different group
     path.) If yes, nothing to do: tag and publish.
  2. If no: the artefacts need a verified reverse-domain group — io.github.day8/* is the
     obvious candidate, verifiable via the GitHub org. That renames EVERY published
     coordinate, which touches deps.edn :clein/build :lib for 18 artefacts, the lockstep
     gate, every release workflow's rewrite + preflight, docs/release-process.md, the
     template's pins, CHANGELOG, and every consumer-facing usage snippet in the repo.

VERIFY BEFORE TAGGING ANYTHING. Clojars has no yank, and a half-published set at a given
VERSION is recovered only by bump-and-supersede.

Flagged in .github/workflows/release-story.yml's header and docs/release-process.md
\u00a7How story-mcp and mcp-base got their publish path.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): recorded 2026-07-28 07:48 AUSEST from ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-verified-group.md (primary analysis + independent Codex second opinion, reconciled; the dossier file is deleted after this note — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD).

DECISION, in three parts:
(1) VERIFICATION-FIRST SEQUENCING STANDS, but the canary-by-tag route is REJECTED as the verification instrument (Codex position, adopted). Mike's authoritative act is the zero-mutation one: verify io.github.day8 via Clojars' self-service GitHub-org proof (see MIKE'S ACT below), optionally glancing at day8's standing from his logged-in account or asking Clojars support as belt-and-braces.
(2) RULED FALLBACK GROUP if day8 is blocked (and the evidence below says it is): io.github.day8 for ALL 18 Maven coordinates, moved in ONE sequenced rename campaign BEFORE anything publishes.
(3) NO-TAG RULE: NO v*, story-v*, xray-v*, or machines-viz-v* tag is pushed until this bead resolves (io.github.day8 badge confirmed + rename campaign merged + lockstep/preflight/release-DAG gates green on the new coordinates). This is STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut-time checklist, ahead of its existing step 1 (credentials); rf2-2ii52 step 3 (manual first publish of mcp-base/story-mcp) is equally blocked on it.

EVIDENCE AND ITS LIMITS (three independent sources; two re-verified from primary sources 2026-07-28):
- The 2026-05-13 403 on day8/de-dupe's tag-triggered publish — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new projects" — is real but was a DIFFERENT project path; on its own it is suggestive, not conclusive (the bead itself warns against inferring from it alone).
- Clojars' Verified Group Names wiki (fetched 2026-07-28): since 2021-04-18 "creating new libraries in non-verified groups will be disabled", while "the group does not need to be verified for new versions" of EXISTING libraries. Bare `day8` is neither reverse-domain nor a githost-org pattern, so it is STRUCTURALLY UNVERIFIABLE — there is no route to a verified bare day8, and seeking a policy exception would couple every release to an exception Clojars explicitly designed away.
- clojars.org/users/mikethompson (fetched 2026-07-28): `day8` is listed WITHOUT the verified badge; only net.clojars.mikethompson and org.clojars.mikethompson carry it. Codex traced the badge to find-group-verification in clojars-web's web/user.clj (not cosmetic) and the enforcement to check-group+project in db.clj: an unverified group is accepted ONLY when that exact group/artifact pair already exists; a new artifact is rejected as group-non-verified.
- All 18 intended day8/* coordinates 404 on Clojars (re-verified 2026-07-27, per-coordinate) — every one is a NEW project as far as Clojars is concerned, so every one enters the rejected branch. The day8 group page returning 200 with mikethompson permitted proves only maintenance rights over existing projects, not creation rights.
- LIMIT: what stays unobservable read-only is Mike's account-side view and any bespoke admin exception. That residual is why this bead stays with Mike — but it is small, and it does not justify a canary.

VERIFICATION ROUTES WEIGHED (canary trade-offs recorded):
- (a) Account/settings check or asking Clojars admins: zero-risk, zero-mutation. Fine as belt-and-braces; not required given (c).
- (b) Canary publish by pushing the ready machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha tag: REJECTED as a probe. A 403 merely re-demonstrates documented policy at the cost of a burned tag-push cycle; a surprise success is an IMMUTABLE public act that permanently pins machines-viz to day8/* — either splitting the family when the rest moves, or accidentally committing the whole family to an unverifiable legacy group. Never use an immutable registry operation to learn an observable fact; if state might have changed, re-read the profile/API or ask support instead. (The primary analysis's "nothing is wasted on success" framing undercounts this: success is exactly the outcome that forecloses the group decision.)
- (c) The act that actually advances things — verify io.github.day8 NOW: create the empty public repo github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson, submit its URL at clojars.org/verify/group while logged in as mikethompson, confirm the badge appears. Cheap, self-service, and harmless even in the unlikely event day8 turns out grandfathered (verifying a group publishes nothing). It doubles as the authoritative test: Clojars' own flow granting io.github.day8 while day8 stays unverified closes the question.

FALLBACK GROUP CHOICE (io.github.day8), alternatives weighed:
- io.github.day8 — CHOSEN. GitHub-org-verifiable self-service; matches the existing in-repo precedent io.github.day8/re-frame2-template; expresses the durable owner users already see (the day8 GitHub org).
- com.github.day8 — the verification flow verifies both com. and io. simultaneously, but io. is the cleaner match to the existing precedent. Publish under ONE only — Clojars itself warns that the same library under two group IDs can put both on a classpath.
- au.com.day8 — DNS-TXT-verifiable via day8.com.au; defensible if Day8 deliberately wants DNS (not GitHub) as the permanent package identity, but it adds a separate DNS proof and stewardship path, has zero consumer precedent, and buys no ergonomics.
- net.clojars.mikethompson — already verified and usable today, but makes organisation-owned libraries look personally owned. Rejected.
- Policy exception for bare day8 — structurally impossible (not reverse-domain) and bad posture even if grantable. Rejected.

WHY DECIDE BEFORE FIRST PUBLISH (irreversibility): Clojars has no yank; a deployed non-SNAPSHOT version is immutable. Any rename AFTER a first publish leaves permanently orphaned day8/* coordinates and creates the two-groups-one-library classpath hazard. The current all-404 state — pre-alpha, zero consumers — is the cheapest this move will ever be.

RENAME BLAST RADIUS (one sequenced hot-zone campaign, NOT parallel work; coordinate work ONLY):
- :clein/build :lib in all 18 publishable deps.edn (13 implementation/ + 5 tools/), plus the internal cross-artefact dependency maps the :local/root rewrite resolves (31 in-repo coordinates inventoried by the lockstep gate).
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh (inventories + assertions).
- Release workflows and their scripts: release.yml (13-coordinate DAG + generated-POM assertions), release-story.yml (mcp-base -> story -> story-mcp ordering), release-machines-viz.yml, .github/scripts/rewrite-in-repo-coords.sh, preflight-tool-package.sh, preflight-story-package.sh.
- docs/release-process.md; CHANGELOG (its roster is gate-pinned to the publishable-runtimes authority); migration guide dep edits; every consumer-facing usage snippet; the setup skill; the template's emitted coordinates (tools/template — interacts with rf2-57bjg, whose template-coordinate fix should land on the NEW group).
- The pre-staged rf2-snjn5 docs-flip PR #7167 (8 sites teaching day8/* coords) must be RE-CUT on the new group.
- day8/reagent-slim — the one deliberately off-pattern coordinate (publication-time rename) — becomes io.github.day8/reagent-slim; give it its final eyeball in the same pass.
- Credentials: the planned group-scoped reusable Clojars deploy token must be scoped to io.github.day8, not day8 (rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist step 1 wording changes accordingly).
- EXPLICIT NON-SCOPE (Clojars documents that the Maven group does not constrain Clojure namespaces): NO Clojure namespace renames, NO repo URL changes, NO npm @day8 scope change.

INTERACTIONS: this bead is now STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut checklist (cross-ref appended there) — its steps 3 (404 re-probe: probe the NEW coordinates), 4/6 (PR #7167 re-cut) and 1 (token group scope) all shift under this ruling. rf2-2ii52's remaining step 3 (manual first publish per release-machines-viz.yml's header protocol) proceeds only after this resolves, on io.github.day8 coordinates.

MIKE'S ACT (why this stays OPEN and assigned to him): 1. create the empty public repo day8/clojars-mikethompson; 2. submit https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson at clojars.org/verify/group as mikethompson; 3. confirm io.github.day8 shows the verified badge (optionally also glance at day8's standing / ask support); 4. say go — the rename campaign is then worker-dispatchable as one sequenced campaign, and this bead closes when the badge is confirmed AND the campaign is merged with gates green.
RUNBOOK CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-28): Codex second-opinion review of the operator runbook (ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-group-verification.md, written 2026-07-28 16:36 AUSEST) CONCURS with the morning RULING on every decision point — io.github.day8 destination, canary-by-tag rejected, no-tag rule, verification-first sequencing, and the group-alternatives weighing all match. No contradictions; this is a consolidation, not a re-ruling. It adds the following NEW verified mechanics the ruling did not yet carry. The dossier file is deleted after this note — this note is the canonical record of its Codex section.

(1) VERIFY-FORM MECHANICS (verified against clojars-web verification.clj, 2026-07-28): the clojars.org/verify/group flow's GitHub/GitLab repository section takes the FULL proof-repo URL (https://github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson) — the form does NOT ask for the group name. It accepts exactly https://github.com/<org>/clojars-<clojars-user>, checks the public repo exists, and creates/verifies BOTH com.github.day8 AND io.github.day8 in one act. Publish under io.github.day8 as the ONE public Maven identity (per the ruling; never both). KEEP THE PROOF REPO PUBLIC PERMANENTLY — it is the standing evidence of org control, not a one-shot token. (As of the 2026-07-28 check, github.com/day8/clojars-mikethompson returned 404 — the verification act has not yet happened.)

(2) TOKEN ORDER (inserts a step between MIKE'S ACT and the rf2-vxgfnd.99 checklist's credentials step): create or replace the CI deploy token scoped to io.github.day8 only AFTER verification — Clojars does not allow a group-scoped token before the group exists (Deploy-Tokens wiki, Scoping). Verification usefully creates the group before any artifact exists, which is what makes the scoped token mintable at all. Sequence: badge confirmed -> mint io.github.day8-scoped token -> cut checklist step 1 (credentials) proceeds with that token, never a bare-day8-scoped one.

(3) ENFORCEMENT CONFIRMATION: current clojars-web db.clj check-group+project structurally confirms the ruling's reading — it first accepts an exact EXISTING group/artifact pair, then rejects a NEW artifact when the group has no verification record. Existing day8 projects therefore do NOT grandfather any new day8/re-frame2-* artifact.

(4) CAMPAIGN COMPLETION CRITERION (tightens the ruling's "gates green" close condition): a hand-written file roster is NOT a safe completion criterion — an exact-token scan (2026-07-28 snapshot) found ~428 candidate references to the 18 published coordinates across hundreds of tracked files, and the repo is still moving, so the count itself must not be relied on. Required instead: a structural re-scan at campaign START and again at COMPLETION; then generate and INSPECT all deploy POMs, proving every in-family GAV uses io.github.day8 at the lockstep version with NO old-group dependency (a partial migration can publish a valid jar whose POM points at an old-group coordinate that will never exist); plus verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test, the normal lockstep gate, the release-script policy tests, and each tool/package preflight — ALL green before the tag freeze lifts. Re-cut any staged documentation change (PR #7167) against the new group from the same structural inventory.

(5) COORDINATE-SPECIFIC FENCE (sharpens the ruling's explicit non-scope): NO repository-wide day8 -> io.github.day8 text replacement. GitHub org URLs, @day8 npm packages, Clojure namespace names, and ordinary prose about the Day8 organisation do not change. Any RETAINED legacy day8/* Maven coordinate must be an intentional historical example or negative test, and explicitly allowlisted as such.

(6) GROUP-ALTERNATIVES RECORD: Codex's independent weighing matches the ruling exactly — au.com.day8 defensible only as an explicit branding decision (adds DNS access/propagation/stewardship without solving anything the GitHub route leaves open); net.clojars.mikethompson rejected for org stewardship (org-owned libraries under a personal account); bare day8 / policy exception / publish canary all rejected. Recorded as concurrence.

Codex go/no-go, adopted as the operational phrasing of the ruling: go on verification now; go on the rename campaign as soon as the io.github.day8 badge is visible; no-go on every v*, story-v*, xray-v*, and machines-viz-v* tag until the migrated release graph and generated POMs are green.
FINAL CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-29): Codex Recommendation in the final revision of ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-group-verification.md (2026-07-28 23:02 AUSEST) CONCURS with the ruling and both prior consolidations on every point; its four-step path (verify -> badge + io.github.day8-scoped token -> one coordinate-only migration -> lockstep/preflight + structural old-coordinate scan + generated-POM inspection before the first tag) matches the bead's runbook exactly. 2. Badge on record -> mayor dispatches the campaign carrier rf2-fo4ng (created this pass; scope, fence, and Codex acceptance boundary carried there; HOLD line says do-not-dispatch until the badge is recorded here). The primary analysis's material insight, kept: the stop-boundary was built for the dormant era and its own release clause has been satisfied — the question "does Mike do the act" was never really open; the live question was the campaign, and the trigger answered it.

title: skill(reagent-migration): three leftover-Reagent failures, three ids — the render-time refusal seam (:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused) and the complaint shape are untaught
description:
## CLAIM

- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md:306-325` (MIG-26): "Under Hicasso an `h/sub` from an ordinary `defn` **is legal** ... What fails is a read or a dispatch with **no active render**: a timer, a callback the browser invokes later, a foreign listener." and "An ambient `rf/dispatch` from a callback raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — **core's id, not a `hicasso-*` one** — at click time."
- `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:104` (cardinal rule 2): "A converted `h/defview` has no ambient `subscribe`/`dispatch`, so a body with some sites rewritten and some not does not work." — states the law, never the diagnostic.
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:7-31`: only the click-time closure trap is taught. Every diagnostic id the skill names anywhere (grep over the package): `:rf.error/no-frame-context` x9, `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` x9, `hicasso-intent-needs-the-event`, `hicasso-intent-outside-boundary`, `hicasso-malformed-prevent`, `:rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key`, `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`. Neither `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` nor `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` appears in any file.
- Nothing in the skill says what a Hicasso complaint IS (the four ex-data slots) or where the index lives.

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:64-118` — `with-frame` binds `frame/*ambient-frame-refusal*` for the whole render extent "so ambient `rf/subscribe` and `rf/dispatch` refuse for the extent (HD-002 clause (a))"; the substrate's `:reason` names the recovery verbatim: "Read through the boundary's own collector (`sub`) ... and dispatch through an intent at a handler position ...".
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:595-601, 637-640` — that refusal surfaces as **`:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`**, "rather than the generic `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — a refused ambient read and a genuinely frameless one are different mistakes and must not share a diagnostic". `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1991` rows it; firing case "a Hicasso boundary body".
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:584` — `h/sub` invoked outside a body raises **`:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render`** (`implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:102`; guide `docs/core/hicasso/02-views-and-reads.md:241`, `16-diagnostics.md:158`).
- `implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:27-42` — every complaint is an `ex-info` whose `ex-data` carries four required slots: `:rf.error/id` (branch on this), `:where`, `:reason` (names the fix), `:recovery`; `:view`/`:source` are dev-only context. That file is the index; meaning per id is Spec 009 §Hicasso.

So the three commonest leftovers in a converted Reagent view map to three DIFFERENT ids at three DIFFERENT times:

| leftover | fails when | id |
|---|---|---|
| `@(rf/subscribe ...)` or `(rf/dispatch ...)` in a converted body, or in a helper `defn` it calls | at RENDER | `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` |
| `#(rf/dispatch ...)` closure surviving at an `:on-*` | at CLICK | `:rf.error/no-frame-context` |
| an `(h/sub ...)` moved into a callback / timer / promise | at FIRE | `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` |

## IMPACT

The skill teaches only row 2. An author who converts a view whose helper `defn` still derefs `rf/subscribe` — the most common shape in a Reagent codebase — gets `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` at FIRST RENDER, and the skill's text points them at a click-time / frameless problem with the wrong id. MIG-26's "if it runs during render, leave it in the helper — that is the supported shape" is true only once the helper reads through `h/sub`; the skill never says the helper is ALSO deref-dropped (MIG-02 reaches helpers). And the complaint catalogue with stable ids is a headline Hicasso feature; the skill hands the author no way to read one, so the `:reason` that names the fix goes unread.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill files only)

1. `references/gotchas.md` — extend the lead trap into "Three leftovers, three ids" with the table above, and add a short "Reading a complaint" paragraph: the four slots, branch on `:rf.error/id`, `:reason` names the fix, index at `implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md`, meaning in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Hicasso.
2. `references/catalog-judgment.md` MIG-26 — add the render-time arm: a leftover ambient `rf/subscribe`/`rf/dispatch` anywhere inside the render extent (body OR helper) refuses at render with `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`, whose reason names `h/sub` / an intent; deref-drop the helper too. Name `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` for the hoist-to-render-time case.
3. `SKILL.md` §Gotchas: one line pointing at the three ids. `evals/evals.json`: eval 17 (or a new M-tier eval) gains an expectation that distinguishes the render-time refusal id from the click-time one.

Keep it tight — one table and two paragraphs, not a catalogue restatement.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --ci` (all exit 0 at tip). The ids themselves are verified by hand against `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` rows and `implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md` — no gate reads prose; say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

The skill names all three ids with their timing; MIG-26 names `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` for the render-time ambient read and says helpers deref-drop too; gotchas.md teaches the four complaint slots and links the index; the three gates exit 0.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 (HEAD d12181c4c3; `git diff --stat 72df4dd915..HEAD -- skills/ implementation/hicasso/ docs/core/hicasso/` empty) on 2026-09-02 12:00:31 AUSEST.
acceptance_criteria: gotchas.md teaches render/click/fire = ambient-frame-refused / no-frame-context / hicasso-sub-outside-render plus the four complaint slots and the index; MIG-26 names the render-time id and says helpers deref-drop; doc_slugs, package_refs --ci, eval_docs --ci exit 0
close_reason: Done in PR #9008, commit 062387ba7d. gotchas.md's lead trap is now 'Three leftovers, three ids' with the render/click/fire table (ambient-frame-refused / no-frame-context / hicasso-sub-outside-render) plus a 'Reading a complaint' section teaching the four ex-data slots, branch-on-id, and the complaints.md + Spec 009 owners. MIG-26 gained the render-time arm and states the refusal extent reaches helpers, so MIG-02's deref-drop applies to them. SKILL.md routes to the three ids; eval 17 gained an expectation distinguishing the render-time id from the click-time one. All three ids verified by hand at source (frame.cljc payload builder + Spec 009:1991, impl/intent.cljs with-frame, impl/collector.cljs fail!, complaints.md:102). Table column counts hand-counted 3/3/3/3/3. doc_slugs, package_refs --ci, eval_docs --ci all exit 0 on the final rebased base.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): spec/ re-authoring triad still says shims are on disk, tests are smoke-only, and names hot-reload/wait + an unemitted connect reason
description:
## CLAIM

The re-authoring scaffolding under `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/` is labelled "exists to re-author the skill from inputs" (each file's banner). Four statements in it no longer describe the skill as shipped, and one contradicts a sibling sentence in the same file:

1. `spec/inputs.md:42` — "**Bash shims** — `skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts/*.sh`. Retired from the skill's tool surface …; **on disk only for the project's own e2e harness and ad-hoc shell use**."
2. `spec/design.md:274` (OQ3) — "`tests/` exists but **only carries connection smoke tests**."
3. `spec/design.md:105` — "the skill returns `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair` on connect."
4. `spec/design.md:156` (L4) and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:57` (cardinal rule 4) — "the AI **must** call `hot-reload/wait` before dispatching"; `design.md:251` "Skipping `hot-reload/wait`".
5. `spec/inputs.md:26` lists `register-epoch-listener!` among `re-frame.core`'s "public single-import API"; `authoring-prompt.md:51,55` and `design.md:138` use the same name as a facade surface.

## TRUTH AT TIP

1. `git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/e2e skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/shim` returns nothing — no `scripts/` dir exists; `tests/shim/` on disk is an untracked empty `target/` leftover. The same file says so eleven paragraphs later (`inputs.md:69` §7.5: "has been **removed**"), as do `design.md:161` (OQ1 "Resolved: yes, removed"), `docs/TESTING.md:5` and `docs/initial-spec.md:15-20`. §4 is the one surviving copy of the pre-removal wording.
2. `tests/` today: `fixture/` (a shadow-cljs counter app + the `:pure-test` node-test build with 27 deftests over the shipped `pure.cljc`), `runtime/` (12 Babashka AST pins), `prompts/` (prompt_regression_test.clj, ~25 deftests). `docs/TESTING.md` §1–3 describe all three. There are no "connection smoke tests".
3. `grep -rn 're-frame2-tool-pair' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload` returns nothing. The connect verdicts the server actually emits are the `discover-app` ladder in `tools/discover_app.cljs:25-26,193,207` (`:debug-disabled`, `:no-frames-registered`, `:build-not-running`, `:no-runtime-connected`, `:nrepl-unreachable`, `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing`), catalogued in `references/errors.md`.
4. There is no op named `hot-reload/wait` in `references/ops.md`; the protocol is `tail-build` with a pre-edit `baseline` (`ops.md:249-275`, post rf2-1f60u). The name is a pre-MCP placeholder the shipped catalogue never used.
5. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` has no `defn register-epoch-listener!`; the facade is the stream-parameterised `(rf/register-listener! :epoch id cb)` (`core.cljc:2158` dispatches to `rf-epoch/register-epoch-listener!` on the epoch artefact). `SKILL.md:79` and `design.md:137` (L1) already state the facade form correctly — the `register-epoch-listener!` mentions are the older name surviving beside it.

`python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py --verbose` is green on all of this (it scans for retired tool/transport *names*, and none of these five is on its list).

## IMPACT

authoring-prompt.md is a one-shot "drop into a fresh session and it produces the skill" prompt. A re-author following it would (1) go looking for `scripts/*.sh` to keep "on disk for the e2e harness", (2) treat `tests/` as smoke-only and not know the pure-core node-test and AST pins are the behaviour + wiring gates, (3) teach a connect reason the server never emits, (4) teach an op name that does not exist instead of `tail-build` + baseline, (5) cite a facade fn that does not exist. Each is a P3 "historical claim not labelled historical" — here it is worse than initial-spec.md because these files are NOT labelled historical; they are labelled as the current re-authoring inputs.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR, three files, prose only:
- `inputs.md:42` — replace the bullet with the §7.5 wording (removed; MCP is the one implementation; live coverage in `live-e2e-fixture.cjs`), or delete it and let §7.5 stand.
- `inputs.md:26` — move `register-epoch-listener!` off the core.cljc list; name `(rf/register-listener! :epoch …)` as the facade form (matching L1 in design.md:137).
- `design.md:105` — cite the real ladder (`references/errors.md`) instead of `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair`.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): LOCAL_DEV.md troubleshooting describes a port-discovery mechanism the server does not have (mtime pick, implementation/ scan)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/LOCAL_DEV.md:153` (§Troubleshooting → "`discover-app` can't find the nREPL"):

> The MCP server discovers the port automatically (it scans `target/shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`, `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`, `.nrepl-port` at the CWD and under `implementation/`, and picks the most-recently-modified one).

## TRUTH AT TIP

`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs` (`discover-port*` docstring, :123-175) and `server.cljs:18-35`: discovery is a **five-step cascade** — (1) `--port-file`, (2) `$SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT`, (3) MCP `roots/list` workspace walk for `shadow-cljs.edn` + adjacent port file (one hit attaches; several → `elicitation/create`; `roots_discovery.cljs:79` skips `node_modules` / `.git` / `.shadow-cljs` / `target` / `out` / `.cpcache`), (4) shadow HTTP probe `GET :9630/api/project-info` → `:project-home`, (5) CWD-relative scan of the three candidates in fixed order (`nrepl.cljs:48-50`, `(some read-port-file port-file-candidates)` — **first hit wins**).

- There is no modification-time comparison anywhere in the server: `grep -rnE 'mtime|lastModified|statSync' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src` returns nothing. "picks the most-recently-modified one" is invented.
- There is no cwd scan "under `implementation/`". The only `implementation/` mention is `roots_discovery.cljs:23,59` — the roots walk (step 3) treats `<root>/implementation/` as a typical `shadow-cljs.edn` location. The sentence conflates the roots walk with the cwd scan.
- The sentence omits the two paths that actually resolve most sessions (steps 3 and 4), so an operator reading this section when discovery misses will look at the wrong thing (port-file mtimes) instead of the right ones (is the workspace root exposed via `roots/list`; is shadow's HTTP server on 9630 or does `--http-port` need setting).

The skill's own transport leaf has the correct description at `references/mcp-transport.md:38-47` (five steps, in order, with the restart-absorption note).

## IMPACT

Wrong mental model in the one place an operator goes when attach fails. The `--port-file` / `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` override advice in the next paragraph (:161) is still correct, so the operator can escape — but only by skipping the diagnosis the section pretends to give.

## FIX SHAPE

Replace the parenthetical at `docs/LOCAL_DEV.md:153` with a one-sentence pointer: "The MCP server discovers the port through a five-step cascade (`--port-file` → `$SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` → MCP `roots/list` walk → shadow HTTP probe → cwd scan) — see [`references/mcp-transport.md` §Install / configure](../references/mcp-transport.md#install--configure-one-time)." Do not restate the cascade; the transport leaf is the single source. While there, the same section's :161 mention of `--port-file` / `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` is correct and stays.

## GATE

No gate covers this prose. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates the new relative link + anchor (skills/ is in its roots). Verify the cascade wording by hand against `nrepl.cljs` `discover-port*` and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`docs/LOCAL_DEV.md` no longer claims an mtime pick or an `implementation/` cwd scan; its discovery sentence names the five-step cascade (or links to mcp-transport.md's description); `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 on 2026-09-02 11:04:06 AUSEST (skills review, partition B).
acceptance_criteria: LOCAL_DEV.md no longer claims an mtime pick or implementation/ cwd scan and names/links the five-step cascade in mcp-transport.md; check_doc_slugs.py green
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9007 (commit 2c389e03a4, rebased 75765280c4). docs/LOCAL_DEV.md's discovery sentence (line 152, not the cited 153) no longer claims an mtime pick or an implementation/ cwd scan. It now names the five-step cascade in precedence order and links to references/mcp-transport.md #install--configure-one-time as the single source, then points the operator at steps 3-4 -- the two that resolve most sessions -- instead of at port-file mtimes. Verified by hand against nrepl.cljs discover-port* (five-step precedence; step 5 is (some read-port-file port-file-candidates), first hit wins) and roots_discovery.cljs (the only implementation/ mention, and it is the step-3 roots walk). No mtime comparison exists in the server: mtime|lastModified|statSync|birthtime returns 0 hits, control readFileSync returns 8. check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, and proven to read this worktree by a planted broken anchor on this very link (went exit 1 naming it; restored, blob hash verified).

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): mcp-transport.md dispatch-dry-run row advertises fx-overrides (schema-absent, runtime-refused) and omits cofx
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md:90` (the "MCP tool reference (args)" table — the transport index the drift gate cross-checks):

> | `dispatch-dry-run` | `{event, frame?, fx-overrides?}` — simulate WITHOUT committing; not `--allow-writes`-gated | [`ops.md` §Write](ops.md#write) |

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs` — the `dispatch-dry-run` descriptor's `inputSchema` properties are `event, frame, cofx, elision, include-sensitive, include-fx-args, build` with `:additionalProperties false`. There is no `fx-overrides` property.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch_dry_run.cljs:93-100` ("## Rejects fx-overrides"): a caller `:fx-overrides` is REJECTED loudly with `:reason :fx-overrides-unsupported` (isError); `fx-overrides-rejected` at :132.
- The skill's own semantics home already says so: `references/ops.md:79` — "A caller `:fx-overrides` is **rejected** (`:reason :fx-overrides-unsupported`)". `tests/runtime/dry_run_sink_pin_test.clj` (`dispatch-dry-run-rejects-caller-fx-overrides`) pins the refusal in the preload.
- `cofx` IS accepted on dry-run (descriptor + `dispatch_dry_run.cljs`), and the fixture's `:counter/stamp` event exists precisely for scripted-cofx dispatches — the transport row omits it.

## IMPACT

The two leaves contradict each other on one tool: the transport index advertises `fx-overrides?` as an accepted arg while the semantics leaf and the server refuse it. An agent composing a dry-run from the arg table gets an isError round-trip it did not expect; an agent wanting a reproducible dry-run cannot see from the index that `cofx` is available. Low blast radius (the `tools/list` descriptor is what the agent sees at call time, and it is right) — hence P3, not P2 — but it is a one-line contradiction inside the skill's own contract, on the one table the family README calls "complete by gate".

## FIX SHAPE

One row in `references/mcp-transport.md`: `{event, frame?, cofx?}` — and keep the row's existing "not `--allow-writes`-gated" note. Optionally add "(a caller `fx-overrides` is refused — see ops.md §Write)". No other file.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose` (doc-coverage axis: the row must still be present, 29 = 29). No gate reads the arg-signature column — verify the new signature by hand against the descriptor's `:properties` in `descriptors_data.cljs`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`references/mcp-transport.md`'s `dispatch-dry-run` row lists no `fx-overrides` arg and does list `cofx`; `check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose` exits 0 with `doc=29 rows`.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 on 2026-09-02 11:04:06 AUSEST (skills review, partition B).
acceptance_criteria: mcp-transport.md dispatch-dry-run row lists no fx-overrides arg and does list cofx; check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose exits 0 with doc=29 rows
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9007 (commit a81ba8d566, rebased 75765280c4). references/mcp-transport.md's dispatch-dry-run row now reads {event, frame?, cofx?} and names the refusal, keeping the 'not --allow-writes-gated' note. Verified by hand against descriptors_data.cljs (inputSchema properties: event, frame, cofx, elision, include-sensitive, include-fx-args, build; :required [event]; :additionalProperties false; no fx-overrides) and dispatch_dry_run.cljs (fx-overrides-rejected carries :reason :fx-overrides-unsupported as an isError). check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose exit 0. NOTE: the acceptance text's 'doc=29 rows' was stale -- the tool count moved to 30 when replay-epoch landed; the gate now reports server=30 tools, doc=30 rows, so the invariant (doc rows == server tools) holds. Clojars has never seen. A :hicasso scaffold emitted before then hands a new

Split off rf2-48rk3, which implemented that bead's OTHER ground (the two-value
substrate idiom) and is closed. The blocking work it left is only this.

RULING 2026-09-02 10:24:53 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-02, dossier review; ai/decisions/rf2-8urba.template-hicasso-variant-axis.md folded here and deleted — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). Ruled at tip 102558e1b3. AXIS RULED — the "wants a ruling before code" hold in the description is discharged; the TAG GATE (first v* tag, rf2-kmqx3) still stands, and so does the sequencing behind rf2-zq34m recorded below.

DECISION — OPTION A. The template keeps exactly ONE template-specific selector, :substrate, and Hicasso becomes its THIRD VALUE. A user writes `:substrate :hicasso` (beside the existing `:reagent` default and `:uix`); no second selector (no :views, no :authoring, no :adapter key) is added, now or later, to express Hicasso-over-a-foreign-adapter — that pairing stays a documented recipe (docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md's adapter section plus the use-uix-or-slim how-to), not a scaffold cell. Reagent stays the default. What the variant emits, on the collapsed rf2-zq34m shape: the three per-substrate files, and nothing else diverges — `_hicasso/deps.edn` (ONE view coordinate: the published re-frame2-hicasso artefact at {{rf2-version}}; core and ssr arrive transitively through its published :deps; NO re-frame2-uix, NO uix npm/clj pins), `_hicasso/core.cljs` (boot with Hicasso's OWN adapter: `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` from `re-frame.hicasso.substrate`, then `(h/mount! el {:frame :rf/default :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]} [views/counter-app])` with the handle retained in a defonce atom, and a `^:dev/after-load` that calls `(h/render! @!root [views/counter-app])`), and `_hicasso/views.cljs` (`h/defview` + `h/sub` + intent vectors at :on-click — hiccup, no hooks, no `$`). The shared files (events.cljs, subs.cljs, the shell, package.json, shadow-cljs.edn, README, the focused event-flow test) are substrate-invariant and stay shared; the substrate-registry entry declares every surviving capability key false (`:xray? false`, and `:story? false :ssr? false` for as long as those keys exist — zq34m is expected to delete the latter two with the flags they serve). Sequencing is part of the decision, not advice: this lands (1) AFTER rf2-zq34m's collapse has merged, on the collapsed shape, and (2) AFTER the first v* tag has made the Hicasso coordinate resolve from a clean consumer. The rf2-kmqx3 edge enforces the second mechanically; the first is a sequencing instruction to whoever dispatches, because both PRs touch the tools/template/** fence and zq34m explicitly excludes Hicasso from its own diff.

HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED. Two voices in the dossier, and they agree on the axis; the ruling adopts both and records where each was sharper.

Dossier author (sections "Summary", "The problem, carefully and fully", "Options", "Recommendation"): A, folded into the zq34m act. Its load-bearing argument is that the bead's premise ("Hicasso mints no adapter") died on 2026-08-18 with rf2-hvr5h, so Hicasso now has its own coordinate, its own canonical :rf.adapter/hicasso, and its own shape for all three per-substrate files — a peer of Reagent and UIx on the axis the template already has. Its rejection of B (dead as motivated; what B now buys is expressiveness for a migration/mixing pairing no greenfield scaffold should ask about; contradicts zq34m's "exactly one selector" the day it lands), of C-permanent (honest today, but makes the native view layer the one substrate a newcomer must hand-build, and silently converts the bead into a wontfix nothing in the record supports), and of D-now (zq34m keeps Reagent deliberately; the pilot programme rf2-hic-063 has not run; it would reopen a P1 on zero evidence) is adopted as written. Its three premise corrections (adapter, deps.edn shape, boot model) are confirmed at tip in the next section.

Reviewer (section "Codex Recommendation"): also A, keep the Reagent default, no second selector — and it is the sharper half on four points, all adopted. (i) Terminology: spec/006 §9-13 defines substrate as the abstract contract and adapter as its implementation, and the install chapter says "Hicasso is a view layer, not a substrate" — but the template's :substrate is already operationally a STARTER-STACK selector (notation + adapter + boot code + deps as one bundle), so `:substrate :hicasso` is a consistent extension of the key's existing meaning; the docs must say so plainly and link the foreign-adapter recipe rather than pretend the key is a taxonomy. (ii) Asymmetry: an :authoring × :adapter matrix is not a symmetric product — Reagent deref and UIx hooks are adapter-specific authoring contracts, and Hicasso is the ONE layer designed to run over a foreign adapter — so a second selector buys invalid-cell rules and asymmetric docs for an advanced interop case; adopted as the reason B stays rejected even after zq34m lands. (iii) Precondition: a v* tag is a TRIGGER, not sufficient evidence — the acceptance check is that the exact group/artifact/version the emitted deps.edn will carry resolves from OUTSIDE this checkout, and the group may be io.github.day8 (rf2-uelji; rf2-kmqx3's own title), so nothing in this variant hard-codes `day8/` from this note. (iv) Runner trap: emitted_test_run_test.clj's local-root rewrite derives the adapter root as `implementation/adapters/<substrate>`, which is wrong for Hicasso (`implementation/hicasso`), so the string convention is replaced with an explicit coordinate-to-local-root map BEFORE the cell is added — adopted as a hard requirement, since the alternative is a smoke that silently tests the wrong package. Its risk list (public-surface permanence, Xray capability asymmetry, naming ambiguity) is recorded; its remedy — keep optional tools OUT of the base scaffold rather than add a selector — is the direction zq34m already takes.

Disagreements: none on the axis. One difference of emphasis, preserved: the dossier author wanted this folded into the zq34m ruling so the two beads could not settle the selector count differently; the reviewer treated the collapse purely as a sequencing precondition. Ruled HERE, on this bead, as the canonical record, with a one-paragraph cross-reference appended to rf2-zq34m — which achieves the author's consistency goal without making this bead's answer live on another bead. Dissent to preserve from the bead's original author: they were right that the emitted-app divergence is variant-shaped (all three files change) and right to withhold the axis until ruled; the only thing that changed between 2026-08-16 and today is the tree.
PREMISE CORRECTIONS AT TIP (102558e1b3, 2026-09-02 10:24:53 AUSEST). A worker briefed from the description alone would build three things wrong; brief from these instead.

1. THE ADAPTER EXISTS. The description says ":rf.adapter/hicasso exists nowhere" and ":xray? false is CORRECT because Hicasso rides the UIx adapter". Both false since 4cb9e16951 (2026-08-18, rf2-hvr5h): `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:137-160` defines `adapter` via `spine/make-react-adapter` with `{:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso :frame-provider frame-provider}`; `spec/Conventions.md:103` rosters :rf.adapter/hicasso as a canonical :rf.adapter/* member; spec/API.md:863 and spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2137,2207 carry it. `:xray? false` STAYS correct, for a new reason: Xray's mount denylist refuses :rf.adapter/hicasso BY NAME (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:222-241`, rf2-zkjd5) because the spine's :render is element-shaped, so the refusal fires on Hicasso's own kind rather than through UIx's.

2. DEPS.EDN SHAPE. The description says "gains day8/re-frame2-hicasso while KEEPING day8/re-frame2-uix (the adapter is still UIx's)". Wrong: the emitted deps.edn carries the Hicasso coordinate ALONE. `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn:93-94` names `day8/re-frame2` and `day8/re-frame2-ssr` as its published :deps (core and ssr arrive transitively); the UIx adapter appears only in the :test alias at :148, commented "Test-only: shipping source names no adapter at all". React/ReactDOM are npm deps declared in implementation/package.json (hicasso/deps.edn:23-24), and the emitted `_shared/package.json` already carries `react`/`react-dom` at {{react-version}}, so Hicasso adds NO npm package and NO Clojure view-library pin — nothing for version_lockstep_test.clj to lock beyond {{rf2-version}}. Group: today every scaffold emits `day8/…`; if rf2-uelji / rf2-kmqx3 land the coordinate under io.github.day8, that is a template-WIDE group change owned by the publication beads, and the _hicasso files follow whatever mechanism they settle. Never hard-code a group from this note.

3. BOOT MODEL. The description says "Model on implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:878-884". title: day8/re-frame2 has no performance regression gate (every bench in the repo covers an UNPUBLISHED artefact)
notes:
MAYOR RULING: DEFER, on a MEASURED ground rather than a preference (2026-07-26). Do not dispatch.

THE REASON IS THE NOISE FLOOR, and it was measured today by the compiled-tier report (rf2-lnecd, docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md): THE NO-SUBSTRATE FLOOR ARM DRIFTED 37% ACROSS ROUNDS — larger than most of the effects being measured — which is why every claim in that report is stated as a RATIO TO THE IN-RUN FLOOR rather than an absolute. On the same box, the same primitive measured 10.4ns and 21.7ns across two JVMs.

A REGRESSION GATE ON A SUBSTRATE WITH A 37% FLOOR DRIFT IS A FLAKE GENERATOR. It would red on noise, and this repo has a standing rule that A FAILING TEST ON A TOUCHED SURFACE IS NEVER A FLAKE — which is exactly the rule that makes a false red expensive to dismiss. We already have one such gate (rf2-yumaq: G-8 dying because its baseline was TOO FAST) and fixing it took a worker. Adding a second, broader one before the measurement is stable would manufacture that cost at scale.

A PREMISE CORRECTION THE BEAD INHERITS FROM ME: its notes classify the Freehand benches as covering an artefact that is "NOT published". Freehand is PRE-PUBLICATION and expected to ship — docs/release-process.md forecloses only day8/re-frame2-ui, and implementation/freehand/deps.edn:29 says staying out of the lockstep inventory "leaves the release train untouched until Freehand actually ships". I propagated that error into six briefs today. So the gap this bead describes is narrower than stated: the benches cover artefacts that are not published YET, not artefacts that never will be.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DISPATCHABLE, in order: (1) a stable measurement method — the report shows allocation via getThreadAllocatedBytes gave min = p50 = max in nearly every arm, so an ALLOCATION gate is buildable where a wall-clock gate is not; (2) a named regression the gate would have caught, because a perf gate with no historical catch is an assertion that the future will resemble a past nobody measured; (3) the alpha tag, after which "published artefact" stops being a moving target.

NOT A REJECTION. The operator has ruled that performance matters — the compiler is KEPT for performance-critical applications not yet seen. A gate is the right long-term instrument; it is the wrong instrument today because it cannot yet distinguish signal from a 37% floor.
*** THE DEFER LAPSES 2026-09-01 AND NOTHING IN THE GRAPH HOLDS THIS BEAD. DO NOT DISPATCH ON THE DATE ALONE. ***

value:
skills/**/README.md IS OWNED BY check_doc_slugs.py, NOT check_readme_links.py — a mayor mis-nomination repeated across six dispatch briefs on 2026-09-02 before a worker caught it.

THE FACT, verified at source: scripts/check_readme_links.py defines DOCS_GATE_ROOTS = {docs, spec, migration, skills} and SKIPS every path under them (plus tools/*/spec/). So a skill's README.md, STATUS.md and every other markdown file under skills/ is validated by check_doc_slugs.py alone.

WHY THE MISTAKE IS EASY, because this is the part worth remembering: check_readme_links.py's remit is genuinely 'README.md beside source code, and repo-root markdown' — implementation/**, examples/**, tools/** (outside their spec/ dirs), README.md, CLAUDE.md, TESTING.md. The word README in the script name and in that remit makes 'this file is a README.md' feel like the discriminator. IT IS NOT. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE ROOT, NOT THE FILENAME: any markdown under docs/, spec/, migration/ or skills/ goes to the docs gate whatever it is called, and any markdown outside them goes to the readme gate whatever it is called.

CLAUDE.md already states this correctly under Build & Test ('the docs-gate roots ... still excluded'); the error was reading the remit and not the roster.

CONSEQUENCE WHEN WRONG: mild but real. Coverage was never actually lost — the docs gate does cover skills/ and workers ran both gates anyway — but a brief that nominates the wrong gate either sends a worker to hand-verify what a gate already proved, or invites it to trust a green that inspected nothing. Nominate by PATH against the roster, never by filename.

CAUGHT BY: the pairskill-b worker (PR #9007), which read DOCS_GATE_ROOTS rather than the brief.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): auto-call-site-rewrites M-1 row swaps get-handler -> handler-meta without the corpus flag for INVOKING call sites (a called map returns nil silently)
description:

TRUTH AT TIP
Corpus M-1 (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:92-133), row `re-frame.registrar/get-handler`: "it returns the registration *metadata map*, not the raw handler fn ... For call sites that introspected the registration this is the right surface; **a call site that actually *invoked* the returned handler fn needs a rethink (flag for review)**." `handler-meta` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1828) returns a map. title: skill(re-frame2-setup): executor preconditions missing -- no JVM on PATH and :dev-http 8280 already bound have no line, and the handoff URL is read from config not from the watch
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:43 -- "the skill is the **executor**: it writes the files, runs `npm install`, runs a terminating `npx shadow-cljs compile app`, starts the watch, and reports the URL". TRUTH AT TIP. Two environment failures sit in front of every command the executor now runs, and neither has a line. (1) `npx shadow-cljs` is an npm wrapper that spawns a JVM; with no `java` on PATH it fails before compiling anything (the wrapper cannot spawn `java`), the granted commands include nothing that checks for one, and the failure the agent sees is not a re-frame2 failure. (2) `:dev-http` binds a fixed port; when 8280 is already bound -- a second `shadow-cljs watch` in another project is the ordinary way -- shadow reports the bind failure for the dev-http server, and the URL the skill hands off (`http://localhost:8280/`) serves whatever is already listening there: a wrong page rather than an error, so the "click +1, expect 0 to 1" handoff sends the author to someone else's app. The generated project's README names JDK 21 + Node 22 (tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:322); the skill states no precondition.

FIX SHAPE. Two or three lines, not a manual -- a precondition in step 6 (or a "Before you run" line above it): (a) `java -version` must succeed -- shadow-cljs runs on the JVM, the npm package only wraps it; if it fails, say so and stop (no version claim without a source; the template README's JDK 21 is one if the fixer wants a number); grant `Bash(java -version)` in allowed-tools. (b) Report the URL from the watch's own dev-http output line, never from the config: if 8280 is already bound, pick another `:dev-http` port, restart the watch, and report THAT URL. Node version: nothing, unless a source is cited.

Here the instrument was broken, so the control returned zero too — and a reader who checks only 'did my census return zero?' sees a confirmed premise. The worker caught it because it noticed the CONTROL had also failed, which is the only signal available. A zero control is not a weak result; it is evidence the instrument is broken, and it must never be read as 'the control does not apply here'.

THE REMEDY THAT WORKED: re-run the census in Python, once line-oriented and once flattened. Do not reach for another grep flag combination.

BOUNDS: measured on this repo's Git-Bash on Windows 11. The -F (fixed-string) flag is implicated in both failures; plain grep and rg were not observed failing this way. Re-measure before asserting the scope is wider.

THIS IS THE SECOND INSTRUMENT IN ONE DAY that answered 'nothing here' while broken — the other was the surface classifier, which reports every surface unaffected when handed revisions where it wants PATHS (hit by three separate workers). Same class, different tool: any instrument that can answer 'nothing here' gives that answer when misused, and raises no error.

title: skill(re-frame2): reg-machine.md and spawn.md remain over the 16 KB leaf ceiling after the rf2-udtw3 duplication trim — the residual is content, not duplication
description:
MEASURED at PR #8995 (rf2-udtw3 commit 953e14249d). Both leaves were trimmed of every restated passage the bead named, plus two more. Neither reaches the 16,384 B ceiling, and the remainder is unique teaching rather than duplication, so the trim stopped there per the no-teaching-loss stance.

FINAL: reg-machine.md 208 L / 20,785 B (4,401 over). spawn.md 199 L / 19,358 B (2,974 over).

WHY rf2-udtw3's premise did not hold, independent of the sibling beads:
- Its five targets measured smaller than estimated. The reg-machine.md trio spans 4,593 B TOTAL and that figure INCLUDES the replacement text the bead says to keep (a pointer sentence, a two-sentence warning, the ctx shape + destructure trick), so the realistic yield is ~1.5-2 KB, not the projected ~4 KB.
- spawn.md settles the either/or arithmetically: the :spawn-all section is 1,950 B, not ~2.5 KB. Even moving it WHOLESALE to a new spawn-all.md leaf leaves 17,408 B — still 1,024 B over — while costing a SKILL.md routing row and two roster rows in another partition's serial-lane files. The split cannot satisfy the acceptance criterion, so it was declined on measurement rather than preference.
- rf2-hgyeg/dwkj0/if5q9 legitimately grew reg-machine.md by ~2.5 KB of required new teaching (descriptor tiers, :reenter? geometries, the region-only ctx keys, defmachine). That widened the gap but did not create it.

OPTIONS for a ruling, none of which is a pure trim:
1. Accept both leaves over the byte ceiling and record them as exceptions (they are 208/199 lines, inside the 250-line ceiling; the overrun is long unwrapped prose lines).
2. Split reg-machine.md along a real seam (for example a transitions/grammar leaf) — a partition-A change touching SKILL.md routing and the rosters.
3. Re-examine whether the 16 KB byte ceiling in skills/README.md is right for dense reference leaves of this kind.

This needs an operator call on which, so it is filed rather than actioned.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling on which of the three options applies; if a split, the SKILL.md routing row and roster rows land with it
notes:
FENCE 2026-09-02 19:57:00 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the live rf2-machskill-b worker. skills/re-frame2/** is ONE SERIAL LANE, HELD by PR #8995 until it MERGES. rf2-ytkt additionally carries a QUESTION FOR MIKE rather than work: both state-machines leaves ship over the 16 KB ceiling after the worker refused to cut teaching to hit the number, and it offers three options for a ruling. INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION OF THE REFUSAL, 2026-09-02 (worker rf2skill-e, PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9017). NOT actioned and NOT closed: this bead's acceptance criterion is an operator ruling among three options and its fence says surface-do-not-dispatch, so a worker cannot satisfy it. Re-measured at base 1ed3b5e9b7 and confirmed: reg-machine.md 208 L / 20,807 B, spawn.md 199 L / 19,435 B — within 22 and 77 bytes of the figures this bead records, so PR #9009 did not move them. THE REFUSAL HOLDS ON FRESH MEASUREMENT. A shingle-based near-duplicate scan over reg-machine.md returns ZERO intra-file near-duplicate pairs at a 0.30 Jaccard threshold: the leaf is fully de-duplicated and the residual is unique teaching, exactly as rf2-udtw3 concluded. spawn.md returns six pairs, all false positives on inspection — structurally parallel but semantically distinct rules (:output-key-requires-:final? vs :error?-requires-:final?, two different error ids) and adjacent fence lines showing two different keys. Cross-file scans surface only conventional shared framing (the footer provenance boilerplate shared with history.md, the XState-v6 parity statement each leaf needs as its own frame, the choice-state rule split between the declaration grammar and the translation catalogue) — nothing extractable. NEW EVIDENCE FOR OPTION 3, which is the reason this note is worth reading. The three sibling beads dispatched alongside this one (rf2-lpanl, rf2-x43bk, rf2-67d2e) hit the SAME WALL on EIGHT FURTHER LEAVES across three more partitions: websocket, resources, form-action, resources-mutations, testing, privacy-and-elision, routing, stories. Two leaves were brought inside both ceilings by de-duplication (cofx.md 18,865->16,311 B; forms.md 17,510->16,310 B) and testing.md was genuinely split, so the ceiling is not unreachable in general — but everywhere it was NOT reached the diagnosis is identical to this bead's. Only 2,680 B of reg-machine.md and 3,757 B of spawn.md are code fences. So this is precisely the case skills/README.md says the byte ceiling exists to catch — and on these leaves the catch is a true positive about DENSITY that has no remedy, because the two remedies the contract offers are both unavailable: de-duplication is exhausted (measured zero), and splitting fails the catalogue test's OWN criterion in the direction that forbids it, since an author needs the whole of one canonical declaration and a split raises tokens-per-session rather than lowering it. DO NOT tell a worker its cluster is 'the ENTIRE remaining open backlog' for a lane — the mayor made that claim twice on 2026-09-02 and was wrong BOTH times, caught by the workers rather than by itself.

THE TWO INSTANCES. (i) pairskill-c was told its four beads were the whole of skills/re-frame2-pair; rf2-pra5 was open on that skill at P2 — HIGHER than three of the four dispatched — and was visible in the same ready list the cluster was drawn from. (ii) retro-b was told the same about skills/re-frame2-pair-retro; rf2-d4h52 and rf2-vdqr9 were open on it.

THE MECHANISM, which is why this recurs rather than being one slip: the merged-PR AUDIT reopens beads into a lane continuously and asynchronously. Twelve closures from one session read open on a later sweep, every one a legitimate audit reopening with a NEW residual finding. So a lane that was empty when the ready list was read is not empty when the brief is written, let alone when the worker starts. The claim is a snapshot dressed as an invariant — the exact shape CLAUDE.md's ledger bullet warns about for its own header.

WHY IT MATTERS rather than being cosmetic: 'this clears the lane to zero' invites a worker to treat leftover beads as out of scope, and it is stated with the authority of someone who can see the tracker. Both workers correctly refused it, but that cost each of them a paragraph of report and could have cost a wrong scoping call.

WHAT TO SAY INSTEAD. Name the beads and stop: 'these four are your cluster'. If completeness genuinely matters, re-read the lane at DISPATCH time and say 'these were the only open ones in this lane as of <timestamp>' — a dated observation, not a property. And carry the standing instruction that a worker should say so if it finds others, which is what caught both of these.

title: EPIC ssr-node crossing: make the bounded Node renderer a first-class ssr-ring path (RULED 2026-09-02 — six children rf2-8arzr.1..6; do not dispatch this bead)
description:
## Scope

Make the bounded Node/React renderer a supported opt-in renderer for the non-streaming re-frame.ssr.ring request path. The outcome includes the smallest useful Ring render seam, the JVM side of the v1 crossing, an explicit post-drain render-state projection, a supported Node package/launcher entry point, and one canonical runnable native-Hicasso example with its tests and documentation. The existing JVM/Reagent renderer remains the default.

## Findings

- The three components are individually substantial and well tested, but they do not compose into a public product path. re-frame.ssr.ring owns request frames, event/resource drain, head, hydration payload, shell, response and teardown; implementation/ssr-node owns a bounded React render service; no caller joins them.
- build-full-response* resolves a JVM hiccup root and directly invokes ssr/render-to-string. That API shape cannot name a native JavaScript root which exists only in the application bundle.
- The Node request already has a stable entry, EDN root args, build identity, and allowlisted state, but its state shape is only top-level app-db key -> EDN value text. The JVM does not produce that projection, and route/machine/runtime facts needed by a real SPA have no inbound door.
- Render visibility and hydration egress are different policies. The server must be able to render from state that is intentionally absent from __rf_payload; deriving one projection from the other would either leak server-only state or silently render nil.
- The documented consumer API imports implementation/ssr-node/src/*.cjs directly. implementation/ssr-node has README.md, src/ and test/ but no package manifest/export or supported launch command of its own.

title: ssr-node crossing (E/6): native-Hicasso product witness — hicasso.server body-only entry + login example server bundle
description:
Slice E of the ssr-node crossing programme — the PRODUCT witness. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 first; this description carries only E's own brief. Depends on D being MERGED. The ruling settled the witness question: it is native Hicasso; a Reagent example does NOT substitute (a Reagent root already renders on the JVM, so Reagent-over-Node proves machinery nobody would ship).

## Scope (fence)

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: ADD a body-only entry beside `render`; do NOT change `render`'s settled spellings (naming-ledger row 22, `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md`). Its CLJS test lives in `implementation/hicasso/test/` under the existing `:node-test-hicasso` build (no build change for the test).
- `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/`: extend the ONLY native-Hicasso example rather than start a new app — add `server.cljs` publishing the sidecar module contract (`{protocol, buildId, entries, render}`) with an entry table naming the login root, its `stateAllowlist` and the runtime-partition allowlist from slice C, and a small Clojure `server.clj` wiring `ssr-handler` + `re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer` + `:render-state` + `:payload`. Update the example README.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (HOT-ZONE — queue): ONE `:examples/login-hicasso-server` `:node-library` build beside `:examples/login-hicasso` (~:1622).
- No Playwright spec under `examples/` (examples are test-free — rf2-8cevm); the witness lives under `implementation/hicasso/test/` or `implementation/ssr-ring/test/`.

## Do

`re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (name is the worker's within the naming ledger's rules): takes the restored snapshot via `render-state/restore!` (slice C) into a FRESH per-request frame — no boot-event replay, no `:snapshot`/`:initial-events` re-seeding — then `mount/tree` + `renderToString` with `:identifier-prefix`, returns the INNER markup only (no payload, no document), tears the frame down in a `finally`, and FAILS the render (throws, which the sidecar turns into a refusal) if the Hicasso runtime recorded a recovered render error during the pass — the JVM's post-render error accumulator cannot see inside the Node frame, so a swallowed error there would ship a wrong page as a success. The module wrapper publishes `render-body` as the entry's `render`. The client boots with `hydrate-root!` and the SAME `identifierPrefix`, reading the `__rf_payload` the JVM wrote.

## Acceptance

1. `npx shadow-cljs compile :examples/login-hicasso-server` and the `:examples/login-hicasso` client build both green; `npm run test:examples-compile` green.
2. An end-to-end test (CLJS in `implementation/hicasso/test`, or JVM in `implementation/ssr-ring/test` — worker's call) proving: the login page is server-rendered from a server-only value that is ABSENT from `__rf_payload`; route or machine runtime state is rendered (the login example has a machine — use it); build-id skew is refused with the distinct code; hydration succeeds with no recoverable error and matching `identifierPrefix`.
3. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` stays green — `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` must still find each login bundle carrying only its own view runtime, and the server bundle must not leak into the browser build.
4. `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py` stays green (a browser build must not reach `server.cljs`).
5. Example README updated (build, run the sidecar, run the JVM host, open the page).

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`npm run test:cljs` or the focused `:node-test-hicasso` build (name which); `npm run test:examples-compile`; `npm run test:bundle-isolation`; the reachability script above. Cite CI for the rest.

## Stop and report to Mike

If the login root turns out to need the whole unprojected frame rather than an explicit render snapshot, or cannot hydrate cleanly from the JVM-owned payload. Leave the PR open with what works and say so on this bead.

## Traps

`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` is hot-zone — queue; the testbed/example build-ids and `:dev-http` ports live there. No Playwright under `examples/`. No `git stash`; commit then rebase. Worker worktree guard first; report `WORKTREE_ROOT`. Remove the `node_modules` junction as your last act.
notes:
DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 19:43:14 AUSEST by the mayor. SOLO, LARGE, fresh worktree worker/product-8arzr5 off origin/main 4c351a44ba — the FIRST slice whose whole chain (A #8981, B #8985, C #8982, D #8991) is MERGED beneath it, so the worker builds against the real seams. Premises verified at that tip: render_state/restore! at ~:400; ssr/ring/node.clj renderer at ~:360; hicasso/server.cljs defines payload-script/document/render and no body-only entry; examples/substrates/hicasso/login/ is README+core.cljs+index.html only; shadow-cljs.edn :examples/login-hicasso at ~:1622; both named gates exist (check_optional_module_reachability.py, test:bundle-isolation releasing six builds). Brief foregrounds the error-accumulator clause as THE risk (a swallowed recovered render error inside the Node frame ships a wrong page as a success, invisible to the JVM accumulator) and repeats the bead's STOP condition verbatim as Mike's call, not a problem to engineer around. shadow-cljs.edn authorised as the one hot-zone touch, own commit. Fence: worker/hicptr-slril is live in implementation/hicasso/** but its remaining carriers are forms.cljs + impl/mount.cljs + one test — server.cljs is NOT among them, so the two are file-disjoint; the worker re-derives before its first hicasso edit.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02. Three findings the mayor should carry to slice F / Mike.

(1) THE ACCUMULATOR INSTRUMENT IS NOT THE ONE THE BEAD IMPLIED, and it was settled by measurement. The bead's clause names 'the JVM's post-render error accumulator' — re-frame.ssr's per-frame pending-error-traces buffer. The first cut of render-body used exactly that, and its refusal row RENDERED MARKUP: Hicasso reads its subscriptions through the pure compute-sub path (impl.collector's cold read), whose :rf.error/sub-exception record is stamped ':frame nil' BY CONSTRUCTION and documented as such in re-frame.subs ('a compute-sub-driven SSR harness that wants the per-frame projection must use the reactive subscribe path'). candidate-frame-for-error returns nil for such a record, so the buffer never fills and a per-frame check reads CLEAN on the exact failure the clause exists to catch. render-body therefore watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream (rf/register-listener! :errors) for the extent of the render — strictly stronger, since that stream is what the per-frame buffer is filled FROM, plus the frame-nil records it drops. NOTE THE STANDING IMPLICATION: server/render (the whole-page door, unchanged here) has the same blindness on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host today.

(2) ACCEPTANCE 2 ASKS FOR TWO PROPERTIES THAT CANNOT BOTH HOLD OF ONE RENDER, and this is Mike's call rather than a defect. 'Server-rendered from a server-only value ABSENT from __rf_payload' and 'hydration succeeds with no recoverable error' are incompatible on the same node: the hydrating client renders from the payload, so a node the two halves disagree about is one React recovers. That is React, not re-frame2. The witness proves BOTH, on two render-state/payload configurations of the same page, and MEASURES the tension (its section 6 is clean; its section 7 costs exactly one recovered adoption). The shipped example ships the clean configuration and the rule — a render-state key the payload does not carry must not change the markup — is stated in the README and beside the sub in core.cljs. If Mike wants the example page itself to carry a rendered server-only value, that is a decision to accept one recovered adoption per page.

(3) host.clj IS THE WIRING, NOT A RUNNING SERVER, and one file outside this slice's fence is why. A JVM host must hold the application's state, so login.model has to be loadable from Clojure; it is examples/core/login/model.cljs and the single line keeping it CLJS-only is a localStorage write in the demo session fx. Making it .cljc is a change to a file all three login arms share. Named in host.clj and in the README.

Two smaller notes for slice F (rf2-8arzr.6): spec/009's :rf.error/ssr-render-failed row now has a SECOND emitter (re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body) — the id was reused rather than a new one minted because spec/*.md was fenced out of this dispatch; and examples/substrates/README.md + examples/README.md describe the three login arms without mentioning the server build.

One deviation from the bead's text, with its reason: the Clojure host is host.clj / ns hicasso.login.host, NOT server.clj. ClojureScript implicitly requires foo/bar.clj as the MACRO namespace of a foo/bar.cljs, so a server.clj beside server.cljs would be loaded into every compile of the server bundle, as macros, on a classpath with no Ring on it.

## Post-close: PR #8997 CI fix (rf2-8arzr.5, follow-on worker, 2026-09-02)

The bead's change was complete but PR #8997 was red on one check, `tests :: JS
harness self-tests`. Fixed on the same branch without changing what the change
does. Recorded here because the PR's file set grew by two files the bead's own
work did not touch.

RED ASSERTION (implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs):
  parseExampleBuilds(shadow-cljs.edn) is non-vacuous and every build has out+init
  -> build examples/login-hicasso-server missing :init-fn

CAUSE, and it is a real one rather than a test artefact: the assertion held
out+init of EVERY `:examples/*` build, which was true only because all 43 of
them were `:browser` pages. This slice adds the first that is not. A
`:node-library` publishes an `:exports-var` for the Node sidecar to `require`;
it carries no `:init-fn` and no colocated index.html because it is not a page.
So the assertion, not the build, was overstated. Adding an `:init-fn` to the
build to quiet it would have been a lie about the artefact.

FIX: `examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs` now recovers `:target` alongside
`:output-dir` and `:init-fn`, and the real-repo assertion holds out+init of the
`:browser` builds only. The non-page build is still PARSED — it is an example
build and check-examples-compile.cjs compiles it warnings-fatal — merely absent
from the runnable manifest, which is what listStandaloneExamples' pre-existing
null-filter already did without saying so. Two anti-vacuity guards: every build
must declare a `:target`, and the page count keeps its own >=30 floor rather
than inheriting the total. The synthetic fixture gains a `:node-library` entry.

Script and test moved in ONE commit (two halves of one contract).

GOVERNING CONCLUSION, for anyone adding a non-page `:examples/*` build later:
the out+init invariant is a PAGE-build invariant, discriminated by `:target`,
not a roster-wide one. It lives in comments in both files.

TWO COVERAGE LIMITS RESTATED, one of them corrected. `host.clj` is loaded by no
gate — but not for the reason previously given: implementation/deps.edn's test
alias DOES put ../examples/substrates on the JVM test classpath. Nothing loads
it because no namespace requires `hicasso.login.host` and its name does not
match the runner's `-test` selector. A compile error in it passes every gate
silently. Separately, the witness's protocol.cjs require resolves at run time
from js/__dirname, so a package move fails in the node lane, not at compile.

The three design findings carried up at close (the pending-error-trace? buffer,
acceptance clause 2's two properties, host.clj as wiring) were NOT revisited.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8997 — REOPENED. The slice was titled and accepted as the native-Hicasso product witness, but examples/substrates/hicasso/login/host.clj comments out login.model and the README explicitly says the JVM host cannot run. Its :initial-events therefore name registrations the host never loads; no gate requires the namespace or drives the advertised Ring handler. Complete the existing owner by making the shared model JVM-loadable (without duplicating the three substrate arms), requiring it from the host, and adding a focused JVM compile/request smoke that proves the documented build → sidecar → Ring page path. While there, make or mechanically pin the render-state policy as one source across host and server: server.cljs derives the entry allowlists from render-state-policy, but host.clj currently repeats the same map twice, so the prose's “one list, two readers” claim is not true and a host-side omission can render incomplete state without the sidecar's extra-key refusal firing. This is the existing acceptance-5/runnable-example owner, not a new task.
MORE SLICE-E FALLOUT, MEASURED 2026-09-02 BY SLICE F -> filed as rf2-8arzr.9 (P2). Slice E broke ssr-node's absence witness in FIVE places across three of its commits (ae858bf329 x3, bbc97a5678, ff6698f794): four sites spell the :rf.ssr-node/ refusal namespace outside the package, and one comment in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn names the package path. absence.test.cjs fails two rows as a result. THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHETHER TO FIX IT OR DOCUMENT IT, and that is a judgement the worker should make and argue rather than assume. Skipping fenced blocks may be DELIBERATE — a fence often carries illustrative or third-party markdown that is not meant to resolve, and validating it would red on examples by design. DO NOT grow this into a rewrite of the checker. Read what it does, establish which case this is, and land the smaller of the two.
