description:
CLAIM. The catalogue (`references/README.md:7-14`) is 6 leaves; `spec/design.md` §4 "Deferred catalogue candidates" (`:86-91`) holds 2. Compared against the 15 pattern leaves under `skills/re-frame2/patterns/`, the fundamentals leaves, `spec/Principles.md`, and Mike's standing rules (frames are isolated contexts; no raw atoms through views; no frame-ids as view args; no over-engineering), the common consumer misuses below have no leaf and are not queued. L6 (`design.md:57`) says a leaf lands only after 3+ real reviews — so the landable shape is the DEFERRED LIST, ranked, with detection signals, so the growth procedure has a queue rather than a blank.

TRUTH AT TIP — 13 candidates, ranked (source that discourages it -> canonical idiom):
1. Frame leakage / frame-ids as view args — a sub or handler reading another frame (`rf/app-db-value other-frame` in a sub; `(rf/dispatch ... {:frame :other})` from inside a handler of a different frame; views taking `frame-id` args and threading `capture-frame`). `fundamentals/frames.md:9,82`; Mike's rule "frames are isolated contexts". Already deferred as "foreign-frame write"; widen to reads + view args. Signals: `app-db-value` / `{:frame ...}` inside `reg-sub` / `reg-event` bodies; view params named `frame` / `frame-id`.
2. Views that fetch / boot in a mount hook — `:component-did-mount`, `use-effect`, `r/with-let` init dispatching `:*/load` / `:*/fetch` / `[:rf.resource/ensure ...]`. `patterns/resources.md:9,29` ("views are passive reads — they never trigger a fetch"), `patterns/boot.md:138` ("Boot logic in a view's `:on-mount`"). Fix: route entry / `:initial-events` / machine `:entry`.
3. Secrets in machine `:data` or `app-db` — bearer/refresh tokens in `:data`, passwords retained in a form's `:submitted` / `:draft`. `patterns/websocket.md:30,216`, `patterns/forms.md:34-36`. Signals: `:token` / `:bearer` / `:password` keys assoc'd into `:data` / db without `:sensitive`.
4. App code reading runtime-db through `:db` — `(get-in db [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots ...])` in a sub/handler instead of `[:rf/machine id]` / `[:rf.route/*]`. `fundamentals/frames.md:33`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md:146` (MUST NOT). Greppable: `:rf.runtime/` in app source.
5. Host reads in machine callbacks folded into `:data` — `(js/Date.now)` / `(random-uuid)` in `:action` / `:entry` / `:guard`. `spec/005` §Causal host facts, `patterns/websocket.md:198`. A leaf-5 extension (its signals are scoped to `reg-event` bodies; only `subscribe-once` is covered for callbacks).
6. Ad-hoc HTTP fx bypassing `:rf.http/managed` — a `reg-fx` wrapping `js/fetch` / `cljs-http`, or `:http-xhrio`, with no `:status` envelope, stale suppression or failure taxonomy. `patterns/managed-http.md:5,27`. Today flagged only when a retry loop is also present.
7. Positional multi-arg event payloads — `[:cart/add id qty price]`. `spec/Principles.md` §Name over place; migration M-19. Signal: `(fn [_ [_ a b c]] ...)` with 2+ positional args.
8. Top-level `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-later` keys outside `:fx` — dropped with `:rf.error/effect-map-shape` (`fundamentals/fx.md:36,87`). A v1 habit; fails at runtime as a trace, not a throw.
9. Reactive `@(subscribe ...)` in a lifecycle hook — `patterns/stateful-components.md:98`. Sibling of leaf-5's reactive-read rule, on the view side.
10. Post-mutation watcher reactions for workflow -> call-site `:reply-to`. `patterns/stale-detection.md:24`.
11. Anonymous `:on-click` doing logic beyond one dispatch — `spec/Principles.md` §Named things over anonymous things.
12. View renders only the happy state — already deferred (`design.md:90`); keep.
13. Boot dispatched after `make-frame` instead of `:initial-events` — `fundamentals/frames.md:164`, `spec/002-Frames.md:660`; an idempotent `frame-root` re-mount does not replay them.

IMPACT. None of these is a false critique today (the catalogue is honest); the gap is coverage — a consumer review misses the frame-isolation and view-fetch misuses that re-frame2's own principles name most loudly, and the growth procedure has no ranked queue to draw from.

FIX SHAPE. One PR to `spec/design.md` §4 Deferred catalogue candidates: replace the 2-item list with the ranked list above (one line each: name -> signals -> canonical idiom), keeping L6's 3+-review bar. If Mike wants to pre-empt L6 for #1 (his standing rule), promote it as a seventh leaf in the L5 five-section format plus catalogue + routing rows in `references/README.md` — a separate PR, not this one.

GATE. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (design.md is under `skills/`, a docs-gate root). The ranking is prose — no gate; say so.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): stories.md teaches the run-variant loop with no adapter prerequisite — run-variant refuses with :rf.error/no-adapter-installed on a bare launch, and the pair skill OWNS the run side
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md teaches the run-variant / read-failures self-healing loop and states no host prerequisite for it. Grepping that file at tip: no occurrence of 'no-adapter-installed', 'plain-atom/adapter', or any adapter/substrate prerequisite at all (the only 'substrate' hit is a snapshot-identity hash tuple).

This matters more here than in the authoring skill, because the pair skill is the OWNER of the run side. skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md explicitly hands off to it: 'switch to the re-frame2-pair skill (it owns run-variant / read-failures against a running app behind shadow-cljs watch) and run the self-healing loop there'.

TRUTH AT TIP

  - tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md, section 'Running a variant needs an installed adapter (rf2-c9t52)': catalogue reads work on a bare launch; RUNNING one does not. run-variant and preview-variant allocate a variant frame, and a frame takes its state substrate from an installed re-frame adapter. The server deliberately installs none — per spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md the substrate choice belongs to the app — so a consuming project installs one in the namespace its launch alias preloads ((rf/init! plain-atom/adapter), the renderer-free choice). With none installed both lifecycle tools REFUSE before any lifecycle work: isError true, :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, plus :tool and a :recovery naming the boot. They never return a :status.
  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc implements it as a pre-flight before story/run-variant allocates, returning {:rf.error :rf.error/no-adapter-installed :tool <tool> :recovery :init-an-adapter-in-the-preloaded-namespace}. Its docstring gives the reason: with no substrate the setup dispatches reach nothing and the script plays nothing, yet the run settles the ordinary :status :pass envelope over {} and [] — a success-shaped NON-RUN indistinguishable on the wire from a genuine green (measured under rf2-3n3dk).
  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc's run-variant descriptor carries the prerequisite in the tool description an agent reads.

PREMISE CORRECTION worth recording, because a reader of rf2-2ktuc will otherwise think this is already done: that bead's TRUTH AT TIP says commit 8cae7ca102 'carried the prerequisite into ... skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md'. It did not. Reading that commit's diff for that file, the single hunk rewrites the read-a11y-violations gotcha from 'return an empty list ... expect the no-op' to the capability-unavailable refusal. The adapter prerequisite landed in that commit on tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md, spec/API.md and tools/story-mcp/README.md only.

IMPACT

An agent driving the pair skill's loop on a consumer project whose launch alias preloads no adapter gets isError true / :rf.error/no-adapter-installed on its first run-variant, with the leaf offering neither the error name nor the boot. Worse than the authoring case: the refusal is easy to misread as :cannot-run (a runner that could not attempt the plan, whose remedy is to change the runner) when it is a host prerequisite to satisfy, and the leaf teaches the :pass / :fail / :cannot-run / :error verdict vocabulary right beside it.

FIX SHAPE (one file)

Add the prerequisite where the loop is set up — the error id, that it carries :tool and :recovery and never a :status, the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot in the preloaded namespace, and that catalogue reads are unaffected. Note explicitly that the refusal is NOT a :cannot-run verdict. Cite tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md section 'Running a variant needs an installed adapter'.

Consider matching skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md, which PR #8999 gave the same treatment for preview-variant — same facts, run side instead of authoring side. Write it from the spec section and lifecycle.cljc rather than from that leaf, so the two do not become a copy that drifts.

GATE

scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py and scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pin neither this prose nor per-tool behaviour text. Verify by hand against the spec section and lifecycle.cljc; say so in the PR body. skills/re-frame2-pair/** is a serial lane — sequence, do not parallelise, against anything else touching it.

ACCEPTANCE

stories.md names :rf.error/no-adapter-installed and the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot, and distinguishes the refusal from a :cannot-run verdict; check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py and check_doc_slugs.py exit 0.

FOUND BY rf2-2ktuc's worker (PR #8999) while checking that bead's premise about which surfaces commit 8cae7ca102 reached. skills/re-frame2-pair/** was outside that dispatch's fence.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 20:55:27 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2skill-c worker as a correction to rf2-2ktuc's premise — commit 8cae7ca102 did NOT carry the adapter prerequisite into skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md, so the PAIR skill, which owns the RUN side, still has no adapter prerequisite for run-variant. The pair skill lane is FREE (PR #8996 merged at 4813c62323). Dispatchable, and it pairs with rf2-16q1 — same reading of the Story tool contract, adjacent surfaces.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02 23:38 AUSEST, PR #9020. Census confirmed the premise: stories.md had 0 hits for no-adapter-installed line-oriented AND flattened, with controls that bite in the same file (:cannot-run 2/3, run-variant 7/7).

DIVERGENCE FROM THE FIX SHAPE, recorded because it is a correction to this bead rather than a shortcut. The FIX SHAPE says to write the error id plus :tool and :recovery and never a :status, and the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot in the preloaded namespace. Those are the HEADLESS story-mcp facts, and this leaf documents the BROWSER heap over eval-cljs -- the host it explicitly disclaims in its own section Headless Story is a different task. Writing them verbatim would have created a fresh instance of the defect class this bead is about.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE. (1) tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src has NO run-variant tool (grep exit 1, zero hits; control eval-cljs exit 0 with hits in 5 files), so the pair skill run side is re-frame.story/run-variant evaluated in the browser. (2) tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1295-1301 wraps prepare-ctx! and resume-ctx! inside the promise executor under try/catch and routes every throw to handle-run-error!, which CALLS RESOLVE. So the browser path has no pre-flight refusal at all and does not reject -- the exact opposite of lifecycle.cljc:63-79, which refuses before allocating and never returns a :status. (3) The underlying condition is core's: frame.cljc:2381 reaches adapter/make-state-container, then require-adapter! in substrate/adapter.cljc:293-345, throwing :rf.error/no-adapter-installed when rf/init! never ran and :rf.error/adapter-disposed after destroy-adapter! -- two ids, two remedies. (4) plain-atom is the renderer-free choice and renders nothing, so it is wrong advice for a browser canvas.

RESOLUTION. The prerequisite is written per host: the browser contract where the loop is set up, and the headless refusal envelope including (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) inside the section that already owns that host. Every acceptance item is met -- stories.md names :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, names the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot, and distinguishes both from a :cannot-run verdict -- and check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py and check_doc_slugs.py all exit 0. Written from the spec section and the sources above rather than copied from skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md, so the two do not become a drifting copy.
close_reason: PR #9020: stories.md now carries the run-variant adapter prerequisite. Names :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, names the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot in the Headless Story section that owns that host, and distinguishes both from a :cannot-run verdict. Written per host after verifying at source that the browser path has no pre-flight refusal (runtime.cljc:1295-1301 resolves through handle-run-error!) and that the pair MCP server ships no run-variant tool -- see the appended note for the divergence from the fix shape. check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py and check_doc_slugs.py all exit 0.

title: impl: re-frame.core facade + late-bind directory still claim resolve-resource-scope emits :rf.resource/scope-resolved
description:
CLAIM

Two implementation-side descriptions of `resolve-resource-scope` still say it emits
`:rf.resource/scope-resolved` dev-time trace evidence. Both are false, and both
contradict the artefact and the defwrapper in the SAME tree.

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc (the re-frame.core facade `def` for
  `resolve-resource-scope`): "It is not a pure data helper, though: like every
  resolution site it emits `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` dev-time trace evidence."
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc (the
  `:resources/resolve-resource-scope` directory entry `:description`): "Not a pure
  data helper, though: like every resolution site it emits
  :rf.resource/scope-resolved dev-time trace evidence."

TRUTH AT TIP (read, not inferred)

- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc, the public
  `resolve-resource-scope` defn: its body is
  `(resolve-scope*-pure scope-id spec db 'rf/resolve-resource-scope)` and its
  docstring says "NO observability side effect either: it routes through the
  trace-free `resolve-scope*-pure` evaluator, so a passive read advertised as pure
  does NOT emit `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` into the trace bus."
- Same file, `resolve-scope*-pure`: "PURE ... WITHOUT emitting any observability
  state (rf2-ru73k6 F3)". Its sibling `resolve-scope*` is "the TRACED wrapper ...
  for use at CAUSAL resolution boundaries (resource events, route entry, mutation
  settle)".
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_resources.cljc, the `defwrapper` for
  `resolve-resource-scope`, is already CORRECT: "It is a PURE data helper
  (rf2-ru73k6 F3): it routes through the trace-free `resolve-scope*-pure`
  evaluator and so does NOT emit `:rf.resource/scope-resolved`".

So core_resources.cljc and the artefact agree; core.cljc's facade docstring and the
late-bind directory entry are stale against them. The facade docstring is the one a
reader reaches from `(doc rf/resolve-resource-scope)`.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY

Found while fixing rf2-537sf, whose audit note (AUDIT PR #9004) asked for BOTH the
skill leaf and the facade docstring. The skill half is fixed on that bead's PR
(skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md, the Resources row).
The worker's write scope was skills/re-frame2/** only, so implementation/** was
read as ground truth but not edited. The directory.cljc site is a THIRD carrier the
audit note did not name -- a single-string grep for the facade wording alone would
miss it.

FIX SHAPE

Two docstrings, no behaviour change: restate both as the pure/trace-free contract
already spelled out in core_resources.cljc and scope_registry.cljc, naming the
causal boundaries (resource events, route entry, mutation settle) as the sites that
do carry the row.

GATE

No gate reads a docstring's prose. Verify by hand against
implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc and say so; run
whatever JVM suite the touched artefacts gate on.

ACCEPTANCE

Neither implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc nor
implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc claims
resolve-resource-scope emits :rf.resource/scope-resolved; both state the pure,
trace-free contract and attribute the trace row to the causal boundaries.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): pre-rename index still omits M-31a and over-broadens the new M-74 machine-id rewrite

- **M-44** (README.md:1799) "`:timeout-ms` REMOVED from `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` - use parent state's `:after`. **Type A** - pre-1.0 spec lock; mechanical rewrite" - machines-only, so pre-rename-only; cited in breaking-changes.md and sequencing.md but not in this index.

title: docs/core/hicasso/15-testing.md: the published :local/root test-kit route (:extra-paths to ../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src) prints a Clojure CLI deprecation warning on every build
description:

  :test {:extra-paths ["../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src"]}
and the pilot workspace page copies that. Every shadow-cljs invocation then prints, before compiling:
  WARNING: Use of :paths external to the project has been deprecated, please remove: ../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src
tools.deps has deprecated paths that escape the project root. Nothing fails today, but (a) a pilot following the published chapter meets a deprecation warning on the first build, which the friction log will (correctly) record against the published docs; (b) a future Clojure CLI may refuse it, at which point the published route breaks. The chapter is outside rf2-xkhul's fence (docs/core/hicasso is the published guide), so this is filed rather than fixed.

OPTIONS, not ruled. (1) Publish the kit through a coordinate instead of a path: a second :local/root to a tiny deps.edn placed in test_kit/ (e.g. day8/re-frame2-hicasso-test-kit {:local/root "../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit"} with test_kit/deps.edn {:paths ["src"]}) is inside the project boundary of THAT root and prints nothing; the chapter's line changes shape but stays one line. (2) Put test_kit/src on the hicasso artefact's :paths (rejected before, rf2-hic-020 kept it off :paths so a no-test app carries none of it; but reachability already keeps it out of a bundle that never requires ht/hm, per the chapter's own 'From a published coordinate' paragraph). (3) Leave it and add one sentence to the chapter naming the warning as expected. value:
WRITE EVERY DISPATCH BRIEF TO A FILE BEFORE SENDING IT, BECAUSE THE POSTURE LOOP'S FIDELITY CHECK IS OTHERWISE TESTIMONIAL RATHER THAN MECHANICAL (2026-09-03).

THE PROBLEM. loops.md section 4 asks the mayor to confirm that every dispatch since the last posture tick pasted the stance VERBATIM and carried the boundary and gate-mechanics blocks. If the brief was assembled inline in the Agent call and never written down, there is nothing left to check against afterwards — the mayor's own recollection is the only witness, and a mayor that had summarised the stance would recall having pasted it. That is precisely the failure mode the loop exists to catch, so the check silently degrades to self-report at exactly the moment it matters.

THE FIX IS ONE EXTRA STEP AND IT COSTS NOTHING. Build the brief mechanically into a scratchpad file — stance header, then the extracted preamble / boundary / gates blocks appended, then the task body — and dispatch by telling the worker to read that file as its FIRST action. Then the posture check is three greps with counts, run against bytes that still exist: grep -c on a distinctive line of each block. Anything other than 1 is a defect you can name.

TWO SECOND-ORDER WINS, BOTH REAL. (1) Telling the worker to cat the file is MORE faithful than pasting, because the bytes it reads are the extractor's output rather than anything that passed through the mayor's hands again. (2) The file survives compaction. Measured this session: four dispatches made before a compaction could not be re-verified at all, because their briefs had only ever existed inside the Agent call, and the only surviving evidence was one worker's report happening to describe gate-block-specific behaviour (planted-fault runs, git blob-hash restore). That is corroboration, not verification, and it was luck.

THE ANCHOR-DUPLICATION DETAIL. Repeat the worktree path, branch, base oid, bead ids and the premises-are-claims sentence INLINE in the Agent prompt as well. A worker that fails to read the file then contradicts an anchor visibly instead of improvising a task silently — the failed read becomes detectable rather than silent.

DO NOT read this as licence to skip the extractor. The file is where the extractor's output lands; it is not a substitute for extracting. See never-retype-a-verbatim-block.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): known-frictions.md is saturated at 3 bytes under the 16 KB leaf ceiling — the next addition forces a split
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md sits at 241 lines / 16,381 LF-normalised bytes against the family ceiling in skills/README.md (Leaf size discipline: each leaf SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB, i.e. 16,384 bytes). That is 3 bytes of headroom and 9 lines. Measured at tip after PR #9016.

HISTORY. PR #9006 left it at 241 lines / 16,336 bytes (48 B headroom) and its author predicted the next addition would force a split. rf2-wz1qa (PR #9016) was that next addition: its three corrections cost ~96 bytes gross, which did not fit, so two genuine restatements were trimmed to pay for them -- 'cross-reference the live catalogue rather than the skill's docs alone -- a live-catalogue check is' shortened to 'cross-reference the live catalogue -- that check is', and 'the pair-MCP conformance corpus' to 'the conformance corpus'. Both were honest de-duplications, and that seam is now spent: there is no comparable restatement left to trade.

IMPACT. The leaf is the skill's one on-demand reference and is still growing (rf2-vdqr9 is an open item against this same file, and would breach on its own). The next author either breaches the ceiling silently -- nothing gates it, wc -l -c is the only instrument -- or trims load-bearing content under time pressure.

DECISION NEEDED (not taken here, deliberately). Three options, and this is a judgement call rather than a mechanical fix:
(a) SPLIT the leaf by friction family. But SKILL.md routes to exactly one on-demand leaf and the family rule is one-level routing, so a split needs a routing decision, not just a file move.
(b) CLAIM the catalogue exemption. skills/README.md already carves one out: 'catalogue-shaped leaves (for example re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md) may exceed the ceiling if splitting would multiply file-handle overhead without reducing tokens-per-session.' known-frictions.md is a catalogue of friction classes and plausibly qualifies -- the stated test is 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?', and since the whole leaf loads on one trigger, a split arguably would not.
(c) TRIM content rather than structure, accepting the loss.

(b) looks strongest on the file's own shape and is much the cheapest, but it is a family-contract call the mayor/Mike should make, not a worker.

GATE. None -- the ceiling has no gate. wc -l -c before and after, plus check_doc_slugs.py if the routing changes.

Filed from PR #9016 (rf2-wz1qa + rf2-fpeig) rather than splitting on worker initiative, per the dispatch brief.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:1x AUSEST — OPTION (b), THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION, IS TAKEN. Recorded as MY call rather than Mike's so he can reverse it cheaply; the bead correctly refused to take it on worker initiative.

MEASURED AT bddc39f415 BEFORE RULING: 241 lines, 16,622 raw bytes, 16,381 LF-normalised. Ceiling at skills/README.md:239 is <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (16,384). So 3 bytes and 9 lines of headroom — the bead's figures reproduce exactly.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a) OR (c). The exemption at skills/README.md:245-248 states its own test: 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?' known-frictions.md is loaded on ONE trigger — the retro's pattern-check step, SKILL.md:81 — and the whole leaf is consulted to answer 'is this a one-off or a product gap?', which is a question you answer by scanning the classes until one matches. A session cannot know in advance WHICH half holds its friction, so a split into two sibling leaves would load both on most sessions and add a file handle and a routing hop for nothing. The test therefore answers NO for this leaf, which is precisely the case the exemption exists for. (a) is refused on that reasoning, not on the routing objection the bead raises — a split into two siblings is still one level deep and would not be a SKILL->A->B chain. (c) is refused because the bead's own history shows the trim seam is spent: PR #9016 already paid for ~96 bytes by de-duplicating two genuine restatements, and there is no comparable restatement left to trade, so the next trim comes out of load-bearing content.

WHAT LANDS. skills/README.md's exemption bullet names known-frictions.md alongside re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md, with the one-trigger reasoning stated in a clause so the next reader does not re-derive it. The exemption is for THIS leaf on THIS shape; it is not a family-wide licence and no other leaf inherits it.

THE BOUND, because an exempt catalogue is not an unbounded one: each class stays at the density the existing nine already set. rf2-vdqr9's four new classes are written to that density, not longer. No second numeric ceiling is invented — per the stance, that would be litigating minutiae.

CONSEQUENCE: rf2-vdqr9 is unblocked and dispatches WITH this bead in one cluster, since its four classes are exactly the growth this ruling authorises.
CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING NOTE, same tick, before dispatch. The last paragraph said 'rf2-vdqr9's four classes are exactly the growth this ruling authorises'. That is wrong and I caught it by reading the file rather than the bead: the four classes ALREADY LANDED — known-frictions.md carries 'Dry-run versus a live write' (:119), 'Wire-boundary privacy elision and the raw-eval carve-out' (:132), 'Wire-size caps and pagination' (:145) and 'Hot-reload baseline misuse' (:156), and the 16,381-byte measurement INCLUDES them. rf2-vdqr9 was reopened by the PR #9006 audit and its live residual is much smaller: split the one Signals bullet at :124 by reason, so :rf.error/writes-disabled (the closed default-OFF gate, lifted at server launch) is separated from :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected (post-gate runtime refusals with their own epoch/drain/frame/schema remedies).

THE RULING IS UNCHANGED AND THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENS IT. Splitting one bullet into two costs bytes against 3 bytes of headroom, so even this small correctness fix cannot land without the exemption — the leaf is saturated at a point where a genuine repair is blocked by structure. That is the situation the exemption is for, and it is a better argument for (b) than the one I wrote.

The density bound stands, now stated against the right work: the split bullet is written at the density the surrounding Signals bullets already set.

title: MIGRATION.md M-51 calls the unary reg-fx failure a language-level arity error; the skill's three leaves class it SILENT on CLJS (the failure-visibility axis that picks the sweep method)
notes:
FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING rf2-a75ai (PR #9010), which added an M-51 section to skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md. Not fixed there: MIGRATION.md is a one-toucher hot-zone file and the worker's write scope was skills/re-frame-migration/** only.

THE TENSION.
- CORPUS, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1984 (inside M-51, heading :1980, Type line :1982 'Type A - pre-1.0 spec lock; mechanical rewrite.'): 'The runtime invokes every registered fx handler with two args; a unary handler raises a language-level arity error at the call site (ArityException on JVM, TypeError / "Cannot read ... of undefined" or similar on CLJS depending on shape).' That leads with the LOUD reading.
- SKILL, three leaves, mutually consistent and all SILENT for CLJS:
  - breaking-changes.md:208 (failure-visibility axis row): 'on CLJS (no arity check) the runtime context-map binds to args and the real fx args are silently dropped - the handler runs against the wrong value, no error (on JVM it throws an ArityException - loud - but v1 migration targets are CLJS)'.
  - inventory-and-plan.md:66 lists 'unary reg-fx handlers -> M-51' among the rules that 'compile clean and break only at runtime'; :81 repeats the silent-drop mechanism.
  - sequencing.md:82 row 14a: 'Type A but SILENT-fail - so swept by an exhaustive up-front grep'.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic). Loud-vs-silent is the axis that selects the SWEEP METHOD, and the skill says so explicitly: silent-fail rules get an exhaustive up-front grep and 'never march-the-wall', because a loud rule can be found by following compile/runtime errors while a silent one cannot. A reader who takes the corpus sentence at face value would conclude M-51 is discoverable by running the app and reading errors, and could legitimately skip the exhaustive grep - on a rule that fires in nearly every real v1 app with a custom reg-fx.

WHICH SIDE LOOKS RIGHT. The skill's, on CLJS. A single-arity CLJS (fn [request] ...) compiles to a one-parameter JS function; JS silently ignores extra arguments, so the v2 call with two args binds the CONTEXT MAP to request and drops the real fx args, with no ArityException and no TypeError at the call site. Any TypeError arrives LATER and elsewhere - when the handler destructures the context map and downstream code uses the nils - which is a different failure at a different place from 'at the call site'. The corpus's JVM half (ArityException) is correct; note the skill's own remark that v1 migration targets are CLJS. The corpus does hedge with 'or similar ... depending on shape', so this is an emphasis/accuracy problem rather than a flat contradiction - but the sentence's leading clause is the part a reader acts on.

NOT VERIFIED AT RUNTIME by this worker - the reasoning above is from CLJS/JS calling semantics plus the skill's three concurring statements, not from an executed repro. Anyone actioning this should confirm with a two-arg call into a single-arity CLJS fn before rewording the corpus.

Downstream, (:real wrongly-bound) is nil. title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): re-authoring sources still drop the new draft-ownership citation contract
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:87` (§Issue drafts): "A good draft carries, in natural prose: the concrete session evidence, the missing `re-frame2-pair` or `re-frame2` behaviour, one implementable desired outcome, and a completion signal ... with the pair-tool-versus-framework ownership plain in the title and body."

That is the whole instruction on ownership. SKILL.md never names `spec/Tool-Pair.md` (grep: lines 6 and 62 say "Tool-Pair contract" / "Tool-Pair surfaces" without a path or a section), never says WHAT a framework-shaped draft must cite, and carries no worked example of either title. README.md:38 lists surface families in prose only.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`skills/README.md:183` (family contract, §Routing for friction found mid-pair retro): "framework / Tool-Pair contract friction — ... Name the specific Tool-Pair surface from the consolidated capability table in `spec/Tool-Pair.md` (the shipped tool catalogue is `re-frame2-pair/README.md`)." `skills/README.md:185`: "The draft contract lives in `re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` §Issue drafts."

`spec/Tool-Pair.md:36-52` §What re-frame2 commits to (the runtime contract) — the `| Capability | re-frame2 surface | Spec |` table, e.g. row: `| **Read registry** | (rf/registrations kind), (rf/handler-meta kind id), (rf/frame-ids), (rf/frame-meta id) | 001-Registration, 002 |`; and `spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126` the restore-failure table (seven rows, `:operation` + `:tags`).

The skill is self-contained by lock (design.md L7: "Nothing loads from outside the package root"), so the family-contract sentence is unreachable from inside a retro unless SKILL.md restates it.

## IMPACT

The family contract promises that a framework-shaped draft names a capability-table row; the skill that owns the draft contract does not instruct it. A framework-shaped draft therefore lands as "re-frame2 should surface X" with no row and no tool named — the vague draft that §Anti-patterns :97 ("without naming the concrete missing behaviour") forbids — and a maintainer cannot tell a Tool-Pair gap from a pair-skill recipe gap from the title.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR against `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` §Issue drafts, at most 10 lines:

1. One sentence: a framework-shaped draft names the row of `spec/Tool-Pair.md` §What re-frame2 commits to (or the §Time-travel restore-failure row) it falls short of, and the shipped pair tool that exposed the gap (catalogue: `skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md`); a tool-shaped draft names the pair-skill leaf or tool descriptor to change.
2. Two two-line worked examples, titles from the safe alphabet (letters, digits, spaces, `- . , / ( ) :`): tool-shaped — `pair-tool (discover-app): ladder hint for no-runtime-connected should say reload the tab`; framework-shaped — `framework (Tool-Pair Time-travel, restore-epoch): restore-unknown-epoch tags should carry the oldest retained epoch id` with a body line that quotes the row.

Optionally mirror the one sentence in README.md:38. SKILL.md is 98 lines; stays far under 500.

## GATE

`bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` from the skill root (it re-reads SKILL.md; must stay green — the grant and the prescribed `gh issue list` argv are untouched). `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for any link added. Prose verified by hand.

## ACCEPTANCE

§Issue drafts instructs a framework-shaped draft to name a Tool-Pair capability-table row and the shipped tool, a tool-shaped draft to name the pair-skill leaf/descriptor, and shows one worked title+body line of each; `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` exit 0.

The skill's only security pointer is the tooling subset (file-path + editor-URI) in the checklist.
4. spec/011-SSR.md §Frames are per-request (line 31) and §`:platforms` metadata on `reg-fx` (line 194) — spec/README.md Track 3 item 6: "even non-SSR implementations consume the `:platforms` and frame-per-request rules." `:core/*`-only fixtures carry it: construction-in-handler-guard.edn:27 and cross-spec-dispatch-sync-in-handler.edn:52 both register fx with `:platforms #{:client :server}` under capabilities `#{:core/event-handler :core/frame :core/fx}` / `#{… :core/error :core/trace}`.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): dry-run/write friction conflates runtime rejection with the --allow-writes gate
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` §re-frame2-specific classes (:82-196) carries nine classes. None covers the four frictions the pair skill itself flags as its commonest footguns, and its only observation class is framework-listener-shaped:

- grep for `privacy|elide|elision` hits only §Production-elision confusion (:121-132), which is BUILD elision (`goog.DEBUG=false`), not wire-boundary privacy elision.
- grep for `wire-size|truncat|max-tokens|dedup|cursor` — no hits.
- grep for `tail-build|baseline` — no hits.
- grep for `dry-run|undo|allow-writes|replace-app-db` — no hits.
- §Wrong listener for the question :96-106 reasons about `register-listener!`'s `:trace` vs `:epoch` streams ("default to the `:epoch` stream ... reach for the `:trace` stream only for per-emit detail") — the FRAMEWORK listener API, not the MCP tools a pair session actually calls.

## TRUTH AT TIP

- Privacy carve-out: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:218` — structured reads (`snapshot`, `get-path`, `read-sub`, `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`, `dispatch-dry-run`, recorders) elide server-side (`:rf/redacted`, `:rf.size/large-elided`) under `--allow-sensitive-reads` (OFF by default); `eval-cljs` is un-elided and default-ON. Two friction shapes follow: an agent reading `:rf/redacted` as "the data is missing/broken", or reaching for raw eval and shipping secrets.
- Wire-size caps: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:193` + `references/wire-size-budget.md` — `max-tokens`, `:rf.mcp/dedup-table`, `limit`/`cursor`, `max-buffered-*`; a truncated page read as a complete answer is a classic weak-trust-signal friction with a re-frame2-specific shape.
- tail-build baseline: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:111` — "Capture your probe's current value BEFORE the edit (that's the `baseline`)... or you'll interact with pre-reload code"; `tools/tail_build.cljs:148,172` refuse with `:baseline-without-probe` / `:missing-baseline`.
- Dry-run / write gate: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:207-208, 219` — `dispatch-dry-run` rolls back and fires no fx; a live `dispatch` of a handler returning `{:db <bare-map>}` REPLACES app-db wholesale ("unrecoverable without `restore-epoch`"); `restore-epoch` / `replace-app-db` are gated by `--allow-writes` (OFF by default) and refuse with `:restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`) / `:reset-rejected` (`tools/replace_app_db.cljs:114`).
- Observation after PR #8815 (2026-08-31): `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, `get-stream-controls` are gone from the registry (29 tools; grep of `descriptors_data.cljs` finds no such `:name`). `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:208`: "`watch-epochs` polls the assembled-epoch history — the one live-watch route, and every observation arrives as a completed tool result." The returned-result routes a session chooses between are `dispatch` (settled envelope with the assembled epoch, `spec/Tool-Pair.md:79`), `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`, `watch-until`, and `record` / `read-recording` — all registry names.

## IMPACT

The retro's pattern-check leaf is where "is this a one-off or a product gap?" is decided (SKILL.md:81, design.md L6). A session that burned time on `:rf/redacted` confusion, a truncated `snapshot`, a `tail-build` timeout from a missing baseline, a wholesale app-db replace, or a write refused by the OFF-by-default gate finds no class and gets scored as a one-off — or worse, a "why didn't they just subscribe?" reasoning path that no longer exists. These are the frictions the pair skill's own style guidance spends the most words warning about, so they are the likeliest retro inputs.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR against `known-frictions.md`: add four re-frame2-specific classes in the existing Signals / Typical improvements shape (≤12 lines each) — (1) privacy elision vs raw-eval carve-out, (2) wire-size caps and pagination, (3) hot-reload baseline misuse, (4) dry-run vs live write and the write gate — and add one line to §Wrong listener mapping the framework streams onto the tool routes (`dispatch` envelope / `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `watch-until` / `record`+`read-recording`), noting that live-watch is poll-only and no subscription tool exists. The leaf is 195 L / 12.7 KB; ~50 lines fits under 250 L / 16 KB. If it does not, split the re-frame2-specific classes into a second leaf linked from SKILL.md:81 (still one level deep).

## GATE

No gate — verify by hand: every tool name against the `descriptors_data.cljs` `:name` list; `wc -l -c` on the leaf under 250 / 16384; `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` if a new leaf/link is added.

## ACCEPTANCE

known-frictions.md carries a class for each of: privacy elision/raw-eval, wire-size caps, tail-build baseline, dry-run/write gate; §Wrong listener names the five returned-result tool routes and states that no subscription tool exists; leaf within ceiling.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 on 2026-09-02 12:04:19 AUSEST (re-confirmed unchanged at d12181c4c3).
acceptance_criteria: known-frictions.md names :rf.error/writes-disabled as the closed --allow-writes result and treats :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected as post-gate runtime refusals with distinct remedies; no text suggests lifting the gate fixes those runtime refusals; leaf remains within its existing ceiling
notes:
AUDIT PR #9006 (2026-09-02): REOPENED for correctness. The new "Dry-run versus a live write" Signals bullet joins :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected to "a closed gate." Those are runtime-level refusals returned only after the named write reached the runtime: restore target absent/drain in flight, or frame/drain/schema rejection. A closed --allow-writes gate refuses earlier with :rf.error/writes-disabled and never touches nREPL. As written, a retro can recommend lifting the gate for a rejection that enabling writes cannot fix.

Split the one bullet by reason: :rf.error/writes-disabled means the default-OFF gate and is lifted at server launch; :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected mean the gate was already open and need their own epoch/drain/frame/schema remedies. Keep the existing class; no new section or machinery.
close_reason: Audit-note instruction implemented; description was stale as flagged. Confirmed the four friction classes already landed and did NOT re-add them (Dry-run versus a live write :119, Wire-boundary privacy elision and the raw-eval carve-out :132, Wire-size caps and pagination :145, Hot-reload baseline misuse :156). Split the one conflating Signals bullet at :124 by reason: :rf.error/writes-disabled is the default-OFF --allow-writes gate refusing before the write reaches the runtime and lifting at server launch; :restore-rejected / :reset-rejected are post-gate runtime refusals (restore target absent, drain in flight, frame/drain/schema rejection) for which lifting the gate does nothing. Existing class kept, no new section or machinery, written at the surrounding Signals density. All three keywords verified at source at exact spelling before writing: writes.cljs:85 emits :rf.error/writes-disabled and server.cljs:521 confirms it is refused BEFORE ensure-connection! (never touches nREPL); restore_epoch.cljs:106 emits :restore-rejected; replace_app_db.cljs:114 passes :reset-rejected through from the runtime's app-db-reset!. PR #9028.

title: three example suites share the rf2-k4oe make-frame-before-register! ordering; latent, not broken
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-k4oe co-load sweep (PR #9027).

rf2-k4oe fixed re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test, whose init! created a
:url-bound? frame BEFORE reinstating the :resource/:mutation registrar rows the
shared reset hook clears, so the route-entry resource plan ran inside make-frame
against an empty registrar.

THREE OTHER SUITES SHARE THAT EXACT ORDERING and are green today only because
their "/" route declares no BLOCKING resource:

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/infinite_feed_example_cljs_test.cljs
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/resources_example_cljs_test.cljs

MEASURED. Each was built in its own single-app :node-test bundle on
690b99309f + the rf2-k4oe fixes, and each passed:
infinite-feed-example 5 tests / 38 assertions, realworld-resources 33 / 286,
resources-example 9 / 39 — all 0 failures, captured exit 0.

A census of every reg-route form under examples/ (paren-balanced over flattened
text, control-checked against a known-present site first) found seven apps
registering a route at "/" — infinite_feed, linearlite, realworld_http,
realworld_resources, resources, routing, todomvc — and LinearLite is the ONLY
one with a blocking route resource there. That is the whole reason it was the
only hard failure.

SO THIS IS LATENT, NOT BROKEN. Adding a blocking resource to any of those three
root routes reproduces rf2-k4oe exactly, silently, and only in a bundle where no
sibling owns "/". The cheap prophylactic is to move make-frame last in all three,
matching the committed pilot baseline
(docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/linearlite/baseline_test.cljs,
which documents "the frame is made last"). Deliberately NOT done under rf2-k4oe:
churning three passing suites was out of that bead's scope, and the call on
whether to harden them prophylactically is worth making explicitly.

RELATED, and the more interesting half: rf2-ma8r stays open for Mike's ruling on
the two framework questions this exposed — whether a :url-bound? frame planning
route resources AT CONSTRUCTION is correct, and whether a FAILED route plan
should ever be retried (today an app that recovers stays wedged in
:transition :error permanently). If either is ruled on, this bead may become
moot: the ordering only matters because the plan is both construction-time and
un-retried.

SWEEP COVERAGE, so the remainder is not lost. Fifteen example suites were run in
single-app bundles (155 tests / 1180 assertions, all green). NOT covered:
the ~11,000-test framework remainder of the :node-test lane was not swept for
co-load masking among framework suites;
re-frame.example-frame-scoping-cljs-test is excluded by construction (it loads
seven apps deliberately and cross-app scoping is its subject).

title: hygiene: two worker branches carry unmerged work with no PR and closed beads — receipts-hic081 and retire-delete need a disposition
description:
FOUND BY the hygiene loop, 2026-08-20 23:55 AUSEST, sweeping worktrees and branches. Both branches survived a cleanup that deleted 12 others, because git cherry reports them as carrying patches NOT upstream. That protection is working as designed; what is missing is a recorded reason for keeping them, so every future sweep re-derives it.

MEASURED at origin/main (git cherry origin/main <branch>, plus a direct read of the trunk):

1. worker/receipts-hic081 — THREE commits, 3 files, last commit 2026-08-11. A capability-receipts spike: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/receipt.cljs (which does NOT exist on main), a change to impl/collector.cljs, and test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs. Its bead rf2-hic-081 is CLOSED. So a spike was built, the bead closed, and the spike never landed. This is the exact branch .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md names as the measured case that patch-equivalence protects — 'ignoring it would have destroyed the 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits on worker/receipts-hic081' — so it is known and deliberately preserved, but nothing records whether the spike is wanted.

2. worker/retire-delete — ONE commit, 273 files, last commit 2026-08-15, subject 'refactor(ui): PARTIAL R2b — delete implementation/ui and its in-fence consumers (rf2-0yp7w.4)'. Its bead rf2-0yp7w.4 is CLOSED. PARTLY SUPERSEDED: implementation/ui is already gone from main (0 tracked files, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16), so that half is done. BUT examples/real-apps/realworld_resources still holds 14 tracked files on main and this branch deletes them. So the branch carries a deletion main did not take, and it is not obvious whether those 14 files were deliberately KEPT or simply missed when #8322 landed the retirement by another route.

THE QUESTION FOR EACH: keep the branch, land the work, or delete the branch on a recorded decision. Do NOT delete either without one — a branch is the only copy of unmerged work, and both beads are closed so the tracker no longer points at them.

CHEAPEST NEXT STEP for retire-delete, and it is a read not a change: establish whether examples/real-apps/realworld_resources' 14 surviving files still reference the removed re-frame.ui tree. If they do, they are residue and rf2-0yp7w.9's prose sweep or a sibling owns them. If they do not, they were correctly kept and this branch is fully superseded and safe to delete.

NOT URGENT. Both branches are inert and cost nothing but a line in a listing. Filed P4 so the next hygiene sweep reads a decision instead of re-deriving the measurement.
notes:
=== DISPOSITION READ, 2026-08-20 23:32 AUSEST — read-only, no worktree, no edits, no PR ===
All measurements re-taken at origin/main = fd061748234fef3a51c28672786ec72a1c2d05f8.
Every search excluded the tracker export (-- ':!.beads') and every search carries a
positive control. Ref-scoped greps were done per file via "git show <ref>:<file> | grep",
never "git grep <ref> -- <dir>/".

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BRANCH 1 — worker/receipts-hic081 : RECOMMEND **KEEP**
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLAIMS THAT HELD, all of them:
  "git cherry origin/main worker/receipts-hic081" -> 3 unmerged commits
  (fece72f80a, 418312d680, ae14841ab3); last commit 2026-08-11 13:06:01 +1000.

  (minus .beads) returns ZERO files repo-wide. Local ref == origin ref for both branches.
  rf2-hic-081 is CLOSED.

THE CLAIM THAT DID **NOT** HOLD — and it is this bead's stated premise:
  "nothing records whether the spike is wanted" is FALSE. rf2-hic-081's close reason
  records it verbatim: "Spike commits are pushed on worker/receipts-hic081 and retained

  where a BRANCH sweep does not look. This note is that pointer.

SUPERSESSION — the design landed, the code deliberately did not:
  Verdict was SPLIT: counts graduate as DESIGN, self-time KILLED. The design is on main at
  docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md:363 (capability-receipts row: "Adopt (counts

RECOMMENDATION: **KEEP**, and it is a demonstrated need, not a hypothetical one. The branch
is the experiment's designated primary record and has ALREADY been used as one after the
close: rf2-eoo9's close reason says "Confirmed the audit at source in fece72f80a". Two
witnesses are recorded as OWED and unmet (cache-hit stability; thrown/Suspense), and the
199-line spike harness is the natural starting point for whoever discharges them.
RELEASE CONDITION: delete the branch once a capability receipt is actually IMPLEMENTED on
main with those two owed witnesses discharged — or once the design is abandoned. Either

COST OF ERROR: deleting loses the only copy of a 381-line spike whose design product is on

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Claimed: "examples/real-apps/realworld_resources still holds 14 tracked files on main and
this branch deletes them." The branch does NOT delete those 14 files and never touched them.

Main's commit ef3131f4a2 (2026-08-15, "ATOMIC R2b ... (rf2-0yp7w.4, rf2-0yp7w.10)") made
the IDENTICAL change: same M, same seven D. 21 files existed there at the merge-base;

WAS THE SURVIVAL OF THE 14 DELIBERATE, OR MISSED? DELIBERATE, by construction — the
question as posed is malformed, because they were never in scope for either arm.
  - Zero of the 14 reference the removed tree: per-file grep for the re-frame.ui / re_frame.ui
    / re-frame2-ui spellings returns 0 on all 14, with a positive control (ns-form count = 1

    ("realworld_resources complete re-frame.ui full-app variant (S7 P-1, rf2-nn5s8)").

DOES THE BRANCH CARRY ANYTHING MAIN LACKS? NO — measured exhaustively over all 273 paths:

  - ALL 256 deletions are ALREADY DONE on main: each path checked against

  - routing.cljs is BYTE-IDENTICAL on branch and main (diff exit 0, 0 lines).
  - For the other 16 modified files, every line the branch REMOVES was checked for survival
    on main. The apparent survivors are all boilerplate or benign:
      * shadow-cljs.edn 26/205 survivors = generic recurring config lines
        (:asset-path ".", :compiler-options, {:target :browser ...) belonging to OTHER build
        entries. No ui build id survives: ui-g8 / ui-g13 / node-test-ui / proof-pack /
        :ui/testbed -> no match on main.
      * examples-asset-manifest.cjs 8 survivors = the Reagent arm's own entry; main has

        examples/realworld-resources-ui entry the branch removes is already gone.
      * check_gate_scheduling.py 3 survivors = generic DISPOSITIONS boilerplate
        ("kind": "covered-by", "by": "test:cljs", and a closing brace).
      * _adapter-smoke-filter.test.cjs 1 survivor = the string ui/testbed inside a DELIBERATE
        negative-control added by main and citing rf2-0yp7w.4: a test asserting the retired
        filter ui/testbed selects nothing, plus a sibling asserting the build-id shape

HYGIENE SWEEP RE-MEASUREMENT, 2026-09-03 01:2x AUSEST — worker/retire-delete IS NOT DELETED THIS TICK, AND THE REASON IS THAT THIS BEAD'S OWN AUTHORISATION HAS PARTLY GONE STALE. Appended rather than reopened; the close reason above stands as the record it is.

WHAT THIS BEAD AUTHORISED: 'THE ACTUAL DELETION IS LEFT TO THE HYGIENE LOOP, not because it is in doubt but because keeping a branch costs one ref and deleting the wrong one is unrecoverable. The evidence above is the recorded decision that authorises it.' That is exactly the shape section 5 asks for, and this sweep DID read it instead of re-deriving from scratch — which is the bead's deliverable working.

WHAT I RE-MEASURED at origin/main 0cb599f704, because the audit above was taken at fd06174823 and main has moved thirteen days since. THE DELETION HALF STILL HOLDS EXACTLY: all 256 paths the PARTIAL commit deletes are absent from main, re-checked one by one with git cat-file -e, still-on-main count 0. THE MODIFICATION HALF NO LONGER DOES. I am NOT concluding that, because a blob-inequality is not evidence about direction, and section 5 is explicit that a line-level scan is triage rather than a verdict in either direction. Establishing it properly means comparing the commit's whole patch against the tip at eleven paths, deletions included, which is a worker's job and not a mayor's.

AND THE TICK'S OWN CRITERION REFUSES IT INDEPENDENTLY: git cherry reads 1 '+' and 0 '-', and there is no PR at all, so it fails BOTH halves of 'all minus AND state MERGED'. The recorded authorisation was written to override the cherry reading on the strength of an exhaustive audit; with part of that audit measurably stale, the override no longer rests on what it rested on.

SO THE DISPOSITION IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND ITS TRIGGER IS NOW NAMED: keep the branch; the cost is one ref. title: CLAUDE.md Build&Test states a false gate model: mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/ (docs.yml stages it into docs/), and it catches link-resolution failures check_doc_slugs passes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by the specdrift-a worker (PR #9019) and confirmed by the mayor at source in mkdocs.yml.

WHAT CLAUDE.md SAYS, under Build & Test: that mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs is the authority on what the build cannot see from WITHIN docs_dir, and that 'docs_dir is docs, so anything outside it -- implementation/**, examples/**, tools/**, .github/**, repo-root markdown -- was never a candidate for exclusion and will never appear in that block.' A reader takes from this that spec/ is outside the strict build's reach.

WHAT IS TRUE AT TIP: the docs.yml CI step COPIES spec/ into docs/spec/, so the spec tree is STAGED INTO docs_dir and the strict build does see it. docs_dir: docs is true but not dispositive.

THE MEASUREMENT, on one tree, which is the part that makes this a defect rather than a wording quibble: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 ('no broken links') while mkdocs build --strict exit 1 on the SAME tree, naming spec/conformance/README.md's link to ../../docs/EP/EP-0012-....md as unresolvable. The link is CORRECT repo-relative -- which is what the slug gate validates and what GitHub browsing needs -- and wrong site-relative, because from staged docs/spec/conformance/ it resolves to docs/docs/EP/. mkdocs_hooks.py rewrites ../../spec/ -> ../spec/ for exactly this class but has NO ../../docs/ rule, so a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path at all.

THE TWO GATES ARE COMPLEMENTARY, NOT REDUNDANT, and CLAUDE.md should say so: check_doc_slugs.py validates ANCHORS (which strict grades at INFO and therefore never fails on) and repo-relative targets; mkdocs --strict validates LINK RESOLUTION INSIDE THE BUILT SITE, which the slug gate cannot see. Each is blind to the other's subject.

WHY IT MATTERS: the mayor nominated gates from this model in roughly a dozen briefs this session, telling workers editing spec/ that the strict build was not their gate. Nobody was harmed -- the doc gates ran in CI regardless -- but the nomination was wrong, and a worker acting on it would hand-verify what a gate already proved or trust a green that inspected nothing.

FIX SHAPE. Correct the Build & Test paragraph so it states: (1) docs.yml stages spec/ into docs/, so the strict build covers spec/ despite docs_dir being docs; (2) the two gates check different things -- anchors and repo-relative targets vs site-relative link resolution -- and neither substitutes for the other; (3) a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path, because mkdocs_hooks.py has no ../../docs/ rewrite rule. Keep the existing true parts: exclude_docs, the fence blindness both gates share, and the check_readme_links roster split.

DO NOT edit CLAUDE.md from the mayor checkout -- the commit guard refuses it. Dispatch to a worker in its own worktree.

PREMISES ARE CLAIMS: re-read mkdocs.yml, docs.yml and mkdocs_hooks.py at tip before writing, and reproduce the two-gate pairing rather than quoting this bead.
notes:
MAYOR ADDENDUM, 2026-09-03 00:5x AUSEST — A SECOND HALF OF THE GATE MODEL, MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO WORKERS AFTER THIS BEAD WAS FILED, AND THE BEAD IS INCOMPLETE WITHOUT IT.

This bead currently says 'mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/'. True of CI, and MISLEADING AS A LOCAL GATE INSTRUCTION — which is exactly how a worker will read it, because a gate nomination is a thing you run. A BARE LOCAL 'mkdocs build --strict' DOES NOT COVER spec/ AT ALL. The coverage comes entirely from docs.yml's staging step copying spec/ into docs/spec/ BEFORE the build; run the build without replicating that staging and it inspects none of your spec/ edits and exits 0, which is a green that proves nothing.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, BY WORKERS WHO DID NOT SHARE A CONTEXT. corpus-b (PR #9026) reported it in those words and replicated the staging so its strict run genuinely covered both edited paths. specdrift-b (PR #9025) reported 'mkdocs build --strict 0, AFTER staging spec/ -> docs/spec as docs.yml does — it built spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md'. Two workers, two trees, same finding, neither prompted for it.

SO THE CORRECTED PARAGRAPH NEEDS A FOURTH POINT alongside the three in FIX SHAPE: (4) the strict build reaches spec/ only through docs.yml's staging step, so CI covers it and a bare local run does not — a local run must replicate the staging (copy spec/ into docs/spec/, and migration/ into docs/migration/) or be cited as CI rather than as a local pass. Say it in the same breath as (1), because (1) alone is the sentence that misleads.

THIS ALSO CORRECTS MY OWN BRIEFS AGAIN, in the opposite direction from the first correction. I spent a dozen briefs telling workers the strict build was not their gate for spec/. Then I spent several telling them it was — without the staging caveat. The second error is smaller than the first but it is the same class: a gate nomination stated without the condition that makes it true.

The crossing now exists, and an application that HANDLES refusals has honest reasons to name them. Two coherent repairs, and choosing between them is Mike's / the mayor's call:

For ROW 2 the likely repair is different again: either reword the shadow-cljs comment so it does not spell the path, or fix the row to read loader positions the way Reading 1 does, since a comment genuinely is not a source path.

ALSO WORTH FIXING, and arguably the most valuable part: THE JOB CANNOT SEE ITS OWN BREAKAGE. The absence witness makes claims about the WHOLE repo (implementation/, examples/, tools/, scripts/, .github/) but is armed only by changes to implementation/ssr-node/**. Any change ANYWHERE ELSE can break it silently, which is exactly what happened -- three commits, five sites, zero signal. value:
bd's --json OUTPUT CARRIES CRLF ON THIS SETUP, SO EVERY ID YOU LOOP OVER ENDS IN A CARRIAGE RETURN — AND THE LOOPS BUILT ON IT RETURN A CLEAN, REASSURING, WRONG ANSWER (2026-09-03).

MEASURED. 'bd list --status open --limit 0 --json | jq -r .[].id > ids.txt' writes lines ending ^M$ (confirmed with cat -A). Any subsequent 'git log --grep=$id' or 'grep -F $id' therefore searches for 'rf2-xxxxx\r' and finds nothing.

WHAT IT COST HERE. The backlog-reread loop's done-in-tree sweep — the one check loops.md section 3 says NOTHING ELSE PERFORMS — reported ONE open id with a merged-history hit. Run correctly it reports THIRTEEN. And the single hit is what made the broken run look like a clean run: a wholly empty result would have sent me looking, while one plausible hit read as a survey that found almost nothing. That is the same shape loops.md records for the empty per-agent scratch sink, reached through a line ending.

WHY THE CONTROLS DID NOT CATCH IT. I ran both controls the method asks for — an invented id returned 0, a known-merged id returned a hit — and BOTH PASSED, because I typed those two ids as literals on the command line rather than drawing them from the pipeline. A control that does not travel the same path as the data is not a control for that path. THE CONTROL THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: take an id FROM the pipeline that you know is in the history, and assert a non-zero count.

THE FIX IS ONE FILTER: pipe through 'tr -d \r' immediately after jq, every time. Do it at the source of the list, not at each use.

AND PREFER ONE GIT CALL PLUS LOCAL MATCHING over N git invocations in a loop: 'git log origin/main --oneline -n 4000 > hist.txt' once, then grep -F each id against that file. Faster, and the history file is inspectable when a count surprises you — which is how this was diagnosed at all.

SUPERSEDED AND WRONG — DO NOT ACT ON THE CLAIM THIS KEY'S NAME MAKES. Corrected 2026-09-03 after a worker refuted it by measurement. The key name is left in place deliberately so a search for it lands here rather than on the false version.

THE TRUTH AT TIP: A BARE LOCAL 'mkdocs build --strict' DOES COVER spec/. mkdocs_hooks.py carries an on_pre_build hook that stages spec/ -> docs/spec and migration/ -> docs/migration on ANY mkdocs invocation, local or CI. Its own docstring says that is why it exists and calls docs.yml's staging step 'redundant belt-and-braces'. It landed 2026-05-19 in b2e622c316 (rf2-qw5mh). MEASURED: both staged directories deleted, a bare 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' run with no staging of any kind — both recreated by the hook, 52 spec pages built, exit 0.

WHAT I HAD WRITTEN HERE, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. I wrote that the coverage was entirely docs.yml's staging step and that a bare local run inspects nothing. TWO WORKERS INDEPENDENTLY 'CONFIRMED' IT and neither had tested it: both replicated the staging by hand and then reported strict green 'after staging spec/ -> docs/spec as docs.yml does'. That is a report of what they DID, not a measurement that it was NECESSARY. I read two agreeing reports as corroboration when neither had run the negative case — which is the actual lesson and the reason this entry is kept rather than deleted.

THE GENERAL RULE: TWO INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATIONS OF A PRECONDITION ARE WORTH NOTHING IF NEITHER PARTY TESTED WHETHER THE PRECONDITION WAS REQUIRED. Agreement between two workers who both took the same precaution is agreement about the precaution, not evidence about the mechanism. Ask what the instrument compared, not what it answered.

THE BELIEF HAD A CARRIER IN THE TREE, WHICH IS WHY IT KEPT REGENERATING: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh around :1310-1312 states it verbatim, attributed to PR #7496, and git blame dates that comment 2026-08-05 — three months AFTER the hook landed, so it was already false when written. The same file contradicts itself at :1406. Filed as rf2-4cbx (P2).

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED, because it was measured and is not affected: the two doc gates are COMPLEMENTARY, not redundant. check_doc_slugs.py owns anchors (strict grades those INFO and exits 0 on them) and repo-relative targets; mkdocs --strict owns link RESOLUTION inside the built site, which the slug gate cannot see. Reproduced on one tree with a planted link in spec/conformance/README.md: strict exit 1 naming the unresolvable target, slug gate exit 0 and silent. See rf2-3r2t.

This is one coherence sweep, not a request to redesign effect maps or add machinery. Ordinary examples may continue to show {:db ... :fx ...}; only prose that labels an exhaustive closed set or states recovery behavior must be exact. No exact existing Bead was found (title/description searches for effect-map, seven-key, classification keys, spec/API.md, and partial commit); rf2-n3mya is deliberately skill-scoped and is reopened separately for its two missed sites.

title: spec(story-mcp): 002-Tool-Registry.md contradicts itself on list-substrates — its own list-substrates section still says the JVM host returns [], which its Host execution model section and the implementation both refuse
description:
CLAIM

tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md says two incompatible things about list-substrates on the JVM stdio host.

  - Section 'Host execution model' (near the top): 'list-substrates and read-a11y-violations return a machine-readable capability-unavailable error (isError true, :rf.error :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable) rather than a false-empty []/{:violations []} success. []/#{} is reserved for a REACHED provider that genuinely holds nothing — capability absence is not answered emptiness (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - Section '### list-substrates' (in the Docs tool catalogue, further down): 'Returns the set registered via re-frame.story/register-substrate! (Reagent canonical; UIx opt-in per host). The JVM stdio server returns [] because it has no bridge to the CLJS registry.'

TRUTH AT TIP — the implementation agrees with the FIRST, so the per-tool section is the stale one:

  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc, tool-list-substrates: '(if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result {:tool "list-substrates" :capability "substrate-registry" ...}))'. Its docstring: 'this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error — NOT a false-empty {:substrates []} success that an agent could mistake for no substrates registered (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - The same file's registry descriptor for list-substrates spells the JVM case out in the tool description an agent actually reads: 'when the browser registry is UNREACHABLE (the JVM stdio server has no browser bridge) this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error ... NOT a false-empty {:substrates []}'.

The read-a11y-violations per-tool section was already corrected (commit 8cae7ca102, rf2-6j0yl, PR #8865's follow-through) and now states the refusal at length. The list-substrates section was not — the same commit's census reached the a11y half only.

IMPACT

This is the exact confusion rf2-3fc89f.21 closed in the runtime, reopened in the document that tools and agents are pointed at. A reader who takes the per-tool section at face value writes a client that treats [] as 'no substrates registered' and never handles isError — and the whole reason the contract refuses instead of answering [] is that EMPTY (a reached registry holding nothing) and UNAVAILABLE (the host could not look) are different states.

FIX SHAPE (one file, one paragraph)

Rewrite the '### list-substrates' section's last sentence to match the Host execution model section and the shipped handler: on the JVM stdio server it returns isError true with :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable, never an empty list; an empty :substrates vec is reserved for a REACHED registry that genuinely holds nothing; read it from a browser-local Story host. Model the wording on the read-a11y-violations section, which already says exactly this.

GATE

No gate pins this prose. scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pins the tool-name allow-list split, not per-tool behaviour text. Verify by hand against dev.cljc's tool-list-substrates and its registry descriptor, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

002-Tool-Registry.md's list-substrates section names :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable and no longer says the JVM stdio server returns []; the two sections agree.

FOUND BY rf2-2ktuc's worker (PR #8999) while sourcing the skill leaf's list-substrates footnote — the leaf was written from the implementation and the Host execution model section, deliberately not from the stale per-tool section. tools/** was outside that dispatch's fence.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 20:55:27 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2skill-c worker. This is a SPEC self-contradiction in tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — the host-execution-model section says list-substrates is capability-unavailable while its own per-tool section says the JVM host returns an empty vector, and the implementation agrees with the FIRST. Not fenced by any live worker; tools/** is nobody's surface right now. Dispatchable, and it pairs naturally with rf2-pra5 (the pair skill still has no adapter prerequisite for run-variant) since both came out of the same reading of the Story tool contract.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:5x AUSEST — THE tools/ COMMIT STAYS. THE FENCE WAS MINE AND IT WAS WRONG.

WHAT HAPPENED: my specdrift-c brief said 'You may edit spec/** and nothing else', and this bead's file is tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — under tools/, which that sentence forbids, while the same brief's item-1 section instructed the worker to correct exactly that file. There is no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md. The worker did the right thing in a contradiction it did not create: it followed the explicit item instruction, ISOLATED the change in its own tip commit 82c488329d so I could drop it alone, and said so rather than quietly widening or quietly skipping.

THE RULING: KEEP IT. The bead's subject is unambiguous and tools/story-mcp/spec/ is exactly where a story-mcp spec lives; the fence sentence was a copy-paste generalisation that contradicted the item it accompanied. Nothing else in the repo makes tools/ off-limits here — no live worktree holds it, and this project already has a STANDING rule pulling the other way for the sibling tool: every dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR. A tool's spec is part of that tool's surface, not a separate lane.

AND THE FIX IS SETTLED BY THE IMPLEMENTATION RATHER THAN BY EITHER SECTION'S PROSE, which is what this bead asked for: tool-list-substrates returns capability-unavailable-result when the provider is unreachable, never []. So the PER-TOOL section was the stale one and is what the worker rewrote; '## Host execution model' was already correct and is untouched. That is the right way round — a document contradicting itself has a right answer and a wrong one, and the implementation decides which, not whichever section is easier to edit.

LESSON FOR MY OWN BRIEFS, recorded here rather than only felt: a scope fence written as a blanket path glob can contradict the items it fences. When a cluster's beads name files, the fence should be derived from those files, not asserted over them — and where the two disagree, the item wins and the worker should say so, which is exactly what happened.
