Premise CONFIRMED at tip before editing: tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:298-303 still read 'The JVM stdio server returns [] because it has no bridge to the CLJS registry', contradicting its own Host execution model section at L27-33. The implementation decides, and it agrees with the FIRST: dev.cljc:196-201 tool-list-substrates is (if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result ...)) -- it never returns []. So the per-tool section was the stale one and is what I rewrote; Host execution model is untouched. Modelled on the read-a11y-violations section that 8cae7ca102 corrected the same way, stating the EMPTY (registry answered, held none) vs UNAVAILABLE (host could not look) distinction explicitly. Verified by hand against dev.cljc and its registry descriptor as the bead asked, since no gate pins this prose; check_skill_mcp_drift.py exit 0. SCOPE FLAG FOR THE MAYOR: this file is tools/story-mcp/spec/, not spec/. The dispatch brief's scope fence forbade tools/** while its own item-1 section instructed correcting exactly this file, and no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md exists. I followed the explicit item-1 instruction (this bead's triage records 'tools/** is nobody's surface right now'; no live worktree holds it) and isolated the change in its own tip commit so it can be dropped alone if the fence is ruled binding.

title: ssr-node README's Reading 2 prose predates #9024's loader-position rescope; only Reading 1 was updated
notes:
FOUND BY THE FIX-FORWARD REBASE OF PR #9015 (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-03 01:20:24 AUSEST, at base 2e7d21d9cb. NOT FIXED THERE deliberately: implementation/ssr-node/** is #9024's tree (rf2-8arzr.9) and #9015 was fenced from widening its diff.

THE DRIFT. implementation/ssr-node/README.md documents absence.test.cjs in 3 readings. #9024's commit 96ce8bb3d2 rescoped READING 2 ('it is on no build's source path') from a raw-text scan of implementation/shadow-cljs.edn + implementation/deps.edn to a LOADER-POSITION read -- for .edn, the value form after each of EDN_LOAD_KEYS, where :source-paths, :deps and :local/root live. The README's Reading 2 bullet was not updated to match.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. Reading 1's bullet already carries the equivalent narrowing in prose, at length, citing rf2-6ovv: it explains loader positions, says a format that cannot resolve a module offers no loader position, and states that no allowance list was added. Reading 2's bullet still reads as an absolute claim about MENTIONING -- 'implementation/shadow-cljs.edn names no build reaching it'. Post-#9024 that file DOES name the package: a ;; comment at implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1629 explains which sidecar loads the module the :examples/login-hicasso-server build emits. That comment is what earned the original red, and rescoping the row is exactly how #9024 fixed it.

So a reader checking Reading 2's claim greps shadow-cljs.edn, finds the package named, and concludes the README is wrong -- when the row is correct and the PROSE is merely one revision behind. The two sibling readings now describe the same narrowing at different levels of honesty.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not inferred: (a) 96ce8bb3d2 is an ancestor of origin/main; (b) grep -n ssr-node implementation/shadow-cljs.edn returns exactly one hit, line 1629, a ;; comment; (c) main did not touch implementation/ssr-node/README.md since 7f6533dd0b -- the intersection of #9015's changed files with main's was empty, and the README is in #9015's set; (d) the suite is green at this tip: node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs exits 0, 9 suites, absence.test.cjs 18/18.

THE FIX is prose only, in implementation/ssr-node/README.md's Reading 2 bullet: say that the row reads EDN loader positions rather than raw text, that a ;; comment is not a source path, and that nothing was forgiven and no allowance list exists -- mirroring the argument Reading 1's bullet already makes. Cite rf2-8arzr.9. No test change: absence.test.cjs already carries the reasoning in its own header comment, and its control row ('a doctored build config is caught, and a comment about one is not') already pins both directions.

title: spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md misrecords the retired Fiber hierarchy as never built and says Xray has no Views panel
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 by worker specdrift-b while indexing View-Hierarchy-Capture.md for rf2-f9wfd. The document was read-only ground truth for that bead and this finding is outside it, so it is handed back rather than fixed there.

DEFECT. spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md's own "Ownership + cross-references" table (the table under the heading at the foot of the document) names SIX paths. FOUR of them do not exist in the tree:

  MISSING  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/fiber_walker.cljs        (row: Fiber-walker implementation (CLJS))
  MISSING  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/group_by_tree.cljs       (row: Group-by-tree renderer)
  MISSING  tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/views_view.cljs         (row: Views panel toggle wiring)
  MISSING  tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/fiber_walker_cljs_test.cljs  (row: React-version regression smoke)
  EXISTS   implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs                 (row: Production DCE contract)
  EXISTS   tools/xray/spec/012-Views.md                                      (row: Xray Views panel)

WHAT XRAY ACTUALLY SHIPS. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/view_walker.cljs — the data-rf-view attribute walker, whose own docstring says "Status: FALLBACK SAFETY NET only" and names the Fiber-walker (rf2-mxkq7) as the primary path, citing this same spec document. So the fallback is present and the primary is not.

RELATED, AND PART OF THE SAME PICTURE. The __rf2_view_id__ property the document's §View-id tagging convention specifies appears in NO source file in the repository (grep over implementation/ and tools/ for cljs/cljc/clj: zero hits). The convention is a SHOULD, so its absence is not itself a contract violation, but it means every read path the document specifies as primary is unrealised in the CLJS reference: no Fiber walker, no view-id property, only the fallback.

WHY IT MATTERS. The document is a v1 pattern contract every React-backed port MUST implement (its own Normative-status header), and §React-version regression check requires a smoke test at a path that does not exist. An implementor following the ownership table to see how the reference does it finds nothing there. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md line 713 also calls the Fiber-walker "the primary path".

THE DISPOSITION IS AN OPERATOR CALL, not a mechanical fix, which is why this is filed rather than patched:

  (a) The walker was never built and the document describes intent. Then the ownership table's four rows should say so (planned / not yet shipped) rather than citing paths, and §React-version regression check's MUST needs a home or a deferral.
  (b) The walker was built and later removed or renamed. Then the rows need re-pointing, and the retirement wants the same bookkeeping treatment as the ui/freehand retirement (a dated statement naming the deciding bead).
  (c) The walker is still wanted. Then this is an implementation gap against a v1 MUST, and the bead is the place to size it.

Not bisected — git log for tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/ would settle (a) vs (b) cheaply.

CONTEXT. The rf2-f9wfd PR adds View-Hierarchy-Capture.md to spec/README.md's index and spec/Ownership.md's surface map. The Ownership row it adds is deliberately worded to avoid asserting WHICH walker ships: its Artefact cell says the walk is tool-side (day8/re-frame2-xray in the CLJS reference) and that the data-rf-view tagging the fallback reads is emitted by the Reagent and UIx adapter artefacts, both of which are true today. Whatever disposition this bead reaches, that cell may want revisiting alongside it.
acceptance_criteria: View-Hierarchy-Capture.md records that the Fiber walker, group-by-tree renderer, associated Views wiring, and React smoke were built under Causa in PR #1533 and deliberately removed by the Reactive-panel rebuild in PR #1741/rf2-wyvf2; it no longer describes them or the smoke as never built. The ownership row distinguishes the currently shipped Views panel from the absent hierarchy/group-by-tree mode. Any claim that reinstatement is tracked separately names an actual durable owner. The normative product call remains unpreempted, and the doc-slug gate passes.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:5x AUSEST — SPLIT THE BEAD'S TWO QUESTIONS AND DO ONLY THE FIRST. Recorded as my call.

specdrift-b filed this and correctly said the disposition — never built / removed / still wanted — is an operator call. It is, but only HALF of it is, and holding the whole bead for Mike would park a factual defect behind a product question that need not gate it.

THE HALF THAT IS BOOKKEEPING AND IS MINE TO CALL. An ownership table's job is to say WHERE a contract surface lives. Citing four source paths that do not exist (fiber_walker.cljs, group_by_tree.cljs, views_view.cljs, fiber_walker_cljs_test.cljs) is not a normative claim about what the product should become — it is a false statement about the repository as it stands, and it is wrong the same way a stale line number is wrong. Correct the table to cite what SHIPS: view_walker.cljs, the data-rf-view fallback walker. That is dispatchable now.

THE HALF THAT IS MIKE'S AND IS NOT BEING PRE-EMPTED. Whether the Fiber walker is still wanted as the primary path is a product call, and this ruling does not make it. So the correction must NOT quietly demote the Fiber walker to 'never existed' — where the spec means it as the intended primary path, the table says so IN THOSE TERMS (a normative-future row, marked as not yet shipped), rather than deleting the intent or asserting a file. The distinction to hold: the table stops claiming a path exists; it does not stop claiming the design is wanted.

WORTH KNOWING, because it is the evidence that the fallback is a fallback rather than the whole design: view_walker.cljs's own docstring names the Fiber walker as the primary path, and __rf2_view_id__ appears in no source file. So the spec is describing something real that was not built, not something imaginary. Verify both at source before writing.

I am surfacing the product half to Mike in chat as a fourth item alongside rf2-2oug, rf2-9vm0 and rf2-t9rq, which are the same shape. It does not block this bead.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9030 — REOPENED.

The bead itself named three dispositions and said a cheap history bisection would distinguish them; PR #9030 did not perform it and implemented (a), “never built.” Git history proves (b): commit fe4ff001b9 / PR #1533 created the Fiber walker, group-by-tree renderer, Views wiring, and React-prefix smoke under tools/causa; commit 9781aa4e24 / PR #1741 (rf2-wyvf2) explicitly deleted those files while replacing that Views implementation with the Reactive-panel rebuild. title: core(derivation/egress): dead-frame-sentinel is a registrable keyword, so a colliding live frame fails the graph egress open
description: implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc defines dead-frame-sentinel as ::no-egress-frame (the public keyword :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame) and stamps it as elide-wire-value's :frame opt whenever project-graph's governing frame is nil or unreachable, so the walker takes its unresolvable-frame arm. Its docstring says the keyword is namespaced into this ns so it can never collide with a real frame id. That claim does not hold: make-frame validates no :id type and the frame registry is keyed by whatever public keyword it is handed, so an app that registers a frame under that literal id turns the fail-closed stamp into a live-frame walk under that frame's empty declaration registry, and the graph's value-bearing fields ship raw. This is exactly the class the rf2-7htk7 audit of PR #8972 named for Xray's ::no-frame, which the third pass (PR #8987) fixed by making the substitute a private identity value (a fresh host object) that no registration can equal, with a collision regression (register a live frame under the literal id, leave the target unselected, assert :rf/redacted). Not done in PR #8987 because that audit note scoped the completion to Xray and forbade widening. Remedy options, smallest first: (a) make dead-frame-sentinel a private identity value the same way, plus a collision regression in the derivation egress tests; (b) have elide-wire-value distinguish a present nil :frame key from an absent one, which retires both sentinels but changes the :frame opt's documented override semantics (spec/API.md elide-wire-value and project-egress rows, spec/015 §Projection promise fallback to the carried scope when the record's own :frame is unknown) and so drags hot-zone spec prose. Verify the premise first: register a frame under :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, call project-graph with a nil frame-id on a graph carrying a sensitive value under an ambient live frame, and observe whether the value egresses raw.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:4x AUSEST — OPTION (a), THE PRIVATE IDENTITY VALUE, PLUS THE COLLISION REGRESSION. Option (b) is refused.

WHY (a). It is not a new design decision — it is the SAME fix this repo already made for the SAME defect class one artefact over. The rf2-7htk7 audit of PR #8972 named this class for Xray's ::no-frame, and PR #8987 fixed it by making the substitute a private identity value (a fresh host object) that no registration can equal, with a collision regression that registers a live frame under the literal id, leaves the target unselected, and asserts :rf/redacted. That is a worked precedent with a shipped test shape, so this is applying a settled answer rather than choosing one. The bead itself records that (a) was not done then only because the audit note scoped the completion to Xray and forbade widening — the scope, not the reasoning, is what kept it out.

WHY NOT (b). Two reasons, and the second is what settles it. First, it changes the :frame opt's DOCUMENTED override semantics, which is a public-contract change made in service of an internal sentinel — the tail wagging the dog. Second, it drags hot-zone spec prose (spec/API.md's elide-wire-value and project-egress rows, and spec/015's Projection promise fallback), and a worker is live in spec/** right now, so (b) would be a lane collision on top of a larger change. Neither reason alone would be decisive; together they are.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST, and the bead tells you exactly how, so do it rather than trusting the docstring's claim OR mine: register a frame under the literal :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, call project-graph with a nil frame-id on a graph carrying a sensitive value under an ambient live frame, and observe whether the value egresses raw. IF IT DOES NOT, the premise fails and saying so is the whole deliverable — the docstring's collision claim would then be true and there is nothing to fix.

THE REGRESSION IS NOT OPTIONAL. A private identity value with no test asserting the collision case is the same fix without the thing that keeps it fixed, and this defect has now been found twice in two artefacts because the first fix's scope was drawn too tight.

title: skill(re-frame2): patterns managed-http and boot — the 401-refresh auth-machine worked example is promised by each leaf to the other and exists in neither (spec/Pattern-Boot §Worked example has it)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md:127`: "The full auth-machine worked example combining 5xx-retry-at-transport AND 401-refresh-at-semantic lives in `patterns/boot.md`." Again at L154: "For the machine-form wrapper in production, see the auth-flow in `patterns/boot.md`." and L160 "Retry-ownership worked example → `patterns/boot.md`".

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/boot.md:264` (§Variations, *The retry-ownership boundary*): "Mixed transport-vs-semantic retry — e.g. auth machine handling 401-then-refresh-then-retry — sits at the boundary … Both compose. See `patterns/managed-http.md`." and L298 "Retry-ownership boundary → `patterns/managed-http.md`".

## TRUTH AT TIP

Neither leaf contains the example. `boot.md`'s canonical machine spawns an app child `:auth/restore-session` and retries it with a fixed `:after {2000 …}` (L212-222) — no 401 detection, no refresh-then-loop-back, no `:rf.http/managed` `:retry` on the auth request. `managed-http.md` has the retry-ownership TABLE (L117-125) and an `:app/auth` wrapper sketch (L76-92) that transitions `:failed → :login-failed` with no refresh path. The example does exist — in the spec: `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:297-330` "Semantic retry — state machine handles 401-vs-200-vs-fatal" (`:got-401?` guard L318-320; "`:failed` whose `:error` is `{:kind :rf.http/http-4xx :status 401}` → `:refreshing` … loops back to `:loading-me`" L300-306), and `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:446` points at "Pattern-Boot §Worked example — auth-machine and the retry-ownership boundary" for it. The skill leaves point at each other instead of at that section.

## IMPACT

The single worked example the skill offers for the boundary it makes load-bearing ("does the retry decision depend on anything other than failure category and attempt count?") is a circular pointer. An agent asked to "refresh the token on 401 and retry" loads both leaves, finds the table and the rule, and no shape — and the shape has a trap (the refresh request is itself a managed request; the loop-back target must be the ORIGINAL request's state, not `:refreshing`) that the spec example resolves and the leaves do not. Gap, not contradiction: P3.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, both leaves; ~30 lines net)

Either (a) lift a compact `:refreshing` branch into `boot.md`'s canonical machine — `:got-401?` guard on `:authenticating`'s `:failed`, a `:refreshing` state that `:spawn`s the refresh `:rf.http/managed` and on `:succeeded` targets `:authenticating` (the loop-back), with the 5xx `:retry` map on the auth request — and make `managed-http.md:127,154,160` point at `boot.md` §Canonical declaration by anchor; or (b) leave `boot.md` as is and retarget all three `managed-http.md` pointers plus `boot.md:264,298` at `SKILL-REDIRECT.md → Pattern — Boot §Worked example — auth-machine and the retry-ownership boundary`, the way `managed-http.md:158` already routes the full 014 spec. (a) keeps the skill self-contained; (b) is one line per pointer. Either is acceptable; the patterns leaf-size bead argues for (b).

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates any in-skill anchor added (it does not validate `SKILL-REDIRECT.md` prose pointers — verify the spec heading by hand and say so).

## ACCEPTANCE

`grep -n "boot.md" skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md` and `grep -n "managed-http.md" skills/re-frame2/patterns/boot.md` no longer promise each other a worked 401-refresh example; the example is reachable in one hop from `managed-http.md` §The retry-ownership boundary.

title: docs(hicasso): 04-controlled-inputs.md promises a throw for a controlled :value on contenteditable, and nothing throws
description:
https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md

CLAIM. docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md L93-95 reads: "Unsupported
controlled shapes are rejected rather than approximated. In particular, a
contenteditable region has no single value that Hicasso can reconcile.
Binding :value to it throws at the source."

TRUTH AT TIP. Nothing throws. The controlled converge recognises exactly
`input` and `textarea` (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/
controlled.cljs:158 `("input" "textarea") true`, and :331 "itself for
everything that is not a controlled input / textarea"), so a :div carrying
:contenteditable and a :value is passed straight through to React with no
refusal on any path.

CENSUS. The 27 distinct :rf.error/hicasso-* ids emitted under
implementation/hicasso/src carry no contenteditable refusal and no generic
unsupported-controlled-shape refusal; the nearest neighbours are
:rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled and
:rf.error/hicasso-file-input-value-marker, both bound to other surfaces.
Control: the same scan returns those 27 ids, and every live id named by
docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md's index resolves to both a spec/009 row
and an emitter, so the instrument bites and the zero is real.

THIS IS THE REFUSAL THAT IS RESERVED, NOT BUILT.
:rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable is one of five ids in
troubleshooting.md's "Reserved" table, whose contract is exactly "a refusal
this guide already teaches by mechanism, on a surface that is not built yet"
and "none of them can appear in an error you caught". Chapter 04 is the
guide's teaching-by-mechanism half — but it states the refusal in the PRESENT
TENSE, which the reservation says is not yet true. The testbed agrees with the
reservation and not with chapter 04: implementation/hicasso/testbed carries a
dedicated case `contenteditable-is-not-a-controlled-field` and says in terms
"NOT a controlled field, and this testbed does not pretend it is".

IMPACT. A reader binds :value to a contenteditable expecting a loud refusal at
the source and gets silence plus whatever React does with a stray :value —
which is the approximation the sentence promises will not happen.

FIX SHAPE, not ruled. Either (1) soften chapter 04 to describe the behaviour
without promising a throw — the reservation stays accurate and nothing else
moves, a one-file docs change; or (2) build the refusal and promote
:rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable out of Reserved into the
index, which is an emitter plus a spec/009 row plus the table move, all in one
change per that table's own "promoted, never drifted into" rule. (1) is the
proportionate one while the surface is unbuilt.

PROVENANCE. Found by the rf2-wr0w0 census (docsdrift-a), which REFUTED its own
premise: troubleshooting.md:531 is correct, because the Reserved table means
precisely "no emitter and no spec/009 row yet". Chapter 04 is where the same
subject is actually overstated. Out of that worker's write fence, so filed.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:3x AUSEST — OPTION (1), SOFTEN THE CHAPTER. Recorded as my call so Mike can reverse it cheaply.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE FIRST, at 76ffd860b4, because the bead's own premise is the thing the ruling rests on: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/controlled.cljs:158 recognises exactly ("input" "textarea"), and a grep for contenteditable across that file returns NOTHING — there is no refusal path of any kind, so 'throws at the source' is false in the plain sense, not merely imprecise. docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md carries the sentence verbatim at ~:93-95.

WHY (1) AND NOT (2). Option (2) — build the refusal and promote :rf.error/hicasso-contenteditable-not-controllable out of the Reserved table — is refused on the stance rather than on cost alone, and the reasoning is worth writing down because the opposite conclusion is tempting: a loud refusal DOES read as better ergonomics than silence, and this project does prefer catching a footgun at the source. What decides it against is where the check would have to live. The controlled converge's business is recognising the two shapes it can reconcile; making it also refuse a shape it does not handle means inspecting every non-controlled element for a stray :value, on the converge path, for one footgun that the testbed already documents by name (contenteditable-is-not-a-controlled-field, which says in terms 'this testbed does not pretend it is'). That is a cost on the common path to serve an uncommon mistake, which is the gold-plating the stance names.

AND THE RESERVATION IS ALREADY THE PROJECT'S OWN ANSWER HERE. The Reserved table's contract is 'a refusal this guide already teaches by mechanism, on a surface that is not built yet', with a 'promoted, never drifted into' rule. The reservation is therefore not an omission awaiting repair — it is a deliberate position, and chapter 04's present tense is the thing that drifted away from it. The testbed agrees with the reservation. Only the chapter disagrees, so the chapter is what moves.

WHAT LANDS: chapter 04 describes the behaviour truthfully — Hicasso does not treat a contenteditable region as controlled, so a :value on it is not reconciled and is passed through — while KEEPING the teaching the paragraph exists for (a contenteditable region has no single value to reconcile; use a declared foreign host or named native island). Do not delete the teaching to fix the tense. One file, no emitter, no spec/009 row, no table move.

OPTION (2) STAYS AVAILABLE AND THE ID STAYS RESERVED. If a real user hits this silently, promote it then, in one change per that table's own rule. This ruling closes the drift, not the design question.

title: re-frame.hicasso.server/render is blind to sub exceptions on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host: cold reads go through compute-sub, whose :rf.error/sub-exception is stamped :frame nil
notes:
CARRIED FORWARD FROM SLICE E (rf2-8arzr.5, now closed) BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. Filed so a measured finding does not die with the bead that found it.

THE FINDING, as slice E measured it: the per-frame `pending-error-trace?` buffer reads CLEAN on exactly the failure it was named for. Hicasso s cold reads go through pure `compute-sub`, and `compute-sub` s `:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION -- it is a pure fn with no frame in scope to stamp. `re-frame.ssr.error-listener` buckets by frame address (`pending-error-traces` swap at error_listener.cljc:178, keyed by `frame/frame-address`), so a `:frame nil` record is not in any frame s bucket and a per-frame peek finds nothing.

WHAT SLICE E DID ABOUT IT: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (the new body-only entry, implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:331) watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream instead of the per-frame buffer, so the new crossing path is not affected. That was the right local fix and it shipped.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` (server.cljs:145), the DOCUMENT door used by a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host, has the same blindness today and was not changed. A sub that throws during a Hicasso server render can therefore go unreported on that path.

NOT A DOCS PROBLEM -- CHECKED. Slice F was asked to verify whether any doc describes the blind instrument as though it worked, and none does. docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md s error content is declaration/boot errors (`:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy`, `:rf.error/hicasso-bad-host-declaration`, `:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy`) and the `window is not defined` Render-assertion case; it makes no claim about sub-exception detection during a server render. spec/009:2125 s `pending-error-trace peek` sentence is about `:rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed`, a DIFFERENT path (error-view rendering under the Ring host) that IS frame-stamped and does work. So nothing needed correcting in prose, and slice F corrected nothing here.

SIZING NOTE for whoever takes it: the likely fix is the one slice E already made one file over -- move `render` s detection to the always-on error-emit stream the way `render-body` does -- so this is probably small and has a worked precedent in the same namespace. Worth confirming that `:frame nil` is the only leak before changing anything: `error_listener.cljc:85-100` carries a long comment about a related skip whose reasoning is adjacent and worth reading first.
MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-03 00:3x AUSEST — THIS AND rf2-ypom ARE ONE DEFECT, REACHED FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, AND THEY ARE DISPATCHED TOGETHER. rf2-ct24 was carried forward from slice E; rf2-ypom was filed by the PR #8997 audit. Both name re-frame.hicasso.server/render (server.cljs:145) as blind to recovered sub errors, and both prescribe the same fix: give it the verdict render-body already has. Verified at source at 76ffd860b4 — render is at :145, render-body at :331, and the :errors listener is registered at :323 and unregistered at :413, entirely inside render-body's extent. render has no corresponding registration.

NEITHER IS CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE, because each carries measured evidence the other does not: rf2-ct24 has slice E's mechanism (compute-sub stamps :frame nil BY CONSTRUCTION, being a pure fn with no frame in scope, so error_listener.cljc's per-frame bucketing at ~:178 can never see it) plus the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom has the acceptance criteria (a throwing sub through server/render must get :rf.error/ssr-render-failed, a non-throwing control must return the existing shape unchanged, and the listener and request frame must be released on success, on refusal, and on a direct render throw). One PR closes both with a cross-reference each way.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9035 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9035), the same PR that closes rf2-ypom — SAME DEFECT reached from two directions, cross-referenced both ways. This bead carried slice E's measured mechanism and the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom carried the acceptance criteria. One fix, one PR.

THE FIX: re-frame.hicasso.server/render now watches the always-on :errors stream for its render extent and raises :rf.error/ssr-render-failed on any recovered record — the fix this bead's sizing note predicted, the one slice E had already made one file over. The doors share the lifecycle helpers but register under DIFFERENT ids (::render-recovered-error / ::render-body-recovered-error), because the shipped single id's justification rested on the sidecar isolate's one-render-at-a-time guarantee, which is render-body's premise and not render's.

THE BEAD'S QUESTION ANSWERED: ':frame nil is the only leak' — NO, and error_listener.cljc:85-100 is exactly where the adjacent reasoning starts. Those lines are the :rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed paragraph, the second member of non-projection-eligible-errors: a record that is well-formed AND frame-stamped and still never reaches the buffer, skipped so a re-buffered trace cannot flip a 4xx to a 5xx under a custom projector plus a future re-flush. Reading error-emit-projection-listener out, it buffers only when ALL THREE hold: (1) the category is outside that skip set; (2) (:frame record) is non-nil — the leak this bead names, which compute-sub produces by construction; (3) (error-projector/server-frame? frame-id), i.e. the frame's :platform is :server.

CONDITION 3 IS A SECOND LEAK ON THIS DOOR SPECIFICALLY, and it is the finding worth more than the fix: render does NOT set :platform :server on its per-request frame — only render-body does — so on render the buffer could not fill even for a correctly frame-stamped record. Leaks 2 and 3 each independently suffice. NOT repaired here: giving render a :platform would change client-only-fx gating for every existing caller, well outside a bounded correctness fix. Flagged for whoever wants it.

The fix is unaffected and better justified than argued: the always-on stream sits upstream of all three conditions. refuse-recovered-render-error!'s docstring previously asserted the false premise this bug is made of — that a JVM host is survivable because the same process holds the record — and now states the three measured conditions instead.

WITNESS: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_recovered_error_ssr_cljs_test.cljs (refusal, non-throwing control, release of frame AND listener on all three exits, and the two doors' ids read from INSIDE each render). One existing row changed — see rf2-ypom's close reason for the frame_doors_ssr ambient-read row and the deliberate bluntness of the verdict.

- `grep -rn "npm publish|NPM_TOKEN|registry.npmjs" .github/ scripts/` returns NOTHING. The repo has no npm publishing path at all, for any package.
- .github/workflows/release.yml publishes Maven/Clojars artefacts only. Its jobs are verify-version-lockstep, test, deploy-core, deploy-leaf, deploy-ssr-ring, deploy-hicasso, github-release. The GitHub-release body (:936-949) enumerates fourteen `day8/re-frame2-*` Clojars coordinates and nothing else.
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:100-140 keys ARTEFACT_PATHS off implementation/*/deps.edn entries carrying a :clein/build alias. ssr-node has NO deps.edn and no :clein/build, so the inventory guard at that site correctly leaves it alone -- it is not an omission there, it is out of that mechanism s domain entirely.

So the roster is a Clojars/Maven roster. Adding a plain Node package to it would be wrong in kind, not merely premature.

WHAT THE README ALREADY ASSUMES: implementation/ssr-node/README.md s Deployment section tells an operator to run `re-frame2-ssr-node --module <bundle>` -- the `bin` name from that same private manifest. There is no documented way to get that binary onto a production host. Today the honest answer is "from a checkout of this repo", and the recipe slice F wrote (docs/ssr/concepts.md §Render on Node) uses the bare command without claiming an install channel, which is accurate but incomplete.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS (Mike s, not a worker s): does the sidecar ship? Three coherent answers.
(a) Publish to npm -- drop `private: true`, add an npm publish job to release.yml with a token, and put the package on the release body s roster beside the Clojars coordinates. Version lockstep would then need a fourth mechanism, since the existing one is deps.edn/:clein-shaped.
(b) Vendored-only, deliberately -- keep it private, and say so in the README and the recipe: operators copy the package tree into their deployment. Cheapest, and defensible pre-alpha.
(c) Ship it inside an existing artefact s jar as a resource the JVM host can unpack.

Until one of those is ruled, the recipe and the README should not imply an install channel that does not exist. NOT URGENT: pre-alpha, and (b) is the de facto status quo and works.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST — SPLIT THE BEAD. DO THE HONEST-DOCS HALF NOW; THE SHIPPABILITY HALF IS MIKE'S AND GOES BEHIND THE PUBLISHING CHAIN.

Slice F refuted its OWN dispatch premise here and that refutation is the bead's most valuable content: it was told to grep for the release roster and add ssr-node wherever shippable artefacts are enumerated, and it established there is NOWHERE HONEST TO ADD IT. Measured: package.json declares private:true; a grep for npm publish / NPM_TOKEN / registry.npmjs across .github/ and scripts/ returns NOTHING, so the repo has no npm publishing path AT ALL for any package; release.yml publishes Maven/Clojars only and its GitHub-release body enumerates fourteen Clojars coordinates and nothing else; and verify-version-lockstep.sh keys its inventory off implementation/*/deps.edn entries carrying a :clein/build alias, which ssr-node has none of — so the inventory guard is not omitting it, it is correctly out of scope there. A worker sent to 'add it to the roster' would have had to invent a roster.

THE HALF THAT IS MIKE'S. Publishing an npm artefact from a repo that publishes none is a new distribution capability, not a docs sweep — a product call about what this project ships and supports. It also belongs behind the publishing chain that already holds seven items (rf2-uelji -> rf2-fo4ng -> rf2-kmqx3), because the same question — what gets published under what identity, and who verifies the group — is unresolved one level up. Surfaced to Mike; not dispatched.

THE HALF THAT IS DISPATCHABLE TODAY, and it is the half the bead's TITLE actually names: 'the crossing recipe cannot tell an operator how to obtain the sidecar'. That is a docs-truth defect with an honest answer available right now — say how an operator obtains it TODAY (from the repo, by the route that actually works) and state plainly that no published artefact exists and none is planned as of this writing. That is shippable, costs nothing, and does not pre-empt the product call. What it must NOT do is imply a package is coming, or invent a coordinate; a recipe that names an unpublished coordinate is worse than one that says there is none.

title: adapters/reagent: linearlite_example_cljs_test is green only because a co-loaded sibling owns "/" (false green; 16/51 red in a single-app bundle)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by the rf2-ma8r diagnosis (PR #9000, closed no-change).

re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test passes in the consolidated :node-test
bundle for a reason unrelated to its own subject, and fails 16 of 51 assertions
across 7 of 10 tests the moment it runs in a bundle where the LinearLite app is
the only app.

MECHANISM. Its init! calls (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true})
BEFORE reinstating the :resource/:mutation registrar rows the shared fixture's
reset hook cleared. A :url-bound? frame performs a synchronous initial URL sync
at construction (frame/upsert-frame! post-create hook -> routing's
:routing/on-frame-registered! -> reconcile-url-listener!, syncing
history/current-url, which is "/" under Node). The example registers
:linearlite.app/board at "/" with :resources [{:resource :linearlite/board
:blocking? true}], so the route-entry resource plan runs INSIDE make-frame,
finds the registrar empty, and records :transition :error /
:rf.error/resource-route-plan on the slice. The suite's own navigate never
re-plans, so the error is sticky and 16 assertions read nil.

WHY IT PASSES IN-REPO. At least seven in-tree apps register a route at "/"
(infinite_feed, linearlite, resources, routing, todomvc, realworld_http,
realworld_resources), plus many test suites. In the consolidated bundle "/"
resolves to a SIBLING's route, so LinearLite's board resource is never planned
at construction and the explicit navigate is a genuine transition with
everything registered. The suite's colour therefore depends on which siblings
happen to be co-loaded — it is not evidence about its own subject, and it would
flip red on an unrelated co-load change.

MEASURED. Workspace built per docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md
on the :local/root route: committed baseline exit 0 (10 tests / 51 assertions);
adapter suite verbatim exit 1, 16 failures; changing ONLY the example's route
path from "/" to "/board" -> exit 0, 0 failures.

FIX SHAPE (one line, but NOT dispatched here — the file is inside a live peer's
fence, worker/clientroot-k5r9t owns implementation/adapters/reagent/**):
reorder init! so the registrar/register! reinstatement loop runs BEFORE
(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}), matching the committed
pilot baseline's ordering. That removes the masking dependence entirely.

RELATED. rf2-ma8r carries the full diagnosis and stays open for Mike's ruling
on the two framework questions this exposed: whether a :url-bound? frame
planning route resources at construction is correct, and whether a FAILED route
plan should ever be retried (today an app that recovers stays wedged in
:transition :error permanently).

WORTH A SWEEP: whether any OTHER in-repo example suite is green only by the
same co-load masking. The "/" census above is where to start; the cheap test
is to build each app's suite in a single-app bundle.
notes:
FENCE 2026-09-02 20:41:11 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2-ma8r worker. Its one-line repair (reinstate the registrar rows BEFORE the :url-bound? make-frame) sits in implementation/adapters/reagent/**, which worker/clientroot-k5r9t holds. Dispatch after that PR merges. NOTE WHAT THIS BEAD IS: not a flaky test but a FALSE GREEN — the suite passes in-repo only because a co-loaded sibling owns the "/" route, so its colour is not evidence about its own subject. The worker's residual question is worth carrying into the dispatch: no other in-repo example suite has been swept for the same co-load masking, and the cheap test is one single-app bundle per app.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-02 22:52:40 AUSEST (mayor): the 20:41 fence is DISCHARGED — worker/clientroot-k5r9t's PR #8992 MERGED at cd6fd08587 (53 files, the adapter client root plus the examples sweep), so implementation/adapters/reagent/** is held by nobody. Dispatched solo this tick.

RE-DERIVE BEFORE EDITING: #8992 changed this very adapter — it added public client-root / render! / unmount! on re-frame.adapter.reagent and reagent-slim, regenerated the api manifest 491->494, and rewrote 24 example entrypoints plus 3 SSR examples to mount through the adapter's client root. The example whose route path this bead discusses is among the files it touched. Every line number here predates it.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by PR #9027 (head 051f8976a7, base c06b76dc36).

REPRODUCED FIRST, on a tree that had moved past PR #8992. The bead's mechanism
held verbatim at tip: init! still created the :url-bound? frame before the
registrar/register! reinstatement loop. Built in a single-app :node-test bundle
(ns-regexp anchored to this suite alone), the committed tree gave
"Ran 10 tests containing 51 assertions. 16 failures, 0 errors.", captured
exit 1 — the bead's 16-of-51 across 7-of-10 exactly. After the fix, same bundle:
"Ran 10 tests containing 51 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.", captured exit 0.
That red-then-green pair is the control; it is also what proves the instrument
was reading the worker's own worktree.

WHICH REPAIR. The bead's FIX SHAPE section rules for reordering init! so the
registrar reinstatement runs BEFORE the :url-bound? make-frame, matching the
committed pilot baseline. That is what landed, and it is the right call: the
alternative one-liner the bead records under MEASURED — moving the example's
route off "/" — also goes green, but only by dodging the collision, leaving the
ordering bug intact and the suite still dependent on nobody else owning "/".
Followed the baseline's stricter form (make-frame LAST, after the fx stubs and
install-routing-integration! too, not merely after the doseq), since the baseline
is what the bead nominates and it documents the rule as "the frame is made last".
The ordering constraint and its cause are now in the init! docstring so a future
edit cannot silently undo it.

SECOND DEFECT, found by the sweep and fixed in the same PR.
re-frame.resources-example-cljs-test was green by the same disease through a
different organ: examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs calls
rf/reg-machine :resources.app/reader but required neither re-frame.machines nor
anything pulling it in. Machines are an optional artefact, so the call resolves
only when a co-loaded sibling has already loaded it. Alone, the example's ns-load
throws :rf.error/machines-artefact-missing before a single test runs (captured
exit 1, 0 tests). Every other example calling reg-machine already requires
re-frame.machines in the same file; this was the sole omission. After: 9 tests /
39 assertions, 0 failures.

CO-LOAD SWEEP — the bead's residual question, answered. Fifteen example suites
each built in their own single-app bundle: 155 tests / 1180 assertions, all green
on the final base. All SEVEN apps registering a route at "/" are covered
(infinite_feed, linearlite, realworld_http, realworld_resources, resources,
routing, todomvc). A census of every reg-route form under examples/
(paren-balanced over flattened text, control-checked first) shows LinearLite is
the ONLY app with a BLOCKING route resource at "/", which is exactly why it was
the only hard failure of that mechanism.

NOT COVERED, named rather than left open: the ~11,000-test framework remainder of
the :node-test lane was not swept for co-load masking among framework suites, and
re-frame.example-frame-scoping-cljs-test is excluded by construction (it loads
seven apps deliberately; cross-app scoping is its subject). Three suites share
the make-frame-before-register! ordering and are green only because their "/"
routes declare no blocking resource — infinite_feed_example,
realworld_resources, resources_example. Latent rather than broken; carried by
rf2-djqm rather than churned here.

METHOD NOTE for the next person building a single-app bundle. Narrowing
:ns-regexp against the shared :node-test id is what rf2-6t03c forbids doing
directly, so go through scripts/compile-node-test.cjs's cache-isolation helper
(core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache.cjs). But that script clears the build cache
AFTER compiling, and a dev-target :node-test bundle SHADOW_IMPORTs its modules
from that same directory at RUN time — so running the bundle after the script
exits dies with ENOENT on goog.debug.error.js before any test executes. The run
must happen inside the isolated window: clear -> compile -> RUN -> clear.
Runtime selection (node out/node-test.js --test=<ns>) does NOT substitute: it
filters which tests RUN while leaving every sibling namespace LOADED, which is
precisely the co-load this bead is about.

STILL OPEN AND NOT ADDRESSED HERE: rf2-ma8r's two framework questions — whether a
:url-bound? frame planning route resources AT CONSTRUCTION is correct, and
whether a FAILED route plan should ever be retried (an app that recovers stays
wedged in :transition :error permanently). This fix removes the masking; it does
not answer either question.
AUDIT PR #9027: REOPENED FOR COMPLETENESS. Both repairs are source-correct, and the isolated red/green probes are persuasive, but neither repair has a durable non-vacuous gate. This matters because the PR proves the ordinary consolidated :node-test bundle was green before both fixes: a sibling route masked LinearLite's make-frame ordering, and a sibling namespace loaded re-frame.machines for the resources example. The committed diff changes only those two subjects. The fifteen single-app builds were one-off audit evidence, not a checked-in regression instrument; test:cljs-isolation also runs selectors against the already consolidated bundle and therefore cannot remove ns-load co-loading. Moving make-frame back up or deleting the new machines require can consequently leave current CI green again.

Minimal completion: add one focused, durable bundle-isolation control covering the two fixed subjects. It must compile/load each subject without sibling example namespaces, go red on the pre-fix LinearLite ordering and missing machines require, and stay cheap enough for the existing example/adapter lane; do not institutionalise the full fifteen-build sweep. Keep the three merely latent fixture orderings on rf2-djqm and the route-retry ruling on rf2-ma8r.

title: skill(re-frame2-setup): first_counter_derivation.clj silently regenerates on any argument, and its writeback dirties the tree on Windows (LF + a stray blank line)
description:
FOUND while running gates for PR #9012 (rf2-pygpw/0ddz3/6uq6n cluster).

CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/first_counter_derivation.clj is documented in README.md and spec/design.md as the script that renders the two generated regions from the template. A worker reasonably reaches for a no-write verification mode.

TRUTH AT TIP. There is no such mode and no argument parsing at all: the script has no reference to *command-line-args*, and its last act is an unconditional (spit leaf (replace-region (slurp leaf) region)) at line 246. So 'bb tests/first_counter_derivation.clj --check' does NOT check — the argument is ignored, the script runs its normal generate-and-write path, exits 0, and the operator reads the 0 as a passing check. That is the failure-open shape: a well-formed green from an instrument that did the opposite of what was asked.

SECOND, and what makes it visible: the writeback is not byte-idempotent on Windows. Running it against an unmodified tip checkout leaves BOTH leaves modified — references/first-counter.md and references/entry-namespace.md — each with exactly one added blank line, plus git warning 'LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it' on both. The committed files are CRLF; the script writes LF. The content is otherwise correct: bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj Lock 0 (first-counter-region-is-the-template-render) passes at 35 tests / 271 assertions both before and after, so this is a line-ending and trailing-newline artifact of the writeback, NOT drift in the rendered region.

IMPACT. Low severity, but it fails open twice over. A worker who runs it 'to verify' gets a green that verified nothing AND a dirty tree carrying two files they did not edit — which, staged with a careless 'git add', lands a spurious whitespace diff on two drift-locked generated leaves. FIX SHAPE (skills/re-frame2-setup/** only). close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9036 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9036). Both symptoms reproduced from a clean checkout first, then fixed.

(1) Ignored argument. 'bb tests/first_counter_derivation.clj --check' wrote both leaves and exited 0 - the script parsed no arguments at all. It now fails CLOSED on any argument before a byte is written, mirroring the template's own hooks/gate-arg-keys! (which this script already loads for its substitution values). Chose the bead's option (a), not (b): the script only ever writes, so no argument is meaningful, and rather than growing a second checker the usage line routes the caller to the no-write check that already exists - 'bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj'. That avoids a divergent second source of truth. Junk argument now exits 2 with nothing written.

(2) Dirty tree - two distinct causes, and separating them was the substance. A REAL content change: replace-region emitted a newline the tail already carried, appending a blank line per leaf. The bead says 'exactly one'; it is in fact CUMULATIVE - three runs produced three added lines per leaf. A PHANTOM modification: the LF writeback over CRLF-checked-out leaves is not a content change at all (git diff empty, git hash-object --path matches the committed blob) but git status reports the file modified and every later git command warns 'LF will be replaced by CRLF'. Fixed by rendering on LF (the convention setup_drift_test.clj already uses, since LF is what git stores) and restoring the leaf's existing endings on write.

Verified: three consecutive regenerations leave git status CLEAN, both leaves' blob hashes identical to the committed objects, CRLF preserved (401/185 CRLF, 0 bare LF). bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj green at 35 tests / 271 assertions, captured exit 0, and proven to read this worktree by planted fault (exit 1, 11 failures naming the plant; restore verified by blob hash 99af663ea1a3137cf5861b55e995f811b8b701d4).

notes:
MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-03 04:1x AUSEST — THIS IS ONE OF THREE, AND THE CLASS IS NARROWER THAN IT FIRST LOOKS. Three open beads now report the same shape: a marker in the tree gated on a bead id that does not exist. rf2-fgwf cites rf2-k0rbk, rf2-rn3u cites rf2-mxkq7, and rf2-0d1w reports an ambient-frame-refused PROVISIONAL note citing a nonexistent bead. All three ids confirmed absent by bd show.

I TRIED TO CENSUS THE CLASS AND THE CENSUS WAS INVALID — recording that here so nobody repeats it. Matching every rf2-* token in implementation/, tools/, docs/, spec/ and examples/ against the tracker export returns 5,179 distinct cited ids of which 4,997 are absent. That number is meaningless: this repo deliberately keeps historical bead citations in prose as provenance, and the tracker holds only ~516 issues, so essentially every citation older than the current tracker reads as absent. CLAUDE.md itself cites rf2-0yp7w as the authoritative ui/freehand retirement disposition, and rf2-0yp7w.4 — its own child — is likewise absent. A scan returning EVERYTHING is not corroboration; it means the comparison set was wrong.

THE REAL CLASS IS NOT 'A CITATION TO A DEAD BEAD', WHICH IS NORMAL HERE. It is A LIVE CONDITIONAL GATED ON NOTHING — a PROVISIONAL marker, a pending-on annotation, a 'revisit when X lands' note whose X cannot be found. A historical citation records why something is the way it is and ages harmlessly; a pending marker is a promise to revisit that nobody can ever discharge, and it will sit in the tree forever looking like live tracking.

SO A SWEEP HERE IS WORTH DOING AND MUST BE SCOPED TO PENDING MARKERS, NOT TO CITATIONS. Search for the marker vocabulary (PROVISIONAL, pending, 'until rf2-', 'when rf2-', 'blocked on rf2-', 'revisit') and resolve only the ids those markers gate. Exercise the instrument in both directions: a marker citing a REAL open bead must be found and left alone, and one citing a real CLOSED bead is a third case — the promise was discharged and the marker is stale, which is a different fix from a phantom.

Whoever takes this bead: do the scoped sweep as part of it and report the count. Two siblings (rf2-rn3u, rf2-0d1w) are the other known instances.

## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md` is 318 lines / 63,758 bytes — 4x the 16 KB per-leaf byte ceiling in `skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline (1.3x the 250-line ceiling; the byte ceiling exists precisely for long unwrapped table rows like this file's). The catalogue exemption there is a test, not a pass: "would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?"

## APPLYING THE CATALOGUE TEST HONESTLY

ops.md is two things stapled together:

**Catalogue (keep together, locked):** §Read, §Frames, §Write, §Trace, §Live watch, §Signal recording, §Hot-reload coordination, §Time-travel, §Dropped from v1 — op tables plus the protocol sections that `spec/design.md:134` and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:33` explicitly LOCK into ops.md ("The hot-reload protocol and v1 → v2 surface-map both live in ops.md as sections rather than separate leaves"), and that `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` reads from ops.md by anchor (`ops.md#hot-reload-coordination`, `section-from @ops-md "Hot-reload coordination"`). Roughly 42 KB.

**Not catalogue (split candidate):** lines 108–203, ~22 KB — §DOM source bridge, §Reading what's on screen (`read-dom` vs `read-ui`), and §Hicasso evidence (mounted boundaries / read attribution / render cause). This is a self-contained "what is on screen and why did it render" concern: the Hicasso block alone is ~10 KB of honesty-marker prose (added under rf2-6c12m, `3043d1aca4`, AFTER the file-structure lock was written), not op rows. SKILL.md's loading map already routes to it as its own task shape (`SKILL.md:186-188`: two rows pointing at `ops.md#view--rendered-content…` and `ops.md#hicasso-evidence…`), and `mcp-transport.md:84-88` links the five screen/evidence tools to those anchors.

Token test, both directions: an agent doing a read/dispatch/trace/time-travel session loads 64 KB and never reads the 22 KB screen block; an agent answering "why did this boundary render?" loads 64 KB for a 10 KB section. A split reduces tokens-per-session for every session that is not both — which is nearly all of them. That is the opposite of the "multiplies file handles without reducing tokens" case the exemption protects.

## RECOMMENDATION (one PR)

- New leaf `references/screen-reads.md` (~22 KB — itself still over the ceiling, but one concern; name is a suggestion) holding ops.md lines 108–203 verbatim: DOM source bridge, read-dom vs read-ui, Hicasso evidence.

- Do NOT split hot-reload or the v1 map (locked + tested), and do not split the op tables (that is the catalogue the exemption is for).

If the maintainer would rather keep ops.md whole, the honest alternative is to record ops.md as an accepted exception in `skills/README.md` §Leaf size discipline with the reasoning — the current state is neither.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose` (mcp-transport.md rows survive; 29 = 29); `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (every moved anchor resolves — skills/ is in its roots; this is the gate that catches a broken `ops.md#hicasso-…` link); `bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` (`skill-router-still-points-at-hot-reload`, `hot-reload-*`, `ops-md-raw-eval-rows-carry-privacy-carveout` all read ops.md and must stay green — they will, since nothing they name moves). value:
A CENSUS THAT FLAGS ALMOST EVERYTHING IS NOT A DEFECT CLASS — IT IS A BROKEN COMPARISON SET, AND IT READS AS CORROBORATION (2026-09-03).

WHAT HAPPENED. Three beads independently reported the same shape: a marker in the tree gated on a bead id that does not exist. I tried to census the class by matching every rf2-* token across implementation/, tools/, docs/, spec/ and examples/ against the tracker export. Result: 5,179 distinct cited ids, 4,997 absent. I nearly reported that as a finding.

IT IS MEANINGLESS. The tracker holds ~516 issues; the tree carries thousands of historical citations, and this repo DELIBERATELY keeps them as provenance. CLAUDE.md itself cites rf2-0yp7w as the authoritative ui/freehand retirement disposition, and rf2-0yp7w.4 — its own child — is absent from the tracker too. So 'cited but absent' is the NORMAL state of a citation older than the current tracker, and a scan that flags 96% of its subject has told you about its own scope, not about the tree.

THE SHAPE OF THE MISTAKE, which loops.md already names for the inverse: a search returning ZERO is not a check that passed. THE INVERSION READS EVEN BETTER, because a scan returning EVERYTHING looks like a rich finding rather than like silence. Ask what the instrument COMPARED, not what it answered.

THE REAL CLASS, once scoped correctly, is narrow and worth fixing: not 'a citation to a dead bead' but A LIVE CONDITIONAL GATED ON NOTHING — a PROVISIONAL marker, a pending-on annotation, a 'revisit when X lands' note whose X cannot be found. A historical citation records why something is as it is and ages harmlessly. A pending marker is a promise to revisit that nobody can discharge, and it sits in the tree forever looking like live tracking. Search the MARKER VOCABULARY (PROVISIONAL, pending, 'until rf2-', 'when rf2-', 'blocked on rf2-'), then resolve only the ids those markers gate — and expect THREE outcomes, not two: phantom id, real-and-open (leave alone), real-and-closed (the promise was discharged, so the marker is stale, which is a different fix).

THIS IS THE SECOND INSTRUMENT FAILURE IN TWO BACKLOG-REREAD TICKS AND THEY ARE THE SAME FAMILY — a sweep whose comparison set was wrong. The other was bd-json-piped-to-jq-emits-crlf-and-silently-breaks-id-loops, where the set was right and the KEYS were corrupted. Both produced a confident number. The defence that works for both: exercise the instrument in both directions using data drawn from the SAME pipeline as the real input, never a literal typed on the command line.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): the ops.md catalogue-exemption ruling and the package's own spec contradict each other
description:
FOUND BY worker pairskill-e while executing rf2-wgvyx's ruling (PR #9037). NOT a re-argument of that ruling — a contradiction it leaves standing, which needs a maintainer call rather than a worker's reflex.

THE MAYOR RULING on rf2-wgvyx (2026-09-03 03:2x AUSEST) says: 'SPLIT THE HICASSO-EVIDENCE BLOCK OUT... THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION IS REFUSED FOR THIS LEAF.'

SO THE REFUSAL NOW HAS NO EXECUTABLE REMAINDER, and that is the problem:

1. ops.md is 220 lines / 46,461 LF-normalised bytes — 2.8x the 16 KB per-leaf ceiling in skills/README.md.
2. Every section left in it is one rf2-wgvyx EXPLICITLY FORBIDS splitting: 'Do NOT split hot-reload or the v1 map (locked + tested), and do not split the op tables (that is the catalogue the exemption is for)'. Remaining headings: Read, Frames, Write, Trace, Live watch, Signal recording, Hot-reload coordination, Time-travel, Dropped from v1.
3. The hot-reload protocol and v1 surface-map placement is LOCKED by skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:33, and tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj reads ops.md by anchor (ops.md#hot-reload-coordination).
4. AND THE PACKAGE'S OWN SPEC STILL GRANTS THE EXEMPTION IN WRITING, in both places, unchanged: design.md:135 'the two catalogue leaves (ops.md, recipes.md) run longer where a split would not reduce tokens-per-session', and authoring-prompt.md:49 the same clause. A future re-authoring pass reads those and keeps ops.md whole, because that is what they say.

So the tree currently asserts both things at once: the ruling refuses ops.md the exemption, the package spec grants it.

THE DECISION NEEDED is one of three, and it is Mike's or the mayor's, not a worker's:
(a) RECORD THE EXEMPTION HONESTLY — accept ops.md as a documented exception in skills/README.md Leaf size discipline with the reasoning, and leave design.md:135 as is. rf2-wgvyx's own DESCRIPTION already names this as the honest alternative: 'If the maintainer would rather keep ops.md whole, the honest alternative is to record ops.md as an accepted exception... the current state is neither.'
(b) NAME WHICH LOCKED SECTION MOVES, and lift the lock on it in design.md + authoring-prompt.md in the same PR, re-pointing the prompt-regression anchors.
(c) RESTATE THE REFUSAL as applying only to non-catalogue blocks, which is what it in fact achieved, and strike the ceiling claim against ops.md.

Note recipes.md sits in exactly the same position (424 lines / 46,086 B) and is the exemption's own worked example, so whichever way this goes should say whether it binds recipes.md too.

NOT URGENT AND NOT A BUG: nothing is broken, no gate is red, no reader is misled by ops.md's content. What is wrong is that two normative records disagree, so the next re-authoring pass gets a different answer depending on which it reads.

WHAT I DID. Two hours ago I ruled that ops.md is REFUSED the catalogue exemption, reasoning that a leaf from which a self-contained block can be lifted entire is not catalogue-shaped. I derived that from the first split's success and from the leaf still measuring 46 KB. I did not check whether any record already GRANTED the exemption. Two do, in writing: skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/design.md:135 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:49.

SO THERE ARE NOW TWO NORMATIVE RECORDS IN DISAGREEMENT, and that is a maintainer call rather than something a worker should resolve by picking the newer one. Filing it was the correct response and I am not overriding it here.

AND MY RULING'S FACTUAL PREMISE WAS ALSO WRONG, which the same worker established: the Hicasso-evidence block did NOT remain in ops.md. It came out WITH the screen-read block in the same commit eaf6591310 — 105 lines removed, screen-reads.md created with 106, carrying all three sections the bead's own recommendation nominated, Hicasso evidence among them. ops.md's only case-insensitive hicasso match is a Contents pointer. title: conformance corpus has no EDN well-formedness gate — a fixture with trailing text loads and passes having verified less than it claims
description:
DISCOVERED while fixing rf2-5mr6 (PR: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn had one extra closing brace).

GAP. No gate in the tree checks that a conformance fixture is a well-formed EDN file containing exactly ONE top-level form. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string over the whole file, which returns the FIRST form and IGNORES everything after it. A fixture whose expectation block is closed early therefore loads, runs, and reports as PASSING while the assertions that fell outside the block are silently discarded. That is exactly what rf2-5mr6 was: bracket depth -1, two trace assertions never executed, green for however long it had been there (introducing commit not bisected).

WHY IT WAS NOT ADDED IN THAT PR. No script under scripts/ or .github/ iterates spec/conformance/fixtures/ at all — check_retired_spellings.py and report-changed-surfaces.sh only NAME the directory. So the check has no existing home; it is a new script plus its own CI wiring plus a fast-PR spine entry, which is a bigger call than the one-character fix it would have guarded.

TWO SHAPES, AND THE SECOND IS THE SHARPER ONE.

(a) A corpus scanner. Python, stdlib only, in the shape of the repo's other spec-coherence gates. The scanner used to measure rf2-5mr6 works and is the algorithm to lift: walk the text, blank ;; comments to end of line, treat a double-quoted string as opaque (honouring backslash escapes), treat a backslash as introducing a one-character char literal, then count ([{ against )]}. Report a defect when final depth is not 0, when min depth ever goes negative, or when the file holds other than exactly one top-level form. Measured 2026-09-03: 247 fixtures scanned, 0 defects after the fix; the pre-fix routing-not-found.edn reports final-depth=-1 top-level-forms=1 neg-at-line=60. Exercised in BOTH directions before either result was believed.

(b) Make the LOADERS refuse trailing text. This is the better fix because it cannot drift from what the runner actually parses, and it is a few lines in each of the two host-specific loaders: implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj (load-fixture-from-file) and the JVM leaf's slurp + read-string in implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj. Read with a PushbackReader and assert EOF after the first form, or read (str "[" content "]") and assert exactly one element. A fixture with trailing text then fails LOUD at load, in the same run that would otherwise pass it, on every host that loads the corpus. The CLJS leaf inlines fixtures at compile time, so it needs the equivalent at its macro seam.

Prefer (b), or (b) plus (a) — (a) also catches a fixture that never reaches a loader because its capabilities are unclaimed, which (b) cannot see. A fixture whose capabilities are out of claim is SKIPPED by the runner, so a defect in one is invisible to (b) forever.

ACCEPTANCE. A fixture with a deliberately misplaced brace fails a gate that runs on every PR touching spec/conformance/. Prove it by planting one and showing the red, not by showing the green on a clean corpus — a search that returns zero is not a check that passed.
close_reason:
Shape (a), the corpus scanner, landed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9038 as scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py, wired as two unconditional STEPS in the existing verify-skill-mcp-drift invariant job (no new job key: the two-space discriminator reads 0 on the diff and 1 on control commit 366e4fca79) plus an always-on lane in the fast-PR spine, which check_fast_pr_gap.py requires.

The scanner lifts the algorithm recorded on this bead: ';' comments blanked to end of line, double-quoted strings opaque with backslash escapes, a backslash outside a string consuming a one-character char literal, then brackets counted. It reports a defect on negative depth, on non-zero final depth, on an unterminated string, and on anything other than exactly one top-level form. Both halves are load-bearing and the self-test proves each separately: a balanced '{:a 1} {:b 2}' passes a depth-only check and is still caught, and a 'reads without error' check catches nothing at all since that is exactly what read-string does.

MEASURED. 247 fixtures, 0 defects at the PR's base - both numbers re-measured rather than carried over. Against the pre-fix routing-not-found.edn recovered from a54088ee7e^: exit 1, final-depth=-1, closing bracket at line 60, matching this bead's recorded measurement. title: 398 links in shipped skill docs resolve outside their own package and are broken in the published tarball
description:
MEASURED while fixing rf2-kgw8z (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9038).

FINDING. check_skill_package_refs.py now scopes links by where they RESOLVE rather than by how they are spelled. Classifying every ../-shaped link across the nine published skills:

  outside the package root          398   currently OUT OF SCOPE
  inside the package, shipped        52   checked, passes
  inside the package, unshipped       3   checked, all carry a monorepo-only marker

The 398 are real breakage in the published artefact. skills/re-frame2-improver/references/README.md links ../../re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md and ../../../spec/014-HTTPRequests.md; skills/re-frame2/references/** does the same. Each skill publishes as its OWN npm package (package.json) and its OWN plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) with its own name, version and repository.directory - so in an installed package there is no sibling re-frame2/ to resolve against and no monorepo spec/ above it. A reader following one of those links from a tarball install gets nothing.

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED IN THAT PR. It is deliberate documented behaviour, not an oversight: check_skill_package_refs.py's docstring has always said links escaping the package point at the monorepo rather than the tarball and are out of scope, with check_doc_slugs.py validating that their targets exist IN THE REPO. That rationale is sound for a monorepo reader and silent for a package reader. Turning 398 links red across nine packages is a ruling about what a published skill promises, not a worker's call, and it is far larger than the bead that surfaced it.

THE OPTIONS, none costed here. (i) Accept as-is - cross-skill links are for monorepo readers, and the packages are understood to be read in place. (ii) Mark them - the existing _MONOREPO_ONLY_MARKERS mechanism already excuses a line, and the three improver ../spec/design.md links show the pattern working; 398 markers is a lot of prose. (iii) Rewrite the escaping links as absolute GitHub URLs, which resolve for both readers. (iv) Ship the referenced trees. Mike rules.

MECHANISM NOTE. The gate is ready for whichever way this goes: the check already resolves every link and already knows which side of the package root it lands on. Making the outside-the-package case a finding is the ValueError branch in _broken_package_links, plus a self-test case. The marker mechanism needs no change.

GATE. scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --self-test, then the live scan.

title: bug(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render accepts recovered render errors
description:
## Finding

PR #8997 measured that Hicasso's pure compute-sub SSR reads emit recovered subscription failures with `:frame nil`, so the per-frame SSR error accumulator cannot see them. Its new `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` correctly watches the always-on error stream for the synchronous render extent and refuses the page. The sibling whole-page `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` remains unchanged: it renders markup and assembles the payload/document without the same verdict. A registered sub can therefore throw, recover to `nil`, and still produce a successful but wrong SSR page.

## Recommended action

Apply the same bounded recovered-error verdict to `render`, sharing the smallest lifecycle helper with `render-body` if that keeps the two doors aligned. Preserve the settled public spellings and response shape; this is one missing correctness check, not a renderer redesign.

## Evidence

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: `render-body` registers the `:errors` listener and refuses `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`; `render` has no corresponding check.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_body_ssr_cljs_test.cljs` proves an ordinary throwing sub otherwise recovers and returns markup.
- The rf2-8arzr.5 implementation note explicitly records the standing implication that whole-page `server/render` has the same blindness.
- Duplicate searches for `whole-page Hicasso recovered render error`, `server/render blindness`, `pending-error-trace Hicasso`, `compute-sub-driven SSR`, and `ssr-render-failed` found no owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused test renders an ordinary registered sub that throws through `server/render` and gets `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`, while a non-throwing control returns the existing map/document shape unchanged.
- The error listener and request frame are released on success, recovered-error refusal, and a direct render throw.
- `render-body` retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions or residue.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #9035.

The recovered-error fix uses one fixed listener id per door, so it closes cross-door replacement but not same-door replacement. server.cljs explicitly acknowledges the remaining hole in render-body-listener-id's docstring: a door re-entering itself reuses its id, registration REPLACES the outer listener, and the inner finally unregisters it. The same mechanics apply to render-listener-id.

Concrete failure sequence: an outer render arms its atom; a view enters the same door; the inner registration replaces the outer callback; the inner finally removes that id; the outer view catches/continues, then a later subscription error recovers to nil. No listener remains to record it, so the outer render returns the same successful wrong page this bead owns. React rejecting a nested render does not make this safe: the inner finally still removes the outer listener when the view catches that direct throw.

The new test section 4 observes each door separately and proves only that their two fixed ids differ. It never nests render inside render or render-body inside render-body, so the acceptance requirement that the sibling retain refusal semantics without listener collisions is not fully met.

Minimal repair: make the registration key unique per invocation (for example, pair the door tag with the already-unique request frame id) and unregister that exact key. Its ruling said explicitly: if a half still exceeds 16 KB after the split, report the figure and stop rather than trimming to reach it. The obvious instinct — split again — is the thing to check rather than assume: SS-M-11 is one migration rule, and a rule split across two leaves is a SKILL -> A -> B routing problem or a reader who has to load both, either of which is worse than the ceiling breach. Establish first whether the section has a genuine internal seam the way runtime-smoke-test.md had a checklist/loop seam. If it does not, the honest options are the catalogue exemption (test: would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?) or an explicit recorded exception, and BOTH are family-contract calls for the mayor or Mike, not a worker.

A catalogue reader at least MIGHT need only one entry; an M-11 reader needs M-11. Splitting a single rule across two leaves produces either a SKILL -> A -> B chain, which the family contract forbids outright, or a reader loading both halves every time plus an extra file handle. So the test's answer is NO with no ambiguity, and the shape qualifier is the part that does not fit.

WHY THAT IS NOT A LOOPHOLE. The test is what the bullet says decides; the shape is how it describes the case it had in mind. A leaf that passes the test for a reason the bullet did not anticipate is a gap in the bullet's wording, not a licence to ignore the ceiling — which is exactly why this ruling is RECORD THE EXCEPTION rather than CLAIM THE EXEMPTION. Write it as a named exception with its reason, so the next size audit reads a decision instead of re-deriving one, and so nobody generalises it to leaves that merely happen to be large.
