WHAT I HAD BEEN WRITING, correctly, until this merge: 'it passes green on a link to a non-existent file, because it checks allow-list membership and delegates existence to check_doc_slugs.py, so its green is not evidence a link resolves.' That was measured and true. STOP WRITING IT.

WHAT IT DOES NOW: it judges an in-package link by WHERE IT RESOLVES rather than skipping every ../ form. The old skip's premise was that a ../ link escapes the package; the worker established that premise is what fails — a ../ from a nested doc usually lands back INSIDE the package. Measured on the live tree: 398 links resolve outside, 52 inside-and-shipped, 3 inside-and-unshipped, and 55 moved from UNEXAMINED to EXAMINED with the tree still green. A self-test case pins that it did NOT become an existence checker, which remains check_doc_slugs.py's job.

ALSO LANDED IN THE SAME PR: scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py, a new stdlib-only lexical scanner over spec/conformance/fixtures/ that refuses a file which is not a SINGLE well-formed EDN form with nothing after it. It catches both shapes — an unbalanced brace AND a balanced second top-level form — which matters because both loaders use edn/read-string, which returns the FIRST form and ignores trailing text. Live corpus reads 247 fixtures / 0 defects. It is wired as STEPS inside an existing job plus a fast-PR spine lane, NOT as a new job key, deliberately: a new job key would move the check set every open PR is measured against. Verified after the merge — the band stayed at 86.

THE 398 IS NOT A DEFECT COUNT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE HERE. Those links resolve outside their own package and so are broken in the published tarballs, which is real and is filed separately as rf2-nvbz — a ruling rather than a worker's call. The gate leaves them alone today.

NOMINATION GUIDANCE FROM HERE: for a skill-package link question, check_skill_package_refs.py --ci is now a real check of package boundaries; check_doc_slugs.py still owns anchors and target existence; neither looks inside a fenced code block.

title: skill(reagent-migration): the fully-migrated end state is untaught — with zero Reagent views left, (rf/init! substrate/adapter) retires the Reagent dependency
description:
## CLAIM

- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:259-270` (MIG-15): "**`(rf/init! ...)` stays** ... Keep the app's existing adapter install; it is not Reagent-specific scaffolding to be deleted. ... Hicasso does ship an adapter of its own (`re-frame.hicasso.substrate`), but it is an optional module nothing under Hicasso's own source requires, so `h/mount!` neither installs it nor displaces what the app has."
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:283-293` (MIG-24): "drop `reagent.*` requires **only when the namespace has zero remaining uses**".
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md:390-394` (MIG-23, the one mention, buried in the SSR recipe): "Adapter selection is not part of this migration ... (a Hicasso-only app may deliberately choose `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, but that is its own decision)."
- `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:138-150` Done checklist and hand-off: "Views rewritten into Hicasso where it made sense; the rest stay on Reagent" — nothing for the case where nothing stays.
- `evals/evals.json` notes: "Do NOT re-grade this fixture [25] as 'switch to the Hicasso adapter': choosing an adapter is not part of this migration." (Correct for the part-migrated boot it grades; this bead does not touch it.)

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:1-25` — "Hicasso's own reactive-substrate adapter — the value an application installs with `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` ... what lets a Hicasso application depend on core plus Hicasso and nothing else: without this namespace an interactive one would have to add a SECOND dependency coordinate — `day8/re-frame2-uix` or a Reagent one — purely to obtain the second half, and then never write a line of that substrate's notation."
- `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:144-160` §Hicasso needs a substrate adapter: "every Hicasso application calls `rf/init!` with an adapter ... `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` ... ships inside `day8/re-frame2-hicasso`, so that line costs no coordinate."
- rf2-hvr5h (closed 2026-08-19, PR #8512): "a Hicasso application depends on core plus Hicasso and nothing else". `spec/Conventions.md:103` rosters `:rf.adapter/hicasso`.

## IMPACT

The part-migrated guidance is right and stays: while any Reagent view remains, the Reagent adapter stays. But the skill never names the END state. Once every view is converted, `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is the last `reagent.*` require standing, and its only job was the substrate. Read together, MIG-15's "not scaffolding to be deleted" and MIG-24's "zero remaining uses" tell that author to keep `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and `reagent` in `deps.edn` indefinitely — exactly the second-coordinate cost rf2-hvr5h built the substrate to remove. For a consumer that migrates to completion (the trigger the skill exists for), the skill leaves a dead dependency and never says the option exists. Trust-the-programmer means naming the choice, not withholding it.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill files only; eval 25's part-migrated grading unchanged)

1. `references/catalog-mechanical.md` MIG-24 — one closing paragraph: "When the last Reagent view is gone, `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is the last `reagent.*` require, and it was only ever the substrate. `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` from `[re-frame.hicasso.substrate :as substrate]` (`:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso`) replaces that line and lets the app drop `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and `reagent` from `deps.edn`. The author's call, not this skill's (cardinal rule 5), and never while a Reagent view remains." Add a one-line pointer from MIG-15's "stays" bullet.
2. `SKILL.md` Done checklist — one line: "If no Reagent view remains, the author was told the adapter choice is now open (MIG-24) — not switched for them."
3. Optional: a new M-tier behavioural eval ("every view is converted — can I drop Reagent now?") passing an answer that names `substrate/adapter` and the dependency drop as the author's decision, failing one that says the Reagent adapter must stay.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --ci`. The `substrate/adapter` spelling and `:kind` verified by hand against `substrate.cljs` (no gate reads prose).

## ACCEPTANCE

MIG-24 names the completed-migration option with the exact require, the `rf/init!` line and the two dependencies it retires; the done checklist carries the line; eval 25 unchanged; gates exit 0.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 (HEAD d12181c4c3; no relevant diff) on 2026-09-02 12:00:31 AUSEST.
acceptance_criteria: MIG-24 names re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter (:rf.adapter/hicasso) as the completed-migration option that lets the app drop day8/re-frame2-reagent + reagent, as the author's call; done checklist carries the line; eval 25 unchanged; gates exit 0
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9008 — REOPENED. MIG-24 and eval 29 now infer that when no Reagent VIEW remains, re-frame.adapter.reagent is the last Reagent use and both day8/re-frame2-reagent and reagent/reagent may go. That implication is not established: this skill is explicitly views-only, and a consumer can retain non-view reagent.core / reagent.ratom use (or another namespace requiring Reagent) after every view is Hicasso. Removing the coordinates then breaks the build. Keep the ergonomic option, but gate it on the reporter plus a repository-wide remaining-requires/API census. Distinguish the adapter-coordinate decision from removing a direct reagent/reagent entry, and add an eval case with zero Reagent views but a surviving non-view Reagent use so the skill says what must stay. This is the exact completed-migration owner, not a new bead.
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #9036.

The coordinate split is directionally right, but its new proof for dropping reagent/reagent asks a call-site census to prove dependency absence. The reporter explicitly estimates Reagent API CALL SITES; it does not enumerate Reagent Vars/types/macros/config references used outside call-head position. The shipped text nevertheless says zero call sites plus no UNRESOLVED clause licenses dropping the coordinate.

Reproduced against the reporter at this PR tip with a live non-call use:

(ns app.core (:require [reagent.core :as r]))
(def factory r/atom)

census/scan-string returns {:entries [], :reagent? true, :unresolved? false}; census/describe prints 0 Reagent API call site(s) across 1 file(s) that name Reagent, with no UNRESOLVED clause. Under the new MIG-24 rule this licenses removal, but factory still resolves reagent.core/atom and the build still needs reagent/reagent. The same blind class includes Reagent Vars passed as values, type/protocol references, and build/preload configuration outside scanned CLJS call heads.

The reporter already exposes the crucial distinction as files-with-reagent. Minimal repair: do not call zero calls/no unresolved a dependency proof. Require zero files naming the recognised Reagent namespaces after removing proven-orphan requires, and pair that with a whole-repository textual/dependency-config sweep for non-call references the reporter does not claim to census; otherwise keep reagent/reagent. An equally small tool-side alternative is a dedicated dependency-use census, but do not inflate the existing call-site estimand silently. Add one compact eval/control where r/atom is retained as a value rather than called, so the answer keeps the coordinate. Keep the two-decision ergonomic structure and eval 30; only the removal proof is unsound.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): PR #9033 left stale M-11 and split-routing prose outside the retarget fence

Four prose mentions outside that PR's dispatch fence still name the old owner. SITES (verified at PR #9033's tip):
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2815 - the '(row #6 - the boot smoke-test catches survivor throws on the console)' parenthetical. TWO separate drifts here: the M-11 owner, and 'row #6', which now lives in references/silent-runtime-failures.md after the rf2-su7xh checklist/loop split in the same PR. This file's two links to runtime-smoke-test.md are also what forced that leaf to keep its filename and its loop half, so read it before changing anything there.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:98 - 'the migration skill's exceptional imperative-subscription Form-3 (guided-handlers-state.md SS-M-11)'.

CAUTION - migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md is a hot-zone file; sequence this against any other bead touching it rather than running them in parallel. The two .cljs files are comments/docstrings only; no code behaviour depends on them.

Both were green on these paths before and after PR #9033, since none of the four is a link - so neither gate will confirm this fix. notes:
AUDIT EXPANSION AT PR #9033 (three-lens review): the original four-site inventory is incomplete, so keep this one owner and widen the same retarget sweep.

Additional direct stale sites:
- scripts/check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py:101-102, 227-228, 2216-2217, and 2272-2273 still name guided-handlers-state.md (and, in the latter two, its obsolete line 90) as the M-11 canonical recipe even though this PR retargeted the executable constant and adjacent checker prose to guided-views-m11.md.

- skills/re-frame-migration/spec/inputs.md:63 still routes every Type-B view rule to guided-handlers-state.md, omitting the dedicated M-11 owner.

- skills/re-frame-migration/spec/design.md:134 still opens with Type A / Type B split into two leaves each while the same paragraph now records M-11 as a third Type-B leaf.

Acceptance: retarget the explicit M-11 carriers, make the maintenance/router prose describe the 23-leaf and three-destination topology, and re-grep the package plus checker for old-owner M-11 claims. Do not broaden this into unrelated historical documentation inventory cleanup.
IN-FENCE HALF LANDED IN PR #9039 (worker migskill-h); BEAD LEFT OPEN for the out-of-fence remainder. I closed this bead once against the PRE-WIDENING text and reopened it: the audit expansion landed at 2026-09-03 02:11:24 AUSEST, minutes after my history walk had truthfully reported zero text changes, and I caught it only because bd close echoed a title I had never seen. title: skill(re-frame-migration): authoring-prompt.md says 21 reference leaves; design.md and the tree say 23
description:
skills/re-frame-migration/spec/authoring-prompt.md:19 says the design.md file-
structure block "lists all 21 reference leaves", then enumerates them.

MEASURED at 89e6f32a75: skills/re-frame-migration/references/ holds 23 .md files,
and spec/design.md itself says "23 reference leaves" in its Totals paragraph and
"The twenty-three reference leaves" in section 6. So the authoring prompt is two
leaves stale against the design doc it defers to.

WHY IT MATTERS rather than being a typo: authoring-prompt.md is a LIVE re-authoring
prompt -- its own header says it "re-authors the `re-frame-migration` skill from
this `spec/` folder alone". A stale count there is an instruction to regenerate a
smaller tree. This is the same failure class as the M-11 owner drift PR #9039 fixed
in the adjacent sentence of the same file (rf2-6me0).

FIX: reconcile the count with design.md, and prefer deferring to design.md over
restating a number -- line 19 already says "Do not restate the tree here; read it
from `design.md` so the two meta-docs cannot drift apart", which is precisely the
rule this count breaks.

Noticed while editing line 21 of the same file for rf2-6me0 and deliberately left
alone there: it is a different claim from the M-11 ownership one, and widening that
PR's diff into an unrelated correction was not warranted.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9039, and folded back into rf2-6me0 rather than kept separate. I filed this while rf2-6me0 still read as the narrower four-site bead; its audit expansion (2026-09-03 02:11 AUSEST) then named authoring-prompt.md:19 explicitly and ruled 'These are one cohesive split-completeness repair, not separate issues'. So the split was mine and wrong. THE FIX: authoring-prompt.md:19 said the design.md block 'lists all 21 reference leaves'; design.md's Totals paragraph and section 6 both say 23, and references/ holds 23 .md files. Corrected to 23, and the enumeration now names guided-views-m11.md and silent-runtime-failures.md -- the two leaves whose omission from that list is what let the count drift. That matters because authoring-prompt.md is a LIVE re-authoring prompt ('re-authors the skill from this spec/ folder alone'), so a stale count there is an instruction to regenerate a smaller tree.

value:
A BEAD CAN BE WIDENED BY THE AUDIT WHILE A WORKER IS ALREADY HOLDING IT, AND A CORRECT NEWEST-FIRST WALK AT DISPATCH TIME WILL MISS IT (2026-09-03).

MEASURED. A worker on rf2-6me0 did the history walk exactly as prescribed and CORRECTLY reported zero text changes — because at that moment there were none. The audit's expansion landed at 02:11:24, minutes later, while the worker was mid-task. It discovered this only because 'bd close' echoed back a title it had never seen; it re-walked the history, REOPENED the bead, and did the widened work in a second commit.

WHY THE EXISTING RULES DO NOT COVER THIS. Everything written about bead currency is about the read at the START — order by tracker timestamps, walk newest-first, the description is the oldest text. All of that is correct and all of it is a read of a SNAPSHOT. Nothing says the snapshot can move under you, and on this project it routinely can: the merged-PR audit runs continuously and reopens or rewrites beads as it goes, which is the same mechanism that makes 'this cluster is the entire remaining backlog for the lane' a false claim.

THE CHEAP DEFENCE, WHICH COST THIS WORKER NOTHING AND SAVED THE TASK: READ WHAT bd ECHOES BACK. Close and update commands print the bead's CURRENT title. If that title is not the one you have been working from, the bead moved — stop and re-walk before believing your work is complete. That is a free check on every mutation you were going to make anyway.

THE SECOND DEFENCE, for a long task: re-walk the history once more before writing the PR body, not only at dispatch. A bead held for an hour on this project has a real chance of having been rewritten.

AND THE MAYOR-SIDE VERSION OF THE SAME THING: do not treat a brief's account of a bead as durable. Tell workers the bead outranks the brief — which the dispatch template already says — AND that the bead outranks the bead as they first read it.
